providers.description: CrowdMade partners with online creators from YouTube, Instagram, Snapchat and beyond to design, produce, warehouse, and ship official merchandise their fans are proud to wear. The public storefront at crowdmade.com runs on Shopify and, as of 2026, exposes a machine- and agent-facing commerce surface: a published Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP shopping endpoint, Shopify Customer Accounts OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, an llms.txt, and an agents.md describing how AI shopping agents can search the catalog, build a cart, and complete a buyer-approved checkout. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Faro
providers.description: Faro Health is an AI platform for clinical development that helps biopharma and clinical research teams design and execute better studies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Diego, California, Faro provides study design optimization, automated protocol document authoring, and clinical workflow automation, digitizing and structuring trial protocols so teams can accelerate development without compromising scientific rigor, patient safety, or patient-centricity. Faro is backed by investors including General Catalyst.

providers.name: FieldEdge
providers.description: FieldEdge is field service management (FSM) software for HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and other home- and commercial-services contractors, owned by Xplor Technologies (branded "FieldEdge by Xplor"). It provides customer management, dispatching and scheduling, work orders, a technician mobile app, flat-rate pricebook, service agreements, invoicing and payments, and QuickBooks accounting sync. FieldEdge operates a partner-gated API delivered through an Azure API Management developer portal (docs.api.fieldedge.com); API products and keys are restricted to approved integration partners rather than being openly self-serve. The logical APIs listed here are honestly modeled from FieldEdge's documented product modules and its partner/integration surface - endpoint paths are modeled, not copied from a published public reference, because the reference and OpenAPI live behind the partner portal sign-in.

providers.name: IgGenix
providers.description: IgGenix, Inc. is a clinical-stage antibody discovery and development company in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2019 on work from Stephen Quake's laboratory at Stanford in collaboration with allergy clinician-researcher Kari Nadeau. Its SEQ SIFTER platform uses single-cell RNA sequencing to capture the rare IgE-producing B cells circulating in allergic patients' blood, then re-engineers those sequences into fully human, high-affinity, allergen-specific IgG antibodies designed to block the allergic cascade before it starts. Lead program IGNX001 is a human IgG4 monoclonal antibody for peanut allergy, in the Phase 1 ACCELERATE Peanut trial, with discovery programs against alpha-gal syndrome, nsLTP allergens and atopic dermatitis autoantigens. The company has raised roughly $75M across seed, Series A and a $40M Series B. IgGenix publishes no product or developer API and no developer program; the only machine-readable surface on iggenix.com is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) served at https://iggenix.com/wp-json/, which returns the company's press releases, peer-reviewed publications, conference abstracts, careers post type, pages, media library, taxonomies and site search as anonymous JSON. The OpenAPI definitions in this repository were derived mechanically from that route index; IgGenix publishes none of its own.

providers.name: Issa
providers.description: Issa Compass is a software platform that simplifies Thailand visa applications, operated by Issara Platforms Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) and Issa Systems Co, Ltd. (Bangkok). The platform helps users identify which Thai visa they qualify for and manages the end-to-end application process: a two-minute eligibility questionnaire, document verification and pre-qualification checks, real-time tracking of requirements against thousands of criteria, and a money-back guarantee if a pre-qualified application is rejected. Supported visa types include the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV), Long-Term Resident (LTR), Retirement, Spouse, and Student visas. Issa is a portfolio company of 500 Global. There is no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Kin Insurance
providers.description: Kin Insurance is a direct-to-consumer home insurance platform founded in 2016 that leverages data and artificial intelligence to provide homeowners insurance in high-risk coastal and weather-exposed markets. The platform uses thousands of property data points for automated underwriting, enabling online quote generation, policy binding, and claims management without the need for traditional agents. Kin offers homeowners, condo, flood, and auto insurance across multiple states with a focus on affordability and accessibility in markets traditionally underserved by major carriers.

providers.name: Leal Health (fka TrialJectory)
providers.description: Leal Health (formerly TrialJectory) is an AI-powered, patient-first decision-support platform that matches cancer patients to advanced treatments and clinical trials. Its patented natural language processing engine reads inclusion/exclusion eligibility criteria and connects to ClinicalTrials.gov so patients, caregivers, and oncologists can self-screen against every recruiting oncology trial in roughly two minutes. For pharma, biotech, and CRO customers, the Patient Match Optimizer SaaS dashboard delivers de-identified, aggregate real-time datasets on patient barriers, motivators, geography, and competitive landscape to shorten enrollment timelines and improve minority representation in trials. The company was founded as TrialJectory by Tzvia Bader (CEO), Avital Gaziel, Guy Gildor, and Noam Geva, later rebranded to Leal Health, and lists a Clifton, New Jersey mailing address. Leal Health operates no public developer program: a live platform API host exists at api.leal.health, but every path behind the root returns HTTP 401 and no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation is published.

providers.name: Level Frames
providers.description: Level Frames is a New York City based online custom framing company founded in 2014 by Josh Hubball and Damian Sowers and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2015). The company lets customers design and order handcrafted, made-to-order picture frames from home, either by uploading a digital photo for printing and framing or by shipping in physical artwork, posters and prints. Its catalog covers custom frames, framed canvas prints, framed vinyl records, collage frames, gallery walls, personalized framed photos, and framed chalkboards, whiteboards and corkboards, alongside at-home and in-studio framing services. Level Frames operates a direct-to-consumer web storefront and publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK surface as of this profile.

providers.name: MentorCloud
providers.description: MentorCloud is an AI-enabled, enterprise mentoring software platform that helps organizations optimize employee engagement, retention, and career development through structured mentoring programs. It serves HR and Learning & Development teams and enterprise leaders looking to scale human-led learning across engineering, management, higher education, hospitality, and non-profit contexts. The platform covers mentor/mentee matching, program management, sessions, circles, learning, and community, with use cases spanning new-hire onboarding, leadership development, career progression, and Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) initiatives. MentorCloud is delivered as a hosted B2B SaaS product with managed, custom two-way integrations to enterprise CRM, HR, and single sign-on systems rather than a self-serve public developer API. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Metric
providers.description: Metric is an AI-powered financial intelligence and accounting platform built for business owners, founders, and CEOs. It replaces spreadsheets and expensive CFO teams with a real-time financial dashboard and Max, an AI co-pilot (CF-AI) that answers financial questions such as runway, hiring capacity, and spending in plain language, drawn from live financial data. Metric handles accounting and bookkeeping, payables and receivables, invoicing, eight report types, and UAE VAT compliance, and connects to QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Xero, and Shopify. Headquartered in Abu Dhabi with offices in Rawalpindi, Singapore, and Riyadh, it is backed by 500 Global and serves businesses across 190+ countries. Metric is a SaaS web application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Nauto
providers.description: Nauto is a predictive AI platform for commercial fleet safety. Using in-vehicle AI dash cams and computer vision, it monitors driver behavior in real time, delivers predictive collision alerts before incidents occur, scores driver risk with its VERA system, and powers driver coaching, exoneration, and incident intelligence. Nauto also supports DVIR, IFTA, and ELD fleet-compliance workflows across trucking, delivery, construction, passenger transit, and field-service fleets. Backed by Greylock, Playground Global, and SoftBank Vision Fund, Nauto is SOC 2 Type 1/2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified.

providers.name: nference
providers.description: nference is a healthcare-AI company that builds an agentic intelligence layer for clinical research and drug development. Its nSights platform aggregates and analyzes de-identified multimodal patient data at massive scale — 1.4 billion+ clinical notes, 10 billion+ radiology images, 20 million+ digitized pathology whole-slide images, 12 million+ ECG waveforms, and 100 million+ echocardiogram videos — extracting 30,000+ clinical biomarkers to help life-sciences and health-system partners design patient cohorts, explore patient journeys, annotate data for model development, and run advanced data-science workflows across cardiology, oncology, immunology, rare diseases, neurology, infectious diseases, and nephrology. nference spun out the venture companies Anumana (ECG-based biomarker discovery) and Pramana (digital pathology). The company operates as an enterprise B2B platform with no public self-serve API; it is profiled here for its security, compliance, and governance posture. Backed by Matrix Partners.

providers.name: Omnitracs
providers.description: Omnitracs is a commercial fleet management, telematics, and transportation-management provider, now part of Solera Inc. (acquired 2021, operating under Solera Fleet Solutions). Its Omnitracs One platform and the Omnitracs Roadnet routing platform serve roughly 15,000 fleet customers with ELD / Hours-of-Service compliance, telematics and GPS positioning, driver workflow and messaging, routing and dispatch, and video safety. Omnitracs exposes real integration APIs and web services (Roadnet Web Services, the Services Portal Entity Management web services, and the SOAP/XML Event Subscription Service that streams positions, messages, HOS, and critical events), but access is partner- and customer-account gated - there is no open, self-service public developer portal. API credentials (a username/password with API access) and the integration developer wiki are provisioned to contracted customers and integration partners. Endpoints documented here for gated surfaces are honestly modeled from public integration notes, not from an open reference.

providers.name: Palm HR
providers.description: Palm HR (palm.hr, operating on palmhr.net) is an HR management and payroll platform built specifically for the UAE and broader MENA region, trusted by organizations from startups to enterprises for local labor-law and WPS compliance. The platform spans people management (employee profiles, onboarding and offboarding, document management), attendance and time tracking (mobile check-in/out, timesheets, shift scheduling, project time), payroll automation (WPS-compliant processing, expenses, loans, multi-country and multi-currency), performance management, and recruiting, plus an outsourced-HR service. Palm HR exposes REST APIs with API keys carrying granular permissions so customers can push data to ERPs and external tools, and ships prebuilt integrations with accounting suites (Xero, QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Wafeq, Qoyod, Odoo, Tally), biometric devices (ZKTeco, CAMS), and automation platforms (Zapier, Make, Power Automate). The company is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. This profile was enriched from public web surfaces; no public OpenAPI specification or developer portal was discovered.

providers.name: Parrot
providers.description: Parrot is an AI-powered legal technology platform purpose-built for the litigation, court reporting, and insurance community. Its proprietary large language models are trained on legal and insurance terminology to deliver audio/video-synced deposition transcripts, AI-generated deposition summaries (narrative, page:line, or topic-based), remote deposition scheduling and livestreaming, and AI-enabled medical record summaries with chronologies and source linking. Trusted by law firms, insurance carriers such as USAA and Travelers, and Fortune 500 corporations, Parrot operates under SOC 2, HIPAA, and HITECH controls. Backed by Amplify Partners and XYZ Venture Capital ($11M Series A, 2023); Parrot is now part of Filevine. Parrot is a product and services company; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Peppy
providers.description: Peppy is a global employee healthcare benefits platform, delivered through a mobile app, that connects workers with specialist clinicians across key life stages. Offered by employers as a benefit, Peppy provides unlimited access to practitioners covering women's health, men's health, fertility, pregnancy and early parenthood, menopause, and neurodiversity, alongside lifestyle support for nutrition, fitness, and mental wellbeing. Peppy operates a consumer and employer facing service and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its published web properties and security posture. Peppy is a Seedcamp portfolio company.

providers.name: Pietra
providers.description: Pietra is an AI-powered commerce platform for fast-growing consumer brands and creators. It unifies sourcing, production, fulfillment, logistics, marketing, and operations in a single platform — giving brands access to a network of 40,000+ global suppliers and factories, integrated third-party (3PL) fulfillment infrastructure, AI assistants that automate content creation and affiliate/influencer campaigns, competitive intelligence and social listening, and e-commerce software to run a direct-to-consumer business. Founded in 2019 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). As of this profile, Pietra does not publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Pillar Biosciences
providers.description: Pillar Biosciences is a Natick, Massachusetts molecular diagnostics company, founded in 2014, that develops targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) solutions for precision oncology. Its proprietary SLIMamp (Stem-Loop Inhibition Mediated amplification) chemistry enables highly multiplexed, single-tube PCR library preparation from as little as 2.5 ng of DNA, and its oncoReveal panel portfolio covers solid tumour tissue, liquid biopsy, haematologic malignancy, BRCA/HRD/methylation and inherited disease testing, alongside an InheritReveal line and a VersaTile machine-learning panel-design platform. Sequencing data is processed by PiVAT (Pillar Variant Analysis Toolkit), a secondary-analysis pipeline available as a local install or a HIPAA-scoped cloud deployment, with optional OncoKB-powered tertiary reporting. Pillar ships both research-use-only kits and an IVD product line, and raised a $34.5M round led by Illumina in 2025. Pillar publishes no public API, SDK or developer program; PiVAT's integration surface is bioinformatics file formats (FASTQ, BAM, VCF, PDF) behind a customer login.

providers.name: Pluton Biosciences
providers.description: Pluton Biosciences is a microbial discovery company that uses a proprietary Discovery Platform - high-throughput soil microbiome screening combined with computational analysis - to find naturally occurring microbial consortia for agriculture and carbon sequestration. Its lead product is a Biological Nitrogen System: photosynthetic microbial consortia that operate at the soil surface to fix atmospheric nitrogen and mobilize phosphorus. Pluton is a research-and-product company, not an API company; it has no public developer portal. Partnership and licensing inquiries are handled directly.

providers.name: Pointone
providers.description: PointOne is an AI-powered legal practice management platform that automates time entry, billing compliance, and analytics for law firms. Its products include PointOne Time (automatic cross-device time capture with AI-generated narratives), PointOne Review (pre-bill review with AI markup and collaboration), and PointOne Intelligence (time analytics and resource-allocation insights), along with automatic enforcement of Outside Counsel Guidelines. The platform syncs with billing systems including Aderant, Clio, Filevine, QuickBooks, Actionstep, Elite 3E, Surepoint, MyCase, and LeanLaw, and serves 200+ law firms. PointOne is backed by Bessemer, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and 8VC. No public developer API is currently published; integrations are delivered as pre-built connectors.

providers.name: Railinc
providers.description: Railinc, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Association of American Railroads, delivers IT and information services to the North American freight rail industry. Railinc's suite of APIs empowers customers to simplify and automate business processes essential to the lifecycle of freight rail operations.

providers.name: Rapchat
providers.description: Rapchat is a mobile-first music creation platform for artists, rappers, singers, and producers, founded in 2014. Creators use the Rapchat iOS and Android apps to find professionally-produced beats from top producers, record studio-quality vocals with effects and audio filters, write lyrics, join music challenges, collaborate, and share finished songs with a creator community. The platform reports 15M+ creators, 100M+ tracks, and over one billion plays, and offers free web-based artist tools (rap name generator, lyric generator, rhyme finder, BPM mood guide) alongside Free, Premium, and Pro subscription tiers. Rapchat is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its /api endpoint is an internal application backend (HTTP 403).

providers.name: Resy
providers.description: Resy is a restaurant reservation and discovery platform owned by American Express. Resy does not maintain a publicly self-serve developer portal; integration is restricted to approved partners (POS, CRM, loyalty, marketing, and discovery) under direct partnership agreements. The primary public surface is the consumer web and mobile app and an embeddable "Book with Resy" booking widget for restaurants. The unofficial internal client API at api.resy.com has been widely reverse-engineered by the community, but it is undocumented, unsupported, and may change without notice.

providers.name: Runbooks
providers.description: Runbooks is an all-in-one IT operations platform purpose-built for IT teams and managed service providers (MSPs). It consolidates ITSM (service desk, ticketing, incident management, knowledge base, SLA management), ITAM (hardware and software asset tracking, lifecycle management, warranty tracking, QR code asset labels), BizOps (CRM, client management, quarterly business reviews, budget forecasting, vendor management), SecOps (audit logs, MFA, password management), and Insights (automated reports, satisfaction tracking, quality assurance, KPI analytics) into a single integrated system. The platform targets IT departments and MSPs managing 50-5,000 users at a flat $25 per tech per month pricing model with no tiers or hidden fees. Runbooks is SOC 2 compliant with 99.9% uptime.

providers.name: SendCutSend
providers.description: SendCutSend is a rapid custom manufacturing service offering online sheet metal fabrication, laser cutting, waterjet cutting, CNC machining, CNC bending, tapping, hardware installation, and finishing across 175+ materials, with instant online pricing from uploaded STEP or DXF files and parts delivered in as little as a few days. Customers quote, configure, and order parts through the app.sendcutsend.com web application. The company reached a $1.01B valuation following a $110M investment co-led by Sequoia, Paradigm, and Patrick and John Collison. SendCutSend does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, pricing, and content surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Shopventory
providers.description: Thrive by Shopventory is inventory management, catalog control, and reporting software for small and medium-sized retail, restaurant, and hospitality businesses. Founded in 2012 out of a San Diego boutique and a graduate of the Techstars Boulder accelerator, Shopventory syncs stock, sales, and cost-of-goods data across multiple locations and sales channels, and integrates with Square, Shopify, Clover, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, and QuickBooks Online. The platform offers barcode scanning, purchase-order automation, demand forecasting, bundles and component-level tracking, price-tag printing, and advanced custom reporting. The company operates as Thrive by Shopventory (thrivemetrics.com). Its former public developer API (apidocs.shopventory.com) is no longer resolvable, so this profile captures the company's live web, support, and integration surface plus probed domain-security posture rather than a public API specification.

providers.name: Skootar
providers.description: Skootar is a Thai on-demand courier, messenger, and logistics platform serving Bangkok, its surrounding provinces, and Chonburi. It offers same-day document delivery, cheque and bill collection, parcel shipping, business food delivery, and on-demand pickup-truck and moving jobs across a fleet of motorcycles, cars, and trucks, all with real-time tracking. Orders can be placed 24/7 through the website, the mobile app, or an API intended for high-volume businesses to wire delivery ordering into their own back-office systems. Skootar reports more than 130,000 business customers, 26,000+ drivers, and 9.2 million+ completed deliveries over 12 years, and is backed by 500 Global. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK is published; API access is arranged through its business/enterprise channel.

providers.name: Skuad
providers.description: Skuad is a global HR and employment platform (now part of Payoneer as Payoneer Workforce Management) that lets companies hire, onboard, pay, and manage full-time employees and contractors across 160+ countries without setting up local legal entities. It provides employer-of-record (EOR) services, international payroll in 70+ currencies, contractor management and payments, benefits administration, background verification, and built-in compliance with local employment, tax, and labor laws. Skuad was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network; this profile has been enriched from Skuad's public web presence. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Snap-on
providers.description: Snap-on Incorporated is a global manufacturer and marketer of tools, equipment, diagnostics, repair information, and systems solutions for professional users in vehicle repair, industrial, and other industries. The company provides diagnostic tools, electronic parts catalogs (EPC), repair information systems (ShopKey Pro, SureTrack), and shop management software. Snap-on integrates with dealer management systems (DMS) through its EPC integration program and strategic technology partnerships.

providers.name: Stoik
providers.description: Stoïk is a European cyber-insurtech, founded in 2021 and headquartered in Paris, that pairs cyber insurance with active security prevention for small and mid-market businesses (up to roughly €1B revenue). Insurance coverage of up to €10M is backed by Tokio Marine HCC, Swiss Re and Axeria IARD and sold 100% online through a broker platform used by 1,500+ partner brokers across France, Germany, Spain, Austria, Belgium and the Netherlands. Beyond insurance, Stoïk ships a free risk-monitoring suite — Stoïk Protect (external scan, phishing simulation, Active Directory and cloud scanning, leaked-credential monitoring), Managed Detection & Response (MDR), and managed email security — plus 24/7 incident response. Stoïk is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Anthemis. No public developer API is published today; the developer-adjacent surface is a GitBook help center (docs.stoik.io, with an llms.txt index and a dated changelog), the insured/broker platform at app.stoik.io, and the GitHub org github.com/stoikio.

providers.name: Toonimo
providers.description: Toonimo is a digital adoption platform (DAP) that overlays personalized, interactive on-screen guidance onto enterprise software and websites. Using patented voice, text-bubble, and visual-cue walkthroughs, Toonimo guides end users and employees through onboarding, self-service, and complex workflows to increase conversions, accelerate software adoption, and reduce support costs. It layers on top of platforms such as Salesforce, SAP SuccessFactors, Workday, ServiceNow, Oracle Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics, Coupa, and SharePoint, and enables subject-matter experts (not just developers) to build and maintain adoption content. Toonimo is a marketing/product company backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners; it does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: TransparentBusiness
providers.description: TransparentBusiness is a New York based SaaS company, founded in 2012 by Alex Konanykhin and Silvina Moschini, that sells a cloud platform for managing and monitoring remote workforces: a desktop timer, screenshot-based activity verification, timesheets, task assignment, and real-time project cost and progress reporting for distributed teams and contractors. The company also operates the SheWorks! and Yandiki talent marketplaces and the CloudWorking Academy training platform, and was later renamed Unicoin, Inc. The product is delivered as a hosted web application plus downloadable desktop timer clients; the company publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Vanilla Steel
providers.description: Vanilla Steel is a Berlin-based B2B steel trading platform (Vanilla Steel GmbH, backed by seedcamp) that matches European steel buyers and sellers, arranges financing, and manages logistics end-to-end, connecting 500+ European suppliers with 5,000+ buyers and sellers and returning a best offer within 48 hours from a single format-agnostic request. Its SaaS products — the RFQ Classifier Outlook add-in, the RFQ Extractor OAuth mailbox-ingestion service for Microsoft 365 and Gmail, and the Quoting App — use AI to turn inbound Requests for Quotation into structured trading workflows. Vanilla Steel publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: VendorPM
providers.description: VendorPM is a PropTech procurement and vendor-lifecycle-management platform for the commercial real estate industry, unifying vendor credentialing, compliance screening, eTendering/eBidding, procurement, and contract management under a single login. Its marketplace connects property managers with a network of 50,000+ vendors to fulfill building services and contracts of all sizes, while an AI Procurement CoPilot surfaces recommendations and a Yardi Voyager ERP integration syncs vendor compliance and profile data. VendorPM serves 100+ property management groups and 6,000+ buildings across the US and Canada. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio company; VendorPM exposes no public self-serve developer API — its Yardi/ERP integration is provisioned through a Customer Success Manager.

providers.name: Virta Health
providers.description: Virta Health is a virtual, nutrition-first healthcare company delivering sustainable weight loss and type 2 diabetes reversal. Its program combines personalized nutrition plans, continuous expert health coaching, physician-led medication management, and connected devices, delivered through a consumer mobile app and sold to employers, health plans, and healthcare providers. Virta is HITRUST- and SOC 2 Type II-certified and operates as a HIPAA-covered clinical service. As of this enrichment pass Virta publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface; this profile captures its public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: Weav
providers.description: Weav.ai is an AI-native decisioning platform for property & casualty (P&C) insurance, applying agentic AI and document intelligence across underwriting, premium audit, and claims. The platform pairs pre-configured, line-of-business knowledge graphs and scorecards with an agentic decision engine and human-in-the-loop review, delivered through an API-first, no-code architecture that integrates with existing insurance systems. Developers integrate via a documented REST surface (documents, folders, forms, agents, workflows, actions, and chat services) and a first-party Python developer library (weavaidev) published through the weav-ai GitHub organization, authenticated with a Bearer token against a per-tenant environment host. Weav.ai is backed by Sierra Ventures and is a member of the Guidewire Insurtech Vanguards program.

providers.name: Zenbu 2
providers.description: Zenbu is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) developer-tools startup building a fully hackable desktop interface for managing AI coding agents. The macOS app is a customizable client for the "Pi" coding agent, letting developers run multiple agents in parallel across Git worktrees, review changes, and extend the app at runtime through plugins. Zenbu is built on Zenbu.js, the company's open-source TypeScript framework for building extensible ("hackable") applications, which handles plugin loading, cross-process state sync, RPC, and hot reloading. The framework and its scaffolding tooling are published to npm under the zenbu-labs organization. Zenbu does not currently expose a hosted HTTP/REST developer API; its developer surface is the client-side Zenbu.js framework, its plugin model, and its command-line scaffolders. Founded by Rob Pruzan (ex-Vercel Next.js core, co-author of React Scan).

providers.name: Ziff Davis Enterprise
providers.description: Ziff Davis (Nasdaq: ZD) is a vertically focused digital media and internet company whose portfolio includes leading brands across technology, entertainment, shopping, health, cybersecurity, and marketing technology. Its brands include PCMag, Mashable, IGN, Lifehacker, RetailMeNot, Spiceworks, Everyday Health, IPVanish, Ookla (Speedtest), FullContact, and iContact, among others. The company operates a portfolio of advertising, subscription, and performance-marketing businesses rather than a single first-party public API product. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead; a public web crawl of the corporate site found an active investor-relations, newsroom, brands, privacy, and terms surface but no developer portal, API reference, or published API specification at the corporate (ziffdavis.com) level. A second enrichment pass on 2026-08-13 ran full contract discovery against www.ziffdavis.com — OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, MCP, llms.txt and every /.well-known/ path returned 404, and the WordPress REST root returned 401 — confirming the absence, while surfacing three real corporate programs: a Bugcrowd-hosted Responsible Vulnerability Disclosure Program, a published data-protection compliance program (Data Privacy Framework self-certification for 32 named group entities, GDPR DPAs, CCPA request metrics, EU DSA statement, NIST SP 800-88 vendor security exhibit), and five first-party PHP packages in the ziffdavis Packagist namespace — none of which is an API client library. Ziff Davis brands with their own API surfaces are profiled as separate entries.

providers.name: 10x Genomics
providers.description: 10x Genomics is a life sciences technology company building instruments, reagents, and software that resolve biology at single-cell and spatial resolution. Its Chromium platform delivers single-cell gene expression, immune profiling, and multiomic analysis; its Visium and Xenium platforms deliver spatial transcriptomics and in situ single-cell spatial biology. The company supports researchers with analysis software (Cell Ranger, Space Ranger, Xenium Onboard Analysis, Loupe Browser), a cloud analysis platform, and open datasets. 10x Genomics does not publish a general-purpose public REST developer API; its developer surface is command-line analysis pipelines, file-format tooling, and open-source repositories on GitHub.

providers.name: 1touch.io
providers.description: 1touch.io is an enterprise data-security and data-intelligence vendor whose Kontxtual platform (previously shipped as Inventa) performs automated, near real-time discovery, classification, mapping and cataloging of sensitive data across cloud, on-premises, SaaS and IBM z/OS mainframe environments. The platform combines passive network analysis, ML/NLP classification and an LLM-driven contextual graph to deliver enterprise DSPM, attribute-based access control, access intelligence, DLP for streaming data, mainframe security posture management, cryptographic discovery and AI security. The technology is also OEM-distributed by IBM as Guardium Discover and Classify. Everpure (formerly Pure Storage, NYSE: PSTG) completed its acquisition of 1touch.io on 2026-05-11. Product documentation is published to a MadCap Central portal that requires a customer login, and no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is available.

providers.name: 4DReplay
providers.description: 4DReplay is a media technology company that builds multi-camera, time-slice ("bullet-time") video capture and replay systems for live sports, entertainment and events. Arrays of roughly 50 to 120 synchronized cameras — locked to within 1/10,000 of a second — are processed in real time to produce any-angle replay highlights within seconds of a play and deliver them to broadcast, mobile and OTT audiences. The product line spans 4DReplay (premium broadcast instant replay), 4DReplay+ / 4DLive (5G-based interactive multi-view live streaming with speed, angle and tracking overlays), and 4Dist, a browser-based interactive OTT platform that adds automated AI motion and swing analysis for academies, coaches and players. Founded in 2012 by Hongsu Jung and headquartered in San Mateo, California, with offices in Seoul and Tokyo, the company has worked with ESPN, NBC, CBS, FOX Sports, the NBA, MLB, NHL, the PGA Championship and the Olympics. As of August 2026 4DReplay publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; its surfaces are broadcast integrations and the consumer/operator 4Dist web and mobile apps.

providers.name: Agari
providers.description: Agari is an email-security provider that pioneered and helped author the DMARC email-authentication standard to protect organizations from phishing, business email compromise (BEC), email spoofing, and brand impersonation. Founded in 2009, Agari was acquired by HelpSystems (now Fortra) in May 2021 and is delivered as Fortra's email-security portfolio, including DMARC Protection / Brand Protection, Phishing Defense, and Phishing Response. The Agari Platform exposes a RESTful JSON API secured with OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials for retrieving security telemetry, auditing users and domains, tracking DMARC policy enforcement, and integrating Agari data into SIEM and SOAR tooling. It was originally backed by Norwest Venture Partners and other venture investors before its acquisition.

providers.name: Base Power
providers.description: Base Power (Base Texas REP, LLC, PUCT License #10338) is an Austin, Texas home energy company that pairs an installed home battery (40–80 kWh) with retail electricity service across Texas and Illinois. The battery powers a home automatically during outages with no manual switch and helps lower the energy bill: batteries charge when grid demand is low and send power back to the grid when demand is high (grid-balancing), and that grid revenue helps keep member energy rates low. Base can be the retail electricity provider with or without a battery, works with existing solar, and serves the Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP, CoServ, GVEC, Farmers Electric, and El Paso Electric areas in Texas plus ComEd in Illinois. Led by CEO Zach Dell and co-founder Justin Lopas; named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies (2026); backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Addition, Bond Capital, Ribbit Capital, and Spark Capital. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Base publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Ben
providers.description: Ben (thanksben.com) is an AI-native global employee benefits and rewards platform for enterprises. It unifies benefits eligibility rules, policy configuration, employee enrollment and access, spend and compliance dashboards, and rewards/recognition into a single system spanning 140+ countries, replacing fragmented regional benefits tooling. Customers include Moet, Henkel, Virgin, Zalando, Deliveroo, and Octopus Energy. Ben is backed by Seedcamp and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company; it publishes no public developer API today, so this profile captures the company's identity and its public security and trust surface (RFC 9116 security.txt, a Vanta-hosted Trust Center, and probed domain security).

providers.name: BreezoMeter
providers.description: Environmental intelligence REST API providing real-time and forecast air quality, pollen counts, wildfire data, and weather information with street-level accuracy. BreezoMeter was acquired by Google in September 2022 and its technology is now integrated into Google Maps Platform.

providers.name: Cardboard
providers.description: Cardboard is an agentic AI video editor that runs entirely in the browser. Users import raw footage and describe the edit in natural language — "make a 60-second recap", "cut this into ads" — and Cardboard cuts, captions, reframes (vertical/square/landscape), removes silences, generates and clones voiceovers, translates and dubs across languages, and composes a first draft on a real timeline the user can refine. It is built on multimodal LLMs plus WebGPU/WebCodecs to make a genuine non-linear editor possible in the browser, with real-time collaboration and frame-pinned comments. Cardboard was founded in the Y Combinator Winter 2026 batch and is a consumer/prosumer creative application; it does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Civitas Learning
providers.description: Civitas Learning is a higher education technology company whose Student Impact Platform unifies student data, predictive analytics, and coordinated workflows to help colleges and universities improve enrollment, persistence, and completion outcomes. The platform consolidates data from SIS, LMS, CRM, and event systems into a data lakehouse, layers institution-specific predictive models (CivIQ) on top, and surfaces real-time, actionable insights to advisors, faculty, and administrators through products such as Explore, Inspire, Impact, Illume, College Scheduler, Degree Map, and Academic Planning. Civitas Learning serves institutions of all sizes and pairs its software with strategic advisory services. It does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public operational, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Evidation Health
providers.description: Evidation Health is a San Mateo, California digital health company, founded in 2012, that measures health in everyday life and runs permissioned real-world data research at scale. Its consumer app and platform — Achievement — rewards members for connecting wearables, apps and health records, and its enterprise Research & Engagement Platform gives life-sciences, payer, government and non-profit customers eConsent and onboarding, ePRO and survey capture, passive and active device monitoring, program analytics, and participant education. Evidation combines data from sources including Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Dexcom and EHR/claims records (via a partnership with 1upHealth's FHIR-based Patient Connect, and with HealthVerity), and has enabled 175+ virtual real-world studies and 70+ peer-reviewed publications. Evidation publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surfaces are the member app backend and enterprise data deliveries, neither of which is publicly documented.

providers.name: Express
providers.description: Express is a fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework for Node.js, providing a robust set of features for building web and mobile applications and APIs. Maintained under the OpenJS Foundation, Express is one of the most widely used HTTP server frameworks in the JavaScript ecosystem.

providers.name: Flexitricity
providers.description: Flexitricity Limited is an Edinburgh-based energy flexibility aggregator and licensed electricity supplier operating what it describes as the first, largest and most advanced demand response portfolio in Great Britain — a virtual power plant exceeding 1GW. Founded in 2004 by Dr Alastair Martin, acquired by Alpiq in 2014, merged with Quinbrook's Velox Power in 2022, and per the company's own timeline acquired by Drax in 2026, it sits in the value chain between commercial, industrial and aggregated domestic energy assets and the GB wholesale and balancing markets. It routes customer assets — batteries, standby generation, industrial load, hydrogen electrolysers, co-located sites and, through its FlexGO product, residential EV charging — into the Balancing Mechanism, Capacity Market, frequency response, reserve services, the Demand Flexibility Service, DNO flexibility markets and wholesale trading. Its API posture is closed: Flexitricity publishes no developer portal, no documented public API, no OpenAPI, and no open market data of its own. The developer-facing subdomains developer., developers., docs., api. and data. do not resolve; the only interactive surface is portal.flexitricity.com, which requires a customer account. The United Kingdom has no consumer data-portability mandate comparable to Australia's Consumer Data Right, so nothing compels Flexitricity to expose customer usage data through an API. The open, machine-readable data about Flexitricity is published by Elexon, not by Flexitricity — its 63 registered BM Units under lead party FLEXTRCY are retrievable anonymously from the Elexon BMRS Insights API. Open on the regulator's side, closed on its own: that split is the finding.

providers.name: Humio
providers.description: Humio is a log management and observability platform built for ingesting, storing, and searching machine data in real time at scale. Backed by Accel and acquired by CrowdStrike in 2021, Humio is now delivered as CrowdStrike Falcon LogScale. It provides high-throughput streaming ingest (including Splunk HEC and Elastic bulk compatible endpoints), a live query language for dashboards and alerts, and index-free retention. Developers integrate through a REST API for ingest and search plus a GraphQL API for administration (repositories, parsers, users, ingest tokens), with official client libraries for Python, Node.js, Go, and JavaScript and the humioctl command-line client.

providers.name: InvestCloud
providers.description: InvestCloud is a wealth-management technology company that provides an AI-driven digital wealth platform connecting advisors, financial institutions, asset managers, TAMPs, RIAs and investors across the full investment lifecycle. Its product surface spans front-office advisor and client solutions, a wealth data platform ("Digital Warehouse") that aggregates custodial, market and portfolio data, managed account solutions including the Advisor Programs List (APL) and Private Markets Account, post-trade processing and settlement, revenue management, and the NaviPlan and RetireUp financial planning products acquired with Advicent. InvestCloud markets a developer platform — branded "Wealthsqope Digital Developer" — offering web-service APIs, embeddable widgets, code recipes, client libraries and application API keys, but that platform and its reference documentation sit entirely behind a portal login, and no machine-readable API contract is published publicly.

providers.name: Joor
providers.description: JOOR is a New York-based SaaS company (founded 2010) operating a leading B2B wholesale fashion commerce platform and digital marketplace that connects fashion brands with retailers to run their wholesale business end to end. The platform digitizes wholesale buying with online linesheets, lookbooks, virtual showrooms, order management, and the JOOR Marketplace, alongside products such as JOOR Pay (wholesale payments), JOOR Passport (virtual trade shows), and Retail data/analytics. JOOR connects thousands of brands with hundreds of thousands of retail doors globally. Its production platform is fronted by a Kong API gateway and secured with Keycloak-based OpenID Connect authentication; API access is partner/integration-oriented rather than a self-serve public developer program. This profile was enriched from JOOR's live public surface (OIDC discovery, GitHub organization, and status page).

providers.name: Maryland Transit Administration
providers.description: The Maryland Transit Administration (MDOT MTA) supports open transit data initiatives and makes resources available to developers and applications. It primarily uses the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) and GTFS-RT to convey schedule, geographic, fare, vehicle position, and trip update data for Local Bus, Light Rail, Metro Subway, MARC Train, and Commuter Bus services in a standardized format.

providers.name: Nordigen
providers.description: Connect to bank accounts using official bank APIs and get raw transaction data

providers.name: Polars
providers.description: Polars is a blazingly fast, open-source DataFrame library and query engine written in Rust, with first-party bindings for Python, Rust, Node.js, and R. It provides lazy and eager execution, streaming for larger-than-memory datasets, automatic query optimization, multi-threading, and the Apache Arrow columnar memory format. Polars Cloud extends the same DataFrame API to managed and on-premise distributed compute with zero code changes. The project is developed by pola-rs and backed by Accel and Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Polimorphic
providers.description: Polimorphic is a New York-based government technology company building a complete AI platform for local, county, state, and federal government service delivery. Its product suite pairs a Constituent Relationship Manager (CRM) with an AI Chatbot & Search, a Voice Agent (VoiceAI), and Workflows so public agencies can answer residents 24/7 in 75+ languages and guide them through permits, licenses, applications, and payments from intake to resolution. Polimorphic connects to existing government systems of record (ArcGIS, Tyler, Accela, Salesforce, Laserfiche, Stripe, and more) and is used by 200+ public-sector departments serving tens of millions of residents. Founded by Parth Shah (CEO) and Daniel Smith (CTO), the company is backed by General Catalyst, M13, and Shine.

providers.name: Roofstock
providers.description: Roofstock is a residential real estate investment platform and online marketplace for buying, selling, and managing single-family rental (SFR) homes. It gives individual and institutional investors research, analytics, certified property listings, and end-to-end services spanning acquisitions, property management (Mynd), portfolio accounting software (Stessa), tenant screening (RentPrep), asset management, and dispositions across dozens of U.S. markets. The company reports hundreds of thousands of users and over $10B in transacted volume. Roofstock operates a private web API (api.roofstock.com) and a GraphQL endpoint powering its marketplace applications; it does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, first-party SDKs, or documented API access. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and SoftBank Vision Fund and enriched from Roofstock's public web surface.

providers.name: Seatti
providers.description: Seatti is a hybrid-workplace management platform that helps organizations run desk, room, and parking booking, track real office occupancy and utilization without hardware sensors, manage visitor check-ins, and coordinate team presence. It integrates deeply with Microsoft Entra ID, Outlook, and Teams, and serves 100+ companies across 30+ countries including OSRAM, Sartorius, and IKB. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech (Applicative SaaS) and enriched in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Snappy
providers.description: Snappy is a corporate gifting platform that lets businesses send curated gifts, branded swag, and recipient-choice collections to employees and customers. Beyond its web app, Snappy publishes a developer API suite that embeds gifting into CRMs, HRIS platforms, and marketing-automation tools, triggering gifts from business events such as recognition moments, loyalty milestones, and sales-pipeline events, with budget controls and approval workflows. It also ships Slack and Microsoft Teams integrations. Backed by GGV Capital; sector hr-tech / corporate gifting.

providers.name: Spike
providers.description: Spike is an AI-powered email and team collaboration platform that turns standard email accounts (Gmail, Outlook, IMAP) into a chat-like, conversational experience. Its consumer Email App reformats existing inboxes into threaded conversations, while Spike Teamspace is an end-to-end email and team-chat service with shared inboxes, channels, groups, collaborative docs, tasks, notes, and built-in video meetings. Spike layers AI features across the inbox for smart prioritization, thread summaries, and draft assistance. The company is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass Spike ships consumer and team applications but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; the profile below captures its real product, security posture, and public link surface.

providers.name: SPREAD
providers.description: SPREAD is a Berlin-based, AI-native engineering intelligence platform for complex product development and manufacturing. It connects fragmented product lifecycle data across PLM, CAD, ERP, requirements, and simulation systems into a unified engineering ontology, so teams building automotive, defense, and industrial products can find issues earlier and ship faster. The platform surfaces a set of engineering intelligence solutions — Requirements Manager, Product Explorer, Error Inspector, and Action Tower — on top of SPREAD Studio, a low-code environment for building custom analyses, with 40+ connectors to systems such as Teamcenter, Windchill, 3DEXPERIENCE, SAP, Polarion, JIRA, CATIA, and Creo. Customers include Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Ford, Bosch, Audi, and Daimler Truck. Backed by HV Capital; added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Stryker
providers.description: Stryker Corporation is a Fortune 500 medical technologies company offering products in orthopedics, medical and surgical equipment, and neurotechnology and spine. Stryker provides Connected OR integration platforms and Smart Equipment Management (SEM) systems for healthcare facilities. The company does not currently offer a publicly documented developer API. Stryker's digital health products include the Mako robotic arm for orthopedic surgery, iSuite integrated OR technology, and asset tracking systems. Integration with hospital EHR and OR management systems is done through vendor partnerships rather than public APIs.

providers.name: Tawkify
providers.description: Tawkify is a US personalized matchmaking service that pairs paying clients with a trained human matchmaker rather than offering a self-service dating app. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, the company screens and hand-selects introductions from a network of several million singles, arranges curated first dates, and collects structured feedback after each match. Packages are sold by consultation through a client experience specialist instead of a published price list. Tawkify operates a consumer web application at app.tawkify.com for onboarding, profiles and match feedback, but publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind; its engineering surface is entirely internal.

providers.name: The Black Tux
providers.description: The Black Tux is an online formalwear company offering premium suit and tuxedo rentals and purchases for weddings and formal events. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Santa Monica, California, it pairs a direct-to-consumer online store with roughly 50 physical showrooms nationwide, home try-on, group wedding coordination with party pricing, free shipping over $200, and a perfect-fit guarantee. The storefront runs on Shopify; The Black Tux does not publish a first-party developer API. The only machine-readable surface on the domain is Shopify's managed Customer Account identity service (OIDC / OAuth authorization server discovery). This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and enriched with the verifiable public identity and web properties the company genuinely publishes.

providers.name: The Lafz
providers.description: Lafz is a halal-certified cosmetics and personal-care brand, founded in 2019 and headquartered in Singapore as part of the Believe PTE FMCG group. It sells hair care, skin care, makeup, a caffeine range, deodorants and fragrance made without alcohol, parabens or animal by-products. The direct-to-consumer storefront at lafz.com runs on Shopify and exposes real agent-facing surfaces: a Shopify customer-account OpenID Connect provider, an /llms.txt agent guide, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) shopping MCP server for buyer-approved agent-driven checkout. thelafz.com is the corporate "halal compliant factories" site. Added to the API Evangelist network as an Accel portfolio-graph lead and enriched from its live public surfaces.

providers.name: Universe
providers.description: Universe is a no-code website builder that lets anyone design and publish a custom website from a phone, tablet, or computer, using a drag-and-drop GRID block system with built-in commerce, mail tools, analytics, and SEO. A 2023 Apple Design Award winner with more than one million sites built, Universe is a Y Combinator W18 company backed by GV and General Catalyst. Universe is a consumer creation platform and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Urban Sports Club
providers.description: Urban Sports Club is a Berlin-based sports and wellness membership platform. One flexible subscription gives members access to more than 50 sports and wellness activities across thousands of partner venues in Europe, plus online classes, and employers can offer it as a corporate fitness benefit. The company publishes no public developer API; partner studios and gyms connect through third-party booking-software integrations such as Eversports, Magicline, bsport, Virtuagym, and Mindbody. A Partech portfolio company.

providers.name: Veritas Software
providers.description: Veritas Technologies (originally Veritas Software) is an enterprise data management and protection vendor whose products — NetBackup, Alta, Backup Exec, and InfoScale — expose RESTful APIs for automating backup, recovery, storage provisioning, and data governance. NetBackup ships Swagger/OpenAPI-documented REST APIs served from the master server, with first-party code samples published under the VeritasOS GitHub organization. The company runs a public trust and compliance program covering SOC 2, FedRAMP, HIPAA, FIPS 140, GDPR, and CCPA. Accel is among its historical investors.

providers.name: Wikimapia
providers.description: Wikimapia is a collaborative geographic wiki that layers crowdsourced place information onto satellite imagery. Launched in 2006, the platform covers over 32 million geographic objects contributed by its community. The REST API provides programmatic access to places, categories, streets, and geographic searches using API-key authentication. Responses are available in JSON and KML formats. The API supports bounding-box queries, coordinate-based nearest-place lookups, full-text search, and detailed place retrieval including geometry, photos, comments, and community-tagged categories.

providers.name: Worklittle
providers.description: Worklittle is a workforce-intelligence platform covering job discovery, auto-apply, embedded careers boards, ATS sync and sourcing over one API. It splits into two halves: Jobs, the market-wide index plus candidate-facing apply and document tools including commute search on a geocoded job map, and Business, an employer hiring workspace with postings, an ATS pipeline, employees, HR documents and webhooks. The public contract is an OpenAPI 3.1 document of 59 paths and 59 operations served from api.worklittle.com with bearer authentication. Worklittle also operates an MCP server documented for Cursor, Claude and VS Code, and publishes a 1.4MB agent manifest alongside a 97KB llms.txt.

providers.name: Workrise
providers.description: Workrise - which returned to its original RigUp brand in September 2024 - is an Austin-based source-to-pay platform for the energy industry, combining vendor management, contingent workforce staffing, bid management, capital management, and field-service payments for upstream and midstream oil and gas operators. Backed by a16z and Founders Fund. The company publishes no public developer portal or API documentation; platform access is through accounts.rigup.com (OpenID Connect via Auth0), and its engineering org open-sources utilities at github.com/rigup.

providers.name: WSDL
providers.description: WSDL (Web Services Description Language) is a W3C standard XML format for describing web service interfaces. It defines services as collections of network endpoints (ports) that exchange messages, specifying the abstract operations, message formats, and protocol bindings needed to interact with a web service. WSDL 2.0 became a W3C Recommendation on June 26, 2007, and adds support for all HTTP request methods, making it more suitable for RESTful web services than its predecessor WSDL 1.1.

providers.name: Yaak
providers.description: Yaak is an open-source desktop API client for organizing and executing REST, GraphQL, WebSockets, Server Sent Events, and gRPC requests. Built with Tauri, Rust, and React, it is a privacy-first, fast desktop client with no telemetry and no cloud lock-in.

providers.name: Anduin
providers.description: Anduin (Anduin Transactions) is a private-markets technology company that digitizes investor onboarding and fund operations for venture capital, private equity, and hedge funds. Its platform replaces paper-based subscription workflows with electronic fund subscription documents, secure data rooms, investor data management, an engagement hub, an integration hub, automated data extraction, and e-signature. The company reports 1,305+ funds served, $244B+ capital raised, and 74,000+ investors subscribed. Anduin publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI; this profile captures its public company, trust, and security surfaces (Trust Center, RFC 9116 security.txt, and domain-security posture). Backed by 8vc; surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Attivo Networks (SentinelOne)
providers.description: Attivo Networks was a pioneer in identity threat detection and response (ITDR), cyber deception, and Active Directory attack protection. SentinelOne acquired Attivo Networks in 2022 and folded its technology into SentinelOne Singularity Identity, part of the AI-powered Singularity security platform spanning endpoint (EDR/XDR), identity, and cloud security. There is no standalone public Attivo API; programmatic access is delivered through the SentinelOne management console REST API (v2.1), which is scoped to a customer's console URL rather than a public developer portal. This API Evangelist profile tracks the combined entity's public security, trust, disclosure, and compliance surface: a published RFC 9116 security.txt, a HackerOne-hosted bug bounty, and a SafeBase trust center carrying SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001/27017/27018, FedRAMP, and TX-RAMP certifications.

providers.name: Ava
providers.description: Ava is a consumer financial-technology company that helps people build credit and reduce the cost of debt. Its products include the Ava Credit Builder Mastercard (a no-interest card usable at approved subscription merchants), a Save & Build secured savings loan, and rent and utility payment reporting to the three major U.S. credit bureaus (TransUnion, Equifax, Experian). Ava operates as a mobile app on a subscription model and partners with regulated banks and lenders (including Patriot Bank, N.A. and Pier Lending) to deliver its products. This profile was surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Ava is a consumer app and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Brightfield
providers.description: Brightfield is an extended-workforce intelligence company whose TDX (Talent Data Exchange) and TDX AI platform give enterprises data, automation, and precision over contingent-labor and statement-of-work (SOW) spending across 100+ countries. Products include Rate Intelligence, Rate Card Manager, SOW Rate Insights, SOW Quality and Risk Analytics, Supplier Scorecard, and an ROI Dashboard, built on transaction-level data from 700+ companies and $500B+ of global spend. Founded and led by CEO Jason Ezratty and headquartered in Washington, DC, Brightfield is backed by Sapphire Ventures. The product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS application; no public developer API or documentation surface is published at this time.

providers.name: CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act)
providers.description: The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA), is a state statute that grants California residents rights over their personal information: the right to know, delete, correct, opt-out of sale/sharing, limit use of sensitive personal information, and non-discrimination for exercising privacy rights. It is enforced by the California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) and the California Attorney General. Technical interoperability mechanisms include the Global Privacy Control (GPC) browser signal and the IAB Tech Lab US Privacy (USP) / Global Privacy Platform (GPP) signals for advertising technology. This index tracks the official regulatory resources, technical privacy signals, and commercial APIs that help businesses comply with CCPA/CPRA obligations.

providers.name: Cleerly
providers.description: Cleerly is a digital healthcare company building an AI-powered platform for the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease (heart disease). Its software analyzes coronary CT angiography (CCTA) imaging to automatically quantify and characterize atherosclerotic plaque, measure stenosis severity, and stage disease, giving physicians a precise, personalized picture of a patient's heart-disease risk. The goal is to move heart-disease care from symptom-based testing toward direct measurement of plaque, reducing unnecessary invasive procedures while improving diagnostic accuracy. Cleerly operates as an enterprise clinical SaaS delivered to health systems, cardiologists, and imaging centers rather than a public developer API program; it publishes a marketing and clinical-evidence site plus a clinician-facing application (Cleerly Labs) and a public trust center. Cleerly is backed by Battery Ventures and Insight Partners.

providers.name: Coravin
providers.description: Coravin is a consumer beverage-technology company best known for its wine preservation systems, which use a thin needle and inert argon gas to pour wine by the glass without pulling the cork, leaving the remaining wine unoxidized for weeks or months. Its product line spans the Timeless, Pivot, and Sparkling systems plus Pure argon capsules, sold direct-to-consumer and through retail and trade channels. Coravin does not operate a standalone public developer API; its direct storefront runs on Shopify, which exposes a real agent-native commerce surface — a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, a hosted shopping MCP endpoint, and OIDC / OAuth 2.0 authorization-server metadata for Shopify Customer Accounts. Backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Decorte Future Industries
providers.description: Decorte Future Industries (DFI) is a UK healthtech company building AI that extracts clinical health signals from sound. Its technology turns the microphone in an ordinary smartphone into a screening device, analyzing audio to detect signs of heart, breathing, brain, and gut conditions at a standard targeting in-clinic specialist examinations. DFI's first commercial product, Sonus Health, is a veterinary heart-screening platform: clinics and pet owners record 30 seconds of heart sound from dogs (cats and horses coming soon) with a phone, and AI returns heart rate, heart rate variability, murmur detection, and a composite Heart Health Score in seconds, with a full report reviewed by a board-certified veterinary cardiologist within 48 hours. Sonus Health ships as iOS and Android apps for pet owners and a web dashboard for veterinary clinics.

providers.name: Descartes Labs
providers.description: Descartes Labs was a Santa Fe, New Mexico geospatial intelligence company founded in 2014 as a spin-out from Los Alamos National Laboratory. The company built the Descartes Labs Platform, a cloud-native geospatial data refinery and analytics environment combining a petabyte-scale satellite imagery archive (Landsat, Sentinel-1/2, MODIS, NAIP, PlanetScope, SkySat, commercial radar, NEXRAD weather radar, plus client-uploaded data) with a Python client library, JupyterHub-based workbench, and distributed compute for training and running deep learning and remote-sensing models at scale. Customers in agriculture, mining, energy, defense, insurance, and the U.S. government used the platform to build production geospatial machine learning pipelines covering crop forecasting, mineral exploration, infrastructure monitoring, methane detection, wildfire response, and ESG reporting. The Platform exposed a Catalog (imagery, bands, products, blobs, events), a Compute service (containerised functions, jobs, schedules), a Vector service (tabular and geospatial features), Dynamic Compute (lazy raster algebra and tiling), Auth, and a `descarteslabs` CLI. In October 2024, EarthDaily Analytics — backed by Antarctica Capital — acquired Descartes Labs and the Descartes Labs Government, Inc. subsidiary, folding the team, customers, and platform into the EarthDaily Constellation programme. The product was rebranded EarthOne in 2025; the `descarteslabs` Python package has been formally discontinued in favour of `earthdaily-earthone` (v5.x), the github.com/descarteslabs organisation has been renamed to `dlarchives`, www.descarteslabs.com is now a parked domain, and the docs.descarteslabs.com developer portal has been retired in favour of EarthDaily-hosted EarthOne documentation. This catalog entry preserves the historical Descartes Labs Platform surface as an archive — see the EarthDaily / EarthOne profile for the active product.

providers.name: Dialogue
providers.description: Dialogue is a leading Canadian virtual healthcare and employee wellness provider operating an Integrated Health Platform that delivers primary care, mental health support, Employee Assistance Programs (EAP), and wellness programming to members through a single mobile and web application available 24/7/365. The company serves more than 52,000 Canadian organizations — including Sun Life, National Bank of Canada, Via Rail, Lightspeed, and Samsung — connecting employees and their families with multidisciplinary care teams of nurses, physicians, and mental health specialists. Dialogue is a consumer-facing digital health application; it does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Duco
providers.description: Duco is an AI-powered operational data automation platform for financial services. It helps banks, asset managers, brokers, asset servicers and market infrastructure firms normalize, validate and reconcile any data in the cloud — cutting the time spent on manual data work, reducing operational risk and accelerating front-, middle- and back-office processes. The no-code platform ingests data from any source (including unstructured documents via Adaptive Intelligent Document Processing), then transforms, matches, reconciles and publishes it with full audit and control. Duco's Agentic Workspace layers agentic AI over these operations so agents can handle repetitive extraction, matching and exception-labelling work under human oversight. Use cases span securities and derivatives reconciliation, ETD clearing, OTC confirmations, custody, cash accounts, crypto holdings and transaction/regulatory reporting (EMIR, CFTC, MiFID II, ASIC, MAS, T+1). Customers include HSBC, Deutsche Bank, ING, Santander, Northern Trust and Fidelity Digital Assets. Duco is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Farmers Business Network
providers.description: Farmers Business Network (FBN) is a direct-to-farmer ag platform combining a member network, e-commerce for crop inputs (seed, chemistry, animal health), agronomy and precision analytics, financing and crop insurance, and a sustainability / Scope-3 program (Gradable). FBN Analytics ingests precision data from 60+ monitor types and integrates with John Deere Operations Center and CNH AFS Connect to pull machine, planting, application, and harvest data into the FBN platform. FBN is a Field to Market Qualified Data Management Partner via the Fieldprint API. FBN does not publish a public developer portal; partner integrations are arranged directly.

providers.name: Fifteenth
providers.description: Fifteenth is a San Francisco-based fintech company operating an AI-powered personal tax platform for ambitious earners — founders, investors, executives, and technology professionals with complex financial situations such as equity compensation (ISOs, RSOs, RSUs, NSOs), liquidity events (IPOs and acquisitions), partnership income (K-1s), and active stock and crypto trading. The service pairs dedicated human CPAs with AI-driven automation: users link their banking, payroll, and investment accounts via one-click integrations (Workday, Rippling, Robinhood, Wealthfront, Carta, Charles Schwab, AngelList, Coinbase and more), and the platform automatically detects tax-relevant transactions, organizes documents, models scenarios, and delivers proactive quarterly planning plus unlimited year-round advice at flat-fee pricing starting around $1,000 per year. Fifteenth raised $8.25M in seed funding (February 2025) led by A* and General Catalyst. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Foraged
providers.description: Foraged is a community marketplace for wild and specialty foods, connecting independent foragers, farmers, fishers, and artisan food producers directly with home cooks and professional chefs across the United States. Founded in 2021 and built on a custom Medusa commerce stack, Foraged provides an end-to-end platform covering vendor storefronts, product listings, shipping logistics, and secure payment processing for hard-to-source ingredients like wild mushrooms, truffles, foraged berries, sea vegetables, and other specialty foods. Sellers manage their entire shop from a vendor dashboard while buyers discover seasonal wild foods through the marketplace website and mobile app. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Foraged publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Immersed
providers.description: Immersed is a spatial-computing company that turns AR/VR headsets into portable multi-monitor workspaces for remote work, coding, and collaboration. Its free desktop agent streams up to five virtual screens into headsets such as Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, GalaxyXR, and Pico, adding solo focus environments plus multi-user telepresence with screen sharing and whiteboarding. Immersed is also building Visor, its own lightweight 4K-per-eye standalone headset. The company is Techstars-backed. Immersed publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, product, security, and llms.txt surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Insta360
providers.description: Insta360 (Arashi Vision Co., Ltd) is a consumer and professional imaging company best known for its 360-degree and action cameras (the X, GO, ACE, Link, and Pro/Titan lines). For developers, Insta360 runs a first-party developer program through its Insta360Develop GitHub organization and a VitePress developer-documentation site. Cameras expose on-device HTTP control APIs: consumer models implement Google's Open Spherical Camera (OSC) API over the camera Wi-Fi AP, and the Pro/Titan line adds a JSON-over-HTTP command API (ProCameraApi) for capture, live streaming, and file access. Native SDKs wrap this surface for C++ (camera control and media stitching/editing), Android, and iOS so third-party apps can connect to, configure, capture from, and post-process footage from Insta360 hardware.

providers.name: Kiwibot
providers.description: Kiwibot — legally Kiwi Campus, Inc., and rebranded to Robot.com in October 2025 — builds and operates fleets of autonomous sidewalk delivery robots, warehouse logistics robots, quadruped and humanoid platforms, and robot-mounted advertising units. Founded in Berkeley, California in 2017 by Felipe Chavez and Jason Oviedo out of a UC Berkeley campus food-delivery pilot, the company reports more than 1.7 million completed real-world autonomous tasks for campus dining, retail, grocery and enterprise customers across the United States, Canada, Colombia, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, and acquired mobile-advertising firm Nickelytics in 2023. Its B2B delivery platform is exposed as an API-key-gated REST service on a Google Cloud Endpoints gateway at api.kiwibot.com — historically integrated by ordering partners such as Shopify and Ordermark — but the company publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no machine-readable contract; access runs through the sales/demo form. Its autonomy team publishes substantial first-party open source ROS 2 tooling from the github.com/kiwicampus organization.

providers.name: Koltin
providers.description: Koltin is a Mexican health membership company serving older adults, aimed at people aged roughly 50 to 84 and at the adult children who want to protect their parents and grandparents. Koltin is explicit that it is not an insurer and does not sell traditional policies: it packages access to private medical care, preventive follow-up, and financial protection against costly illness or accident into a membership. The membership pairs a major-medical expense insurance product operated and issued by BBVA Seguros Salud with preventive medicine — longevity assessments, an integrated medical check-up, video consultations, and continuous follow-up — plus a social community program (painting, tai chi, film discussion, dance). It operates across CDMX, Estado de Mexico, Guadalajara, Monterrey, Queretaro, Puebla, Guanajuato, Cuernavaca, Merida, and Veracruz, and publishes a member portal, a hospital network directory, and an extensive Spanish-language blog on aging and preventive health. Koltin is a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification; it does publish a first-party llms.txt describing the site for language models.

providers.name: Liveu
providers.description: LiveU is a provider of cloud-based, IP-bonded live video contribution, production, and distribution technology for broadcasters, sports, news, public safety, and enterprise. Its portfolio spans field encoders (the LU-series and the Q Era LU900Q), the LiveU Central cloud management platform, LiveU Studio and Nexus production tools, the LiveU Matrix distribution grid, DataBridge and LU-LINK connectivity, and the LiveU Solo streaming line. LiveU pioneered bonded-cellular transmission that aggregates multiple LTE/5G, Wi-Fi, and satellite links into a single reliable, low-latency video feed. This profile was surfaced as a venture-capital portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; LiveU publishes marketing, support, and training surfaces but no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or open API documentation was found - the LiveU Central API is available to customers behind authentication.

providers.name: Makersite
providers.description: Makersite is an AI-powered Product Lifecycle Intelligence platform that helps manufacturers manage product sustainability, cost, and compliance by connecting products to deep-tier supply chain, material, and chemical data. The platform automates lifecycle assessments (LCA) and product carbon footprint (PCF) calculations, supports eco-design and cost optimization, and produces regulatory reporting such as EU Taxonomy and CBAM. It integrates with enterprise CAD, ERP, and PLM systems (PTC Windchill, Siemens Teamcenter, Autodesk, ANSYS). Makersite is a portfolio company of Partech. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Moonvalley
providers.description: Moonvalley is an AI research lab building Marey, a studio-grade generative video model for filmmakers. Marey generates cinematic image-to-video and text-to-video with precise creative controls — pose transfer, camera control, motion transfer, and trajectory control — and is trained exclusively on licensed data, which Moonvalley markets as a "commercially safe" model for professional production.
