Marey launched publicly in July 2025. A first-party public API is announced but currently waitlist-only; developers can run Marey today through inference partners fal.ai and ComfyUI. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and General Catalyst.

providers.name: MTN OPS
providers.description: MTN OPS is an American-owned outdoor performance nutrition and lifestyle brand founded in 2014 and headquartered in Fruit Heights, Utah. The company develops, manufactures, and sells energy and nutrition supplements (pre-workout, protein, hydration, creatine, and energy bars) alongside apparel and gear for hunters, tactical professionals, military, and outdoor athletes, running a "Conquer Hunger" program that donates one meal for every order placed. MTN OPS is a direct-to-consumer, internet-first retailer operating on the Shopify platform and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It publishes no bespoke developer API; the only machine-readable surfaces on its domain are the Shopify New Customer Accounts OIDC discovery documents and a Shopify-generated agent-commerce llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Norwest portfolio lead and enriched from the provider's live public surface.

providers.name: mxHero
providers.description: mxHERO Inc. is the pioneer of email-to-cloud content management, based in San Francisco and a long-time Box partner. Its Mail2Cloud platform is a bridge that intelligently captures email and attachments (in-flight or at-rest) over SMTP/S and IMAP/S and routes them, bi-directionally, into cloud content platforms such as Box, Egnyte, Microsoft OneDrive, Google Drive, and Dropbox — without retaining the content itself. Mail2Cloud Advanced adds an AI email-knowledge layer: captured email is deduplicated, metadata-preserved, and stored in an isolated per-tenant vector database that an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes to AI agents for secure email search and knowledge recovery, with a V3 REST API for dataset and S/MIME management.

providers.name: NoScrubs
providers.description: NoScrubs (NoScrubs, Inc., dba NoScrubs Laundry Delivery) is an on-demand wash-and-fold laundry pickup and delivery service operating across US metros including the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Dallas-Fort Worth, Miami, Phoenix, Austin, and Houston. Customers schedule a pickup through the NoScrubs mobile app or website; trained laundry professionals ("Scrubbers") collect laundry from the doorstep within a two-hour window, professionally wash, dry, and fold it using hypoallergenic unscented detergents, and return it the same day in as little as four hours. NoScrubs also offers monthly subscription plans, gift cards, and a wash-and-fold service for businesses. It is a consumer service company with no public developer API; the site publishes an llms.txt for AI agents.

providers.name: OLX
providers.description: OLX is a global online classifieds and marketplace operator, part of OLX Group (owned by Prosus / Naspers), running consumer buy-and-sell marketplaces across 30+ countries under 20+ brands including OLX Poland (olx.pl), OLX Brazil (olx.com.br), OLX Portugal, OLX Bulgaria and OLX Romania, spanning general classifieds, motors/autos, and real estate. OLX Poland publishes a public Partner API (OAuth2) that lets integrators and sellers manage adverts, categories/attributes, and delivery settings programmatically. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and General Catalyst and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Palm
providers.description: Palm is an AI cash flow forecasting platform for corporate treasury and finance teams. It sits above existing Treasury Management Systems (TMS) and ERPs, unifying visibility across cash positions and forecasting liquidity directly from bank and transaction data. Palm learns the timing and size of recurring cash flows from historical transactions to keep a rolling 13-week-and-longer forecast current automatically, and combines ERP data, bank transactions, and 25+ AI models to improve forecast accuracy by over 60%. The product spans AI cash forecasting, what-if scenario modeling, continuous forecast-vs-actual variance analysis, automated daily cash positioning across banks and currencies, surplus-cash investment identification, board-ready treasury reporting, and a "Pulse" anomaly-detection assistant. Palm is a speedinvest portfolio company. It integrates with TMS (Coupa, FIS, ION, Kyriba), banks (Citi, HSBC, J.P. Morgan), investment platforms, data warehouses, and ERPs (SAP, IFS), but does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Petfolk
providers.description: Petfolk is a Charlotte, North Carolina based veterinary care company that operates a network of modern, company-owned pet care centers across the US Southeast and Texas, paired with a consumer mobile app. Founded and led by veterinarian Dr. Audrey Wystrach, Petfolk provides primary and wellness care, sick and urgent care, dentistry, surgery, spay and neuter, vaccinations and diagnostics for dogs and cats, delivered under a "gentle handling" clinical model with seven-day-a-week hours and published, transparent pricing. The Petfolk iOS and Android app lets pet parents book in-person or virtual appointments, message their care team around the clock, request medications and access their pet's medical records; a paid PetfolkCare membership layers on 24/7 veterinary support and per-visit savings. The company raised a $40M Series B in October 2023 led by Movendo Capital, with White Star Capital and Idea Farm Ventures participating. Petfolk is a consumer veterinary services operator, not an API provider: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/GraphQL contract, SDKs or MCP server. It does publish a hand-authored llms.txt at the site root, which is the company's only machine-readable, agent-facing surface.

providers.name: Qualifyze
providers.description: Qualifyze is a supplier risk management and audit platform for the life sciences and pharmaceutical industries. It helps quality, procurement, and compliance teams qualify suppliers faster, run and manage GxP audits globally, and monitor supplier risk continuously. Its Audit Management Platform streamlines audit execution, CAPA management, and real-time visibility with access to a shared library of 5,000+ audit reports, while its Quality Insights Platform layers AI-driven predictive risk monitoring on top of the supply chain. Qualifyze is a delivered SaaS product for enterprise life-sciences customers; it exposes no public developer API, portal, or documentation at this time. The company publishes ISO 9001, ISO 27001, and SOC 2 compliance posture.

providers.name: Sage Care
providers.description: Sage Care (sagecare.ai) builds an AI-native, HIPAA-compliant software platform made exclusively for home care agencies. Its product bundles an AI receptionist, a purpose-built CRM, an AI notetaker and a clinical scribe that automate the intake, referral, scheduling and documentation work that home care operators handle every day. Sage Care integrates with existing home care management systems such as WellSky and AxisCare rather than replacing them, and ships native iOS and desktop applications for caregivers and office staff. The company is backed by General Catalyst and surfaced through its portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Sage Care publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation — it is an application vendor rather than an API provider, so this profile captures company identity and security/compliance posture only.

providers.name: Sazabi
providers.description: Sazabi is an AI-native observability platform that helps engineering teams find and fix production issues faster. Autonomous agents watch application logs (stdout/stderr) to detect anomalies, unfamiliar errors, traffic spikes, and failed deployments without traditional dashboards, then deliver contextual, root-cause alerts into Slack and Microsoft Teams. Engineers investigate in natural language by mentioning the Sazabi agent, and the platform can hand off context to coding agents such as Claude, Cursor, and Codex or open pull requests to remediate. Sazabi instruments 35+ hosting providers with no code changes and exposes a hosted Sazabi MCP server so agents can query logs, inspect issues and projects, and discover Sazabi tools. Founded by Sherwood Callaway; part of the Y Combinator P26 (Spring 2026) batch; backed by an $8M seed round led by J2 Ventures, Village Global, and Y Combinator, with an open beta.

providers.name: SchemaSure
providers.description: Structured data extraction API that converts unstructured text or HTML into JSON guaranteed to validate against a caller-supplied JSON Schema, or returns a typed error at no charge. Access is gated by x402 pay-per-call micropayments (USDC on Base), with no accounts or API keys.

providers.name: Sunset Header
providers.description: The Sunset HTTP header field (RFC 8594) is an informational IETF specification that allows servers to communicate to clients that a URI is likely to become unresponsive at a specified future point in time. Published in May 2019, it provides a standardized mechanism for API deprecation signaling, enabling clients to plan migrations before service retirement. The header value is an HTTP-date timestamp following RFC 7231 syntax. A complementary sunset link relation type allows resources to reference documentation covering the sunset policy, migration guidance, and alternatives. RFC 9745 (Deprecation HTTP Header Field) extends this pattern by providing a two-phase deprecation + sunset lifecycle where Deprecation marks the start of deprecation and Sunset marks the end-of-life. These two headers are widely adopted in REST API governance practices and API lifecycle management tooling.

providers.name: terralayr
providers.description: terralayr is a German energy-flexibility company that develops, owns and operates utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) and runs LAYR, a cloud platform that aggregates heterogeneous storage assets and makes their flexibility available as bookable capacity to utilities, grid operators, power traders, aggregators and asset owners. The platform lets customers buy and sell dispatchable capacity to balance renewable generation against fluctuating grid demand, with storage bookable via API and no complex hardware onboarding. terralayr is backed by Creandum and Earlybird. Its LAYR product API is B2B/private and publishes no public OpenAPI, SDKs or developer documentation; this profile captures the public well-known discovery, security and operational surface.

providers.name: Ultromics
providers.description: Ultromics is a UK-based clinical AI company, spun out of the University of Oxford and backed by GV, whose EchoGo platform applies FDA 510(k)-cleared AI to routine echocardiograms to help clinicians detect heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and cardiac amyloidosis. EchoGo integrates into existing hospital echo workflows and PACS environments, delivering results through clinical systems rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: UMB Bank
providers.description: UMB Bank, National Association is the primary banking subsidiary of UMB Financial Corporation (Nasdaq ticker UMBF), a Kansas City, Missouri financial services holding company. UMB is a commercial bank operating under a national (federal) bank charter supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), with roughly $70 billion in assets following its 2025 acquisition of Heartland Financial and branches across the central United States. It offers personal, commercial, and institutional banking, including asset servicing, corporate trust, and healthcare (HSA) services. UMB runs a partner-facing open-banking and Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) program through its Institutional & Fintech Banking group, exposing REST APIs across risk & compliance, customer onboarding, accounts, information (statements/check images), and cash management. Access is partner-gated through a consultation and contracting process — there is no public self-serve developer portal, no publicly downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification, and no published FDX or CFPB 1033 posture. Consumer-permissioned account data is reached primarily through the Plaid aggregator rather than a first-party public API.

providers.name: Uno Health
providers.description: Uno Health is a New York-based healthcare technology company that helps Medicare members enroll in the government assistance programs they are eligible for — such as SNAP and utility assistance — saving members an average of $4,500 per year. Medicare Advantage health plans partner with Uno's technology-driven member engagement platform to simplify eligibility checks, subsidy enrollment, plan optimization, and benefits matching, increasing Part C revenue, member retention, and star ratings. Members run a 5-minute savings check, upload enrollment documents, and track recurring monthly savings through the Uno Health Member Portal. Backed by Cowboy Ventures and General Catalyst. Uno Health publishes no public developer program; its API (api.unohealth.com, AWS API Gateway) is private and partner-facing.

providers.name: Valyuu
providers.description: Valyuu is an Amsterdam-founded embedded recommerce service provider offering a plug-and-play trade-in platform that businesses integrate to buy back, resell, and recycle used consumer electronics such as smartphones, tablets, and smartwatches across Dutch, German, and English-language markets. Its partner-facing Trade-In API powers embedded trade-in flows covering device catalogs, condition questions, offers, payments, and shipping. Valyuu is a Techstars portfolio company; as of mid-2026 valyuu.com redirects to prioont.com, whose storefront is currently unreachable.

providers.name: Walgreens Boots Alliance
providers.description: Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) is a global pharmacy-led health and wellbeing enterprise operating in more than 25 countries, with pharmacy chains Walgreens in the US and Boots in the UK, pharmaceutical wholesale and distribution through Alliance Healthcare, and specialty pharmacy operations. WBA operates as a Fortune 100 company and global healthcare platform, leveraging data science, AI, and digital health technologies to serve patients, customers, and health systems. While WBA's primary developer APIs are offered through the Walgreens Developer Program, the enterprise also uses healthcare data platforms for population health management, specialty pharmacy integration, and digital health services.

providers.name: Wochit
providers.description: Wochit is an enterprise-grade, cloud-based video creation platform that helps organizations produce professional, on-brand videos at scale. It offers three products: Studio, an AI-powered video creation workspace paired with one of the world's largest licensed content libraries; Frame, a white-label, embeddable video editor that SaaS platforms and marketplaces integrate into their own products; and WAVE, an automated video engine that mass-produces videos from templates and data. Wochit serves media companies, publishers, nonprofits, and enterprises that need repeatable, high-volume video production. Wochit does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Yulife
providers.description: YuLife is a London-founded (2016) technology-driven insurtech and employee benefits platform offering group life insurance, group health insurance, income protection and a gamified wellbeing app. Employees complete everyday wellness activities to earn YuCoin rewards, with access to an EAP, telemedicine and wellbeing apps such as Meditopia. A certified B Corp, YuLife insures 400k+ lives across the UK and US and sells to employers and brokers. It publishes no public developer API or portal; api.yulife.com is the internal app backend (issuer api.uk.yulife.com), and a Vanta Trust Center is at trust.yulife.com.

providers.name: 3P Learning Pty
providers.description: 3P Learning is an educational technology company that builds blended learning software for mathematics and literacy used by schools and families worldwide. Its product family includes Mathletics, Mathseeds, Reading Eggs, Writing Legends, LiteracyPlanet and Brightpath, reaching more than 20 million students across 130+ countries. The programs pair interactive student activities with teacher dashboards, reporting and curriculum-aligned content, and integrate into school systems via single sign-on and rostering standards such as Clever and LTI. 3P Learning is backed by Insight Partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network. This company publishes consumer and school-facing web and mobile products but does not expose a public first-party developer API or documented API surface.

providers.name: 7 Cups
providers.description: 7 Cups (7cups.com) is an on-demand emotional health and online therapy service founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator. It connects people seeking support with a network of trained volunteer listeners for free, anonymous one-on-one chat, and matches members with licensed therapists and social workers for paid online therapy delivered by messaging, audio, or video. The platform also runs peer community forums, group support chat rooms, and self-help "growth path" content. 7 Cups operates across 189 countries in 140 languages with hundreds of thousands of trained listeners. It is a consumer web and mobile product rather than an API-first developer platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and carries no public API at this time.

providers.name: Admiral Group
providers.description: Admiral Group plc is a FTSE 100 personal-lines insurance group headquartered in Cardiff, Wales, and listed on the London Stock Exchange since 2004. Its home market is the United Kingdom, where it is one of the largest motor insurers, trading through the Admiral, Bell, Diamond, elephant.co.uk and Veygo brands and underwriting through EUI Limited and Admiral Insurance Company Limited. Beyond UK motor it writes household, travel and pet insurance (expanded by the 2024 acquisition of RSA's UK home and pet book, including the MORE THAN brand), runs the Admiral Money consumer lending arm, owns the Confused.com price comparison site, and operates internationally as ConTe.it in Italy, L'olivier in France and Admiral Seguros in Spain. Its Admiral Pioneer venture arm builds new businesses including Veygo, Admiral Business and the API-first embedded insurance venture Connect by Admiral, and in 2026 it agreed to acquire the commercial fleet insurtech Flock. Admiral's API posture is honestly recorded here as closed: it is a direct-to-consumer and price-comparison distributor, not a broker-channel or platform carrier. No developer, developers, docs or api subdomain resolves on admiralgroup.co.uk; the corporate site is bot-blocked to automated probes; admiral.com publishes 837 sitemap URLs with no developer, API, partner or integration page; and the only API hosts that resolve (api.admiral.com, api.veygo.com) are undocumented private mobile and web backends that return 502 and 403 respectively. No public self-serve API, no OpenAPI, no Postman collection, no GraphQL surface, no webhook or event catalog, and no ACORD, AL3 or NGDS reference was found. Distribution integration runs through price-comparison-website connections and partner agreements, not through a published developer program.

providers.name: AMI Paris
providers.description: AMI Paris is a French contemporary ready-to-wear fashion house founded in 2011 by Alexandre Mattiussi and headquartered in Paris, known for its "Ami de coeur" heart logo. It sells menswear, womenswear, and accessories direct-to-consumer through amiparis.com, an online store built on Shopify. The store exposes a real agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, ucp.dev) MCP endpoint advertised in /.well-known/ucp, a published /llms.txt and /agents.md with agent instructions, Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth2 authentication, and read-only product/collection JSON endpoints. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of HongShan (Sequoia China) and profiled by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: AMPAworks
providers.description: AMPAworks builds AI-powered smart-shelf inventory management for healthcare and defense supply chains. Its platform pairs computer-vision cameras and rolling kiosks that image inventory to auto-count stock in real time with software that tracks supplies 24/7, automates reordering, and gives teams live visibility to prevent stock-outs. The company reports outcomes such as $15M in cost reduction, 25,000 hours saved on hand counting, and 72% fewer stock-outs across more than 28 healthcare and operational organizations. Backed by 500 Global, AMPAworks operates from offices in Santa Monica CA, Buffalo NY, Hackensack NJ, and Ann Arbor MI.

providers.name: Assured
providers.description: Assured is an AI platform for end-to-end property and casualty (P&C) insurance claims processing, positioning itself as the most widely deployed AI in P&C and processing tens of millions of claims annually. Its modular, interconnected products span the claims lifecycle: FNOL (First Notice of Loss) digital intake, Voice AI telephonic intake, First Contact document gathering, Service Assignment contractor scheduling, omnichannel Messaging, the Emma agentic claim-analysis assistant, the Sidekick telephonic FNOL assistant for adjusters, Fraud Detection, and CAT catastrophe triage. The platform is model-agnostic (working across multiple frontier AI providers), with claims-specific safety controls, explainability, human-in-the-loop workflows, and enterprise-grade monitoring and guardrails. Assured serves personal and commercial auto, homeowners, commercial property, and workers' compensation lines. It is an enterprise, sales-led product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or self-serve documentation. Backed by Costanoa Ventures, DCM Ventures, ICONIQ Capital, Kindred Ventures, and Kleiner Perkins.

providers.name: Benchmark Minerals
providers.description: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence is the world's leading market intelligence and price reporting agency for the lithium-ion battery supply chain and energy transition materials. The company provides mine-to-grid supply chain data, price assessments, forecasts, and databases covering lithium, nickel, cobalt, graphite, batteries, electric vehicles, rare earths, and permanent magnets. Benchmark's proprietary price assessment methodologies are assured to Type 2 IOSCO standards. API access is available to subscribers for programmatic integration of price data, supply chain data, and market intelligence into business systems and analytics platforms.

providers.name: BRICK Schema
providers.description: BRICK is an open-source community-driven ontology standard for standardizing semantic descriptions of physical, logical, and virtual assets in buildings and the relationships between them. Using Semantic Web (RDF/OWL) technology, BRICK v1.4.4 enables interoperability across building management systems, reducing the cost of deploying analytics and energy efficiency initiatives. It supports HVAC, lighting, fire, security, and other building subsystems under a unified extensible vocabulary with SHACL-based validation.

providers.name: Buildforever
providers.description: BuildForever is a consumer software company building products that feel personal, magical, and deeply human. Its first product, Extra (extra.email), is a free AI email app for iPhone, Mac, and Gmail that automatically organizes the inbox into smart categories, summarizes what matters in a daily digest, cleans up subscriptions and unwanted senders, answers natural-language questions about your mail, and drafts replies in your own tone. Founded and led by CEO Naveen Gavini (formerly SVP/CPO at Pinterest), BuildForever is backed by Abstract Ventures, Felicis, and DST Global, with angel investors including Ben Silbermann, Guillermo Rauch, and Paul Buchheit. The company does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its consumer product surface and identity.

providers.name: Cap'n Proto
providers.description: Cap'n Proto is an open-source binary data interchange format and capability-based RPC protocol specification originally created by Kenton Varda. Unlike Protocol Buffers, Cap'n Proto's in-memory representation is identical to its wire format, enabling zero-copy deserialization, incremental reads, random field access, and memory-mapped I/O. The reference implementation is in C++; a broad ecosystem of community-maintained bindings covers C#, Erlang, Go, Haskell, JavaScript/Node, OCaml, Python, Rust, C, D, Java, Lua, Nim, Ruby, and Scala.

providers.name: CMA CGM
providers.description: CMA CGM is a Marseille-headquartered French container shipping, logistics, and port operator and the third-largest ocean carrier in the world. Founded in 1978 by Jacques Saadé and led today by Chairman & CEO Rodolphe Saadé, the CMA CGM Group operates a fleet of 593 vessels with 4.5 million TEU of capacity calling 420 ports across 160 countries on 257 maritime services. The group includes maritime brands ANL, APL, CNC Line, Containerships, Comanav, and Mercosul Line; terminal operator CMA Terminals and Terminal Link; the CEVA Logistics contract logistics and freight forwarding business (acquired 2019); CMA CGM Air Cargo; Brittany Ferries and La Méridionale passenger ferries; and the CMA Média portfolio (La Provence, La Tribune, BFM-RMC, Brut). Through api-portal.cma-cgm.com the group exposes a DCSA-aligned REST API surface — Track and Trace v1 (DCSA v2.2.0), Schedules, Booking Request, Quotation, and Invoice — plus a parallel EDI catalog (EDIFACT IFTSAI, IFTMBF, IFTSTA, INVOIC) and group-level digital initiatives including ZEBOX (startup accelerator), Traxens-based IoT smart containers, and a strategic AI partnership with Mistral.

providers.name: CommitChange
providers.description: CommitChange is an all-in-one nonprofit fundraising platform providing online donation processing, recurring giving, embeddable donation widgets, crowdfunding and peer-to-peer fundraising campaigns, professional event pages with ticketing, donor management, and a real-time analytics dashboard. Founded in 2012 and acquired by Software for Good (Minneapolis, MN) in 2022, the platform charges no monthly fees or long-term contracts, taking 5% + $0.30 per transaction with payments processed securely via Stripe. CommitChange is built on the open-source Houdini Project (AGPL) and has helped 1,000+ nonprofits raise $82M+ across 4,700+ campaigns and 2,900+ events.

providers.name: creativeLIVE
providers.description: creativeLIVE (CreativeLive) is an online learning platform offering more than 2,300 on-demand courses and live interactive classes taught by working professionals across photography, video and filmmaking, graphic and web design, business and entrepreneurship, arts and crafts, audio and music production, and AI and technology. Learners access practical, skill-based instruction through a subscription, with certificates of completion available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network; creativeLIVE exposes no public developer API, but does publish a machine-readable llms.txt course index for AI agents.

providers.name: Dework
providers.description: Dework is a Web3-native task-management and bounty platform for DAOs and decentralized teams. Organizations create bounties, projects, and task boards; contributors build an on-chain reputation profile, claim or apply to tasks, and get paid in the DAO's own token or stablecoins from supported wallets (Gnosis/Safe, MetaMask, Phantom, WalletConnect). Dework offers token- and Discord-role gating, two-way Discord and GitHub sync, Notion and Coordinape integrations, batch payments, reputation staking, roadmaps, and leaderboards. It aggregates bounties and grants from hundreds of DAOs. The app is backed by an Apollo GraphQL API at api.dework.xyz; product documentation lives on GitBook. Backed by Paradigm.

providers.name: DomScan
providers.description: Domain intelligence API for domain availability, DNS, WHOIS/RDAP, valuation, security checks, email posture, social handle checks, and monitoring workflows. Offers REST API, machine-readable contracts, a hosted MCP server, and llms.txt.

providers.name: Easol
providers.description: Easol is an experience commerce platform for creators of festivals, adventure and travel operators, entertainment venues, and multi-day events. Its all-in-one system combines a branded website builder, booking and ticketing, packages and upsells, global payments and on-site POS, marketing and CRM, operations analytics, AI support agents, and creator capital/funding, letting experience businesses move beyond rigid legacy ticketing systems and sell and scale on their own platform. Plans range from Easol Stride (from $250/month) to a custom-priced Easol Pro tier. Easol does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile captures its public commercial, support, security, and status surfaces, and is backed by Tiger Global.

providers.name: Ediphi
providers.description: Ediphi is a cloud-native preconstruction platform for commercial construction contractors that unifies estimating, cost modeling, general conditions and general requirements (GCs & GRs) tracking, bid-package contracting, and a shared cloud unit-price catalog in one real-time collaborative workspace. Founded by Dustin DeVan (founder of BuildingConnected, acquired by Autodesk), it is used by ENR Top 400 general contractors including Hensel Phelps, Suffolk Construction, and DPR Construction. Its "Last Mile" module provides API-driven automation for Excel integration and reporting. Ediphi runs a private application API at api.ediphi.com; as of this profile there is no public developer portal or published API specification.

providers.name: Graffer
providers.description: Graffer, Inc. (株式会社グラファー) is a Tokyo-based GovTech and generative-AI company founded in 2017 whose mission is to change behavior and society through the power of products. It operates two pillars: the Graffer Platform, a suite of digital-government services for municipalities and national agencies (Smart Application for online applications, Procedure Guide, Window Reservation, and Graffer Call AI voice guidance), adopted by 179+ Japanese municipalities including Fukuoka, Sapporo, Kyoto, and Oita; and Graffer AI Solution, a generative-AI adoption offering for enterprises (consulting, training, and the Graffer AI Studio product). Graffer also runs the citizen-facing お悩みハンドブック benefits-discovery service and the Govtech Trends media. In 2023 it entered a capital and business alliance with Change Holdings. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Hebrew University of Jerusalem
providers.description: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem (HUJI) is Israel's leading research university, ranked #272 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates multiple campuses in Jerusalem, Rehovot, and Eilat across the humanities, sciences, medicine, and law. HUJI does not publish a dedicated public developer portal or documented open API program. Its developer-relevant surface is limited to standards-based academic infrastructure: an Ex Libris Primo/Alma library discovery system (whose APIs require institution-issued keys), the OpenScholar profile/CMS platform, Shibboleth/SAML single sign-on (internal/gated), and a number of research-lab open-source GitHub organizations. No public, self-service API endpoints were confirmed.

providers.name: Indian Institute of Technology Madras
providers.description: Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) is a public technical and research university in Chennai, India, ranked #227 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates an institutional website (iitm.ac.in), a central library with electronic databases, a large online BS degree program in Data Science and Applications, and SSO/OAuth2-based identity endpoints. As of this review IIT Madras does not publish a public, documented developer portal or open API program. Its official GitHub organization exists but currently exposes no public repositories. The properties cataloged below reflect only publicly confirmed institutional web properties and identity endpoints, not documented third-party APIs.

providers.name: Keatext
providers.description: Keatext is a Montreal-based AI text analytics platform that unifies customer feedback from surveys, online reviews, and support tickets into a single dashboard and produces AI-generated reports identifying themes, sentiment, satisfaction drivers, and blind spots. It is purpose-built for customer experience (CX) teams, surfacing prioritized, actionable recommendations to improve CSAT and reduce churn. Keatext integrates natively with feedback and service platforms including SurveyMonkey, Zendesk, QuestionPro, Alchemer, ServiceNow, Qualtrics, Intercom, Salesforce, and Yotpo, and connects to 400+ additional systems through the Tray.io integration platform. Customers include Intuit, Lenovo, Hilton, and COOLA. The company does not publish a public developer REST API or OpenAPI; custom integration is handled via Tray.io and direct partner engagement. Added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: KiwiCo
providers.description: KiwiCo, Inc. is a direct-to-consumer education company headquartered in Mountain View, California, founded in 2011 by Sandra Oh Lin. KiwiCo designs and ships hands-on STEAM (science, technology, engineering, art and math) project kits — branded as crates — on a monthly subscription, with distinct lines aimed at every age from infants through teens and adults, alongside single-purchase kits sold through its online store. A KiwiCo Education division supplies the same project kits and NGSS-aligned lesson guides to schools, homeschools, after-school programs and camps. KiwiCo operates as a consumer e-commerce and subscription business and publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDK, CLI or webhook surface, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents on any of its hosts. This profile therefore captures verified company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: MarqVision
providers.description: MarqVision is a brand-integrity and intellectual-property protection platform (Y Combinator S21) that uses AI-powered image recognition and semantic analysis to detect and remove counterfeits, unauthorized sellers, brand impersonation and pirated content across more than 1,500 online marketplaces, e-commerce sites, social platforms and app stores. The product line spans MarqCommerce (marketplace enforcement), MarqContents (content and piracy protection), MarqFolio (trademark portfolio management), MarqLaw (legal services) and a Brand Intelligence Agent for natural-language brand-threat analytics. MarqVision operates a customer-facing "MarqAI API" — named as a component on its own public status page and described in its engineering blog as the "Action-Enabled API" behind the Marq AI Slack app — but publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract; programmatic access is arranged through a customer success manager or the demo waitlist.

providers.name: Meitu
providers.description: Meitu (美图) is a Chinese visual-technology company best known for its photo- and video-editing apps (Meitu, BeautyCam, Meitu Xiuxiu). It operates the Meitu AI Open Platform, which exposes 100+ image and video AI capabilities as a Web API (OpenAPI) plus native/mobile SDKs — image generation and editing, portrait beautification, face and body analysis, cutout and segmentation, virtual try-on, and image/text-to-video. Access uses a per-application access key and secret key signature; an official Node.js CLI (meitu-cli) wraps the OpenAPI. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Moritz
providers.description: Moritz is an AI-native law firm delivering commercial, corporate, and employment legal work with same-day turnaround at transparent flat-rate pricing. Founded in 2025 by Pamir Ehsas (former outside counsel to OpenAI and Google) and Stefan Mandaric (ex-Fulbright scholar at MIT), the firm uses AI to complete roughly 80% of the work (intake and first draft) with 50+ contracted co-counsel lawyers finalizing every matter. Moritz operates across the EU, US, and Australia and reports having supported more than 100 companies in closing agreements representing over $2B in aggregate contract value. It is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company that raised a $9M seed round backed by 20VC, the Urban Innovation Fund, and 20 unicorn founders. Moritz is a legal-services company; it does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Northspyre
providers.description: Northspyre is a real estate development management platform that gives owners, developers, and project teams an end-to-end system for managing deals, projects, and portfolios across the full development lifecycle — acquisition, early planning, pre-development, construction, and stabilization. It unifies siloed project data and automates routine work with tools for financial modeling and deal pipeline management, budget and cost control, vendor procurement and management, forecasting, portfolio analytics, and investor and lender reporting. Northspyre is delivered as a hosted SaaS application and is SOC 2 Type II certified. It exposes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity, compliance posture, and domain security.

providers.name: NumPy
providers.description: The fundamental package for scientific computing with Python. NumPy provides multi-dimensional array objects, various derived objects, and an assortment of routines for fast operations on arrays, including mathematical, logical, shape manipulation, sorting, selecting, I/O, FFT, and random number generation.

providers.name: OXIO
providers.description: OXIO is a Telecom-as-a-Service (TaaS) platform that lets brands, enterprises, and fintechs launch and operate their own branded mobile networks (MVNOs) through a single API, without building traditional telecom infrastructure. Its API-first platform unifies multiple carriers behind one integration and layers on no-code service creation (BrandVNO), AI-driven subscriber and network intelligence (BrandIQ), and multi-carrier connectivity (OXIO Network). Developers use OXIO's RESTful APIs and sandbox for programmatic line and subscription management, payments, fraud detection, and CRM/ERP synchronization. OXIO was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital (its GitHub org carries Stellar blockchain SDK forks) and enriched from its public web surface; the full developer documentation is gated behind authorized-customer access.

providers.name: Pensando *
providers.description: AMD Pensando (formerly Pensando Systems, acquired by AMD in 2022) builds programmable Distributed Services Cards (DPUs) and the Policy and Services Manager (PSM) control plane that operates them across cloud, distributed services switch, and enterprise deployments. PSM exposes a REST API — surfaced through auto-generated, first-party Python bindings on PyPI (pensando-cloud, pensando-dss, pensando-ent) and a Terraform provider — for managing clusters, networks, security policy, and services on Pensando infrastructure. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: People.ai
providers.description: People.ai is an AI-powered revenue intelligence platform for enterprise sales teams. It automatically captures sales activity and contact data from email, calendar, and meetings, matches it into CRM systems like Salesforce and Microsoft Dynamics 365, and delivers AI-driven forecasting, opportunity management, account execution, and engagement forensics to improve pipeline visibility and drive predictable revenue growth. People.ai integrates with Salesforce, Microsoft, Oracle, Slack, Zoom, Webex, 6sense, and ZoomInfo. It is delivered as an enterprise SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API; its trust and security posture is documented with SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, GDPR, and CSA STAR. As of 2026 People.ai has rebranded to Backstory (www.people.ai now 301-redirects to www.backstory.ai); the product login remains at app.people.ai.

providers.name: Pindrop Security
providers.description: Pindrop is an Atlanta-based voice security and identity company founded in 2011 by Georgia Tech researchers. Its "Real Human + Right Human" platform detects deepfakes, prevents fraud, and authenticates callers across voice, video, and digital channels for contact centers and virtual meetings. Core products are Pindrop Pulse (deepfake and synthetic-voice detection), Pindrop Protect (near real-time fraud risk assessment), and Pindrop Passport (multifactor voice, device, and behavioral authentication, including VeriCall technology). Pindrop holds 300+ patents and integrates with contact-center and meeting platforms such as Amazon Connect, Genesys, Five9, NICE, Cisco Webex, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams. The company is an enterprise, sales-led vendor and does not publish a self-serve public developer portal or open API.

providers.name: Primodium Inc.
providers.description: Primodium Inc. (primodiumxyz) is a developer-focused studio building fully on-chain applications and games on Ethereum and Solana. It ships two on-chain games — Primodium, a space-based factory-building game, and Primodium: Empires, a turn-based prediction-market game — both built with MUD and Phaser, alongside a suite of open-source developer libraries and infrastructure: Reactive Tables (a strictly-typed reactive table library for MUD apps), a Solana DEX Indexer Stack exposing a GraphQL API over Hasura/Timescale, a tRPC transaction-sponsoring DEX server, an off-chain MUD indexer, and gasless-transaction relayers. All tooling is published open-source under the MIT license via the primodiumxyz GitHub organization and the @primodiumxyz npm scope.

providers.name: Queen Mary University of London
providers.description: Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) is a public research university in London, United Kingdom, and a member of the Russell Group, ranked #120 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-accessible footprint is research- and library-oriented rather than a formal developer program: Queen Mary Research Online (QMRO) is an open-access DSpace institutional repository that exposes a standards-based OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting interface, and the university maintains a public GitHub organization (QMUL) for code released by its staff. QMUL does not publish a central, branded developer portal with signup-gated REST APIs; core student, timetable, and library platforms (QMplus/Moodle, MyQMUL, library discovery) sit behind institutional authentication.

providers.name: Queensland University of Technology
providers.description: Queensland University of Technology (QUT) is a public research university based in Brisbane, Australia, ranked #213 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. QUT serves around 50,000 students with an applied emphasis in teaching and research. Its public, machine-accessible developer footprint is modest and centered on open research infrastructure: the QUT ePrints institutional repository exposes a live OAI-PMH metadata harvesting interface, and QUT maintains several active research-group GitHub organizations (eResearch, Centre for Robotics, Aerospace Systems, Digital Observatory). Most other institutional systems (Library Search built on Ex Libris Primo VE / Alma, the Timetable Planner, the QUT mobile app backend, and the SSO identity layer) are internal or gated and do not publish open developer documentation.

providers.name: Spline
providers.description: Spline is a real-time collaborative 3D design tool with AI-driven object generation, web embedding, and animation. Spline does NOT publish a REST API for 3D scene generation as of May 2026; instead it exposes Code APIs (Web, SwiftUI, Kotlin) for embedding scenes, plus a real-time API for variables/data and webhooks for event-driven integrations.

providers.name: Sportwey
providers.description: Sportwey is a Mexican SaaS platform that digitizes and automates the operations of sports organizations across multiple segments — tournaments and leagues, training academies, and sports facilities. It provides team management, scheduling, results and statistics, attendance and membership tracking, payments, class scheduling, court and field reservations, and referee coordination. The company reports more than 10,000 organizers and 2.3 million players using the platform, delivered through dedicated player and referee apps and a manager back office. Sportwey is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: StorSimple
providers.description: StorSimple was a Santa Clara, California hybrid cloud storage company founded in 2009 by Ursheet Parikh and Guru Pangal. Its appliances combined primary storage, tiered cloud archiving, deduplication, compression, and encryption behind iSCSI/SMB interfaces, backed by $31.5M from Index Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Ignition Partners, and Mayfield Fund. Microsoft acquired StorSimple in November 2012 and folded it into Azure as Azure StorSimple (8000 series physical and virtual arrays, plus the StorSimple Data Manager). The product is managed through Azure Resource Manager under the Microsoft.StorSimple resource provider and its REST API. Azure StorSimple reached end-of-life in December 2022 and is out of support; Microsoft directs customers to Azure File Sync and Azure Files.

providers.name: Tebi
providers.description: Tebi is a hospitality management platform that unifies point-of-sale, payments, and back-office operations for restaurants, bars, cafes, bakeries, quick-service venues, and events. The system connects front-of-house service to back-office administration in a single product spanning Point of Sale, Kitchen Display System, Reservations, integrated card Payments (with invoicing and split-bill), QR ordering, inventory management, CRM, recipe management, and AI-driven insights. Tebi is priced on a revenue-based subscription (the first EUR 10k of monthly revenue is free, each additional EUR 10k costs EUR 20/month) with no long-term contracts, and it bundles its own payment processing with transparent per-transaction fees. The company is backed by Index Ventures. Tebi does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its production identity, help center, changelog, status page, and security posture as surfaced by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Tianjin University
providers.description: Tianjin University (TJU) is a national public research university in Tianjin, China, founded in 1895 as Peiyang University and recognized as the oldest modern university in China. It is ranked #269 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. TJU operates the usual institutional web properties (official site, library OPAC, faculty and international-cooperation portals) but does not publish a public developer portal or documented, openly accessible API. No public API documentation, base URLs, or sign-up flows could be verified at the time of cataloging; the entries below reflect only confirmed public web properties, not documented APIs.

providers.name: Traba
providers.description: Traba is a New York City-based staffing marketplace and AI operating layer for the industrial supply chain, founded in 2021 and backed by Founders Fund. Traba connects vetted, high-reliability light-industrial workers with production plants, warehouses, and distribution centers, and pairs that staffing marketplace with Neo, an AI intelligence layer that unifies live operational data across WMS, ERP, HRIS, TMS, and payroll systems, surfaces root causes, and automates approved supply chain workflows. Traba publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Tynker
providers.description: Tynker is a coding platform for kids and teens ages 5-18 that makes it fun to learn programming through game-based, interactive courses, with students starting in visual block-based coding and progressing to real-world languages like Python and JavaScript. The platform powers the creativity of over 100 million students and serves thousands of schools and educators worldwide, spanning home plans for parents, K-12 school curriculum, Hour of Code activities, and Minecraft modding. Tynker is a 500 Global and Felicis portfolio company, now part of CodeHS, and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Ultimagenomics
providers.description: Ultima Genomics develops high-throughput, low-cost DNA sequencing platforms built on a novel semiconductor-inspired architecture, aimed at driving the cost of a genome dramatically down to unlock population-scale genomics. Its systems support germline and somatic (oncology/MRD) sequencing, single-cell and spatial workflows, methylation/epigenomics, and proteomics, and integrate with an open ecosystem of third-party library-prep providers (10x Genomics, Olink). Rather than a public REST API, Ultima exposes its developer surface as open-source bioinformatics tooling and analysis pipelines: a large GitHub organization (Ultimagen) of UG-adapted variant callers and genomics utilities (GATK, Picard, STAR forks, ugbio-utils) and AWS HealthOmics WDL workflows for running cost-effective secondary analysis in the cloud.

providers.name: WEC Energy Group
providers.description: WEC Energy Group (NYSE: WEC) is one of the nation's premier energy companies, serving 4.4 million customers across Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, and Minnesota with electricity and natural gas service. The company operates through regional utilities including We Energies, Wisconsin Public Service, Peoples Gas, North Shore Gas, Minnesota Energy Resources, Michigan Gas Utilities, and Upper Michigan Energy Resources. WEC Energy Group offers customer-facing digital services including account management portals, mobile apps, and Green Button energy usage data access.

providers.name: Wuhan University
providers.description: Wuhan University (WHU), founded in 1893 and located in Wuhan, Hubei, China, is one of China's oldest and most prestigious comprehensive research universities, ranked #194 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates under the Ministry of Education of China and is recognized for surveying and remote sensing, geoinformatics, and the sciences. WHU does not publish a centralized, publicly documented developer or API portal; its official web presence (en.whu.edu.cn) is informational only. Discoverable developer activity is concentrated in research-group GitHub organizations rather than institutional API products. No public, documented institutional API endpoints could be confirmed at the time of review.

providers.name: Xh
providers.description: xh is a friendly and fast command-line HTTP client written in Rust, designed as a modern, high-performance alternative to HTTPie. It reimplements HTTPie's request-item syntax and design with improved startup speed, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support, and availability as a single statically-linked binary. xh supports JSON and form data serialization, session management, authentication (basic, bearer, digest), SSL/TLS customization, multipart uploads, proxy configuration, and built-in curl command translation. Installable via Homebrew, Cargo, apt, pacman, and other package managers.

providers.name: Accord
providers.description: A UK-based financial services company operating within the Allianz group, providing insurance and financial products to retail and business customers across the United Kingdom.

providers.name: Alberta
providers.description: Alberta is a open data portal open-data portal for Canada running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 33,436 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: AmeriGEOSS Community Platform
providers.description: AmeriGEOSS Community Platform is a organization open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 645,296 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Analyze Boston
providers.description: Analyze Boston is a municipal government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 231 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Aporia
providers.description: Aporia was an AI guardrails and observability platform for production LLM and ML applications, known for low-latency guardrails covering hallucination, prompt injection, PII, toxicity, off-topic responses, and custom policies, alongside full ML monitoring for drift and data quality. Coralogix acquired Aporia in late 2024 and the Aporia guardrails technology is now offered as part of the Coralogix AI Observability and AI Guardrails product line, with the standalone Aporia.com experience consolidated into Coralogix's portfolio.

providers.name: Aragón Open Data
providers.description: Aragón Open Data is a open data portal open-data portal for Spain running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 2,429 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Avoindata.fi
providers.description: Avoindata.fi is a national government open-data portal for Finland running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 2,521 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Barnet Open Data

providers.name: BBDO Worldwide
providers.description: BBDO Worldwide is a global advertising agency network founded in 1928 and headquartered in New York City. It is the largest of the creative-agency networks owned by Omnicom Group, with roughly 15,000 employees across approximately 289 offices in 81 countries (per Wikipedia, citing company data). The agency's positioning is "Do Big Things," and its public work is campaign-led — Pepsi, Budweiser, McDonald's, M&M's, Snickers, Visa, AT&T Business, Volkswagen, Skoda, Whiskas, and many more. BBDO has been named Cannes Lions Network of the Year multiple times since 2007 and Network of the Decade in 2020. BBDO does not publish a developer portal, public REST APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, status page, or pricing — its product is creative work delivered to brand clients, not software offered to developers. The one machine-readable surface bbdo.com serves is the WordPress REST API behind the site itself: /wp-json/ answers anonymously with a 200-route discovery document, and the agency's own `work` and `news` custom post types are readable without credentials — 46 campaign case studies and 60 press items with draft-04 JSON Schemas available from each collection's OPTIONS response. That is a CMS byproduct, not a product BBDO designed, documents, prices, or supports. This repository indexes the public properties (homepage, network site, news, parent company, GitHub org, and notable agency network members), captures what the WordPress API actually serves, and links BBDO to its parent Omnicom and sibling networks (DDB Worldwide, TBWA Worldwide).

providers.name: Ebix
providers.description: Ebix is a United States insurance software and exchange company headquartered in Johns Creek, Georgia, operating as market infrastructure between carriers, MGAs, brokers and agencies rather than as a carrier itself. Its portfolio spans property and casualty agency management (EbixASP), P&C policy administration and broker systems (EbixEvolution, PlacingHub, Sunrise Exchange, iClose), life insurance and annuity distribution connectivity (EbixExchange), health insurance and employee benefits administration, health content, risk and compliance (RiskEnvision, WCExchange), and — through the EbixCash arm — travel, payments and forex services. Its core P&C plumbing is ACORD-native rather than API-native: TEAM-UP moves policy, claims and direct-bill commission download to agency management systems as ACORD-standard AL3 files, its Translation Services practice converts carrier-proprietary formats into ACORD AL3 and ACORD XML using Java/XML/XSLT, EbixASP maintains a continuously updated ACORD forms library with bi-directional exchange against ACORD applications, and the EbixASP Real-Time Interface synchronizes carrier credentials and service transactions with IVANS. Ebix markets API-driven quote-to-bind workflows and, since October 2025, a plug-and-play connector platform built with 1SilverBullet that exposes quoting, eApp, enrollment, underwriting checks, payments and policy servicing as modular APIs with "a standardized connector fabric with pre-built mappings and a developer portal" — but no public self-serve developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification could be confirmed as of 2026-07-25. Every probed developer path on ebix.com (/developers, /api, /developer, /partners, /integrations) returns the site's single-page-app homepage shell rather than a developer surface; developer.ebix.com and docs.ebix.com do not resolve; api.ebix.com answers with a JSON 404 and no documented routes; and the live EbixCash API Hub at api.ebixcash.com serves an OpenAPI document that returns HTTP 401 "Missing Authorization header". The one agent-facing discovery document Ebix does publish is a real llms.txt at www.ebix.com/llms.txt, which indexes the solution, service and corporate pages but names no API, portal or specification; every /.well-known/ probe across www.ebix.com, api.ebix.com, api.ebixcash.com and ebixasp.com missed, no first-party SDK exists in any public package registry, and no trust center, security.txt or vulnerability-disclosure program was found. Ebix's integration surface is therefore customer- and partner-gated, sold and documented under contract, which is the norm for United States insurance infrastructure where no federal regulator and no open-insurance mandate exists. Ebix filed Chapter 11 in December 2023, sold its North American life and annuity assets to Zinnia, and exited bankruptcy on 30 August 2024 consolidated with Eraaya Lifespaces.

providers.description: The US Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board (CSB) is an independent federal agency responsible for investigating chemical accidents and hazards across the United States. The board conducts thorough investigations into incidents involving the release of hazardous chemicals, explosions, fires, and other accidents that pose a threat to public safety and the environment. The CSB publishes investigation reports, safety recommendations, and incident data, and maintains a public database of completed investigations and safety recommendations. While no formal public API is available, the CSB makes incident data available through its website and periodic compiled reports under its Accidental Release Reporting Rule transparency initiative.

providers.name: US Small Business Administration Open Data
providers.description: US Small Business Administration Open Data is a federal government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 41 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Verax
providers.description: Verax AI is an enterprise AI security platform that gives organizations real-time visibility and control over how employees and agents use generative AI. Its flagship product, Verax Protect, discovers shadow AI usage across every LLM tool, enforces identity- and role-aware access policies, and applies content-aware data-loss prevention to stop sensitive data from leaking into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot and other AI services. Verax Control Center adds monitoring and governance for LLM-based products running in production. Verax deploys via an endpoint agent and integrates with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID and Google Workspace for identity. Founded in 2023 (Dallas, Tel Aviv, London) and backed by TQ Ventures, Seedcamp and others.

providers.name: Virginia Open Data
providers.description: Virginia Open Data is a state government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 33,247 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Western Australia Data Catalogue
providers.description: Western Australia Data Catalogue is a state government open-data portal for Australia running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 2,909 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Wonderschool
providers.description: Wonderschool is a child care platform that connects families with licensed care and equips providers with software and services to start, operate, and grow their child care programs. It also serves government agencies with licensing, subsidy management, enrollment coordination, and statewide substitute-teacher pools, and offers employers child care benefit programs. Backed by a16z and Uncork Capital, Wonderschool operates as a B2B/B2G SaaS business; it publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center (SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF) but no public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Wuzzuf
providers.description: Wuzzuf is Egypt's leading online recruitment platform, operated by Cairo-based BasharSoft and backed by investors including 500 Global. It connects millions of job seekers with tens of thousands of employers across Egypt and the Middle East, offering job search, applicant tracking, employer branding pages, and recruitment products for companies. Wuzzuf does not currently publish a public developer API, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Yampa
providers.description: Yampa is a Paris-based B2B platform for deploying and operating fleets of autonomous AI agents that handle customer service end-to-end across voice, chat, email, ticketing, and messaging channels. Its Y.core orchestration platform provides a visual workflow builder, guardrails, a knowledge layer, multichannel orchestration, QA and auditing tools, and observability, with connectors to CRMs, helpdesks, and telephony systems (Salesforce, Zendesk, Intercom, Twilio, Genesys, and others). Founded in 2024 by Marin Huet, Baptiste Saintot, and Patrice Mazoyer, Yampa raised a ~EUR 3M seed led by Partech and emphasizes sovereign EU-hosted infrastructure with GDPR and SOC 2 aligned security. Developer documentation at docs.yampa.ai is gated behind an access code; the public status page lists an API component alongside chat, email, calls, and console services.

providers.name: Yokohama City Open Data
providers.description: Yokohama City Open Data is a municipal government open-data portal for Japan running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 657 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Zinier
providers.description: Zinier is a no-code field service management platform that helps enterprises schedule and manage their workforce, assets, and customers, powered by generative AI. Its office and field experiences pair ready-to-use productivity tools with a no-code Task Builder for building custom workflows, and an Integration Marketplace advertising 1,000+ out-of-the-box connections to ERP, CRM, and EAM systems such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, Salesforce, Zendesk, ServiceNow, IBM, and Infor. Zinier targets asset-intensive field-service operations, from scheduling and dispatch through mobile task execution and customer communication. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and ICONIQ Capital. No public developer API, API reference, or OpenAPI surface is published today — integration is delivered through the marketplace and end-user product documentation.

providers.name: Aluna
providers.description: Aluna is a digital respiratory health company behind an FDA-cleared, portable Bluetooth spirometer and companion mobile app that let people with asthma, COPD, and cystic fibrosis measure lung function (FEV1) at home and share the results with their care teams. The platform pairs a hospital-grade sensor with a gamified app and machine-learning analytics to encourage proper technique, track symptoms, triggers, and medications, and surface trends that help clinicians intervene before an exacerbation. Founded by Charvi Shetty and Inderjit Jutla out of UC Berkeley's bioengineering program, Aluna raised a $15.3M Series B and is a Matrix Partners portfolio company; the product is now operated under Huma Therapeutics. Aluna publishes consumer, clinical-provider, and clinical-trial surfaces but no public developer API.

providers.name: AMMP
providers.description: AMMP (AMMP OS) is a distributed energy monitoring and operations platform for operators of commercial and industrial (C&I) solar and battery-storage portfolios. It unifies visibility across multi-vendor fleets, pulling data directly from more than 30 manufacturer cloud platforms and its own AMMP Edge data logger, and layers on monitoring, alerting, stakeholder reporting, commercial (SLA/cost) tracking, and customizable dashboards. AMMP OS monitors over 10,000 sites across 35+ countries and emphasizes vendor independence and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified security. Surfaced as a portfolio company of point-nine and enriched by the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Apero
providers.description: Apero Health is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed healthcare technology company that provides an integrated practice-management and revenue-cycle-management (RCM) platform for medical practices. Its cloud software unifies scheduling, clinical visit notes, insurance eligibility verification and claims billing, patient billing and payments, e-prescriptions, and financial reporting, and claims to reduce billing time by up to 80% while helping practices scale operations. Apero exposes a fully-featured REST API, webhooks, and CSV import that connect healthcare and finance workflows, and integrates with payers (Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield) and platforms including Stripe, QuickBooks Online, Google, and Snowflake.

providers.name: Arrived
providers.description: Arrived is a real estate investment platform that lets individuals buy, own, and sell fractional shares of income-producing residential properties without the work of being a landlord. Investors browse curated single-family rentals, vacation rentals, funds, and real-estate debt offerings, invest in minutes, and receive passive rental income through dividend distributions plus potential appreciation while Arrived handles acquisition and property management. The company reports roughly 981K registered investors, $445M invested, and $95M distributed. Arrived is a consumer-facing investing product with a web and mobile app; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: beva
providers.description: beva (贝瓦网), operated by ProKids Technology Corp / 芝兰玉树（北京）科技股份有限公司, is a Chinese IP-and-technology driven family education and entertainment company. Its flagship original IP is the little beaver "Beva" (贝瓦) and the "Beva Children's Songs" (贝瓦儿歌) brand, spanning children's music, animation, literature and interactive entertainment, distributed across web, mobile, OTT, IPTV and television channels. Through its ProKids Copyright Content Open Platform (open.beva.com) beva offers online-application and offline content-access APIs that let third-party mobile apps and smart hardware — story machines, smart speakers and kids' robots such as MiTu, Rokid and the Doraemon story machine — embed licensed children's audio and video content. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Bippit
providers.description: Bippit is a UK-based financial wellbeing platform that gives every employee access to personal, qualified financial coaching alongside AI-powered guidance available 24/7, planning and budgeting tools, payroll savings, and educational content and webinars. Sold to employers as a workplace benefit, it also provides organisations with aggregate financial-wellbeing insights and analytics. Bippit is FCA-regulated (No. 845814), ICO-registered (No. ZA533579), ISO 27001:2022 certified, and GDPR / UK DPA 2018 compliant, with data stored in the EEA. Backed by Techstars. Bippit publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and compliance surface.

providers.name: Braid Social
providers.description: Braid Social, Inc. is a venture-backed startup that has run two products under the Braid name. It launched as a creator-economy, direct-to-fan engagement platform — founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro — letting creators build customizable landing pages that consolidated their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts, and commerce links), collect fan phone numbers, and reach followers directly through SMS, push notifications, and mailing lists, with link tracking and cross-platform analytics. It raised a $6.8M seed round in August 2023 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Initialized Capital. The original domain braid.ai is now a domain-for-sale listing at atom.com and braid.social no longer resolves. The same legal entity now ships "Braid Teams" at trybraid.io (mirrored at braidsocial.com) — an AI-powered employee-engagement copilot that runs inside Slack, automating icebreakers, games, polls, events, reminders, leaderboards, and engagement reporting for distributed teams, on a free / $5-per-user Premium / contact-us Enterprise plan. Braid Teams is a Slack-app product with no public developer program: no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI, no SDKs, and no GitHub organization. The only machine surface is the private application backend at core.trybraid.io, which answers {"status":"ok"} at its root and 404s every spec, docs and /.well-known/ path. The homepage states the product is "Currently not accepting new users" and the Slack install endpoint returns HTTP 500.

providers.name: Built Robotics
providers.description: Built Robotics is a San Francisco robotics company, founded in 2016 by Noah Ready-Campbell and Andrew Liang, that turns conventional heavy construction equipment into AI-powered autonomous robots. Its Exosystem retrofit kit converts excavators and other earthmoving machines into self-operating robots for trenching, foundation excavation and pad grading, while the RPD 35 and RPS 25 autonomous pile drivers install foundations for utility-scale solar farms. Machines are supervised from the Everest command center, and field deployment is run through its Built Solar Technologies (built.solar) division. The company reports $114M raised and 25+ commercial deployments across the United States and Australia. Built Robotics publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its only public developer artifact is the open-source rsplan Reeds-Shepp path-planning library on PyPI and GitHub.

providers.name: CloudEagle.ai
providers.description: CloudEagle.ai is an AI-powered SaaS management and procurement platform that helps IT, security, finance, and procurement teams discover, govern, optimize, and renew their SaaS and AI application portfolio. The platform offers application discovery via 500+ direct integrations with SSO, HRIS, finance, and CASB systems; license harvesting and spend optimization; identity and access governance with automated access reviews; onboarding/offboarding automation; SaaS procurement and renewal orchestration; and shadow IT/shadow AI detection. CloudEagle exposes an enterprise API to programmatically access these capabilities for partners and customers; specific endpoint paths and authentication details are provided to customers via the in-product developer settings rather than a public docs site.

providers.name: Coachup
providers.description: CoachUp is the nation's leading private sports coaching marketplace, founded in 2012 in Boston by Jordan Fliegel, Arian Radmand, and Gabe Durazo. It connects athletes of all levels — and the parents of young athletes — with vetted, background-checked private and small-group coaches across basketball, soccer, football, baseball, running and track and field, volleyball, swimming, softball, tennis, lacrosse, fitness, and dance. Coaches are discoverable by sport and location, sessions average $40–$60 per hour, and every session is backed by $1 million liability insurance. The platform has hosted more than 13,000 coaches serving over 100,000 athletes, with Boston, New York, Los Angeles, Dallas, and Chicago among its top training markets. CoachUp is backed by General Catalyst, Point Judith Capital, and Techstars. As of this profile CoachUp exposes only a consumer web and mobile experience with no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: CPower, Inc.
providers.description: CPower Energy is a commercial and industrial (C&I) virtual power plant (VPP) operator that helps organizations monetize the flexibility of their energy assets through demand response and distributed energy resource (DER) programs. Its CPower CONNECT platform lets customers view, manage, and unlock revenue from energy assets while supporting grid reliability and sustainability goals. CPower serves data centers, crypto mining, healthcare, education, retail, commercial real estate, industrial operations, and the public sector, and has operated distributed energy programs across the U.S. since 2015. CPower was acquired by NRG Energy and operates a combined C&I VPP platform. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent deep-tech lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; CPower publishes a customer portal and a security and compliance posture but no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Cross River Bank
providers.description: Cross River Bank is an FDIC-insured chartered bank that operates as a sponsor bank and banking-as-a-service (BaaS) provider for fintech companies, embedded-finance platforms, and crypto / stablecoin issuers. The product surface is delivered through the Cross River Operating System (COS) - a proprietary API-driven banking core with real-time subledger generation - and includes accounts, ACH and Same-Day ACH, RTP and FedNow instant payments, wires, card issuing and processing (Visa / Mastercard), merchant acquiring, stablecoin rails, consumer and SMB lending, and capital markets / loan participation services. API access is gated behind a partner onboarding process; documentation and sandbox are at docs.crossriver.com.

providers.name: CStorePro
providers.description: CStorePro is a convenience-store back-office and retail-management software platform for independent and chain c-store operators. Founded as CStorePro and later rebranded to CStore Essentials (CSE), it is now part of PDI Technologies and marketed as PDI Essentials. The platform provides back-office operations, pricebook and inventory management, lottery and fuel tracking, automated financial reporting and reconciliation, Skupos scan-data submission for tobacco manufacturer rebates, tobacco loyalty (Skupos Engage), and GasBuddy Business Pages reputation management. It connects directly to POS systems including Gilbarco, Verifone, and NCR for automatic sales and inventory sync. There is no public developer API or documented API program at this time; the product is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application.

providers.name: DoubleDutch
providers.description: DoubleDutch was a San Francisco mobile event technology company backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Its Developer Platform (DDDP) let event organizers and third-party developers build React Native extensions that install into any DoubleDutch event app, with a Firebase-backed data layer, a UI component library, an admin/CMS client, and a command-line interface — all published as official @doubledutch npm packages. DoubleDutch was acquired by Cvent in 2019 and its technology now lives under Cvent's mobile event apps product; www.doubledutch.me redirects to Cvent. The developer surface (GitHub org, the doubledutch.github.io documentation site, and the npm packages) remains published but is unmaintained. There is no public REST OpenAPI — the platform is a client-side extension SDK rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Framewise Health
providers.description: Framewise Health is an AI-native patient engagement platform (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) that converts a patient's medical records into personalized, clinically-reviewed educational videos. The platform pulls patient data from electronic health records over any FHIR R4 endpoint, generates discharge and treatment-adherence education tailored to the individual using institutional protocols and drug-information databases, and delivers it by SMS in 75+ languages with no app and no login.
