The storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface: a published /llms.txt and /agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (ucp.dev) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, and a live UCP shopping MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout. Customer authentication is provided by Shopify's Customer Account API over OpenID Connect. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of Index Ventures, this profile has been enriched from the brand's real public agent, auth, and discovery surfaces.

providers.name: Aristotle
providers.description: Aristotle (heyaristotle.com) is an AI tutoring platform that delivers personalized, one-on-one, dialogue-based instruction across all subjects. Rather than lecturing or simply marking answers wrong, it uses a Socratic, voice-first approach to diagnose conceptual misconceptions and verifies each response turn-by-turn before delivering it to the student. Positioned as an affordable alternative to human tutors, its methodology is grounded in learning science (Bloom's two-sigma work, ICAP, LearnLM benchmarks). Backed by True Ventures. Sector: EdTech / AI education. No public developer API or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Aunt Flow
providers.description: Aunt Flow is a woman-owned company on a mission to end period poverty by making menstrual products freely accessible in public restrooms the same way toilet paper is. It manufactures and sells free-vend period product dispensers (models P, E, R, and O), organic cotton tampons and pads, touch-free disposal systems, and retail display boxes, serving schools, universities, offices, airports, stadiums, ski resorts, restaurants, health systems, amusement parks, and coworking spaces. Since 2021 the company has donated over 6 million period products to people in need. Aunt Flow is a physical-products and e-commerce business (Techstars-backed) with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity, commercial links, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aviyair
providers.description: Aviyair provides global coverage of flight and airport information including real-time and historical flight tracking, flight schedules with airline arrival and departure times, IATA and ICAO codes, airline routes, and flight delays information.

providers.name: Big Sky Health
providers.description: Big Sky Health (now operating as Zero Longevity Science, Inc.) is a Bozeman, Montana consumer digital-health company best known for Zero, one of the most popular intermittent-fasting and nutrition-tracking mobile apps. Zero combines a fasting timer, photo-based meal and protein logging, a personalized Protein Score, and water-intake tracking to help users manage body composition and adopt science-backed longevity practices. The company runs as a direct-to-consumer mobile subscription business (Zero Plus) on iOS and Android. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer program. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Trinity Ventures portfolio company awaiting enrichment.

providers.name: Blackberry
providers.description: BlackBerry Limited is a Canadian intelligent security software and services company headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, and listed on the NYSE and TSX as BB. Once known for its smartphones, BlackBerry today builds embedded and cybersecurity software for enterprises and governments. Its portfolio spans QNX (a real-time operating system for automotive and embedded/IoT systems), Cylance AI-driven endpoint protection, BlackBerry UEM (Unified Endpoint Management), BlackBerry AtHoc critical event management and mass notification, BlackBerry SecuSUITE secure voice and messaging, BlackBerry Workspaces secure file sharing, and the BlackBerry Dynamics secure mobility platform. Developers integrate with these products through REST APIs and SDKs, including the BlackBerry UEM Web Services REST API, the BlackBerry AtHoc API (v2, REST with OpenID Connect / OAuth 2 auth), and the BlackBerry Dynamics SDKs for iOS, Android, Cordova, and React Native. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline from BlackBerry's public developer surface.

providers.name: Boldfit
providers.description: Boldfit is an Indian direct-to-consumer fitness and sportswear brand selling workout equipment (pull-up bars, resistance bands, massage guns, yoga mats and lifting gear), performance footwear (running, trekking, walking, cricket and badminton shoes) and athletic apparel for men and women. The brand positions itself around fitness and performance, partnering with athletes, and sells primarily to the Indian market through a Shopify-hosted online store at boldfit.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Boldfit does not run a public developer program or API; the only programmatic surface is the Shopify Customer Account OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect layer exposed on the storefront.

providers.name: Caliber Fitness
providers.description: Caliber Fitness, Inc. is a consumer strength-training and fitness-coaching company behind the Caliber: Strength Training app (iOS and Android). Caliber combines data-driven resistance-training and nutrition programming, a library of 600+ exercises, workout tracking, and one-on-one video coaching from certified personal trainers across free, Caliber Plus, and Premium Coaching tiers. Founded by Justin Fauci and Chris Muir, the company is backed by Trinity Ventures. Caliber operates as a consumer mobile app and coaching service; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time. This profile tracks its public web, legal, and membership surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Campus
providers.description: Campus (campus.edu) is an accredited, for-profit online community college offering associate degree programs built on the CUNY ASAP high-touch support model, with live classes taught by faculty from top universities, personal success coaching, and tuition capped at the Pell Grant maximum. Founded by Tade Oyerinde and backed by Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Bloomberg Beta, 8VC, Rethink Education and others, Campus focuses on affordable, accessible higher education and career preparation across programs such as applied AI, business, information technology and healthcare administration. This profile was surfaced as a venture portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web surface; Campus is a consumer education provider and publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Chatter Research
providers.description: Chatter Research (now Chatter by Stingray) is a customer feedback and experience management platform built for modern retailers. It engages shoppers in AI-driven conversational text-message and QR-code surveys that deliver higher response rates and real-time feedback, then uses the Stingray-Chatter AI (trained on 7000+ retail topics) to categorize free-text replies into topics and sentiment. Role-based dashboards surface NPS/CSAT, benchmarks, topic explorers, and NPS boosters so store teams can save lost sales, drive loyalty enrollment, and generate online reviews. Founded in 2016 and acquired by Stingray, the company is a former 500 Global portfolio company. The product is a SaaS dashboard with a help center and CSV data exports; it publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: checkout51
providers.description: Checkout 51 is a consumer cash-back rewards service, delivered as a free mobile app and website, that lets shoppers earn money back on everyday grocery and gas purchases. Members browse weekly offers, buy participating brands at any store, then upload a photo of their receipt to claim cash back; balances are paid out by check once they reach a $20 threshold. The company earns revenue from partner brands that fund the offers. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Slow Ventures portfolio company; it operates a consumer app plus a partner/brands program, but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or specifications at this time.

providers.name: Component Model
providers.description: The WebAssembly Component Model is a broad-reaching architecture for building interoperable WebAssembly libraries, applications, and environments. It defines components as portable, sandboxed units of code that can compose with each other across language and runtime boundaries. The model introduces interfaces, worlds, and the WebAssembly Interface Type (WIT) language, along with a canonical ABI, binary and text formats, and a concurrency model. The Component Model underpins the WebAssembly System Interface (WASI) Preview 2 and is the foundation for portable Wasm on browsers, servers, edge, and embedded environments.

providers.name: Customer Database
providers.description: Customer Database is the topic dedicated to APIs, schemas, vocabularies, and reference designs for the systems of record that store customer identity, profile, contact, preference, consent, and account data. A customer database underpins CRM, marketing automation, customer data platforms (CDPs), customer service, billing, and analytics use cases, and is increasingly expected to support API-first access, schema-on-write data quality, real-time eventing, GDPR/CCPA consent and erasure workflows, and identity resolution across web, mobile, and offline channels. This repository tracks the vendors, standards, and patterns that make customer data accessible, governed, and portable.

providers.name: Empathy
providers.description: Empathy is a support platform that helps organizations guide people through loss, leave, and legacy moments, combining AI with human care to serve individuals navigating grief, estate planning, and major life transitions. Its products include LifeVault digital estate planning, Loss Support for beneficiaries handling claims and grief, Leave Support for employees during difficult life events, and Client Connect for advisors. Empathy sells to life insurance companies, banks and wealth managers, employers, health plans, and benefit consultants, covering 50M+ individuals. Backed by General Catalyst and Index Ventures. As of this profile Empathy publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Floreo
providers.description: Floreo is a research-based virtual reality (VR) digital therapeutics company that delivers immersive lessons teaching social, behavioral, communication, and life skills to neurodiverse individuals, including autistic children and adults. The platform runs across mobile (iPhone with Google Cardboard) and standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2/3/Pro, PICO), with a companion clinician portal for supervised sessions, progress tracking, and telehealth-style delivery. Floreo holds an FDA Breakthrough Device designation and participates in the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP), and works with schools, behavioral-health providers, Medicaid programs, and research partners. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Goodr
providers.description: Goodr is an Atlanta-based sustainable surplus food management and hunger-relief logistics company founded in 2016 by Jasmine Crowe-Houston. Goodr helps businesses divert edible and inedible food waste from landfills by scheduling pickups, donating surplus edible food to local nonprofits, and providing donors with the tax deductions and impact reporting tied to those donations. Alongside its food-waste solutions, Goodr runs hunger-relief programs including pop-up grocery markets, meal delivery, student snackpacks, and community grocery stores. The company reports more than 30 million meals served and 4 million pounds of food diverted from landfills for enterprise partners such as Amazon, Google, NASA, and Fulton County. Goodr operates through a partner portal rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Granthika
providers.description: Granthika is a writing-software company founded by novelist Vikram Chandra (author of Sacred Games) and Borislav Iordanov. Its product is a first-of-its-kind semantic editor for professional and aspiring writers that lets authors capture and manage the knowledge inside a manuscript — characters, locations, events, and narrative structure — as they write, then integrate that knowledge back into the text. Features include universe/knowledge building, a timeline, semantic search, an intelligent analyzer, and language assistance, delivered as both an online app and a desktop application with free trials and educational subscriptions. Granthika was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. It publishes no bespoke developer/product API; its marketing site runs on Wix, which exposes a public Wix Site MCP endpoint and an llms.txt for agentic access to public site content.

providers.name: Headlight
providers.description: Headlight is a US mental health services company delivering teletherapy, in-person therapy, psychiatry, and medication management through a clinician-centered care model. Founded by Drs. Manish Sheth and Shashita Inamdar, it helps patients move from initial interest to a well-matched therapist or prescriber with less friction, treating conditions including depression, anxiety, ADHD, bipolar disorder, PTSD, trauma, OCD, panic disorder, postpartum depression, and insomnia. Headlight is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Cross, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Kaiser, Moda) and operates across Alaska, California, Colorado, Oregon, Texas, and Washington. The company raised $18M led by Matrix and EPIC Ventures. This is a consumer clinical services provider with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Homage
providers.description: Homage is a Singapore-headquartered holistic health and caregiving platform that connects families with screened, professional caregivers, nurses, and therapists to deliver personal care, home nursing procedures, rehabilitation, and health services where people live. Founded in 2016, Homage operates across Singapore, Malaysia, and Australia through consumer mobile apps and a care-management operations platform, offering flexible on-demand and recurring visits, care assessments, custom care plans, and teleconsultations for conditions such as dementia, stroke recovery, and post-surgical care. Homage does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web properties and probed domain security.

providers.name: HomeTouch
providers.description: HomeTouch (myhometouch.com) is a UK-based live-in home care marketplace founded in 2015 by Dr Jamie Wilson, a former NHS dementia specialist. The CQC-regulated service connects families with vetted professional carers for live-in, overnight, and visiting care, with a specialism in dementia and complex-needs support, hospital discharge, end-of-life, respite, and companionship care. Backed by 500 Global and other impact investors, HomeTouch operates a carer marketplace alongside a fully managed care service. The company publishes no public developer program or API; this profile tracks its identity, published web properties, and domain security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Horizon Media
providers.description: Horizon Media is the largest independent media agency in the United States, founded in 1989 by Bill Koenigsberg and headquartered at 75 Varick Street in New York with offices in Los Angeles and Toronto. The agency employs roughly 2,300+ people, is ranked the third largest US media agency by COMvergence, and manages an estimated $8.7 billion in billings. Horizon operates a portfolio of specialty units (Horizon Next for performance, Blue Hour Studios for social/creator, Night Market for retail media, Scout Sports for sponsorship via Horizon Sports & Experiences, and the WHY Group for cultural insights) and runs a proprietary data and AI stack anchored by the Blu platform. In 2025 Horizon formed Horizon Global, a 50/50 US joint venture with Havas positioned at roughly $20 billion in combined billings, merging Blu with Havas Converged into a shared platform branded BluConverged, and is also building Horizon OS (Open Sphere) as an orchestration layer over the programmatic ad-tech stack. In June 2026 Horizon launched an agentic integration layer around Blu — a set of Blu audience APIs, MCP endpoints and agent-based integration points that ad-tech, media-owner and martech partners can build on — but that surface is partner-gated: Horizon publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no SDKs in any public registry, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The only route to the API is the corporate contact form. All platforms documented here are proprietary systems reachable through a commercial partnership rather than open developer APIs.

providers.name: HTTP Client
providers.description: HTTP Client is JetBrains' built-in tool for creating, editing, and executing HTTP requests directly from the IDE. Requests are stored in .http and .rest files alongside source code, with code highlighting, completion for hosts and methods, code folding, inline documentation, and live templates accelerating composition. The client supports HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 requests, gRPC unary and server-streaming calls, WebSocket connections, GraphQL operations, server-sent events, and imports from cURL and Postman collections. Environment files define reusable variables across global, request, and secured scopes; the cookie jar, request history, run/debug configurations, and Services tool window response viewer round out a workflow tightly integrated with the IntelliJ-based IDE family.

providers.name: Ionic
providers.description: Ionic is a platform for building and deploying modern mobile applications and micro frontend experiences. Ionic provides tools, guides, and APIs to help developers build and ship incredible apps faster, including cross-platform mobile development capabilities.

providers.name: Joinmidi
providers.description: Joinmidi (Midi Health) is a virtual care company for women in midlife, providing insurance-covered telehealth from women's health specialists across all 50 states. Its clinicians deliver personalized, evidence-based care for perimenopause and menopause plus weight management, sexual wellness, mood, sleep, hair and skin health, and cancer survivorship, backed by custom prescription medications (Midi Custom Rx) and a targeted supplement line. Midi is NCQA accredited, works with major insurance plans, and partners with health systems and Fortune 100 employers as a covered benefit. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer or API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Kismet
providers.description: Kismet is an Australian digital-health marketplace that connects people with disability — primarily National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) participants — to verified, available service providers across occupational therapy, speech therapy, physiotherapy, support coordination and plan management. The platform pairs a searchable provider marketplace and care index with a Concierge AI matching service that builds a shortlist of suitable, available providers within 48 hours, alongside budget-tracking and plan-management tools for participants. Kismet is backed by Prosus Ventures and ships consumer iOS and Android apps. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Metromile
providers.description: Metromile is a pay-per-mile auto insurance platform powered by telematics and data science. Customers attach the Pulse OBD device to their vehicle to track mileage; premiums consist of a base monthly rate plus a per-mile charge, rewarding low-mileage drivers with significant savings. Beyond consumer insurance, Metromile Enterprise offers a cloud-based REST API platform for property and casualty insurers covering touchless claims automation, accident reconstruction (Replay), fraud detection (Detect), digital FNOL reporting (Report), and back-office workflow automation (Streamline). Metromile was acquired by Lemonade in July 2022.

providers.name: PREDIK Data-Driven
providers.description: PREDIK Data-Driven is a big-data analytics and location-intelligence research firm (founded 2008, Coral Gables, Florida) that builds enriched geospatial datasets for site selection, demand forecasting, and web/reference intelligence. Its products cover Point-of-Interest (POI) data, aggregated foot-traffic and human mobility data derived from anonymized mobile devices, company and commercial-area intelligence, and socio-demographic enrichment - divided into geohash-7 (150x150m) cells with 100-200+ variables and coverage of up to 96 countries. PREDIK is a data-delivery / contact-sales provider - datasets are licensed and delivered as managed feeds via REST API, SOAP API, Feed API, or S3 bucket in JSON, CSV, and SQL formats. There is no public self-serve developer API portal or published API reference; access is arranged directly with PREDIK or through the Datarade marketplace. Endpoints are not publicly documented and are therefore not modeled here.

providers.name: Prenuvo
providers.description: Prenuvo operates a preventive healthcare screening service built around whole-body MRI imaging paired with blood biomarker panels and personalized results reviews. A single scan captures on the order of a billion data points while screening for hundreds of conditions across major organ systems, without radiation or contrast agents, and completes in under an hour. Blood panels measure 80+ biomarkers tied to inflammation, hormone levels, and metabolic health, with optional advanced imaging for brain, heart, and body composition. Prenuvo runs clinics across the US, Canada, Australia, and the UK, and works with research institutions including Mount Sinai, UCLA, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, and Penn. Prenuvo does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: QXO Building Products
providers.description: QXO is a publicly traded company focused on building a tech-forward leader in the building products distribution industry through acquisitions and operational improvements. QXO offers a suite of customer-facing APIs for ordering, pricing, account management, product catalog, delivery tracking, and invoicing.

providers.name: RBAC
providers.description: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is a security paradigm that restricts system access based on assigned roles rather than individual user identities. Users are granted permissions through role membership, simplifying access management and ensuring the principle of least privilege. RBAC is foundational to enterprise identity, authorization, and compliance programs and is implemented across operating systems, cloud platforms, databases, and APIs. The NIST/ANSI/INCITS 359-2004 standard formally defines the RBAC model across four components: Core RBAC, Hierarchical RBAC, Static Separation of Duty, and Dynamic Separation of Duty. Cloud platforms (AWS IAM, Azure RBAC, GCP IAM) and Kubernetes all implement RBAC natively, making it the de facto authorization standard for enterprise and cloud-native environments.

providers.name: RDP
providers.description: The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) is a proprietary network protocol developed by Microsoft that provides a graphical interface to connect to another computer over a network. RDP transmits keyboard, mouse, display, and audio data between client and host, enabling remote administration, virtual desktops, and remote work scenarios. The protocol typically operates on TCP and UDP port 3389 and is defined in the MS-RDPBCGR open specification. It is implemented by Microsoft's Remote Desktop Services as well as third-party clients across Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android. The RDP acronym is also shared with the Refinitiv Data Platform (LSEG), a cloud REST API platform for financial market data, historical pricing, ESG, and analytics.

providers.name: Rentals.ca
providers.description: Rentals.ca is a Toronto-headquartered residential rental marketplace and the flagship brand of the Rentals.ca Network, which also operates Rentfaster.ca, Louer.ca, Rentboard.ca, RentCanada.com and TorontoRentals.com across more than 100 Canadian cities. The network is owned and operated by Rentsync (formerly Landlord Web Solutions Inc.), which also acquired the research firm Urbanation in January 2026 and co-publishes the monthly Rentals.ca / Urbanation National Rent Report; Rentals.ca listing data also feeds a Statistics Canada rental housing index. In the Canadian real estate value chain it sits on the rentals side of the market, outside CREA's REALTOR.ca and Data Distribution Facility, which syndicate member boards' for-sale listings. Its API posture is honest but closed: rentals.ca itself publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI, and no documented public endpoint, and the entire consumer site sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that returns HTTP 403 to anonymous clients. The real developer surface belongs to the parent, at the Rentsync Partners portal (partners.rentsync.ca, branded "LIFT System API"), which publicly names a REST API, an Ad Syndication API and a Search API but places all documentation behind an account whose registration form requires a written application explaining what you intend to build. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document, no Universal Property Identifier, and no open dataset published by the company.

providers.name: Reynolds and Reynolds
providers.description: Reynolds and Reynolds is one of the automotive industry's largest Dealership Management System (DMS) providers, running the ERA-IGNITE and POWER platforms that operate the core of thousands of franchised car dealerships - sales and desking, F&I, service and repair orders, parts inventory, CRM, and dealership accounting. Reynolds does NOT publish an open, self-serve developer API. All programmatic access to DMS data flows through the Reynolds Certified Interface (RCI) program, a certification-gated, contract-and-NDA partner program run by Reynolds Data Management. RCI provides secured, real-time, bi-directional interfaces so certified third parties can read from and write back to a dealer's Reynolds DMS. There is no public developer portal, no public API reference, and no published OpenAPI. The APIs below are logical groupings of the DMS data domains exposed through RCI; endpoints are modeled, not sourced from public documentation.

providers.name: Rookout
providers.description: Rookout is a live application debugging platform founded in 2017 in Tel Aviv, Israel that lets developers set non-breaking breakpoints in running production, staging, and development applications to capture full-stack debug data — variables, stack traces, logs, and metrics — without redeploying, restarting, or stopping services. Rookout pioneered the "live debugger" category for cloud-native and Kubernetes-hosted applications and shipped language agents/SDKs for Python, Java/JVM, Node.js, .NET, Go, and Ruby that attach to running processes and stream snapshots back to the Rookout web IDE or developer's IDE. Dynatrace announced its acquisition of Rookout on July 31, 2023 and closed the deal in Q2 of Dynatrace's fiscal year ending September 30, 2023. The standalone Rookout product has since been folded into the Dynatrace platform as the Dynatrace Live Debugger (and Live Logger), and the rookout.com and docs.rookout.com domains now redirect to dynatrace.com. There is no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, webhook catalog, or CLI for Rookout — the developer surface consists entirely of language agents, deployment integration examples, IDE extensions, and the Explorook desktop helper that exposes local source folders to the Rookout web debugger. The Rookout GitHub organization remains public and continues to maintain those agents, tutorials, and integration samples under Apache-2.0.

providers.name: Shift Technology
providers.description: Shift Technology is a Paris-founded InsurTech company delivering AI-native decisioning and automation for the global insurance industry. Its purpose-built AI agents automate core insurance workflows — claims coverage and liability, fraud and risk detection, subrogation, injury evaluation, payment integrity, and process orchestration — for property & casualty and health insurers. Shift serves 120+ insurers across 30+ countries, including 100% of the top five U.S. P&C carriers, and has analyzed more than four billion policies, claims, and documents covering 350M+ policyholders. The company also operates the Insurance Data Network (IDN). Shift is a General Catalyst portfolio company; it markets an enterprise, contact-sales product and does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs.

providers.name: ShopShops
providers.description: ShopShops is a livestream commerce marketplace for authenticated pre-owned luxury and designer goods — handbags, jewelry, watches, accessories, and shoes sold through live shopping events and an online store. Buyers shop curated secondhand inventory with authentication (via Entrupy), buy-now-pay-later (Afterpay / Shop Pay), and return assurance (Seel). The storefront runs on Shopify and publishes a live agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, an MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search and buyer-approved checkout, an OIDC/OAuth2 Customer Account API, and an llms.txt describing how AI shopping agents may transact with the store.

providers.name: Simpleclub
providers.description: Simpleclub is a German digital learning platform serving over two million students (grades 5-13), apprentices, and organizations across school, vocational training (Ausbildung), continuing education, retraining, and workforce upskilling. The product pairs curriculum-aligned content (including IHK-aligned vocational tracks) with an AI-powered learning assistant, trainer/learning-management tooling, and the ability for organizations to upload custom content. It counts 750+ corporate clients such as Deutsche Bahn, Bosch, and Vodafone. Simpleclub maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source Flutter tooling (math keyboard, flutter_math, design-token builder) but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification; this profile is an end-user/EdTech company record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Summer Health
providers.description: Summer Health is a pediatric health company offering families fast, board-certified pediatric care. Its flagship consumer service provides comprehensive at-home blood work for children ages 8-18 (one blood draw covering 74 biomarkers) reviewed by board-certified pediatricians over video, alongside text-based urgent-care messaging with pediatric clinicians. The service is HSA/FSA eligible and LegitScript-approved. Summer Health is a consumer-facing telehealth offering and does not currently publish a public developer program, API documentation, or third-party integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Teal Health
providers.description: Teal Health, Inc. is a women's health company behind the Teal Wand, the first and only FDA-approved at-home self-collection device for cervical cancer screening in the United States. Its end-to-end telehealth service pairs the self-collection kit with virtual Teal medical providers who prescribe the kit, review Roche cobas HPV lab results, and support patients aged 25-65 throughout the screening experience. Now available in all 50 states, Teal Health runs a HIPAA-compliant direct-to-consumer telehealth platform and is a consumer of third-party healthcare APIs (Healthie for scheduling/telehealth, Candid for billing) rather than a publisher of a public developer API.

providers.name: Truist
providers.description: Truist Financial Corporation is a U.S. bank holding company headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, formed in December 2019 through the merger of BB&T and SunTrust Banks. Its principal subsidiary, Truist Bank, is a North Carolina state-chartered commercial bank and member of the Federal Reserve System, ranking among the largest U.S. commercial banks by assets and serving consumer, small-business, commercial, and wealth clients. On the API and open-finance side Truist runs a first-party Truist Developer Center at developer.truist.com that publishes registration-gated Open Banking APIs in a sandbox environment returning mock data (personal and small-business accounts, balances, transactions, and credit-transfer payments), and it operates a separate Truist Open Banking API Developer Portal for consumer-permissioned data sharing. Consumer data access is delivered largely through FDX-aligned, tokenized connections and aggregator partnerships (notably a Plaid data-access agreement) rather than an open first-party production API, and Truist states it monitors and complies with evolving CFPB Section 1033 personal-financial-data rules.

providers.name: Valero Energy
providers.description: Valero Energy Corporation is the world's largest independent petroleum refiner and a leading producer of low-carbon transportation fuels. Headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, Valero operates 14 petroleum refineries with 3 million barrels per day capacity, 12 ethanol plants, and renewable diesel production facilities across the US, Canada, and UK. The company trades on NYSE as VLO and is a Fortune 100 company.

providers.name: Vega Security
providers.description: Vega (vega.io) is an AI-native security operations platform that bills itself as the operating system for agentic SecOps in the post-SIEM era. Its Security Analytics Mesh (SAM) federates queries across security data sources in place -- with no ingestion, migration, or egress -- and powers agentic detection engineering, autonomous alert triage, and security analytics, continuously assessing detection coverage against MITRE ATT&CK. Backed by Accel. The product app and documentation are login-gated and no public API surface has been published yet.

providers.name: Xelix
providers.description: Xelix is a London-based company (with a US office in Wilmington, DE) providing an AI-powered Accounts Payable control platform that bolts onto existing ERP, P2P, and email systems. Its five modules — Transactions (duplicate/incorrect payment and fraud prevention), Statements (supplier statement reconciliation), Helpdesk (generative-AI vendor query resolution), Vendors (master vendor data cleansing), and Reports — process 115M+ invoices annually for 200+ global customers. Backed by Insight Partners ($160M raised July 2025 to advance agentic AI in AP). Xelix is ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certified, GDPR compliant, hosted on AWS (EU/US/UK data residency), and publishes a Vanta trust center and an UptimeRobot status page. Integration is file-based (daily SFTP transfer of invoice, workflow, and master vendor data) plus optional SSO and email integrations; the company publishes no public developer portal or documented API surface, though its platform runs on api.xelix.com and its engineering team maintains open-source Python/Rust packages on GitHub (xelixdev).

providers.name: Afiniti
providers.description: Afiniti is an enterprise contact center AI company whose patented behavioral pairing technology matches inbound customers with the agent most likely to produce a desired business outcome, measured against a continuously alternating ON/OFF control benchmark. In 2026 the company extended pairing into what it calls Outcome Orchestration, a unified AI decisioning platform spanning four products: Afiniti Pairing, Afiniti Orchestrator, Afiniti Intelligence and Afiniti Agents. Afiniti sits as a decisioning layer above existing CCaaS, ACD, IVR/IVA, CRM and workforce platforms rather than replacing them, and is deployed at telco, financial services, insurance, healthcare and travel/hospitality enterprises. Integration reaches customers through host platform ecosystems (Genesys AppFoundry, NICE CXexchange/DEVone, Five9) and through the Afiniti Link partner program, which advertises APIs and SDKs to certified partners but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Afori
providers.description: Afori is a Barcelona- and Germany-based insurtech building an AI software platform designed specifically for insurance brokers (Versicherungsmakler). Its first product is an AI Sidebar that lives inside Microsoft Outlook and broker management systems (Maklerverwaltungsprogramme), turning unstructured emails and documents into structured, review-ready cases with tasks and reminders, context-aware email drafts, and prefilled claim notifications. Specialized AI agents (KI-Helfer) automate insurance-specific back-office work while keeping every action documented and auditable. The platform is EU-hosted, GDPR (DSGVO) compliant, ISO 27001:2022 certified, and built within the European regulatory framework (IDD, EU AI Act). Founded in 2025 by former wefox leaders Fabian Wesemann (CEO) and Sergi Banos (CTO), Afori raised a EUR 4M round led by General Catalyst. This API Evangelist profile was created as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched from Afori's public web surface; the company currently publishes no developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Any-API
providers.description: Any-API was a directory and documentation platform for discovering and testing public APIs with interactive Swagger-based API explorers. The domain now redirects to APILayer, a curated API marketplace offering reliable and scalable APIs across categories including AI, finance, content, and data. APILayer provides a unified developer experience with sandboxing, SDKs, and a single subscription for access to multiple API products.

providers.name: Appriss Retail
providers.description: Appriss Retail provides AI-powered solutions that help retailers manage Total Retail Loss across in-store and online channels. Its SaaS platform combines data intelligence, decision intelligence, and workflow intelligence to reduce returns fraud, shrink, and exceptions in real time. Marquee products include Appriss Engage (return and claims authorization, incorporating the Verify return-authorization engine), Appriss Secure (shrink and exception analytics), Appriss Incident (case management), Sidekick (an AI collaborator for loss-prevention teams), and the APIS performance-intelligence platform. Appriss Retail serves more than 60 of the top 100 U.S. retailers, drawing on 20+ years of retail data science. Programmatic integration is delivered to retailer clients through the APIS Online cloud portal rather than a public self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Arvist
providers.description: Arvist AI is a Chicago-based computer-vision platform for warehouse and supply-chain operations that turns existing cameras, scanners, and WMS/ERP data into automated quality control, safety and compliance monitoring, load verification, inbound shipment inspection, and freight-claims management. The system deploys on-premise edge servers, integrates with 80+ leading WMS and ERP platforms without new hardware, and detects damage, defects, unsafe behavior, and outbound shipping errors in real time. Backed by Techstars, Arvist is ISO 27001 certified and SOC 2 Type I compliant. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from Arvist's public web surface; the company currently publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Astrix
providers.description: Astrix Security is a non-human identity (NHI) and AI agent security platform. It gives enterprises a real-time inventory of every AI agent, MCP server, service account, OAuth app, API key, SSH key and IAM role across their environment, then detects excessive privileges, misconfigurations, anomalous activity and policy violations and drives automated remediation. Its Agent Control Plane provisions secure-by-design AI agents with short-lived, precisely scoped credentials. Astrix became part of Cisco in 2026 and ended standalone sales of new licenses effective June 30, 2026. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures. Sector: cybersecurity. This is a company profile — Astrix publishes no public developer API, so the profile carries identity, security-posture, and compliance signals rather than API specifications.

providers.name: Atlys
providers.description: Atlys is a digital visa application platform that helps travelers obtain tourist, business, and transit visas on time for 150+ destinations, backed by a guarantee. Founded in 2020 by Mohak Nahta and headquartered in San Francisco, Atlys asks travelers a short set of questions and then automates form-filling, document compilation (itineraries, cover letters, NOCs, flight and hotel confirmations), payment, and appointment booking against official government and embassy requirements that are refreshed monthly. It covers e-visas, visa-on-arrival, Schengen, US, UK ETA and more, and serves travelers from India, the United States, the United Kingdom, the UAE, Australia, Singapore, and Saudi Arabia. Atlys Enterprise adds group processing (up to 1,000 travelers), HRMS/payroll integrations (Workday, Rippling), concierge support, and secure passport logistics for corporate travel teams. Atlys is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Sequoia, Accel, and others, having raised over $40M across multiple rounds.

providers.name: Atom Learning
providers.description: Atom Learning is a UK edtech company providing an online, adaptive exam-preparation and learning platform for children aged 7 to 16. Its consumer product, Atom Home, delivers personalised practice, unlimited mock tests with instant marking, and progress tracking for 11+ grammar and independent-school entrance exams (GL, CEM, CSSE, ISEB), CAT4, Key Stage 2 SATs, and GCSE revision. Its schools product, Atom School, gives teachers curriculum-mapped resources and assessment tools and is used by over 1,000 schools. Founded by educators and assessment specialists, Atom has supported hundreds of thousands of families as a lower-cost alternative to private tutoring. The company was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a consumer web/app product surface but no public developer API.

providers.name: Axion
providers.description: Axion (formerly Axion Ray) is an AI platform for manufacturing quality intelligence that helps global manufacturers detect, diagnose, and resolve product quality and warranty issues faster. It unifies customer, service, field, and telematics data to deliver early problem detection, root-cause analysis, and improvement tracking, reducing warranty costs and investigation time. Customers include Daikin, Harley-Davidson, SharkNinja, Cummins, and Schneider Electric. Founded by Daniel First, Axion has raised Series A (led by Bessemer Venture Partners) and Series B (led by Salesforce Ventures). Axion is an enterprise SaaS product with no publicly documented API or developer platform at this time; this profile captures its company identity, legal, and security/compliance surface.

providers.name: BC Hydro
providers.description: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority (BC Hydro) is a provincial Crown corporation whose sole shareholder is the Province of British Columbia, and which states that it generates and delivers electricity to "95% of the population of B.C." and serves "over five million people." It is the vertically integrated end of the value chain in a market with no retail competition: BC Hydro owns the generation fleet (predominantly large hydroelectric), owns and operates the provincial transmission and distribution system, and is the monopoly retailer that bills the customer — all under rate regulation by the B.C. Utilities Commission (BCUC), not under any consumer data right. That regulatory fact drives the entire API posture. Ontario Regulation 633/21 compels Ontario distributors to implement Green Button Download My Data and Connect My Data; British Columbia has no equivalent, and no Canadian federal energy data mandate exists. BC Hydro has nonetheless adopted Green Button voluntarily — but only the file half of it. BC Hydro's own MyHydro billing pages state that a customer can "Download a CSV or Green Button XML file with your metered electricity use," available through the previous day and up to three years back. There is no Connect My Data, no OAuth authorization surface, no third-party vendor onboarding, and no published resource base URI: a third party cannot obtain a customer's usage data through any documented API, only the account holder can, by logging in and downloading a file. On the market-data side the picture is just as closed. There is no developer.bchydro.com, api.bchydro.com, data.bchydro.com or docs.bchydro.com (all DNS failures), no /developers, /api or /data path, no OpenAPI or Swagger definition anywhere, and no open data portal. Wholesale transmission information is posted to an OATI-hosted OASIS node that only registered transmission customers may use, and the BCUC-ordered transaction-data postings are documents rather than feeds. The single deliberate open-data artifact is one 2013 mapping layer published to the provincial BC Data Catalogue under the org "bc-hydro-and-power-authority." The finding is a utility that is closed on both axes: consumer data exists in a real standard but only as a human-initiated download behind a customer login, and grid/market data is either registration-gated or absent.

providers.name: Beeline
providers.description: Beeline makes smart navigation devices and a companion mobile app for cyclists and motorcyclists. Its compact handlebar-mounted devices — Beeline Velo for bicycles and Beeline Moto for motorcycles — use a simple directional and turn-by-turn interface to help riders find their way around towns and cities, discover better routes, and record their journeys. The London-based company is backed by Seedcamp. Beeline sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted storefront at beeline.co, which exposes an agent-facing commerce surface — a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint, Shopify customer-account OIDC, and an llms.txt agent policy — rather than a first-party developer product API.

providers.name: Bold Security
providers.description: Bold Security provides real-time, on-device (endpoint) data security. Its on-device AI classifies data interactions across every application in real time and detects and prevents user- and AI-agent-driven data exfiltration before sensitive data leaves the endpoint, without requiring policy configuration or cloud round-trips. The platform gives security teams visibility into data movement, intent and risky-behavior analysis, and full-context investigation across employees and AI agents. Bold Security is ISO 27001 certified and SOC 2 compliant, and is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, specification, or SDK; this entry captures its identity, security posture, and public properties.

providers.name: Capella University
providers.description: Capella University is an accredited online university owned by Strategic Education, Inc. (SEI), offering competency-based bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees plus graduate certificates across business, counseling and therapy, education, health sciences, information technology, nursing, psychology, and social work. Capella is regionally accredited by the Higher Learning Commission and delivers coursework through two learning formats — FlexPath, a self-paced competency-based model, and GuidedPath, a structured-timeline model — serving working adults and professional learners entirely online.

providers.name: Cloaked
providers.description: Cloaked is a consumer privacy and identity-protection platform that lets people create unlimited unique identities to shield their real personal data. Each identity bundles a masked email address, a virtual phone number, an auto-generated password, and virtual payment cards so users can sign up for services without handing over their real contact information. The platform adds a built-in password manager, AI-powered spam call screening (Call Guard), dark web and SSN monitoring, automated data-broker removal across 120+ sites, and up to $1M in identity theft insurance. Cloaked emphasizes a zero-knowledge architecture with end-to-end encryption and is SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, and PCI DSS compliant. Backed by General Catalyst, Cloaked ships consumer apps (iOS, Android, web, browser extension) and a Cloaked Enterprise offering for businesses; it is a consumer-facing product with no publicly documented developer API at this time.

providers.name: Complori
providers.description: Complori is a Berlin, Germany based online education company that teaches children and young people to code through live, small-group video classes led by qualified coaches in a protected digital space. Its programs span programming with Minecraft, Python, JavaScript game development, app development, and financial literacy, backed by a learning platform with challenges and exercises, a mobile learning app, completion certificates, flexible family-friendly scheduling, and holiday camps. Complori operates a B2C consumer education service (with parents as the decision-makers) rather than a developer-facing API product, and runs an education scholarship program to broaden access across socioeconomic backgrounds. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Comply365
providers.description: Comply365 is an enterprise SaaS provider of operational content, safety, and training management software for highly regulated, safety-critical industries including airlines, defense, rail, and MRO (maintenance, repair, and overhaul). Its AI-powered platform unifies three mission-critical products: ContentManager365 for authoring, managing, and distributing controlled operational documentation and manuals; SafetyManager365 for safety reporting, investigation, and root-cause analysis; and TrainingManager365 for workforce readiness and compliance training. Comply365 helps regulated operators shorten document change cycles, maintain regulatory compliance, and connect frontline teams to the current, approved content they need. The company is an Insight Partners portfolio company and is an ISO 27001 and ISO 9001 certified organization.

providers.name: Credit Sesame
providers.description: Credit Sesame is a consumer financial health platform that provides free daily credit-score monitoring, credit reports, and personalized recommendations for credit cards, loans, and insurance based on a member's approval likelihood. Members can build credit through everyday debit purchases and upgrade to the Sesame+ premium tier for three-bureau credit reports, advanced credit tools, and identity-theft protection. Credit Sesame operates consumer web and mobile applications and, as of this profile, does not publish a public developer API; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile backed by Menlo Ventures.

providers.name: d-Matrix
providers.description: d-Matrix builds ultra-low-latency, energy-efficient AI inference infrastructure for generative AI in the datacenter. Its memory-centric compute architecture, next-generation I/O, and stacked-DRAM approach are delivered through the Corsair inference accelerator (chiplet-based, supporting models up to 100B parameters), the JetStream accelerator-to-accelerator communications platform, the SquadRack disaggregated rack-scale solution, and the 3DIMC 3D digital in-memory compute technology. Founded by Sid Sheth and Sudeep Bhoja and headquartered in Santa Clara, the company has raised roughly $450M (including a $275M Series C) from investors such as Qatar Investment Authority, Temasek, and SK Hynix. d-Matrix also maintains the open-source dmx-compressor (DMX) PyTorch toolkit for co-designing models to its inference hardware. This API Evangelist network profile tracks d-Matrix as a compute-hardware provider; it does not currently publish a public web API.

providers.name: DayDream Dental
providers.description: DayDream Dental is a full-service dental billing and revenue cycle management (RCM) provider that runs the insurance and billing operations for dental practices and DSOs so clinical teams can focus on patient care. Services span insurance verification with custom coding breakdowns saved directly to the practice management system (PMS), clean claims submission with attachments and narratives, payment posting with accurate insurance adjustments, diligent claim follow-up every seven days until paid with denials appealed, and patient billing via text, email, and mail. DayDream operates a HIPAA-focused trust center and a client dashboard app, and publishes a blog, CDT-code and payer references, videos, and demo scheduling for onboarding new offices. This is a service company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: DeepStream Technologies
providers.description: DeepStream Technologies (deep.stream) is a London-based AI-enhanced eSourcing and source-to-contract platform for mid-market procurement teams. It digitalizes buyer-to-supplier sourcing with best-of-breed eRFx, supplier discovery, supplier pre-qualification, eAuctions, contract management, management reporting, and AI-driven RFP generation and conversational analytics, aiming to help procurement teams work faster, reduce risk, and gain visibility while keeping implementation simple. Customers include Walkers Shortbread, BrewDog, Abbott, and Free Now. DeepStream does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation; integrations with ERP and PO systems are delivered as a service. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched with public company and infrastructure signals.

providers.name: Defense Health Agency
providers.description: The Defense Health Agency (DHA) is a joint, integrated combat support agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to combatant commands. DHA operates the Military Health System (MHS), MHS Genesis electronic health record, the Military Health System Data Repository (MDR), and the Enterprise Intelligence and Data Solutions (EIDS) program. Data exchange inside MHS Genesis uses SMART on FHIR APIs, but DHA does not currently publish a general-purpose public developer API.

providers.name: Dezerv
providers.description: Dezerv (Dezerv Investments Private Limited) is an Indian wealth-management platform building a house of investment solutions for affluent Indians. It offers discretionary Portfolio Management Services (PMS), curated mutual-fund portfolios, bonds, an Investment Portfolio Analyser (IPA), a Wealth Monitor for tracking held-away assets, and ESOP financing, alongside a research-led investment philosophy and a weekly money newsletter. Dezerv is a SEBI-registered Portfolio Manager (INP000007377) and Investment Manager to a Category-I AIF / Angel Fund; mutual-fund distribution is via its AMFI-registered subsidiary. The company is client-facing (client.dezerv.in portal) and does not publish a public developer API surface. This API Evangelist profile enriches the company identity, links, and security posture rather than an API.

providers.name: DIY
providers.description: DIY.org is a safe, ad-free creative platform where kids turn ideas into real games, apps, and websites — guided by AI tools like Vibe Coding and KidsGPT and reviewed by human moderators. Serving over 500,000 young creators, it pairs game-building templates, AI image and art tools, badge-based learning, and 75+ standards-aligned courses with parent and classroom dashboards, SSO, and safety controls. Originally a maker community for kids, DIY is backed by Kleiner Perkins and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: Eden Network
providers.description: Eden Network is an Ethereum MEV, block-building, and orderflow infrastructure project (EDEN token, launched 2021, evolving from the earlier Archer DAO relay). It operated a gRPC mempool streaming service, an Eden block builder and reverse proxy (eden-geth / eden-proxy), subgraph-backed data tooling, and a DEX API for the Ethereum ecosystem. The original edennetwork.io web property has since lapsed; the canonical, still-live developer surface is the eden-network GitHub organization and the published npm and Go packages. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and enriched from those public sources.

providers.name: Employee Cycle
providers.description: Employee Cycle is an HR analytics and reporting platform that bills itself as "the first Employee Data Platform." It connects a company's HRIS, ATS, payroll, performance, and engagement systems into one place and turns that data into automated, real-time dashboards and reports covering headcount, turnover, tenure, DEI, and other people metrics. The no-code dashboard and report builder lets non-technical HR teams run multi-dimensional workforce analysis without manual spreadsheets, with a claimed one-day implementation. Employee Cycle integrates with 20+ HR systems (ADP, BambooHR, Greenhouse, Lattice, Rippling, UKG, and more) and is aimed at enterprise HR teams, typically at organizations with 500+ employees. The company is SOC 2 compliant (audited by Sensiba San Filippo, monitored by Drata), GDPR and CCPA aligned, and built on the NIST Cybersecurity Framework. It is backed by the Techstars accelerator and venture funding. Employee Cycle offers pre-built data integrations rather than a public developer REST API; this profile tracks the company's identity and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Finaloop
providers.description: Finaloop is a real-time, ecommerce-native bookkeeping and accounting platform for direct-to-consumer (DTC) and multichannel brands. It replaces QuickBooks/Xero, human bookkeepers, and integration tooling with automation plus a team of ecommerce accounting experts, delivering always-current financials. Finaloop continuously syncs sales, returns, fees, reimbursements, inventory movements, COGS, and banking across 60+ ecommerce, marketplace, payment, banking, lending, and 3PL integrations (Shopify, Amazon, TikTok Shop, Walmart, PayPal, Stripe, Chase, ShipBob, and more) to produce real-time P&L, balance sheet, and cash-flow statements, inventory analytics, and tax services. Finaloop exposes no public developer API; its APIs are internal connectors to source platforms, so this profile is identity- and posture-focused rather than spec-bearing.

providers.name: Firstory
providers.description: Firstory is a podcast hosting and monetization platform for creators, holding the leading share of the Mandarin-language podcast market and a growing presence across the Asia-Pacific region with over 14,000 shows. Creators upload an episode once and distribute it to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, KKBOX, YouTube, Amazon Music, Pocket Casts, and more than ten other players, then use AI Studio to auto-generate transcripts, summaries, highlights, and newsletter drafts. Firstory layers on second-by-second analytics, dynamic ad insertion, membership subscriptions, listener donations, cross-promotion, a personal website builder, the Flink universal link, and embeddable players. It does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public surface and infrastructure signals.

providers.name: Forte
providers.description: Forte is a Web3 economic infrastructure company building compliance and economic tools for games and digital-asset economies. Its flagship product is the Forte Rules Engine, a free, open-source, EVM-compatible on-chain policy engine that lets smart-contract developers define composable, adaptive rules (KYC gates, OFAC/sanctions screening, vesting schedules, circuit breakers, and other economic guardrails) without hardcoding logic into their contracts. The Rules Engine ships a TypeScript SDK and Solidity client contracts, and is complemented by a ZK Policy Engine for privacy-preserving policy enforcement. Forte is backed by a16z, Canaan Partners, and Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: GirnarSoft
providers.description: GirnarSoft is an India-based enterprise software engineering and IT services company headquartered in Jaipur, Rajasthan, with a second delivery centre in Gurugram. Founded in 2007 by IIT Delhi alumni Amit and Anurag Jain, it is the technology arm of the CarDekho Group and built the consumer marketplaces CarDekho, BikeDekho, Gaadi, ZigWheels and PriceDekho. The firm sells outsourced product engineering rather than a product API: staff augmentation, dedicated teams and software outsourcing across web and mobile development, QA and test automation, business intelligence, data science, AI/ML, cloud and DevOps, plus AI-augmented engineering pods and agentic-AI automation. It works in banking, insurance, automotive, retail and e-commerce, edtech, SaaS, travel and government/PSU, and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification of its own.

providers.name: Hanover Park
providers.description: Hanover Park is an AI-native ERP and fund administration platform for private market investors, unifying fund accounting, portfolio intelligence, and the LP experience in a single system of record. It pairs a proprietary general ledger, waterfall engine, investor portal, and portfolio management layer with AI agents that read email, propose journal entries, and extract portfolio updates, all reviewed by expert fund accountants. The platform automates capital calls, cash reconciliation, general-ledger posting, KPI collection, and reporting for venture capital, private equity, and other private-market firms. Founded in 2024 and headquartered around a modern back-office thesis, Hanover Park raised a $27M Series A led by Emergence Capital (with Lux Capital and Susa Ventures) and has grown from $1B to $15B in assets under administration. The company is SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certified with a zero-trust, client-isolated AI architecture. No public API or developer program is published at this time; the product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS application.

providers.name: Home From College
providers.description: Home From College (H\FC) is an AI-powered growth platform that connects college students with paid work from consumer brands. Students earn money and build professional experience through microGIGs (quick paid tasks such as app installs, surveys, product feedback, and social sharing with instant payment) and GIGs (larger, ongoing opportunities including content creation, brand-ambassador roles, product testing, and internships), while brands reach and activate Gen Z talent for marketing campaigns. Backed by GV, Home From College runs a two-sided marketplace across a student mobile app and a brand-facing web platform. No public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Hopper
providers.description: Hopper is a travel marketplace and fintech, best known for consumer flight, hotel, car, and homes booking with fintech ancillaries such as Price Freeze, Cancel for Any Reason, and Disruption Assistance for Any Reason. Hopper Technology Solutions (HTS) is the B2B arm that exposes Hopper's e-commerce (Stays, Cars, Packages), fintech ancillaries, loyalty portals, and HTS Assist agentic AI to banks, airlines, and travel providers including Capital One, Air Canada, Virgin Australia, Tripadvisor, Frontier, Wizz Air, and Porter.

providers.name: Innovist
providers.description: Innovist is an Accel-backed, science-backed direct-to-consumer personal care house based in India, building and operating a portfolio of skincare, haircare and suncare brands including Chemist At Play, Bare Anatomy and Sunscoop. It sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-powered online store at innovist.com, offering free delivery and category-wide discounts across skin, hair and sun care. While Innovist does not publish a traditional developer API program, its storefront natively implements agent-facing commerce surfaces: a customer-account OpenID Connect identity layer, a published llms.txt / agents.md for AI shopping assistants, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint that lets approved agents search the catalog, build carts and complete buyer-approved checkouts.

providers.name: Interintellect
providers.description: Interintellect is the world's leading salon platform, a creator-led cultural center for intellectual conversation founded in March 2019 by art philosopher Anna Gat. The platform lets people attend and host high-quality salons and discussions online and offline, across philosophy, technology, poetry, history, and the arts, building community around shared intellectual interests. It supports independent thinkers and hosts through ticket revenue, training, and a peer community, with paid membership tiers granting event access, members-only sessions, community forums, and global in-person gatherings. Interintellect is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; it publishes no public API or developer platform, so this profile carries identity and website-property signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: JMS
providers.description: Java Message Service (JMS), now known as Jakarta Messaging, is a Java API that allows applications to create, send, receive, and read messages. It defines a common enterprise messaging API for loosely coupled, reliable, and asynchronous communication between distributed application components. Current release is Jakarta Messaging 3.1 (Jakarta EE 10).

providers.name: Jobandtalent
providers.description: Jobandtalent is an AI-powered workforce marketplace that connects companies with reliable staff for temporary and permanent roles across logistics, warehousing, manufacturing, retail, and hospitality. Its platform combines a worker-facing mobile app for finding shifts and jobs with an employer-facing business platform for recruitment, shift planning, attendance management, and performance coaching. Founded in Spain and backed by Atomico, Jobandtalent operates across Europe, the US, and Latin America. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer, security, and compliance surface; the company publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: LifeSite
providers.description: LifeSite is a data protection and digital asset company that helps organizations safeguard sensitive information, simplify compliance, and digitally verify ownership. Its Vault product is an encrypted store for personally identifiable, financial, and health information used by both enterprises and families to organize and collaborate on vital documents. TokenX, its Web3 arm, tokenizes real-world assets — critical minerals, carbon credits, and sports and consumer goods — so provenance and ownership can be authenticated without blockchain expertise. A Wellness product covers health, testing, and vaccination tracking for enterprises and events, and a Platform offering exposes LifeSite's building blocks and APIs for partners building tailored data-management applications. LifeSite is sales-led: the Platform APIs are described publicly but no developer portal, API reference, or specification is published, and access is arranged through a demo request.

providers.name: LiveAuctioneers
providers.description: LiveAuctioneers is the world's largest online marketplace for fine art, antiques, jewelry, collectibles, and luxury goods, connecting bidders with thousands of vetted auction houses worldwide. Founded in 2002 and headquartered in New York, it is part of Auction Technology Group (ATG). The platform offers live and timed online bidding, absentee and proxy bids, an auction-results and price-research database, seller consignment services, and an auctioneer partner portal. It is included in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-marketplace company profile surfaced from the Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio; it does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Lord & Taylor
providers.description: Lord & Taylor is one of the oldest American department-store apparel and home-goods retail brands, now operating as a direct-to-consumer online store at lordandtaylor.com. The storefront runs on the Shopify commerce platform, so its public, agent-accessible API surface is the Shopify commerce stack: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect customer authentication (issued via Shopify Customer Accounts) plus two hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers — an unauthenticated Storefront MCP exposing product search, cart, product-detail and store-policy tools, and an OAuth-protected Customer Account MCP exposing order-status, return-request and store-credit tools. Surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched from live discovery documents and MCP tool listings.

providers.name: Menlo Security
providers.description: Menlo Security is a cybersecurity company that secures the enterprise browser, positioning the browser as the point of control for protecting both human users and AI agents. Its cloud-native Secure Enterprise Browser and Menlo Cloud Security Platform apply remote browser isolation to prevent zero-day phishing, ransomware, and malware from ever reaching the endpoint. The platform spans AI agent security and governance, AI Adaptive DLP (data loss prevention), file security for downloads and uploads, zero-trust remote access to private applications, and threat prevention. Menlo Security is headquartered in Mountain View, California and is backed by investors including General Catalyst, Vista Equity Partners, JPMorgan, American Express Ventures, and HSBC. Menlo does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface; administration is handled through its cloud console and a customer support portal.

providers.name: Mirage JS
providers.description: Mirage JS is an open source API mocking library for JavaScript that lets you build, test, and share complete frontend features without depending on a backend. It runs alongside your frontend code as in-browser middleware, providing a built-in database, factories for seeding data, route handlers, and serializers. It is framework-agnostic and works with React, Vue, Angular, Ember, and any modern test runner. Mirage JS is itself a library (not a hosted REST API), so this entry indexes its documentation and project resources.

providers.name: Napatech
providers.description: Napatech is a Danish provider of programmable FPGA-based SmartNICs and network-acceleration hardware used for high-speed network monitoring, cybersecurity, and telecom/5G workloads. Its Link-Capture and Link-Inline software, together with the NTAPI/NTPL developer SDK, let applications capture, filter, and process network traffic at line rate with zero packet loss. The developer surface is a C/C++ hardware SDK (NTAPI) plus the NTPL programming language rather than a web/REST API; integrations ship as open-source additions to DPDK, VPP, Open vSwitch, Scapy, and Zeek via the napatech GitHub organization. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Native Security
providers.description: Native Security is a cloud security control plane that unifies security posture and enforcement across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and OCI. The platform translates security intent expressed in natural language into enforceable architectural controls, shifting teams from reactive detection toward proactive, secure-by-design defense using built-in cloud security primitives. Capabilities include multi-cloud policy enforcement from a single definition, automated organization topology discovery and mapping, architectural segmentation and perimeter enforcement, AI-agent guardrails through architectural boundaries, and compliance automation with audit readiness. Native Security is backed by General Catalyst. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; product documentation and the application console sit behind authentication.

providers.name: Nomi Health
providers.description: Nomi Health is a Utah-based direct healthcare and healthcare fintech company founded in 2019 that operates a payments, claims and analytics platform for self-funded employers, health plans, brokers and providers. Its stack spans real-time provider payments and claims adjudication (Healthcare Financial Services), directly contracted provider networks (Direct Network / Open Network), benefits-data analytics through Artemis by Nomi Health, and direct patient care services. Nomi Health operates authenticated web portals for providers, members and employers, but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Own (OwnBackup)
providers.description: Own (formerly OwnBackup, now Own from Salesforce) is a SaaS data protection platform that provides backup, recovery, archiving, sandbox seeding, and data security and compliance for cloud applications including Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, and ServiceNow. Founded in 2015 and acquired by Salesforce in 2024, Own helps organizations protect and manage the data held in their business-critical SaaS systems against loss, corruption, and compliance risk. Own is delivered as a managed product rather than a public developer API platform: it operates a public system status page and a trust center listing its security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001/27701, FedRAMP, HDS, GDPR, HIPAA/HITECH) and a published vulnerability disclosure policy, but does not currently publish an open, self-serve REST/OpenAPI developer surface.

providers.name: Pasito
providers.description: Pasito is an AI-native workspace for employee benefits that helps benefits consultants, insurance carriers, and employers simplify every part of the benefits journey — from proposal and quoting through enrollment to year-round employee engagement — using agentic AI workflows. The platform turns unstructured plan documents and census data into a structured data layer that powers a conversational AI benefits assistant, automated proposal/RFP intake, benefits guides and microsites, decision support, and communications. Pasito reports supporting over 6.6 million employees, managing $106B in premiums, and serving 3,600+ employers, integrating with 950+ TPA systems and 260+ HRIS platforms. Backed by Google, Y Combinator, and Core Innovation Capital, the company is building a public-facing API but does not yet publish a developer portal, documentation, or API reference.

providers.name: People Ai
providers.description: People.ai is an AI-powered revenue intelligence platform for sales leaders, RevOps, and CROs, now operating under the Backstory brand (people.ai redirects to backstory.ai). The platform automatically captures customer-facing activity (emails, meetings, calls, chats) from existing tools such as Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, Gmail, Outlook, Zoom, Teams, and Slack, then analyzes that activity against deal history to answer which deals are real, which are at risk, and what to do next. Core capabilities include deal-risk identification, pipeline visibility and touchpoint mapping, revenue forecasting validation, and automated CRM hygiene. People.ai is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface; integrations are delivered as managed native connectors rather than a documented public API.

providers.name: PickTrace
providers.description: PickTrace is an agricultural workforce and harvest management SaaS platform for large-scale farms, founded by brothers Austin and Harrison Steed and a Y Combinator (Summer 2015) alumnus headquartered in Glendale, California. The platform captures time-and-attendance, piecework, productivity, onboarding, payroll, and receiving data in the field, office, and packinghouse, giving growers real-time visibility across their entire workforce year-round. It is used daily by tens of thousands of farm workers at some of the largest berry, citrus, and apple growers in the United States, Mexico, Peru, Chile, and Australia. PickTrace exposes a RESTful API that lets customers and third-party developers create, update, and extract objects from all PickTrace tools and bi-directionally sync labor data into and out of the platform for automation, payroll efficiency, and audit-ready compliance.

providers.name: Runsybil
providers.description: RunSybil is an AI-native autonomous offensive security platform. Sybil — a system of AI agents — continuously penetration tests live applications and infrastructure, finding, exploiting, and validating real vulnerabilities without a human in the loop. It tests live applications black-box by default (no source code required), integrates with GitHub and GitLab to trigger targeted change testing on every code push, and validates every finding through a multi-agent pipeline before it surfaces, aiming to eliminate triage and false positives. RunSybil positions as a replacement for point-in-time penetration testing, legacy DAST/SAST scanners, and bug bounty programs, and also offers white-box testing for deeper codebase exploration. Founded in 2023 by Ari Herbert-Voss (OpenAI's first security hire) and Vlad Ionescu (Offensive Security Tech Lead at Meta), the company raised $40M led by Khosla Ventures and is trusted by security teams at Notion, Cursor, Turbopuffer, Baseten, and Thinking Machines Lab. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface is published at this time.

providers.name: Rupa Health
providers.description: Rupa Health (now a Fullscript company) is a healthcare platform that lets functional and root-cause medicine practitioners order, track, and receive results from specialty and functional lab tests across hundreds of lab companies through a single unified dashboard. It provides a lab test catalog, patient result portals, practitioner ordering and billing, phlebotomy coordination, and educational resources (Rupa University, the Root Cause Medicine podcast, and a lab reference guide). Rupa integrates with a range of EHR/EMR systems used by independent practitioners but does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at this time. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: SAP America
