The platform pairs a community of hundreds of thousands of vetted candidates with thousands of companies through job matching, curated talent search, and managed hiring services such as pay-per-hire and access plans. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, The Mom Project operates a consumer/employer web product and consumes third-party APIs (for example a Docusign eSignature integration for hiring workflows) but does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API surface of its own.

providers.name: TourAmigo
providers.description: Tour Amigo is a cloud-based booking and operations platform for multi-day tour operators, destination management companies (DMCs), and river and expedition cruise operators. The platform covers itinerary building, supplier and contract management, direct online selling, agent and customer portals, financial management with native Xero integration, and an API-powered channel manager that distributes tours to partners such as GetYourGuide, TourRadar, and Tourhub. Backed by 500 Global, with core markets in Australia, New Zealand, and Europe.

providers.name: Upwage
providers.description: Upwage is an AI interview platform that helps employers hire faster and more fairly with lower turnover. Its emotionally intelligent AI interviewer conducts 24/7 multilingual candidate screening, scoring competencies consistently to reduce bias in high-volume hiring across retail, healthcare, logistics, and staffing, with ATS integrations including Ashby, Greenhouse, iCIMS, Lever, SmartRecruiters, and Workday. Founded by Diana Tsai and Greg Call and backed by Bloomberg Beta, Upwage publishes a SOC 2 Type 2 trust center with third-party bias audits, but no public developer API surface yet.

providers.name: Verdant
providers.description: Verdant is an AI-native land-use permitting and planning software platform for local governments, spanning the entire process from a resident's first question through plan review to a commission's final vote. Applicants file complete, compliant applications upfront, and Verdant's AI reads documents, site plans, and diagrams to flag issues and draft staff review reports that municipal staff can approve. The platform is modular, letting jurisdictions buy only the modules they need, configured to their ordinances, workflows, and forms, and includes ordinance-research tooling to benchmark against peer jurisdictions and find gaps in local codes. Verdant is a Y Combinator Summer 2026 company; it currently ships an application product for cities and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: VWR International (Avantor)
providers.description: VWR International, now part of Avantor, is a global distributor of laboratory supplies, chemicals, equipment, and services for the life sciences, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and research industries. With over 180 years of history, VWR serves more than one million customers in over 30 countries. The company operates as Avantor's distribution and procurement platform, providing laboratory consumables, reagents, instruments, and cold chain solutions. VWR/Avantor offers e-procurement integrations and eProcurement APIs to support laboratory supply chain automation for enterprise customers through EDI, OCI/PunchOut, and catalog integration.

providers.name: Wave AI
providers.description: Wave AI (WaveAI) is a Sunnyvale, California AI music company founded in 2017 by David Loker, Dr. Maya Ackerman, and Chris Cassion, building foundational generative AI models for music and songwriting. Its flagship product LyricStudio is an AI-powered lyric-writing assistant used by millions of artists and creators to generate genre- and topic-aware lyrical suggestions, rhymes, and full songs, and MelodyStudio adds generative vocal-melody and chord generation. The company is backed by 500 Global, Horizon 3 Venture Capital, Kilowatt Capital, and angel investors. Wave AI ships consumer web applications rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity and public web properties. Added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with a domain-security probe and verified public link properties.

providers.name: WorkForce Software
providers.description: WorkForce Software, an ADP company since October 2024, makes the WorkForce Suite, an enterprise workforce management platform covering time and attendance, employee scheduling, absence and leave management, labor forecasting, data capture, and payroll compliance for large, complex organizations. The Suite integrates with leading HCM and ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, Workday, ADP) via RESTful APIs, SOAP APIs, and file-based interfaces, with SSO/SLO and MFA support; API and integration documentation is provided to customers through the WorkForce Software community portal rather than a public developer portal.

providers.name: 3PAR (HPE 3PAR StoreServ)
providers.description: 3PAR is an enterprise storage platform, now part of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE acquired 3PAR in 2010), that powers mission-critical applications with HPE 3PAR StoreServ and Primera arrays. For developers and automation engineers, 3PAR exposes the HPE 3PAR Web Services API (WSAPI) — a REST interface that manages storage provisioning, virtual volumes, hosts, ports, CPGs, snapshots, and remote copy on 3PAR/Primera/Alletra arrays, offering a more flexible and programmable alternative to the 3PAR Command Line Interface. HPE publishes first-party client libraries (Python, Ruby, PowerShell) plus Ansible, Puppet, Chef, OpenStack Cinder, and Docker volume integrations against WSAPI. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead (Mayfield, Menlo Ventures backed the original 3PAR before its IPO and HP acquisition) and enriched from HPE's public developer surface.

providers.name: Ampere Computing
providers.description: Ampere Computing is a Santa Clara, California semiconductor company founded in 2018 by Renee James and now part of the SoftBank Group. It designs Arm-based Cloud Native Processors — the Ampere Altra and Altra Max families (up to 128 cores) and the flagship AmpereOne family (up to 192 single-threaded cores) — for cloud, AI inference and edge deployments. Alongside the silicon it ships a software stack: Ampere Optimized AI frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX Runtime, llama.cpp, Ollama) distributed as first-party container images, tuned GCC/glibc/binutils builds, performance and porting tooling, and an arm64 developer community. Ampere publishes no public developer API — its developer program is a hardware, tooling and porting program rather than an API program.

providers.name: Arrcus
providers.description: Arrcus is an AI-native networking software company that builds policy-driven routing, switching, and AI fabric spanning the edge, datacenter, and cloud. Its flagship ArcOS network operating system runs on merchant-silicon hardware and is complemented by ArcRR (scale-out route reflector), ArcIQ (analytics and visibility), ACE / ACE-AI (the Arrcus Connected Edge control and AI-networking platform), AINF (Arrcus Inference Network Fabric), and the TGAX AI switch. Arrcus targets GPU cluster connectivity for AI training and low-latency inferencing networks that reduce token cost. The company is venture backed by General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It exposes a login-gated customer portal and academy rather than a public developer API; no public OpenAPI, SDKs, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Balloon
providers.description: Balloon is a research-backed team collaboration and decision-making platform built to eliminate groupthink and give quieter voices a psychologically safe way to contribute. Its core workflow, called a "flight," is a two-stage, partly anonymous process in which a leader poses a question, team members submit ideas ("balloons") and discuss them, and the group then evaluates and "pumps" the strongest ideas on merit, surfacing a Balloon Score that shows consensus and buy-in. Balloon ships 150+ expert-authored flight templates across 25 business areas and supports asynchronous, time-zone-independent participation, positioning itself as a replacement for status and ideation meetings (the company cites a 70% reduction in meeting time and that ~80% of information shared is new to the organization). Founded by Amanda Greenberg and Noah Bornstein, Balloon is backed by 500 Global and other investors, with an advisory board including Adam Grant, Amy Edmondson, and Daniel Pink. It is a SaaS web application (app at balloon.app) with no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: BevSpot
providers.description: BevSpot is a Boston-based food and beverage inventory management platform for restaurants, bars, and hospitality groups. The web application streamlines back-of-house operations including inventory counting, ordering, invoice management, recipe and menu costing, and sales-driven analytics. BevSpot ingests point-of-sale data through integrations with more than a dozen POS systems (Toast, Square, Clover, Lightspeed, SpotOn, NCR Aloha, Upserve, Brink, Lavu, and others), plus accounting and vendor connections (QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics GP, Ottimate, Fintech, US Foods, Sysco). It is a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures. BevSpot does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, commercial, and security surface.

providers.name: BrightInsight
providers.description: BrightInsight is a regulated digital health platform for biopharma and medtech. Its cloud-based, microservices platform captures, transmits and analyzes data from CE-marked and FDA-regulated medical devices, combination products, apps and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) in compliance with global security, privacy and regulatory requirements. The platform integrates with 400+ medical devices across 50+ manufacturers, connects to EHRs in 500+ U.S. provider networks, and is available in 48 countries. Founded in 2017 (formerly Flex Digital Health) and based in Alviso, California, BrightInsight is used by top biopharma and medtech companies to build and launch commercial regulated digital health solutions. It is a sales-led enterprise platform with no public developer portal or public API; integration is delivered under managed engagements.

providers.name: Distyl
providers.description: Distyl is an applied-AI company architecting the AI-native enterprise. Rather than layering automation onto broken processes, Distyl reimagines enterprise operations from the ground up with AI at the core, partnering with Fortune 500 organizations across Telecom, Healthcare, Manufacturing, Insurance, Retail, and Financial Services to design and operationalize AI transformations and deploy production-grade agentic AI systems in weeks. Its product suite includes Weave, Distillery, Context Mesh, Context Views, Journey, Personalization, and Apprentice. Founded by operators and researchers from Palantir, CIA, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Tesla, NASA, Stanford, and MIT, and backed by Coatue, OpenAI, Lightspeed, Microsoft, and Khosla Ventures. Distyl is a services/platform company with no public developer API; this profile captures its published web surface. Distyl is SOC 2 certified and GDPR compliant.

providers.name: Dtexsystems
providers.description: DTEX Systems (DTEX) is a cybersecurity company delivering a risk-adaptive insider risk management platform. Its DTEX InTERCEPT product and Platform v7 unify insider threat detection, data loss prevention (DLP), user activity monitoring (UAM), and AI/agentic risk governance through behavioral intelligence rather than intrusive content inspection. The platform correlates human behavior across endpoints to surface early-warning indicators along the insider threat kill chain, uses OCSF-aligned connectors and standardized schemas to export enriched telemetry to SIEM, SOAR, and ITSM tooling, and ships agentic defenders (Triage Guardian and Threat Hunter) to automate investigations. DTEX is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and serves enterprise and government customers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network; no public developer program, OpenAPI, or self-serve API documentation is currently published — integration is via the enterprise platform and OCSF connectors.

providers.name: Fhenix
providers.description: Fhenix is a blockchain R&D company building confidential computing for EVM-compatible chains using Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE). Its CoFHE (FHE Coprocessor) lets Solidity smart contracts compute directly on encrypted data — encrypt inputs client-side, operate on ciphertexts on-chain via the FHE.sol Solidity libraries, and unseal results through a threshold decryption network, so sensitive state stays private without ever being decrypted on-chain. The developer stack is a smart-contract-plus-client-library surface (not a REST API): the cofhejs TypeScript SDK, Hardhat/Foundry plugins and starters, the fhenix-contracts Solidity libraries, and mock contracts for local testing. CoFHE is live on public testnets (Ethereum Sepolia, Arbitrum Sepolia, Base Sepolia) with mainnet planned. Fhenix is backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: FineDine
providers.description: FineDine is an AI-powered restaurant growth platform that helps restaurants increase revenue through digital menus (QR code, tablet, and web), online and in-venue ordering, reservations, a lite point-of-sale, CRM and loyalty programs, menu-engineering and pricing analytics, and an AI business agent (FineDine IQ). It markets to restaurants and hospitality operators with tiered SaaS pricing (Starter, Growth, Premium). As of this API Evangelist profiling, FineDine publishes no public developer API, SDKs, webhooks, CLI, MCP server, or OpenAPI specification — this profile captures its public commercial and content surface. FineDine is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Flightfox
providers.description: Flightfox is a managed travel platform for complex group travel, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado. It helps educational institutions, humanitarian and faith-based organizations, and corporate teams book and manage flights, hotels, and ground travel through a combination of self-serve booking software and 24/7 human travel-agent support. Flightfox emphasizes lowest-fare guarantees, bulk and group booking discounts, real-time flight tracking and travel alerts, branded booking pages, and custom reporting including CO2 emissions and flight manifests. The company was originally a Y Combinator and a16z-backed crowdsourced flight-search marketplace and has since pivoted to full-service managed group travel. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: General Legal
providers.description: General Legal is an AI-native law firm for high-growth startups and SMBs, offering flat-fee commercial, corporate, and employment legal work delivered by U.S.-barred attorneys augmented with proprietary AI workflows. The firm focuses on contract review, redlining, negotiation, and drafting with transparent flat pricing (from $250) and fast turnaround (median under three hours), positioning itself as "outside counsel that scales like software." Practice areas include technology transactions, employment, data privacy, financial regulatory, blockchain/cryptocurrency, and emerging companies / VC. Founded in 2026 by Ryan Walker (ex-Casetext CTO), J.P. Mohler, and Javed Qadruddin, the company is a Y Combinator (W26) portfolio company that raised $11.5M across pre-seed and seed rounds. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from public sources; General Legal is a legal-services company and does not currently publish a developer API.

providers.name: GORGIE
providers.description: GORGIE is a direct-to-consumer beverage brand making a sparkling, zero-sugar energy drink with functional benefits from green tea, natural flavors, Biotin, B Vitamins, and L-Theanine — only 5 calories, no preservatives. Built by a women-led team on a mission to make wellness fun, GORGIE sells its variety of flavors through a Shopify-powered online store at getgorgie.com and on retail shelves including Target, supported by a store locator, wholesale program, and an Instagram/TikTok community. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of ggv-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer packaged goods brand it exposes an ecommerce storefront and customer-account surface rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: HostnFly
providers.description: HostnFly is a French short-term-rental (Airbnb) concierge and property-management company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Paris. It manages the full lifecycle of short-stay rentals on behalf of property owners: listing creation and optimization, multi-platform distribution (Airbnb, Booking.com, Abritel), guest screening and 24/7 communication, check-in/check-out and key handling, hotel-grade housekeeping and linen, maintenance, short-term-rental insurance, and dynamic revenue optimization. HostnFly operates on a commission-only model (from ~20% of nightly revenue, no fixed fees) and covers 340+ cities across metropolitan France and Corsica. It is a Partech portfolio company. HostnFly publishes an llms.txt agent-discovery file but does not expose a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: IBM App Connect
providers.description: IBM App Connect is an integration platform that enables organizations to connect applications, data, and services across cloud and on-premises environments. It provides low-code integration capabilities with pre-built connectors and a flow editor for building integration flows.

providers.name: IKI AI
providers.description: IKI AI is an AI-native workspace for knowledge, research, strategy, and creative work, backed by 500 Global. It pairs an AI assistant that summarizes, highlights, and connects saved content with an AI editor that grounds writing in a user's personal knowledge base, plus shared Team Spaces and a browser extension for one-click webpage saving with notes. The product targets researchers, students, consultants, copywriters, coaches, lawyers, founders, and venture teams, and emphasizes privacy with a choice of top-tier LLMs. IKI AI is delivered as a consumer and team SaaS (web app at app.iki.ai and a Chrome extension) with subscription plans; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI. This profile tracks its public identity, commercial, and security surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Jetstream
providers.description: Jetstream (jetstream.security) is a security-first AI governance platform for enterprises, backed by Redpoint Ventures. It helps organizations discover, control, and monitor AI systems at scale across five capabilities: AI Visibility (discovering and inventorying AI agents, models, tools, and workflows across environments), AI Design Control (documenting how agentic systems are assembled), Agentic Identity (binding human and AI identities to responsible owners), Runtime Governance (enforcing real-time behavioral compliance against approved designs), and AI FinOps Accountability (tracking usage and spend by model, agent, and workflow). The company positions governance as an accelerator for AI adoption, addressing shadow AI, cost control, accountability, and compliance. No public API, SDK, CLI, or developer portal is published as of this profile; the company pursues SOC 2, FedRAMP High, and DoD IL5 compliance.

providers.name: Keep Financial
providers.description: Keep Financial Technologies, Inc. is a compensation technology company that provides a vesting cash bonus platform. Employers deliver upfront cash to employees that is earned (vests) over a customizable time period with a legally enforceable right to repayment, automating signing bonuses, retention bonuses, annual and performance bonuses, spot bonuses, tuition reimbursement, M&A retention packages, and severance. The platform serves compensation, HR, finance, legal, and executive leaders across healthcare, construction, logistics, technology, retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and other industries. Keep Financial was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; it operates a SaaS web application and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Kitterly
providers.description: Kitterly, Inc. was a direct-to-consumer craft commerce startup that sold knitting and crochet kits, yarn, needles and notions online, and ran a monthly Kit Club subscription that shipped members a pattern plus the yarn required to complete it. Kitterly was backed by 500 Global (500 Startups) along with Manatt Ventures and the Jordan x 2080 accelerator. The company was later consolidated under the Cotton Cuts brand, a Chesterfield, Missouri based quilting fabric shop selling designer die-cut and pre-cut fabric, threads, patterns and notions, plus quilting memberships and the Puzzle Mystery Quilt program, serving roughly 4,000 members across more than 15 countries. The kitterly.com domain now redirects to cottoncuts.com. The business is a consumer retail and subscription commerce operation running on a hosted e-commerce platform, and it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: KOHO
providers.description: KOHO is a Canadian financial-technology company (neobank) founded in 2014 by Daniel Eberhard and headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, serving more than 2.5 million Canadians through a mobile-first money app. KOHO is not a chartered bank; it issues a KOHO Mastercard prepaid card through KOHO Financial Inc. and places customer balances in trust with CDIC-member institutions (its longstanding banking partner is Peoples Trust Company), while offering high-interest savings, cash back, credit building, Cover cash advances, and Pay Later. The company is in the final stages of pursuing a federal Schedule I banking licence, which would make it one of Canada's first new federally regulated banks in decades, and in May 2026 it joined the Interac e-Transfer network directly as a Participant under the broadened access for Payment Service Providers. On the open-finance front, KOHO exposes no first-party public developer API or portal; consumer account and transaction data access today is available only through third-party aggregators (Plaid and Flinks), consistent with Canada's voluntary, not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework.

providers.name: Liquidly
providers.description: Liquidly (Liquidly, Inc.) is a New York based financial technology company building infrastructure for illiquid assets — a permission-based secondary marketplace that lets holders of private fund interests transact without disrupting the fund. The platform serves three sides: fund managers, who get a streamlined and centrally supervised transfer process, market data, and the flexibility to structure longer lock-up vehicles; seller investors, who get a manager-approved selling process, access to a network of prospective buyers, and standardized commercial terms; and buyer investors, who get manager-granted asset permissions, standardized diligence materials, and technology-enabled execution. Liquidly targets the secondary market for the roughly $13.1 trillion invested in private funds across buyouts, venture capital, real estate, private debt, infrastructure, and growth. Broker-dealer services are offered through Liquidly IAS, LLC, registered with FINRA and a member of SIPC. Liquidly is backed by Anthemis, Portage Ventures, Village Global, and AmTrust Financial. As of this enrichment pass Liquidly publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation; the product is reached through an authenticated web application.

providers.name: Meisterwerk
providers.description: Meisterwerk is a modular all-in-one SaaS platform for German-speaking (DACH) trades and craft businesses (Handwerk), built by MEISTERWERK APP GmbH in Berlin. It gives small and medium craft firms (1-50 employees) a single operating system for job and resource scheduling (Einsatzplanung), a native mobile app for iOS, Android and Windows, chronological job documentation with photos and chat, quoting and invoicing with e-invoice support, EU-compliant mobile time tracking with GPS, digital forms and signatures, absence/holiday planning, and configurable workflows. AI features (planning assistant, speech-to-text documentation and time entry, and the standalone "Frag Maxi" phone assistant) are built in. It integrates with lexoffice, sevdesk, bexio and orgaMAX accounting software; a public open interface (Offene Schnittstelle) is announced but not yet publicly documented. Over 8,000 active users; data is hosted on servers in Germany and the platform is GDPR (DSGVO) compliant.

providers.name: Metra
providers.description: Metra provides GTFS API data for the Metra commuter rail system in the Chicago metropolitan area. The API is hosted at gtfsapi.metrarail.com and provides both RAW data and JSON for schedules, trips, stops, and real-time updates.

providers.name: Milo Credit
providers.description: Milo (formerly Milo Credit) is a Miami-based financial technology company and licensed mortgage lender that pioneered crypto-backed lending. Milo lets cryptocurrency holders access cash or finance U.S. real estate without selling their digital assets, offering crypto-backed mortgages with up to 100% financing, self-custody mortgages, and crypto-backed loans funded in as little as 24 hours, with rates starting around 7%. The company was an early portfolio investment of QED Investors and operates as a consumer-facing lending platform rather than a developer/API-first company. As of this enrichment pass Milo publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; its public surface is a consumer web application (app.milo.io), a marketing site, a blog, an FAQ, and a hosted trust/security center. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Novoic
providers.description: Novoic is a London-based clinical AI company building speech biomarkers for the early detection of Alzheimer's disease and cognitive impairment. Its technology analyzes how people speak - acoustic and linguistic patterns - to screen for subtle cognitive change in about ten minutes on any smart device. Products include Storyteller (automated, browser-based speech-based cognitive testing), Dashboard (an enterprise platform for running screening programs across sites with AI-assisted triage and analytics), and a Speech API for direct access to their speech processing, automated speech recognition, quality control, and speech-biomarker models. Novoic is deployed across 50+ medical institutions, partners with the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, and emphasizes HIPAA/GDPR compliance. It also publishes two open-source feature-extraction libraries, surfboard (audio) and blabla (linguistics).

providers.name: OZON.ru
providers.description: OZON is one of Russia's largest e-commerce marketplaces, offering retail across electronics, apparel, groceries, and more, plus its own logistics and fulfillment network (FBO/FBS). For developers, OZON exposes the OZON Seller API, a POST-based RPC-over-HTTP JSON API at https://api-seller.ozon.ru that lets marketplace sellers manage products, prices, stock, warehouses, orders, returns, analytics, and finances programmatically. Authentication uses two headers, a numeric Client-Id and a secret Api-Key issued in the seller cabinet. OZON was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from live probes of its API host and public developer documentation.

providers.name: Pepper Content
providers.description: Pepper (formerly Pepper Content, peppercontent.io, now pepper.inc) is a content-led growth platform that combines content strategy, AI technology, and a network of subject-matter-expert creators to help brands build predictable organic growth across search (SEO), generative-engine optimization (GEO), social, and creative. Its offerings span SEO/GEO visibility, expert-produced content (ebooks, whitepapers, blogs, thought leadership), creative and video production, and agentic AI workflows that automate content operations. The company reports serving 2,500+ brands including Amazon, Google, Atlassian, and HSBC. It is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Pepper runs a real first-party API gateway at hub.peppercontent.io (Kong 3.6.1) fronting a pepper-editor-service, a user-service and an atlas-service, and its openapi.json route exists but answers 401 "Session Expired" to anyone without a product session — so the contract is gated, not absent. Pepper publishes no developer portal, no documentation, no SDK, no pricing and no /.well-known discovery document; the only publicly documented integration surface is a single Zapier trigger, and access is granted through a sales demo.

providers.name: Phind
providers.description: Phind was an AI answer engine and coding assistant built for developers, offering conversational, multi-step technical search on the web and through a VS Code extension. Founded in 2022 by Michael Royzen and Justin Wei (Y Combinator S22), Phind trained its own code models and briefly held the top-ranked open-source coding model on Hugging Face. The phind.com product was a consumer/subscription service and never shipped an official public or partner developer API - the only genuinely public developer artifacts were its open-weight models on Hugging Face (Phind-CodeLlama-34B v1/v2, Python-v1, and later Phind-70B). Community "Phind API" projects on GitHub and RapidAPI are unofficial reverse-engineered wrappers, not an official interface. Phind shut down on January 16, 2026; Pro subscribers received prorated refunds and could export chat history through January 30, 2026 before servers were wiped. This entry is a historical record; API surfaces are modeled, not officially documented.

providers.name: PostgreSQL
providers.description: PostgreSQL is a powerful, open-source object-relational database system with over 35 years of active development. It provides advanced SQL compliance, ACID transactions, and extensibility. PostgreSQL exposes a binary wire protocol via libpq and language bindings rather than a public HTTP REST API, so there is no canonical OpenAPI specification. HTTP access is typically layered on top via PostgREST, Hasura, or application code.

providers.name: Prudential plc
providers.description: Prudential plc is a life and health insurance and asset management group incorporated in England and Wales and listed on the London, Hong Kong, Singapore and New York exchanges, with its principal operating office in Hong Kong and roots in London going back to 1848. Its home market for this profile is the United Kingdom, but its book is almost entirely Asian and African: life protection, health and medical, savings and retirement, takaful, pensions and Hong Kong Mandatory Provident Funds, plus asset management under the Eastspring brand, across Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Taiwan, India, mainland China, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and a dozen African markets including Kenya, Uganda, Ghana, Nigeria and Zambia. It is no longer a UK retail insurer at all - the UK and Europe business was demerged as M&G plc in 2019 and the US business as Jackson Financial in 2021 - so the familiar UK "Pru" brands at pru.co.uk belong to M&G, not to this company. Its API posture is that there is no public API posture. Prudential plc publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger document and no partner integration surface of any kind: developer, developers, docs, api, apis, partners, portal and sandbox subdomains of prudentialplc.com all fail to resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer, /partners and /integrations on the corporate site all return HTTP 404. The group's stated technology strategy is inward-facing - AI, automation, cloud and a global AI Lab running over a hundred internal use cases - and its distribution is built on tied agency forces and exclusive bancassurance partnerships with banks such as Standard Chartered, CIMB, MSB, SeABank, Bank Syariah Indonesia and UOB, which are commercial and contractual relationships rather than published API programmes. The Pulse by Prudential health and wealth app onboards health-tech and wealth-tech partners (Babylon, Tictrac, Halodoc, Smarter Health, Prive Technologies, OVO, Google Cloud) but every announcement describes the arrangement in commercial terms and none exposes a developer programme, SDK or public API. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference was found anywhere in Prudential plc's public estate. Recorded honestly as a large carrier with a fully partner-gated, non-public integration surface. One genuine machine-readable surface does exist, and it is not an API: six of the group's market operating companies - Prudential Hong Kong, Prudential Singapore, Prudential Indonesia, Prudential Vietnam, Pru Life UK in the Philippines and Prudential BSN Takaful in Malaysia - publish real first-party llms.txt documents for grounding large language models, with Prudential Vietnam declaring a per-user-agent bot access policy for gptbot, claudebot, google-extended, perplexitybot and six other crawlers. The corporate domain publishes none. Underneath that, the group runs a visibly centralised security posture: TLS 1.3 and HSTS on every market host, and one shared PowerDMARC/PowerSPF tenant with a common aggregate-report mailbox across all seven domains, at p=reject on the corporate domain and p=quarantine in the markets, with no CAA record anywhere.

providers.name: Rainwalk Technology
providers.description: Rainwalk Technology is a white-label, embedded pet insurance provider founded in 2018 and based in Columbia, South Carolina. Rainwalk lets partners such as shelters, breeders, veterinary practices, and consumer platforms launch and distribute accident-and-illness pet insurance directly at the point of sale through its APIs and hosted quoting/enrollment flows, keeping partners in control of the customer experience. Coverage includes accidents, illnesses, diagnostics, surgery, and medications, with hassle-free reimbursements and free virtual vet consultations. The company operates a partner/embedded API surface (api.rainwalk.io) plus hosted quoting, insured, and agent portals, and is backed by Techstars Ventures, ManchesterStory, Insurtech Gateway, Bridge Capital, and Seaplane Ventures. Rainwalk was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched via the pipeline.

providers.name: Roadsurfer
providers.description: Roadsurfer is a Munich-based camper van, motorhome, and RV travel company founded in 2016, operating a fleet of 10,000+ vehicles across 100+ pick-up/drop-off locations in 16 countries in Europe and North America. Beyond flexible RV rentals it offers RV subscriptions, RV sales, one-way "Rallies," and roadsurfer Spots, a network of 10,000+ hand-picked European campsites. Roadsurfer is a consumer-facing brand with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and published llms.txt for the API Evangelist network. Backed by HV Capital.

providers.name: Roper Technologies
providers.description: Roper Technologies is a diversified technology holding company (NASDAQ: ROP) that acquires, manages, and develops niche market-leading software and technology-enabled businesses. Over three-quarters of revenue comes from software products across three segments: Application Software (legal, healthcare, government, education, and insurance vertical SaaS), Network Software (construction, transportation, and insurance network platforms), and Technology Enabled Products (medical devices, industrial, and RF identification). Key subsidiaries include Aderant (legal software), Clinisys (laboratory informatics), Deltek (project-based business ERP), Frontline Education (K-12 HR software), Vertafore (insurance technology), IntelliTrans (supply chain visibility), ConstructConnect (construction information), DAT Solutions (freight matching), and iPipeline (life insurance SaaS).

providers.name: SafeGraph
providers.description: SafeGraph is a geospatial data company that builds and maintains high-quality Point of Interest (POI), building geometry, and geocoded address datasets used for location intelligence, site selection, competitive analysis, and machine-learning models. Its core products are Places (millions of POIs with base, rich, and premium attributes), Geometry (building-footprint polygons), Address (structured geocoded addresses across 25+ countries), and Spend (transaction data). Rather than a hosted REST API, SafeGraph delivers data as bulk parquet files via S3, Snowflake, AWS Data Exchange, CARTO, Databricks, and ArcGIS. Surfaced originally as a Sapphire Ventures portfolio company and enriched here from SafeGraph's public documentation, changelog, and packages.

providers.name: ScreenPoint Medical
providers.description: ScreenPoint Medical is a Netherlands-based healthcare AI company, founded in 2014 by Professor Nico Karssemeijer and Professor Sir Michael Brady, that develops Transpara Breast AI for earlier detection of breast cancer in 2D (FFDM) and 3D (DBT) mammography. Transpara is vendor-agnostic, integrates into PACS and reading workflows via medical-imaging (DICOM) pipelines rather than a public developer API, and is FDA cleared (K241831, K232096) and CE marked (0344). The product is used in over 200 clinics across 25+ countries and is backed by three randomized controlled trials (including MASAI in The Lancet). The company is backed by Insight Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline: no public developer/API surface exists, but real security-disclosure and compliance posture were captured.

providers.name: Securiti
providers.description: Securiti is a San Jose, California data security, privacy, and AI governance company that markets the Data Command Center, a unified hybrid multicloud platform for sensitive data discovery, classification, security posture management, privacy operations, and AI governance. The platform is built on the Data Command Graph, a knowledge-graph layer that correlates data assets, identities, regulations, and AI systems across 1,000+ pre-built connectors spanning AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Snowflake, Databricks, and major SaaS applications. Securiti's product surface includes Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), Sensitive Data Intelligence, Data Access Intelligence, Data Flow Governance, Data Minimization, Breach Impact Analysis, Data Subject Request (DSR) Automation, Universal Consent Management, Mobile App Consent SDKs, Assessment Automation, Data Mapping, Privacy Center, the People Data Graph, Data Catalog, Data Lineage, Data Quality, Compliance Management, AI Security and Governance, Agent Commander for AI risk detection, Security for AI Agents and Copilots, and the Gencore AI suite for safe enterprise AI copilots, vector-database synchronization, unstructured data curation, and context-aware LLM firewalls. The platform exposes REST-based APIs, a turnkey JavaScript consent library, standards-based webhook interfaces, no-code/low-code workflow integrations, and native mobile SDKs for iOS and Android consent capture. The API reference, SDKs, consent banner generators, and connector catalog are all reached through the Securiti app and Privacy Center; full API documentation requires an authenticated tenant. Securiti was founded in 2018 by Rehan Jalil and has been recognized as a Gartner Customers' Choice and an IDC Worldwide Leader in data privacy and data security. The company's revenue model is enterprise SaaS subscription with usage-based connector and module pricing; no public free tier or self-serve API key issuance is currently offered.

providers.name: Sweep
providers.description: Sweep is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed company (originally launched as "Sweep — AI-powered junior developer") that has pivoted from being a GitHub App which turned issues into pull requests into an AI coding assistant delivered primarily as a JetBrains IDE plugin, with autocomplete-only support for VS Code and Zed. The current Sweep product pairs a proprietary "Tab model" next-edit autocomplete with an in-IDE Agent for chat, inline editing, AI commit messages, and AI code review across IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, PhpStorm, Rider, Android Studio, RustRover, RubyMine, CLion, and Aqua. The plugin indexes the local codebase for context, supports Remote MCP Servers with OAuth, web search and fetch tools, and ships under a commercial credit-based pricing model (Free Trial, Basic $10/mo, Pro $20/mo, Ultra $60/mo) with enterprise SOC 2 and zero-data-retention options via contact sales. Sweep has no public developer REST API, no SDK, and no documented webhooks; the company's primary distribution surfaces are the JetBrains Marketplace, the VS Code Marketplace, and the Zed extension registry, and its open-source footprint on GitHub has narrowed to research forks (SWE-bench, SGLang), tokenizer/diff utilities (bpe-qwen, difflib-rs), and the now-legacy sweepai/sweep repository that documented the original GitHub PR agent. Sweep is profiled here as an AI developer-experience vendor rather than as an API provider.

providers.name: Tillpoint
providers.description: Tillpoint is a modular, cloud-based EPOS (electronic point of sale) and business management platform for retail, hospitality, and services. A single subscription bundles 25+ modules - Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers/CRM, Staff, Accounting, Purchase Orders, Reporting, and more - across one terminal or thousands of locations. As of this review Tillpoint does not publish a documented public or partner developer API - there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no OpenAPI. Connectivity is delivered through pre-built integrations (QuickBooks Online, Xero, WooCommerce, PayPal, Worldpay, Mailchimp). The API surfaces catalogued here (Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers, Accounting) are logical capability areas of the platform and are honestly marked as endpointsModeled - no endpoints are fabricated. Direct/programmatic access requires contacting Tillpoint.

providers.name: Twingate
providers.description: Twingate is a Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) platform that replaces legacy VPNs with software-defined perimeters, providing identity-based, least-privilege access to private resources without exposing them to the public internet. The Twingate Admin API is a GraphQL API authenticated via API key (X-API-KEY header) that enables programmatic management of remote networks, connectors, resources, users, groups, service accounts, devices, policies, and DNS filtering profiles.

providers.name: Vennre
providers.description: Vennre is a Sharia-compliant private-market investing platform built for HENRYs (High Earners, Not Rich Yet). It curates and vets institutional-grade opportunities across real estate, private equity, venture capital and private credit from leading global managers, lowering entry thresholds so members can start building wealth from as little as $5,000. Delivered through a mobile app and web experience with a smart wallet, portfolio tracking and personalized wealth coaching, the platform is regulated in the UK as an appointed representative of Talbot Capital Ltd (FCA FRN 489839) and operates in Saudi Arabia under the Capital Market Authority (CMA License 19206-20). Vennre is a consumer wealthtech product; no public developer API or developer platform is published at this time.

providers.name: 28 labs
providers.description: 28labs Inc. operates She's Well (sheswell.co), a consumer fertility-care platform that bundles egg freezing, fertility testing, IVF coordination, clinic visits, labs, medications, and concierge nurse support into a single transparent subscription plan starting at $249/month over up to 60 months. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a business-to-consumer digital-health service with no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Aquant.io
providers.description: Aquant is an agentic AI platform purpose-built for organizations that build, sell, and service complex equipment. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in New York, the company turns service content — equipment manuals, service histories, parts and warranty data, and case notes — plus the expertise inside technicians' heads into AI agents that help field technicians, call-center staff, and self-service customers diagnose issues, surface verified troubleshooting steps, predict equipment failure, and act faster across the entire service lifecycle. Access is available by web, mobile, API, and voice. Aquant serves medical-device, industrial, food-equipment, high-tech, printing, and energy manufacturers, with customers including Siemens Healthineers, The Home Depot, Sysmex, and 3D Systems. The company has raised roughly $113M and is backed by Insight Partners and Lightspeed. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Arf
providers.description: Arf is a Switzerland-regulated liquidity and settlement platform for cross-border payments, providing short-term, receivable-backed, revolving working capital to licensed payment institutions and money-transfer operators. Its core product, Arf Liquidity, lets payment companies settle across any corridor 24/7 without prefunding destination accounts, using regulated real-world-asset-backed digital assets and stablecoins (including USDC) for native on-ramp/off-ramp value transfer and real-time treasury management. Arf is a compliance-first, VQF self-regulatory-organization member serving only licensed financial institutions, and partners with Circle, Stellar, and Visa. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from Arf's public web presence; Arf does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: AVAP BRUNIX
providers.description: AVAP BRUNIX is an AI-powered API development platform that serves as a copilot for developers, integrating artificial intelligence directly into the core of the AVAP framework to enhance efficiency and productivity in API development, testing, and management.

providers.name: Binadox
providers.description: Binadox is a SaaS spend management and optimization platform providing usage monitoring, license optimization, shadow IT discovery, and cloud cost management to help organizations reduce wasted SaaS and cloud spend while gaining complete visibility into their software and infrastructure portfolio. Binadox integrates with AWS, Azure, GCP, and 100+ SaaS applications.

providers.name: Birches Health
providers.description: Birches Health is a fully virtual behavioral addiction treatment provider specializing in gambling disorder and related compulsive behaviors such as sports betting, day trading, video gaming, and pornography. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, the company delivers confidential online care from licensed gambling counselors, peer mentors, financial coaches, and group therapy across all 50 states. Birches Health partners with 18+ state governments that have legalized sports betting and 100+ national insurance plans (including UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Aetna, and Blue Cross Blue Shield) so most clients pay $0-25 per session, with a core program completed in about 12 weeks. The company has raised approximately $20M from AlleyCorp, General Catalyst, and Will Ventures. Birches Health does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or specification; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Boundless
providers.description: Boundless is a Seattle-based technology-enabled immigration company that pairs an intuitive online platform with licensed immigration attorneys to help individuals and businesses navigate U.S. immigration. Its consumer products cover family-based green cards, marriage and fiancé (K-1) visas, naturalization and citizenship, and employment-based visas such as H-1B, EB-1, O-1, and E-2, while its business offering adds corporate case management, workflow automation, employee engagement, compliance management, HR-system integration, and global mobility support for immigration teams. Boundless is backed by Foundry Group and Seedcamp. No public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs are published at this time.

providers.name: Chemius
providers.description: Chemius is a cloud-based chemical compliance platform that automates Safety Data Sheet (SDS), Technical Data Sheet (TDS), and regulatory label creation in 38+ languages for organizations handling chemical products. The platform exposes an API suite covering SDS, TDS, ADR transport documentation, ERP integration, labels, web shop product data, and PDF generation, and offers AI-assisted authoring through the Chemius AI SDS assistant. Chemius is hosted in DIN ISO/IEC 27001-certified German data centers and supports CLP 1272/2008, REACH 1907/2006, detergents, aerosols, and US OSHA / GHS regulatory frameworks.

providers.name: CIRCOR International
providers.description: CIRCOR International is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The CIRCOR International API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Crux
providers.description: Crux is a capital platform for the clean economy, connecting clean energy and manufacturing developers with buyers, lenders, and investors. Its marketplace facilitates the sale of transferable clean energy tax credits created under the Inflation Reduction Act, alongside debt capital markets, tax equity, and preferred equity solutions and advisory services. Crux pairs a transaction platform and secure data room with market intelligence drawn from tens of billions of dollars in deal data, serving project developers, manufacturers, tax credit buyers, banks, tax advisors, and legal teams. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Crux operates a customer application but does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Duolingo
providers.description: Duolingo (NASDAQ: DUOL) is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania based learning technology company best known for the Duolingo language-learning app, the world's most-downloaded education app, offering courses in more than 40 languages including Spanish, English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, and Chinese. Founded in 2011 by Luis von Ahn and Severin Hacker, Duolingo has expanded its consumer learning footprint beyond languages with Duolingo Math, Duolingo Music, a newly rolled-out Chess course, and Duolingo ABC for early literacy, all delivered through the same gamified, streak- driven mobile experience. The Company also operates the Duolingo English Test, a digital English-proficiency exam accepted by thousands of higher- education institutions, certification programs, and government agencies worldwide as an alternative to TOEFL and IELTS. Duolingo monetizes through Super Duolingo and Duolingo Max subscriptions, in-app advertising, in-app purchases, and Duolingo English Test fees. The company surpassed 50 million daily active users in Q3 2025 and reported 41% revenue growth in Q2 2025. Duolingo does not publish an official public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integrations with the Duolingo English Test (score-send to institutional CRMs such as Slate) are handled through a private API-key program negotiated directly with accepting institutions. Community- maintained reverse-engineered clients exist against the unofficial https://www.duolingo.com/api/1 surface but are not endorsed by Duolingo.

providers.name: Flannel
providers.description: Flannel is a simple overlay network that satisfies the Kubernetes networking requirements. It runs a small single binary agent called flanneld on each host and is responsible for allocating a subnet lease to each host out of a larger preconfigured address space. Flannel does not expose its own HTTP/REST API; it stores network configuration in either the Kubernetes API or etcd directly and is managed via configuration files, kubectl, and Helm.

providers.name: Fort
providers.description: Fort is a Y Combinator (W26) hardware startup building a screenless wearable that automatically tracks strength training for people who care about longevity. Founded by three former Tesla engineers, the device uses heart rate and motion sensing to detect gym sessions, workout classes, sleep, and recovery without requiring the wearer to manually log reps, sets, or exercises, then delivers actionable feedback on how lifestyle factors affect strength progress. Fort is styled as jewelry rather than performance gear, ships in three finishes with 7+ day battery life, and pairs with Fort Foundations, an expert-led training program built around core movement patterns. The product is currently available for pre-order and has no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public web and commercial presence.

providers.name: Games24x7
providers.description: Games24x7 is a Mumbai-headquartered Indian online skill-gaming company founded in 2006 by Bhavin Pandya and Trivikraman Thampy, operating consumer real-money and casual gaming platforms rather than a developer API business. Its portfolio spans RummyCircle (online rummy), My11Circle (fantasy cricket, football, kabaddi and ludo) and Wowzy (a three-dice ludo variant), backed by Tiger Global, The Raine Group and Malabar Investment. The company publishes engineering writing on distributed systems, Cassandra, Amazon Aurora, ksqlDB and React Native through its Resources section, runs the TechXpedite accelerator, and maintains a small public GitHub organization (games24x7-opensource) plus one first-party npm package for AI-assisted Appium test automation. As of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no machine-readable specification, and no partner or affiliate API of its own.

providers.name: Huginn
providers.description: Huginn is an open-source system for building agents that perform automated tasks online. Self-hosted agents can monitor the web, send and receive events, and trigger workflows. Each Huginn instance exposes a JSON-based HTTP interface (the Web Requests API) that lets external systems trigger scenarios and post events into the platform.

providers.name: illoca
providers.description: illoca is an AI-native design engine built for professional architects and design studios, delivered through its product Tracing Paper. It helps architects move from early ideas to editable 2D and 3D designs with more speed and control, supporting sketches, redlines, prompts, floor plans, massing studies, iterative refinements, and exports for professional design workflows. Tracing Paper is built for controllable architectural ideation and iteration with editable outputs that hand off into BIM/CAD tools such as Autodesk Revit and Rhino. illoca is a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners (sector: ai-ml). As an application-first company it currently exposes a marketing site and web application rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Inkling
providers.description: Inkling is a frontline employee training and enablement platform (now part of Echo360) that delivers mission-critical knowledge, learning pathways, and operational workflows to essential workers across retail, hospitality, healthcare, and manufacturing. Its products include the Habitat content authoring tool, mobile Knowledge & Training modules, InkForms operational checklists, certification pathways, reporting and analytics, and LMS/LXP integrations. Inkling publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; integration is delivered through LMS/LXP connectors and professional services. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Sapphire Ventures portfolio company and enriched with the provider's public identity, security posture, and site properties.

providers.name: Jib
providers.description: Jib is an open-source container image builder from Google that builds optimized Docker and OCI images for Java applications without requiring a Docker daemon or writing a Dockerfile. It is available as plugins for Maven and Gradle, and integrates directly into the Java build process to produce reproducible container images.

providers.name: Jify
providers.description: Jify is an India-based financial wellness platform (part of the Moneyview group) that partners with employers to give employees earned wage access: its On-Demand Salary lets workers draw already-earned pay before payday. Beyond earned wage access it offers salary advances, a rewards and discount marketplace, micro-savings, digital gold investing, credit-score tracking, smart tax tools, and a money manager for budgeting and expense tracking, delivered through Android and iOS apps. Jify is a consumer / B2B2C fintech app and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity, domain-security posture, and published compliance claims (ISO 27001, CISA-certified, independently tested by Appknox).

providers.name: K3s
providers.description: K3s is a lightweight Kubernetes distribution designed for resource-constrained environments, edge computing, IoT devices, and CI/CD pipelines. K3s is a fully compliant Kubernetes distribution with a reduced memory footprint and simplified installation.

providers.name: Kabal
providers.description: Kabal is the energy industry's leading logistics management SaaS platform. Founded in Norway in 2011 (formerly Wellit), Kabal provides an integrated, cloud-native platform that manages cargo, marine, transport, personnel, warehouse, rig and installation logistics across both offshore and onshore operations for oil & gas operators. The platform spans planning, execution and optimization, plus cost and emissions tracking and KPI reporting, connecting operators with their suppliers and vessels to share business-critical logistics data. Kabal is trusted by energy supermajors including ExxonMobil, Shell, Chevron, BP, TotalEnergies, Equinor, Petronas, Repsol, Eni and ADNOC, with tens of thousands of users across dozens of countries. Kabal received a growth investment from Insight Partners in 2023.

providers.name: Kayrros
providers.description: Kayrros is an environmental-intelligence and geospatial-AI company that independently tracks human activity and its physical footprint worldwide by combining satellite imagery, alternative data, and machine learning. Its products span energy markets — crude oil and jet fuel intelligence, LNG, renewables, solar and battery-storage construction monitoring, industrial and on-road energy demand, and stockpiles — and environmental risk — methane emissions via Methane Watch, wildfire risk, forest-carbon and deforestation monitoring, and carbon accounting. Kayrros delivers asset-level data feeds, APIs, and dashboards to traders, operators, financial institutions, regulators, insurers, and the public sector. The company was acquired by Energy Aspects in May 2026.

providers.name: Ko
providers.description: ko is a simple, fast container image builder for Go applications that does not require Docker, producing small images by building Go binaries and layering them on a minimal base image for deployment to Kubernetes.

providers.name: Kustomize
providers.description: Kustomize is a Kubernetes-native configuration management tool that lets you customize untemplated YAML files for multiple purposes, leaving the original YAML intact and usable as-is, using a template-free approach to configuration customization.

providers.name: Lastro
providers.description: Lastro is a Brazilian proptech company building artificial intelligence for the real estate market. Its product, Lais (lais.ai), is a generative-AI platform for real estate agencies that engages and qualifies inbound leads over WhatsApp and other channels, then follows the customer journey from first contact through to a closed deal — covering property listing and management, marketing and lead generation, pre-qualification, visit scheduling, administrative service and strategic reporting. Human agents and the AI work the same queue inside Casa da Lais, the operator dashboard. Lastro reports more than 1,000 real estate agency customers, over 5 million people served and more than R$ 12 billion in sales volume (VGV) managed in Brazil. The company is backed by Prosus Ventures and QED Investors. Lastro publishes no public developer API; the only programmatic surface found is the Wix platform-provisioned site MCP endpoint on lastro.co.

providers.name: Lizzyai
providers.description: Lizzy is a generative-AI platform for legal professionals, delivering a secure Gen AI workspace across all practice areas through both a web application and a Microsoft Word/Outlook add-in. It supports contract drafting, review, analysis, and proofreading, customizable legal workflows and playbooks, in-document citations, redlining and track-changes, and the handling of long, scanned, watermarked, and multiple documents. A multi-LLM approach routes each task to the most capable model, and firms can train a private model that embeds their own know-how. Built for enterprise IT with a zero-trust architecture, no training on customer data, PII anonymization, SSO via SAML and OAuth 2.0, and shared, VPC, or self-hosted deployment options.

providers.name: Mainspring Energy
providers.description: Mainspring Energy is a Menlo Park, California power-infrastructure company that designs, manufactures, and deploys the Linear Generator, a modular, fuel-flexible onsite power generation system. Its technology delivers firm, dispatchable, and low-emission electricity for data centers, utilities, and industrial and enterprise facilities, running today on natural gas and biogas with a seamless transition to zero-carbon fuels such as hydrogen and ammonia. Backed by Khosla Ventures and other investors, Mainspring has more than one gigawatt of Linear Generator capacity in late-stage development and operation. Mainspring is a hardware and power-systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Multus CNI
providers.description: Multus CNI is a container network interface plugin for Kubernetes that enables attaching multiple network interfaces to pods. It acts as a meta-plugin that can call multiple other CNI plugins, allowing pods to have connectivity to multiple networks simultaneously.

providers.name: Ntopology
providers.description: nTop (formerly nTopology) is a computational design software platform for engineering teams building complex, high-performance products. Its parametric, field-driven modeling engine combines geometry, simulation data, and manufacturing constraints so engineers can move from requirements to production-ready designs in a fraction of the traditional time. nTop is used across aerospace and defense, automotive, medical, and industrial energy sectors for lightweighting, lattice and implicit modeling, thermal and structural optimization, and additive manufacturing. nTop also ships nTop Core, a first-party developer library (C++, .NET, and Python) for working with implicit bodies exported from nTop. The company is headquartered in New York City and is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners and DCVC.

providers.name: Parcel Monitor
providers.description: Global parcel tracking REST API aggregating real-time tracking data from 1,000+ carriers worldwide, enabling e-commerce shipment visibility, delivery analytics, and webhook-driven notifications across 170+ countries.

providers.name: PartySlate
providers.description: PartySlate is a Chicago-based dual marketplace and SaaS platform for the events industry, connecting people planning weddings, galas, corporate events, birthdays, and holiday parties with the leading venues, event professionals, and vendors across the country. The photo-rich platform lets vendors showcase their work through millions of real event photos, build networks of industry partners, and connect directly with prospective clients, while PartySlate Pro provides venues, planners, and vendors an AI-powered SaaS suite to organize, search, and share their photo portfolios with Canva integration and content-management tools built for events. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: PlusMargin
providers.description: PlusMargin (Plus Margin) is a Bangkok, Thailand based digital marketing and business consulting practice operating under the tagline "Connect | Engage | Convert." The firm focuses on inbound marketing strategy, personalized and AI-assisted marketing, buyer-persona development, and customer-journey mapping for its clients, and publishes Thai-language editorial content across marketing, business, advertising, technology, learning, insurance, and lifestyle topics. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global — where secondary sources describe an earlier Singapore-founded "predictive persuasion" e-commerce personalization product — but the domain today serves a four-page consulting and content site with no trace of that platform. Enrichment on 2026-08-12 confirmed no product API, no developer portal, no SDKs on any package registry, no /.well-known/ discovery surface, no llms.txt and no agent card. The one callable, machine-readable surface is the stock WordPress REST API the marketing site exposes at /wp-json — 237 routes across 11 namespaces, anonymously readable for content — which is WordPress core's API rather than a product PlusMargin designed, documents, or supports.

providers.name: ProsperOps
providers.description: ProsperOps is an autonomous cloud cost optimization platform that uses AI-driven algorithms to manage AWS Reserved Instances and Savings Plans, maximizing discount coverage while minimizing commitment risk.

providers.name: Regrello
providers.description: Regrello is an AI operating system for manufacturing and supply chain operations, giving teams that are stuck in email and stifled by decades-old ERPs an agentic AI platform to accelerate innovation and productivity. Its product, Agentforce Operations, orchestrates enterprise manufacturing and supply chain workflows with generative AI. Regrello was acquired by Salesforce and is backed by a16z and Bloomberg Beta. This profile currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network for its identity, security posture, and published compliance program.

providers.name: Replica Studios
providers.description: Replica Studios (operated by Replica Media Pty Ltd) built AI voice, text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-speech (STS) technology for creators, game developers, and software teams. Its platform offered an AI Voice Library of 40+ expressive voices, Voice Lab for blending up to five voices into a custom character, and Voice Director for generating voice overs and dialogue. Developers integrated these capabilities through the Replica API v2 (OpenAPI 3.0.0) — a REST API supporting text-to-speech, speech-to-speech, and voice-listing operations, authenticated with API keys or Bearer JWTs minted at the /v2/auth endpoint. Replica Studios was a Techstars portfolio company. The company ceased operations on 2025-06-30; the marketing site now shows a farewell page and the api.replicastudios.com host no longer resolves, so this profile is a historical/discovery record captured from public documentation.

providers.name: Ruzuku
providers.description: Ruzuku is a hosted online course platform for coaches, authors, and subject matter experts to create, teach, and sell online courses and learning communities. Ruzuku does not publish a documented public REST API or developer program. Its programmatic surface is exposed exclusively through a Zapier integration - authenticated with an API Key, API Secret, and Site URL generated under Account then Integrations then Configure Zapier - that offers event triggers (enrollments, lesson and course completions, quiz and assignment submissions, comments, cancellations) and a small set of student enroll, unenroll, and lookup actions. The APIs modeled below are honest logical groupings of that Zapier-mediated surface, not endpoints from a public Ruzuku API reference.

providers.name: Sable Bio
providers.description: Sable Bio is a London-based drug-safety intelligence company building an AI-augmented platform, Sable Target Intelligence, that helps toxicologists, informaticians, and drug discovery scientists assess and mitigate target safety risk earlier in the drug development process. The platform aggregates and quantifies clinical, genetic, experimental, and literature evidence into a unified Target Safety Intelligence surface so safety teams can systematically prioritize and de-risk drug targets faster than traditional manual review. The company is headquartered in East London (Runway East Aldgate) and is backed by Episode One, Seedcamp, and MMC Ventures. Sable Bio was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it operates a public marketing and product site with a Vanta-hosted trust center but does not yet publish a developer-facing API, documentation, or data-access surface.

providers.name: Showbie
providers.description: Showbie is a K-12 learning platform for iPad that streamlines teaching workflows across assignments, feedback, grading, and classroom communication for teachers, students, and parents. Backed by Point Nine, it combines a digital classroom, annotation and file-sharing tools, and messaging into a single app used by schools worldwide. Showbie exposes no public developer API, SDK, or docs surface; this profile captures the company's public web, support, compliance, privacy, and terms properties, plus a live domain security probe.

providers.name: Sprague Resources
providers.description: Sprague Resources (operating as Sprague Energy) is one of the largest independent suppliers of energy products and related services in the northeastern United States and Quebec, founded in 1870. The company distributes refined fuel products (heating oil, diesel, gasoline, kerosene, biofuels), natural gas, and electricity to commercial and industrial customers, and operates 20+ port terminal facilities for materials handling. Sprague was acquired by Hartree Partners in 2024 and continues to expand through strategic acquisitions. While Sprague does not publish a public developer API, the company operates SpraguePORT, a digital customer portal for account management, pricing, and order history, and Sprague Real-time for market pricing.

providers.name: Taito.ai
providers.description: Taito.ai is an AI-native people operations (HRIS) platform headquartered in Helsinki, Finland, built for teams scaling from roughly 30 to 300 employees. It unifies the employee lifecycle in one system — a people directory, time-off and attendance, documents and eSignatures, and performance reviews — alongside AI "people agents" that handle onboarding, reminders, payroll reporting, and policy questions on demand from Slack, Claude, or any MCP-compatible tool. Every platform action is exposed over the Model Context Protocol rather than a public REST API. Pricing is a single per-seat tier covering both the people-ops and performance modules. The company is ISO 27001 certified and GDPR compliant, publishing audit reports on a Vanta-hosted Trust Center, and raised a $2.7M seed round led by Accel.

providers.name: Tier
providers.description: Tier (now operating as Dott following the 2024 merger of TIER Mobility and Dott) is a European micromobility operator providing shared e-scooters and e-bikes across more than 400 cities in Europe and the Middle East. The company exposes a partner-facing Dott Partner API — an API-Key-gated data feed (including GBFS-style vehicle-availability data) governed by its published API Licence — alongside consumer rider apps for iOS and Android. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Amsterdam, Tier/Dott was backed by Northzone, Point Nine, and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Uhnder
providers.description: Uhnder is an Austin, Texas fabless semiconductor company founded in 2015 that designs the S80 and S81 77 GHz 4D digital imaging Radar-on-Chip (RoC) for automotive ADAS and automated mobility. Its Digital Code Modulation (DCM) approach on a 28nm RF CMOS process replaces analog FMCW radar with a software-defined sensor, and each RoC ships with an ASPICE-qualified Software Development Kit carrying ready-to-integrate software APIs, on-chip user algorithm support and system tools for Tier-1 and OEM radar stacks. Uhnder is a chip supplier rather than a web-API provider: the SDK and its APIs are embedded interfaces delivered under a commercial customer relationship, and the company publishes no public developer portal, documentation host or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Vertical Bar Inc.
providers.description: Vertical Bar Inc. builds CrossCheck, a DevOps and operations-visibility platform for NetSuite environments. CrossCheck gives NetSuite teams configuration tracking, change management and deployment safety: environment snapshots, comparisons and restore, automated record-and-replay regression testing that catches issues before production, AI-assisted error analysis with fix suggestions, and process mining to surface workflow delays and inefficiencies. Vertical Bar also offers managed services and industry-specific solutions for medical device, food and beverage, chemical, and aerospace and defense manufacturers, plus the FieldTrail browser extension for NetSuite field customization. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Acheel
providers.description: Acheel is a French digital insurance company — a néo-assureur that carries its own insurance licence rather than broking someone else's. Founded in 2020 by Ralph Ruimy and Francky Défossé, it received its ACPR agrément and launched in 2021, and now reports more than 800,000 policyholders. ACHEEL SA (879 605 350 RCS Paris) underwrites; ACHEEL FRANCE (ORIAS 21003575) distributes. The range spans nine lines — habitation, auto, santé, animaux, PNO (propriétaire non occupant), emprunteur, scolaire, protection juridique and RC pro — sold 100% digitally, with a quote in about two minutes and subscription in five. Roughly 70% of revenue comes from B2B2C distribution: partner brokers are served under the Charlee brand (charlee.fr, broker portal "Acheel Omega" at back.charlee.fr) and partners embed a per-tenant white-label customer area served from *.widget.acheel.com. Acheel's own partner FAQ stated it makes its APIs available to partners ("nous mettons à votre disposition nos APIs afin de vous faire bénéficier de notre Tech et de nos produits"), but no developer portal, API reference, base URL or machine-readable specification is published anywhere on its public surface; API access travels with a brokerage partnership. Acheel is a certified B Corp.

providers.name: Agency
providers.description: Agency (agency.inc) builds Kai, an autonomous AI co-worker for customer success — an AI agent that works a company's entire book of B2B SaaS accounts, monitoring product usage, surfacing churn and expansion signals early, and running personalized onboarding, adoption, and renewal outreach so revenue and customer-success teams have command over their book. Agency raised a $20M Series A led by Menlo Ventures with participation from Sequoia Capital, Felicis, Snowflake Ventures, and Databricks Ventures. It is a demo-led enterprise product and does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Alif
providers.description: Alif Semiconductor is a Silicon Valley fabless semiconductor company building secure, ultra-low-power 32-bit microcontrollers and fusion processors for edge AI/ML. Its Ensemble, Ensemble Gen AI, and Balletto product families pair Arm Cortex-M and Cortex-A cores with dedicated Ethos-U55 neural processing units, hardware AI acceleration, wireless connectivity, and a multilayered security architecture so machine-learning and generative-AI workloads can run directly on battery-powered devices. Developer resources center on Zephyr-based SDKs, CMSIS device family packs, VS Code project templates, evaluation kits, datasheets, reference manuals, and the Conductor configuration tool rather than a hosted web API. The company is backed by Kleiner Perkins.

providers.name: Bestow
providers.description: Bestow is a Dallas, Texas life insurance technology company building a unified SaaS platform for life insurance carriers, agents, and embedded partners. Founded in 2016, Bestow provides end-to-end and modular solutions across new business and policy administration, including a digital Application Suite for quote, illustration, and application journeys; an Underwriting engine and workbench with instant, fully automated decisioning powered by machine learning on actuarial data; an Agent Portal and sales management tooling; an Admin Portal and Customer Portal for self-service; TPA (Third-Party Administrator) services; a Performance IQ analytics surface; and a Data Optimization Suite for modeling, integrations, and activation. Bestow's Protect API and associated SDK power embedded life insurance — letting fintechs, banks, financial institutions, P&C carriers, mortgage platforms, and benefits providers offer instant term life, final expense, and IUL coverage inside their own apps and websites, with Bestow handling underwriting, payment, billing, policy delivery, and ongoing administration behind the scenes. Integrations span ACORD life and annuities data standards, Adyen for payments, Cloudflare for identity and security, and data vendors including Bevel, Clareto, EIS, ExamOne, and Human API ReFlex Select. There is no publicly accessible developer portal or API reference — partner documentation, sandbox access, and Protect API onboarding are gated behind a partner login at docs.bestow.com and arranged through Bestow's sales and partnerships team.

providers.name: Blindmate
providers.description: Blindmate is a friend-based dating app that inverts the swipe model: instead of writing their own profile, a single person's friends answer questions about them, and matches are made through character-first "Blindchats" that surface compatibility before appearance. Founded in Germany and available on iOS and Android in German, English, and Spanish, the app reports over one million users and positions itself around trust, reduced harassment, data privacy, and green-energy infrastructure.
