Blindmate is a Speedinvest portfolio company; it is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public developer API, so this profile captures its web, security, and policy surface rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Brightline
providers.description: Brightline is an award-winning pediatric mental health practice delivering therapy, psychiatry (including medication management), and psychological testing for children and adolescents up to age 18, using an evidence-based, family-focused model that begins with a structured diagnostic evaluation. It treats anxiety, OCD, ADHD, disruptive behavioral disorders, depression, trauma, grief, and autism-spectrum symptoms via in-person clinics in New York and telehealth across NY, NJ, CT, MA, and WA, and operates BrightLife Kids, a free California state-funded behavioral health program for families with children up to age 12. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Threshold Ventures; Brightline is a consumer/clinical healthcare provider with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Buildvision
providers.description: BuildVision is an AI bid-management and equipment-procurement platform for the construction industry. It monitors email inboxes and construction plan rooms for incoming bids, extracts equipment specifications from construction documents, matches them against a company's line card, and drafts quotes with automatic conflict detection and RFI generation. Products span bid triage automation, a "spec memory" of historical engineer data, equipment quoting, and channel intelligence for OEMs. BuildVision integrates with Microsoft Outlook and BuildingConnected and offers direct API / browser-agent integration to selection software by request, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from BuildVision's public surface.

providers.name: Bureau of International Labor Affairs
providers.description: ILAB strengthens global labor standards; enforces labor commitments; promotes equity; and combats child labor, forced labor, and human trafficking.

providers.name: Cofertility
providers.description: Cofertility is a human-centered fertility and family-building platform built around an egg-sharing model. Through its Split program, women can freeze their eggs at no cost when they donate half of the retrieved eggs to another family who cannot otherwise conceive; its Keep program offers self-funded egg freezing at a discount where members retain all of their eggs. On the family-building side, Cofertility matches intended parents (including LGBTQ+ families and single parents) with fresh and frozen egg donors, working with 225+ clinic partners nationwide and a donor community spanning 270+ ethnicities. Founded by Lauren Makler, the company operates a consumer web platform (match.cofertility.com) plus an extensive fertility education library. It is a consumer health company with no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time; this profile captures its public web properties and posture.

providers.name: Credit Genie
providers.description: Credit Genie is a consumer fintech operated by Creditly Corp. (Wilmington, Delaware, founded 2019) that runs a mobile-first money app for people living between paychecks. Its Cash Boost product advances $10-$150 with no interest and no hard credit check, funded against a linked bank account rather than a credit score, while Money Manager layers spending tracking, cash-flow prediction and subscription detection on top of that same bank connection. A Line of Credit product and AskGenie, an AI financial assistant, are in early access. Creditly Corp. is registered with the California DFPI under the CCFPL (registration 04-CCFPL-1956127-3514680) and has raised roughly $21M from Fortress Investment Group, Khosla Ventures, Sutter Hill Ventures, Tippet Venture Partners and Gabriel Investments. Credit Genie is a direct-to-consumer app company: it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Crozdesk
providers.description: Crozdesk helps businesses find and compare software across all major software categories. The platform indexes 43,000+ products across 377+ categories with expert reviews, user ratings, and AI-powered recommendations to guide software purchasing decisions. Vendors can list and advertise their products through the SoftwareSelect vendor portal.

providers.name: Crux OCM
providers.description: CruxOCM builds AI-powered automation software for industrial control-room operations in the energy-infrastructure sector. Its Industrial Automation Hub (IAH) delivers closed-loop automation on top of existing SCADA and DCS systems to increase pipeline throughput, cut operating and energy costs, and improve safety without replacing installed control infrastructure. The product family includes pipeBOT, gatherBOT, draBOT, maxOPT, leanOPT, and powerOPT, supported by a Deployment Manager, Log Analyser, and real-time Status Dashboard. Founded by control-room engineers and operators (CEO Vicki Knott, co-founder Roger Shirt) and headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, the company raised a $17M Series A led by Microsoft's M12 and serves midstream operators including ONEOK, Delek US, Enbridge, HF Sinclair, and Alliance Pipeline. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cult.fit
providers.description: Cult.fit (Curefit / cure.fit, operated by Diverse Retails Private Limited) is an Indian health and fitness company offering a connected consumer experience across group fitness classes, gyms, at-home workouts, mental well-being and meditation, healthy food, and diagnostics. Its flagship products include CultPass gym and class memberships, sport and fitness centers, live and on-demand digital workouts, and the cult.fit and cure.fit mobile and web apps. Backed by Accel and other investors, the company operates a large consumer platform but does not publish a public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity, corporate web properties, and engineering surface (the curefit GitHub organization and engineering blog).

providers.name: Deepjudge
providers.description: DeepJudge is an AI-powered legal knowledge search and intelligence platform for law firms and in-house legal teams, founded by ex-Google search engineers and legaltech veterans. It unifies scattered institutional knowledge across document management systems, SharePoint, HighQ, OneDrive, email, and intranets into a single governed, permission-aware search layer, then layers LLM-agnostic AI agents and workflow automation on top. Products include DeepJudge Knowledge Search, AI Workflows, Negotiation Intelligence, Multi-Document Chat, Matter & Client Overview, and SuperSearch for cross-matter analysis. The platform can be hosted in DeepJudge's cloud, the customer's cloud, or on premises, supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) for governed AI access to firm knowledge, and does not train on customer data. DeepJudge is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified.

providers.name: depthfirst
providers.description: depthfirst is an applied AI lab building an autonomous application security platform that protects software from design through production. Its General Security Intelligence platform builds context across a company's code, infrastructure, and business logic to detect complex vulnerabilities, cut false positives, and generate merge-ready fixes. Product surfaces include a code scanner, dependency firewall, secrets detection, supply-chain mapping, and agentic pentesting, alongside in-house security models such as dfs-mini1. Backed by Accel, Meritech Capital, Forerunner Ventures, and The House Fund, depthfirst works with companies including ClickUp, Lovable, Supabase, incident.io, and Moveworks.

providers.name: Economic Research Service
providers.description: The Economic Research Service (ERS) is a division of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) that conducts economic research and analysis related to agriculture, food, and rural development. ERS provides policymakers, stakeholders, and the public with valuable information and data to help inform decision-making and policy development.

providers.name: Escale
providers.description: Escale is a Sao Paulo-based sales technology company founded in 2013 that builds aisa, an AI sales agent trained on millions of real sales conversations. aisa automates lead qualification, objection handling, deal personalization, and sales closure across text and voice channels for enterprise brands in financial services, banking, telecommunications, automotive finance, and education. Escale manages the full customer-acquisition funnel from demand generation through closing, having processed over 7 million leads and generated more than R$2.1 billion in GMV. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile captures its corporate identity, trust/compliance posture, and legal properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Evvy
providers.description: Evvy is a women's health company offering at-home vaginal microbiome testing and personalized care. Its CLIA-certified metagenomic (mNGS) Vaginal Health Test identifies over 700 bacteria and fungi from a self-collected sample, with results reviewed by licensed clinicians who deliver personalized insights and clinician-designed treatment programs for conditions such as bacterial vaginosis, aerobic vaginitis, yeast infections, recurrent UTIs, and fertility-related concerns. Evvy also sells a line of vaginal health products including probiotics and boric-acid, hyaluronic-acid, and probiotic suppositories, plus a provider program for clinicians and a large library of science-backed educational content. Backed by General Catalyst, Evvy was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Evvy is a direct-to-consumer health and e-commerce business and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Fiveable
providers.description: Fiveable is an Advanced Placement (AP) exam preparation platform covering all 38 AP subjects. It provides study guides, unit-organized subject review hubs, practice questions modeled on real AP exam formats, AI-scored free-response questions (FRQs), cheatsheets, key-term glossaries, and AP score calculators that predict likely exam outcomes. Fiveable serves three audiences - secondary students cramming and reviewing for AP exams, teachers seeking classroom and assessment materials, and schools needing district-wide exam-prep support. The platform blends traditional study resources with AI-powered scoring and feedback. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; Fiveable publishes a consumer web application but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: FreeWill
providers.description: FreeWill is an online estate-planning platform that lets people create legal documents for free, including last wills, revocable living trusts (California only), advance healthcare directives, financial powers of attorney, and beneficiary designations, through a guided questionnaire. It runs a dual model: individuals use the tools at no cost, while more than 2,400 nonprofit organizations partner with FreeWill for planned-giving and legacy-gift features. Related surfaces include the Estately advisor platform and a Nonprofit Solutions offering. FreeWill was surfaced as a portfolio company of iconiq-capital and qed-investors. Enrichment found no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or API documentation — this profile is a consumer/nonprofit company record, not an API producer, with security and legal properties captured from the public site.

providers.name: Gronda
providers.description: Gronda is a professional community and learning platform for chefs and hospitality professionals, offering 70+ masterclasses and 20,000+ exclusive restaurant recipes from leading chefs, a chef directory and creator program, and team and culinary-school plans. Members share culinary creations, follow world-class chefs, and access PRO subscription content through the Gronda web and mobile apps. Backed by Speedinvest, Gronda was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and profiled through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; it is a consumer/community product that does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Hadrius
providers.description: Hadrius is an AI-native compliance platform for SEC- and FINRA-regulated financial firms, including broker-dealers, registered investment advisors (RIAs), private funds, and compliance consultants. The platform consolidates multiple compliance functions into a single system of record with human governance: a testing program that automates compliance testing and audit reporting, AI-powered marketing review and content approval workflows, people oversight for personal trading, attestations and certifications, communications archiving that supervises email, chat, and social media with zero-retention AI, and account surveillance that monitors trades against restricted lists and blackout windows. Hadrius serves 500+ institutions managing over $5 trillion in AUM, raised a $22M Series A, and is backed by Y Combinator and CRV. The company is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified and GDPR compliant. This profile currently documents no public developer API; it is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Heartland Payment Systems
providers.description: Heartland Payment Systems is a payment processing company offering payroll, customer engagement, point-of-sale, and other business solutions to merchants across the United States. Heartland is now a brand of Global Payments, and developer resources for Heartland integrations are published through the Global Payments developer portal. The platform supports online and in-person payments, bill pay, IoT/connected device payments, gift and loyalty, payroll, and PCI-validated point-to-point encryption.

providers.name: Jala
providers.description: JALA is an Indonesian aquaculture technology company providing end-to-end solutions for the shrimp farming industry, describing itself as a fully connected system powered by data farmers can trust. It connects farmers, processors, and buyers through the JALA App for real-time pond monitoring and data analytics, the Baruni technology platform, farming supplies (post-larvae, feed, technical assistance), harvest and cold-chain logistics services, and traceable certified supply chains for processors and buyers. Backed by 500 Global, JALA operates a consumer/operator SaaS platform (app.jala.tech) rather than a public developer API program. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: jQuery
providers.description: jQuery is a fast, small, and feature-rich JavaScript library that makes HTML document traversal and manipulation, event handling, animation, and Ajax much simpler with an easy-to-use API that works across a multitude of browsers. Only about 30kB minified and gzipped, available as an AMD module, and CSS3 compliant. jQuery 4.0 is the current release; jQuery 3.x receives critical updates only.

providers.name: Kredete
providers.description: Kredete is an intelligent global finance app for diaspora and emerging-market communities, founded in 2022 and operating across four continents. It moves money across 60+ markets at the mid-market rate with settlement in about ten seconds, issues US dollar Visa cards accepted in 170+ countries, opens multi-currency accounts in the customer's own name, pays yield on US dollar savings held through partner US chartered institutions, and reports rent and repayment history to the major US credit bureaus so customers build a US credit file. Kredete for Business adds multi-currency operating accounts, corporate cards, FedWire routing, payroll, and invoicing. An in-app agent runs these actions on the customer's behalf with confirmation. Kredete is a financial technology company, not a bank; remittance and banking services are provided by partner US licensed financial institutions. Backed by Partech and Techstars. As of this enrichment pass Kredete publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API description.

providers.name: Manex AI
providers.description: Manex AI (Manex AI GmbH) is a European enterprise AI company that builds Kosmos, an Autonomous Enterprise AI Platform for industrial and manufacturing OEMs and their suppliers. Kosmos models the domains a business runs on and lets AI agents, workflows, and applications act on full enterprise context instead of fragments. On top of Kosmos, Manex ships purpose-built autonomous suites: Blackbelt (computer-aided quality / CAQ), Takt (manufacturing execution / MES), and Gemba (shopfloor operations), plus Horizon, a distribution platform that makes a solution built at one site instantly available to every other. Manex serves aerospace, automotive, chemistry, electronics, semiconductors, pharma and biotech, heavy equipment, industrial machinery, and home-appliance manufacturers. Made in Europe and built for the strictest compliance standards, the platform runs in cloud, on-premise, or hybrid environments with customer-controlled data residency, GDPR options, ISO 27001 and TISAX certification, enterprise access control, and full audit history. Manex AI is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Paperplane
providers.description: Paperplane is an AI sales-productivity tool (Y Combinator W23, backed by Bloomberg Beta) that automatically takes notes on sales calls and keeps a rep's CRM up to date. It connects to a team's calendar and to conversational intelligence and call-recording tools such as Gong and Chorus, transcribes and analyzes each call, then writes the results back to Salesforce — updating opportunity fields, notes, and action items so sales teams spend less time on manual CRM data entry and stay on top of their deals. The product is organized around opportunities, calls, and notes, with integrations for Google Calendar, Gong, Chorus, and Salesforce. Paperplane appears to have wound down: Y Combinator lists the company as Inactive (and now describes it as a credit risk management platform for builders' merchants, so it pivoted at least once before stopping), its marketing site presents no TLS certificate, its application host returns a Vercel 402 DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED, and its API host is an Envoy ingress that 404s every path with an empty body. Two surfaces remain live: a GitBook documentation site — which is an unfilled starter template carrying GitBook's own placeholder copy, last updated three years ago — with an llms.txt index, and a Clerk-hosted OpenID Connect identity instance at clerk.paperplane.ai that still serves real OIDC and RFC 8414 discovery documents. There is no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, MCP server, or agent card.

providers.name: Picnicai
providers.description: PicnicHealth (PicnicAI; legally Mission Health Labs, Inc.) is a San Francisco health-data company and Y Combinator alum (S14, founded 2014) that turns patients' fragmented medical records into structured, research-ready real-world datasets. Its consumer product gives patients a unified timeline of care across every provider, while PicnicResearch supplies de-identified, ontology-mapped (RxNorm, SNOMED, LOINC, ICD) real-world data to biopharma via AI extraction plus human clinical curation. The primary developer surface is a first-party R package distributed through PicnicHealth's own Posit/RStudio Package Manager for importing and visualizing research cohorts.

providers.name: PiggyVest
providers.description: PiggyVest is a Lagos-based Nigerian fintech (operated by Piggytech Global Limited, RC 1405222) running the country's largest online savings and investment platform, with 6M+ registered users as of 2026. Founded in January 2016 by Somto Ifezue, Odunayo Eweniyi, and Joshua Chibueze as Piggybank.ng and rebranded to PiggyVest in April 2019, the company digitizes the traditional Nigerian "kolo" piggy-bank, layering automated savings, fixed-term safe-locks, naira and dollar wallets, and curated investments on top of licensed banking partners (originally United Bank for Africa) and a PCI-DSS-compliant payment stack. The consumer product family includes Piggybank (automated daily/weekly/monthly savings), SafeLock (fixed-tenor savings with up-front interest), Target Savings (goal-based saving, solo or group), Flex Naira (flexible wallet with free transfers), Flex Dollar / SafeLock Dollar (USD savings), HouseMoney (rent wallet), Investify (curated investment opportunities), GetIT (lifestyle purchase plans), Piggy Points (rewards), and an Accountability Partner feature, all delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps published by Piggytech Global. On the developer side, PiggyVest operates a separate B2B brand — PiggyVest Business — at piggyvest.business and exposes the PiggyVest Business API at api.piggyvest.business, documented at www.piggyvestbusiness.com/docs. The Business API is a Bearer-token authenticated REST API (secret key in Authorization header) covering customer creation and retrieval, customer wallets (create / retrieve / list, accrued-interest tracking, reserved account numbers, funding accounts), wallet-to-wallet and bank transfers (with name inquiry and bank lookup), transactions (status, history, T+1 settlement), scheduled payments (create / cancel / reactivate), webhooks for real-time event notifications, and a "Pay with Pocket" SDK / hosted-checkout integration that lets merchants accept payments funded from a Piggyvest user's Pocket balance. Default rate limits are approximately 100 requests per minute. No public OpenAPI specification, official SDK packages, or open-source client libraries are currently published; access is gated by signing up for a PiggyVest Business dashboard account. Alongside the API, PiggyVest Business offers Invoicing, Customizable Accounts, Business Safelock, Investify for Business, and business savings earning up to 18% per annum. Public engineering presence is limited — the Piggytech Global GitHub org (github.com/PiggyTech) hosts a small set of community wrappers (react-paystack, Smile Identity Node.js and React Native wrappers) and the consumer brand maintains a static piggyvest.github.io site, but there is no developer org publishing official Piggyvest Business SDKs.

providers.name: PsyOptions
providers.description: PsyOptions is a decentralized options protocol built on Solana by Mithraic Labs, providing on-chain American-style options contracts originally designed for use with the Serum/OpenBook DEX. Rather than a hosted REST API, it exposes its functionality through open-source on-chain Anchor/BPF programs and first-party TypeScript client libraries (the @mithraic-labs npm scope: psy-american, psyoptions, market-meta, psy-token-registry, psy-metrics) plus a Rust crate. The project has since been sunset: its documentation and marketing sites are shut down, though the GitHub repositories and published packages remain available for reference. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. Sector: crypto / DeFi.

providers.name: Radical Health
providers.description: Radical Health is a Khosla Ventures-backed healthcare AI company that produces personalized, expert-reviewed cancer treatment reports for patients in the United States. Its platform ingests a patient's medical records and synthesizes oncology research, clinical trials, and prior patient outcomes into a tailored report within days, drawing on 5.3 million research papers, 11.8 million patient journeys, 20,000 treatment options, and 48,800+ active US clinical trials. The service pairs an always-on AI nurse navigator ("Alice") with human oncology oversight from institutions including UCLA, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, and Kaiser Permanente, and connects to 70,000+ US healthcare institutions (Epic, Kaiser, Ascension, HCA, Medicare) for records access. Reports are informational and educational only, not medical advice. Radical Health is HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II certified and operates as a consumer subscription product ($110/month with a 7-day free trial); it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Regard
providers.description: Regard is an AI-powered clinical diagnosis and documentation platform for hospitals and health systems. It reviews 100% of a patient's electronic health record (EHR) to surface and recommend evidence-supported diagnoses, then generates clinical documentation at the point of care. Regard positions itself around "earning revenue through better care, not queries," spanning clinical notes, mid-revenue-cycle denial prevention and revenue capture, HCC risk-adjustment capture, and screening for care gaps. The company reports 12.9M+ recommended diagnoses accepted by clinicians and $50M+ in revenue generated for health systems. Regard integrates directly with EHRs rather than exposing a public developer API; its Health IT Module is ONC 2015 Cures Update certified. Backed by Foundry Group and Techstars. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Silo Finance
providers.description: Silo Finance is a decentralized, non-custodial lending protocol built around isolated money markets. Each market pairs a single collateral asset with a borrowable asset in its own risk silo, so the failure or manipulation of one asset cannot cascade into unrelated markets — the isolation model that distinguishes Silo from pooled lenders. The protocol is delivered as onchain smart contracts (Silo V1, V2 and V3) deployed across Ethereum and other EVM chains, with an application at silo.finance, developer and protocol-architecture documentation at docs.silo.finance, third-party security audits, and an open GitHub organization publishing the contracts, subgraph and indexer. Silo Finance is backed by Electric Capital and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a DeFi lending provider.

providers.name: Spirl
providers.description: Spirl is a non-human identity and access management (IAM) startup that in 2025 rebranded to Defakto (defakto.security); spirl.com now redirects to the Defakto site. The company secures automated systems — workloads, services, CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes, and AI agents — by replacing static secrets and hardcoded credentials with short-lived, cryptographically verifiable identities built on open workload-identity standards (SPIFFE/SPIRE style). Co-founded by Eli Nesterov (ex-ByteDance infrastructure) and Danny Oliveri, it targets the enterprise gap where organizations run millions of non-human identities protected only by static secrets. Defakto was named a 2025 Gartner Cool Vendor in Identity-First Security. It is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing site, blog, and security page but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, CLI, or developer portal — access is via demo request, so there is no API surface to enrich at this time.

providers.name: TransferRoom
providers.description: TransferRoom is football's real-time transfer marketplace, connecting clubs, agents and players to buy, sell and loan players and to recruit head coaches. Its API delivers verified, real-time market intelligence — Expected Transfer Value (xTV) benchmarks, player availability and deal-viability signals, contract-expiry and estimated-salary data, agent and coach representation, and head-coach ratings — returned as JSON for clubs to integrate directly into their own systems (SQL databases, BI dashboards, spreadsheets and code notebooks). Trusted by 800+ clubs across 130 leagues and 500+ agencies, covering 130,000+ players and 7,000+ head coaches, and powering 7,500+ transfer deals. The API is sales-gated: technical reference (endpoints, authentication, base URL) is provided to clubs on engagement and is not published publicly.

providers.name: Uptake
providers.description: Uptake Technologies is a Chicago-based industrial AI and predictive-maintenance software company founded in 2014 by Eric Lefkofsky and Brad Keywell. Its SaaS platform ingests telematics, sensor, fluid-analysis and work-order data from heavy commercial fleets and industrial assets, then applies machine-learning failure models — backed by an Asset Strategy Library of roughly 800 equipment types and tens of thousands of failure modes acquired with Asset Performance Technologies in 2018 — to predict component failure before it happens. Products include Uptake Fleet and Radar (predictive maintenance alerts), Compass (work-order data cleansing), Fusion (operational-technology data to cloud) and Scout (rules-based alerting), delivered through the fleet.uptake.com web application, a Geotab Marketplace add-in, and a customer-provisioned REST API gateway at api.uptake.com. Bosch announced its acquisition of Uptake in March 2026.

providers.name: UptimeHealth
providers.description: UptimeHealth is a healthcare operations platform for managing medical equipment service, compliance documentation, and facility maintenance across dental, medical, and veterinary practices from a single dashboard. The platform tracks devices, automates compliance tasks and logs, and coordinates repair service requests, reporting 73,000+ devices protected across 6,000+ facilities. UptimeHealth publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation — its platform (uptimecontroller.com) is a closed SaaS application.

providers.name: Vuori
providers.description: Vuori is a California-based performance athletic apparel and activewear brand founded in 2015 in Encinitas, offering men's and women's clothing built for training, running, yoga, and everyday wear. The direct-to-consumer business runs on a Shopify storefront at vuoriclothing.com plus a growing retail footprint, and is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners (and later SoftBank Vision Fund). Vuori publishes no public developer API or developer portal; it exposes a consumer web/mobile storefront, a help center, and a brand blog. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's real public web surface — its security.txt vulnerability-disclosure contact, domain-security posture, and customer-facing pages — rather than a developer program, which does not exist.

providers.name: Wayhome
providers.description: Wayhome (formerly Unmortgage) is a London-based property technology company founded in 2016 by Nigel Purves and Josef Wasinski. It offers "Gradual Homeownership" — a part-buy, part-rent alternative to a traditional mortgage in which a customer buys at least 5% of a home and pays rent on the remainder, gradually increasing their ownership stake over time. Wayhome pairs aspiring homeowners with institutional investors (including Allianz), letting people who can afford rent but cannot secure a conventional mortgage move into a home of their choice with a deposit as low as 5%. Wayhome is authorised and regulated in the United Kingdom. It is backed by fintech venture investors including Anthemis, Augmentum Fintech, Allianz X and Accelerated Digital Ventures. Wayhome operates as a consumer-facing service and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and domain-security surface.

providers.name: Wiz
providers.description: Wiz is a cloud-native application protection platform (CNAPP) that provides agentless security across AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and containers, covering CSPM, CWPP, CIEM, vulnerability management, DSPM, and threat detection in a unified security graph. The Wiz GraphQL API exposes inventory, issues, vulnerabilities, configurations, and reporting using OAuth 2.0 client credentials authentication.

providers.name: WizerMe
providers.description: WizerMe (Wizer) is an edtech platform used by more than 700,000 teachers to build interactive, self-grading digital worksheets. Educators turn existing PDFs and documents into engaging assessments with multiple-choice, video, audio, open-response, and puzzle question types, record video or audio instructions, apply differentiation rules, monitor student work in real time, schedule availability and time limits, and sync grades with Google Classroom. Students submit answers as text, audio, or video. Wizer offers a free tier (Wizer Create) and a premium tier (Wizer Boost) plus school and district plans, and is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Zubale
providers.description: Zubale is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of felicis, qed-investors and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ecommerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau
providers.description: The Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB), statutorily named the Tax and Trade Bureau, is a bureau of the United States Department of the Treasury. TTB regulates and collects federal excise taxes on alcohol, tobacco, firearms, and ammunition. The bureau enforces Federal laws and regulations related to alcohol and tobacco products, issues permits for producers, importers, and wholesalers, approves label applications for alcohol beverages, and provides open data on tax collections, permit holders, and approved product labels. TTB administers approximately $20 billion in annual federal excise tax collections from the alcohol and tobacco industries.

providers.name: Aledade
providers.description: Aledade is a physician-led public benefit corporation and national leader in value-based care, partnering with independent primary care practices, community health centers, and health systems. It pairs data analytics, guided clinical workflows, integrated care solutions, and payer contracts to help primary care organizations succeed in accountable care organizations (ACOs) and value-based payment models, improving patient outcomes while supporting the business sustainability of independent practices. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of gv, ivp, and lightspeed-venture-partners.

providers.name: AMC Networks
providers.description: AMC Networks is a global entertainment company that owns and operates distinctive cable television and streaming brands including AMC, BBC America, IFC, Sundance TV, and We TV, as well as the AMC+ streaming service. The company operates 33 FAST channels across 22 platforms and delivers digital advertising through its Audience+ data platform. AMC Networks provides affiliate partnership services, advertising solutions, and streaming content distribution through its network of cable and digital properties.

providers.name: Apron
providers.description: Apron is a London, UK-based financial technology company that helps small business owners, accountants, and bookkeepers automate supplier payments, payroll, expenses, and payment collection. The platform captures invoices, batches and pays bills directly from a business bank account, and reconciles transactions in real time with accounting software such as Xero and QuickBooks Online. Founded by Bogdan Uzbekov (an early Revolut operator), Apron serves more than 10,000 businesses and is an FCA-authorised Electronic Money Institution (firm reference 1004915), ISO 27001 certified, and regulated under the UK Payment Services Regulations 2017 and Electronic Money Regulations 2011. Apron does not currently publish a public developer API; it integrates as a consumer of the Xero and QuickBooks accounting APIs.

providers.name: BillionToOne
providers.description: BillionToOne is a molecular diagnostics company using proprietary single-molecule Quantitative Counting Template (QCT) technology to detect disease at the DNA level from cell-free DNA. Its Unity prenatal screening suite (Unity Complete, Unity Confirm, and Unity fetal antigen tests) delivers non-invasive prenatal testing from maternal blood at nine weeks, and its Northstar oncology line (Northstar Select and Northstar Response) provides liquid-biopsy therapy selection and real-time treatment-response monitoring. BillionToOne integrates with electronic medical records through a collaboration with Epic and delivers results through its provider and patient portals. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global, Norwest Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Bluecoat (Symantec)
providers.description: Blue Coat Systems was a web-security and network-forensics vendor best known for its ProxySG secure web gateway appliances, SSL Visibility, WebPulse/Global Intelligence Network threat intelligence, and cloud web security (the Web Security Service). Bain Capital led a consortium that took Blue Coat private in 2015; Symantec acquired the company in 2016, and Broadcom acquired Symantec's enterprise security business in 2019. Blue Coat's technology now ships inside Broadcom's Symantec Enterprise Cloud portfolio as Cloud Secure Web Gateway (Cloud SWG), Secure Web Gateway (ProxySG/ASG), SSL Visibility, CASB (CloudSOC), and DLP. Product documentation and REST APIs are published on the Broadcom TechDocs portal.

providers.name: Brisk Teaching
providers.description: Brisk Teaching is a K-12 education technology company that integrates AI directly into the tools teachers already use. Its platform spans three connected products: the Brisk Extension (which brings AI into Google Docs, Slides, PDFs, and YouTube), Brisk Boost (a safe, teacher-controlled, student-facing AI workspace), and Brisk Next (a web-based planning and instruction hub). Brisk helps educators give feedback, create instructional materials, change reading levels, inspect student writing, and generate presentations, lesson plans, rubrics, quizzes, IEP goals, and math problems. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Brisk publishes an llms.txt for AI representation and a public status page, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks its public surface.

providers.name: Bureau of Land Management
providers.description: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) is a U.S. government agency responsible for managing vast stretches of public lands across the country, primarily focused on activities like outdoor recreation, livestock grazing, mineral development, and energy production, aiming to sustain the health and diversity of these lands for future generations.

providers.name: Bureau of Ocean Energy Management
providers.description: The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) manages the nation's offshore resources in an environmentally and economically responsible way. BOEM oversees the responsible development of U.S. Outer Continental Shelf energy and mineral resources while protecting the environment and conserving natural resources.

providers.name: Canadian Tire Bank
providers.description: Canadian Tire Bank (operating as Canadian Tire Financial Services) is a federally regulated Schedule I bank, wholly owned by Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited and federally chartered in 2003. Headquartered in Oakville, Ontario with operations in St. Catharines and Welland, the bank is the financial-services arm of one of Canada's best-known retailers. It issues the Triangle Mastercard, Triangle World Mastercard, Triangle World Elite Mastercard, Gas Advantage and Cash Advantage Mastercards, and offers high-interest savings accounts and GICs, all tied to the Triangle Rewards loyalty program. On open finance, the bank exposes no first-party public developer API or banking API portal. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, overseen by the FCAC) is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer data access today is voluntary and aggregator-based — Canadian Tire Bank card and account data is reached through aggregators such as Finicity (by Mastercard), Flinks and Plaid rather than a first-party API. The cantire.com developer portal is run by the retail parent Canadian Tire Corporation, not the bank, is gated behind sign-in, and its TLS certificate expired in February 2026.

providers.name: Cents
providers.description: Cents is an all-in-one laundry business management platform for laundromats and dry cleaners. It combines point of sale, self-service machine payment systems, wash-and-fold order management, online ordering, pickup-and-delivery route management, memberships and recurring billing, inventory tracking, team management, marketing tools, customer-facing websites, commercial invoicing, and reporting and financial tools into a single operating system for local laundry businesses. Cents also offers an AI Receptionist team and laundry-first insurance, and has acquired Insight Systems and Laundroworks to extend support for dry cleaners and card-based self-service payment technology.

providers.name: Clearvector
providers.description: ClearVector is an identity-driven detection and response platform for cloud production environments. It attributes every action in real time to human, non-human, and third-party identities across AWS, GCP, and Azure, threading together activity across GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, cloud control planes, and runtime (EC2, Lambda, containers). Per-customer predictive behavioral models surface risky behavior, and one-click isolation contains compromised identities and resources without disrupting production. Offered as SaaS, an Enterprise plan, and a ClearVector Private SaaS deployment for teams that need complete infrastructure control. Backed by Menlo Ventures. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; ClearVector publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — the product is delivered through a login-gated application at app.clearvector.com.

providers.name: Corduro
providers.description: Corduro is a payments-as-a-service company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Southlake, Texas, offering a mobile, online, and point-of-sale payment platform for small businesses, enterprises, and organizations. Its platform enables merchants to accept credit-card and electronic-check payments, bill pay, recurring billing, text giving, and event and donation payments through a single intelligent payment gateway that is advertised to reduce processing fees by 20% or more. Corduro bundles eCommerce, Engage, Events, Text Giving, and Developer Tools products, provides embeddable iFrame and API-based payment integrations, and markets PCI compliance as a managed capability. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and enriched from the company's public web presence; Corduro publishes no public OpenAPI, developer portal, or API reference, gating developer/API access behind sales contact.

providers.name: CRS Credit API
providers.description: CRS Credit API delivers credit data-as-a-service for fast, compliant financial decisioning. The platform aggregates consumer and business credit, identity, fraud, and public records data from major bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion, LexisNexis, CIC, PitchPoint) through a single contract and developer interface.

providers.name: Defense Intelligence Agency
providers.description: The Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) is the U.S. Department of Defense combat support agency that produces, analyzes, and disseminates military intelligence on foreign militaries and operating environments to support warfighters, defense planners, and national-security policymakers. As an intelligence agency, DIA does not publish a general-purpose public API; its developer-facing surface is largely internal or restricted to the Intelligence Community. Public touchpoints include the GAMECHANGER policy analytics initiative, the DIA FOIA reading room, public news and article feeds, and procurement and recruiting portals.

providers.name: Domo
providers.description: Domo is a cloud-based software company that specializes in providing business intelligence tools for organizations. Their platform allows businesses to gather, analyze, and visualize data from various sources in order to make more informed decisions. Domo helps companies streamline their data management processes and gain valuable insights into their operations, sales, marketing, and overall performance.

providers.name: Eudia
providers.description: Eudia is an enterprise augmented-intelligence platform for in-house legal, compliance, and procurement teams at large organizations and government agencies. Its "Enterprise Brain" ingests a company's contracts, policies, precedents, and prior decisions and codifies the judgment of its legal experts into governed AI workflows, while "Expert Digital Twins" let business teams self-serve governed legal guidance without direct attorney involvement. Products span compliance automation, contracting, decision self-service, mergers and acquisitions, and litigation support, with connectors into Microsoft, Google Drive, SharePoint, Box, Salesforce, DocuSign, OnIt, and LinkSquares. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Eudia raised a Series A of up to $105M led by General Catalyst with Sierra Ventures, Floodgate, and Defy Partners. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity, trust, and security posture.

providers.name: Exa Finance
providers.description: EXA Finance is a French Web3 company, founded in 2021, that builds EXA Market — a peer-to-peer NFT and multi-asset marketplace on the Algorand blockchain. Because Algorand represents both fungible tokens and NFTs under the single ASA (Algorand Standard Asset) standard, the EXA Market protocol lets users bundle up to four assets into a "basket" and trade them in a single transaction, sell NFTs for any ASA rather than only the native ALGO token, make peer-to-peer offers, and run standard sales, normal and Dutch/reverse auctions, and multi-mints. Creators set an on-chain royalty fee of up to 15% globally against their creator address, payable in ALGO, USDC, USDT and other opted-in assets. The protocol is governed by the EXA token (ASA ID 1888888888) through the EXA Community DAO, whose EXRC/EXIP proposal lifecycle is modeled on Uniswap, dYdX, Tinyman and Blur. EXA raised a $2M seed round in January 2022 with Speedinvest, Lemniscap, Big Brain Holdings, Borderless Capital, Encode Club, Meld Ventures, 11-11 DG Partners and 0x Ventures. EXA Market publishes no public HTTP/REST API: its programmable surface is on-chain Algorand smart contracts (listing, offer and auction contracts, published as TEAL approval programs), reached through standard Algorand algod and indexer node APIs and the Algorand SDKs.

providers.name: Federato
providers.description: Federato is an AI-native insurance technology platform built for the full policy lifecycle, from submission through policyholder management. Its RiskOps-style tooling spans underwriting workflow, automated submission triage, portfolio and appetite alignment, rate/price/quote, a configurable forms engine, federated data infrastructure, and producer, partner, and policyholder portals. Federato serves insurance carriers, managing general agents (MGAs), MGA aggregators, and mutual insurers. The company is backed by Emergence Capital and announced a $100M Series D led by Goldman Sachs. No public API or open developer reference was found during enrichment; the developer documentation portal (Archbee) is magic-link protected, and the GitHub organization holds only forks of third-party infrastructure tools.

providers.name: Fishbrain
providers.description: Fishbrain is a Stockholm-based consumer technology company behind the largest social network and mobile app for recreational anglers, with a community of around 20 million fishermen and roughly 14 million logged catch locations. The app blends a social feed, a digital catch logbook with AI-powered species recognition, depth charts (from Garmin), local fishing reports with weather and bait intelligence, an AI-driven fishing-spot prediction map, and a searchable database of fishing regulations covering seasons, bag limits, and size rules. Fishbrain monetizes through a Fishbrain Pro subscription and is backed by Northzone and Seedcamp. It exposes no public developer API — api.fishbrain.com is a private backend for the iOS/Android apps — so this profile captures the company's public security, engineering, and web surface rather than an API.

providers.name: Foodspark
providers.description: Foodspark is a data-as-a-service platform that delivers real-time grocery, restaurant, and food-delivery data extracted from 100+ platforms including DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Instacart, McDonald's, Starbucks, and many others. Foodspark sells access to curated food and grocery datasets rather than a publicly documented self-serve API.

providers.name: Gaia
providers.description: Gaia (Gaia Family) is a value-based family-building company that makes fertility treatment financially accessible. Founded by Nader AlSalim after his own multi-year IVF journey, Gaia replaces unpredictable cycle-by-cycle IVF billing with fixed-price, all-inclusive plans and monthly payments, backed by a protection model that offers more tries — or money back — if treatment does not succeed. It partners with 180+ fertility clinics across the US and UK, covering IVF, egg freezing, embryo transfer, hormone and lab testing, and fertility navigation, and also offers fertility benefits to employers. This profile is a company lead (no public API surface) maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Gnowbe
providers.description: Gnowbe is an AI-powered workforce enablement and performance platform for enterprise learning, enablement, and alignment. It turns static content and communication into mobile-first microlearning experiences with AI-powered activation and execution tracking, so teams do not just learn but perform. Trusted by 500,000+ learners across 100+ countries, Gnowbe combines authoring, AI content creation, group-based delivery, completion and engagement analytics, and integrations (SSO/SAML, LMS/SCORM, xAPI/LRS, HR systems, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Zapier's 5,000+ tools). Gnowbe is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Go Micro
providers.description: Go Micro is a distributed systems framework for building microservices in Go, providing service discovery, load balancing, message encoding, RPC, and async messaging out of the box.

providers.name: Goals
providers.description: Goals (playgoals.com, formerly goals.co) is a free-to-play competitive football (soccer) video game studio backed by Northzone. It positions itself as a gameplay-first football game — "No scripts, no excuses, just football" — with fast, skill-based competitive matches, unique player squads, card-pack collection, ranked leaderboards, and multiple game modes across Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, and the Epic Games Store. A companion app lets players manage squads and open packs. This profile was surfaced as a Northzone portfolio company (consumer sector) and added to the API Evangelist network; the studio publishes a consumer game and a community surface (Discord, guides, leaderboards) but no public developer API.

providers.name: GreenSky
providers.description: GreenSky is a financial-technology company that powers point-of-sale consumer financing. Through a network of federally insured bank partners and enrolled merchants, GreenSky enables consumers to apply for and use installment loans and revolving credit lines at the point of sale, with programs concentrated in home-improvement and elective-healthcare financing. GreenSky Servicing, LLC (NMLS #1416362) originates and services the loan program on behalf of its lending partners. Merchants enroll to offer financing to their customers and manage applications through the GreenSky merchant portal, while consumers manage accounts and payments through the customer portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of ICONIQ Capital and QED Investors and added to the API Evangelist network. GreenSky is a consumer/merchant fintech with no public developer API surface; this profile is enriched with identity, link, and security metadata only.

providers.name: Gruve
providers.description: Gruve Inc. is an AI-driven enterprise services and technology company that helps large organizations adopt and secure artificial intelligence. Its portfolio spans private AI infrastructure (PulseAI, deployable in under two weeks for data sovereignty), AI-powered cybersecurity (AI SOC, digital forensics and incident response, and managed AI security services), Data & AI strategy and infrastructure, and Customer Experience delivered on Salesforce. Gruve targets enterprises of roughly 5,000 to 50,000 employees and serves CXOs, IT, security, and data leaders globally. Backed by Mayfield, the company operates a public trust center (SafeBase by Drata) attesting SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and ISO/IEC 42001:2023. This is a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network; Gruve is a services and platform provider and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Harpoon
providers.description: Harpoon is a no-code Kubernetes deployment platform that lets teams deploy commercial or open-source software to Kubernetes clusters in seconds using a drag-and-drop interface, without writing code or configuration scripts. It automates cloud account security, cluster provisioning and autoscaling across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and VMware, and integrates with CI/CD tooling such as GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Argo, Docker Hub and Harbor. The product is delivered as a hosted web application (app.harpooncorp.com) aimed at both startups and enterprises; it is surfaced here as an a16z portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass Harpoon publishes no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI or webhook surface.

providers.name: Hello Heart
providers.description: Hello Heart is a digital health company that combines a mobile app, connected blood-pressure monitors, a smart pill box, and the Nia AI assistant (trained on ACC/AHA guidelines) to help people proactively manage cardiovascular health. Sold primarily to employers, health plans, unions, and public-sector benefits programs as a covered heart-health benefit, the platform pairs self-monitoring with clinically-grounded, "safe AI" coaching to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiac risk. Hello Heart is HITRUST CSF certified, SOC 2 Type 2 audited, NIST CSF aligned, and HIPAA compliant, with data encrypted in transit and at rest and stored within U.S. borders. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public identity, security, and compliance posture.

providers.name: IBM Db2
providers.description: IBM Db2 is a family of data management products from IBM that includes relational and hybrid database servers running on cloud, distributed, and z/OS platforms, supporting transactional, analytical, and AI workloads. Db2 exposes RESTful services that let applications create, discover, execute, and manage user-defined services natively against the database, and IBM Db2 as a Service on IBM Cloud provides a managed REST API for administering and querying cloud-hosted Db2 databases. Authentication is performed via HTTP basic auth, client certificates, or IBM Cloud IAM Bearer tokens depending on the deployment.

providers.name: Irhythmtech
providers.description: iRhythm Technologies is a publicly traded (NASDAQ: IRTC) digital healthcare company specializing in ambulatory cardiac monitoring for the detection and management of heart arrhythmias. Its Zio service pairs a wearable single-lead ECG biosensor patch (Zio monitor and Zio AT) with FDA-cleared AI/deep-learning algorithms, qualified cardiac technician verification, and cloud-based data analytics to produce end-of-wear diagnostic reports for clinicians. The platform includes the ZioSuite clinician portal for report interpretation and patient management, the MyZio patient app for symptom logging and education, EHR integration, and telehealth workflows. iRhythm was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It does not publish a public developer API or documentation portal; enrichment is limited to public identity, trust, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Latenode
providers.description: Latenode is an enterprise-grade low-code integration and AI automation platform with prebuilt SaaS integrations and native access to top-tier LLMs. It combines the ease of no-code tools with the flexibility of low-code development for building automated workflows. Latenode supports inbound webhooks and JavaScript-based custom logic within scenarios but does not currently publish a public OpenAPI specification for an external REST API.

providers.name: LevelTen Energy
providers.description: LevelTen Energy operates a two-sided digital marketplace and transaction platform for carbon-free energy, describing itself as the transaction infrastructure for the energy transition. Clean energy buyers, advisors, project developers, utilities and financiers use the LevelTen Energy Marketplace to compare thousands of power purchase agreement (PPA) offers, run NPV and settlement cashflow analysis, evaluate risk scenarios and track a Development Maturity Score across projects in North America and Europe. The platform also covers granular certificates, hybrid and storage PPAs, and performance monitoring, alongside market intelligence products including MarketPulse, the LevelTen PPA Price Index and Market Transparency Reports. The marketplace is served by an authenticated API at api.levelten.energy, which is gated behind marketplace login and publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: Matic
providers.description: Matic is a digital insurance marketplace and independent insurance agency that lets consumers compare and buy home, auto, pet, umbrella, jewelry and other personal-lines insurance from a network of 60+ A-rated carriers in one place. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, Matic is best known for its embedded-insurance model: it integrates insurance shopping into the digital experiences of mortgage lenders, servicers, banks and other financial-services partners so borrowers and account holders can obtain coverage at the point of need. Matic is a licensed agency operating in all 50 states and is backed by investors including Anthemis. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; this enrichment pass confirms Matic operates as a consumer-facing insurance marketplace with a partner/embedded-insurance business but no publicly documented developer API surface.

providers.name: MediaCaption API
providers.description: A credit-billed REST API for retrieving public YouTube transcripts, with single and bulk transcript jobs, job-level webhooks, and AI transcription/translation capabilities. Backed by a public OpenAPI 3.1 contract with bearer/X-API-Key authentication.

providers.name: MoonLake AI
providers.description: Moonlake AI Inc. is a San Francisco based company building world models and simulation infrastructure for embodied AI. Its platform turns an image, video, or text description into physically accurate, simulation-ready 3D models of the world — assets shipped with baked-in physics and articulation (joints, ranges, drive limits) that export directly to USD, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, and MuJoCo. Teams generate sim environments and digital twins in hours instead of weeks via a hosted generation API. Moonlake is backed by Threshold (formerly DFJ), AIX Ventures, and NVIDIA's venture arm, and was named to the CB Insights AI 100 in 2026.

providers.name: MyTime
providers.description: MyTime is an all-in-one business management platform for retail service chains and franchises, combining point-of-sale (POS), online appointment scheduling, integrated payments, customer management, inventory, staff and payroll tools, loyalty, reputation management, and marketing automation across single- and multi-location operations. It serves beauty salons, barbershops, pet grooming, wellness spas, and learning services, offering omnichannel booking (web, Google Reserve, Instagram/Facebook, ClassPass) and analytics. MyTime runs a first-party API host (api.mytime.com) that backs its web and native iPhone/Android apps, and offers partner integrations (Stripe, QuickBooks, Shopify, ADP, Zapier), but does not publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI definition. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Naluri
providers.description: Naluri is a digital health and corporate wellness platform operating across Southeast Asia. It delivers Employee Assistance Programmes, chronic disease management (mental health, obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and cholesterol), health coaching and consultations, performance workshops, and Mental Health First Aid training for employers, insurers, and individuals. The company reports serving over one million members and 200-plus companies, and states it is certified for HIPAA, GDPR, and ISO/IEC 27001. No public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Observe.AI
providers.description: Observe.AI is a contact center artificial intelligence platform that deploys purpose-built AI agents across voice and chat to resolve customer inquiries end-to-end, assist frontline agents in real time, and evaluate performance at scale. Its conversation intelligence suite spans automated quality assurance, agent coaching, speech and sentiment analytics, and operational insights, with 250+ out-of-the-box integrations into CCaaS, CRM, and business-intelligence systems. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures, it was added to the API Evangelist network and enriched with its public trust, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Ordr
providers.description: Ordr provides AI-powered security for connected devices, delivering a Cyber Asset Attack Surface Management (CAASM) platform that discovers, classifies, and secures IT, IoT, OT, and IoMT devices across enterprise networks. The platform combines device intelligence, risk and vulnerability management, network segmentation, and zero-trust enforcement to move organizations from visibility to action. Ordr integrates with existing security and networking infrastructure (Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Fortinet, Aruba, Juniper) and serves healthcare, manufacturing, financial services, government, and retail sectors. The company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and enriched from Ordr's public web surface; Ordr does not publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Pluto
providers.description: Pluto (Pluto Health, trypluto.com now pluto.health) is an AI-powered clinical intelligence and care-delivery platform that unifies fragmented health data from roughly 90% of US health systems. It aggregates medical records, insurance data, and social determinants of health, then applies AI-driven clinical intelligence to surface care gaps, coordinate preventive care, screenings, vaccines and at-home lab testing, and match patients to clinical trials. Pluto offers turnkey, white-label, or API-based deployment of its clinical operations. It is backed by Sierra Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: Power
providers.description: Power (withpower.com) is a clinical-trial search and matching platform that helps patients find and enroll in research studies. It maintains a database of tens of thousands of active clinical trials searchable by condition, location, and drug type, and connects patients, providers, research coordinators, and trial sponsors. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Anthemis and CRV; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Prodigal
providers.description: Prodigal is an AI company building purpose-built agents and intelligence for the loan-servicing and debt-collections industry. Its products include proAgent (end-to-end collections automation across voice and digital), PIE (an intelligence layer trained on more than half a billion consumer-finance interactions), proCollect (omnichannel digital orchestration), proScore (propensity-to-pay scoring from 500+ consumer attributes), proPay (an AI-native self-serve payment portal), proNotes (automated call notes), proInsight (QA automation, scorecards, and revenue analytics), and proAssist (real-time agent assistance). Prodigal serves auto finance, collections, healthcare revenue-cycle management, and lending, integrating with dialers and contact-center platforms such as Five9, Genesys, NICE, TCN, and DialConnect. It is backed by Accel and Menlo Ventures. Prodigal exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and compliance program.

providers.name: Progressive Insurance
providers.description: One of the largest auto insurance providers in the United States offering personal auto, motorcycle, boat, RV, home, renters, and commercial insurance. Progressive is known for its direct-to-consumer model (1-800-PROGRESSIVE and progressive.com), its independent-agent channel, the comparative rate quoting experience, and the Snapshot usage-based insurance program that prices premiums against telematics-captured driving behaviour from a plug-in OBD-II dongle or the Snapshot mobile app. Progressive also runs the ForAgents agent portal and a public Developer Portal at developer.progressive.com that hosts embedded-quoting APIs for partners — including the Embedded Direct auto quoting API, the Commercial Auto Quoting product, and the Certificate of Insurance API — alongside private B2B integrations with comparative-rater carriers, agency-management systems, and telematics providers.

providers.name: Qevlar AI
providers.description: Qevlar AI is an autonomous Security Operations Center (SOC) platform that investigates every security alert the way a top analyst would — without playbooks, without hallucinations, and without adding headcount. Founded in 2023 by Ahmed Achchak and Hamza Sayah and headquartered in Paris, France, the company runs a proprietary graph-based AI orchestrator (not an LLM agent) that delivers deterministic, evidence-based investigations across the full security stack. As soon as an alert fires from SIEM/EDR tools, Qevlar autonomously pulls, enriches, and analyzes internal and external data, then returns a conclusive malicious/benign verdict, a full investigation report, and recommended remediation — typically in under three minutes, closing up to 80% of tickets automatically. The SaaS platform is SOC 2 Type 2 certified, hosted in the EU (Belgium) on GCP, and connects via API to 50+ security tools (Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, CrowdStrike, Cortex, Google SecOps, and more). It is trusted by Fortune Global 500 enterprises and leading MSSPs/MDRs across Europe and the US. Backed by EQT Ventures and Partech.

providers.name: Qognitive
providers.description: Qognitive, Inc. is an AI company that develops QCML (Quantum Cognition Machine Learning), an analytical AI architecture positioned as an alternative to classical statistical modeling. Its product, Hone, targets high-dimensional, multi-modal, and noisy structured data — claiming near-linear scaling with feature count and accuracy improvements over industry-standard models, with peer-reviewed backing in Nature Scientific Reports and Risk.net. Hone is distributed as first-party Python packages (hone-io community edition and hone-io-enterprise) exposing scikit-learn-compatible regression and classification wrappers. The company was surfaced as a Ribbit Capital portfolio company. There is no public REST/HTTP API surface; integration is via the Python SDK.

providers.name: RetailNext
providers.description: RetailNext is an AI-powered in-store retail analytics platform that helps physical retailers understand shopper behavior and optimize store operations. Its product suite spans traffic analytics (real-time foot-traffic counting and benchmarking across locations), shopper journey and zone insights (which layouts convert and where shoppers are lost), asset protection and loss prevention that combines video intelligence with shopper analytics, and Pulse AI, a conversational layer for answering retail questions in plain language. The platform is used by 600+ retailers across 100+ countries, including brands such as Macy's, Sephora, and Calvin Klein. RetailNext is a Battery Ventures portfolio company. It maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source infrastructure tooling and publishes a responsible-disclosure security program, but does not currently expose a publicly documented developer API or portal.

providers.name: Root Insurance
providers.description: Root is a U.S. app-first auto insurer that prices policies primarily on real driving behavior captured by smartphone telematics. The Root mobile app handles enrollment, telematics scoring, policy management, claims, and optional roadside assistance, with renters insurance as an add-on line. Root has reorganized its tech stack around APIs to power embedded auto insurance with partners such as Carvana and Hyundai Capital America; partner APIs are gated and not publicly documented. Note: Root Insurance (joinroot.com) is distinct from the unrelated Root Platform (rootplatform.com) insurtech in South Africa / UK.

providers.name: Secuvy
providers.description: Secuvy is an AI data filtering and data security platform that combines data discovery, classification, data security posture management, privacy automation, and AI governance into a single product. The platform automates detection and classification of sensitive data across hybrid and multi-cloud environments and prevents regulated data from leaking into AI tools, assistants, and inference pipelines. Secuvy offers more than 250 connectors covering AWS, Azure, GCP, Microsoft 365, Salesforce, Slack, Jira, ServiceNow, Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, MongoDB, and on-premise systems like Windows File Servers, SharePoint, and NFS. Authentication options include OAuth, SAML, and API key based integration, and developers can build custom connectors against any system with a public API. Public API reference documentation was not located during research; technical detail is provided through Secuvy's sales and onboarding teams.

providers.name: ServiceMax
providers.description: ServiceMax is asset-centric field service management (FSM) software that helps equipment manufacturers and service organizations maximize equipment uptime, optimize technician productivity, and streamline service delivery. Its cloud platform, built natively on the Salesforce platform (ServiceMax Core and Asset 360), spans work order and workflow management, scheduling and dispatch (Service Board), preventive and predictive maintenance, contract and entitlement management, parts and inventory, offline-capable mobile tools (ServiceMax Go), real-time technician collaboration (Zinc), and customer self-service (Engage). Founded in 2007 and acquired by PTC in 2023, ServiceMax integrates with PTC's IoT and PLM portfolio (ThingWorx, Windchill) and exposes its data and workflows through the underlying Salesforce API surface rather than a standalone public developer API.

providers.name: ShapeCI
providers.description: ShapeCI is software for industrials — a next-generation PDM (product data management) platform enabled by modern version control that helps hardware enterprises go from design to start of production in weeks rather than years. It brings a Git-style workflow to hardware and CAD: teams and projects hold design files under version control with merge requests, documents, and the ability to review 3D models in-browser and auto-sync engineering knowledge with the model-base. A desktop Connector application lets engineers clone a project, create workstreams, and publish or sync changes. ShapeCI is currently an invite-only beta and does not publish a public developer API; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Sofia
providers.description: Sofía is a 100% Mexican digital health insurance company that modernizes traditional medical coverage for enterprises, individuals, and families. Its plans combine zero-deductible major and minor medical care, preventive care with an assigned primary-care physician, and unlimited no-cost video consultations, all managed through a mobile app and an HR administrative portal. Sofía operates its own integrated medical network (SofíaMed) of hospitals and specialists, offers add-ons such as maternity, mental health, dental, and international coverage, and reimburses claims in an average of five business days. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Sofía positions insurance as a digital-first, member-centric health experience rather than a paper policy.

providers.name: Structure
providers.description: Structure (Structure Financial Inc.) is a Web3 platform for designing, backtesting, and deploying fully automated, permissionless crypto trading strategies without writing code. Its visual strategy editor and AI-assisted code generation let users build algorithmic strategies that compile to Rust and deploy non-custodially to decentralized exchanges including Hyperliquid, Drift, and Jupiter; strategies receive trading-only permissions so funds never leave the user's vault. The company documents live, paper, and backtest execution paths and references MCP-agent and code-based access alongside its no-code visual interface. Founded by MIT and Jump Trading alumni and backed by the investors behind Coinbase and Solana.

providers.name: Suzy
providers.description: Suzy is an AI-driven consumer insights platform that unifies quantitative surveys (Suzy Insights), qualitative research (moderated Suzy Live IDIs and AI-moderated Suzy Speaks voice interviews), real-time cultural trend intelligence (Suzy Signals), and on-demand access to 1M+ verified consumers protected by BIOTIC fraud detection (Suzy Audiences). Its AI Suite adds screeners, summaries, themeing, and predictive heatmaps so enterprise brand, product, marketing, shopper, and insights teams can validate ideas and move at the speed of culture. Surfaced as a foundry-group portfolio company and enriched from public web sources; Suzy publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Tabnine
providers.description: Tabnine provides AI code completion, chat, and agentic workflows across IDEs and CLI, with strong support for SaaS, VPC, and air-gapped on-prem deployments. The Enterprise Context Engine indexes a customer's codebase, dependencies, and architecture. Tabnine's consumer surface is via IDE plugins (VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse) and the Tabnine CLI; there is no general-purpose public REST inference API for end-developers.

providers.name: Tech Soft 3D
providers.description: Tech Soft 3D builds developer SDKs and enterprise applications that power 3D data exchange, visualization, and analysis across engineering, manufacturing, and design. Its HOOPS toolkits (Exchange for CAD data translation and access, Visualize for high-performance 3D graphics, Access, Mesh, Solve, and Envision) are licensed to OEMs and independent developers building CAD, CAM, CAE, and PLM software, and it also distributes Siemens Parasolid and Polygonica. Alongside the native toolkits it publishes the HOOPS Visualize Web Components (open, first-party npm packages), SpinFire enterprise viewing/conversion apps, and OEM technologies such as AutoCAD OEM, Inventor OEM, and RealDWG. Tech Soft 3D is backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Tendo Systems
providers.description: Tendo (Tendo Systems) is a healthcare technology company founded in 2020 by siblings Dan and Jen Goldsmith, building software, analytics, and healthcare marketplaces on a next-generation platform that connects patients, clinicians, and providers across the fragmented care experience. Its application suite spans Tendo Insights (clinical quality and financial analytics), Tendo QDI (clinical documentation integrity and workflow optimization), Tendo Outreach (targeted patient engagement), and Care Connect, a shoppable bundled-procedure marketplace built on its 2023 acquisition of MDsave. Tendo does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or open developer portal; its documentation and support portals are gated behind authentication. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's public identity and security posture.

providers.name: TMRW Life Sciences *
providers.description: TMRW Life Sciences is a medical technology company that builds the world's first and only FDA-cleared automated platform for the safe management and storage of frozen eggs and embryos used in IVF and fertility treatment. Its cryo-storage hardware combines robotic specimen handling with digital tracking, chain-of-custody monitoring, and real-time visibility for fertility clinics and their patients, replacing manual, paper-based handling of irreplaceable reproductive tissue. Deployed at clinic networks including CCRM Fertility, Pinnacle Fertility, RFC, and IVIRMA North America. TMRW is a private company backed by GV (Google Ventures). It publishes a Security & Trust program (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27018) but does not expose a public developer portal, API, or specification surface.

providers.name: Trovy
providers.description: Trovy (Trovy Technologies, Inc.) is a Kleiner Perkins-backed fintech building "the homeowner platform" -- consumer credit products that turn home equity into a flexible financial tool. Its flagship Trovy HELOC Card is a credit card powered by home equity with variable APRs as low as 5.99%, alongside the Trovy 1Loan home-equity loan, with preapproval in minutes and rewards, balance-transfer, and payment-calculator features. Trovy is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API, docs, or SDK surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Upstream
providers.description: Upstream is a no-code, full-stack platform for launching and operating DAOs (decentralized autonomous organizations), letting communities create a DAO with a Gnosis multi-signature wallet, DAO contract, and vote delegation contract without technical experience. The platform blends on-chain smart contracts (built on OpenZeppelin, audited by Upshield) with off-chain forums, proposals, polls, and events, and maintains the open-source Fortuna service that indexes ERC20/ERC721/ERC1155 transfer events on Ethereum. Upstream is backed by Bloomberg Beta. The company does not currently publish a public developer API; its backend at api.upstreamapp.com is undocumented and product documentation lives at guide.upstreamapp.com.

providers.name: XAG
