Cherry does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: ChipAgents
providers.description: ChipAgents is the Agentic AI Chip Design Environment, helping semiconductor engineers iterate on chip design and verification up to 10x faster by collaborating with AI agents inside their favorite code editor. The platform spans design and verification workflows, coverage analysis, and Root Cause Analysis (RCA), surfaced through a project dashboard and the ChipAgents CLI, and is powered by the company's first model, Renoir. ChipAgents is delivered as a managed, authenticated web application (agent.chipagents.ai) rather than a public API; the company holds a SOC 2 Type II attestation and is backed by Micron, Samsung, MediaTek, and Bessemer Venture Partners, with a team drawn from Cadence, Synopsys, and Mentor Graphics.

providers.name: Click Mechanic
providers.description: ClickMechanic is the UK's leading online car-repair marketplace, founded in 2012, that connects car owners with vetted mobile mechanics and independent garages for repairs, servicing, diagnostics, and MOTs. Customers enter their registration and symptoms to get an instant fixed-price quote, then book a vetted mechanic for same- or next-day work at home or the roadside, with payment taken only after the job is completed. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. ClickMechanic operates a consumer- and mechanic-facing web platform (Ruby on Rails on Heroku) and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API catalog at this time; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CodeKarma
providers.description: CodeKarma is a production intelligence platform that maps 100% of production traffic directly to source code, giving engineering teams and AI agents code-level visibility into how software actually behaves in production. Its products include KarmaLens (an IDE plugin for JetBrains and VS Code surfacing dead code, method frequency, and performance hotspots), KarmaDomain (live API-level dependency graphs across microservices, databases, and async systems), KarmaPulse (an operations command center with API health, error drift, and AI root cause analysis), and KarmaIQ (an MCP server that feeds production context to AI coding agents such as Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and Claude). Deployed as managed SaaS or bring-your-own-cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), CodeKarma is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and collects only behavioral telemetry — no PII, payloads, or request bodies. Founded by Anantharam Vanchi Prakash and Priyanka Nahata, based in Bengaluru, India, and backed by Prosus, Accel, Xeed Ventures, SenseAI Ventures, and Stargazer Ventures.

providers.name: Defense Logistics Agency
providers.description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is the U.S. Department of Defense combat support agency that manages a global supply chain spanning roughly five million items in nine supply chains plus storage, distribution, fuel, construction, and disposition missions. DLA operates an extensive catalog of business applications used by suppliers, the military services, and federal partners. Most DLA applications require account registration and operate behind authentication; public-facing surfaces include the DLA Internet Bid Board System (DIBBS), the DLA Disposition Services storefront, the FedMall procurement marketplace, and federated logistics search tools.

providers.name: Defense Security Cooperation Agency
providers.description: The Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA) is the U.S. Department of Defense agency that leads, directs, and manages security cooperation programs and resources to support U.S. policy and interests with foreign partners. DSCA administers the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program, Foreign Military Financing (FMF) execution, International Military Education and Training (IMET), and humanitarian assistance programs. Public-facing surfaces include the Major Arms Sales notifications published in cooperation with Congress, the DSCA newsroom and library, and the Security Cooperation Workforce certification portal. DSCA does not publish a general-purpose developer API; partner-nation systems interact through controlled, government-to-government channels such as the Security Cooperation Information Portal (SCIP).

providers.name: Defense Threat Reduction Agency
providers.description: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) is the U.S. Department of Defense combat support agency that counters and deters weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and improvised threats. DTRA leads the chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and high-yield explosive (CBRNE) mission for DoD and supports the Cooperative Threat Reduction (CTR) Program with partner nations. Public-facing surfaces include the DTRA website, the DTRA Information Analysis Center (DTRIAC) for technical reports, the DTRA Mission Network public information, and small-business and broad-agency-announcement procurement portals. DTRA does not publish a general-purpose developer API; partner systems interact through controlled, government-to-government channels.

providers.name: Denticon
providers.description: Denticon is a cloud-based dental practice management platform built for dental service organizations (DSOs) and multi-location group practices, owned and operated by Planet DDS (which also owns Cloud 9 Ortho and Apteryx imaging). The Denticon API program - relaunched in July 2024 on a new developer portal powered by Azure API Management - exposes RESTful APIs, webhooks, and batch data extracts covering patient, appointment, financial/ledger, insurance and claims (Revenue Cycle Management), clinical, and practice/office data, with OAuth 2.0 auth, an event-driven architecture for synchronized updates, and writebacks into Denticon. API access is partner-gated - Planet DDS must approve vendors and each client practice authorizes vendor access to specific office locations (OIDs). Public documentation exists, but keys and interactive access require program enrollment, so the endpoint surface below is modeled from the published API categories rather than a downloadable OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Drivio
providers.description: Drivio (Drivio Technologies Pvt Ltd) is a tech-enabled, omni-channel two-wheeler financing marketplace in India that connects motorcycle, scooter, and electric-vehicle buyers with banks and NBFCs. Founded in 2022 by Saurabh Tripathi and Ankur Bhardwaj and headquartered in the Delhi NCR region (Gurugram / New Delhi), the platform offers EMI calculators, instant eligibility checks, curated finance offers, vehicle comparison, and same-day loan approval and disbursal through lending partners including IDFC First Bank, Bajaj Auto Credit, L&T Financial Services, HDB Financial Services, Moneyplus Financial Services, and Arthmate. Drivio is an ISO/IEC 27001 certified company and is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Duna
providers.description: Duna is an AI-native business identity platform for KYB (Know Your Business), KYC (Know Your Customer), AML (Anti-Money Laundering), and lifecycle compliance. It accelerates enterprise business onboarding by turning compliance policy into auditable code via a policy engine, using AI agents for document verification and periodic reviews, with deep localization across 210+ business registries and 7+ languages. Duna serves fintechs, banks, and platforms including Plaid, Moss, and Bol, and is backed by Index Ventures. Note: docs.duna.com is password-protected, so no public API reference, OpenAPI, or developer portal was available at enrichment time.

providers.name: easyJet
providers.description: easyJet Airline Company Limited is a British low-cost short-haul carrier registered in England (company number 03034606, registered office Hangar 89, London Luton Airport, Luton, Bedfordshire, LU2 9PF), flying a point-to-point network that its own trade pages describe as connecting more than 155 airports across 35 countries. Its home market is the United Kingdom and its commercial centre of gravity is intra-European leisure and short-haul business traffic, extended by the easyJet holidays package business and by ancillary products (seat selection, hold and large cabin bags, Flex, Pass Extra, Smart+, Inclusive and Inclusive Plus fare bundles). easyJet sits at the direct end of the airline distribution chain. It was built without a GDS dependency and still sells the overwhelming majority of its seats through its own website and app; agency and OTA access exists but is a controlled secondary channel rather than the primary rail. That channel is governed by a published Distribution Charter (version March 2026) which permits a Reseller to access easyJet Data in exactly two ways — "via an easyJet Approved Channel which has entered into an API agreement with easyJet" or "directly via the easyJet API, if the Reseller has a Direct API Agreement with easyJet" — and which explicitly forbids screen scraping and any other automated extraction. easyJet publishes the list of Approved Channels and a per-partner functionality matrix current to the end of May 2026: Amadeus, Anaxys, Bewotec, Duffel, JFA Systems, Kyte, Paxport, Peakwork, Sabre, Travelfusion, Travelport, Traveltek, Viaxoft and Ypsilon. Its API posture, stated honestly, is commercial-agreement-gated and undocumented. There is no developer portal — developer, developers, docs, apis, ndc, partner, partners, trade, agent, sandbox, dev, portal, connect and xml subdomains of easyjet.com all fail to resolve — and no machine-readable contract of any kind is published: no OpenAPI, no Swagger, no AsyncAPI, no GraphQL schema, no security.txt, no llms.txt and no .well-known API catalogue. Two real API hostnames do exist, api.easyjet.com and b2b.easyjet.com, but both sit behind Akamai and return HTTP 403 Access Denied on every path probed. Just as importantly, easyJet is not an NDC carrier: the March 2026 charter never mentions NDC, easyJet does not appear on ndctracker.com's list of 73 airlines with launched or in-development NDC programmes, and its aggregators describe the connection as a direct-connect API rather than an NDC one — Duffel labels it "Direct Connect". A reseller therefore integrates against a bilateral, proprietary, unpublished interface under an English-law contract that easyJet may amend without notice and under which it reserves the right to restrict, suspend or terminate access and to cancel bookings already made. A second enrichment pass on 2026-07-28 did find one live, anonymously reachable easyJet integration surface the first pass missed: the easyWidget / easyDom partner component platform at brand.easyjet.com, a hosted JavaScript widget service that partner and white-label sites embed for easyJet page chrome and for easyJet customer sign-in, registration and visitor recognition. It is undocumented, partner-scoped by a query-string partner identifier and built on legacy jQuery, but it is real and it is the only easyJet interface that answers a stranger with a 200. The REST hostnames stay closed, and this record stays honest about the difference: only what can be verified is catalogued, and an Akamai-gated hostname is still not listed as an API.

providers.name: Edyoucated
providers.description: Edyoucated is a German SaaS company offering an AI-powered corporate learning and skills-management platform for mid-to-large enterprises. The product combines a learning management / learning experience system (central management of training, mandatory compliance training, seminar administration, AI-assisted content creation, blended learning, and learning analytics) with skills management (skill cataloging, assessments, gap analysis, expert identification, and career guidance) to give organizations a common language for skills and personalized learning pathways. It also offers consulting for custom skill-taxonomy development. Customers include Deutsche Bahn, BASF, Shopware, and Finanz Informatik. Edyoucated is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer/API surface, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation.

providers.name: Eve
providers.description: Eve (branded EveOS) is an AI operating system purpose-built for plaintiff and personal-injury law firms, founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Mateo, California. The platform works alongside attorneys across the entire case lifecycle - intake and lead qualification, document and medical-record review, medical chronology generation, case and risk analysis, damages calculation, and case management - bringing every case, attorney, and dollar into one place. Eve integrates with practice-management systems such as Clio, is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and HIPAA compliant, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Menlo Ventures. Eve is a closed SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Foresight Diagnostics
providers.description: Foresight Diagnostics is a CLIA-certified, CAP-accredited cancer diagnostics company founded in 2020 in Boulder, Colorado by Stanford physicians and scientists, and since February 2026 a wholly owned subsidiary of Natera. Its Foresight CLARITY minimal residual disease (MRD) platform is a liquid-biopsy test powered by proprietary PhasED-Seq phased-variant sequencing and bioinformatics, detecting circulating tumor DNA at an analytical sensitivity below one part per million across lymphoma, lung and other solid tumors. The company sells laboratory testing services to biopharma sponsors, academic researchers and clinicians rather than software: it operates a central laboratory and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Got
providers.description: Got is a human-friendly and powerful HTTP request library for Node.js with support for streams, retries, and pagination.

providers.name: Hawthorne
providers.description: Hawthorne is an internet-first men's personal care and grooming brand founded in 2016 in New York City (a Techstars alum, later Series B). It sells personalized, long-lasting fragrance and grooming products — cologne, deodorant, body wash, face and hair care — tuned to a customer's body chemistry and lifestyle through an onboarding quiz and a smart-subscription model built around its "Surround Scent" technology. The direct-to-consumer storefront at hawthorne.co runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface: a published /llms.txt and /agents.md, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect discovery, and a live Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint so AI shopping agents can search the catalog, build a cart, and complete a buyer-approved checkout.

providers.name: hyperexponential
providers.description: hyperexponential (hx) is a London-based insurtech that builds the #1 pricing and underwriting decision platform for commercial property & casualty (P&C) insurance. Its platform - spanning the Hyperoperator agentic assistant, a no-code Workflow Builder, Calculation Engines, and Portfolio Intelligence - lets actuaries and underwriters build, deploy, and iterate pricing models and underwriting workflows without heavy engineering. Carriers use hx to automate submission triage, risk assessment, renewals, portfolio monitoring, and regulatory compliance, with top global carriers running $75bn+ in annual commercial P&C premium on the platform. hyperexponential is backed by a16z and Battery Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer, security, and compliance surface; hx does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI, so this repo is enriched from identity, trust-center, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Ingresse
providers.description: Ingresse is a Brazilian ticketing-as-a-service (TaaS) platform that powers event ticket sales, access control, and the attendee experience for organizers and partners. Its public developer platform lets integrators build tools and services on top of Ingresse — creating events, selling and validating tickets, managing users, and handling payments — through a versioned REST API (v1 and v2) authenticated with an individually issued API key. Ingresse publishes first-party SDKs for JavaScript/Node, Android, iOS, and PHP, plus message-queue libraries, and hosts its reference documentation on a ReadMe developer portal. Ingresse is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: IXL Learning
providers.description: IXL Learning is a K-12 personalized practice platform with 17,000+ skills across Math, Language Arts, Science, Social Studies, and Spanish, plus the IXL Real-Time Diagnostic and skill recommendations. IXL is sold primarily as a SaaS subscription to families, teachers, schools, and districts. Its integration surface is school-rostering and SSO, not a public developer API: IXL supports Clever (SSO + rostering), ClassLink (SSO + OneRoster auto-rostering), OneRoster CSV/REST, LTI, Google Classroom, and SAML SSO for district deployments. There is no public REST API portal, no published OpenAPI, and no partner developer program.

providers.name: JOLYN
providers.description: JOLYN is an athletic swimwear and apparel brand for competitive and team swimming, water polo, and aquatics, known for durable, functional practice and racing suits, team uniforms, and active lifestyle apparel. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, JOLYN publishes no first-party developer API — its direct-to-consumer storefront at jolyn.com (jolynclothing.com redirects here) is Shopify-hosted. That platform exposes a genuine agent-native commerce surface: a published /llms.txt with agent instructions, OpenID Connect discovery for the Shopify Customer Account API, and a live Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for buyer-approved, agent-driven shopping and checkout.

providers.name: Josys
providers.description: Josys is a SaaS and IT asset management platform providing automated provisioning, license optimization, and device management. Josys publishes a developer API for programmatic access to the platform.

providers.name: Kixeye
providers.description: KIXEYE Inc. is a video game developer and publisher founded in 2009 and headquartered in Victoria, British Columbia, with staff across Canada and the United States. KIXEYE creates, develops, and publishes massively multiplayer online real-time strategy (MMORTS) games for browsers, tablets, and smartphones, including Battle Pirates, War Commander, War Commander: Rogue Assault, and Rise of Firstborn. An early innovator in the free-to-play genre, KIXEYE operates long-lived live-service game worlds with monthly events, alliances, and competitive leaderboards for millions of players worldwide. KIXEYE is part of the Stillfront Group. KIXEYE publishes no public developer program or partner API; its api.kixeye.com host is a private game-services backend that exposes an OpenID Connect discovery document and JWKS for token verification. The company does maintain a public GitHub organization of open-source infrastructure libraries (chassis, kixmpp, janus, scout) used to build its own cloud services.

providers.name: KoRo
providers.description: KoRo (KoRo Handels GmbH) is a Berlin-based direct-to-consumer food retailer that sells nuts, dried fruit, nut butters, snacks, protein products, baking ingredients and drugstore goods in bulk packaging at wholesale-style prices, shipping across Europe from country storefronts in Germany (korodrogerie.de), Austria, Switzerland, France, Italy and the Benelux/EU shop at koro.com. Founded in 2014 and backed by HV Capital and Partech, KoRo runs a headless commerce stack — a Shopware 6 backend fronted by a Nuxt storefront deployed on Vercel — and publishes its engineering work as open source through the KoRoHandelsGmbH GitHub organization, including a Nitro-based Shopware Store-API proxy and several Shopware 6 build-tooling packages on npm under the @korodrogerie scope. KoRo publishes no public developer portal, no documented partner or commerce API, and no API specifications; its Store-API surface is internal and gated behind per-sales-channel access keys.

providers.name: Lennar
providers.description: Lennar Corporation is a Fortune 500 company and one of the leading homebuilders of new homes for sale in the United States. Lennar operates an internal Azure-hosted API Management developer portal where Lennar developers and partners discover and consume Lennar Corporation APIs. Public OpenAPI artifacts have not been observed; access generally requires sign-in and partner approval.

providers.name: Lennox International
providers.description: Lennox International is a global leader in the heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration markets, providing climate control solutions for residential and commercial applications. Lennox does not publish a general developer portal for HVAC system access. Smart-home integrations with the iComfort S30, E30, and M30 thermostat product lines are delivered through partnerships (Control4, Amazon Alexa, Apple HomeKit, Google Assistant, IFTTT) and through community-maintained, reverse-engineered Python and TypeScript libraries.

providers.name: Locale
providers.description: Locale is a no-code workflow automation platform that lets operations, data, and engineering teams build, run, and monitor automated workflows without writing glue code. Its visual builder chains together apps and actions — HTTP requests, AI Actions, run-your-own code, email, Slack, PostgreSQL, Sendgrid, and Fireflies.ai — with flow controls such as conditional branching, delays, and list iterators, then passes data between steps to orchestrate real business processes. Workflows can be built, connected, debugged, and published from the Locale app, and the platform positions itself as an operational automation layer for teams that want internal alerting and process automation without a heavy engineering lift. Locale is backed by a16z. This profile was enriched from Locale's public documentation surface (docs.locale.ai); Locale publishes no first-party public REST API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Monarch Tractor
providers.description: Monarch Tractor is a Livermore, California agricultural-technology company that builds the MK-V, a fully electric, driver-optional smart tractor, together with WingspanAI (Wingspan Ag Intelligence) — an AWS-hosted farm-management and fleet-telemetry platform that collects in-field video, machine telemetry, energy and emissions data from connected tractors and presents it to growers through web and mobile apps. The company markets an "open ecosystem" in which third parties integrate with the MK-V and WingspanAI, and has pivoted toward selling autonomy as software and licensing its autonomy stack to other equipment makers. Monarch publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the WingspanAI platform is reachable only through a customer login.

providers.name: NewCore
providers.description: NewCore is an enterprise identity-security company building an identity platform that governs both human and AI-agent identities across the enterprise. Its three pillars are Identity Discovery (continuously discovering and mapping every identity across directories, PAM, shadow systems, and AI infrastructure), Identity Security (breach prevention through phishing-resistant authentication and device-bound sessions that cannot be stolen or replayed), and Human + AI Agent Governance (minimum-access provisioning, full lifecycle management, and support for ephemeral agentic workloads). NewCore is backed by Index Ventures. It sells to enterprises via demo request and publishes a trust center (SOC 2 Type II, CSA STAR Level 1, GDPR, CCPA) but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: OpenEvidence
providers.description: OpenEvidence is a clinical decision-support search platform that uses generative AI grounded in peer-reviewed medical literature to answer clinical questions for verified clinicians. The product is free for U.S. licensed clinicians and is monetized through pharmaceutical advertising; partnerships include the New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA, NCCN, and the Cochrane Library. As of 2026 it serves more than 860,000 verified clinicians. OpenEvidence does not currently expose a public self-service developer API.

providers.name: Over
providers.description: Overworld is an open-science AI research lab building interactive world models - AI-generated video environments that respond in real time to text prompts and controller input at game-level framerates. Its open-source World Engine is a Python inference library that loads Waypoint world models and LoRA adapters from HuggingFace to generate playable, promptable worlds locally or in the browser. Founded by Louis Castricato (CEO) and Shahbuland Matiana (Head of Mathematical Research), both formerly of CarperAI and Stability AI, the team operates openly and publishes its infrastructure as public open-source repositories. Overworld does not currently expose a hosted REST API; its primary developer artifact is the first-party world_engine Python SDK.

providers.name: Pico
providers.description: Pico was a creator-monetization and CRM platform for online creators, publishers, and media companies, built in New York and backed by Bloomberg Beta. It combined an audience CRM with email capture, landing pages, paywalls, memberships, and subscription payments in a single tool so creators could identify their audience, gate premium content, and convert readers into paying members. Pico raised a $6.5M round in 2021 ("Pico 2.0") and a $10M Series A in 2023, when it rebranded to Hype (hype.co) and refocused on link-in-bio, lead generation, and growth tools for creators, gyms, coaches, and athletes. In February 2026 Hype was acquired by MMA.inc and the product was wound down. The developer API — authenticated with an X-Api-Key header and documented at docs.trypico.com — is retired: the API host api.trypico.com no longer resolves, the reference bucket has been deleted, and hype.co now serves only an acquisition notice directing users to support@hype.co.

providers.name: Privoxy
providers.description: Privoxy is a non-caching web proxy with advanced filtering capabilities for enhancing privacy, modifying web page content, and managing cookies.

providers.name: Rapidminer
providers.description: RapidMiner (now Altair RapidMiner / Altair AI) is a data science and machine learning platform that unites data preparation, machine learning, and predictive model deployment in a visual, low-code environment. The developer surface is centered on the official `rapidminer` Python package for interacting with Altair AI Studio and Altair AI Hub — reading and writing data, running and scheduling processes, managing git-based versioned projects and connections, and calling deployed Web API and Scoring endpoints — plus a Java/Python extension SDK for building custom operators. AI Hub authenticates via OAuth (offline token against a Keycloak-style authentication server). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Earlybird; RapidMiner was acquired by Altair, now part of Siemens.

providers.name: sophiagenetics
providers.description: SOPHiA GENETICS (NASDAQ SOPH) is a healthcare technology company democratizing data-driven medicine through its cloud-based SOPHiA DDM Platform, which analyzes genomic, radiomic, and multimodal data to support clinicians and researchers across oncology, hereditary disorders, rare diseases, and precision medicine. The platform spans SOPHiA DDM for Genomics, Multimodal, and Radiomics, plus Alamut Visual Plus for variant interpretation and the OncoPortal knowledge base. The product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS platform; no public developer API or portal is currently published.

providers.name: Sydney Airport
providers.description: Sydney Airport Corporation Limited (ACN 082 578 809) operates Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport (IATA SYD, ICAO YSSY), Australia's principal international gateway, under private ownership by the Sydney Aviation Alliance consortium since its 2022 ASX delisting. In the travel distribution chain it is infrastructure rather than an intermediary - it sells no seats, holds no inventory, issues no PNRs, and sits outside the GDS and IATA NDC value chain entirely, monetising aeronautical charges, car parking, retail concessions and property instead. Its API posture is effectively nil - Sydney Airport publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI, and no terms of use for machine access. Its public website is backed by undocumented JSON endpoints under /_a/ that return live flight and security wait-time data with no published contract, while its only credentialed partner surface, InfoSYD, is gated behind a ForgeRock OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect identity provider at id.syd.com.au and is restricted to airlines, ground handlers and on-airport tenants. The published terms of use expressly prohibit automated retrieval, scraping and indexing of the site, so there is public data but no public interface - and no documented exit path beyond an Australian Privacy Principle 12 personal-information access request.

providers.name: Teabox
providers.description: Teabox is a premium loose-leaf tea brand and direct-to-consumer e-commerce company backed by Accel. It sources fresh Darjeeling, Assam, Nilgiri and other Indian teas direct from gardens and ships them globally through its online store. The storefront runs on Shopify, which exposes an agent-commerce surface built on the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP): a hosted shopping MCP endpoint, a machine-readable llms.txt / agents.md, and OpenID Connect authentication via the Shopify Customer Account API (including a customer-account MCP scope). Buyer checkout always requires explicit human approval. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and enriched from Teabox's public agent-facing surfaces.

providers.name: TemperPack
providers.description: TemperPack is a Richmond, Virginia based sustainable packaging manufacturer, founded in 2015 and a Certified B Corporation, that designs and manufactures curbside recyclable and compostable alternatives to expanded polystyrene (EPS) and single-use plastic for cold chain and protective shipping. Its three material platforms are ClimaCell, a starch-and-paper thermal liner for cold chain shipments; Green Cell Foam, a certified compostable starch-based insulation with EPS-level performance; and WaveKraft, paper-based cushioning produced on demand. Products span cushioning, mailers, qualified shippers and stock shippers, serving life sciences, food and beverage, pet and veterinary, wine, and packaging distribution customers from ISO 9001:2015 certified plants in Richmond VA, Lansing MI and Las Vegas NV, with in-house ISTA thermal and mechanical testing at its Proving Ground lab. TemperPack operates a customer portal for order tracking, thermal testing results, billing and WaveKraft analytics, and an e-commerce store, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition or developer portal as of August 2026.

providers.name: TicketRev
providers.description: TicketRev (TICKR Holdings, Inc.) is a buyer-first ticketing platform for live sports and entertainment, founded in 2022. Its marketplace lets fans name their own price on tickets while giving teams and venues offer-based selling, flow purchasing, seat upgrades, and premium-inventory tools. Products span four solutions - Core (offer-based purchases), Breeze (flow purchasing), Upgrades (in-seat upgrades), and Premium (premium seating revenue) - and are used by MLB clubs including the Houston Astros, Miami Marlins, and Tampa Bay Rays. TicketRev is backed by Soma Capital, Groove Capital, 500 Global, and Techstars. The company publicly commits to SOC 2 Type II and PCI DSS security and compliance. No public developer API surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: TipLink
providers.description: TipLink is a Solana wallet-link platform that lets anyone create a shareable link or QR code holding crypto or an NFT, so a recipient can claim digital assets without first setting up a wallet. It ships as first-party TypeScript/JavaScript SDKs (notably @tiplink/api) and Solana Wallet Adapter UI components rather than a hosted REST API, and is used for airdrops, tipping, payments, and onboarding new users to Solana. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Transcarent
providers.description: Transcarent is a health and care experience company serving self-insured employers, health plans, and government and labor union clients. Its consumer-facing platform, WayFinding, combines generative AI agents with instant access to human health guides and clinicians to deliver benefits navigation, clinical guidance, virtual primary and specialty care, pharmacy care, surgery care, cancer care, weight-health programs, and 2nd.MD second opinions in a single experience. The platform is built on an API-first, cloud-native architecture with pre-built HL7 FHIR and EDI connectors that integrate with existing eligibility files and medical, pharmacy, and point-solution benefits. Transcarent exposes these integrations to enterprise partners rather than through a public self-serve developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: True & Co
providers.description: True & Co is a direct-to-consumer women's intimates and lingerie brand, originally venture-backed (Cowboy Ventures, Uncork Capital) and now operating under PVH Corp. It sells bras, underwear, and loungewear online through a Shopify-hosted storefront at trueandco.com. The store exposes no traditional developer API, but it does expose a modern agent-commerce surface: a hosted Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for catalog, cart, and checkout, Shopify Customer Account OAuth 2.0 / OIDC for buyer identity, a public read-only storefront JSON surface, and an agent-facing llms.txt / agents.md.

providers.name: Ursa Major Technologies
providers.description: Ursa Major Technologies Inc. is an American aerospace and defense propulsion manufacturer founded in 2015 by Joe Laurienti, a former SpaceX and Blue Origin propulsion engineer, and headquartered at 19750 Co Rd 7 in Berthoud, Colorado, with additive manufacturing operations in Youngstown, Ohio. The company designs, builds and hot-fire tests liquid rocket engines, solid rocket motors and in-space propulsion systems for space launch, hypersonics and U.S. and allied defense customers. Its product line includes the 5,000 lbf Hadley oxygen-rich staged-combustion liquid engine — the first Ursa Major engine to reach flight qualification for hypersonic missions — and Draper, a storable, throttleable, restartable engine for tactical hypersonic strike, missile defense and rapid in-space maneuver, alongside a solid rocket motor line validated through static fire and a chemical propulsion capability for tactical satellite bus systems. Ursa Major was the first American company to successfully fire an oxygen-rich staged combustion engine; it states it has delivered more than 100 engines and logged over 100,000 seconds of hotfire testing, with engines and motors more than 80 percent 3D printed by mass. The company is AS9100D, ISO 9001 and CMMC Level 2 certified. Ursa Major is a hardware manufacturer selling to government and prime-contractor customers: it publishes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, developer portal or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Vinyl Equity
providers.description: Vinyl Equity is a modern transfer agency providing equity, cap-table, and shareholder-management software for private and public companies. Its platform covers registrar services, proxy and AGM (annual general meeting) management, and shareholder security, replacing legacy transfer-agent workflows with a modern web application. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface is documented at this time; the profile currently captures the company's security and compliance posture.

providers.name: VISO
providers.description: viso.ai builds Visual General Intelligence, a new kind of computer vision that understands any scene out of the box without data collection, annotation, or per-question retraining. The company ships two products: Viso Suite, an industry- and hardware-agnostic no-code/low-code cloud platform to build, deploy, scale, and operate real-world computer vision applications; and Viso Now, an agentic computer vision platform whose vision agents connect a camera feed, recognize the scene, write the detection logic, and wire the alerts on auto-pilot. Viso Now plugs into the cameras and video systems teams already run through ready-made connectors, then pushes outputs anywhere: alerts to Slack, Teams, or email, and media forwarded into any ERP, BI tool, or third-party system over a direct API. The Viso Now backend is exposed as an authenticated Apollo GraphQL API at now.viso.ai with Google sign-in.

providers.name: Wiselayer
providers.description: WiseLayer is an AI-powered accounting automation platform that provides named "digital workers" (AI agents) for finance and accounting teams, automating tasks such as accruals, vendor communications, payroll accounting, bank reconciliations, depreciation and amortization, lease accounting, and prepaid expenses. The platform emphasizes transparent, explainable AI ("AI that shows its work") with natural-language interaction, automated email digests, and 300+ integrations into ERPs, billing, procure-to-pay, and HRIS systems. WiseLayer was acquired by BlackLine (NASDAQ: BL) and its product is now offered as Verity Accruals by BlackLine. WiseLayer was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. The company operates a SaaS application at app.wiselayer.com and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Zibra AI
providers.description: Zibra AI is a Ukrainian deep-tech company building AI-powered real-time volumetric rendering and compression technology for VFX, gaming, virtual production, film, and TV. Its flagship product, ZibraVDB, compresses OpenVDB volumetric datasets to roughly five percent of their original size while preserving visual quality, enabling real-time playback of smoke, fire, fog, and other volumetric effects. Zibra ships a native C++ ZibraVDB SDK (DirectX 12, Vulkan, and Metal on Windows, Linux, and macOS) alongside plugins for Unreal Engine, Houdini, and Unity, with Blender support in progress. It exposes no public REST/HTTP API; integration is through the SDK and digital-content-creation plugins. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 1Huddle
providers.description: 1Huddle is a Newark, New Jersey workforce training platform that uses science-backed, quick-burst mobile games to onboard, upskill, and engage employees. Founded by Sam Caucci, the platform offers a mobile library of 3,000+ skill games across 16 workforce skill areas, an on-demand game marketplace, and personalized content, with clients including Loews Hotels, Novartis, Madison Square Garden, PIMCO, and the U.S. Air Force. 1Huddle integrates with LMS, HRIS, authoring, and reporting tools (Microsoft Teams, Slack, Workday, Salesforce, Cornerstone, and more) and exposes flexible SSO, User Feeds, and Reporting APIs through a partner program rather than a public self-service developer portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Akur8
providers.description: Akur8 is a cloud-based actuarial AI platform for P&C and life insurers, covering pricing (Data, Risk, Demand, Rate, Rate Repo, Optim, Discover), reserving, and production deployment of rating models. There is no self-serve public developer API or public API reference published on akur8.com; the platform is sold and onboarded as enterprise SaaS through a sales-led, typically two-week free pilot. The one confirmed API capability is Akur8 Deploy - once a pricing model built in Akur8 Rate is finalized, Deploy auto-generates a private, tenant-specific real-time REST rating/scoring endpoint that a customer's own policy admin or quoting system calls at quote time to return a price in milliseconds. Access to that generated endpoint is provisioned per customer within a paid contract, not published for anonymous developer signup; rating tables can also be exported in CSV, JSON, PMML, and POJO formats for offline integration.

providers.name: ApplyBoard
providers.description: ApplyBoard is a study-abroad application platform that simplifies the international education journey by connecting students, recruitment partners, and partner schools on a single platform. Students explore and apply to more than 1,500 global universities and colleges across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and Germany, with supporting services spanning financial products, English-language test vouchers, and accommodation. ApplyBoard also operates ApplyProof, a document-verification and trust product. The company does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or SDK; its programmatic surface (including ApplyProof) is partner-gated. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Appriss Inc.
providers.description: Appriss Inc. was a Louisville, Kentucky data and analytics holding company whose business units were broken up in 2021: Appriss Insights was sold to Equifax in a $1.825 billion deal, and Appriss Health was rebranded as the independent company Bamboo Health. The surviving Appriss Retail business (apprissretail.com) is an AI-powered retail loss-prevention platform that helps retailers combat total retail loss across in-store and online channels through returns-fraud prevention, shrink and exception analytics, and case and audit management. Its products include Appriss Engage (returns and claims management), Appriss Secure (shrink and exception analytics), Appriss Incident (case and audit management), and the Sidekick AI collaborator. Appriss Retail publishes no public developer API program — its APIS Online portal is an authenticated Asset Protection Information System (customer login), not a developer API surface.

providers.name: AtoB
providers.description: AtoB is a fleet payments platform for the trucking and transportation industry, offering fuel cards, spend-management controls, driver payouts, and trip credit to fleets of every size. Its cards work across a nationwide fuel network with truck-stop discounts, granular purchase controls (fuel-only, category/MCC restrictions, per-transaction and daily limits), telematics-aware fraud prevention, and reporting that supports IFTA fuel-tax and expense compliance. AtoB also runs partner programs for factoring companies, freight brokers, and merchants, and exposes a private Partners API used by telematics and fleet-management integrations (for example Fleetio and Oxmaint) to sync cards, drivers, vehicles, and settled fuel transactions. AtoB was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and General Catalyst; this profile has been enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Barn2Door
providers.description: Barn2Door is a Seattle-based commerce and business-management platform purpose-built for independent farmers and local food producers. It gives farms an online store, order and subscription management, inventory tracking, delivery and pickup logistics, integrated payments, and built-in marketing and customer-relationship tools, consolidating the systems a farm needs to sell direct-to-consumer and wholesale into a single dashboard. Barn2Door connects to partners including Mailchimp, QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Avalara, Shippo, Routific, Squarespace, and Facebook, but does not publish a public developer API or documentation portal at this time.

providers.name: Boxbee
providers.description: Boxbee is an on-demand storage and reusable moving-box rental service operating across California, including the San Francisco Bay Area, San Jose, Oakland, Los Angeles, Orange County, the Inland Empire, and San Diego. It offers valet pickup-and-delivery storage, rentable reusable plastic moving crates for consumers and businesses, and an online inventory system for managing stored items. Boxbee originated as a 500 Startups and Google Ventures-backed app-based valet self-storage startup founded in 2012; after the by-the-box operation was sold, the brand continued as a regional storage and moving-supply provider. No public API or developer program is currently published.

providers.name: Brandback
providers.description: Brandback is a Berlin-based embedded resale infrastructure company (legal entity Arbor Technologies GmbH) that lets online retailers and fashion brands integrate resale directly into their baskets, product listings, and checkouts. Shoppers see an item's future resale value before they buy, resell it later in a single click, and receive store credit, while Brandback's AI handles pricing recommendations, condition checks, customer service, shipping, disputes, and payouts. Retailers can launch a white-label resale marketplace with no upfront cost and integrate with any e-commerce platform. Founded in 2023 and backed by $7.4M in pre-seed and seed funding led by Earlybird VC, Brandback reports a 9.5% average conversion-rate lift with customers including Replay Jeans and Sandqvist.

providers.name: Brigit
providers.description: Brigit is a consumer financial technology company whose mobile app helps people manage everyday money with instant cash advances of up to $500 with no credit check, interest, or late fees, a Credit Builder account, and a Finance Helper for budgeting, spending analysis, bill tracking, and overdraft prediction. The app also bundles identity-theft protection and a deals-and-offers marketplace, and is offered on paid monthly subscription tiers. Brigit reports more than 12 million users. This API Evangelist profile is a company lead surfaced from venture-capital portfolios (Canaan Partners, DCM Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners); Brigit is a direct-to-consumer app and does not currently publish a public developer API, so this record is enriched at the identity and web-property level.

providers.name: Clearco
providers.description: Clearco (formerly Clearbanc) is a Toronto-based fintech that provides non-dilutive, revenue-based working capital to ecommerce and direct-to-consumer brands. Founders connect the sales, advertising and banking platforms they already run on — Shopify, Amazon, Stripe, PayPal, Square, BigCommerce — and Clearco underwrites from that data, funding inventory and marketing spend as a cash advance or as invoice funding, in as little as 24 hours, without equity dilution. The company was founded in 2015 as Clearbanc, rebranded to Clearco in 2021, and reports having deployed more than $3.3 billion to over 10,000 businesses.

providers.name: Cloudgenix
providers.description: CloudGenix was a cloud-native SD-WAN (software-defined wide area network) company founded in 2013 and backed by Mayfield. Its AppFabric platform let enterprises build application-defined, policy-driven WANs managed from a cloud controller, with a full REST API (the CloudGenix Cloud Controller / AppFabric API) and first-party SDKs in Python, C#, Java, and JavaScript plus a CI-capable configuration CLI. Palo Alto Networks acquired CloudGenix in April 2020 for more than $420M and rebranded the product as Prisma SD-WAN, now part of the Prisma SASE portfolio. The public developer tooling remains published under the official CloudGenix GitHub organization.

providers.name: CloudTrucks
providers.description: CloudTrucks (operated by Cloud Technologies, Inc.) is a San Francisco-based virtual trucking carrier and business-management platform for owner-operators and small trucking fleets. The platform aggregates freight loads from more than fifty brokers and shippers into a single app, and layers on load booking, dispatching, real-time tracking, instant pay on proof of delivery, invoicing, factoring, fuel discounts (FuelApp), insurance, and back-office financial tooling so independent drivers can run their business from a phone. CloudTrucks also operates Exchange for shippers and brokers plus a freight-agent program, and is backed by Craft Ventures, Kindred Ventures and Menlo Ventures. CloudTrucks does not publish a public developer API or documentation portal; this profile captures its public web, legal, support and mobile-app surface plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Clover Security
providers.description: Clover Security is a Tel Aviv-based product security company (founded 2023) that builds design-led AI security agents for the software development lifecycle. Its agents plug into the tools engineering teams already use — GitHub, Cursor, Confluence, Jira, and Slack — to automate security design reviews, run continuous threat modeling, detect design-to-implementation drift, and keep agentic and spec-driven development secure by default. Clover has raised $36M from Notable Capital, Team8, and Silicon Valley CISO Investments, serving enterprise, fintech, and banking customers including Lemonade, Plaid, Notion, Udemy, and ServiceTitan. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of ggv-capital and enriched from the company's public web surface; Clover exposes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Confidential Computing Consortium
providers.description: The Confidential Computing Consortium (CCC) is a Linux Foundation project that brings together hardware vendors, cloud providers, and software developers to accelerate the adoption of confidential computing. CCC defines, advances, and standardizes hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) that protect data and code while in use, complementing existing protections for data at rest and in transit. The consortium governs open source projects and specifications spanning attestation, trustworthy workload identity, and TEE runtimes.

providers.name: Control4
providers.description: Control4 is a smart home and building automation platform, now part of Snap One / ADI Global (Resideo), headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah. It unifies control of lighting, audio/video, home theater, climate, security, shades, and voice across residential and commercial spaces through a single interface on smartphones, touchscreens, and on-wall keypads. Control4 is delivered through a network of certified integrators rather than direct-to-consumer sales, and interoperates with more than 25,000 third-party devices. For developers it offers the DriverWorks SDK (a Lua-based framework for building device drivers), the Control4 Developer Portal for OAuth application registration against the Control4 cloud, and public first-party libraries on GitHub.

providers.name: Corma
providers.description: Corma is a SaaS license and access governance platform for modern IT teams that automates SaaS discovery, access reviews, provisioning, and deprovisioning. Recognized in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for SaaS Management Platforms, Corma helps organizations centralize all applications in one place, identify shadow IT, and reduce software spend by 10 to 15 percent. Corma offers extensive native integrations with identity providers (Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace), HR platforms (Workday, BambooHR, Personio), financial tools (Spendesk, Qonto, Pennylane, Agicap), and productivity and business tools (Slack, Notion, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk). A public developer API is not currently published.

providers.name: Cyral
providers.description: Cyral is a data security and governance platform (founded 2018, Milpitas CA; acquired by Varonis in March 2025) that provides an agentless, stateless data-layer sidecar for monitoring and governing access to data repositories such as Snowflake, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Amazon S3, Kafka, and Oracle. Cyral was built API-first: its Control Plane exposes a REST API secured with OAuth2 client-credentials, fully automatable through the official Cyral Terraform provider (cyralinc/cyral) and supporting Terraform modules for AWS, Azure, and Okta. Following the Varonis acquisition, cyral.com now redirects to Varonis' Database Activity Monitoring product, but the first-party developer tooling remains published on the cyralinc GitHub organization and the Terraform Registry.

providers.name: Dance
providers.description: Dance is a Berlin-based electric mobility subscription company that offers e-bikes and e-mopeds as an all-in-one monthly subscription. A single fixed monthly fee bundles the vehicle together with on-demand repairs and maintenance, fast replacements, and theft protection, so members can ride without owning or servicing the hardware themselves. Dance operates in Berlin, Hamburg, and Paris, with product lines including the Dance One and Dance One Step e-bikes and the Dance Moped. Founded in 2020 by SoundCloud co-founders Alexander Ljung and Eric Quidenus-Wahlforss with Jimdo co-founder Christian Springub, Dance is a consumer-facing, app-based service backed by HV Capital. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, help, and security surface.

providers.name: Dyrt
providers.description: The Dyrt is a camping discovery and booking platform for the United States, covering public and private campgrounds, RV parks, glamping, cabins, and free dispersed camping. It is a community-driven service built on user-contributed reviews, photos, and campground details, layered with trip-planning tools, real-time availability, and direct booking for many locations. Its Dyrt PRO subscription adds offline maps, cancellation ("Scan Canceled Sites") alerts, curated free-camping data, and discounts at 1,000+ campgrounds. The Dyrt also offers free listings, dashboards, analytics, and marketing tools for campground owners. It has been featured by the New York Times, NPR, National Geographic, and Forbes. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; The Dyrt publishes a consumer web/mobile product and does not expose a documented public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Enplug
providers.description: Enplug is a cloud-based digital signage and content-management platform that powers communications on screens across retail, hospitality, corporate, and public-venue locations, with content apps for social feeds, dashboards, video, wayfinding, and menus managed from a central web dashboard. Enplug was acquired by Spectrio, and enplug.com now redirects to Spectrio's Enplug acquisition page; the legacy Enplug cloud login remains live at login.enplug.com. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; Enplug exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this repo carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Entelo
providers.description: Entelo is an AI-powered talent-sourcing and recruiting-automation platform for finding, engaging, and hiring candidates using predictive analytics, diversity-aware search, and candidate-engagement tooling. Entelo was acquired and is now delivered as "Entelo Recruit" within Rival (rival-hr.com), an AI-powered HR orchestration suite spanning recruiting, workflow, learning, and performance. Its former domain entelo.com now 301-redirects to Rival. No public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI is currently published for the Entelo/Rival Recruit product.

providers.name: ExaCare AI
providers.description: ExaCare AI is a post-acute and senior care operations platform that applies AI to admissions, referral management, prior authorization, and reimbursement workflows across skilled nursing, home health, hospice, and assisted living providers. It reads inbound referral and admissions packets, extracts clinical and payer data, and automates the back-office work of accepting and reimbursing patients, with integrations into referral platforms, hospital systems, and EHRs. ExaCare is a private company backed by Insight Partners; it ships a customer web application and a Vanta-hosted Trust Center (HIPAA) but publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Expansive
providers.description: Expansive is a Mexican real estate crowdfunding platform (crowdfunding inmobiliario) that lets individuals invest collectively in vetted real estate projects from as little as 1,000 MXN, earning returns backed by real guarantees. It operates as a regulated collective financing institution (IFC) under Mexico's Fintech Law and is supervised by the CNBV (Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores). Expansive handles project vetting, funding, quarterly investor reporting, and payouts through its web platform and investor app (app.expansive.mx). The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing fintech investing product; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Flarion
providers.description: Flarion is a data-processing acceleration company that speeds up distributed compute engines — Apache Spark, Hadoop, and Ray — without code or infrastructure changes. It ships an Arrow-native, DataFusion/Polars-based execution engine written in Rust that installs as a plugin in about six minutes, plus intelligent workload caching (query, data-block, and buffer caching) and a performance-monitoring platform for job metrics, resource tracking, anomaly detection, and failure prevention. Flarion runs on-premises or on Databricks, AWS EMR, GCP Dataproc, Azure HDInsight, and Anyscale, with an agentless architecture that requires no access to customer data, delivering roughly 3x performance and 60% cost savings. Flarion is a portfolio company of Sierra Ventures. The company exposes a product console and a legal/SLA surface but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Flarion Technologies
providers.description: Flarion is a data-processing acceleration company that speeds up distributed data engines without code changes or infrastructure migration. Its plug-and-play engine replaces row-by-row JVM execution with a native, vectorized runtime built in Rust on Apache Arrow and DataFusion, delivering roughly 3x performance and up to 60% cost savings. Flarion ships three capabilities across Apache Spark, Hadoop, and Ray: a Data Processing Accelerator, Workload Caching that eliminates redundant recomputation, and a Performance Monitoring platform with anomaly detection and failure prevention. It integrates with managed services including Databricks, AWS EMR, GCP Dataproc, and Azure HDInsight via simple Spark configuration (dropping in a JAR), with usage-based pricing billed per accelerated CPU-hour. Flarion is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. As of this profile the company exposes a product console and marketing/legal surface but no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Graneet
providers.description: Graneet is a French vertical-SaaS ERP for the construction and public-works (BTP) sector, built for small and mid-sized contractors (roughly EUR 2M to 100M in revenue) to protect project profitability from the office to the job site. It unifies cost estimating and quotations, progress (situation) invoicing, purchase and supplier-invoice management, project planning and labor tracking, cash and bank reconciliation, and real-time margin dashboards, with a companion mobile app and prebuilt integrations to accounting tools such as Sage 100 and Pennylane. The product is delivered as a cloud application (app.graneet.com) backed by internal Main, BFF, and Quotation APIs; there is no public developer API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: GreenFi
providers.description: GreenFi is a climate-focused consumer financial technology company — the rebranded continuation of Aspiration's consumer banking arm. It offers a combined checking and savings account, high-yield savings with goal-based "Savings Pods", a debit card, a GreenFi Plus subscription tier, investing through its Redwood fund, and a cash-back Marketplace of sustainable brands, alongside impact programs such as Plant Your Change, tree planting and carbon offsetting. GreenFi is a financial technology company, not a bank; banking services and the debit card are provided by Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC. Aspiration spun its consumer unit out in 2024 to Mission Financial Partners, LLC, which rebranded it GreenFi in April 2025; Coastal Financial Corporation acquired the GreenFi brand in January 2026. It is a separate company from Aspiration Partners, Inc., the enterprise carbon business that entered Chapter 11. GreenFi ships iOS, Android and web applications to end users and publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Hey
providers.description: heycater! is a B2B catering marketplace that connects companies with vetted catering partners across Germany and the United Kingdom, letting businesses request, compare, and book corporate food services through a single platform. Its service lines span heykantine! (daily office meals for teams of 50+), Meetings & Catering (event catering from 10 people drawing on 700+ vetted caterers), hey! Events (full-service event planning for ~100+ guests), and a Pantry Service for office beverages and snacks. The platform serves 2,500+ companies, including Spotify, Airbnb, Meta, and Salesforce, and has fulfilled more than 250,000 catering orders, returning comparable quotes within 48 hours at no cost. heycater! does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its public web presence and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Intersection
providers.description: Intersection is a New York-based, experience-driven out-of-home (OOH) media and technology company formed from the merger of Titan, a municipal out-of-home advertising operator, and Control Group, a technology and design studio. It operates street-level, transit, airport, bikeshare and place-based advertising networks across 13 major U.S. markets - including LinkNYC, the largest street-level digital network in New York City - and it builds the software behind them: the IxNConnect display-management and communications platform used by cities, transit agencies and airports, and an AI-powered Order Management System (OMS) that exposes inventory discovery, availability, pricing and campaign reservation to AI agents through an MCP server built on the IAB Tech Lab OpenDirect 2.0 specification.

providers.name: Join
providers.description: Join (Join Stories, join-stories.com) is an AI video commerce platform that helps e-commerce brands create, distribute, and measure short-form video across their sales channels. Its products include shoppable video embedded on product and collection pages, user-generated content (UGC) activation from social media, video analytics with A/B testing, an AI Studio that generates video and images from product data, and interactive web stories. Deployment is a single embed snippet with native integrations for Shopify, PrestaShop, Magento, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, WooCommerce, and headless storefronts. The company is backed by Canaan Partners and Seedcamp.

providers.name: KareInn
providers.description: KareInn is a UK-based digital care management and care-home planning software provider whose cloud platform helps residential and nursing care providers streamline operations, evidence CQC compliance, and improve resident care. The product suite spans a care-management dashboard with occupancy and management reporting, a customizable care-plan builder, clinical policy and procedure workflows, care-delivery task assignment and monitoring, pre-admissions and occupancy pipeline management, event and incident tracking, and a resident and family engagement portal. KareInn integrates with partner systems including Civica/Coldharbour income processing, Camscope electronic medication management, and Ally Cares acoustic monitoring, and is positioned as an NHS assured supplier. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio lead; KareInn does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or a machine-readable discovery surface — the artifacts below capture its public product, commercial, and policy pages only.

providers.name: Labcorp
providers.description: Labcorp helps patients, providers, organizations, and biopharma companies guide vital healthcare decisions every day. Labcorp supports HL7 / FHIR-based integration for laboratory orders and results exchange with electronic health record (EHR) systems, but does not publish a fully open public developer portal; access is granted through health-system and biopharma integration agreements.

providers.name: Lepton AI
providers.description: Lepton AI was acquired by NVIDIA in 2025 and the platform is now branded NVIDIA DGX Cloud Lepton. It is a fully managed AI platform that connects developers to global GPU compute across a federated network of cloud providers, with managed endpoints, dev sessions, distributed training, and batch processing.

providers.name: Mero
providers.description: Mero is a Canadian SaaS platform for commercial building cleaning operations that uses smart sensors and analytics to automatically log, validate, and prove cleaning activity without manual input from janitorial staff. Its product is organized into three modules: Validate (hands-free proof that cleaning was completed), Dispatch (occupancy- and supply-driven scheduling), and Inspect (in-app QA and inspection tooling). Mero serves janitorial companies, property managers, and commercial facilities, with data captured across roughly 100M square feet at customers including Harvard, Colliers, and Toronto Pearson Airport. The company advertises a data-integration API and a Zapier connector to send and receive data with other tools, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; API access is gated behind a sales demo.

providers.name: Model ML
providers.description: Model ML is an AI-native platform for financial services that embeds an agentic "finance agent" into the tools professionals already use — Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, its own app, and a firm's internal systems. It automates deliverables through Workflows, runs compound-intelligence analysis via Grids, performs document review and risk assessment, captures information with a Notetaker, and answers questions through Chat and agentic dashboards backed by real-time data connections. It targets investment banking, consulting, private equity and credit, and asset and wealth management. Model ML is a fintech company backed by QED Investors. The company publishes a trust center and a security program (ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR) but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Motif
providers.description: Motif is an AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) software company building an intelligent, browser-based workspace for building design. Founded in 2023 by former Autodesk leaders Amar Hanspal and Brian Mathews, Motif unifies sheet review, live 3D streaming, AI-assisted visual exploration, and real-time collaboration in a single cloud platform that bridges 2D and 3D workflows as a step toward making Building Information Modeling (BIM) a practical reality. The company has raised $46M led by Redpoint Ventures (seed) and Alphabet's CapitalG (Series A), and was named to Forbes' 2025 Next Billion-Dollar Startups list. Motif is a collaboration SaaS product for design and construction teams; it publishes product learning docs and a help center but does not yet expose a public developer API — a plugin/API surface is part of its stated long-term strategy.

providers.name: Navro
providers.description: Navro (formerly Paytrix) is a London-based payments curation platform that lets large businesses move money globally through a single contract and API integration. Rather than stitching together a patchwork of banks and payment providers, Navro routes each payment via the right rail, currency and compliance model, executing millions of payouts across 140+ currencies and 200+ regions. Its products span Navro Workforce (global payroll, contractor and pension payouts), Navro Life (cross-border pensions), Navro Digital (payments for digital platforms and enterprises) and Navro Capital (international fund flows). Clients integrate once via the Navro API or use the no-code Navro Hub portal for real-time payment visibility and reporting. Founded by Aran Brown (CEO) and Eddie Harrison, Navro operates from London with offices in Ireland and the United States, and is authorised by the UK Financial Conduct Authority, the Central Bank of Ireland and FinCEN in the US.

providers.name: NetSuite Accounting
providers.description: NetSuite Accounting is the cloud financial management module of Oracle NetSuite that delivers general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, cash management, tax management, fixed assets, and real-time financial reporting and consolidation for growing businesses. NetSuite exposes its accounting records (invoices, bills, journal entries, payments, accounts, customers, vendors, and ledgers) through SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL queries, and RESTlets, secured with OAuth 2.0 and token-based authentication for ERP and finance integrations.

providers.name: NexMind
providers.description: NexMind (operating as NexLaw) is a legal AI platform for U.S. litigators and law firms, offering secure, hallucination-free AI that drafts, summarizes, and researches legal work up to 10x faster. Its products include NeXa (AI legal research and drafting assistant), ChronoVault (evidence centralization and automated case timelines), TrialPrep (trial preparation workspace for arguments and witness outlines), and a real-time Courtroom Assistant, with capabilities spanning citation-backed legal deep research, deposition and document analysis, case chronology building, legal memo drafting, and contract and breach analysis. NexLaw is a direct-to-user SaaS product; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Nurix
providers.description: Nurix AI is an enterprise agentic AI platform for sales and customer support, delivering AI voice and chat agents that qualify leads, resolve support issues, and automate back-office operations across voice, chat, and messaging channels. Its products include NuPlay (customer-facing conversational AI agents) and NuStack (a workflow automation engine), backed by a library of 400+ pre-built integrations spanning CRM, contact-center (CCaaS), e-commerce/order-management, messaging, and scheduling systems. Nurix is backed by General Catalyst. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API surface — engagement is via sales/demo and pre-built connectors rather than self-serve API keys or developer documentation.

providers.name: Octave Bioscience
providers.description: Octave Bioscience is a precision neurology company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, that develops blood-based multi-protein biomarker tests for chronic neurological disease. Its commercially available Octave Multiple Sclerosis Disease Activity (MSDA) Test measures a panel of serum proteins to produce a quantitative disease activity score used alongside clinical and imaging assessment, and is available across the United States through a strategic collaboration with Quest Diagnostics. The company is also developing a Multiple Sclerosis Disease Progression (MSDP) test and a Parkinson's disease biomarker assay supported by a Michael J. Fox Foundation grant. Octave publishes a public trust center documenting HITRUST, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, HIPAA and GDPR posture, but operates no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: OnStation
providers.description: OnStation is a digital stationing platform for road and highway construction projects, replacing paper station logs and manual chaining with GPS-based field documentation. Its iOS and Android mobile app lets crews, inspectors, and project managers identify exact station locations, drop and share flags, capture timestamped photos and notes, and complete forms in the field without extra hardware. A cloud Data Portal aggregates that field documentation into searchable, exportable DOT-ready reports for compliance and dispute resolution, while Active Worksite alerts drivers through Waze and OEM systems when crews are working. OnStation offers pre-built integrations with construction and survey systems including HCSS HeavyJob, Trimble and Bad Elf GNSS receivers, TransTech density gauges, FleetWatcher e-ticketing, and ESRI GIS, but does not currently publish a public developer API. Backed by Insight Partners and Techstars.

providers.name: Oradian
providers.description: Oradian is an AI-native, cloud-based core banking platform that helps banks, lenders, microfinance institutions, and fintechs in Asia, Africa, and Europe replace legacy core systems and launch, operate, and scale modern banking services from the cloud. Its product, Instafin, is built API-first around an open data model, an extensible architecture, and a native Model Context Protocol surface, exposing capabilities such as ledgers, transactions, deposits, cards, loans, and applications through stable, versioned APIs, webhooks, and event streams. Oradian is independently audited to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 and aligns to CBN, BSP, and OJK regulatory requirements.

providers.name: Panjiva
providers.description: Panjiva is a supply chain intelligence platform owned by S&P Global Market Intelligence that delivers data-driven insights for the global trade community. It combines global import/export shipment records with machine learning analytics to profile companies, map supply chains, benchmark competitors, surface sales leads, and assess counterparty and supply-chain risk. Panjiva covers roughly 9 million companies and more than 2 billion shipment records spanning an estimated 35% of global trade flows. Trade data is also delivered programmatically to CRM systems, quantitative models, and research workflows through S&P Global's XpressFeed data-feed service and is surfaced inside S&P Capital IQ Pro. Access is enterprise and subscription based; Panjiva does not publish a public self-serve developer API portal.

providers.name: Percent
providers.description: Percent is a private credit platform that opens privately negotiated loans and debt financing from non-bank lenders to accredited and institutional investors, specialty-finance borrowers, and debt underwriters. The marketplace lets individual accredited investors access institutional-grade private credit deals (asset-backed securities and corporate loans) with entry points from $500 for direct deals, $5,000 for diversified Blended Notes, and $50,000 for Separately Managed Accounts, alongside a secondary market for eligible positions. Percent Securities, LLC is a U.S. registered broker-dealer and member of FINRA and SIPC; Percent Advisors LLC provides advisory services. Investor, borrower, and manager workflows run through authenticated portals; the public percent.com surface is marketing, education, performance, and regulatory disclosure. Percent has no public developer API — programmatic/deal-level access is not published.

providers.name: Physiohome
providers.description: Physiohome, operating as Ameen (رعاية أمين), is a Saudi Arabia-based, tech-enabled provider of home rehabilitation and physical therapy services. Founded in 2021 out of a Ministry of Health sector accelerator, the company delivers physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, nutritional therapy, and personal training for adults and seniors in patients' homes and rehabilitation centers. Its platform manages the full care journey from assessment and treatment planning through session tracking, provider equipping, and reporting, with 100+ active service providers operating across nine cities and a wider network of 700+ providers. Ameen offers iOS and Android apps, an online booking flow, and a patient portal, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. It is a portfolio company of Sanabil 500 (500 Global) and Saudi Venture Capital.

providers.name: Pinokio
providers.description: Pinokio is an open-source desktop application — self-described as an "AI Browser" — that acts as a 1-click launcher for any open-source AI project. Built by independent developer Cocktail Peanut (cocktailpeanut), Pinokio packages a terminal, package managers (Conda, Homebrew, Pip, NPM), and a graphical UI into a single MIT-licensed desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux with NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple Silicon GPU support. Users install AI apps with one click from a curated "Discover" directory of 160+ vetted scripts spanning image generation, video generation, text-to-speech and voice cloning, large language models, 3D generation, music and audio generation, and face swap. Pinokio is driven by a JSON-based scripting language designed to be both human and machine readable, with primitives like shell.run, fs, input, log, jump, hf (Hugging Face), notify, browser, and json that let publishers describe install and launch flows declaratively. Each script is sandboxed under ~/pinokio with isolated paths and Python virtual environments, and featured scripts must transfer ownership to the Pinokio Factory GitHub organization for admin review. Pinokio is purely client-side open source — there is no public REST API, no hosted commercial offering, and no developer SDK beyond the local script syntax and the desktop app itself.

providers.name: PitchMe
providers.description: PitchMe is a recruitment data intelligence platform that enriches, verifies, and deduplicates candidate records to turn an existing ATS or CRM database into an activated talent pool. It cleans and appends verified contact details, employment history, and skills data, then surfaces career-intelligence signals that power AI-driven sourcing and outreach. PitchMe connects to applicant tracking systems such as Bullhorn, Greenhouse, Salesforce, Lever, JobDiva, Vincere, Avionte, Jobvite, and Ashby via native and certified integrations, plus a custom API for connecting any ATS or recruitment platform. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Porter Airlines
providers.description: Porter Airlines is a Canadian carrier headquartered in Toronto, operating as Porter Airlines (Canada) Limited and Porter Airlines Inc. under IATA designator PD, IATA ticketing plate 451, and ICAO code POE. It is the challenger to the Air Canada / WestJet duopoly in Canada, flying an Embraer E195-E2 and De Havilland Dash 8 fleet across domestic, transborder and sun destinations, and it joined IATA as a member in 2026 following IOSA certification.
