Porter sits in the distribution chain as a conventional GDS-intermediated carrier: agencies reach its inventory through the GDSs (Sabre is named explicitly in Porter's agency terms, and Travelport is the channel Duffel uses to resell Porter content) or through Porter's own ticketless Travel Agency Portal on flyporter.com. Porter's API posture is honestly stated as none-published. There is no developer portal, no public or partner API documentation, no OpenAPI, and no NDC endpoint of any kind. The developer, developers and apis subdomains do not resolve; api.flyporter.com resolves but does not answer on 80 or 443; docs.flyporter.com redirects to an internal Google Drive. Every well-known spec path returns 404 and the whole site sits behind a Cloudflare bot challenge with ai-train=no content signals. Access is accreditation-gated: an agency must hold ARC accreditation or an IATA Passenger Sales Agency Agreement, register on flyporter.com, and accept Porter's Agency Terms and Conditions, which assert Porter ownership of all Porter Data, prohibit scraping and redistribution, and revoke all data rights the moment an appointment is suspended or terminated. There is no exit path beyond a written PIPEDA access request to Porter's Privacy Officer.

providers.name: PreFix
providers.description: PreFix is a Techstars-backed residential home-maintenance service company operating in Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, and Denver. For a flat monthly membership, homeowners get a dedicated neighborhood Home Manager who handles general repairs, twice-yearly 30-point preventive maintenance, HVAC, plumbing, carpentry, painting, appliance and garage-door work, and vetted contractor management through a single email, call, or text. Customers manage their homes through the HomeHub member portal. PreFix operates a consumer home-services business and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and demand-side intelligence.

providers.name: Prenda
providers.description: Prenda, Inc. is a Mesa, Arizona education technology company that makes it possible for an adult to open and run a K-8 microschool — a tight-knit learning community of roughly five to ten students — out of a home, studio, or office. Founded by Kelly Smith out of the Prenda Code Club he started at a public library in 2013, Prenda opened its first microschool in January 2018 and now supports more than 1,000 "guides" running microschools for nearly 10,000 learners across multiple US states, funded largely through school-choice and education savings account programs. The product is a plug-and-play software platform bundled with curriculum, training, and coaching: guides use it to manage enrollment, run adaptive diagnostic assessments in math and reading, track learner progress against Prenda's four-mode "connect, conquer, collaborate, create" learning day, process payments, and publish a marketing site for their school. Prenda is venture-backed, having raised a $20M round led by 776 in 2022. The platform is closed and end-user facing — Prenda publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract of any kind. Its only public developer surface is the Prenda Design System, an open-source MUI v6 React component and icon library published from the prenda-school GitHub organization.

providers.name: Resourcify
providers.description: Resourcify (Resourcify GmbH) is a Hamburg, Germany based digital platform for waste management and circular-economy operations, describing itself as "the operating system for a circular future." Its cloud software helps enterprises digitize and optimize their waste streams end to end - automating waste and recycling operations, optimizing cost, CO2 and recycling rates, tracking compliance, and running take-back systems - across manufacturing, construction, retail, healthcare, and airports. The platform connects waste producers with a network of recyclers and haulers, captures waste data and documentation, and reports on sustainability and material recovery. Resourcify is backed by Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; integrations are delivered as managed connections rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Rilla
providers.description: Rilla is an AI conversation-intelligence and coaching platform built for in-person and outside sales teams. Reps record their face-to-face customer conversations, and Rilla transcribes and analyzes them so managers can run virtual "ridealongs" and deliver targeted, data-driven coaching at scale. The platform surfaces talk patterns, objection handling, and outcome analytics across thousands of field conversations to help teams raise close rates, increase ticket size, and speed up rep ramp. Rilla is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the AI sector. Rilla runs a real production API — api.rillavoice.com/api/v1/, the private backend of its web and mobile apps, which answers every path with 401 Invalid Token — plus an AWS API Gateway webhook receiver its partner SPOTIO documents, but it publishes no developer portal, reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its CRM integrations are delivered by consuming the Merge unified API rather than by exposing a contract. This record captures its public web identity, the RFC 9116 security.txt it serves from app.rilla.com, and live domain-security and well-known probes.

providers.name: Scripbox
providers.description: Scripbox is an Indian direct-to-consumer wealth management and mutual fund investment platform operated by Scripbox Wealth Managers Private Limited. It helps families pursue financial freedom through personalized mutual fund recommendations shaped by expert advisors and data-backed algorithms, offering both regular (commission-based, zero monthly fee) and direct (advisory-fee) plans. The platform bundles portfolio construction and monitoring, financial planning, goal-based investing, tax-saving tools such as its Smart Withdraw algorithm, and multi-channel support. As of this enrichment pass, Scripbox operates purely as a consumer application and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Seer
providers.description: Seer, Inc. (NASDAQ: SEER) is a Redwood City, California life-sciences company pioneering proteomics, the large-scale study of proteins. Its Proteograph Product Suite pairs engineered nanoparticles with automated sample preparation and mass spectrometry to profile tens of thousands of proteins across biological samples at scale, and its cloud-based Proteograph Analysis System (PAS) software processes and interprets the resulting proteomic data for pharmaceutical, biopharma, and academic research. Seer exposes no public developer API; its software surface is the login-gated PAS platform delivered to customers of the Proteograph suite.

providers.name: Stability Audio
providers.description: Stable Audio (by Stability AI) is a generative audio model for music and sound-effect generation. The Stability Developer Platform exposes Stable Audio 2.5 endpoints alongside image, video, and 3D generation. Pricing is credit-based at 1 credit = $0.01; Stable Audio 2.5 generations are reported at $0.20 per generation regardless of duration.

providers.name: Storetasker
providers.description: Storetasker is a curated freelance marketplace that connects direct-to-consumer and e-commerce brands with vetted, expert Shopify developers, designers, and marketers for projects and ongoing retainers. Founded in 2016 and backed by Techstars, the platform has helped over 30,000 brands hire trusted Shopify talent across 200+ countries, handling expert matching, communication, project management, and payments. Storetasker operates as a two-sided hiring marketplace rather than a public API provider — as of this pass it publishes no developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: TherapyNotes
providers.description: TherapyNotes is a HIPAA-compliant practice management and electronic health record (EHR) platform built specifically for behavioral health - therapists, psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers, and group practices. It provides interactive note templates and clinical documentation, scheduling with appointment reminders, a client portal, telehealth, electronic insurance claims and ERA, credit card processing, and TherapyFuel AI tooling. As of this writing TherapyNotes does NOT expose a public or partner developer API, webhooks, or documented programmatic interface; access to client, appointment, clinical-note, and billing data is through the browser application and manual exports only. This entry documents TherapyNotes as an API-relevant provider and honestly models the capability areas a behavioral-health EHR API would cover; the API surfaces below are modeled, not published, and no endpoints are fabricated.

providers.name: Tilda Research
providers.description: Tilda Research deploys AI Teammates that perform the operational work of clinical trials for sponsors, CROs, and research sites — automating study workflows, data capture, trial monitoring, and regulatory compliance. Founded by Ram Yalamanchili and backed by 8VC, the company operates the Tilda Sense clinical-research platform (sense.tilda.bio) and advertises SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance via a Vanta-hosted trust center, but publishes no public developer program or API documentation.

providers.name: Tradespace
providers.description: Tradespace is an AI-powered intellectual property management platform that combines IP management software, AI tooling, and on-demand patent attorneys in a single full-service patent practice. The platform spans the IP lifecycle across four products — Create (invention harvesting and disclosure, with Slack, Gmail, and Notion integrations), Protect (AI-assisted patent drafting and flat-fee prosecution with senior attorneys), Manage (portfolio management and board-ready reporting), and Commercialize (licensing campaigns, claims charts, and licensee identification). It serves corporations, universities, tech transfer offices, startups, law firms, and government agencies, is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant (Vanta trust center), hosts on Microsoft Azure with customer-private AI instances, and is a 500 Global portfolio company. The SaaS application runs at app.tradespace.io; no public developer API is published.

providers.name: Tripo3D
providers.description: Tripo3D (by VAST) is an AI 3D generation platform with text-to-3D, image-to-3D, mesh refinement, and texturing APIs producing game-ready 3D assets. The Tripo API uses an async task-based REST pattern at https://api.tripo3d.ai/v2/openapi/task. Authenticate with API key.

providers.name: VALID8 Financial
providers.description: VALID8 Financial is a Verified Financial Intelligence (VFI) platform founded in 2017 in Seattle that turns raw banking evidence and accounting records into reconciled, evidential-grade transaction data for forensic accountants, CPA firms, law firms, bankruptcy trustees, and government investigators. The AI-powered platform automates extraction and verification of financial evidence across use cases including forensic investigations, financial crime, expert witness support, transaction advisory, bankruptcy and restructuring, and family law. A Techstars portfolio company, VALID8 is SOC 2 Type II audited, HIPAA compliant, and GDPR aligned with a Vanta-hosted trust center, but does not currently publish a developer portal or public API documentation; customers sign in through regional portals (us/ca/eu/uk/aus.valid8.io).

providers.name: Venue
providers.description: Venue is an all-in-one internal communications platform that makes it easy for teams to host, organize, and share all hands, webinars, AMAs, and fireside chats. It combines HD live streaming, recording, automatic transcription and summarization, branded Q&A, engagement tracking, and Channels for centralizing events and videos. Aimed at internal comms and employer-brand teams at companies like Shopify, PwC, Wealthsimple, and Yelp, Venue is a Toronto-based, Accel- and Y Combinator-backed productivity company. As of this enrichment pass Venue publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface — this profile captures its identity, website properties, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Wishup
providers.description: Wishup is a remote-work outsourcing platform that matches businesses with pre-vetted virtual assistants, bookkeepers, and automation specialists, typically onboarding a trained professional within 60 minutes. Its managed talent handles inbox and calendar management, CRM and social-media work, bookkeeping, project management, and AI-driven workflow automation across industries such as healthcare, e-commerce, real estate, startups, nonprofits, and legal services. Wishup runs a client-facing Employee Management App for task tracking and real-time feedback, but publishes no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Yieldify *
providers.description: Yieldify is a website personalization and conversion rate optimization (CRO) platform for ecommerce brands, founded in 2013 in London by Jay Radia and backed by investors including GV (Google Ventures). Its SaaS platform delivers targeted on-site messaging, customer-journey personalization, and A/B testing to lift conversion and revenue. Yieldify was acquired by Publicis Groupe in January 2023 and folded into Epsilon, where it is now sold as Epsilon Accelerate; yieldify.com redirects to the Epsilon Accelerate product page and the legal entity behind the platform is Zeus Enterprise Ltd, trading as Yieldify. Delivery is entirely client-side: a customer-specific JavaScript tag placed before the closing head tag (directly, or via Google Tag Manager, Tealium, Shopify theme.liquid or Recharge checkout) renders a documented library of on-site experience components — overlays, notifications, banners, sticky and embedded experiences, toasters, carousels, countdown timers, lead-capture forms — configured from the Yieldify Conversion Platform at convert.yieldify.com, with a typed dynamic-expression language for personalized copy and client-side yieldify_impression/click/close/form_submit events pushed into the customer's own GA4 property. There is no public developer API: probing every Yieldify host on 2026-08-13 found no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, A2A card, webhooks, SDK, CLI or developer portal, the status page at status.yieldify.com has been deactivated, and no pricing is published anywhere.

providers.name: 80,000 Hours
providers.description: 80,000 Hours is an independent nonprofit, founded in 2011 by Benjamin Todd and William MacAskill out of Oxford, that provides free research and support to help people use their careers to help solve the world's most pressing problems. The name refers to the roughly 80,000 hours a typical person works over their lifetime. It publishes an evidence-based career guide, in-depth problem profiles, a long-form podcast, and one-on-one advising, and runs a curated high-impact job board at jobs.80000hours.org. Since 2016 it has ranked helping navigate the transition to advanced AI as its top priority. It is a content and career-advice organization rather than an API producer; no public developer API is published, though it does serve a machine-readable llms.txt index of its content.

providers.name: Academia
providers.description: Academia (Academia.edu, Academia Inc.) is a San Francisco based platform for sharing and discovering academic research, founded in 2008 by Richard Price. Registered researchers upload papers, build public profiles, follow research interests and track readership analytics across a corpus of tens of millions of documents, and the company also runs the Academia journals program and sells Academia Premium subscriptions for advanced search, mentions, reader analytics and bulk PDF downloads. Academia publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the /v0 JSON endpoints its own web client calls are explicitly disallowed to crawlers in robots.txt. It does publish an RFC 9116 security.txt with a named security contact and a disclosure posture, and a long per-crawler robots.txt that names AI and agent user-agents individually.

providers.name: Activ Surgical
providers.description: Activ Surgical is a Boston, Massachusetts digital surgery company building intraoperative surgical intelligence for the operating room. Its flagship product, the ActivSight Intelligent Light imaging module, attaches to existing laparoscopic and robotic surgical systems and renders augmented-reality overlays on a standard monitor, letting surgeons see physiology the naked eye cannot. ActivPerfusion delivers dye-free, real-time blood-perfusion imaging using laser speckle contrast imaging, while ActivICG supports conventional indocyanine green visualization of structures such as bile ducts. The module is powered by the ActivEdge platform, a hardware-agnostic computer-vision, AI and machine-learning stack the company is building to turn intraoperative data into real-time surgical guidance. Activ Surgical performed the first autonomous robotic soft-tissue surgery in 2018, received FDA 510(k) clearance for ActivSight in April 2021 and CE Mark approval in December 2022, and sells on a subscription model with no capital-equipment purchase. The company publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract as of this profiling pass; its public technical surface is regulatory (EU MDR declarations of conformity, ISO 13485:2016) and clinical (peer-reviewed studies and white papers).

providers.name: Aily Labs
providers.description: Aily Labs is a Munich-based enterprise AI company that builds an AI Decision Intelligence Suite — a platform that connects siloed internal and external data to deliver real-time, explainable predictions and recommendations across Finance, R&D, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, Go-To-Market, Procurement, and People functions. The suite ships with 300+ validated predictive models and an iOS app, and is deployed across Healthcare & Life Sciences, Consumer Goods, Luxury & Fashion, Media & Tech, Retail, and Services (clients include Sanofi). Aily Labs is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's corporate, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Aisin
providers.description: Aisin Corporation is a Japanese global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Kariya, Aichi. Part of the Toyota Group, Aisin manufactures automatic transmissions, drivetrain components, body, chassis, and electronics for major automakers.

providers.name: Approve.com
providers.description: Approve.com is a cloud-based procurement platform founded in 2019 in Israel that lets businesses stand up a proper purchase-order process quickly, streamlining purchase requisitions, multi-step approvals, real-time budgets, and vendor onboarding with real-time spend controls and insights. Tipalti acquired Approve.com in April 2021 and now operates it as Tipalti Procurement (Tipalti Approve). Its Procurement REST API is still served from the approve.com domain (production https://triggers.approve.com, sandbox https://triggers.sandbox.approve.com), authenticating with an x-api-key header and exchanging JSON with ISO 8601 dates; the purchase-orders API exposes GET and Update purchase-order operations so an external system can stay in sync with Tipalti.

providers.name: ASTM International
providers.description: ASTM International is one of the world's largest voluntary standards development organizations, founded in 1898. ASTM publishes more than 13,000 globally recognized consensus standards across 150+ technical committees and 2,100+ subcommittees, developed by 30,000+ volunteer members from 140+ countries. ASTM standards span ferrous and nonferrous metals, cement and concrete, petroleum, plastics, textiles, additive manufacturing, medical devices, consumer products, unmanned aircraft, artificial intelligence in manufacturing, and dozens of other domains. Standards are delivered through the ASTM Compass platform, ASTM Digital Library, ASTM SpecBuilder, and through publisher and reseller channels. ASTM does not publish a public REST API for its catalog; integration with Compass is via SAML SSO, Shibboleth, OpenAthens, and IP authentication.

providers.name: BabyList
providers.description: Babylist is the leading universal baby registry and a baby-focused commerce and content company for growing families. Because the registry is universal, parents can add any product from any store — including Amazon, Target, and Etsy — to a single list. Babylist has grown into a full ecosystem spanning the Babylist registry, the Babylist Shop, Babylist Health (insurance-covered breast pumps), Babylist Money (family financial planning), expert product guides, and a flagship Los Angeles showroom. More than 10 million people shop with Babylist every year. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network; Babylist runs no public developer API, but it does publish an llms.txt agent surface and an OpenID Connect discovery document.

providers.name: Back
providers.description: Back is a Berlin-based employee experience and internal service platform that gives HR, IT, Finance, and Office teams one place to receive, automate, and resolve employee requests. It brings conversations from Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email into a single shared inbox, answers common questions with a self-service knowledge chatbot, and automates lifecycle journeys such as onboarding, offboarding, and leave with approvals, forms, and integrations. Founded in 2018 and backed by Point Nine and Seedcamp, Back is used by companies including Loom, Netlify, Choco, Pleo, Marley Spoon, and Statista. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Back offers an API for custom integrations on select plans, but publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or reference at time of enrichment.

providers.name: Bitmain
providers.description: Bitmain Technologies is a Beijing-based designer and manufacturer of ASIC cryptocurrency-mining hardware, best known for its Antminer line of Bitcoin (SHA-256) and other proof-of-work miners. Bitmain also operates Antpool, one of the world's largest Bitcoin mining pools, which exposes a public HTTP API that lets account operators programmatically read account balances, account and worker hashrate, worker lists, payment history, and pool-wide statistics. The Antpool API authenticates each request with an HMAC-SHA256 signature computed from the operator's user id, API key, and an incrementing nonce, and rate-limits clients to 600 requests per 10 minutes per IP. This company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Black Unicorn Factory
providers.description: Black Unicorn Factory (BUF) is a Los Angeles based pre-IPO business accelerator that prepares companies led by founders from underrepresented communities for direct listings on national stock exchanges, positioning equity rather than debt as the route to capital. Its programs run a four-step readiness pathway — foundation and readiness assessment, compliance and corporate structure, SEC filing and disclosure, and market readiness — alongside the New Black Wall Street pre-IPO program and the Follow Me For Equity (FMFE) platform, an iOS and Android application through which individuals earn stock in participating pre-IPO companies by completing verified social engagement tasks instead of investing cash. Black Unicorn Factory is a private company whose shares appear on secondary marketplaces; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Brit + Co
providers.description: Brit + Co is a lifestyle and entertainment media platform founded by Brit Morin that publishes content and creative education for a primarily women audience. It covers self-care, food, home and DIY, travel, relationships, celebrity and entertainment news, horoscopes, shopping guides, and games, and operates a learning platform (learn.brit.co) offering more than one hundred creative online classes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures. It is a consumer media and e-learning brand and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
providers.description: ATF is a law enforcement agency in the United States Department of Justice that protects communities from violent criminals, criminal organizations, the illegal use and trafficking of firearms, the illegal use and storage of explosives, acts of arson and bombings, acts of terrorism, and the illegal diversion of alcohol and tobacco products. ATF publishes firearms trace data, crime statistics, and regulatory information.

providers.name: Cape Analytics
providers.description: Cape Analytics (now part of Moody's) is a geospatial property intelligence provider that applies computer vision and machine learning to high-resolution aerial and satellite imagery, property records, and other novel data sources to produce inspection-quality condition and characteristic data for over 100 million residential and commercial structures across the United States and Canada. Its insights — roof condition and material, swimming pools, solar panels, accessory structures, tree overhang, wildfire and wind exposure, distance to hazards, and a proprietary Liquidity Score — are delivered to insurance underwriters, lenders, and real estate investors in under two seconds via API, batch/bulk files, an Automated Property Condition Report (aPCR), and a customer web portal, as well as through third-party platforms such as Guidewire and Duck Creek. Cape does not publish a public, self-service developer portal or open API specification; API access is provisioned to customers and partners through a gated onboarding flow.

providers.name: Chubb
providers.description: Chubb Limited is the world's largest publicly traded property and casualty (P&C) insurance company, serving consumers, small businesses, and multinational corporations across 54 countries and territories. Chubb offers commercial and personal property and casualty insurance, personal accident and supplemental health insurance, reinsurance, and life insurance. The company manages more than $200B in global assets, paid $21B in claims (2023), and offers more than 200 insurance products and services. Key personal lines include homeowners, auto, valuables (jewelry, arts, wine), boat and yacht, pet (through a Healthy Paws partnership), and travel insurance. Commercial lines include small business, accident and health, commercial package, cyber, management liability, marine, professional liability, workers' compensation, and industry-specialty programs (construction, financial institutions, healthcare, life sciences, manufacturing, real estate, technology, climate). Chubb Studio is the company's embedded insurance technology platform offering APIs and SDKs for partners to integrate Chubb insurance products into their own digital experiences.

providers.name: Comfi Holdings Limited
providers.description: Comfi (Comfi Holdings Limited) is a UAE-based financial technology company providing B2B working capital solutions for small and medium enterprises and trading businesses. Its three core products are invoice discounting (turning outstanding invoices into immediate cash), Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) for flexible B2B credit terms, and automotive dealer inventory financing. Comfi positions itself around speed — "capital in hours, not weeks" — and reports 1,000+ SMEs served, 15,000+ invoices financed, and $100M+ capital deployed across the UAE market. Eligibility requires a UAE-registered B2B business with at least six months of operating history and AED 100,000+ monthly revenue. Backed by 500 Global. No public API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal was found at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Continuum
providers.description: Continuum (gocontinuum.ai) is an AI-powered platform that automates B2B returns, warranties, and repairs for distributors and manufacturers. It handles the post-sales workflow end to end through four solution hubs: a Customer Hub with self-service warranty and return portals, a Warehouse Hub for one-click receiving, inspection and dispute processing, a Vendor & Finance Hub for automated vendor engagement and accounts-receivable management, and a Manufacturer Warranty Hub for warranty claim automation. The company reports outcomes such as a 70% reduction in returns labor cost, a 30% increase in profitability, and an 8% reduction in customer churn. Continuum integrates with major distribution ERP systems (Infor, NetSuite, Epicor, Oracle, Acumatica). Based in Chicago, it is seed-funded and backed by Cowboy Ventures. Continuum is SOC 2 audited and publishes a public trust center. No public developer API or documentation is available at this time.

providers.name: CoolerX
providers.description: CoolerX — formerly Cooler Screens — is an in-store retail media and merchandising technology company that turns cooler doors, endcaps, checkout coolers and pharmacy fixtures into IoT-connected digital screens. The platform pairs an AI "Intent Engine" for contextual targeting and conversion-funnel optimization with a Dynamic Content Engine for creative optimization, alongside campaign management, real-time measurement, and a data integration hub for product, price, promotion and context data. It is deployed with retailers including Kroger, Walgreens, Giant Eagle's GetGo, Chevron and Western Union, and is built on Microsoft Azure with NVIDIA, BOE, LG, Samsung and Foxconn as hardware and infrastructure partners. CoolerX sells to retailers and brands through a demo and sales motion; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: DELLI
providers.description: DELLI is a UK online marketplace for independent food and drink makers, founded in 2022 by Depop founder Simon Beckerman with co-founder Marie Petrovicka. Often described as "the Depop for food," DELLI curates niche and small-batch products — snacks, sauces and condiments, pantry staples, drinks, alcohol, sweets and lifestyle goods — from micro-bakers, picklers, olive-oil producers and drink makers, and sells them to consumers, in part through a drop-style release model. The platform has since evolved into an AI-powered companion for makers and retailers, adding tools that cut the operational overhead of running a small food business. DELLI is backed by Balderton Capital and HV Capital, the original investors in Depop. The storefront runs on Shopify; DELLI publishes no first-party developer API at this time.

providers.name: Diagon
providers.description: Diagon is a California-based industrial equipment sourcing company building Albus, an equipment intelligence platform for manufacturing buyers and sellers. Buyers search across millions of industrial equipment listings, compare models, specifications, pricing and availability, and connect directly with sellers; sellers publish AI-powered catalogs, reach qualified buyer demand, and see live equipment searches in real time. Diagon indexes manufacturing equipment products, suppliers and service providers, bringing hardware, services and financing into a consolidated procurement experience. Founded by a team out of Tesla, Bright Machines, Rivian and Snackpass, and backed by Anthemis under its data, tech and infrastructure thesis. Diagon publishes no public developer API today; its /api surface is an authenticated first-party application API (Clerk-based session auth) and is disallowed in robots.txt.

providers.name: Diagon Technologies
providers.description: Diagon Technologies operates Albus, an industrial equipment intelligence and procurement platform for North American manufacturing. Albus aggregates millions of industrial equipment listings so buyers can search by make, model, or specification, compare equipment specs, pricing, and availability side by side, and connect directly with sellers to request quotes. Sellers publish AI-powered catalogs, reach qualified buyer demand, and see live equipment searches in real time across categories such as subtractive manufacturing, forming, joining, surface treatment, and polymer processing, and OEMs including DMG Mori, Trumpf, Okuma, FANUC, and Mazak. Diagon is a Techstars portfolio company; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Faks
providers.description: Faks is a French SaaS platform that digitizes and streamlines the commercial relationships across the pharmacy ecosystem. It gives pharmacies, pharmacy groups (groupements), and laboratories a single place to manage supplier relationships, commercial claims and disputes (litiges), expired and returnable product handling, promotions, and sell-in / sell-out performance. Faks connects to pharmacy management systems (LGO), purchasing platforms, and accounting tools through its Konnect integrations to automate what has traditionally been manual, paper, and email-driven work between the ~18,000 pharmacies, ~100 groups, and ~500 laboratories it targets in France. The company is backed by Seedcamp. Faks does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and the enrichment surfaces that could be probed.

providers.name: FLYR Labs
providers.description: FLYR (formerly FLYR Labs) is a San Francisco-headquartered travel technology company, founded in 2013, that builds an AI-native commercial operating system for airlines, cargo carriers and hospitality operators. Its airline portfolio spans the Cirrus Revenue Operating System (deep-learning forecasting, dynamic pricing and revenue management) and an Offer & Order Management System built on IATA open standards — NDC and ONE Order — with a certified NDC+ API, an NDC Gateway for indirect and B2B channels (GDS, OTAs), and a Legacy Translator for backward compatibility with existing PSS estates. Its hospitality arm, FLYR Hospitality (built on the acquired Pace Revenue platform), ships Optimize, Insights, Planning and Groups to 2,300+ properties with native two-way integrations into property management systems including Mews, Oracle OPERA Cloud, Apaleo, Cloudbeds, RMS Cloud, Stayntouch and Planet/Protel. FLYR has raised over $500M and employs more than 700 people. Its APIs are commercial and partner-gated: the developer portal at developer.flyr.com requires an account, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or GraphQL schema is published to anonymous callers.

providers.name: Gameforge
providers.description: Gameforge AG is a German publisher of free-to-play online and browser games, headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany. Its catalog includes long-running titles such as OGame, Ikariam, Metin2, AION, NosTale, and other strategy and MMO games played across dozens of localized game servers. Gameforge's flagship title OGame exposes a public read-only game-data API that returns highscores, player and alliance rosters, universe/planet layouts, and per-server metadata as XML feeds (with an opt-in JSON representation), plus a separate access-controlled API that approved third-party tool developers can request for combat and report data. Gameforge also runs a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program through Bugcrowd. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Gigster
providers.description: Gigster is an enterprise software-development services company that connects businesses with top-tier global talent for custom software development, AI solutions, and digital transformation. Through a network of 50,000+ vetted developers, designers, and product experts, Gigster delivers work under three engagement models: Fully Managed (Gigster owns scoping through delivery), Dedicated Teams (skilled teams that scale with a client's goals), and Talent On Demand (specialists who blend into an existing team). Specialized practices cover AI development, innovation/design/UX, applications and platforms, and system modernization. Gigster reports 1,000+ enterprise engagements, a 95% on-time/on-budget delivery rate, and average staffing under 10 days, and is backed by a16z, Bloomberg Beta, and Redpoint Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio company profile.

providers.name: Hipcamp
providers.description: Hipcamp is the #1 app to find and book campsites globally, with real-time availability across more than 500,000 sites in the United States, Canada, Australia, and the United Kingdom. Campers search national parks, state parks, RV resorts, and private land stays (farms, ranches, vineyards) in one app, with filters, Pro map layers (BLM/USFS land, cell coverage, dark skies), road-trip search, and free availability alerts. Hosts list and manage campsites, sync calendars, and take weekly payouts. Hipcamp integrates with campground reservation systems (ResNexus, Cloudbeds, Newbook, RMS, Bedful) but publishes no public developer API — /api and /graphql are internal-only. Surfaced as an a16z / Bond Capital / Slow Ventures portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Horizon Quantum Computing
providers.description: Horizon Quantum Computing is a Singapore-based quantum software company founded in 2018 by Dr. Joe Fitzsimons. It builds software infrastructure for quantum applications, centered on Triple Alpha, an integrated development environment that lets developers write hardware-agnostic quantum programs at multiple levels of abstraction and deploy them to quantum processors. Triple Alpha's final workflow step packages a program and deploys it as an API so developers can invoke quantum backends from Python scripts, web pages, and other technologies. Horizon operates its own quantum computing testbed at its Singapore headquarters and supports a range of external quantum processors, aiming to bridge the gap between today's quantum hardware and real-world applications. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or client SDK; API-based program deployment is offered to early-access users of the Triple Alpha platform.

providers.name: Housewhisper
providers.description: HouseWhisper (legal name Real Estate Productivity, Inc.) is a Seattle-based AI platform for real estate teams and brokerages, founded by former Zillow executives. It acts as a 24/7 AI teammate that automates the full lead lifecycle through personalized voice and text conversations: a Lead Engine that re-engages and revives cold database contacts, a Rules Engine that routes leads to the right agent with fallback escalations, and an AI Teammate that handles CRM updates, follow-ups, scheduling, reminders, and administrative busywork by call or text. It connects to real estate CRM, dialer, and calendar systems via API keys with no data migration, integrating with Follow Up Boss, Sierra Interactive, kvCORE, MoxiWorks, Salesforce, Lofty, HubSpot, and others. Pricing is outcome-based (a small monthly platform fee plus referral fees on closed deals). HouseWhisper has raised roughly $10M in seed funding led by Mayfield. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Hutchinson
providers.description: Hutchinson SA is a French global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Paris, a subsidiary of TotalEnergies. Hutchinson designs and manufactures anti-vibration systems, sealing systems, fluid transfer, precision rubber components, and aerospace systems for the automotive, aerospace, defense, and industrial sectors.

providers.name: iMotorbike
providers.description: iMotorbike is a Southeast Asian online marketplace and service platform for buying, selling, and servicing pre-owned motorcycles, operating across Malaysia and Vietnam. Sellers submit their bike details, book a free inspection, receive a quotation, and get paid fast, while iMotorbike handles loan settlement and JPJ ownership transfer on their behalf. Buyers shop iM Certified motorcycles backed by a 170-point inspection, a 12-month warranty, and a 6-day return policy, and can book test rides, inspections, and roadside assistance (iM Rescue) through the platform. Founded in 2017 and backed by 500 Global, Headline, Gobi Partners, and Endeavor Catalyst, iMotorbike closed a US$10M Series A in 2025 to expand across the region. The company runs a consumer-facing web marketplace and an internal admin platform; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Incluyeme
providers.description: Incluyeme.com is a Latin American social enterprise, founded in 2013 by Gabriel Marcolongo, working toward the social and labor inclusion of people with disabilities. Its online platform connects candidates with disabilities to inclusive employers, offering job listings, virtual training courses, scholarships, and mentorship for individuals, alongside inclusive-hiring consulting, talent sourcing, staff training, and physical/web accessibility evaluation for companies. Operating across roughly a dozen countries in Latin America (Argentina, Chile, Peru, Colombia, Mexico, Uruguay, Paraguay and more), it has registered hundreds of thousands of people with disabilities and placed thousands into roles with 100+ corporate clients. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Kriptos
providers.description: Kriptos is an AI-driven unstructured data security platform that automatically discovers, classifies, and labels documents across endpoints, servers, and cloud storage, then feeds that business and risk context into the DLP, CASB, SIEM, EDR, and IAM tooling an organization already runs rather than replacing it. The platform spans data discovery and classification, data compliance and risk management, data access governance across Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, insider threat management with UEBA, DSPM, and AI governance covering shadow-AI monitoring for tools such as Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini. Classification results are written back as native Microsoft Purview and Google Drive labels. Founded in Ecuador and backed by Techstars, Kriptos reports more than 1.2 billion documents classified for over 150,000 users, with customers concentrated in banking, insurance, healthcare, and utilities across Latin America. Kriptos is a sales-led product and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation.

providers.name: Lagom
providers.description: Lagom is an open source framework for building reactive microservice systems in Java and Scala, built on top of Akka and Play Framework, designed for distributed architectures.

providers.name: Lamudi
providers.description: Lamudi is an online real estate classifieds marketplace focused exclusively on emerging markets, founded in 2013 and today operating consumer property portals in the Philippines (lamudi.com.ph), Indonesia (lamudi.co.id) and Mexico (lamudi.com.mx). The platform lets buyers, renters, sellers and landlords search and list houses, condominiums/apartments, land, commercial space and offices, filtered by geography, property group and operation (buy/rent). Search results pages carry area market statistics, interactive maps and nearby points of interest, alongside country-specific features such as Philippine foreclosures and home-loan comparison, Indonesian KPR mortgage simulators, and Mexican Infonavit-eligible listings and bank repossessions. Agencies and developers publish inventory through the pro.lamudi.com professional portal. Lamudi operates as part of LIFULL Connect, which supplies its legal notice, privacy policy and contact surface. Lamudi publishes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal; its notable machine-readable surface is a first-party llms.txt on each country site that documents the URL grammar of its search, new development and project pages for AI agents.

providers.name: Legora
providers.description: Legora is a Stockholm- and London-based legal AI company (formerly Leya) building a collaborative AI workspace for lawyers. The platform is centered on Legora aOS, an agentic operating system that connects information, communication, and the execution of legal work across Agent, Monitors, Lists, Legal Research, Tabular Review, Workflows, and the client-facing Portal, with Word and Outlook add-ins, an Editor, and a mobile app. Legora is sold to elite law firms and in-house legal teams via enterprise contracts; customers include Mannheimer Swartling, Goodwin Procter, Cleary Gottlieb, Linklaters, Bird & Bird, and HWL Ebsworth, with 400+ firms across 40+ countries. There is no public, self-serve developer API, SDK, or open-source release; integrations are arranged through enterprise sales and partnership engagements, and the platform runs on Azure OpenAI Service with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, GDPR, and HIPAA controls.

providers.name: Lenskart
providers.description: Lenskart is a direct-to-consumer eyewear company operating an omnichannel retail business across prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, contact lenses and eye-care services. It sells through localized storefronts (India, United States, Singapore and other markets) and mobile apps, and merchandises its own house brands including Vincent Chase, John Jacobs, Lenskart Studio and Lenskart Boost alongside third-party labels. The digital experience layer includes 3D/AR virtual try-on and look comparison, a saved-prescription and prescription-history profile, order tracking and a loyalty program. Lenskart is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. As of this enrichment pass Lenskart publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition or client SDKs; the developer- and docs-named subdomains that resolve are gated behind Cloudflare and return 403 to unauthenticated clients, so no API surface could be verified.

providers.name: Lessen
providers.description: Lessen is a Scottsdale, Arizona based property services and facilities management technology company that connects commercial and residential property owners and managers with a nationwide network of vetted service providers for repairs, maintenance, turns, make-readies and capital projects. The company operates a technology platform stack — One by Lessen for work-order, vendor-sourcing and invoicing workflow, Lessen 360 for multifamily maintenance, Lessen Pro for affiliate contractors, Aiden for AI-assisted work-order creation, and the Lessen Marketplace for procurement — supported by mobile apps for tenants, property managers and vendors. Lessen serves retail, financial services, healthcare, food service, industrial, hospitality and education properties alongside single-family and multifamily residential portfolios. Lessen acquired SMS Assist in 2023 and is backed by Fifth Wall and General Catalyst. Lessen publishes no public developer portal, API reference or OpenAPI definition; its named platform integrations are delivered as private partner connections rather than a self-serve API program.

providers.name: Linux
providers.description: Linux is an open-source Unix-like operating system kernel originally created by Linus Torvalds. This index catalogs the userspace and kernel programming interfaces exposed by Linux, including system calls, eBPF, ioctl, netlink, procfs, sysfs, GPIO, and security interfaces such as Seccomp, Landlock, and Linux Security Modules. It also covers ecosystem APIs for systemd and PAM.

providers.name: Montenegro Open Data
providers.description: Montenegro Open Data is a national government open-data portal for Montenegro running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 894 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: MyBuilder
providers.description: MyBuilder is a UK online marketplace that connects homeowners with local, reviewed tradespeople for home improvement, repair and maintenance work. Founded in 2004 by stonemason Ryan Notz and headquartered in London, the platform lets homeowners post a job for free, review interested tradespeople by their profiles, work history and customer feedback, and shortlist the ones they want to hire. Tradespeople browse leads for free and pay a fee only when a customer shortlists them. MyBuilder was acquired by IAC's HomeAdvisor in 2017 and now operates as part of the Instapro Group of European home-services marketplaces. MyBuilder is a consumer-facing web platform and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, security and domain posture.

providers.name: Opto
providers.description: Opto (Opto Investments) is an end-to-end private markets investment platform built for wealth managers - RIAs, family offices, and private banks. The platform helps advisors build, fundraise for, and manage private investment programs across asset classes including infrastructure, private credit, private equity, real estate, and venture capital. Opto covers the full workflow: modeling allocations and automating operations to build a program, creating client materials and streamlining subscriptions to fundraise, and deploying capital with automated post-trade reporting to manage it. The company connects to existing custodians, investment-management tools, and reporting providers, and was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc. No public developer API or documentation is published at this time; access is through the advisor application and partner program.

providers.name: PACER Case Locator (PCL)
providers.description: The PACER Case Locator (PCL) is a nationwide index of federal court cases. The public PCL API allows users to programmatically search the PCL for federal cases across U.S. district, bankruptcy, and appellate courts using the same search functionality and dataset as the PCL web application.

providers.name: Paro
providers.description: Paro is an AI-powered professional services marketplace that connects businesses and accounting firms with vetted, on-demand finance and accounting experts. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Chicago, Paro uses proprietary AI matching to pair clients with the top 2% of finance professionals across 60+ industries and 250+ skill sets — spanning bookkeeping, fractional CFO and controller services, financial planning and analysis, tax and compliance, and full-time recruiting. For accounting firms it provides staff augmentation, busy-season support, and service-expansion consulting. Paro operates a talent platform (app.paro.io) but does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, content, and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PartyDAO
providers.description: PartyDAO is the decentralized autonomous organization behind Party Protocol, an open, GPL-3.0 protocol for on-chain group coordination that aims to make Ethereum "multiplayer." Party Protocol lets groups form a Party (a shared Ethereum account with members, an inventory, and governance), collectively crowdfund to acquire assets, govern shared holdings, and distribute value to members — all through audited Solidity smart contracts rather than a hosted HTTP API. PartyDAO also ships Party (party.app), a consumer application built on the protocol. The developer surface is entirely on-chain: smart contracts, deployed contract addresses, and technical documentation for integrating via web3 libraries and direct contract calls. There is no REST/HTTP API, hosted SDK, or OAuth surface; integration happens by calling the deployed contracts.

providers.name: Pensive
providers.description: Pensive is an AI grading platform for educators at schools and universities. Its "AI Grader" helps instructors evaluate student work — grading assignments and returning feedback at scale — alongside an AI tutor product for students. Pensive serves distinct teacher, student, and administrator surfaces, publishes case studies with university instructors, and maintains a SOC 2 trust center. It is a seed-stage company backed by Mayfield. As of this profiling Pensive operates a private, authenticated web product and publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Poka
providers.description: Poka is a manufacturing-focused connected worker platform that helps industrial and frontline teams standardize work execution across learning, daily management, and operations. It combines digital work instructions, on-the-job training, skills management, and factory-floor knowledge sharing with embedded Industrial AI. Poka exposes a RESTful Poka API for building integrations with third-party systems (MES, CMMS, LMS, QMS, ERP, BI), SCIM for automated user provisioning from identity providers, the Poka Automate iPaaS, and a Poka Data Lake for BI/reporting. Poka is part of IFS and runs regionally in the US, Canada, and EU.

providers.name: Quantum Machines
providers.description: Quantum Machines is a Tel Aviv, Israel-based quantum control company that builds the Quantum Orchestration Platform (QOP) — a unified hardware and software stack for controlling quantum processors at the pulse level. Its hardware portfolio centers on the OPX+ and OPX1000 controllers, which are built around a custom Pulse Processing Unit (PPU) architecture that executes classical control and real-time feedback alongside arbitrary waveform generation, with sub-microsecond classical-quantum round trips and 160 ns active reset latency. The platform is programmed in QUA, the company's domain-specific pulse-level language, exposed to developers through the qm-qua Python SDK and an extensive open-source ecosystem under the qua-platform GitHub organization (QUAlibrate, QUAM, qua-libs, py-qua-tools, qua-dashboards). Quantum Machines also ships peripheral hardware including the Octave up/down converter (to 18 GHz), QDAC-II ultra-low-noise DACs, QSwitch, QBox, and the QCage/QBoard/QFilter cryogenic line. The platform is qubit-modality agnostic, supporting superconducting, semiconductor spin, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and color-center systems, and is used by university labs (MIT, Caltech, Harvard, Princeton, Weizmann) and quantum startups (Alice & Bob, Diraq, EeroQ). Quantum Machines has partnered with NVIDIA on the DGX Quantum hybrid quantum-classical compute platform and acquired the Delft-based QHarbor Bioscience team as a European R&D hub. Quantum Machines does not currently publish a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or self-service developer signup; the QOP control surface is reached exclusively via the qm-qua Python SDK against an OPX/OPX1000 controller (hardware or qm-saas cloud simulator).

providers.name: Quizlet
providers.description: Quizlet is a San Francisco-based global learning platform offering flashcards, practice tests, and AI-powered study tools used by students, teachers, and lifelong learners. Core features include user-created and expert-verified study sets, Learn mode (adaptive practice), Test mode, Match game, Spaced Repetition, and an AI tutor (Q-Chat / Magic Notes) that generates flashcards, summaries, practice questions, and explanations from uploaded notes, PDFs, slides, and textbooks. Quizlet Plus is the company's consumer subscription, and Quizlet for Schools / Teachers provides licensed offerings for classrooms. The platform integrates with Google Classroom (share-as-assignment) and Canvas (embeddable widgets) but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK — the legacy Developer API 2.0 (`quizlet.com/api/2.0`) was effectively wound down to partners-only and is not openly registrable. Quizlet's GitHub organization (`github.com/quizlet`) hosts internal tooling, GitHub Actions, and forks of OSS dependencies (HHVM/Hack, PHPUnit, Mockery, Stylus, etc.) rather than a developer-facing API platform.

providers.name: RatedPower
providers.description: RatedPower, part of Enverus (ENVERUS RATEDPOWER S.L.U., Madrid, Spain), is a cloud software platform for the design and engineering of utility-scale renewable energy projects. Its pvDesign product automates solar photovoltaic (PV) plant layout, energy-yield simulation, battery energy storage system (BESS) and hybrid plant design, substation and grid-connection engineering, earthwork estimating, and bankable proposal documentation. The platform is delivered as a browser-based SaaS application (login at ratedpower.enverus.com) and reports 64,000+ projects designed and 5.1 TW of simulated capacity. No public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal is published; enterprise automation access exists only behind the authenticated application. This profile was seeded as a Techstars portfolio lead and has been run through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Relay
providers.description: Relay is an online business banking and cash-flow management platform for small and medium-sized businesses, offering up to 20-50 checking accounts, virtual and physical Visa debit/credit cards, accounts payable and bill pay, and one-way data integrations with accounting and payroll tools such as QuickBooks Online, Xero, and Gusto. Banking services are provided by Thread Bank, Member FDIC. Relay does not publish a public developer API; the surfaces below are product features and inbound integrations rather than developer-facing APIs.

providers.name: RippleMatch
providers.description: RippleMatch is an AI-powered early-career recruiting platform that matches college students and recent graduates with internships and entry-level jobs based on their background, skills, and career goals rather than mass applications. For employers it offers "Campus OS", an all-in-one recruiting operating system for sourcing, skills validation, and campus event management, and it transfers matched candidates into most major applicant tracking systems (Greenhouse, Workday, Lever, SmartRecruiters, BambooHR). RippleMatch was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook/event surface; its integrations are one-way ATS data transfers rather than an openly documented API.

providers.name: SkyWest Airlines
providers.description: SkyWest Airlines is the largest regional airline in North America, headquartered in St. George, Utah. Operating under partnership agreements with United Airlines, Delta Air Lines, American Airlines, and Alaska Airlines, SkyWest serves over 256 destinations across the United States, Canada, and Mexico with a fleet of 500+ Bombardier regional jets (CRJ200, CRJ550, CRJ900). Founded in 1972, SkyWest carries over 46 million passengers annually operating as United Express, Delta Connection, American Eagle, and Alaska SkyWest. The company does not offer a public developer API; flight data is accessible through third-party aviation data providers.

providers.name: SMTP
providers.description: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the foundational internet standard for transmitting electronic mail across networks. Defined in RFC 5321 (October 2008), SMTP uses a command-response model over TCP port 25 (or 587 for submission, 465 for SMTPS). It defines commands including EHLO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, and DATA, along with a comprehensive set of response codes. SMTP works in conjunction with RFC 5322 (Internet Message Format) which defines the structure of email messages.

providers.name: Speero
providers.description: Speero (سبيرو) is Saudi Arabia's online marketplace for authentic automotive spare parts, accessories, and professional vehicle services. The platform helps car owners find OEM and aftermarket parts for their specific make and model across all major categories (engine, brakes, suspension, lighting, AC, exhaust, and more) and book maintenance, detailing, paint and dent repair, tinting, and tire care at trusted workshops across the Kingdom. It supports browse-by-vehicle, installment payment options, and WhatsApp-based customer support. Speero is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer marketplace and publishes no public developer API, but it does expose a machine-discovery surface (llms.txt, RFC 9116 security.txt, and an RFC 9727 api-catalog linkset).

providers.name: Step
providers.description: Step is an all-in-one mobile banking platform built for teens, young adults, and families. The Step Visa Card is a secured card that builds credit history reported to Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion, and teens can begin building credit before they turn 18 through parent-managed accounts. Step also offers savings rewards, cashback with partner brands, EarlyPay paycheck advances up to $250, commission-free stock investing powered by DriveWealth, early direct deposit, and the Money 101 financial education hub. Banking services are provided by partner Evolve Bank & Trust, Member FDIC. Founded in 2018 in Palo Alto by CJ MacDonald and Alexey Kalinichenko, backed by General Catalyst, and acquired by Beast Industries. Step publishes no public developer API; its programmatic surface is limited to a consumer service status page and a site llms.txt.

providers.name: Strella
providers.description: Strella is an AI-powered customer research platform that automates qualitative research at scale. It runs AI-moderated interviews with adaptive questioning, auto-generates discussion guides, recruits participants from an 8M+ global panel or a company's own customers, supports 46+ languages, and synthesizes insights and video highlights within hours instead of weeks. Research types span exploratory research, concept testing, usability testing, market research, and customer journey mapping. Strella is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. No public developer API or SDK surface is currently published; this profile captures the company identity, security posture, and product changelog.

providers.name: Sumer
providers.description: Sumer (Sumer.Money) is a blockchain liquidity infrastructure protocol positioning itself as the most capital-efficient way to put crypto assets to work across chains. Users deposit native assets such as liquid staked ETH, and Sumer's correlation-aware risk engine matches assets and liabilities to mint synthetic suTokens (suETH, suUSD) that act as "money multipliers" — travelling across connected blockchains as collateral while the underlying deposit keeps accruing staking rewards and lending interest. The protocol runs an omnichain lending/borrowing market, a points and veSumer staking program, and its Supernova EVM chain, drawing price data from Chainlink, Pyth, RedStone, and Supra oracles. Backed by Pantera Capital and other crypto investors, with contracts audited by Certik, Ancilia, Tikkala, and CD Security.

providers.name: Sweep
providers.description: Sweep is an enterprise carbon and ESG data management platform helping large organizations measure, manage, report, and reduce their carbon emissions and broader sustainability performance across Scope 1, 2, and 3 following the GHG Protocol. Its platform centralizes sustainability data across an organization and its value chain to produce audit-ready data from a single source, covering carbon accounting, ESG disclosure, value-chain engagement with supplier portals and automated data collection, audit and assurance trails, and business intelligence with dashboards and scenario modeling. Sweep supports compliance with the CSRD, ISSB, GRI, CDP, SFDR, TCFD, UK SRS, the GHG Protocol, and US state regulation including California SB 253 and SB 261, with vertical solutions for asset managers, asset owners, private markets, banks, healthcare, manufacturing, retail, energy, and consumer goods. Sweep was named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape 2026 for Carbon Management and recognized in the Verdantix 2026 Green Quadrant. The platform exposes data ingestion via API and SFTP and integrates with ERP, procurement, and HRMS systems, but Sweep does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or open-source repos — API access is delivered through customer engagements rather than a self-serve developer surface.

providers.name: Swept
providers.description: Swept (sweptworks.com) is workforce management software for commercial cleaning and janitorial businesses - scheduling, GPS-verified time tracking and payroll reporting, mobile crew messaging, quality inspections, supply requests, client portals, and one-time work order management. As of this catalog entry, Swept does NOT publish a documented, self-serve public or partner developer API. There is no developer portal, API reference, API key or OAuth signup, published OpenAPI/Swagger specification, or webhook documentation on sweptworks.com or in the Swept Support Center knowledge base. The only documented outbound data path is a one-way, manually-activated QuickBooks Online payroll sync set up per account by a Swept Customer Success Manager - not a self-serve developer integration. Swept's public GitHub organization contains only take-home coding-challenge repositories used for hiring, not a first-party API client, SDK, or spec. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the provider and its access model; no API definitions are asserted because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: Tacto
providers.description: Tacto (Tacto Technology GmbH) is a Munich-based AI procurement intelligence platform for manufacturing companies. It unifies internal ERP and engineering data with external market intelligence to power AI agents that automate procurement work across four areas: Supplier Intelligence (centralized supplier management with documents, evaluations and performance data), Spend & Cost Intelligence (spend analysis and savings identification), Sourcing Intelligence (AI-optimized RFQ and price inquiries) and Compliance Intelligence (automated regulatory and supply-chain due-diligence detection). Tacto is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified and GDPR compliant with EU-only hosting and an audit log of every AI action. It does not publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures the company's corporate, security and compliance surface.

providers.name: Tealet
providers.description: Tealet is a wholesale tea marketplace that connects independent tea growers and family farms directly with retailers and businesses. Buyers browse, trace, and order specialty teas sourced from family farms and cooperatives across 8 countries and 15 growing regions, with grower profiles, farm videos, subscription ordering, and a wholesale request flow that emphasize transparency and direct trade from source to cup. Tealet originated in Hawaii and is backed by 500 Startups and Blue Startups. The company operates a consumer/B2B web storefront with account sign-up, newsletter, and blog; it does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or an MCP server.

providers.name: Tia
providers.description: Tia is a women's healthcare company that operates in-person clinics and a virtual care platform, bringing primary care, gynecology, mental health, and wellness services into one connected care experience. Founded in 2017 and backed by Canaan Partners, Tia runs clinics in New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix, offers virtual visits across multiple states, and partners with health systems. Tia is a consumer healthcare provider and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Trelora
providers.description: Trelora is a technology-driven, full-service discount real estate brokerage founded in Denver, Colorado and now operating as part of HomeSmart. It lets people buy and sell homes for a low, transparent fee instead of the traditional percentage-based commission, helping sellers save thousands of dollars and offering buyers cash-back rebates of up to several thousand dollars at closing. Trelora pairs salaried, non-commissioned real estate agents with an online platform and IDX-powered property search across markets including Colorado, Washington, and other U.S. states, and publishes a real estate blog, glossary, and city-level market reports. Originally a Techstars-backed startup, Trelora is consumer-facing and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Tungee
providers.description: Tungee (Guangzhou Tungee Technology Co., Ltd., 探迹科技) is a Chinese AI sales-intelligence company backed by Qiming Venture Partners. Its Tungee AI Sales Cloud covers the full B2B sales cycle -- AI prospecting over a 300M+ company knowledge graph, inbound capture, outreach via call center, SMS, and email, and an AI CRM -- plus a Sales GPT agent line, a mobile app, and a DingTalk edition. The group also operates Futern, an international B2B leads product, and reports 50,000+ customers. Tungee publishes no public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Tuniu
providers.description: Tuniu (途牛旅游网) is a leading online leisure travel company in China, headquartered in Nanjing and listed on NASDAQ under ticker TOUR. It offers packaged tours, self-guided tours, and a broad range of travel-related services and products including hotels, flights, train tickets, cruises, visas, and local activities. For partners, Tuniu runs an Open Platform (途牛开放平台) at developer.tuniu.com that exposes supplier and retail-partner integration APIs behind developer registration, letting suppliers publish inventory and retail partners distribute Tuniu travel products. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Umrahme
providers.description: Umrahme is a consumer online travel platform from the Traveazy Group focused on the Umrah pilgrimage, letting pilgrims across the GCC, UK, US, Europe, and Egypt book complete Umrah packages as well as individual hotels in Makkah and Madinah, Haramain high-speed train tickets, ground transfers, holiday add-ons, and travel eSIMs. The company is an Accel portfolio company and operates a companion B2B portal for travel agents, mobile apps on iOS and Android, and a travel-guide blog, but publishes no public developer or API program.

providers.name: Varagesale
providers.description: VarageSale is a community-based online marketplace for buying and selling used items locally, founded in 2012 by Montreal teacher Tami Zuckerman and programmer Carl Mercier and headquartered in Toronto, Ontario. Members join a local community, verify their identity, and buy and sell with verified neighbors through native iOS and Android apps and the web, with communities across North America and beyond. Backed by Sequoia Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners, VarageSale was acquired by VerticalScope in 2017, with online auction company MaxSold assuming operational control in early 2026. It is a direct-to-consumer marketplace and does not publish a public developer API, so this record captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Xtime
providers.description: Xtime is Cox Automotive's service experience platform for franchised auto dealerships, combining online appointment scheduling, service-lane check-in, multi-point vehicle inspection, customer communications, service marketing, and payments into one fixed-operations workflow. Part of Cox Automotive since 2014 alongside Dealertrack, VinSolutions, Kelley Blue Book, and vAuto, Xtime integrates with DMS and dealer-website partners through the Cox Automotive ecosystem; it publishes no public self-serve API or developer portal, with partner integration handled via the Cox Automotive Integration Platform.

providers.name: 42 Technologies
providers.description: 42 Technologies is a retail business-intelligence and reporting platform, founded in 2013, that consolidates omnichannel retail data — point-of-sale, ecommerce, wholesale, and online-marketplace sources — into a single unified dashboard. It provides merchandisers, buyers, and retail executives with more than 100 purpose-built retail metrics, NRF retail-calendar-aware analytics, multi-currency support, and automated reporting, integrating with 100+ systems including Shopify, NetSuite, Amazon, Walmart, Magento, and WooCommerce. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; 42 does not publish a public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Alcove
providers.description: Alcove is an AI-powered procurement and project management platform built for interior designers, contractors, event planners, and purchasing agents. It consolidates product details, quotes, financials, and order tracking into a single hub, automatically tracking orders across vendors and projects, managing tasks and timelines, calculating profitability and markups, and offering a purchasing service with Designer Net discounts. An AI assistant surfaces financial insights, suggests markups, reviews approvals, and powers filtering. Alcove is a Menlo Ventures portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing site and web application but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Allocate
providers.description: Allocate is a technology platform positioned as an "operating system for private markets," enabling wealth advisory firms, family offices, and asset managers to source, transact, and manage private-market investments across venture capital, growth equity, buyouts, and private credit. The platform offers white-label fund creation for advisors, AI-powered portfolio management with document aggregation, curated manager access, and SPV infrastructure for aggregating smaller commitments. Allocate reports over $4.9B in assets on platform, 370+ wealth advisory firm clients, and 1,500+ manager relationships. It is a private company backed by investors including Anthemis, a16z, Portage, and M13. Allocate does not currently publish a public developer program or API; this API Evangelist profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Archer Aviation
providers.description: Archer Aviation is a U.S. eVTOL aircraft company developing Midnight, a piloted four-passenger all-electric aircraft designed for rapid back-to-back urban flights of roughly 20-50 miles with a ~10 minute charge between trips. Archer is pursuing FAA Type Certification and operates through commercial and defense business lines. Key partnerships include Stellantis (contract manufacturing at Archer's Covington, Georgia facility), United Airlines (launch routes including the Manhattan-Newark corridor), and a Launch Edition program in the United Arab Emirates with Abu Dhabi Aviation. Archer also has a dedicated defense division (Archer Defense) developing hybrid VTOL platforms with Anduril and supporting U.S. government missions. The company trades on the NYSE under ACHR.

providers.name: Backpack Healthcare
providers.description: Backpack Healthcare is a virtual (telehealth) pediatric and family mental health provider delivering therapy, psychiatry, and medication management for children, tweens, teens, young adults, and adults. It offers age-based care (Littles 4-10, Tweens & Teens 11-17, Young Adults 18+, and Adults) across concerns including ADHD, anxiety, autism spectrum disorder, depression, OCD, maternal mental health, and substance use, alongside a consumer Self Care / Care Companion mobile app. Backpack partners with health plans, schools, health systems, and community and government agencies to expand access to youth behavioral health, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Calibrate
providers.description: Calibrate is a telehealth metabolic-health and weight-loss company that pairs clinician-prescribed GLP-1 medications with 1:1 video coaching and a science-backed educational curriculum to help members improve metabolic health and achieve sustainable weight loss. Programs are sold directly to individuals (from $199/month) and through employer benefits. Calibrate delivers its service through consumer web and iOS mobile apps rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks the company's public web and account surface. Backed by Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: CD Baby
providers.description: CD Baby is an independent music distribution and publishing administration service for songwriters, performers, and independent record labels. Founded in 1998 and now part of Downtown Music Holdings under Virgin Music Group, CD Baby services over 50 million music assets from creators in hundreds of countries across six continents. The platform distributes music to 150+ digital service providers including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Pandora, Tidal, TikTok, Amazon, Shazam, and Deezer, and is a flagship member of YouTube's Preferred Distributor Program plus a preferred partner with Apple and Spotify. Services include digital distribution, physical CD and vinyl manufacturing, publishing administration, cover song licensing, sync licensing through CDB Boost, YouTube and social monetization, performing rights organization (ASCAP, BMI, SOCAN) registration assistance, and promotion tools via SymphonyOS, HearNow, Show.co, Managed Ads, Groover, Laylo, and Internet Radio Airplay. Pricing is a one-time fee ($9.99 single, $14.99 album) with artists retaining over 90% of earnings. CD Baby has paid out more than $1 billion to artists. CD Baby has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; all distribution and reporting workflows are exposed only through the artist member portal at members.cdbaby.com.

providers.name: CenturyLink (Lumen Technologies)
providers.description: CenturyLink is the residential broadband and home services brand of Lumen Technologies, a Fortune 500 telecommunications provider operating one of the largest fiber networks in North America. Following the Level 3 acquisition and rebrand to Lumen, CenturyLink's developer surface is exposed through the Lumen Developer Center and Lumen API Marketplace, which publish REST APIs secured by OAuth 2.0 for enterprise location qualification, quote-to-order, provisioning, billing, notifications, CDN and edge compute, DDoS mitigation, and Public Sector networking products.

providers.name: Choco
providers.description: Choco is an AI-powered digital ordering platform that simplifies how restaurants order from their food suppliers and distributors. Serving tens of thousands of distributors and over one hundred thousand buyers across the US, UK, Europe, and the GCC, Choco lets restaurateurs place orders and chat with all their suppliers in one app while converting orders into a supplier's preferred format (email, WhatsApp, text, fax, or direct ERP integration).
