Choco connects to supplier ERP systems such as Entree, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics, Target Data System, NCR, Sage, and Odoo, and uses AI — including OrderAgent for multimodal order capture and VoiceAgent built on OpenAI's Realtime API — to turn emails, texts, images, and documents into structured, ERP-ready orders. Choco does not publish a public developer API; integration is delivered through managed ERP connections, and its public GitHub organization (chocoapp) hosts only internal data-engineering and infrastructure tooling rather than client SDKs or API specifications.

providers.name: Cladwell
providers.description: Cladwell is a smart-closet and outfit-planning consumer application that helps people build capsule wardrobes and get more wear out of the clothes they already own. The service digitizes a user's closet, then uses AI styling ("Ask Cladwell") together with weather and personal preferences to recommend daily outfits, reduce over-buying, and encourage sustainable, intentional dressing. With more than one million app downloads, Cladwell is delivered primarily as iOS/Android and web apps (app.cladwell.com) with a subscription model; it currently exposes no public developer API. Founded and led by CEO Erin Flynn, it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Cloover
providers.description: Cloover is a climate-fintech company building an all-in-one, "Shopify of energy" platform for the residential renewable-energy transition. It connects the stakeholders of home energy - installers, homeowners (prosumers), manufacturers, energy providers and investors - so small and mid-sized installation firms can sell, quote, finance and manage solar panels, home batteries, heat pumps and EV charging in a single package. The platform pairs installer sales and operations software with embedded financing and energy management, and offers homeowners flexible subscription and financing options. Founded in 2023 and operating primarily in Germany, Austria and wider Europe, Cloover has raised sizeable seed and Series A equity plus a large debt facility and is backed by QED Investors, MMC Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital and others.

providers.name: Continental AG
providers.description: Continental AG is a German multinational automotive supplier and tire manufacturer headquartered in Hanover. As a global Tier 1 automotive supplier, Continental designs and manufactures tires, automotive electronics, brake systems, powertrain components, ADAS, and interior solutions for vehicle manufacturers worldwide.

providers.name: Credi2
providers.description: Credi2 GmbH is a Vienna, Austria based fintech that operates a white-label, cloud-native embedded lending platform enabling banks, card issuers, and merchants to launch Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) and installment financing products under their own brand. The modular platform covers five financing products - pay per invoice (14-day BNPL), split pay (3-12 month installments up to EUR 5,000), installment loans (up to EUR 50,000 over 84 months), revolving credit lines, and subscription financing - and handles the full lifecycle including core banking operations, credit and risk management, servicing, and collections. Use cases span eCommerce and point-of-sale financing, subscription payments, installment-on-cards, and cash loans, with omni-channel integration and go-live in weeks. Credi2 is ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certified and is backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Cypherium
providers.description: Cypherium is a permissionless Layer-1 blockchain built to bridge centralized (CeFi) and decentralized (DeFi) finance and bring real-world assets on-chain at scale. It runs CypherBFT, a hybrid consensus that pairs GPU proof-of-work committee election with HotStuff Byzantine Fault Tolerance for near-instant finality, and is EVM/Solidity compatible (EVM chain ID 16166). Products include CypherLink (cross-ledger notary), Cypherium Connect (bank integration plugin, marketed as ISO 20022 compliant), the Cypherium Validator, and Cypherium ID (decentralized identity). Developers integrate through an Ethereum-style JSON-RPC node API (eth/web3/net/ personal/miner/txpool/admin namespaces over HTTP, WS and IPC) and a Coinbase Rosetta API implementation for exchange and wallet integration. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fab.com
providers.description: Fab.com is a digital content marketplace operated by Epic Games, where creators buy and sell 3D models, materials, environments, VFX, audio, and game-ready assets. Launched in October 2024, Fab consolidated four of Epic's prior storefronts — the Unreal Engine Marketplace, the Sketchfab Store, Quixel, and the ArtStation Marketplace — into a single catalog with unified licensing, and integrates into Unreal Engine, UEFN, and the Epic Games Launcher. The fabcom entry was originally added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead for the earlier, unrelated Fab.com flash-sale design-commerce company (2011–2015), which wound down before the domain passed to Epic Games; see x-identity-note. Fab publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification as of this pass — the surface captured here is its documentation, support, and security-disclosure posture.

providers.name: Fiverr
providers.description: Fiverr is a global online marketplace for freelance digital services, founded in 2010 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, and publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: FVRR). The platform connects businesses and individuals with freelancers offering "gigs" across hundreds of categories including graphic design, writing and translation, programming and tech, video and animation, digital marketing, music and audio, and AI services. Fiverr also operates Fiverr Pro and Fiverr Enterprise for vetted talent and managed teams, Fiverr Workspace for freelancer business tooling, and an affiliate partnership program. Fiverr does not currently publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI-described API; its programmatic surfaces are limited to the consumer marketplace and partner/affiliate integrations. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched with the public identity, security, and discovery signals available.

providers.name: Game Theory
providers.description: Game Theory is a Bengaluru-based recreational sports and fitness membership platform operating 25+ centers across the city. Its consumer mobile app offers unlimited multi-sport coaching for kids and All Access adult memberships spanning 8+ sports — swimming, badminton, basketball, football, pickleball, squash, and table tennis — alongside pay-per-use slot booking, live game feeds, and corporate wellness programs. A Techstars-backed company, Game Theory publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future developer platform.

providers.name: Haven Connect
providers.description: Haven Connect is an affordable-housing software company (founded 2014, San Jose, CA) that streamlines the affordable-housing application and waitlist process for both property managers and low-income applicants. Its web platform lets property managers publish waitlists, collect and screen online applications, and automate waitlist updates — eliminating paper forms and manual data entry — while giving applicants a single portal to find and apply for affordable housing. Haven Connect is a Techstars Impact portfolio company and has raised roughly $2.9M. It is a SaaS product company with no public developer API; this profile captures its public website, support, and commercial surfaces for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Headnote
providers.description: Headnote is a legal payments and accounts-receivable platform built specifically for law firms. Founded in 2016 by attorney Sarah Schaaf, it lets firms accept trust-compliant credit card and eCheck (ACH) payments via shareable payment links and a hosted client payment portal, then automates collections, AR tracking, and client NPS/satisfaction reporting. Headnote is designed to be 100% compliant with IOLTA rules, the ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct, and lawyer trust/operating account requirements across all 50 states, and integrates with existing billing and practice-management software by attaching a Headnote payment link to invoices. Card and bank data are tokenized with Stripe and Plaid and the platform runs on AWS with PCI-compliant, encrypted-at-rest-and-in-transit infrastructure. Headnote was acquired by ASG LegalTech (an Alpine Investors platform, alongside PracticePanther, Bill4Time, and MerusCase) in 2020. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. Headnote does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile is an identity record.

providers.name: HealthEngine
providers.description: HealthEngine is Australia's largest consumer healthcare marketplace and patient-engagement platform, founded in 2006 and headquartered in Perth, Western Australia. Its consumer app and website let millions of Australians search a national directory of primary-care providers and book, manage, and attend appointments (including telehealth) across GP, dental, allied-health, and specialist practices. For practices, HealthEngine sells a SaaS suite - GP Complete, Patient Connect, Online Booking, Appointment Reminders and Recalls, Featured Listings, online payments, patient reviews, and Scripts - that plugs into the practice's existing software. It maintains private, real-time integrations into 25+ Australian practice management systems (Best Practice / Bp Premier, MedicalDirector Pracsoft, Zedmed, Cliniko, Genie, Gentu, Medtech, Nookal, PracSuite, Dental4Windows, and others) so appointment availability and bookings sync directly with the front desk. Home market is Australia. HealthEngine does NOT publish a public developer portal, REST OpenAPI, or HL7 FHIR endpoint - its API surface is a set of gated, partner-only PMS integrations rather than a self-serve developer program, so this profile is an honest identity stub with no public machine-readable contract to harvest.

providers.name: HUNGRY
providers.description: HUNGRY (Hungry Marketplace, Inc.) is an Arlington, Virginia workplace food platform that connects corporate clients to a curated network of independent chefs and local restaurants. Founded in 2016 by Jeff Grass, Eman Pahlavani and Shy Pahlevani, it operates four product lines — office catering, Group Order individual meal pre-ordering, live events and chef pop-ups, and snacks and pantry — plus HUNGRY Last Mile, its own delivery and logistics arm. The platform runs its own admin, chef/food-partner dashboard, client admin dashboard, ops captain app and consumer ordering marketplace across 24 US cities and, following the February 2026 merger with Toronto-based hungerhub, more than ten Canadian markets. Earlier acquisitions include NatureBox and Garten. HUNGRY publishes no public developer program: the backing API at api.tryhungry.com is a private first-party service for its own web and mobile clients, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI, SDK or partner API reference is published anywhere on its public surface. The company does publish a dated, public engineering release-notes site, which is the only machine-adjacent technical artifact it makes available.

providers.name: Illumix
providers.description: Illumix is an enterprise-grade spatial AI company spun out of Stanford's Computer Science Department, providing a core stack for real-world location intelligence that runs at the edge with centimeter-level precision. Its hardware-agnostic platform delivers sub-second localization and 3D mapping across mobile devices, AR/VR wearables, and robotics using standard cameras — with no LiDAR or GPS dependency — combining multimodal vision-language AI with long-term memory that learns behavior over time. Illumix serves AI/XR wearables, enterprise and logistics, defense and security, location-based entertainment, and robotics, with deployments referenced for Disney, Six Flags, Cedar Fair, MGM Resorts, Warner Bros, Verizon, and Sony. The company markets developer APIs and an SDK as part of a full-stack offering, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Intenseye
providers.description: Intenseye is an AI-powered workplace safety platform that applies computer vision to a facility's existing CCTV cameras to detect unsafe conditions and behaviors in real time and prevent Serious Injuries and Fatalities (SIF). Its Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) product surfaces hazards, compliance gaps, and operational risks across manufacturing, logistics, food & beverage, and other high-risk industries, and can trigger Hard Stop emergency alerts. Intenseye offers cloud, private cloud, and on-premise deployment, is SOC 2 / AICPA certified and GDPR-aligned, uses AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS in transit, and does not use facial recognition. Backed by Insight Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Point Nine. Intenseye publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal; product access is through its dashboard and login. It maintains a public GitHub organization of mostly open-source forks and workshops rather than first-party client libraries.

providers.name: Joby Aviation
providers.description: Joby Aviation is a California-based aerospace company developing an all-electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft intended to operate as part of a fast, quiet, and convenient air taxi service. Joby's piloted four-passenger S4 aircraft is designed for a top speed of 200 mph and zero operating emissions, and the company is pursuing FAA Type Certification under Part 23. Joby has strategic relationships with Toyota for manufacturing, Delta Air Lines, Virgin Atlantic and ANA for distribution, Uber for ground integration, the U.S. Department of Defense (Agility Prime), and operates a vertically integrated program covering aircraft, batteries (JoeBen cell technology via Joby's battery group), software, and pilot training. Joby acquired Uber Elevate and is co-located with manufacturing facilities in Marina and Santa Cruz, California, with plans for early commercial passenger service in Dubai and U.S. cities.

providers.name: JSON Processing
providers.description: JSON Processing (JSON-P) is a Java API for parsing, generating, transforming, and querying JSON messages. Standardized as Jakarta JSON Processing, it provides both an object model API and a streaming API for working with JSON data in Java applications. The current stable release is Jakarta JSON Processing 2.1 (Jakarta EE 10), with version 2.2 under development for Jakarta EE 12.

providers.name: JSR-303
providers.description: JSR-303 (Bean Validation) is a Java specification that defines a metadata model and API for JavaBean validation. It provides a standard way to define validation constraints on Java objects using annotations, enabling developers to enforce business rules and data integrity at the object level. Now standardized as Jakarta Validation, with version 3.1 released for Jakarta EE 11 and version 4.0 under development for Jakarta EE 12.

providers.name: Karmada
providers.description: Karmada is a CNCF incubating Kubernetes management system that enables running applications across multiple Kubernetes clusters and clouds. It provides a unified control plane for multi-cluster scheduling, failover, and traffic management. Karmada uses Kubernetes-native APIs and supports propagation policies, override policies, and federated resource management.

providers.name: Kubectl
providers.description: kubectl is the official command-line tool for Kubernetes, used to deploy applications, inspect resources, and manage clusters via the Kubernetes API.

providers.name: KubeEdge
providers.description: KubeEdge is a CNCF graduated project that extends Kubernetes to edge computing. It provides infrastructure support for networking, application deployment, and metadata synchronization between cloud and edge. KubeEdge enables containerized application orchestration at the edge with offline autonomy, ensuring edge nodes continue functioning when disconnected from the cloud.

providers.name: KubeVela
providers.description: KubeVela is a CNCF incubating application delivery and management platform that makes deploying and operating applications across hybrid and multi-cloud environments easier. Built on the Open Application Model (OAM), it provides a higher-level abstraction for defining applications with components, traits, and policies. KubeVela supports workflow-based delivery pipelines and multi-cluster deployment.

providers.name: Launching Next
providers.description: Launching Next is a startup discovery and submission platform that publishes daily listings of new and trending tech startups and side projects worldwide. Founded as a long-running startup directory, the platform has featured over 45,000 startups and side projects, making it a go-to resource for founders, investors, and early adopters looking to discover what is being built next. Entrepreneurs can submit their startups for free, with an optional paid fast-track review.

providers.name: LIFT Aircraft
providers.description: LIFT Aircraft is an Austin, Texas experiential aviation company founded by former Boeing engineer Matt Chasen, built around HEXA — an amphibious electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft with eighteen independent electric motors and propellers, a 432lb carbon fibre airframe, a triply redundant autopilot flown with a single three-axis joystick, an autonomous ballistic parachute, and enough redundancy to fly and land safely with up to six motors disabled. Because HEXA is compliant with the FAA's powered ultralight classification, no pilot's licence is required, and LIFT sells flight as a paid experience rather than selling aircraft — a short training session followed by a solo flight from waterfront bases in Austin and other US cities. The company has raised over $25 million from venture capital, accredited investors and US government grants, has worked with the US Air Force Agility Prime programme and the US Army, and has begun the FAA type certification process for a commercial edition. LIFT publishes no developer REST API or OpenAPI; its only machine-readable surface is a live, unauthenticated Model Context Protocol endpoint and an llms.txt served by its Wix-hosted site.

providers.name: Liftopia
providers.description: Liftopia is a consumer marketplace for advance-purchase ski and snowboard lift tickets, letting travelers browse and buy discounted day tickets and multi-day passes at hundreds of ski areas across the United States, Canada, Europe, South America, Japan, Australia and New Zealand. The site is organized by region, state and destination with dated availability and 1-8 day ticket search, and carries an affiliate program for partners. Liftopia's engineering organization operates on GitHub as Catalate Commerce, Inc., and the site footer points to Spotlio. As of this profile Liftopia publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition or client SDKs.

providers.name: LinuxBoot
providers.description: LinuxBoot is a Linux Foundation firmware project that uses a Linux kernel and initramfs as a bootloader, replacing specific firmware functionality such as UEFI DXE. It provides faster, more reliable, and more secure boot processes by leveraging the well-tested Linux kernel for hardware initialization. Core components include u-root (the ramfs builder), the LinuxBoot build system, and the NERF (Non-Extensible Reduced Firmware) heritage from Google.

providers.name: Meditopia
providers.description: Meditopia is a holistic mental-wellbeing platform founded in 2017 that blends psychology, technology, and wellness to support the mental, emotional, and physical health of individuals and organizations. For consumers it ships a meditation and mindfulness mobile app (sleep programs, guided meditations, personalized assessments, self-guided content) available in nine-plus languages and used by 40+ million people across 60 countries. For organizations it offers Meditopia for Work: a modern Employee Assistance Program (EAP), 1-on-1 expert sessions, a WellnessPass benefits platform, online trainings, and Soul, an AI wellbeing coach. Meditopia is backed by Creandum. The company operates a consumer mobile app and a B2B web platform; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Melonn
providers.description: Melonn is a third-party logistics (3PL) and multichannel fulfillment operator for e-commerce businesses across Colombia and Mexico. Through its proprietary Órbita platform it centralizes inventory, processes and packs orders, manages returns, and offers same/next-day delivery, unifying multiple sales channels into a single operation. Melonn connects to platforms such as Shopify, VTEX, WooCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop, MercadoLibre, Amazon, Walmart, Rappi, TikTok Shop, Liverpool, and Coppel, and exposes a REST API with real-time webhooks so any external platform can drive order management, inventory queries, shipment tracking, and returns. Melonn was surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors. Public developer documentation and a sandbox are provided on request via the Melonn advisory/contact form rather than an open developer portal.

providers.name: Metal3
providers.description: Metal3 (Metal Kubed) is a CNCF incubating project that provides bare metal host provisioning for Kubernetes. It leverages Ironic for hardware management and integrates with the Cluster API to enable Kubernetes-native lifecycle management of bare metal infrastructure. Metal3 automates server discovery, inspection, provisioning, and deprovisioning using Kubernetes custom resources.

providers.name: Nevis Wealth
providers.description: Nevis (Nevis Wealth) is an AI platform built for wealth management firms, giving financial advisors an AI assistant that automates administrative work — AI-generated meeting summaries, automatic task capture from client interactions, intelligent meeting-prep briefs, unified AI search across advisory systems, personalized client email drafting, and account-opening automation — so advisors spend more time with clients and less on paperwork. The company is used by advisory firms including United Capital, GC Wealth, Apollon Wealth, and Dodds Wealth, is SOC 2 Type I certified, and has raised $40M in venture funding. Nevis does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Nexthop AI
providers.description: Nexthop AI is a networking infrastructure company building next-generation, highly efficient AI and cloud networking for hyperscalers and neo-cloud operators. Founded by former Arista Networks operations leader Anshul Sadana, it designs scale-out and scale-across Ethernet switches, a networking software portfolio, and optics and cables engineered to lower the cost per token of large GPU clusters by improving power efficiency, cost, reliability, and speed of deployment. The company raised a $500M Series B led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Andreessen Horowitz at a $4.2B valuation and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio lead. It publishes no public web/REST API surface; this profile captures company identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Nfinite
providers.description: Nfinite (formerly Hubstairs) is a visual intelligence platform for the digital shelf. It helps consumer brands and retailers automatically analyze, generate, and monitor compliant product visuals — detecting visual compliance gaps across every retailer and brand and fixing them at scale using AI-generated 3D and synthetic product imagery. The product is delivered as a web application (my.nfinite.app) rather than a public developer API; no OpenAPI, developer portal, or published documentation exists at the time of enrichment. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Open Podcast API
providers.description: The Open Podcast API is an initiative aiming to provide a feature-complete synchronization API specification for podcast (web) apps and user-focused servers. The specification covers synchronization of subscriptions, listening progress, favorites, queues, and device state across compliant clients and self-hosted servers, with the goal of giving listeners portable control of their podcast data.

providers.name: OpenYurt
providers.description: OpenYurt is a CNCF incubating project that extends Kubernetes for edge and cloud-edge collaboration scenarios. It provides node autonomy for edge nodes to continue operating during cloud-edge network disconnections, seamless node conversion between cloud and edge modes, and unified management of edge resources through NodePool and YurtAppSet abstractions.

providers.name: Ophelia Health
providers.description: Ophelia is a telehealth company providing private, evidence-based medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorder from home. Founded in 2019 by Zack Gray and Mattan Griffel and headquartered in New York City, Ophelia connects patients with licensed clinicians for video visits, prescribes Suboxone (buprenorphine + naloxone) sent to a local pharmacy, and provides ongoing care-team support seven days a week. The subscription service accepts most major insurance plans, including Medicaid, and is licensed to provide care across 49 states and Washington, D.C. Ophelia is a direct-to-consumer clinical service and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner API program; this profile captures its public web presence and domain security posture.

providers.name: Pear Suite
providers.description: Pear Suite is a care management platform built for community health workers, care navigators, doulas, and community-based organizations, describing itself as an operating system for community-based work. The platform provides custom assessments and care pathways, goal and outcome tracking, patient communication over phone, SMS, and encrypted email, client and population-level analytics, and billing and claims integration, connecting community health initiatives with health plans and health systems. Pear Suite reports serving 2,500+ community workers across 300+ organizations nationwide.

providers.name: plancraft
providers.description: plancraft is a German cloud-based business management software for craftspeople and trades businesses (Handwerk). It digitizes administrative workflows end to end — quote and estimate creation, project planning, time tracking, on-site documentation, material and labor costing, and invoicing — inside one integrated platform aimed at small and mid-sized construction and trade companies. plancraft supports DATEV export for tax/accounting workflows and DATANORM and GAEB catalog imports for material data and tender processing. It is a venture-backed SaaS company (portfolio company of Creandum). As of this enrichment pass plancraft publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface — integrations are delivered as prebuilt connectors and standardized file-format import/export.

providers.name: ProfitWell
providers.description: ProfitWell (now ProfitWell Metrics by Paddle, following Paddle's 2022 acquisition of ProfitWell) is a free subscription analytics product that delivers accurate, real-time SaaS metrics such as MRR, churn, ARPU, LTV, retention, and cohort analysis by connecting directly to billing systems like Stripe, Braintree, Chargebee, Recurly, and Paddle. The ProfitWell API at https://api.profitwell.com/v2 provides programmatic access to subscription lifecycle events, customer data, financial metrics, and engagement data, authenticated via a bare API key passed in the Authorization header (no Bearer prefix).

providers.name: PSD Citywide
providers.description: PSD Citywide is a SaaS provider of enterprise asset management (EAM) and public-sector software for North American municipalities and government organizations. Its integrated Citywide platform spans asset management, maintenance and work-order management, GIS integration (ESRI-powered mapping), permitting, planning and licensing with citizen portals, multi-year budgeting and forecasting, facility/space management (Spaces), and a field mobile app, alongside asset-management advisory and grant services. The homepage references a "robust API" for integration and customization, but no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or GitHub organization were found during enrichment; end-user product documentation is published in a HappyFox-powered help center. Added to the API Evangelist network via the norwest-venture-partners portfolio.

providers.name: QuEra Computing
providers.description: QuEra Computing is a Boston-area neutral-atom quantum computing company, founded in 2021 by scientists from Harvard and MIT. Its flagship system, Aquila, is a 256-qubit field-programmable analog neutral-atom quantum processor that has been publicly available since November 2022 through Amazon Braket and through a direct Premium Access channel. QuEra develops Bloqade, an open-source software stack for neutral-atom quantum computing delivered as a Python SDK (Bloqade Python) and as the original Bloqade.jl Julia package, along with surrounding tooling for circuits, analog control, atom shuttling, decoders, and tensor-network simulation. The company is building toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with its Gemini-class next-generation systems and has demonstrated logical-level magic state distillation on neutral-atom hardware. QuEra works with HPC centers, national labs (NERSC, Los Alamos), DARPA, NEDO/AIST, NVIDIA, AWS, BCG X, Deloitte, Classiq, Kipu Quantum, Wolfram Research, and enterprise customers including BP, BASF, Merck, and Amgen. The system is consumed via the Bloqade SDK or AWS Braket; QuEra does not currently expose a public REST API to its QPU.

providers.name: Red Points
providers.description: Red Points operates an AI-powered brand protection and anti-counterfeiting platform used by businesses to detect and remove counterfeits, unauthorized sellers, fake websites, social media impersonation, and digital piracy across more than 5,000 marketplaces, social networks, and app stores. Its software combines automated detection with enforcement and takedown workflows, domain monitoring, gray-market and unauthorized-seller blocking, ad-fraud detection, and revenue-recovery and litigation services. Red Points was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network; it does not expose a public developer API or documented API surface as of this enrichment pass, so this profile captures the company's public web, legal, security, and llms.txt footprint rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: ReDEF
providers.description: REDEF is a media curation and newsletter company founded and led by Jason Hirschhorn (CEO + Chief Curator) that "DJs the internet" — surfacing daily remixes of the stories, people, and ideas that matter across Media, Fashion, Music, Sports, and Tech. Readers follow curated Mixes, Sets, Originals, Charts, and email Newsletters ("interest remixes for curious minds"), and can build and share their own mixes. ReDEF was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a public consumer content website (redef.com) but no public developer program, API, documentation, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: Rent-A-Center
providers.description: Rent-A-Center is a lease-to-own retail company providing furniture, electronics, appliances, and computers through its Rent-A-Center stores and Acima (formerly AcceptanceNOW) in-store kiosk program. Headquartered in Plano, Texas, Rent-A-Center operates thousands of stores across the United States, Mexico, and Puerto Rico. The company's technology platform supports online store management, customer account self-service, lease agreement processing, and the Preferred Lease virtual store integration program for retail partners. No public developer API is currently documented. The Acima platform provides a lease-to-own integration capability for partner retailers via a separate developer program.

providers.name: Retrocausal
providers.description: Retrocausal builds AI-powered copilot software for manufacturing operations, applying patented computer vision and machine learning to manual assembly lines. Its products include Assembly Copilot (real-time AI-tracked work instructions, poka-yoke error prevention, and cycle-level video traceability), Kaizen Copilot (AI-powered time studies, standard work, automatic line balancing, and ergonomic analysis for industrial engineers), and Ergo Copilot (ergonomic risk assessment from smartphone video). The platform runs on AWS, is ISO 27001 certified, and integrates with MES systems, OPC UA for PLCs and smart tools, barcode scanners, torque wrenches, light towers, and projectors, with SSO via Azure Active Directory and Okta. Retrocausal is a Techstars portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API; integrations are delivered as custom MES/OPC UA and identity connections rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Roger
providers.description: Roger (operated by Sanos Services GmbH, Berlin, Germany) is a B2B SaaS practice-management platform for dental clinics. It layers automation and AI onto existing German dental practice-management systems (PVS) such as CGM Z1, Charly, Dampsoft, Evident and Dento Office, adding patient recall, digital intake forms, WhatsApp/SMS communication, AI-assisted documentation with billing-position capture, digital treatment-plan signing, factoring with default protection and instant payout, and outsourced ZMV/reception staffing. The product is DSGVO/GDPR-compliant and hosted in Germany. As surfaced in the API Evangelist network via VC-portfolio discovery, Roger publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: SellerX
providers.description: SellerX is a Berlin-based consumer-brand builder, founded in 2020, that acquires, operates and scales everyday consumer products into omnichannel global brands. Originally one of Europe's largest Amazon FBA aggregators, it merged with KW Commerce in 2021 and with the US aggregator Elevate Brands in 2023, and has since repositioned itself from an aggregator into a brand builder. The group operates 20+ brands and 25k+ products across 10+ countries from hubs in Berlin, London, Manila and Dongguan, and has raised more than $750M in equity and debt from Sofina, L Catterton, Cherry Ventures, Felix Capital, 83North, an ADIA subsidiary, BlackRock and Victory Park Capital. SellerX sells consumer goods to consumers through marketplaces and its own channels; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification of its own.

providers.name: Spill
providers.description: Spill is a UK-based employee assistance programme (EAP) that delivers mental health support to employees directly inside the tools teams already use, such as Slack and Microsoft Teams. The platform offers same-day, message-based counselling, structured multi-session therapy courses for specific mental health conditions, drop-in group sessions, manager mental-health training, and self-guided wellbeing content, all through a single subscription. Spill serves over 600 companies on month-to-month terms and is backed by Seedcamp. It is a B2B software-as-a-service wellbeing product rather than an API provider; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been published.

providers.name: Sword
providers.description: Sword Health is a digital health company delivering AI-powered virtual care for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain, pelvic health, and injury prevention. Founded in 2015 in Portugal by Virgilio Bento, Sword pairs licensed physical therapists with motion-sensor and computer-vision technology so members can complete clinically supervised physical therapy from home. Its platform spans an enrollment platform, a treatment platform, a mobile application backed by a mobile API, a file-exchange platform for enterprise clients, and an AI care system. Sword serves 1,000+ enterprise and health-plan clients across three continents, is backed by investors including General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund, and Transformation Capital, and maintains SOC 2 Type 2, HITRUST, ISO 13485, HIPAA, GDPR, and Cyber Essentials compliance. Sword does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its identity, status, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: TE Connectivity
providers.description: TE Connectivity is a global manufacturer of connectors and sensors headquartered in Galway, Ireland with operational headquarters in Berwyn, Pennsylvania. TE provides electrical connectivity and sensor solutions for transportation, industrial, and communications markets, with strong automotive Tier 1 supply relationships.

providers.name: Teespring
providers.description: Teespring is a creator-commerce and print-on-demand platform, founded in 2011, that lets creators design, launch, and sell custom apparel and merchandise with no upfront cost or inventory, handling production, payment, and fulfillment on the creator's behalf. Backed by a16z, the company rebranded to "Spring" in 2021 and now operates as Amaze Commerce (part of Amaze Holdings): its consumer storefront lives at spri.ng while the creator/merchant SaaS platform runs at amazecommerce.com and amaze.co. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, /.well-known discovery surface, or llms.txt; this profile therefore captures verified company identity and published site properties only.

providers.name: Terapify
providers.description: Terapify is an online therapy platform for the Spanish-speaking market, connecting individuals in Mexico and Latin America with certified psychologists for private, secure video-call sessions. Founded in 2019 and backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator, the platform matches patients to therapists via a therapeutic-affinity test, offers individual and couples therapy, parent orientation, and workplace mental-health programs for companies, plus mindfulness, yoga, and breathing resources. It operates as a consumer web and mobile (iOS/Android) product and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Threat Stack
providers.description: Threat Stack was a Boston-based cloud security company providing full-stack cloud security observability, intrusion detection, and compliance monitoring for infrastructure and applications across cloud-native workloads including virtual machines, containers, and Kubernetes. Its platform combined rules and supervised machine learning to detect threats, vulnerabilities, and attacks in real time. Threat Stack exposed a RESTful V2 API (HAWK/HMAC authenticated) and trigger-based webhook alerts, along with first-party SDKs, a Go CLI, and configuration-management modules (Chef, Ansible, Puppet, Terraform, CloudFormation, Helm). The company was acquired by F5 in 2021 and the product is now F5 Distributed Cloud App Infrastructure Protection (AIP); the original threatstack.com and api.threatstack.com domains have been decommissioned.

providers.name: Tripitaca, Inc.
providers.description: Tripitaca is a Kenya-based travel and hospitality booking marketplace where travelers get the best deals when they travel and where property owners list their properties. The platform lets travelers receive offers from hosts and hotels, while hosts create curated packages and special offers, see travelers interested in their area, and make them offers. Coverage spans destinations including Nairobi, Mombasa, Nakuru, Kisumu, and Maasai Mara safari experiences. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Uplevel
providers.description: Uplevel is an engineering intelligence platform for enterprises — an operating system for engineering transformation that helps leaders see team performance clearly, solve root causes, and sustain improvement in the AI era. The platform pulls data from existing tools and uses machine learning to produce engineering metrics and actionable insights: DORA metrics, time allocation and ML issue classification, deep-work and interruption measurement, developer-experience metrics, and AI-impact analysis, framed by the company's WAVE framework of engineering KPIs. Founded in 2018 and led by CEO Joe Levy, Uplevel is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Madrona Ventures, and Voyager Capital. Uplevel serves enterprise customers such as Xactly, Accolade, Braze, Avalara, and Qualtrics; it operates an internal API behind the product (api.uplevelteam.com, AWS API Gateway) but publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: WalkerCo
providers.description: Walker & Company Brands (WalkerCo) is a health and beauty company founded by Tristan Walker that designs grooming and personal-care products for people of color. Its flagship brand, Bevel, sells shaving systems, razors, skin, hair, and beard-care products direct-to-consumer, and the company also operates the FORM hair-care line. Walker & Company was acquired by Procter & Gamble in 2018 and its storefronts run on Shopify. The company does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its programmatic surface is limited to the Shopify-provided Customer Account OAuth/OIDC endpoints on the Bevel storefront and an internal-tooling GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Xamarin
providers.description: Xamarin was the San Francisco company behind the Mono-based cross-platform mobile development framework, letting developers build native iOS, Android, and Mac apps from a single C#/.NET codebase. Backed by investors including Insight Partners, it was acquired by Microsoft in 2016. Microsoft retired the Xamarin SDKs on May 1, 2024, with Xamarin.Forms succeeded by .NET MAUI. Xamarin shipped developer tooling and SDK packages rather than a public web API; its NuGet packages, docs, and GitHub organization remain its primary artifacts.

providers.name: Zarna
providers.description: Zarna builds autonomous AI associates for private capital firms — private equity, growth equity, private credit, family offices, and investment banks. The platform captures deal information from CIMs, emails, meetings, CRMs, and virtual data rooms into a structured institutional memory, then runs a swarm of specialized agents (Scribe for capture and logging, Memo for screening memos and briefs, Analyst for mandate-fit scoring, and Experts for warm-intro network mapping) that deliver finished work directly into Outlook, Teams, and Slack. Zarna integrates with 30+ deal tools including DealCloud, Affinity, Salesforce, and SharePoint, deploys into VPC or on-premises single-tenant infrastructure, and is SOC 2 Type II certified. A Y Combinator Fall 2025 company founded by an ex-AEA Investors team.

providers.name: Zervant
providers.description: Zervant is an online invoicing and billing platform for freelancers, sole traders, and small businesses. It lets users create, send, and manage estimates and invoices online, automate recurring invoices and payment reminders, track time and expenses, and get paid online across free and paid subscription tiers. Founded in Espoo, Finland and now part of the Ageras group, Zervant is a Northzone portfolio company. No public developer API is currently documented — this profile captures the company identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Zilch
providers.description: Zilch is a London-headquartered "buy now, pay later" and ad-subsidised payments network founded in 2018, and one of the United Kingdom's most prominent BNPL brands. Rather than integrating at each retailer's checkout, Zilch is deliberately merchant-agnostic: consumers apply in the Zilch mobile app, receive a virtual (and physical) Mastercard, and can Pay-in-3, pay over six weeks, or Pay-now-and-earn-cashback anywhere Mastercard is accepted, online or in-store, through Apple Pay and Google Pay wallets. Because Zilch reaches merchants over the open Mastercard card rails and relies on partners such as Mastercard for card issuing and Checkout.com as its payments processor, it does not operate a public merchant-integration or developer platform the way a PSP or open-banking provider does. As of this review Zilch publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification; its public surface is a consumer marketing site, a help centre, and a customer sign-up/login app. This profile therefore records Zilch's verified public web properties honestly and carries no API entries, because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: Accrual
providers.description: Accrual is an augmented accounting intelligence platform for accounting firms and growing service businesses, offering what it calls the complete accounting workspace spanning engagement management, document intake, data processing, tax return generation, assurance workflows, and client collaboration. Backed by General Catalyst, the company emphasizes secure, US-hosted infrastructure with AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS in transit, data isolation, and SOC 2 Type II attestation, and states that customer data is not used to train AI models. Accrual does not publish a public API or developer program at this time; this profile captures the company identity and its published security posture.

providers.name: Actualyze AI
providers.description: Actualyze AI is an enterprise AI governance and management company building tools that give organizations the visibility and control they need to adopt AI at scale without slowing their teams down. Founded by Rafi Khardalian (CEO) and Sean Lynch (CTO) — veterans of building and operating distributed systems at global scale — the company designs for regulated industries from day one, embedding compliance, defense-in-depth data protection, comprehensive audit logging, and continuous monitoring into the platform rather than bolting it on. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Backlotcars
providers.description: BacklotCars, Inc. is a dealer-to-dealer wholesale used-vehicle marketplace, founded in Kansas City and acquired by KAR Global (now OPENLANE, Inc.), whose technology was consolidated into the OPENLANE US marketplace. It connects thousands of franchise and independent dealers through a 24/7 bid-ask marketplace, "Buy It Now" listings, and timed auctions scheduled throughout each week, backed by native mobile apps, in-lane vehicle inspections with AI-analyzed engine recordings, transportation, and floor-plan financing. Commercial sellers and dealer groups can push inventory straight from their own systems into OPENLANE Sell via OPENLANE Connect, a lightweight dealer integration API with a dedicated test environment. This profile began as a 500 Global portfolio lead surfaced into the API Evangelist network and was enriched from OPENLANE's public marketing and product surface; the platform publishes no public OpenAPI or open developer portal.

providers.name: Bloom Institute of Technology
providers.description: Bloom Institute of Technology (formerly Lambda School) is an online coding bootcamp founded in 2017 that trains learners for AI-driven tech careers through part-time and full-time programs in Full Stack Web Development, Backend Development, and Data Science, plus corporate "AI for Developer Productivity" training. It is known for its income-share and deferred-tuition model ($0 upfront with a job-contingent payment plan) and a tuition-refund guarantee. The company reports 4,000+ graduates since 2017. It is a venture-backed consumer education company (backed by GV) and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: BWX Technologies
providers.description: BWX Technologies is a manufacturer of nuclear components and provider of nuclear services to the U.S. government and commercial customers worldwide. The company delivers innovative nuclear solutions across naval propulsion, small modular reactors, nuclear fuel, medical isotopes, and complex site operations.

providers.name: CADDi
providers.description: CADDi is a Tokyo-headquartered manufacturing-technology company that builds an AI Data Platform for industrial manufacturers. Its two products, CADDi Drawer and CADDi Quote, aggregate scattered 2D engineering drawings and supply-chain data into a single searchable asset, offering keyword and drawing-similarity search, automatic extraction of dimensions, text and shapes, and AI-assisted quotation and sourcing. The platform serves procurement, engineering, sales, production, quality, and leadership teams across automotive, robotics, and precision-machinery sectors, and connects to ERP, CAM, CAD, and quality systems via batch and CSV imports. CADDi was surfaced as a portfolio company of Atomico and DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK.

providers.name: Clanbeat
providers.description: Clanbeat is an Estonian education-technology company whose app supports student and staff well-being by nurturing social and emotional learning (SEL) through co-creation. The platform provides well-being tracking, quality reflections, meaningful connections between students and educators, and tools to co-create SEL curriculum. It is used by international schools, educators, students, and fitness and lifelong-learning communities to evidence group emotional well-being and bring classes closer together. Clanbeat is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application at app.clanbeat.com; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or partner integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Cogent
providers.description: Cogent Security is an AI-driven vulnerability management platform whose AI agents discover, assess, remediate, and report on software vulnerabilities at machine speed, before attackers can exploit them. The platform spans the CTEM (Continuous Threat Exposure Management) lifecycle: Discover identifies vulnerable software quickly after disclosures, Assess risk-scores and prioritizes remediation, Remediate applies automated and assisted fixes, and Report produces evidence-backed documentation of risk reduction. It is powered by the Cogent AI Engine and Cogent Research with published safety guardrails and defined autonomy levels. Cogent is a venture-backed security company (Bain Capital Ventures, Greylock). Cogent publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time; this profile captures its public web, security, and trust surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Conicle
providers.description: Conicle is a Thai education-technology company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Bangkok that offers an all-in-one corporate learning platform (ConicleX) letting organizations build, assign, and track online courses, in-house training, and skill-development pathways for their employees. The cloud-based learning management system serves more than 50 leading enterprises — including Honda, Coca-Cola, Unilever, McDonald's, Sansiri, and The Mall — and over one million learners across the banking, retail, healthcare, energy, insurance, and consumer-product sectors. Conicle has raised Series A funding led by InVent (the corporate venture arm of Intouch Holdings), with backing from 500 Global and Stormbreaker Ventures. Conicle publishes a shared design-system web-components library used across its properties but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Contractor Foreman
providers.description: Contractor Foreman is all-in-one construction management software for contractors - estimates, invoicing, scheduling, time cards, daily logs, change orders, and job costing - used by contractors in more than 75 countries. There is no self-serve public developer API or public API reference; the company's dedicated API subdomain (api.contractorforeman.net) displays only a "Coming soon" placeholder as of this review. The one confirmed API capability is a private, account-scoped API key (generated under Settings > Integration > Zapier) that powers Contractor Foreman's official Zapier app, exposing Customer and Lead create/archive/delete triggers and actions plus a File Uploaded trigger. That key and its underlying endpoints are not documented or published for direct third-party use outside the Zapier integration; broader third-party connectivity otherwise runs through native integrations (QuickBooks, Gusto, Google Calendar/Outlook, Stripe, Angi Leads, CompanyCam, MS Project, SweetPay) and Zapier/webhook automation rather than an open API.

providers.name: CounterTack
providers.description: CounterTack, Inc. was a Waltham, Massachusetts endpoint detection and response (EDR) vendor whose Sentinel and Endpoint Threat Platform products applied behavioral analysis, memory forensics and machine learning to detect zero-days, rootkits and advanced persistent threats. In June 2018 CounterTack acquired its channel partner GoSecure, a managed detection and response (MDR) provider, and in March 2019 rebranded the combined company as "GoSecure powered by CounterTack"; the CounterTack name has since been retired in favour of GoSecure, which today markets a managed extended detection and response (MXDR) service and the GoSecure Titan platform covering EDR, IDR, NGAV, SIEM and professional services. The CounterTack surface is therefore historical: countertack.com still resolves to GoSecure infrastructure but serves no valid certificate, and the living platform is customer-only behind a Keycloak single sign-on at titan.gosecure.net.

providers.name: Defense Information System for Security
providers.description: The Defense Information System for Security (DISS) is the enterprise-wide Department of Defense system of record for personnel security, suitability, and credentialing management for military, civilian, and contractor personnel. Operated by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), DISS replaced the Joint Personnel Adjudication System (JPAS) as the system of record on March 31, 2021. DISS is restricted to authorized DoD and federal users and contractor security officers; it does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board
providers.description: The Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board (DNFSB) is an independent organization within the executive branch of the United States Government chartered to provide recommendations and advice to the President and the Secretary of Energy on public health and safety issues at Department of Energy defense nuclear facilities. The DNFSB publishes recommendations, letters, technical reports, weekly site-representative reports, and rulemaking notices through its public website and FOIA reading room. The agency does not publish a developer-oriented API; programmatic users rely on document downloads, RSS feeds, and Federal Register integrations.

providers.name: Dock
providers.description: Dock is a Latin American financial technology infrastructure provider — formerly Conductor Technology — that delivers card issuing and processing, core banking, digital accounts and wallets, Pix instant payments, bank slips, acquiring, loyalty/benefits and transactional anti-fraud from a single cloud-native platform marketed as Dock One. Dock operates in Brazil as a payment institution regulated by the Banco Central do Brasil (bank code 301) and states that it serves more than 400 companies across 11 countries, processes roughly R$1.4 trillion in annual card volume and supports around 70 million active digital accounts. Its API estate is branded Caradhras and is reached through the api.caradhras.io gateway; the developer reference at developers.dock.tech is a private ReadMe hub that redirects anonymous visitors to a login, and the previously public Caradhras reference at lighthouse.dock.tech no longer resolves.

providers.name: Docquity
providers.description: Docquity is a Singapore-headquartered digital health company operating Asia's largest verified professional network for licensed healthcare practitioners, with more than 500,000 verified doctors across nine markets including Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore and Taiwan. Its flagship product, Dx, is an AI clinical thinking partner that bundles clinical search and decision support, accredited continuing medical education, peer community and case discussion, and patient-ready summary notes into an invite-only mobile and web platform gated behind medical-credential verification. For life-sciences and enterprise partners Docquity sells an Intelligence Suite comprising Pulse, which measures healthcare-professional conviction and engagement, and Dialog, which runs field engagement and activation programs against that audience. Docquity also operates Docquity Jobs, a medical recruitment board. The company publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification; its api.docquity.com backend and id.docquity.com identity service exist to serve its own first-party applications and are not offered to third-party developers.

providers.name: Duroflexworld
providers.description: Duroflex (duroflexworld.com) is one of India's most trusted sleep-solutions brands, selling mattresses, sofas, recliners, beds, pillows and mattress protectors direct-to-consumer with up to a 10-year warranty, free shipping and EMI options. The online store runs on Shopify and exposes real agent-facing commerce surfaces discovered by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline: a hosted Storefront MCP server at /api/mcp (catalog search, cart, product details, and shop policy/FAQ tools that conform to the UCP catalog capability) and a Shopify Customer Account API secured with OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect, advertising an agent-oriented customer-account-mcp-api scope. Surfaced originally as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio lead, the profile is now enriched with its MCP, well-known OIDC discovery, authentication, scopes and domain-security artifacts.

providers.name: EditorConfig
providers.description: EditorConfig helps maintain consistent coding styles for multiple developers working on the same project across various editors and IDEs. The EditorConfig project consists of a file format for defining coding styles and a collection of text editor plugins that enable editors to read the file format and adhere to defined styles. EditorConfig files are easily readable and work well with version control systems. The format uses an INI-style syntax compatible with the Python configparser library, with filepath glob patterns similar to gitignore.

providers.name: Ethos
providers.description: Ethos is a US digital life insurance company headquartered in San Francisco, founded in 2016, offering term life, whole life, and indexed universal life policies through an online, mostly no-medical-exam application flow. Ethos operates as a technology-driven insurance agency, distributing policies underwritten by carriers such as Ameritas, Banner Life (Legal & General America), Protective, and TruStage. Coverage is available in 49 states and Washington, D.C., with term policies offered for 10, 15, 20, 30, and 40 year durations and face amounts ranging from $15,000 to $3 million. The company has raised over $400 million from investors including Goldman Sachs, SoftBank, GV, Sequoia, and Accel, and is widely cited as one of the leading insurtech companies modernizing the life insurance buying experience. Ethos exposes a Partnership API that lets approved business partners embed quoting, identity validation, instant underwriting, application capture, billing, and signed policy issuance directly into their own products. The Partnership API uses bearer-token authentication tied to a partner API key and per-applicant session, and consolidates steps such as identity validation and quoting into combined endpoints to enable instant decisioning. There is no public, self-serve OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer signup; access requires a partnership agreement with Ethos. Ethos's only material open-source footprint is the ethos-design-system React component library on GitHub.

providers.name: EXIGER
providers.description: Exiger is an AI-native supply chain, third-party, and software supply chain risk and compliance company. Its 1Exiger platform unifies supplier, product, part, component, and risk data into a single system to help organizations map and orchestrate compliant, resilient physical and software supply chains. Product areas span supply chain visibility and optimization, trade and third-party risk and compliance, due diligence intelligence (DDIQ), and software supply chain security (SBOM analysis, from its Ion Channel acquisition). Exiger serves government and commercial customers and is FedRAMP authorized. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and enriched from Exiger's public corporate, trust, and legal surfaces; Exiger does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Fintor
providers.description: Fintor is an enterprise software company that provides an agentic AI workforce for mortgage lending operations. Its purpose-built, autonomous AI agents execute mortgage workflows end to end - from application through closing - with human-in-the-loop oversight, integrating with existing loan origination systems (LOS), CRMs, and contact centers rather than replacing them. Product modules include a Loan Officer Assistant (document intake, borrower communication, gap analysis), a Processor Assistant (third-party orders, condition tracking, disclosures), Predictive Conditioning, a Closing Agent, and a Manager Assistant for forecasting and reporting. Fintor ships pre-built connectors for Encompass, Salesforce, Five9, Polly, and Blend, exposes documented API integrations, and is SOC 2 Type II certified with encryption, RBAC, approval chains, and audit logging.

providers.name: FitOn
providers.description: FitOn is a consumer digital fitness and wellness platform offering free, on-demand workout classes (cardio, strength, yoga, Pilates, HIIT), guided meditation, personalized meal plans and nutrition tracking, recipes, and social challenges. FitOn serves 15 million+ members with celebrity and world-class trainers across mobile, web, and connected-TV apps (Apple TV, Roku, Chromecast, Fire TV). Its FitOn Health arm delivers an enterprise wellness benefit to employers, health plans, and brokers. FitOn is backed by Accel. As of this enrichment pass FitOn publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI; consumer and B2B integration is handled through partnership programs rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Fleetmatics
providers.description: Fleetmatics was a fleet management, telematics, and GPS vehicle tracking SaaS company whose Reveal platform tracked commercial vehicles, drivers, and mobile assets for small and mid-sized fleets. Founded in Dublin and later headquartered in Massachusetts, Fleetmatics IPO'd on the NYSE in 2012 and was acquired by Verizon in 2016 for about USD 2.4 billion, becoming the core of Verizon Connect. Its Reveal platform exposes a documented REST API and webhook suite - the Fleetmatics Integration Manager (FIM) / Reveal Integration Services APIs - covering vehicles, drivers, GPS positions and history, trips and segments, driver status and safety, hours-of-service logbooks, geofences (places), groups, and non-powered asset tracking. The API gateway still runs on Fleetmatics-branded hosts (fim.api.us.fleetmatics.com); access is gated to Reveal customers and approved integration partners who request Integration Manager and Reveal REST credentials before calling the documented endpoints. The Fleetmatics brand now redirects to Verizon Connect.

providers.name: GetHarley
providers.description: GetHarley is a UK-based telehealth and skincare platform delivering personalised, medical-grade skincare through online consultations. Patients answer questions about their skin concerns, book a video consultation, and are matched with one of a network of over 1,000 licensed dermatologists, aesthetic doctors, and plastic surgeons, who recommend a tailored regimen of medical-grade products delivered to the patient. GetHarley operates both a patient-facing storefront and a practitioner platform used by clinicians to manage recommendations, orders, and client relationships. Backed by Index Ventures, the company addresses concerns such as acne, fine lines, pigmentation, and ageing. As of this profile, GetHarley does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or an MCP server; this record captures its identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Grow Therapy
providers.description: Grow Therapy is a mental-health platform that connects individuals with licensed therapists and prescribers, offering virtual and in-person talk therapy plus medication management in one insurance-integrated experience. The company operates a two-sided marketplace: a client-facing product for finding, booking, and paying for care (with insurance verification and an average session cost around $21 for covered clients) and a provider portal that gives clinicians scheduling, billing, telehealth, and practice-management tooling. Grow also partners with employers, physicians, and payors on B2B mental-health access. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; Grow Therapy publishes a public Statuspage but does not expose a public developer API, so this profile captures its company identity, operational transparency, and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Grpcurl
providers.description: grpcurl is an open source command-line tool for interacting with gRPC servers, like curl for gRPC with support for service reflection and JSON encoding.

providers.name: Hithium
providers.description: HiTHIUM (Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese energy storage company founded in 2019 that designs and manufactures lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, modules and complete battery energy storage systems (BESS) for utility-scale, commercial and industrial, and residential applications. The product line runs from large-format prismatic ESS cells through liquid-cooled multi-megawatt-hour container systems to the HeroEE residential and portable range marketed at hero-ee.com. Company material reports roughly 8,000 staff, more than 1,100 R&D engineers and over 3,900 patents. Product pages publish named certifications including UL 1973, UL 9540, UL 9540A, NFPA 855, IEC 62619, IEC 62477, IEC 63056, IEC 61000 and UN 38.3. HiTHIUM operates a Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) running an IEC 62443-aligned vulnerability management process, and publishes numbered cybersecurity bulletins with CVE references and remediation guidance at hithium.com/support/security.html. HiTHIUM publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or Postman contract, no SDKs, no CLI, no webhook catalog and no MCP or A2A agent surface; third-party integration happens over Modbus/CAN interfaces described in datasheets and manuals that sit behind the download-center account gate, and the HeroEE consumer app's backend is undocumented.

providers.name: Humanitru
providers.description: Humanitru is an integration-first CRM and fundraising platform built for nonprofits, museums, zoos, aquariums, botanic gardens, and food banks. Rather than forcing organizations into an all-in-one ecosystem, Humanitru consolidates donor, membership, ticketing, email marketing, accounting, and volunteer data from more than 40 partner tools into a single 360-degree view, then layers automated insights, reporting, and donor-engagement workflows on top. The company positions itself around data consolidation and retention, citing customer outcomes such as increased active donors and improved donor retention, and pairs the platform with one-on-one support staffed by former fundraisers and database managers. Humanitru (formerly operating as Totem Insights) is a Techstars portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation; all connectivity is delivered through its curated native integration catalog.

providers.name: IgniteTech
providers.description: IgniteTech is a global, AI-first enterprise software company (headquartered in Austin, Texas, and operating remote-first across 30+ countries) that acquires, revitalizes, and supports mission-critical enterprise software and embeds AI-powered capabilities across its portfolio — an operating model the company brands "AI-DNA." Its Native AI products include Eloquens AI (automated, context-aware email response), MyPersonas (AI digital clones of key employees that answer repetitive questions via a video chat-style interface), and Adminio AI (meeting scheduling through intelligent email orchestration). The IgniteTech Unlimited software library spans acquired enterprise brands such as GFI Software, Khoros (Communities and Care), Jive, DNN, Gensym, Computron, GRID (supply chain, via the Suuchi acquisition), Knova, AnswerHub, ACORN, TradeBeam, and SalesBuilder. Led by CEO Eric Vaughan, the company positions itself as an AI enterprise software company rather than only a software holding company.

providers.name: Liveboard
providers.description: LiveBoard is a tutor-management platform that helps tutoring businesses, academies, and independent tutors run their operations end to end. It combines branded virtual classrooms (video calls, screen sharing, an interactive whiteboard, recording, and file sharing) with session scheduling and attendance tracking, tutor/student/parent management, calendar-based billing with online payments, auto-invoicing, payroll, and progress reporting. Liveboard says it serves 200,000+ tutors and companies across 200+ countries, scaling from solo tutors to organizations with thousands of tutors. It is a consumer/SaaS product with no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface at this time; integrations are teaching-focused (Wacom pen tablets, a LaTeX formula editor, and the Desmos graphing calculator). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lootex
providers.description: Lootex is a Web3 infrastructure and AI application development company with eight years in the blockchain space, backed by 500 Global. It built a multi-chain NFT marketplace (Seaport protocol with aggregator support), the Lootex Studio minting tool, the Biru social platform, and Lootex Plus (an API and SDK offering to mint, trade, and integrate NFTs into apps and games). Its core marketplace infrastructure — a NestJS backend and Next.js frontend with blockchain event indexing and Web3 wallet authentication — is published as open source under Apache-2.0. Lootex is now sunsetting its consumer products (marketplace, Studio, and Biru wind down on 2026-04-04; assets stay in users' own non-custodial wallets) and pivoting to full-stack AI/Web3 development partnerships and open-source contributions.

providers.name: MaiCall
providers.description: MaiCall is an AI-powered debt collection platform for non-bank lenders, microfinance companies, and collection agencies. Its self-learning voice agents place outbound collection calls, negotiate payment plans, and follow up across WhatsApp, SMS, and email in 30+ languages and native accents, capturing promises to pay and tracking recovery, contact, and cost metrics in real time. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. MaiCall advertises custom API integrations to loan-management systems, CRMs, SIP trunks, and payment gateways on request, but publishes no self-serve public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition at this time.

providers.name: Melodics
providers.description: Melodics is a New Zealand-based interactive music-learning application that teaches drums, MIDI keyboards, and pad controllers (finger drumming) through gamified, real-time lessons. It connects to electronic instruments and MIDI controllers to give immediate feedback on timing and accuracy, offering guided learning paths, song tutorials, and structured daily practice for beginner through advanced players across desktop and mobile. Melodics is a consumer edtech product and a portfolio company of 500 Global; it publishes no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Misfits Market (fka Imperfect Foods)
providers.description: Misfits Market is an online grocery delivery service that rescues surplus and cosmetically imperfect produce, plus organic vegetables, dairy, meat, seafood, pantry staples, and wine, delivering sustainable groceries across the United States to help reduce food waste. It merged with Imperfect Foods in 2022, and both brands now operate under Misfits Market. The company has no public developer API program: its digital surface is a consumer e-commerce website, a customer help center, and iOS/Android mobile apps. It publishes a machine-readable llms.txt for AI agents.

providers.name: Neurelis
providers.description: Neurelis, Inc. is a privately held San Diego neuroscience and specialty pharmaceutical company founded in 2007 that licenses, develops and commercializes therapies for epilepsy, psychiatry and other central nervous system disorders with high unmet need. Its lead commercial product is VALTOCO (diazepam nasal spray), an FDA-approved acute treatment for intermittent, stereotypic episodes of frequent seizure activity (seizure clusters) in adult and pediatric patients two years of age and older, built on Intravail transmucosal absorption-enhancement technology acquired with Aegis Therapeutics. Neurelis also holds the ProTek and Hydrogel drug-delivery platforms, licenses Intravail to partners such as ARS Pharmaceuticals and Dr. Reddy's/Upsher-Smith, and is advancing the NRL-1049 and NRL-1004 pipeline programs. Neurelis publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract; its only agent-facing machine-readable surface is a set of llms.txt documents served on its corporate, product and patient-support properties.

providers.name: Newfront
providers.description: Newfront is a modern business insurance brokerage and technology company headquartered in San Francisco. It combines a traditional insurance brokerage (commercial business insurance, employee benefits, retirement services, and risk management) with a software platform that gives clients transparent data and analytics to understand and lower their total cost of risk. Formed from the merger of Newfront and ABD Insurance, the company serves technology, venture-backed, and enterprise clients across property and casualty, health and benefits, and personal lines. Backed by Index Ventures, Susa Ventures, and SV Angel. As of this enrichment pass Newfront exposes a client-facing web application (app.newfront.com) but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: OWASP
providers.description: The Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP) is a nonprofit foundation that works to improve the security of software through community-led open source projects, hundreds of chapters worldwide, and educational resources. OWASP does not provide a centralized public API, but maintains many open source projects, standards (such as the OWASP Top 10 and ASVS), and tools (such as ZAP) that include APIs.

providers.name: Pemo
providers.description: Pemo is a UAE-based fintech offering smart corporate cards and an all-in-one spend management platform for businesses across the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. The product combines physical and virtual corporate cards with expense management, automated receipt capture, invoice management, and accounting automation, giving finance teams real-time control and visibility over company spending. Pemo serves more than 10,000 companies and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. Pemo does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; this profile tracks the company's identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Phaidra
providers.description: Phaidra builds AI agents for autonomous data center and industrial operations, using reinforcement learning to control cooling, power, and workloads in mission-critical facilities. Its products include Phaidra Prism, an LLM for data center operations that helps technicians identify, prioritize, and resolve infrastructure issues, and Phaidra Factory, self-learning AI agents that continuously monitor and optimize thermal reliability, energy efficiency, and IT capacity to maximize tokens per watt across AI factories. Phaidra is an enterprise vendor with no public API or developer program; this profile captures its public security, compliance, and web posture. Backed by Index Ventures.

providers.name: Pindrop
providers.description: Pindrop is a voice and audio security company providing a continuous identity verification and deepfake-detection platform for enterprises. Its technology authenticates callers and video-meeting participants, detects synthetic (AI-generated) speech and fraudulent activity, and protects contact centers, virtual meetings, and connected devices. Pindrop's products span call-center fraud detection, passive voice authentication, and liveness/deepfake defense, and are delivered largely through partner platforms (Amazon Connect, Zoom, Webex, and others) rather than a public self-service developer API. The company is backed by Felicis, GV, and IVP and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Plans
providers.description: Plans (plans.app, formerly lun.energy) is a climate-technology company focused on decarbonising the built world. It removes the friction that stands in the way of transitioning homes to low-carbon energy faster, letting professionals capture building data on a mobile device, analyze it, and produce retrofit / energy plans — "capture, analyze, plan, all in your pocket." A web platform (platform.plans.app) and a Chrome extension support the workflow, and the product is offered across English, Danish, and French markets. Plans is backed by Partech. No public developer API has been identified during enrichment; the platform is a login-gated single-page application and the site exposes no OpenAPI, SDKs, docs, or developer portal.

providers.name: PLOS
