It is a consumer packaged goods company with no first-party developer API program; it was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead. This profile captures its real public web surface (storefront, security.txt, well-known documents, P&G legal and vulnerability-disclosure programs) rather than an API product.

providers.name: Wecasa
providers.description: Wecasa is a French on-demand home-services marketplace that connects households with vetted independent professionals who deliver the service at the customer's home. Its catalogue spans household cleaning and ironing, childcare and babysitting, mobile hairdressing, at-home beauty and nail care, massage and wellness, and personal fitness coaching. Customers book, schedule and pay through the Wecasa web site or the iOS/Android app; the professionals who fulfil the work run their business through the separate Wecasa Pro app. Founded in France and backed by Serena, the company operates in France, the United Kingdom, Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Wecasa publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract — the platform is a consumer application and a partner-onboarding funnel, not a developer product.

providers.name: Amperecloud
providers.description: Amperecloud (Amperecloud GmbH) is a German renewable-energy management software company whose cloud platform provides an operating system for monitoring, operating, and commercially managing solar, wind, and other renewable-energy assets at scale. The platform brings asset performance monitoring, maintenance and ticket management, commercial and technical asset management, and virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities into a single system, supported by migration, consulting, and custom-integration services. It is used by more than 300 customers worldwide managing over 8,000 installations and 10+ GWp of capacity. Added to the API Evangelist network as a point-nine portfolio company; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published, so this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: APAC Financial Services
providers.description: APAC Financial Services (Apacfin) is a Mumbai-based, Reserve Bank of India registered Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) that provides customized MSME business loans to underbanked and underserved micro, small, and medium enterprises across India. APAC offers tech-enabled, largely paperless digital onboarding, quick disbursal with minimal documentation, and a mobile app (APACM) for loan tracking, EMI payments, and service requests. The lender reports roughly Rs 2,479 Crore of assets under management across 226 branches in six states, serving more than 52,000 customers, and carries an ICRA A (Stable) credit rating. APAC is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published; customer and partner interaction is via the mobile app and hosted customer/complaint portals.

providers.name: Atolls
providers.description: Atolls (formerly Global Savings Group) is a Munich-based consumer commerce-content company that operates the world's largest shopping engagement platform, running coupon, cashback, deals, and shopping-community destinations across more than 20 markets. Its brand portfolio includes Coupons.com, Cuponation, iGraal, Shoop, Pouch, mydealz, hotukdeals, and Deala, connecting millions of shoppers with offers from thousands of retailers and brands through affiliate marketing, cashback, and AI-enhanced shopping insights. Founded in 2012 as CupoNation with Rocket Internet and rebranded to Atolls in 2024, it is backed by investors including HV Capital, RTP Global, and Rocket Internet. Atolls publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI document or SDK — api., developer. and docs.atolls.com do not resolve — but it does serve real machine-readable documents: RFC 9116 security.txt files on five owned hosts pointing at a single group-wide Intigriti vulnerability disclosure program, and OpenID Connect discovery documents on seven Pepper community properties (mydealz, hotukdeals, Dealabs, Preisjaeger, Chollometro, Pepper PL, Promodescuentos) that expose an OAuth 2.0 authorization server for consumer sign-in. This profile captures that security, identity, and legal surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Celanese
providers.description: Celanese Corporation is a global chemical and specialty materials company that produces high-performance engineered polymers and acetyl products used across automotive, medical, consumer, and industrial applications. Celanese has no publicly documented developer API; digital engagement is delivered through the Chemille digital materials assistant for product search and selection, and a Cognite Data Fusion based manufacturing data platform for internal operations.

providers.name: Corgi
providers.description: Corgi is an AI-native, full-stack business insurance platform for startups, offering modular coverage (Commercial General Liability, Directors & Officers, Tech Errors & Omissions, Cyber, EPLI, and fiduciary) quoted in minutes. Founded in 2024 and based in San Francisco, Corgi is a licensed insurance carrier rather than a broker, underwriting and issuing policies directly with pricing tailored to a startup's stage (pre-seed, Series A, growth). Backed by Kindred Ventures and TCV, the company was reported as an AI insurance unicorn in 2026. This API Evangelist profile was seeded from Kindred Ventures' portfolio; Corgi does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Coursebase
providers.description: Coursebase is an AI-powered corporate Learning Management System (LMS) used by over 1,000 organizations to create, deliver, and manage employee training across online, in-person, and blended formats. The platform offers a library of 1,000+ pre-built eLearning courses, AI-assisted content generation (auto-generated test questions and course summaries), analytics and reporting dashboards, single sign-on, multi-language support, and API-based integration with external HR systems for syncing user account information. Coursebase was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched in the API Evangelist network; the public surface is a marketing site with an enterprise "contact us" API integration offering rather than a self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI.

providers.name: Denso
providers.description: Denso Corporation is a Japanese global Tier 1 automotive components manufacturer headquartered in Kariya, Aichi. Denso designs and supplies thermal, powertrain, mobility electronics, and electrification systems to global automakers.

providers.name: Dredd
providers.description: Dredd is a language-agnostic, open source HTTP API testing framework that validates API implementations against API Blueprint or OpenAPI (2.0/3.0) description documents.

providers.name: Eero
providers.description: eero makes home mesh Wi-Fi systems that are simple, powerful, secure, and reliable. eero pioneered home mesh wifi and sells products for homes, businesses, service providers, pro installers, and communities, including the eero Pro 7, eero PoE 7, and eero Signal, plus the eero Plus subscription for enhanced security and multi-network management. Devices are managed through the award-winning eero app and are deployed across 27+ countries. eero LLC is based in San Francisco, CA and is an Amazon company. eero does not publish a public developer API or first-party SDK; the eero app communicates with a private, unpublished backend.

providers.name: Equipboard
providers.description: Equipboard is a community-sourced music-gear discovery platform where musicians, producers, and DJs find the equipment behind the music. Members browse the gear their favorite artists play — guitars, effects pedals, synthesizers, DAWs, plug-ins, microphones, drum machines, and keyboards — build and share their own rigs and gear lists, read and write reviews, and follow buy-links to retailers. Equipboard is built by musicians for musicians and monetizes primarily through affiliate relationships (including the Amazon Associates Program). Recent product work adds album- and track-level gear attribution. The company is backed by 500 Global. Equipboard does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network and enriched from Equipboard's public web surface.

providers.name: Exaforce
providers.description: Exaforce is a security operations platform that pairs AI agents with a unified data layer to help teams detect, triage, investigate, and respond to threats faster. Its four autonomous "Exabot" agents (Detect, Triage, Investigate, and Respond) automate SOC workflows across 100+ data sources spanning cloud, identity, endpoint, SaaS, and code repositories, and can run as a self-operated platform or as a managed detection and response (MDR) service staffed by expert analysts working alongside the AI 24/7. Exaforce positions itself as an agentic-SOC alternative to traditional SIEM tooling while retaining integration compatibility. The company is backed by Mayfield and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or reference documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, security, and trust surface.

providers.name: Forvia
providers.description: Forvia is a French global Tier 1 automotive supplier formed in 2022 by the combination of Faurecia and Hella. Forvia designs and manufactures cockpits, seating, interiors, lighting, electronics, hydrogen storage, and clean mobility systems for global automakers.

providers.name: Friend
providers.description: Friend is an AI companion pendant — a sub-two-inch wearable with a microphone that pairs with a phone app and communicates back to the user via text messages rather than speech. Originally announced at $99, the product shipped (after delays) in 2025 at $129 in North America. Friend is a consumer hardware company with no public developer API, SDK, or partner program; only the consumer site, an app, and the Wikipedia / press coverage exist as references.

providers.name: Funding Societies
providers.description: Funding Societies (known as Modalku in Indonesia) is Southeast Asia's largest unified SME digital finance platform, founded in 2015 and operating across Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. It provides small and medium-sized enterprises with business financing — term loans, micro loans, revolving credit lines, invoice and trade financing — and offers retail and institutional investors the ability to fund those loans for a return. The group is licensed and regulated in its markets and is backed by investors including SoftBank Vision Fund, Sequoia, and SoftBank Ventures Asia. Funding Societies does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK program; this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web properties and security posture. It will be upgraded if and when a public API surface is published.

providers.name: Gestamp
providers.description: Gestamp Automocion is a Spanish global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Madrid. Gestamp designs and manufactures metal components for vehicle bodies, chassis, and mechanisms, with focus on lightweighting and structural safety for global automakers.

providers.name: Go To-U
providers.description: GO TO-U is an operating system for electric-vehicle charging management, built for Charge Point Operators (CPOs) and businesses that run charging infrastructure. The platform is hardware-agnostic, integrating with 50+ charger manufacturers (ABB, Wallbox, Siemens, EVBox and others), and bundles charge-point management, AI-powered analytics and load optimization, a driver-facing mobile app (iOS and Android), roaming, white-label options, and integrated payment processing. Its Advanced Reservation Technology (ART) lets drivers book charging slots in advance to reduce wait times. GO TO-U is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from the company's public website; no public developer/API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications were discoverable at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Haven Energy
providers.description: Haven Energy is an Austin, Texas based residential clean-energy company that sells, finances, installs and operates home battery storage and solar systems, and then aggregates those systems into one of the largest virtual power plant (VPP) networks in the United States. Homeowners get an instant online quote, a fixed monthly payment over a ten-year term, end-to-end permitting and certified installation through Haven's Channel Partner network of local electricians, and ongoing remote monitoring. Haven then enrolls the installed batteries into utility and grid programs - California SGIP, PG&E, and Massachusetts ConnectedSolutions among them - so customers can monetize grid participation while utilities and community choice aggregators gain flexible local capacity. Founded in 2022 by Jeff Chapin, Philip Krim and Vinnie Campos, the company raised a $40M Series B in December 2025 led by Giant Ventures. Haven operates as a direct-to-consumer and utility-partner business; it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: HiJoJo Partners
providers.description: HiJoJo Partners Inc. (HiJoJo Partners株式会社) is a Tokyo-based independent asset management and fintech group, established in November 2017 and registered with the Director of the Kanto Local Finance Bureau (No. 3065) for Type II Financial Instruments Business, Investment Management Business, and Investment Advisory and Agency Business. The firm forms, sells and manages funds that give Japanese institutional and individual investors access to late-stage private and pre-IPO companies, and works to develop Japan's secondary market for unlisted shares. It operates three lines: HiJoJo Prime (in-person advisory for investors with 100M JPY or more in investable assets), HiJoJo.com (an online fund platform for individual investors with 30M JPY or more), and HiJoJo Private Market Solution for institutional investors and startups. HiJoJo joined the Nasdaq Private Market investor consortium in 2024 to expand secondary-market access in Japan. Its investor-facing platform is delivered as an authenticated member web application; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Hole19
providers.description: Hole19 (Stat Track Technologies Lda) is a golf app for iOS, Android, and smartwatches used by 4.8M+ golfers across 42,000+ golf courses in 200+ countries. It provides GPS rangefinder distances, digital scorecards, shot tracking, performance statistics, an Otto AI game assistant, and a WHS handicap calculator, plus social features such as LivePlay live leaderboards and a social feed. The company also ships CORE Golf, a practice app with structured plans and 100+ drills, and operates a worldwide golf course directory, a golf glossary, and The 19th Hole magazine. The core app is free with two subscription tiers, Premium and Intelligence. Hole19 does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, legal, support, and llms.txt surface.

providers.name: HomeLight
providers.description: HomeLight is a San Francisco–based real-estate technology company that matches home buyers and sellers with top-performing local real-estate agents and operates a stack of consumer-facing products that span the entire residential transaction: agent matching, Simple Sale cash-offer marketplace, Buy Before You Sell (BBYS) bridge financing, HomeLight Home Loans (NMLS #1529229), the HomeLight HELOC Card, and HomeLight Closing Services for title and escrow. The company ranks agents using historical performance data on home sales (price, speed, volume, geography, property type) and routes consumer leads to a curated network of agents, lenders, and cash-buyer investors. HomeLight exposes a private Partner API to lenders, brokerages, CRMs, and marketing partners (NerdWallet is its largest partner) for submitting leads (`/api/partner_lead/v2`), Simple Sale seller leads (`/leads/partner_simple_sale_lead`), and duplicate-lead checks (`/api/partner_dupe_lead_check`); credentials are issued on a per-partner basis via support@homelight.com. Beyond the Partner API, HomeLight has direct integrations with most major real-estate agent CRMs (Follow Up Boss, BoomTown, Sierra Interactive, Firepoint, Real Geeks, Brivity, Chime, LionDesk, KW Command). HomeLight has no public, self-service developer portal — the Partner API is gated by a commercial relationship, and there is no public OpenAPI spec, SDK, or open-source client published by the company.

providers.name: Hyundai Mobis
providers.description: Hyundai Mobis is a South Korean global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Seoul. Part of the Hyundai Motor Group, Mobis designs and manufactures chassis, cockpit, and front-end modules, plus electrification, ADAS, and infotainment systems for global automakers.

providers.name: Inmarsat
providers.description: Inmarsat is a British satellite communications operator founded in 1979, originally as the International Maritime Satellite Organization, providing voice, data, broadband, and IoT services over a global L-band, Ka-band, and multi-band fleet of geostationary satellites. In May 2023 Viasat completed its acquisition of Inmarsat, and the combined company now operates Inmarsat's GX (Global Xpress), BGAN, IsatData Pro (IDP), and Fleet Xpress services alongside Viasat's ViaSat-3 constellation as a unified multi-orbit network. Inmarsat serves four core markets — Maritime (NexusWave, Fleet Xpress, Fleet One, FleetBroadband, Inmarsat C/GMDSS), Aviation (SwiftBroadband, GX Aviation, Jet ConneX, SB-S safety services), Government (L-TAC, GX, BGAN M2M), and Enterprise/IoT (BGAN M2M, IsatData Pro, IsatM2M, NB-NTN). Inmarsat operates a developer program at developer.inmarsat.com with documented APIs for BGAN network management, GSPS voice, Global Xpress, IsatData Pro messaging, Fleet Edge assurance, and Fleet Edge hardware replacement; access to interactive Swagger documentation is gated behind developer registration and approval, though the IsatData Pro Messaging API has an open-source Apache-2.0 Node.js client published on GitHub. Inmarsat is also one of the participating operators in the GSMA NB-NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) standards work for satellite-extended cellular IoT, with Viasat-led proof-of-concept code for NIDD (Non-IP Data Delivery) published under the inmarsat-enterprise GitHub organization.

providers.name: Island
providers.description: Island is the developer of the Enterprise Browser, a Chromium-based browser purpose-built for the enterprise that embeds security, data protection, and governance directly into the last mile of work. The platform unifies an Enterprise Browser, Enterprise AI, and an Enterprise Network (SASE) so organizations can control how users interact with SaaS and internal applications, enforcing data-loss prevention, privileged access, insider-risk controls, and zero-trust policy at the browser layer, and replacing VDI/DaaS for many contractor and BYOD scenarios. Island is a private cybersecurity company backed by Insight Partners and other investors. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is published; administration is via the management console at management.island.io.

providers.name: Junk King
providers.description: Junk King is a professional junk removal and hauling franchise operating across the United States and Canada as part of the Neighborly family of home service brands. Through locally owned and operated locations, Junk King provides full-service junk removal, self-service dumpster rental, and dumpster bag pickup for residential and commercial customers, handling appliance and furniture removal, estate and property cleanouts, construction debris, yard waste, and e-waste. The company emphasizes eco-friendly disposal, recycling, donating, and reusing as much collected material as possible. Junk King offers free estimates, same-day service in many markets, and online, phone, and text-based booking. It is a portfolio company associated with Norwest Venture Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; Junk King publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Kinema
providers.description: Kinema is a social cinema platform and independent film distribution service. It empowers independent filmmakers to release, control, and get paid for their films through global distribution, partner-driven and live screenings, and direct-to-audience streaming, with ownership retention, transparent weekly payouts, and real-time earnings dashboards. Hosts and community builders get screening software and event tools to turn any space into a movie house, in person or online, while audiences discover independent films and attend virtual or in-person screenings, directly supporting filmmakers through ticket and rental purchases.

providers.name: Known
providers.description: Known is a voice-first, swipeless dating application founded in 2025 by Celeste Amadon and Asher Allen and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Instead of profiles, feeds, queues, and swiping, Known onboards users through a voice-AI interview and then sends one curated introduction at a time, with a 24-hour acceptance window on both sides. When both people accept, Known helps pick a restaurant that fits both sets of preferences and checks calendar availability, then collects a short post-date check-in to refine future matches. The company optimizes for in-person dates rather than engagement, and has raised $9.7M from Forerunner Ventures, NFX, and other investors. The product is iOS-only in the United States today, with waitlists for Android and for Apple users outside the US. Known publishes no public developer program, API, or SDKs; it does publish a first-party llms.txt describing the product for AI agents.

providers.name: Last Energy
providers.description: Last Energy is an American developer and operator of micro-modular nuclear power plants, founded in 2019 in Washington, D.C. by Bret Kugelmass as a commercial spinout of the Energy Impact Center. Its flagship PWR-20 is a 20 MWe pressurized water reactor assembled from a few dozen factory-made, steel-encased modules that ship to site and are installed rather than constructed in place. Last Energy sells power rather than reactors: it designs, finances, owns and operates plants under long-term power purchase agreements for energy-intensive customers including data centers, metals, chemicals, cement, pulp and paper, and food and beverage. The company has announced projects in Texas, South Wales, Poland and Romania, entered nuclear site licensing in the United Kingdom, partnered with Texas A&M and DP World, and raised roughly $164M across a $40M Series B and a $100M Series C. Last Energy publishes a marketing site and a gated customer/whitepaper portal, but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: LeaseLock
providers.description: LeaseLock is an insurtech platform for rental housing that replaces the traditional cash security deposit with lease insurance. Its Zero Deposit program embeds coverage into the lease through a signed addendum, removing thousands of dollars of move-in cost for residents while protecting owners and operators against unpaid rent and damage. LeaseLock Shield applies AI to ledger data, market trends and lease profiles to underwrite risk, and LeaseLock Central gives property teams a portal for claims, support tickets and training. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Dallas, Texas, the company says it integrates with all major property management systems, but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, API reference or client SDKs — integration is arranged as a managed engagement. Its public engineering output is two open-source PostgreSQL extensions, pgasync and pgflow.

providers.name: Letswork
providers.description: Letswork is a Dubai-headquartered flexible workspace booking platform that lets members work from coworking spaces, cafes, hotels, meeting rooms, private offices and creative studios through a single credit-based monthly membership with no long-term contract. Founded in 2019 by Omar AlMheiri and Hamza Khan, the platform covers 1030+ workspaces across 63+ cities in 18+ countries, serving 80,000+ members across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa. The product ships as iOS, Android and web apps with one-tap check-in, day passes, hourly meeting-room booking, a private-offices marketplace, and team plans that add a shared credit pool, admin dashboard and usage analytics for hybrid companies. Letswork publishes no public developer API or developer portal; it does publish a first-party llms.txt canonical fact set for AI assistants.

providers.name: Magna International
providers.description: Magna International is a Canadian global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Aurora, Ontario. Magna designs and manufactures vehicle bodies, chassis, exteriors, seating, powertrain, ADAS, electronics, mirrors, and complete vehicle assembly through its global operations.

providers.name: MAHLE
providers.description: MAHLE is a German global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Stuttgart. MAHLE designs and manufactures thermal management, electrification, engine systems and components, filtration, and mechatronics for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and off-highway equipment.

providers.name: Manifest Law
providers.description: Manifest Law operates ManifestOS, a communication and case management platform for the legal industry, and is backed by Menlo Ventures. The platform exposes a standards-based OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization server at app.manifestlaw.com, with an `api` scope for programmatic access and dynamic OAuth client management (`oauth_clients:manage`). This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Manifest Law's public discovery documents; no OpenAPI specification was published at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Mill
providers.description: Mill is a consumer sustainability company that makes a smart kitchen bin which dries and grinds household food scraps overnight into dry, nutrient-rich "Food Grounds," keeping food waste out of landfills and cutting the methane it would otherwise produce. Sold as a membership starting around $799 or roughly $66/month, the bin is odorless, reduces food-waste volume by about 80%, and the resulting grounds are reused in gardens, as chicken feed, or through farm partnerships. Mill also runs a commercial line for grocery, offices, food service, and municipalities. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Mill is a consumer hardware and subscription business with a companion mobile app; it exposes no public developer API — its /api/ path is an internal app backend disallowed in robots.txt.

providers.name: MONI (Ex-Monisnap)
providers.description: MONI, formerly Monisnap, is a Paris-based remittance fintech founded in 2017 by Raphaël Rivière, Jean-Baptiste Bouvier and Jonathan Brossard. It lets diaspora customers in France, Spain and the United Kingdom send money to roughly 150 countries — as cash pickup across a partner network of some 350,000 payout points, as a transfer into a mobile money wallet, as mobile airtime top-up with more than 800 operators, or as a prepaid card recharge — through a consumer app and the monisnap.com and allo.monisnap.com storefronts. Alongside the consumer product MONI runs a B2B "Moni-as-a-Service" remittance-as-a-service platform that banks and neobanks such as Nickel and Bnext embed white-label in their own applications. MONISNAP SAS is registered with the French ACPR as a payment services agent of MPS SAS, an authorised payment institution (CIB 17738). MONI publishes no public API: there is no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract on any MONI host — the partner platform is reached through a sales conversation.

providers.name: Mottu
providers.description: Mottu is the leading motorcycle-rental ecosystem in Latin America, founded in 2020 in Sao Paulo, Brazil by Rubens Zanelatto. It rents motorcycles to gig and delivery couriers who lack access to traditional credit, bundling insurance, maintenance, 24-hour support and financial services (Mottu Pay) so workers can earn income through food delivery, e-commerce and last-mile logistics. Mottu has verticalized the value chain, running its own assembly line, parts and service network, and fleet-management software, and offers white-labeled last-mile delivery (Mottu Entregas) to more than 1,000 retailers across 100+ cities in Brazil and Mexico. Backed by QED Investors, Mottu has raised over US$150M. It operates as a consumer and B2B mobility/fintech app and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Octane Lending
providers.description: Octane (Octane Lending, Inc.) is a New York City fintech founded in 2014 that makes powersports, outdoor power equipment and recreational-vehicle financing as simple as paying cash. It runs an end-to-end digital lending platform — instant soft-pull prequalification for consumers, real-time credit decisioning and eContracting through its in-house lender Roadrunner Financial, Inc., and loan servicing — connecting more than 4,000 dealer partners and 30-plus OEMs with prime through non-prime buyers. Its Dealer Portal 2.0 and dealer-management-system integrations (AppOne, Ekho and similar DMS platforms) submit credit applications and return decisions over a partner API whose credentials are coordinated privately by Octane account managers; Octane publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Opti
providers.description: Opti is an AI-native identity and access management (IAM) platform for enterprises struggling with access sprawl across human, non-human, and agentic identities. Founded in 2024 by Barak Perelman, Mille Gandelsman, and Ido Trivizki, Opti deploys pre-trained, domain-specific large language models trained on curated identity data to interpret risk, recommend least-privilege access decisions, and orchestrate safe permissions. The platform spans Access Intelligence, Risk Mitigation, Lifecycle Management (joiner/mover/leaver), and Compliance, integrating with 250+ identity solutions, IdPs, IGAs, HRIS, and ITSM systems without rip-and-replace. Opti raised a $20M seed round led by YL Ventures, Mayfield Fund, and Hetz Ventures.

providers.name: Posha
providers.description: Posha (formerly Nymble) is a consumer robotics company that makes an autonomous countertop kitchen robot which cooks fresh, home-style meals from raw ingredients across 1,000+ recipes. The device combines robotics, computer-vision cameras, automated heat, timing and stirring control, and culinary AI, paired with an iOS/Android companion app for real-time monitoring and recipe control. Backed by Accel, Posha is a consumer hardware and appliance product with a companion mobile app; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with real, verifiable public properties.

providers.name: Rabbit
providers.description: Rabbit is the maker of the R1, a $199 handheld AI device running rabbitOS 2.1 with no subscription required. The R1 ships with Magic Recorder (unlimited recordings, transcripts, AI summaries), Magic Camera, Magic Voice, and DLAM — the Desktop Large Action Model, a plug-and-play controller that carries out tasks across the user's computer OS. Rabbit's Large Action Model is exposed to users via the LAM Playground on rabbit.tech. Industrial design is by Teenage Engineering. Partner integrations (e.g. OpenClaw for voice-activated task automation) are user-configured. No public developer API or SDK is documented; partner / developer access appears to be gated.

providers.name: Renew Financial
providers.description: Renew Financial (Renew Financial Group LLC) is a specialty consumer finance company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Oakland, California that pioneered and administers Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) financing for residential energy efficiency, renewable energy, water efficiency and resiliency home improvements. It administers the CaliforniaFIRST program in California and RenewPACE in Florida, funding solar, HVAC, roofing, windows, landscaping, hurricane and seismic projects through a voluntary property tax assessment repaid over terms up to 30 years. The company is licensed by the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation as a PACE Program Administrator (#60DBO-90653) and carries NMLS ID 1788120. Renew Financial runs a contractor technology platform and an online homeowner application, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Renovate
providers.description: Renovate is an Open Source, cross-platform dependency automation tool by Mend.io that automatically creates pull requests to keep software dependencies up to date. It supports over 90 package managers and language ecosystems including npm, PyPI, Maven, Docker, Helm, Go modules, Ruby Gems, NuGet, and more. Renovate runs as a CLI, Docker container, GitHub Action, or hosted cloud service (Mend Renovate App). It integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea, Forgejo, and AWS CodeCommit. Configuration is done via a number of different locations in the repository: most commonly a `renovate.json` file in the repository root. The tool supports advanced scheduling, monorepo support, preset sharing, merge confidence scoring, and automatic replacement of deprecated packages.

providers.name: Saronic Technologies
providers.description: Saronic Technologies designs, manufactures, and deploys AI-enabled autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) for maritime security, domain awareness, reconnaissance, logistics, and payload delivery. The Austin-based company sells to the U.S. Navy, allied defense forces, and select commercial and government customers. Vessel models include Spyglass, Cutlass, Corsair, and Marauder, ranging from 6 to 150 feet. The Echelon software platform provides mission planning, high-fidelity simulation, fleet command-and-control, and open architecture for third-party payload integration (ISR sensors, EW, comms, weapons). Saronic does not publish a public, self-service developer API; integrations are arranged through partnership and are subject to U.S. export controls (ITAR/EAR).

providers.name: SurePath AI
providers.description: SurePath AI (now part of F5) is an enterprise AI governance and security platform that lets organizations safely adopt generative AI across their workforce. The platform gives security and IT teams visibility into GenAI usage by recording conversations, mitigates risk by detecting and redacting sensitive data in prompts and enforcing role-based access guardrails to public and private models, and increases safe adoption through a branded enterprise GenAI portal that enriches interactions with enterprise data. It is delivered as a SaaS product with an admin console rather than a public developer API, and maintains SOC 2 compliance.

providers.name: Syndio
providers.description: Syndio is an enterprise workplace-equity and compensation-governance software company. Its AI-assisted platform helps large organizations make defensible, compliant pay decisions at scale, spanning offers, promotions, merit cycles, and pay-equity/pay-transparency compliance (including EU Pay Transparency Directive requirements). The platform is organized into Essentials (foundations for aligned, compliant pay decisions), Decisions (real-time guidance during pay decision-making), and Predict (forward-looking workforce intelligence), all powered by the domain-specific Syndi AI. Syndio reports governing more than $1T in pay decisions for 350+ global enterprises. It is delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS accessed via the app with OAuth 2 / SSO; there is no public self-serve developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition. First-party developer-facing surfaces are limited to the syndioctl command-line tool and a public GitHub organization. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: TriNet
providers.description: TriNet is a Dublin, California-based professional employer organization (PEO) for small and mid-market businesses, founded in 1988 by Martin Babinec and led today by President and CEO Mike Simonds. TriNet delivers full-service HR through a co-employment model — payroll processing, Fortune-500-grade health, retirement and ancillary benefits, workers' compensation, employment-practices liability coverage, compliance and risk management, and strategic HR advisory — to thousands of SMBs across the United States. The company offers two main packages: TriNet PEO (full co-employment) and HR Plus (technology platform plus support). TriNet is publicly traded on the NYSE as TNET with trailing-twelve-month revenue of roughly $5.0B as of FY2025. TriNet exposes its HR Customer Platform through three SwaggerHub-documented API groups — DCP, HRIS, and PEO — covering Employees, Companies, Payroll, Money, and Time-Off domains, with API credentials issued to approved customers and Integration Center partners rather than offered as a fully open developer program; OpenAPI/Swagger, Postman/Insomnia collections, a sandbox, OAuth playground, and webhook management are available to authorized developers. Public 1:1 API access typically requires partner-program qualification and technical review, which is why most TriNet customers consume the platform via the curated Integration Center marketplace (accounting, HRIS, identity, ATS, payroll, benefits and learning partners) or via unified-API aggregators such as Finch, Merge, Apideck and Truto.

providers.name: Urbia
providers.description: Urbia is a German online community and content platform for parents and families, covering fertility, pregnancy, birth, babies, and family life through expert-written magazine articles, active discussion forums, and planning tools. Founded in Cologne in 1998 and backed early by Earlybird Venture Capital, urbia.de is today part of the ELTERN family of parenting brands, operated by Funke Women, People & Family GmbH in Hamburg. Urbia does not publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Velvet
providers.description: Velvet is a multimodal AI model R&D company (the "multimodal data lab") based in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch. It partners with frontier AI labs and enterprises to build state-of-the-art video datasets and evaluation frameworks that improve models' spatial reasoning and interactive, low-latency capabilities. Velvet operates an invite-only platform for sourcing and contributing multimodal training data, with contributor payouts via Stripe and Wise. It was founded by Lucas Mantovani (CEO, formerly video data at Meta FAIR) and Lucas Tucker (CTO, formerly Adobe). As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK.

providers.name: Vistra Corp
providers.description: Vistra Corp (NYSE: VST) is an Irving, Texas integrated retail electricity and power generation company and the largest competitive power generator in the United States, operating roughly 41,000-44,000 MW of natural gas, nuclear, coal, solar and battery storage capacity alongside a retail business serving nearly 5 million residential, commercial and industrial customers across 16 states and the District of Columbia through TXU Energy, Dynegy, Ambit Energy, Energy Harbor, Homefield Energy and U.S. Gas & Electric. Its home market is the United States, where it sits on both sides of the competitive value chain, a merchant generator selling into ERCOT, PJM, ISO-NE, NYISO, MISO and CAISO, and a retail electricity provider (REP) reselling that power to end customers. Its API posture is honestly none. No developer portal, no API subdomain and no machine-readable contract of any kind was found: developer., developers., docs., api. and data. on vistracorp.com do not resolve; /developers, /api, /docs, /data, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /.well-known/openid-configuration all return 404; and TXU Energy's 758-URL sitemap contains no developer or API page. The United States has no consumer energy data mandate. Green Button is an NAESB/NIST ESPI standard adopted voluntarily, and TXU Energy appears on the US Department of Energy's list of "Utilities Committed to Implementing Green Button", a 2012-era commitment list and not evidence of a live endpoint. The only customer-data surface found is Download-My-Data-style export behind the TXU Energy MyAccount login, whose interval readings are themselves sourced from Smart Meter Texas, the shared ERCOT meter-data platform operated by the transmission and distribution utilities (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP) rather than by Vistra. Because Vistra is a retailer and generator and not a wires company, the third-party interval-data API in its home Texas market belongs to Smart Meter Texas and not to Vistra. Vistra likewise publishes no open market or grid data of its own; ERCOT, the other ISOs/RTOs and the EIA publish the market data about Vistra's fleet. Both sides are therefore closed at the company boundary. Not to be confused with Vistra Limited (vistra.com), the unrelated corporate-services and fund-administration firm that does run a real API developer portal at devportal.vistra.com.

providers.name: Whova
providers.description: Whova is an award-winning all-in-one event management platform built around a mobile event app that carries the agenda, speaker profiles, attendee networking, live polls, and session Q&A, plus registration, ticketing, name badges, surveys, abstract/speaker management, and exhibitor/sponsor tools. Whova does NOT publish an open, self-serve developer API - there is no public developer portal, no documented REST reference, no OpenAPI definition, and no SDKs. Its only programmatic surface for organizers is a partner/CRM integration layer exposed through Zapier (triggers for attendee, order, and registrant changes plus a create/update-attendee action), reached from the organizer dashboard under Attendees > Integrations > CRM Integration, alongside prebuilt connectors to Eventbrite, Cvent, Constant Contact, RegFox, OpenReview, SharePoint/OneDrive, MailChimp, Wild Apricot, and Google Drive. The API entries below are logical, HONESTLY MODELED views of that integration surface (see endpointsModeled) - they are not sourced from a public Whova API reference, and no base URL, auth scheme, or endpoint paths are published by Whova.

providers.name: Worq
providers.description: WORQ is Malaysia's largest community-centric coworking space operator, backed by 500 Global, offering private offices, dedicated desks, hot desks, virtual offices, meeting rooms, event spaces, and day passes across twelve locations in Greater Kuala Lumpur and Selangor. WORQ publishes no public developer portal or API as of July 2026.

providers.name: Yazaki
providers.description: Yazaki Corporation is a Japanese global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Tokyo. Yazaki is a leading manufacturer of automotive wiring harnesses, connectors, instrumentation, and electrical distribution systems for global automakers.

providers.name: ZF Friedrichshafen
providers.description: ZF Friedrichshafen AG is a German global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Friedrichshafen. ZF designs and manufactures driveline, chassis, active and passive safety, and ADAS technology for passenger cars and commercial vehicles. ZF acquired TRW Automotive in 2015.

providers.name: 8Tracks
providers.description: 8tracks was a San Francisco-based internet radio and social music-streaming service that let people create and share handcrafted playlists ("mixes") of at least eight tracks, discover mixes by mood, activity, genre, and tag, and play them back through the web, iOS, and Android apps. Founded in 2008, it grew to more than eight million monthly listeners by 2014 before declining. 8tracks published a public REST API (v2/v3) that exposed mix discovery, playback token sessions, track skip/report events, and user likes/favorites, but stopped issuing new API keys in February 2015. The company ceased operations on December 31, 2019, briefly relaunched under BackBeat Inc. in April 2020, and the service has been inactive since. This profile documents the historical API surface and web properties.

providers.name: Airbase
providers.description: Airbase is a modern spend management platform for finance teams that combines accounts-payable (AP) automation and bill pay, guided procurement and purchase orders, corporate cards, and expense reimbursements on a single system with real-time general-ledger sync. Airbase Inc. was acquired by Paylocity in a ~$325M deal announced September 4, 2024 and completed October 1, 2024, and now operates as "Airbase by Paylocity," extending Paylocity's HCM suite into the office of the CFO. Airbase exposes a developer platform at developer.airbase.io (REST API reference, OpenAPI/Swagger, Postman and Insomnia collections, a webhooks management API, an OAuth playground, and a sandbox) used to build custom connections for systems not covered by the pre-built integrations. API access is account-gated - credentials are generated inside the customer's Airbase/Paylocity tenant rather than through open self-serve signup - so the logical APIs below are honestly modeled from the documented product surface and developer portal, and the exact endpoint paths and base URL are not publicly reproduced here (endpointsModeled).

providers.name: Apiphani
providers.description: Apiphani is a technology-enabled application managed-services company dedicated to helping businesses minimize the effort and risk of running their tier-1, mission-critical applications. It combines decades of enterprise operations experience with intelligent automation and machine learning to drive efficiency and reliability across SAP environments (S/4HANA, Business Suite, Cloud ERP) running on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Services span application technical management (ABAP, SAP Basis, application security), application hosting (ALM/APM), application infrastructure (auto-scaling, HA/DR), security management, and cloud migration and optimization. Apiphani's Luumen platform is an AI-native observability product with "Deep Automation" that detects and resolves issues before users notice, unifying application telemetry, security, and self-healing. The company is certified SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and CSA STAR, and is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Azura
providers.description: Azura is an onchain trading platform that lets users trade any onchain asset priced in USD without managing wallets, bridging assets, or paying gas fees. Under the tagline "If it's onchain, it's on Azura," the app offers cross-chain token swaps across multiple blockchains in a single transaction, spot trading with multiple order types, token discovery and analysis, portfolio and PnL tracking, a referral system, and an Azurite rewards program, all with zero platform trading fees. Smart-contract interactions are algorithmically security-audited. Azura is a consumer-facing DeFi product (web app at app.azura.xyz) backed by Initialized Capital; it publishes user documentation and a blog but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or specification surface.

providers.name: Biobot
providers.description: Biobot Analytics is a wastewater epidemiology company that operates a wastewater intelligence platform, analyzing sewage samples to detect and track more than 50 human health indicators — including pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, influenza, RSV, measles, norovirus), substances (fentanyl, cocaine, methamphetamine, buprenorphine), and public-health threats (HIV, mpox, poliovirus, Candida auris) — before they surface in conventional reporting. Founded from MIT research and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Biobot serves federal, state, and local government agencies, pharmaceutical and life-sciences companies, and healthcare systems through dashboards, CSV exports, map visualizations, and enterprise data integrations. Biobot does not publish a public self-serve developer API; data access is arranged directly with the company.

providers.name: Brokk
providers.description: Brokk (Brokk, Inc.) builds AI tooling for large codebases. Rather than a hosted REST API, Brokk ships open-source developer tools centered on "bifrost" — a Tree-sitter-backed multi-language static-analysis engine that gives coding agents structured code intelligence (symbols, definitions, references, call graphs, usage analysis) across 12 languages. Bifrost runs as a CLI, a workspace-aware language server (LSP), and a stdio MCP server, and is published to crates.io (brokk-bifrost) and PyPI (brokk-bifrost-searchtools). The company, founded by Jonathan Ellis (Apache Cassandra / DataStax) and backed by Mayfield, also ships the core Brokk application, the brokk-cli launcher, and Agent Client Protocol (ACP) tooling (anvil, mjolnir).

providers.name: BUX
providers.description: BUX is a European neobroker and mobile-first investing app operated by BUX B.V., a subsidiary of ABN AMRO. It lets retail investors across Europe buy and sell individual stocks and ETFs commission-free starting from as little as EUR 10, build automated BUX Investment Plans (thematic and expert-built portfolios), and earn interest on uninvested cash across BUX Basic, Plus, and Prime account tiers. BUX is authorised and regulated by the Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM), with client financial instruments and money held in segregated custody via ABN AMRO Clearing and deposits protected up to EUR 100,000 under the Dutch Deposit Guarantee Scheme. BUX does not publish a public developer API or SDKs; this profile captures the company's identity, legal, and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CDW
providers.description: CDW is a leading multi-brand provider of information technology solutions to business, government, education, and healthcare customers. CDW offers eProcurement integration capabilities including a Catalog API, PunchOut (cXML/OCI), electronic purchase ordering, and electronic invoicing to enable procurement system integration with partners such as SAP Ariba, Coupa, Oracle, and Jaggaer.

providers.name: Chegg
providers.description: Chegg is an American education technology company that provides direct-to-student learning services, including 24/7 homework and expert Q&A help, step-by-step textbook solutions, practice questions, and writing, grammar, and citation tools. Founded in 2005 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Chegg began as a textbook-rental marketplace and expanded into a subscription study-support platform (Chegg Study, Chegg Writing, Chegg Math Solver) plus tutoring and skills offerings. Chegg operates as a consumer web/mobile product rather than a developer platform: it exposes no public developer portal, published API, or SDKs at this time. Its public technical surface is limited to a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program on HackerOne and standard web security/policy pages. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Comet
providers.description: Comet is Perplexity's AI-native browser built on Chromium (Blink), integrating Perplexity Search and an agentic assistant that can summarize pages, draft emails, and complete tasks. Launched July 9, 2025 on Windows and macOS, with Android (Nov 2025), iOS (Mar 2026), and visionOS support added later. Initially gated behind a paid Perplexity subscription, opened free to everyone in October 2025. This is a consumer browser product with no publicly documented REST API surface.

providers.name: Complyance
providers.description: Complyance is an AI-powered Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform for enterprise security, risk, and compliance teams. It automates manual GRC workflows across controls management, policy management, risk management, third-party and vendor risk management (TPRM), and customer trust, using purpose-built AI agents for evidence review, control advice, policy drafting, and vendor questionnaire and risk scoring. Complyance ships 100+ ready-made frameworks (including SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, NIST CSF 2.0, CMMC, and GDPR) plus 100+ enterprise integrations to centralize evidence and support audits at scale.

providers.name: Compstak
providers.description: CompStak is a commercial real estate (CRE) data platform, founded in 2012, that crowdsources and verifies lease comps, sale comps, loan data, and property data from a network of tens of thousands of brokers and appraisers across US markets. Its products include CompStak One (an all-in-one CRE data platform), CompStak Exchange, CompStak AI, and a contact-sales Data API offering Market Insights, Property Insights, Space Insights, and Property Standardization. CompStak was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Its developer surface is enterprise/contact-sales only — there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or API reference.

providers.name: Dolby
providers.description: Dolby Laboratories is a leading technology company specializing in audio and video. The Dolby developer platform (dolby.io / Dolby OptiView) provides APIs and SDKs for media processing, real-time streaming, video playback, and ad delivery. Dolby is responsible for technologies including Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Dolby Digital.

providers.name: Enosys Markets
providers.description: Ēnosys (formerly Flare Finance) is a decentralized finance (DeFi) platform building on the Flare and Songbird networks. Its product suite spans DEX V2 and V3 automated market makers with liquidity provision, collateralized Loans, yield Farms with a token launchpad, a cross-chain Bridge, DeFi price Oracles built on the Flare Time Series Oracle (FTSO), the Skopos blockchain indexer, Oryy multi-signature self-custody vaults, and an NFT suite (Gallery, Ermis, Clover). Enosys interfaces are smart-contract based rather than a conventional REST API; developer integration happens through published Solidity contracts, subgraphs, and price-feed connectors in the flrfinance GitHub organization.

providers.name: Finley (Concord)
providers.description: Finley (Concord) is Finley Technologies, a cloud-based loan administration and debt-capital-management platform for credit funds, banks, and private credit operators. The software digitizes 200+ credit-agreement fields and covers loan servicing (KYC, money movement, notice delivery), portfolio and borrowing-base monitoring, syndicated-loan management, and backup / credit administration, plus Finley AI for automating calculations, compliance checks, and notices. Finley is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and is delivered as a hosted web application at app.finleycms.com with product documentation at docs.finleycms.com. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK is published at this time.

providers.name: Fizz
providers.description: Fizz is a social platform built for college campuses, connecting students within their own school communities across 700+ campuses in the United States. Founded by Stanford students, Fizz gives verified students an anonymous, hyper-local feed to find their community and join the conversation, buy and sell through Fizz Marketplace, and engage under community values of being supportive, curious, honest, and brave. The platform is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and NEA. Fizz is a consumer mobile social app and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, legal, and security surface for network discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Freed
providers.description: Freed is a San Francisco-based AI medical scribe and clinician assistant designed to reduce the documentation burden on healthcare providers. The product listens to patient visits and generates SOAP-style clinical notes, visit summaries, patient instructions, referral letters, and ICD-10 / CPT coding suggestions, then transfers the finalized note into the clinician's EHR via a browser-resident agent. Freed was founded in 2023 by former Facebook engineers Erez Druk (CEO) and Andrey Bannikov (CTO) after Druk's wife, a practicing family physician, experienced the daily toll of manual charting. The company is consumer self-serve: clinicians sign up for a 7-day free trial and then a monthly Starter, Core, Premier, or custom Groups plan with no enterprise sales required. As of 2025 Freed reported more than 20,000 paying clinician users and raised a $30M Series A led by Sequoia Capital, bringing total funding to $34M. The platform is HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified, and HITECH-ready; patient recordings are not stored. Rather than ship a traditional public REST API, Freed pursues an "anti-integration" model in which a Chrome-extension AI agent navigates any web-based EHR (Athena, Tebra, PracticeFusion, TherapyNotes, SimplePractice, Elation, AdvancedMD, Cerbo, and others) to place the finished note in the correct fields. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release.

providers.name: Geniebook
providers.description: Geniebook is a Singapore-based educational technology company (Geniebook Pte Ltd, incorporated 2016) offering an AI-powered online learning platform for primary, secondary, and JC students. Its product suite includes GenieSmart (AI-personalised worksheets generated from a library of 300,000+ MOE syllabus-aligned questions, using algorithms co-developed with A*STAR), GenieClass (live and recorded online classes taught by experienced teachers), and GenieAsk (real-time moderated teacher chats for after-school academic support), plus a CAMPUS physical-tutoring offering and PSLE/JC preparation programmes. Geniebook serves more than 220,000 students across Singapore, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Indonesia, and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. It is a consumer (B2C) learning application delivered via web and mobile apps; no public developer API is published.

providers.name: Geocomply
providers.description: GeoComply is a geolocation compliance, digital identity, and fraud-prevention company that provides the location-verification and anti-fraud intelligence layer behind many of the world's most regulated digital platforms. Its product suite spans GeoComply Core (location-based fraud detection and geolocation compliance), IDComply (KYC and AML identity verification), GeoGuard (VPN and proxy/spoofing detection), PinPoint (on-property geofencing), the Chargeback Integrator (GCI), and the OneComply licensing-management platform, serving the iGaming, financial services, media/entertainment, and cryptocurrency industries. GeoComply's integrations are enterprise, sales-led engagements rather than a public self-serve developer portal; this profile was surfaced as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company and has been enriched from GeoComply's public security, trust, and discovery surface.

providers.name: Goldbelly
providers.description: Goldbelly is a curated online marketplace for gourmet food and mail-order culinary gifts, shipping iconic meals, desserts, regional specialties, and artisanal products from renowned restaurants, bakeries, and celebrity chefs across the United States directly to consumers' doors. The platform partners with thousands of local and legendary food makers to make hard-to-get regional foods available nationwide, and operates a merchant program ("Sell on Goldbelly") plus corporate and subscription gifting. Goldbelly is a consumer e-commerce brand with no publicly documented developer API; this profile captures its public web, merchant, and corporate identity. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Gomultiply
providers.description: Multiply (gomultiply.com) is an AI-native paid media agency for B2B companies that combines proprietary self-learning advertising AI with human growth strategists. The platform plugs into a customer's sales calls and CRM data to learn why buyers actually convert, then uses 25+ specialized AI agents (customer insights, keyword, creative design, A/B testing, bidding, and attribution) to generate, launch, and continuously optimize hundreds of personalized ad experiments across Google and LinkedIn. Founded by Matt Jayson (formerly Google and Brex) and Ashish Warty (formerly SVP Engineering at HackerOne, Dropbox, and Airship), Multiply emerged from stealth with $9.5M led by Mayfield and reports 300-500% increases in sales meetings booked and pipeline generated for its B2B customers.

providers.name: Kinside
providers.description: Kinside is a modern child care marketplace that connects families with licensed child care providers by surfacing real-time availability across thousands of providers, helping parents find care in minutes rather than months. Beyond the consumer marketplace, Kinside serves child care providers with enrollment and scheduling tools, employers with child care benefit programs, and government agencies seeking community child care supply-and-demand data. Backed by Initialized Capital and Techstars, the company operates alongside UrbanSitter in the family-care benefits space. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from venture-portfolio discovery; Kinside does not publish a public developer portal or API at this time, so this entry captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: Klippa
providers.description: Klippa is a document AI platform whose flagship product, DocHorizon (rebranded as Doxis AI.dp following the SER acquisition), provides OCR, document classification, conversion, verification, fraud detection and anonymization for 50+ document types. Klippa also publishes dedicated APIs for receipts, invoices, IDs/passports and expense management. EU-hosted, GDPR / ISO 27001 certified.

providers.name: LastPass
providers.description: LastPass is a password and identity-management platform offering personal and enterprise vaults, single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, and directory provisioning. The LastPass Enterprise API and Provisioning API let admins programmatically manage users, groups, shared folders, policies, and events. SCIM and SAML endpoints integrate with identity providers; an MFA SDK supports adaptive authentication for custom apps.

providers.name: Leflair
providers.description: Leflair is a Vietnamese online retail brand selling discounted authentic international brands across fashion and accessories, beauty and health, home and lifestyle, and children's products. Its own terms of service describe it as Vietnam's first members-only flash-sale platform, running daily promotional events on branded goods. The live storefront at leflair.com is operated by Cong ty TNHH Sopa Technology of Ho Chi Minh City on the Haravan commerce platform, and is supported by a Vietnamese-language editorial blog, an account/sign-in surface, and published terms, privacy, payment-security, shipping, and tax policy pages. Leflair is a consumer retail brand: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer portal, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API definition, and its historical leflair.vn domain no longer serves the storefront. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Lemonaide
providers.description: Lemonaide is a Bangkok-headquartered B2B used-car and insurtech platform operating across Southeast Asia, positioning itself as a technology and services layer that reduces asymmetric information in the automotive market. The company sells software to used-car dealerships and insurers, including a Dealer Management System, a Dealer CRM with microtargeting, and a Digital Escrow settlement product, alongside operated services such as after-sales BPO, warranty third-party administration, 24-hour digital roadside assistance, vehicle inspection, and repair-workshop audit assessment. Lemonaide states that more than 2,000 dealers use its platform and names Carro, Carsome, and Toyota Sure among its partners. It is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Lemonaide publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Lica
providers.description: Lica is an AI research company building a substrate to train and evaluate AI models to be capable design partners across expressions of taste and consumption. Its research spans spatial reasoning and composition, layout generation and editing, vector-graphics (SVG) understanding, personalization and brand identity, and animation generation. Lica publishes the LICA dataset of layered graphic-design compositions and GDB (Graphic Design Benchmark), a real-world benchmark that scores frontier models on designer workflows across layout, typography, infographics, template semantics and animation. The company is backed by Accel, South Park Commons and Village Global. As of July 2026 Lica ships no public API, developer portal or API reference; product access is an email waitlist and its public developer surface is the lica-world GitHub organization, including the first-party DesignMCP MCP server.

providers.name: Lightship
providers.description: Lightship is an American manufacturer of all-electric travel trailers, co-founded by former Tesla leaders Toby Kraus and Ben Parker, with design and manufacturing in Colorado and offices in San Francisco. Its flagship product, the AE.1, is marketed as the first mass-produced all-electric travel trailer, offering up to 77 kWh of battery capacity, 1.8 kW of integrated solar, and named technologies including TrekDrive self-propulsion, CampQuiet silent operation, and Aero-Electric Design. Owners control the trailer through an onboard Atlas tablet and companion mobile app. Lightship sells direct to consumer and states that more than 85% of its supply chain is in the United States. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-19 found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this is a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API listing.

providers.name: Linkett
providers.description: Linkett is a digital out-of-home (DOOH) analytics platform for digital signage and retail displays. A proprietary WiFi sensor mounted at the screen passively gathers audience data from nearby smartphones with no app required, and a hosted dashboard reports real-time campaign performance metrics such as impressions, dwell time, frequency and conversion rate, alongside demographic and behavioural insight, giving advertising agencies detailed client reporting and giving advertisers measurement they can tie back to return on ad spend. Linkett is a WestonExpressions Inc. company with offices in Toronto, Ontario and Mountain View, California, says it is used by 100+ digital out-of-home networks, and was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio. It sells self-serve at $25 and $50 per month plus a one-time $130 hardware fee, with custom integrations offered only on a contact-sales enterprise tier. As of this enrichment pass Linkett publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API specification on any host it controls, and its marketing site is served behind a bot/CAPTCHA challenge that blocks automated retrieval of every path.

providers.name: Metropolis Technologies
providers.description: Metropolis Technologies is an AI-powered recognition platform that uses computer vision to make real-world physical spaces responsive, best known as the largest U.S. parking operator with checkout-free parking across 4,200+ North American locations. Founded in 2017, the company powers what it calls the "Recognition Economy" — vehicles are recognized on entry and exit so members pay automatically without tickets, gates, or lines. Metropolis scaled through the acquisitions of Premier Parking (2022) and SP Plus Corporation (2024), raised $1.6 billion in financing in 2025, and was named a TIME100 Most Influential Company of 2026. It is backed by Dragoneer. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface has been identified; this profile captures the company's public identity and security/compliance posture.

providers.name: National Health Service
providers.description: The National Health Service (NHS) of England publishes a catalogue of APIs for health and care providers, including the Ambulance Data Submission FHIR API used to submit ambulance data to the NHS Data Processing Service (DPS) for analysis and review by NHS England and ambulance trusts.

providers.name: NewsData
providers.description: NewsData.io provides live breaking news and historical news data going back to January 2018, sourced from over 82,000 sources worldwide. The API supports searching, filtering by source, language, country, and category, and returns results in JSON format suitable for analytics, monitoring, and AI training.

providers.name: nsKnox
providers.description: nsKnox is an Israeli fintech-security company that protects business-to-business payments against fraud and misdirection for corporations and banks. Founded and led by Alon Cohen, the founder and former CEO of CyberArk, nsKnox built its platform on a patented Cooperative Cyber Security (CCS) architecture in which payment and bank-account data is shredded and distributed across multiple independent "Knoxer" systems so that no single breach reveals anything. Its PaymentKnox product line covers outgoing payments (accounts payable), incoming payments (accounts receivable), Bank Account Certificates, Master Data Guard, Payment Check, and an Adaptive Payment Security service that validates payee bank accounts worldwide using Quick Check in-network lookups and Knox Verify out-of-network mini-transactions against the banking system. Customers connect through a hosted portal, scheduled file transfer, or a direct ERP API integration with systems such as SAP and Oracle. nsKnox publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the API surface is documented to onboarded customers only.

providers.name: Offcall
providers.description: Offcall is a career and practice platform for physicians, backed by Bloomberg Beta. It provides confidential, anonymous physician salary and compensation benchmarking, and a verified clinician-to-clinician patient referrals network with HIPAA-compliant messaging for care coordination, delivered through web and mobile (iOS and Android) applications. Offcall does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; this profile was surfaced through the Bloomberg Beta portfolio and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals that are publicly available.

providers.name: Operator Framework
providers.description: The Operator Framework is a CNCF incubating toolkit for building and managing Kubernetes Operators. It includes the Operator SDK for scaffolding and building operators using Go, Ansible, or Helm, the Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) for installing and managing operators on clusters, and OperatorHub for discovering and sharing operators. The framework codifies operational knowledge into software.

providers.name: OSARO
providers.description: OSARO is a San Francisco-based industrial AI company that builds machine-learning software for warehouse and fulfillment robotics. Its SightWorks perception platform and AutoModel learning system let industrial robot arms perceive, grasp and place highly variable goods without per-SKU pre-training, 3D object models or fixed programming, powering piece picking, robotic bagging, kitting and mixed-case depalletizing in production deployments across five countries. OSARO sells complete robotic work cells and licenses its perception software to robot makers and system integrators, wrapping deployments in its HyperCare support program. The company publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; integration with customer estates (WMS/WCS, conveyors, ASRS, AMRs) is delivered as a professional-services engagement through OSARO and its integrator partners rather than through a self-serve API.

providers.name: PetSmart
providers.description: PetSmart is a North American chain of retail stores selling specialty pet supplies, services, and small companion animals. This repository tracks any publicly available APIs, SDKs, and developer resources for PetSmart.

providers.name: Pienso
providers.description: Pienso is an interactive no-code AI and machine learning platform, founded in 2016 out of MIT by Karthik Dinakar and Birago Jones and headquartered in the Washington, DC / Arlington, VA area. It lets subject-matter experts explore, train, fingerprint, annotate, and deploy deep-learning and large language models over unstructured text — customer calls, emails, documents, and social content — through a point-and-click interface with no coding required. Product capabilities include Ingest, Train & Fingerprint, Annotate, Dataset Analysis, and PromptFactory, applied to use cases such as customer insight, content moderation, document intelligence, and risk detection. Pienso is deployed into the customer's own environment — AWS, Azure, GCP, Gcore, or on-premises — so data never leaves the customer's control, and the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; integration is sales-led and the platform runs as a self-contained system. Backed by Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Prophet Security
providers.description: Prophet Security is a cybersecurity company building an agentic AI Security Operations Center (SOC) platform. Its product, Prophet AI, uses autonomous AI agents to automate alert triage, investigation, response, and threat hunting across the security operations lifecycle. The platform ingests from SIEMs, EDRs/XDRs, identity providers, cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), email and network security, threat intelligence, and case-management tools to deliver full-context investigations inside existing analyst workflows. Prophet Security is a Series A company founded in 2023, backed by Accel and Bain Capital Ventures. It is SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR aligned. Prophet does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or MCP server; integration is via read-only connections into a customer's own security tooling.

providers.name: Salient
providers.description: Salient (Skwid Inc.) is an AI-native loan servicing and collections platform for consumer lenders — banks, credit unions, captive lenders, and specialty finance companies. It builds compliance-first AI voice and chat agents that automate servicing, collections, audit, insurance claims, chargebacks, and chargeoff workflows with native FDCPA, TCPA, and CFPB compliance. Its named agent products include Taylor (omnichannel servicing and collections), Marshall (automated audit), Flyn (total-loss insurance claims), Alex (chargebacks and disputes), and Melanie (chargeoffs). Founded in 2023 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Matrix Partners, and Y Combinator, Salient exposes a partner integration and onboarding API behind an authenticated developer portal. This profile was enriched from public web surfaces; the API reference is gated behind login so no public machine-readable specification was harvested.

providers.name: Salt Labs
providers.description: Salt Labs is the New York company behind Salt, an employee rewards and loyalty benefit for hourly and frontline workers. Founded in 2022 by Jason Lee and founding members of DailyPay, Salt turns time worked into a points-based asset: an employee earns one Salt for every hour on the job through the Salt Rewards mobile app, and redeems accumulated Salt for merchandise, travel, experiences, education benefits, and investment products such as stock and treasury bonds. Salt is sold to employers across transportation, contact centers, hospitality, and parking services as a retention and engagement program modeled on airline miles and credit-card points. Salt Labs was acquired by Chime Financial in June 2024 and now operates as "Salt, a Chime Company", with founder Jason Lee leading the Chime Enterprise business unit. Salt Labs publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract; its only machine-readable first-party surface is the Atlassian Statuspage at status.saltlabs.com, which exposes public JSON and RSS availability feeds for the Salt App Backend.

providers.name: SRS Acquiom
providers.description: SRS Acquiom provides deal management solutions for mergers & acquisitions and loan agency transactions, operating across the entire deal lifecycle. Its services span pre-closing tax and accounting advisory, closing-phase escrow, payment disbursement and shareholder solicitation, and post-closing shareholder representation, alongside loan agency roles (administrative, collateral, and facility agent). SRS Acquiom delivers these through digital dashboards and platforms for deal transparency, backed by affiliate broker-dealer Acquiom Financial LLC (FINRA/SIPC). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently exposed.

providers.name: Sumeria
providers.description: Sumeria is a French fintech and mobile-first banking service created by Lydia Solutions in 2024 as a consumer spinoff of the Lydia payment app. It offers free online banking accounts with automatic expense categorization, thematic sub-accounts for budgeting and savings, virtual and physical debit cards with no foreign-exchange fees, an interest-bearing balance, and an AI assistant named Sia for account management and financial guidance. Sumeria is a business-to-consumer banking product; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time, so this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Sync API
providers.description: Sync API is an enterprise API platform for the in-app mobile advertising ecosystem, delivering performance, transparency, and control for marketers. The platform provides a bidder platform and suite of APIs for user acquisition, mobile user growth, and user re-engagement. It enables data-driven, ROI-focused mobile advertising across 1.2 billion global audiences in 50+ countries, with 500+ robust API integrations and advanced algorithms for LTV forecasting and in-app event conversion tracking.

providers.name: Terminal Logistics
providers.description: Terminal Industries (Terminal Logistics) is the company behind the Terminal Yard Operating System (YOS), an AI-native, fully-integrated platform for yard operations across logistics and supply chain.
