Dana's main public API surface is the Dana Aftermarket developer platform; this repository is an alias of the primary "dana" profile.

providers.name: Doctronic
providers.description: Doctronic is a consumer telemedicine platform that pairs an AI doctor with licensed physicians for anonymous, low-cost health care. Users describe their symptoms to an AI assistant that performs a free symptom assessment and health consultation, then can escalate to a real doctor for a video visit ($39/visit), prescription refills, lab orders, and follow-up care. Positioned as "Free. Anonymous. Built by doctors," the product is direct-to-consumer web and mobile rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation. The only public machine-readable surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt with a coordinated vulnerability-disclosure policy. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: doinstruct
providers.description: doinstruct is an AI-powered frontline training and compliance platform for deskless and shift-based workforces. Founded in Osnabrück, Germany in 2021 and now headquartered in Brooklyn, New York with an office in Berlin, it turns internal SOPs, documents, and expert knowledge into mobile-first courses delivered in 35+ languages. Its Genius AI authoring tool, a 400+ lesson training library, a manager dashboard for assigning and documenting training, and a mobile learner experience serve 400+ frontline teams across food & beverage, logistics, manufacturing, construction, and general compliance, with audit-ready reporting for standards such as HACCP, GFSI, and ISO 27001. Backed by Creandum and HV Capital.

providers.name: Earnin
providers.description: Earnin (formerly Activehours) is a consumer financial technology company offering earned wage access (EWA) that lets workers tap the pay they have already earned before their scheduled payday. Its mobile app products include Cash Out (access earned wages up to $150/day and $1,000/pay period with no mandatory fees), Live Pay and the EarnIn Card, Early Pay, Balance Shield overdraft protection, credit monitoring, FDIC-insured Savings Jars, and an EarnIn Payroll offering for businesses. Earnin is a consumer app rather than an API platform; it publishes no public developer portal or API, but does operate a vulnerability-disclosure program (security.txt via Inspectiv) and a trust center. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, Felicis, Matrix Partners, Ribbit Capital, and Trinity Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Equipmentwatch
providers.description: EquipmentWatch (a Fusable brand) provides construction and equipment data APIs that deliver rental rates, ownership costs, market values, and specifications for heavy equipment. Their data is used by contractors, equipment dealers, rental houses, and insurance professionals to make informed decisions about equipment valuation, procurement, and rental.

providers.name: Expedock
providers.description: Expedock is a digital business process outsourcing (BPO) and document-automation company for the logistics and freight-forwarding industry. It pairs AI-powered document automation products (FCL/LCL accounts-payable automation, monthly statement automation, and commercial invoice and packing-list data entry) with tech-enabled remote teams supported by operations managers and QA specialists. Freight forwarders, 3PLs, and supply-chain operators use Expedock to digitize shipping documents, automate back-office workflows, and scale operations without scaling headcount. Customers include Maersk, Gebrueder Weiss, and large shippers such as Nike, Adidas, Coca-Cola, and Shell. Expedock is backed by Insight Partners. The company operates a Digital BPO offering and document-automation product suite; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: F.N.B. Corporation
providers.description: F.N.B. Corporation (NYSE: FNB) is a diversified financial services holding company headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and the parent of First National Bank of Pennsylvania, an FDIC-insured, state-chartered commercial bank. With roughly $50 billion in total assets at year-end 2025, FNB is a regional super-community bank operating around 350 branches across seven states and Washington, D.C. (Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, West Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia), offering commercial banking, consumer banking and wealth management through its eStore digital platform. On open finance, FNB exposes NO first-party public developer portal or documented API: the developer/api subdomains of fnb-online.com redirect to the marketing homepage and no developer documentation is published. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), not a first-party FNB API. No direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership or public CFPB Section 1033 posture is documented by the institution as of this profile.

providers.name: Firstjob.me
providers.description: FirstJob (firstjob.me) is a Latin American employment platform founded in Chile in 2012 to improve working conditions for young professionals by connecting students and early-career candidates (0-2 years of experience) with entry-level jobs and internships at large employers. The platform lists 1,200+ active opportunities across engineering, administration, operations, and technology, maintains an employer directory, and runs networking events and webinars. It also operates related initiatives including Employers For Youth (EFY) and Best Internship Experiences (BIE) employer-ranking programs. FirstJob is a consumer-facing web platform used by more than 500,000 young professionals; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, SDKs, or a developer portal. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Freshop
providers.description: Freshop is an eCommerce platform purpose-built for grocery and specialty retail, now part of NCR Voyix. It powers branded online storefronts, mobile shopping, order fulfillment, pickup, and delivery for independent and regional grocers, and integrates third-party services for loyalty, coupons, email, SMS, and fulfillment. Freshop exposes a live REST API at api.freshop.com that serves store and product data to Freshop-powered storefronts and apps, authenticated with an application key (app_key) query-string parameter and versioned by a numeric path segment.

providers.name: Green Hills Software
providers.description: Green Hills Software is a privately held embedded software company founded in 1982 by Dan O'Dowd and Carl Rosenberg and headquartered in Santa Barbara, California. It builds safety- and security-certified real-time operating systems (INTEGRITY, INTEGRITY-178 tuMP, u-velOSity), embedded hypervisors (INTEGRITY Multivisor, u-visor), optimizing C/C++/Ada/Fortran compilers, the MULTI and AdaMULTI integrated development environments, the TimeMachine back-in-time debug suite, the DoubleCheck static analyzer, the Green Hills Probe hardware debugger, and networking, file-system and USB middleware. Its customers ship these components inside aerospace, defense, automotive, medical, industrial, rail, telecommunications and consumer devices. Green Hills is a toolchain and operating-system vendor rather than an API provider: the programmable interfaces it ships are in-product C/C++, POSIX and MULTI-Python scripting APIs delivered with a licensed installation and documented in manuals distributed with the product, and its technical support portal at support.ghs.com requires an account. No public web API, developer portal, or machine-readable API description was found on any Green Hills host during enrichment.

providers.name: Grover
providers.description: Grover is a Berlin-based consumer technology rental and subscription company that lets people rent smartphones, laptops, gaming consoles, cameras, smart home devices, and audio gear on flexible monthly plans ranging from one to twenty-four-plus months. With more than 500,000 active renters across the United States, Germany, Austria, Spain, and the Netherlands, Grover positions flexible tech access as a circular, subscription-based alternative to ownership, refurbishing and recirculating returned devices for resale. Grover is a consumer-facing service and does not currently publish a public developer portal or API; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Growatt
providers.description: Growatt New Energy is a global manufacturer of solar PV inverters, energy storage systems, and smart energy management products for residential, commercial, and utility-scale installations. Growatt operates the ShineServer / ShinePhone cloud monitoring platform and publishes a token-authenticated Open API (V1) that lets third-party systems read plant and device telemetry, retrieve historical energy data, and read or write inverter parameters for MIN (TLX) string inverters and SPH (MIX) hybrid inverters across regional endpoints. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; enriched from Growatt's public developer surface.

providers.name: HAAS Alert
providers.description: HAAS Alert operates Safety Cloud, a connected-vehicle safety platform that delivers real-time digital alerts to nearby motorists about active emergency responses, roadside hazards, work zones, stopped vehicles, and slow-moving equipment. Using vehicle-to-everything (V2X) and cellular messaging, Safety Cloud gives drivers up to roughly 30 seconds of advance warning to help reduce collisions with first responders, tow operators, and roadway workers. HAAS Alert integrates with telematics platforms, fleet manufacturers, OEM vehicles, in-car navigation (including Waze), and roadway infrastructure to form a large connected-vehicle alerting ecosystem. The company is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from HAAS Alert's public web surface; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs were found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Heartbeat Health
providers.description: Heartbeat Health is a New York-based modern cardiology practice delivering remote and virtual cardiovascular care. The company combines early detection, home-based cardiac diagnostics, remote patient monitoring, risk stratification and evidence-based care coordination to proactively identify, treat and manage moderate-to-high cardiovascular risk. It serves hospitals and health systems, payors and employer groups, providers and ACOs, and in-home care providers, reporting outcomes such as 90%+ of patients reaching target blood pressure and a 53% reduction in cardiac readmissions. Backed by Optum Ventures, DaVita Venture Group and Echo Health Ventures, it is a care-delivery organization rather than a public API provider; no developer portal, API documentation, or public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Hippocratic AI
providers.description: Hippocratic AI builds safety-focused generative AI agents for non-diagnostic healthcare tasks, powered by its Polaris constellation architecture. Polaris 5.0 is a multi-trillion-parameter constellation of specialized models clinically validated by U.S.-licensed clinicians. Hippocratic AI sells agents such as Nurse Co-Pilot and AI Front Door to health systems, payors, and life-sciences organizations through enterprise sales rather than a self-service public API.

providers.name: Hometap
providers.description: Hometap is a Boston-based fintech founded in 2017 that offers homeowners a home equity investment (HEI) — an alternative to home equity loans and HELOCs. In exchange for a share of a home's future value, homeowners receive cash up front with no monthly payments, no interest, and no income or debt-to-income requirements, settling any time within a 10-year term via sale, refinance, or buyout. Homeowners manage their investment and track equity through the free Hometap Home Equity Dashboard. The company has helped more than 26,000 homeowners and completed over $1 billion in investments, and is backed by investors including General Catalyst. Hometap does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its public web properties and identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hrmony
providers.description: Hrmony is a Berlin-based employee-benefits platform that lets German employers offer modern, tax-advantaged perks to their staff — meal allowances (Essenszuschuss), the 50 euro monthly non-cash benefit (Sachbezug) and benefit card, mobility and public-transit budgets, health and recreation benefits, internet-cost subsidies and digital gifts — all managed through an admin portal and employee app with built-in payroll and tax compliance. Its Hrmony Embedded product exposes this benefits infrastructure as a white-label RESTful API so software platforms and SaaS providers can integrate multiple benefit modules without building the tax-compliance, operations or regulatory layer in-house. Hrmony is backed by Techstars. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; no public developer documentation or OpenAPI is currently published (Embedded onboarding is partner-gated).

providers.name: IronPlanet
providers.description: IronPlanet is an online marketplace for buying and selling used heavy construction equipment and trucks across categories including construction, trucks, agriculture, mining, forestry, and oil and gas. The platform offers online auctions, buy-now listings, make-an-offer, sealed auctions, and on-site auctions, with detailed third-party inspection reports backed by its IronClad Assurance certification program. IronPlanet operates regional marketplaces for North America, Europe/Middle East, and Asia-Pacific and is part of the Ritchie Bros. (RB Global) family of businesses. This company was surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: iTrustCapital
providers.description: iTrustCapital (legal entity ITC2.0, Inc.) is a US fintech software platform for alternative assets, offering 24/7 self-directed access to dozens of cryptocurrencies and physical precious metals through three account types: tax-advantaged self-directed Crypto IRAs for retirement savings, Premium Custody Accounts (PCA) for everyday non-retirement investing, and Treasury Accounts for businesses, trusts, non-profits and other entities. The platform charges a 1% cryptocurrency transaction fee with no monthly, annual, startup, exit, storage or transfer fees, and runs a closed-loop system backed by third-party US banks, custodians (iTrust Custodial Services, Fortis Bank) and institutional storage providers. iTrustCapital is not an exchange, custodian, trust company, broker-dealer or investment adviser; all transactions on the platform are self-directed. As of this profiling pass the company publishes NO public developer API — its own help center states that it "does not offer any API integration to any third-party applications, including self-trading bots and coin trackers." Access is via the web app and the iOS/Android mobile apps only.

providers.name: Ivanti
providers.description: Ivanti is an IT asset management and security platform providing unified endpoint management, patch management, and IT service management. The Ivanti Neurons product family exposes REST APIs across People & Devices, MDM, ITSM, and Zero-Trust Access, alongside Endpoint Manager APIs for patch and software distribution.

providers.name: Jinx
providers.description: Jinx is a direct-to-consumer pet nutrition brand selling premium dog and cat food, toppers, and treats at thinkjinx.com. Its product lines span dry kibble, wet food (pate, stews, homestyle), fresh refrigerated meals, jerky and training treats, and meal toppers, formulated with high-quality proteins, probiotics, and superfoods. Backed by Initialized Capital, Jinx sells online and through retail partners. The storefront runs on Shopify; it exposes no first-party public developer API, but the store's Shopify Customer Account API OIDC/OAuth discovery is served live from the domain and is captured in this profile.

providers.name: Joyful
providers.description: Joyful Health provides AI-assisted revenue recovery for healthcare organizations, combining automated claim investigation with expert billing teams to recover unpaid and denied insurance claims. Its platform runs inside an organization's existing revenue-cycle-management (RCM) systems rather than replacing them, covering denial investigation and root-cause analysis, claims recovery and appeals management, historical accounts-receivable (A/R) assessment, payer follow-up, documentation review, and financial insight to prevent future denials. The company operates a customer application at app.joyfulhealth.io and maintains a Vanta-hosted trust center. Joyful is a portfolio company of CRV. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; Joyful does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: JSW One
providers.description: JSW One Platforms is the digital B2B arm of India's JSW Group, operating a full-stack e-commerce and services platform for the country's manufacturing and construction MSMEs. It runs four connected businesses on one technology stack: JSW One Commerce (jswonemsme.com), a multi-brand marketplace for TMT bars, mild/hot-rolled/cold-rolled and structural steel, coated steel, wire rods, cement and bitumen sourced from certified mills; JSW One Homes (jswonehomes.com), a turnkey home-construction service with digital project tracking across fifteen Indian cities; JSW One Finance, the NBFC arm providing digital credit lines, channel financing and invoice factoring to MSMEs and retailers; and private brands JSW One TMT and One Helix. The platform reported FY25 gross merchandise value of INR 12,567 crore across more than 84,000 registered MSMEs, and raised INR 575 crore in a 2025 round led by the State Bank of India. JSW One publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; its customer-facing surfaces are the web marketplace and the JSW One MSME mobile apps. It does publish a maintained llms.txt on both of its consumer properties, plus an explicit AI/LLM bot-access policy on JSW One Homes.

providers.name: Kibin
providers.description: Kibin is a consumer study and academic-writing company operating at kibin.com, trusted by students since 2011. Its newest product is an AI-powered study partner (iOS app) that turns lectures, notes, PDFs, and YouTube videos into personalized study guides, quizzes, flashcards, transcripts, and explanations to help students learn faster and build mastery. Alongside the study app, Kibin also runs its long-standing academic-writing surface — professional essay editing, a paper grader, a thesis-statement generator, essay examples, and a writing blog. Kibin is a B2C, mobile- and web-delivered product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: LIQUiDITY Group
providers.description: LIQUiDITY Group (branded simply "Liquidity") is an AI-native private credit lender and alternative asset manager founded in 2018, headquartered in New York with offices in Tel Aviv, London, Singapore, Tokyo and Abu Dhabi. It underwrites and deploys non-dilutive debt and growth capital — typically $10M to $200M — to late-stage technology and mid-market companies across 35+ countries, using its proprietary DYNAMiCs decision-science platform to compress due diligence from months to days. The firm manages several billion dollars across multiple debt and equity funds, including Mars Growth Capital, a joint venture with MUFG Bank, and is backed by MUFG, Apollo Asset Management, Spark Capital and Meitav Dash. Liquidity is a lender that runs on software rather than a software vendor: its DYNAMiCs platform is operated for its own analysts, borrowers and fund investors at app.liquiditygroup.com and is not offered as a public developer product. No public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/GraphQL schema, SDK or machine-readable contract is published on any host the company controls.

providers.name: Lucem Health
providers.description: Lucem Health is a clinical-AI company founded in 2021 with Mayo Clinic Platform, backed by Mayo Clinic, Commure and Rally Ventures. Its Lucem Health Reveal programs apply clinically validated AI models to a health system's existing data to surface patients at elevated risk of serious or chronic disease — arrhythmias, colorectal cancer, liver disease, lung cancer and Type 1 diabetes — and deliver those insights into existing clinical workflows without changing how clinicians practice. The company also runs a Clinical AI SolutionOps practice that helps AI innovators and life-sciences organizations deploy, scale and commercialize models against provider data. Integration is delivered as a managed service into EHR, PACS and other clinical systems; as of 2026-08-25 Lucem Health publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Manara
providers.description: Manara is an upskilling and professional development platform focused on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, specializing in training for emerging technologies including AI and cloud computing. It runs enterprise workforce-development programs, national government training initiatives, and individual learning and certification courses, connecting a community of MENA software engineers and technologists with global career opportunities. The company reports 300,000+ learners trained, 2,500+ certifications awarded, operations across 40+ countries, and 500+ job placements. Manara publishes no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Marcopolo Learning
providers.description: MarcoPolo Learning is an award-winning early childhood education technology company, founded in 2013, that builds premium video content, instructional support, and learning apps for preschool and kindergarten. Its products include MarcoPolo For Educators (curriculum-aligned classroom video and educator guides), MarcoPolo For Families (Emmy-nominated videos plus literacy and math games), MarcoPolo World School (kindergarten readiness), MarcoPolo Professional Development for teachers, and The Polos animated series. The company was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass MarcoPolo Learning publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable developer surface; it is a consumer/educator app business, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Modern Fertility
providers.description: Modern Fertility is a women's health company offering at-home fertility and hormone testing along with pregnancy, ovulation and prenatal products. Its flagship Modern Fertility Hormone Test lets people measure reproductive hormones from home and review results with providers. The company was acquired by telehealth provider Ro and is now operated as part of Ro: modernfertility.com redirects to ro.co/fertility and the brand's products, accounts, legal terms and security program are served under the parent Ro platform. Modern Fertility exposes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a consumer health brand within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: myLaurel
providers.description: myLaurel is a New York-based healthcare company delivering acute and transitional care in patients' homes. Its hybrid model pairs hands-on clinical teams with virtual technology support to prevent unnecessary hospitalizations, free critical hospital bed space, improve patient outcomes, and lower the total cost of care for both health systems and health plans. Reported results include a 49% reduction in 30-day readmissions, an average 1.5-day length-of-stay reduction, a 97 Net Promoter Score, and 3:1+ ROI within 90 days. myLaurel is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). This profile has been enriched from the company's public web surface; it currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Nile
providers.description: Nile is a San Jose, California enterprise networking company delivering an AI-native Secure Network as a Service (NaaS). Founded in 2018 by former Cisco executives Pankaj Patel and John Chambers (chairman), Nile replaces traditional campus and branch LAN/Wi-Fi hardware-and-license procurement with a subscription-based, outcome-guaranteed wired and wireless network stack delivered as a service. The Nile Access Service combines its purpose-built Zero Trust Fabric (switches, access points, gateways, and sensors) with cloud-based autonomous operations, the Nile Services Cloud, Nile AI, Nile Nav, and Nile Digital Twin to plan, deploy, monitor, and self-heal enterprise networks. The platform emphasizes built-in Zero Trust segmentation, continuous performance guarantees (coverage, capacity, availability), and consumption-based pricing — marketed against 60%+ breach reduction, 99%+ ticket reduction, ~3x faster change management, and ~40% TCO savings versus traditional enterprise networking. Nile does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or Terraform provider; its programmable surface is limited to a closed admin/portal API and outbound webhooks used for documented integrations with ServiceNow (ticket and alert webhooks), Splunk HEC, CrowdStrike, Zscaler ZIA, Microsoft Entra (SCIM), Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Global Secure Access, Palo Alto Networks, Forescout (device inventory API), SecureW2, Aruba ClearPass, VeloCloud, Graphiant, Hamina, and Ekahau. Nile is available through the AWS Marketplace as a SaaS subscription.

providers.name: Novel Effect
providers.description: Novel Effect is a Techstars-backed interactive read-aloud technology company whose voice-recognition platform listens as a person reads a children's picture book aloud and plays perfectly synchronized music, sound effects, and character voices in response, turning any book into an immersive shared experience. Delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps, Novel Effect is used by families, teachers, and libraries to make reading aloud more engaging for young children. Novel Effect is a consumer and education (EdTech) product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: OpenChain
providers.description: OpenChain is an international standard (ISO/IEC 5230) under the Linux Foundation for open source license compliance programs. It helps organizations manage open source licensing consistently by providing a benchmark for trust between organizations in the software supply chain.

providers.name: Orbital Materials
providers.description: Orbital Materials (rebranded Orbital Industries in 2026) is an AI industrial company founded in 2022 by Jonathan Godwin, a former DeepMind researcher, with offices in London and San Francisco. It applies frontier AI to the discovery, testing and deployment of advanced materials and to the hardware and manufacturing built around them, co-designing materials and hardware together rather than sequentially. Its public technical output is a family of open-source machine-learned interatomic potentials — the Orb, Orb-v2/v3 and OrbMol foundation models for atomic simulation — distributed as the Apache-2.0 licensed `orb-models` Python package on PyPI and GitHub and as model weights on Hugging Face. Its internal platform, CurieOS, and its Orbital IT data-center module business are marketed through a contact form rather than a developer program. The company publishes no public HTTP API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Peace Corps
providers.description: The Peace Corps is a U.S. government agency that sends American volunteers abroad to work with communities on development projects. They provide data APIs for accessing Peace Corps volunteer data, country information, and project statistics.

providers.name: Pebblely
providers.description: Pebblely creates AI product photos that help you sell more. No Photoshop skills required. The Pebblely API allows programmatic access to AI-powered product photography generation, background creation, and image styling.

providers.name: Pharmeasy
providers.description: PharmEasy is one of India's largest digital healthcare platforms, operating a consumer online pharmacy and health marketplace at pharmeasy.in. It lets users order prescription and over-the-counter medicines (with prescription upload and verification), buy health and wellness products, book diagnostic lab tests and health checkup packages, and consult doctors via telemedicine, plus a PLUS subscription for recurring savings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Prosus Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. PharmEasy runs an internal API at api.pharmeasy.in but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI; it does operate a responsible-disclosure security program (infosec@pharmeasy.in). Sector: healthcare / e-pharmacy.

providers.name: Playbite
providers.description: Playbite is a free mobile arcade app - "an arcade in your pocket" - built by Digital Media Technology SL and backed by 500 Global. The app offers an ever-expanding library of simple, casual games spanning multiplayer, rhythm, puzzle, matching, relaxing, and racing categories, with over 500,000 players who play games and earn rewards. The service is free to users and monetized through non-intrusive advertising. Playbite is a consumer-facing mobile gaming product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures its company identity, public web properties, and domain security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: PocketHealth
providers.description: PocketHealth is a patient-centric medical imaging platform that lets patients access, view, store, and share their diagnostic imaging (DICOM) and reports online, and lets healthcare providers exchange imaging across institutions and networks. PocketHealth also publishes an open, RESTful developer API aimed at RIS/PACS/VNA vendors, letting them embed PocketHealth's patient enrollment, electronic consent, and background record-delivery workflows natively into their own clinical software. The developer API is partner-gated - it is free forever for RIS/PACS vendors, healthcare providers, and physicians, but the full technical reference (base URL, endpoint paths, authentication) is not published on the open web; engaged vendors are assigned a dedicated integration rep who provides testing resources and detailed documentation. As a result the APIs below are modeled from PocketHealth's public developer-program descriptions rather than a public API reference or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: Polaron
providers.description: Polaron is a London-based AI software company that builds "the intelligence layer for materials science." Its platform applies machine learning to microscopy and image data to automate microstructure analysis, connecting process, structure, and performance so materials engineering teams can characterise, design, and manufacture materials faster and with less uncertainty. The platform centers on three core model families: Segmentation (identifying and measuring microstructural features), Reconstruction (converting 2D micrographs into 3D representations), and Design (optimising microstructural parameters). It is applied across batteries, metals and alloys, composites, ceramics, additive manufacturing, and pharmaceuticals, spanning R&D, quality and qualification, and modelling and simulation workflows. Polaron is backed by Speedinvest and research institutions including Imperial College London, Manchester, Oxford, and Cambridge.

providers.name: QiDZ Holding
providers.description: QiDZ Holding operates theQapp (formerly QiDZ), a consumer mobile platform that helps families discover, compare, and book activities, entertainment, and dining experiences across the United Arab Emirates and the wider Middle East (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh, Jeddah, Eastern Province, Manama, and Cairo). The app curates theme parks, water parks, indoor play areas, sports and creative classes, kid-friendly restaurants, camps, staycations, museums, and birthday and event packages, and offers a Q-Club membership with exclusive promo codes and discounts. Backed by 500 Global, QiDZ is a B2C mobile experience distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine specification, so this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Qventus
providers.description: Qventus is a healthcare technology company that provides an AI-powered automation platform for hospital operations. Its "AI teammates" combine machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science to streamline care-coordination workflows across surgical growth and operating-room utilization, perioperative and pre-admission-testing coordination, inpatient capacity and discharge planning, and care-gap and coding automation. Qventus sells to health systems and hospitals as a B2B SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Mayfield, Norwest Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Riff
providers.description: Riff is an Oslo, Norway based enterprise software company building AI agents for supply chain, procurement, planning, and logistics operations. Its agents automate repetitive back-office work such as chasing supplier order confirmations, updating order and delivery status, matching invoices, and monitoring deliveries, while keeping actions deterministic, auditable, and team-controlled rather than purely generative. Riff integrates non-disruptively with existing ERP systems including SAP, Oracle, Infor, and Microsoft, is EU-based with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 aligned and GDPR compliant data handling, and was founded by veterans of Cognite. The company raised a $16M Series A backed by Northzone and other investors. Riff has no public developer or API program at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Sally Beauty Holdings
providers.description: Sally Beauty Holdings, Inc. is a leading international specialty retailer and distributor of professional beauty supplies. Operates through two segments: Sally Beauty Supply (consumer-facing beauty retail) and Beauty Systems Group (BSG, professional-only distribution). The company serves salon professionals, colorists, and beauty enthusiasts with over 4,800 stores globally.

providers.name: Sirius
providers.description: beSirius is an Amsterdam-based AI platform for the critical minerals and metals value chain. It builds a continuously verified digital Twin of every supplier, mapping each company's data to the frameworks, questionnaires, and regulations its buyers, auditors, and regulators require - including CSDDD, CMRT/EMRT/AMRT conflict-minerals reporting, EcoVadis, CDP, S&P CSA, UN Global Compact, LME Passport, and the Consolidated Mining Standard Initiative (CMSI). The platform automates supplier due diligence, sustainability and ESG data collection and verification, certification readiness, customer KYC, and ratings improvement across mining, processing, and trading supply chains, reducing manual audit and disclosure effort. beSirius is backed by Techstars and other investors.

providers.name: Solventum
providers.description: Solventum is a Fortune 500 healthcare company spun off from 3M in 2024, focused on healthcare technology including medical-surgical solutions, dental and orthodontic products, health information systems, and purification and filtration technologies. Solventum serves hospitals, clinics, dental practices, and healthcare IT organizations worldwide.

providers.name: SplashLearn
providers.description: SplashLearn (operated by StudyPad, Inc.) is a game-based learning platform offering math and English/ELA curriculum for preschool through Grade 5 students, used by parents, teachers, schools, and homeschoolers. It delivers interactive games, worksheets, lesson plans, and progress tracking across web and mobile (iOS/Android) apps, plus homeschool, summer-learning, and SpringBoard programs. Surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and public web/security surface.

providers.name: Tass Vision
providers.description: Tass Vision is a venture-backed technology startup that operates a product website at tassvision.ai. It markets two named products, SITRAC and VITRAC, each with its own product page and pricing page, alongside About, How It Works, Blog, Calendar, and Contact sections. The public site is a Vue single-page web application with Zendesk-based customer support. The company is backed by 500 Global and Big Sky Capital among a cluster of Central Asian venture funds and accelerators (IT Park Uzbekistan, Astana Hub, National UzVC, and others). As of this profiling the company exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Terra
providers.description: Terra Security operates an agentic-AI-powered continuous offensive security (penetration testing) platform. Founded in 2024 and based in Tel Aviv, Terra runs a swarm of AI agents with a human-on-the-loop workflow that continuously validates every attack surface — web and internal applications, external and internal networks, and AI systems such as LLMs, copilots, MCP servers, and autonomous agents (AI red teaming). The platform compresses multi-week legacy pentests into hours, produces verified (low-noise) findings, and generates audit-ready evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA programs. Terra raised a $30M Series A led by Felicis in 2025. Terra publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web surface and security posture.

providers.name: The Learning Experience
providers.description: The Learning Experience is an early childhood education and childcare franchise operating academies of early education for children from six weeks to six years old across a nationwide network of centers. Its programs span infant, toddler, preschool, and pre-kindergarten care built on a proprietary curriculum. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer-facing childcare operator it publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain security posture.

providers.name: TOCA Football
providers.description: TOCA Football, Inc. is a technology-enabled soccer experience and entertainment company headquartered in Costa Mesa, California, founded on the training methodology of former US international and Premier League player Eddie Lewis. It operates two businesses: TOCA Soccer, a network of indoor soccer training centers across the United States, Canada and Mexico offering private training, classes, clinics, camps, youth and adult leagues, tournaments and pickup play; and TOCA Social, a soccer-themed dining and entertainment venue brand. Its training centers pair a proprietary ball-delivery machine and digitalized smart targets with the MyTOCA player app, which tracks session performance, player cards, leaderboards and progress. TOCA is the official soccer training partner of Major League Soccer. TOCA publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer program: its software ships only as end-user consumer apps and in-venue systems.

providers.name: Truemeds
providers.description: Truemeds is an India-based online pharmacy and digital healthcare platform operated by Intellihealth Solutions that lets consumers order branded and generic prescription and over-the-counter medicines for home delivery across India, typically positioned around savings on genuine medicines, free teleconsultation with doctors, and substitute-medicine recommendations. It runs a consumer web and mobile app experience (order medicines, upload prescriptions, health blog, help center) rather than a public developer API program; no public API documentation, developer portal, OpenAPI, or partner API surface was found during enrichment. Backed by Accel and other investors, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: UBIO Automation Cloud
providers.description: UBIO (ubio.ai, formerly ub.io) is a London-based, Techstars-backed web automation company. Its Automation Cloud platform runs automation scripts as jobs through a REST API, automating end-to-end website flows such as flight and hotel booking, broadband signup, insurance quotes, and job applications. Developers create jobs with inputs, receive outputs and lifecycle events, and handle deferred inputs and 3-D Secure through official JavaScript/TypeScript client libraries, with the ubio Automation Protocol defining typed input/output schemas for more than 50 automation domains.

providers.name: Upwave
providers.description: Upwave (formerly Survata) is the Brand Outcomes Measurement Platform — it brings science to top-of-funnel advertising by measuring Brand Lift, validating Brand Reach, and surfacing optimization insights for brand campaigns across CTV, digital, linear TV, audio, and social channels. Advertisers, agencies, and media platforms use Upwave dashboards and its Bayes AI layer to quantify how campaigns move awareness, favorability, consideration, and intent. Upwave is delivered as a SaaS application with a managed partner ecosystem of ad servers and DSPs, and does not publish a public developer portal or API documentation. It is a portfolio company of Y Combinator, Uncork Capital, and Initialized Capital.

providers.name: Vastu Housing Finance Corporation
providers.description: Vastu Housing Finance Corporation Limited (Vastu HFC) is an Indian, technology-enabled affordable housing finance company backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It provides home purchase, construction, extension, and improvement loans, plot-plus-construction loans, commercial property loans, and loans against property through 200+ branches across 17 states, serving 1.6+ million customers, and participates in government subsidy schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Urban 2.0. Vehicle, business, and construction-equipment lending is offered through its subsidiary Vastu Finserve. The company operates as a digital-first lender with a customer mobile app, but publishes no public developer portal or API surface.

providers.name: Whip Media Group
providers.description: Whip Media is a SaaS company powering the global media and entertainment industry through its AI-native Helix platform, which connects content licensors and licensees across the rights-to-royalties value chain. Helix spans supply-chain modules for licensees (avails management, contract management, royalties processing) and distribution modules for licensors (asset order management, performance tracking, revenue recognition), plus AI-powered Title Management for metadata enrichment and standardization. Customers include NBCU, Warner Bros. Discovery, Paramount, Sony, and Lionsgate. The company publishes an SEO llms.txt and reports SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II audits for a sixth consecutive year, but does not expose a public developer portal or documented API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IVP.

providers.name: YAZIO
providers.description: YAZIO GmbH is an Erfurt, Germany based digital health company whose nutrition app pairs calorie and macro tracking with barcode scanning, AI photo food logging, an intermittent-fasting timer, a 3,000-recipe library and body-metric tracking across iOS, Android and the web. The company describes itself as remote-first, cites more than 100 million downloads across over 150 countries, and sells a freemium product: a free tier plus a "YAZIO PRO" subscription transacted through the Apple App Store and Google Play rather than through a pricing page on yazio.com. YAZIO publishes no developer program of any kind — no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or GraphQL contract, no SDKs, no CLI, no MCP server, no changelog, no status page and no security.txt. Its apps talk to a private backend at https://yzapi.yazio.com, which is live but answers 401 with an empty body to anonymous requests and issues OAuth client credentials through no public process. Every YAZIO OpenAPI description, client library and MCP server in circulation is third-party reverse-engineering that states in its own README that it is unofficial and unaffiliated.

providers.name: Adient
providers.description: Adient is a global automotive seating supplier headquartered in Plymouth, Michigan. Spun off from Johnson Controls in 2016, Adient designs and manufactures seating systems for global automakers across passenger and commercial vehicles.

providers.name: AdStage.io
providers.description: AdStage was a cross-network advertising management, reporting, and automation platform (a 500 Startups / 500 Global portfolio company, founded 2013) that let marketers pull normalized advertising data from Google Ads, Microsoft/Bing Ads, Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, Pinterest, Amazon, Google Analytics and more through a single unified interface. Its AdStage Data API (v1 and v2, HAL+JSON over HTTP with bearer-token / OAuth 2 auth) exposed user, organization, and advertising-entity data plus customizable cross-network reports. AdStage was acquired by TapClicks in April 2020 and folded into TapClicks' Marketing Intelligence platform; the standalone AdStage Data API (platform.adstage.io) is now defunct, though the AdStage GitHub organization and its API Blueprint documentation remain public. The adstage.io domain now serves unrelated PPC/advertising content under new ownership.

providers.name: Ali Tech
providers.description: Ali Tech (operating as Xaim) is an AI infrastructure platform that gives startups and AI-driven businesses affordable, predictable compute for running AI workloads. Instead of token-based pricing, Xaim sells reserved processing capacity so teams can reduce processing costs without modifying their existing AI models. The platform is delivered as APIs through an Azure API Management developer portal, and advertises three products - a Compute API for running existing AI models cost effectively, an Insights API for real-time performance-optimization signals, and an Automation API for automating and scaling AI processes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Astronergy
providers.description: Astronergy (Chint New Energy Technology Co., Ltd.) is the photovoltaic cell and module manufacturing arm of China's CHINT Group. Founded in 2006, it is one of the earliest private Chinese enterprises in the PV sector and is ranked among the world's largest module suppliers. It designs, manufactures and sells high-efficiency crystalline-silicon PV cells and modules — notably the n-type TOPCon ASTRO N series in bifacial and monofacial form — for utility-scale power stations, commercial and industrial rooftops, and residential systems. Astronergy sells into more than 140 countries and regions and operates manufacturing bases and sales centers in markets including Germany, Spain, the USA, Brazil and Turkey. Its public web surface is a marketing and product-download site: datasheets, installation manuals, warranty and certification PDFs, a module-authenticity checker and a PV Planner yield calculator. It publishes no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Atari
providers.description: Atari is one of the founding brands of the interactive entertainment industry, originally established in 1972, and today operates as a global video game and consumer-hardware company. It publishes classic and modern titles, manufactures the Atari VCS console and retro hardware (Atari 2600+, Atari 400 Mini), licenses its catalog and brand, and sells games, collectibles, and merchandise through its official online store at atari.com. Atari does not publish a general-purpose public REST API; its developer surface is limited to Atari VCS content-submission guidance (developers email vcs@atari.com and use the VCS submission portal) and legacy HTML5 Atari Arcade SDK libraries on GitHub. This profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company — a nod to Mayfield's foundational 1970s venture investment in Atari — and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Boardable
providers.description: Boardable is board management software for nonprofits, associations, foundations, and other mission-driven organizations, covering meeting scheduling, agenda building, a document center, minutes and AI-generated meeting summaries, e-voting, task assignments, groups/committees, member directories, and built-in video conferencing. As of this review Boardable does NOT publish a documented public developer API: there is no developer portal, no published API reference, no OpenAPI, no self-serve API keys, and no documented webhooks. A private, authentication-gated backend API exists at https://api.boardable.com (for example, GET https://api.boardable.com/accounts returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized) that powers the Boardable web and mobile apps, but it is undocumented and not offered as a public/partner integration surface. Third-party listings occasionally describe Boardable as having an "open API," but Boardable provides no public developer documentation to substantiate that. Integrations are delivered through pre-built connectors (Salesforce, Microsoft 365 / Teams / Outlook / SharePoint / OneDrive, Google Drive & Calendar, Zoom, Dropbox, LinkedIn) rather than a documented API. This entry is therefore an honest stub: no APIs are listed because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: Bristle
providers.description: Bristle (Bristle Health) is a consumer health company that makes the world's first at-home oral microbiome saliva test, helping people measure, understand, and improve their oral health. Customers order a mail-in saliva collection kit, and Bristle sequences the oral microbiome to report on bacteria associated with cavities, gum disease, and bad breath, then pairs the results with guidance and a line of targeted oral-care products including probiotics. Bristle also works with dental professionals who offer microbiome testing to their patients. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted storefront at bristlehealth.com and is backed by Initialized Capital. There is no first-party public developer API; this profile captures Bristle's public web, commercial, and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Calo
providers.description: Calo is a food-tech company founded in Bahrain in 2019 that operates a personalized meal-subscription and delivery service. Nutritionist-designed, chef-prepared meals are portioned to each customer's health goals and lifestyle, with 80+ new meal options rotated weekly and flexible pause/cancel anytime. Built by chefs, nutritionists, and software engineers around proprietary nutritional algorithms, Calo has expanded to seven markets across the GCC and beyond (Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, and Oman), ordered through its consumer apps. Calo is backed by 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API or documented client SDKs.

providers.name: Cambly
providers.description: Cambly is an online English-language learning platform, founded in 2012 and based in San Francisco, that connects English learners in more than 190 countries with native-speaking tutors over on-demand video chat. Its consumer products include Cambly (adult learners), Cambly Kids (ages 4-15), Cambly Pro, and Cambly for Organizations/Business. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, and Y Combinator, the company operates a marketplace connecting students and tutors with weekly payouts. Cambly does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures its public company surface, GitHub organization, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Clear Ballot
providers.description: Clear Ballot Group, Inc. is an election technology company that builds transparent, verifiable voting systems for election administrators across the United States. Its flagship ClearVote platform spans vote-by-mail processing, in-person voting, ballot design, and independent post-election audit and results-verification software, alongside offerings for ranked-choice voting and elections-as-a-service. Clear Ballot operates as a closed, certified election-systems vendor rather than a public API platform, so this profile is identity- and security-focused: it captures the company's public web presence, domain-security posture, and its published vulnerability-disclosure program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Countable
providers.description: Countable was a civic-engagement technology company backed by Canaan Partners (seed, partner Joydeep Bhattacharyya) that built a digital platform helping citizens understand what Congress was doing in Washington and contact their elected representatives directly, later extending the same advocacy tooling to organizations and brands. As of this enrichment pass the Countable brand is no longer operating independently: both countable.com and countable.us HTTP 302 to https://www.myactionable.com/, the home of Actionable, a self-service advocacy campaign platform made by CSAG that offers petitions, pledges, lawmaker-message campaigns, supporter video collection, lead capture, polling and in-platform real-time campaign reporting on a $29.99/month self-service plan. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDK, package, webhook catalog, MCP server or /.well-known discovery surface was found on either the legacy Countable hosts or the successor Actionable host during this pass.

providers.name: Curve Dental
providers.description: Curve Dental is a cloud-based, all-in-one dental practice management software company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Alpharetta, Georgia. Its flagship platform, Curve Hero, serves more than 80,000 dental professionals across the United States and Canada, unifying scheduling, clinical and perio charting, imaging, billing, insurance, smart forms, reporting, patient engagement, and business analytics in a single browser-based system. Curve is privately held and backed by Battery Ventures, and connects to a growing ecosystem of integration partners (including DentalXChange, DentalHQ, Pearl AI, Bola AI, and Mango Voice) rather than exposing a public self-serve developer API. This profile was seeded from Battery Ventures' portfolio and enriched from Curve Dental's public web surface; no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Dandelion Energy
providers.description: Dandelion Energy is a residential geothermal heating and cooling company that designs, engineers, and installs ground-source heat pump systems for homeowners and new-home builders. Its systems tap the earth's stable subsurface temperature to heat and cool homes year-round, cutting utility bills and carbon emissions versus conventional fossil-fuel HVAC. Dandelion delivers end-to-end service from ground-loop drilling through turnkey installation, and offers a leasing program that removes the upfront cost for buyers. The company reports thousands of installations across the United States. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), it operates in the frontier-tech and climate sector; it currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Eunice
providers.description: Eunice is a London-based AI fintech building institutional-grade due diligence and monitoring infrastructure for digital assets and private markets. Its platform automates token due diligence, classification, risk analysis, and disclosure requirements — including an AI-powered MiCA whitepaper library for streamlining compliance with the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation — and delivers insights through a dashboard and API to exchanges, funds, custodians, issuers, and regulators. Founded in 2021 by Yi Luo, a second-time fintech entrepreneur and former VC, Eunice raised $8M in combined Seed and Pre-Seed funding led by Moonfire Ventures and Speedinvest with participation from Openspace Ventures in 2026, and counts Coinbase, Crypto.com, Copper, and Zodia Custody among its clients.

providers.name: Fastshot
providers.description: Fastshot is an AI-powered, no-code mobile app builder that turns a plain-language prompt into a real native iOS and Android application. A multi-agent AI workflow handles design, branding, asset generation, and functionality end to end, then deploys the finished app to the Apple App Store and Google Play. The platform includes integrations for a Supabase backend (authentication, database, storage), GitHub source-code management, Expo builds, and in-app-purchase monetization, letting non-technical founders and businesses ship a working mobile app in minutes rather than hiring an agency or in-house team. Fastshot is a Y Combinator (Fall 2025) company founded by ex-Google engineers Dmitry Fatkhi and Elvira Dzhuraeva.

providers.name: FeezBack
providers.description: FeezBack is an Israeli open-banking fintech, founded in 2016, that builds the technological infrastructure and consumer products enabling financial players to compete in Israel's open-banking ecosystem. Its products cover account-to- account payment initiation (direct bank payments with no card-processing fees integrated into sales and point-of-sale flows), aggregated financial data for underwriting and risk assessment, and financial analysis for investment portfolio and risk allocation. FeezBack holds a Bank of Israel financial information service provider (AIS) license and a payment initiation (PIS) approval, and is ISO 27001 certified for information security. The company describes an API-based integration model for partners but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Fertifa
providers.description: Fertifa is Europe's reproductive healthcare benefits provider for employers, giving companies a way to offer fertility, family-forming, women's health, maternity, menopause, men's reproductive health, and neurodiversity support to their employees. The platform pairs an in-house clinical team with education and training, diagnostics and testing, prescriptions and medication delivery, and financing/reimbursement, delivered to staff through a mobile app and to HR teams through enterprise and SME plans. Fertifa is London-based, backed by Speedinvest, and works with employers including Lululemon, Meta, Bain Capital, and Virgin. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, and support properties.

providers.name: Flatiron Health
providers.description: Flatiron Health is a healthcare technology company focused on oncology, combining real-world data from millions of cancer patients with software and AI to support life sciences research and clinical care. Its platforms include OncoEMR and OncoCloud for oncology practices, Flatiron Vessel (clinical research EDC, formerly Protocol First) and Clinical Pipe for clinical trials, and real-world evidence products for life sciences. Flatiron data has informed thousands of peer-reviewed publications and regulatory submissions. The company is part of Roche.

providers.name: Gecko Robotics
providers.description: Gecko Robotics is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania based AI and robotics company that inspects and manages critical physical infrastructure. Its wall-climbing, aerial and submersible robots capture full-coverage ultrasonic, visual and other sensor readings from boilers, pressure vessels, tanks, pipelines, ship hulls and decks, which are fused with facility records and operational data inside Cantilever, the company's AI-powered operating platform for the built world. Cantilever quantifies corrosion rates, predicts remaining asset life and prioritizes capital and maintenance decisions for customers across defense, power, oil and gas, steel, pulp and paper, mining and advanced manufacturing. Cantilever is delivered as a closed, authenticated enterprise SaaS at cantilever.app; Gecko Robotics publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or self-serve API program, and integrations are arranged through the company directly.

providers.name: GoSky AI
providers.description: GoSky AI Inc. is a Taipei-based no-code conversational marketing and social CRM platform that helps creators, brands, and enterprises automate customer engagement across Instagram, Threads, and Facebook Messenger. Founded in 2018, its product suite spans the GoSky AI Chatbot Platform (build no-code chat flows, capture leads, and auto-reply to comments and DMs in minutes), GoSky Loyal (a digital loyalty and membership points program), GoSky Ads (precision ad placement across Google, Meta, and Shopee), and GoSky AI Customer Service (generative-AI-powered 24/7 support). The company operates a hosted SaaS console at platform.goskyai.com and reports serving 400+ enterprises including Mercedes-Benz, VOGUE, and Lazada. GoSky AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass GoSky AI publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Grabr
providers.description: Grabr is a peer-to-peer cross-border shopping marketplace, founded in 2015 in San Francisco, that connects shoppers wanting products unavailable or expensive in their home country with travelers who deliver those items during trips in exchange for a reward. Grabr handles secure online payments, calculates duties and fees upfront, and holds funds in escrow until delivery is confirmed, operating across 75+ countries. It is a consumer mobile-app marketplace (iOS and Android) with a sibling fintech product, GrabrFi (US banking for non-residents). Grabr does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity, support, legal, and domain-security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hesai Technology
providers.description: Hesai Technology is a global leader in 3D LiDAR perception, designing and manufacturing high-performance lidar sensors for autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), robotics, and industrial automation. Its sensors are deployed by major automotive OEMs and autonomous-vehicle companies across more than 40 countries. Hesai does not expose a public REST/HTTP API; its developer surface is source-distributed C++ SDKs, ROS and ROS2 drivers, and integration plugins (including an NVIDIA DriveWorks plugin) published on the HesaiTechnology GitHub organization, alongside a developer portal and downloadable firmware, manuals, and tools. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Hesai's public developer resources.

providers.name: Ideal Invest
providers.description: Ideal Invest (operating as Pravaler) is a Brazilian fintech founded in 2002 and headquartered in Sao Paulo that provides private student financing for higher education. Through its Pravaler platform, students can split tuition payments across roughly twice the duration of a course, with a 100% digital, low-bureaucracy application, competitive monthly interest rates, and no ENEM requirement. Pravaler works with a network of 500+ partner higher-education institutions and has financed more than 400,000 students, channeling over R$12 billion into Brazilian education. The company is backed by Ribbit Capital. As of this enrichment pass Pravaler exposes a consumer web platform (simulation, application, digital signature) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or partner integration surface.

providers.name: Iris Telehealth
providers.description: Iris Telehealth is an Austin, Texas telepsychiatry company, founded in 2013, that delivers virtual behavioral health care to healthcare organizations rather than direct to consumers. It contracts psychiatrists, psychiatric nurse practitioners, LCSWs and LPCs to hospitals and health systems, community mental health centers, community health centers and FQHCs, and Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics, covering pediatric through geriatric populations and low-acuity therapy through high-acuity psychiatry. Its service lines are Virtual Clinic (comprehensive care and behavioral health integration), On-Demand Services (24/7 emergency department psychiatry support), Scheduled Services (matched provider staffing), Bridge Clinic, and Iris Insights, an AI-enabled behavioral health analytics platform covering risk optimization, capacity management, a behavioral health command center and revenue cycle analytics. The company reports over 430 clinicians and over 210 partner organizations, and has been accredited by the Joint Commission for behavioral health care since 2019, earning recertification since. Its delivery model is deliberately technology-agnostic: Iris clinicians work inside each partner's existing EMR/EHR and e-prescribing tools over HIPAA-compliant video, so the integration burden sits with the partner's systems. Iris Telehealth publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract, and operates no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: JAX-WS
providers.description: JAX-WS (Java API for XML Web Services) is a Java standard for building and consuming SOAP-based XML web services. Originally specified as JSR 224 under the Java Community Process, JAX-WS is now part of Jakarta EE as Jakarta XML Web Services. It defines annotations and runtime APIs that allow developers to expose Java methods as SOAP web service operations and to generate Java client stubs from WSDL documents. Reference implementations include the Eclipse Metro project and Apache CXF.

providers.name: Layer
providers.description: Layer is a living digital art platform that curates code-based generative artwork and ultra-high-resolution video art for everyday display. Its developer surface is an artist-facing, first-party TypeScript SDK (a browser global, $layer) that lets creators declare customizable parameters, register a canvas for screenshot capture, and supply generated video previews back to Layer Studio, alongside published guidelines for generative and Ultra Res artwork. Layer is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and Emergence Capital, added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public developer documentation. Layer exposes a client-side SDK rather than a public REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Lightbeam
providers.description: Lightbeam is an AI data security and guardrails platform that discovers and classifies sensitive data across cloud, SaaS and on-premises systems, ties that data to identity and access context through its Data Identity Graph, and enforces guardrails on how users, applications, copilots and AI agents reach it. Capabilities span AI security and shadow-AI detection, data security posture management (DSPM), data classification, risk scoring, automated remediation, access governance, privacy operations, data retention, breach and ransomware blast-radius reduction, and user entity behavior analytics. Founded by former Nutanix leaders and backed by Vertex Ventures US, 8VC, Village Global, Monta Vista Capital and Dropbox. Lightbeam sells to the enterprise and publishes no public API - its documentation portal is authentication-gated.

providers.name: Long-Term Stock Exchange
providers.description: The Long-Term Stock Exchange (LTSE) is a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission-registered national securities exchange headquartered in New York, built to support companies and investors committed to long-term value creation. LTSE operates a principles-based equities trading platform that accepts order entry over the MEMO FIX and MEMO SBE (Simple Binary Encoding) protocols and distributes real-time market data - depth of book, top of book, and last sale - via the MEMOIR multicast feed. Beyond the exchange it offers private-markets and cap-table software plus long-term listing standards. LTSE does not publish a public REST/OpenAPI developer API; participant connectivity (Direct, Extranet, Telco via NY4) and technical specifications are provided through its Market Operations team.

providers.name: MicroTech Medical
providers.description: MicroTech Medical (Hangzhou) develops user-friendly diabetes glucose monitoring devices — blood glucose monitoring systems (BGMS), the AiDEX continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system, the Equil patch insulin pump, a closed-loop artificial pancreas, point-of-care testing (POCT), and LinX. Its AiDEX API Platform (aidexapi.microtechmd.com) is a self-service developer portal that registers developers and issues API credentials for accessing blood glucose data resources from AiDEX CGM devices, with separate global and China regional endpoints. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Mutual of Omaha
providers.description: Mutual of Omaha is a Fortune 500 mutual insurance and financial services company headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, providing life, disability, dental, vision, critical illness, accident and long-term care insurance, Medicare supplement and Medicare Advantage plans, annuities, retirement services, mortgage lending and investment products to individuals, employers and groups across the United States. Its Workplace Solutions unit runs an API integration program for group and voluntary benefits — Plan Setup, Evidence of Insurability and Enrollment — but those APIs are delivered through benefits administration platform partners such as ADP Workforce Now, bswift, Employee Navigator and PlanSource rather than through a public developer portal, and no machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Netflix Zuul
providers.description: Netflix Zuul is a JVM-based API gateway providing dynamic routing, monitoring, resiliency, and security for microservice architectures.

providers.name: Onebrief
providers.description: Onebrief is a defense-technology company building a unified command workspace for military planning, decision-making, and staff collaboration. The web-based platform centralizes live, synchronized operational data into reusable "Cards" that produce C2 charts, maps, timelines, presentations, documents, and whiteboards from live data rather than static content, with doctrine-aware AI assistance (built on Anthropic Claude) that anticipates dependencies and surfaces critical information early. In August 2024 Onebrief launched a policy-aware, versioned API that accepts data in common DoD formats and connects key mission systems such as Maven Smart System and Advana into a live, shared mission picture, supporting bidirectional data flow across classified and unclassified networks (SIPR, NIPR, JWICS) in alignment with JADC2 data interoperability goals. Backed by Battery Ventures, General Catalyst, Insight Partners, and Sapphire Ventures. The API is a government-deployed product with no public developer portal, specification, or self-serve base URL.

providers.name: Photys Therapeutics
providers.description: Photys Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Waltham, Massachusetts advancing proximity-based, targeted protein modulation medicines across three heterobifunctional modalities: PROTAC-based protein degradation (lead program PHT-776/HPB-143, an oral IRAK4 degrader that entered Phase I in August 2026 for autoimmune and inflammatory disease), PHICS (Phosphorylation-Inducing Chimeric Small molecules, partnered with Novo Nordisk since December 2024 for cardiometabolic disease), and tPRIME for restoring protective proteins such as p53 Y220C in oncology. Founded in 2022 out of Amit Choudhary's lab at the Broad Institute and Brigham and Women's Hospital with a $75M Series A led by MPM Capital and Longwood Fund. Photys operates no developer program and publishes no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, WSDL or gRPC contract; its only machine-readable, agent-facing surface is the platform-provided Wix Site MCP endpoint served from its own host at www.photys.com/_api/mcp, which answers anonymously with nine tools over site content and business details.

providers.name: Piazza
providers.description: Piazza is an online question-and-answer platform for higher education that connects students, teaching assistants, and professors in a single wiki-style collaborative space for each class. Instructors run a Piazza for their course where students ask and answer questions, post anonymously, use a LaTeX and code editor for technical content, and receive instructor-endorsed answers. Piazza integrates with every major learning management system (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, Sakai, Desire2Learn, and others) via the LTI standard for single-click class creation, roster-based automatic enrollment, and automatic single sign-on. It is used across thousands of universities in more than 90 countries and is FERPA-compliant. Piazza does not publish an official public developer API; LMS connectivity is delivered through LTI, and only community projects wrap its internal endpoints.

providers.name: Podcast API
providers.description: An API for developers to get information on over 4 million podcasts, 180 million episodes, and 1.5 million transcripts. Powered by Taddy's GraphQL API, the Podcast API supports search across podcast series, episode details, transcripts, top charts, popularity data, and webhook subscriptions.

providers.name: Puppeteer
providers.description: Puppeteer is a Node.js library providing a high-level API to control headless Chrome or Chromium browsers for web scraping, testing, and automation.

providers.name: Quadric
providers.description: Quadric is a semiconductor IP company based in Burlingame, California that licenses the Chimera GPNPU (general-purpose neural processing unit) processor IP and its accompanying software stack for on-device and edge AI inference. The Chimera architecture unifies scalar, vector, and matrix compute in a single fully C++ programmable core so both AI graph operators and classic DSP/C++ code run on one pipeline, giving SoC designers a future-proof target for evolving model roadmaps. Quadric ships a developer toolchain rather than a hosted web API: the cloud-based DevStudio portal, the Chimera SDK (ONNX import from PyTorch and TensorFlow), the ChiPy Python programming interface, an LLVM-based C++ extensibility path, and an instruction-set simulator for pre-silicon performance modeling. This profile catalogs Quadric's developer surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SAVA
providers.description: SAVA (sava.health) is a health-monitoring company developing a minimally invasive, continuous multi-molecule biosensor worn just beneath the skin. The platform is designed to capture real-time molecular data - glucose, lactate, ketones, sodium, histamine, urea, alcohol, and cortisol - and surface it through a connected mobile app, aiming to shift healthcare toward preventative monitoring and personal wellness. The company is early stage and pre-launch, operating a waiting-list model for early access to its device rather than a public product. It publishes no first-party developer API or health-data API; its marketing site is built on Wix and exposes the Wix Site MCP endpoint and a published llms.txt for agentic access to public site content only. Backed by Balderton Capital.

providers.name: ScaleFlux
providers.description: ScaleFlux is a semiconductor and systems company, founded in 2014 and headquartered in Milpitas / San Jose, California, that designs enterprise NVMe SSD controllers, computational storage drives and CXL memory products. Its FX-series SoC controllers (SFX 3016, FX 5016) embed transparent hardware compression, so drives such as the CSD 2000, CSD 3000 and CSD 5000 series present substantially more logical than physical capacity while offloading compression and data-shaping work from the host CPU. The company also ships non-compressing NSD drives and CXL memory expansion silicon aimed at AI, cloud and database infrastructure. ScaleFlux is a hardware vendor rather than a web-API provider: it publishes no public REST, GraphQL or webhook API. Its programmable surface is the NVMe standard command set plus the vendor-specific "sfx" extensions shipped as an upstream plugin in linux-nvme/nvme-cli (sfx-nvme), together with kernel driver and utility packages distributed through packagecloud.io.

providers.name: Stader Labs
providers.description: Stader Labs is a non-custodial, smart-contract-driven liquid staking platform for Proof-of-Stake networks. It lets retail users, exchanges, and custodians stake crypto and receive tokenized liquid staking tokens (ETHx, MaticX, BNBx, NEARx and others) that stay usable across 40+ DeFi protocols while earning auto-compounding rewards, with no lock-up and no minimum stake. Stader operates as multi-chain middleware infrastructure across Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain, Hedera, Fantom, and NEAR, and its contracts have been audited by Sigma Prime, Halborn, Peckshield, Code4rena, and OtterSec. The project is on-chain and open source rather than a REST/OpenAPI provider; developer surface area is Solidity/Go/Rust smart contracts, node software, and CLI tooling on GitHub.

providers.name: Taptap Send
providers.description: Taptap Send is a mobile money-transfer (remittance) application that lets people send money from Europe, the UK, the US, and Canada to family and businesses across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. The service supports bank deposits, mobile-money wallets, and cash pickups in 100+ receiving countries with competitive exchange rates and low fees, and operates as a licensed and regulated money transmitter (FCA regulated, SOC 2 and PCI DSS attested) with bank-level encryption. Taptap Send is a consumer-facing app and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures its company identity, security posture, and compliance program.

providers.name: The Clearing House (RTP)
