It builds the "Leaner" (リーナー) cloud suite for corporate procurement and purchasing departments: Leaner購買 (purchasing), a purchase-to-pay system covering quotation, approval workflow, ordering, receiving and payment; Leaner sourcing, a quotation and sourcing workspace; Leaner Connect, an SRM supplier-relationship platform; plus procurement BPO and consulting services. The platform aggregates supplier and EC catalogs (including Amazon Business and MonotaRO) into cross-catalog search, and applies AI to classify purchasing data for indirect-spend visibility and cost optimization. The company holds ISMS ISO/IEC 27001:2013 / JIS Q 27001:2014 certification (registration JP21/080659, February 2021). Leaner publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs as of this enrichment pass — its integration surface is delivered through partner catalog connections rather than a self-serve API program.

providers.name: Liftoff
providers.description: Liftoff (onliftoff.com, formerly liftoff.xyz) is a B2B network-based hiring and networking platform for startup leaders and hiring managers. Rather than cold applications or job-board sourcing, companies create a job search, attach a self-set "Match Incentive" referral bonus, and share the search link with their own network or with Liftoff's curated "Top Connectors" — senior leaders who refer pre-vetted candidates from their professional circles. Candidates surface through 2nd- and 3rd-degree trusted connections, and companies pay on a success-only basis, with fees due after a new hire completes 90 days. Liftoff targets seed-to-Series-B technology companies, primarily in the New York City and San Francisco ecosystems, and positions itself between LinkedIn recruiting and traditional retained search. Backed by Forerunner Ventures. Liftoff publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal; it does publish an llms.txt for AI agent grounding. Not to be confused with Liftoff Mobile (liftoff.io, ad tech) or useLiftoff (useliftoff.com, job-seeker interview practice).

providers.name: MANTL
providers.description: MANTL is an account and deposit origination software company for banks and credit unions. Its omnichannel platform lets financial institutions open consumer and business deposit and loan accounts across online and in-branch channels, integrating with existing core banking systems to modernize onboarding and accelerate deposit growth. More than 100 institutions raise over $1 billion in deposits monthly through the platform. MANTL was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public API or developer portal — this profile captures its public web, legal, support, and system-status surfaces.

providers.name: MemVerge
providers.description: MemVerge is a memory and AI-infrastructure software company whose Memory Machine and Memory Machine Cloud (MMCloud) platforms virtualize and orchestrate memory and compute for AI, high-performance computing, and life-sciences workloads. MMCloud is operated through the OpCenter control plane and the first-party "float" command-line interface, which submits, migrates, checkpoints, and monitors containerized jobs across cloud and on-prem infrastructure, with spot-instance resiliency (SpotSurfer / WaveRider). MemVerge integrates with Nextflow, Snakemake, and Flyte through open-source plugins and SDKs published on its GitHub organization. Originally surfaced as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company, this profile is enriched from MemVerge's public documentation, CLI reference, and GitHub org.

providers.name: Menlo Security
providers.description: Menlo Security provides a cloud-delivered Browser Security Platform that protects enterprises and their AI agents at the browser session layer, where most modern attacks and data loss occur. Its core capabilities include pre-render threat prevention using multimodal visual and DOM analysis, patented Positive Selection file security that reconstructs documents to strip malware and macros, AI Adaptive DLP for real-time detection and masking of PII/PHI and financial data, invisible browser isolation for high-risk activity, and Menlo Secure Application Access for identity-based zero-trust access to SaaS, legacy, and private applications for both human users and autonomous agents. The platform integrates with existing SASE/SSE, EDR/EPP, and SOC tooling through a single unified control plane. Menlo Security is privately held and backed by investors including General Catalyst. The company operates primarily as an enterprise security vendor and does not publish a public developer API program; administrative and reporting APIs are available to customers through the authenticated admin console.

providers.name: MHub
providers.description: MHub is a Malaysian property-technology (proptech) platform operated by TRB Ventures Sdn Bhd and backed by 500 Global. It gives real-estate developers an integrated system to manage the entire new-property sales cycle — from lead generation, launch, and online booking (Showroom, CRM, SalesCandy) through automated billing and collections (Credit Control), accounting and financial reporting, statutory compliance (HIMS/KPKT registry synchronization and LHDN-compliant e-invoicing), commission control, and handover/defect management. MHub runs a developer portal at developer.mhub.my and an authentication-gated REST API at api.mhub.my for platform integrations.

providers.name: NeuralMagic
providers.description: Neural Magic was an AI software company that spun out of MIT in 2018 to build high-performance deep learning inference software. Its flagship open-source products were DeepSparse, a sparsity-aware inference runtime delivering GPU-class performance on commodity CPUs, together with SparseML, SparseZoo, and Sparsify for model compression, sparsification recipes, and a curated model repository, plus nm-vllm, an enterprise LLM inference server for GPUs. Neural Magic was a prolific contributor to the community vLLM project. The company was acquired by Red Hat (agreement announced November 2024, completed January 2025) and its engineering now advances vLLM and Red Hat AI. The community versions of DeepSparse, SparseML, SparseZoo, and Sparsify were deprecated on 2026-06-02. Neural Magic exposed no commercial REST API; its developer surface was a set of first-party Python libraries published to PyPI and open source on GitHub.

providers.name: Pentera
providers.description: Pentera is an AI-driven automated security validation (exposure validation) platform that lets organizations continuously test their security defenses through automated penetration testing, red teaming, and adversarial validation across internal networks, external attack surface, credentials, and cloud environments. The platform safely emulates real attacker techniques at scale to surface exploitable exposures, validate remediation, and prioritize risk. Pentera is enterprise/on-prem software consumed via its own console and a broad set of product integrations (SIEM/SOAR, ticketing, cloud, EDR, vulnerability management); it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal. Pentera is backed by Insight Partners. Sector: cybersecurity.

providers.name: Perf.ai
providers.description: PerfAI is an autonomous agentic AppSec and auto-fix platform for AI-built apps, helping teams deliver privacy, security, and governance for APIs and applications.

providers.name: Rimac Automobili
providers.description: Rimac Automobili d.o.o. is a Croatian electric hypercar manufacturer and automotive technology company founded by Mate Rimac in 2009 and headquartered at the Rimac Campus in Kerestinec, near Zagreb. It designs and builds the Nevera and Nevera R all-electric hypercars, and develops the vehicle software, infotainment, connectivity and telemetry stack that runs them in-house. Since the 2021 formation of the Bugatti Rimac joint venture with Porsche, the group's component and OEM-supply business was carved out into the sister company Rimac Technology, while Rimac Automobili remains the vehicle brand. Rimac operates a private, customer-only connected-vehicle backend — an MQTT-based telemetry platform feeding first-party iOS and Android owner apps with location, charging, battery and driving-performance data, plus over-the-air update and remote command channels — but it publishes no public developer program, developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract of any kind. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and portfolio tracking.

providers.name: Robotiq
providers.description: Robotiq designs and manufactures collaborative robotics hardware and software — adaptive grippers, vacuum grippers, force-torque sensors, wrist cameras, and pre-engineered workcells for palletizing, machine tending, screwdriving, and assembly. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lévis, Quebec, Canada, the company helps manufacturers automate repetitive tasks by embedding task intelligence ("Intelligence Made Physical") directly into end-of-arm tooling for platforms such as Universal Robots, FANUC CRX, and Omron/Techman. Robotiq publishes open-source ROS drivers and a C++ gripper SDK through its GitHub organization, but it does not operate a public web/REST API — this profile captures its developer-facing identity, open-source SDKs, and domain security posture rather than a hosted API surface.

providers.name: Roofline
providers.description: Roofline (RooflineAI GmbH, Köln, Germany) is a 2024 RWTH Aachen University spin-off building a retargetable AI compiler stack for edge deployment. Its three products are an SDK that compiles models ahead of time from any framework — the product page shows a single Python call, attic.compile(model, (input,)) — a lightweight C runtime with Python bindings that executes the compiled model and orchestrates heterogeneous SoCs, and a Performance Dashboard fed by a roofbench command-line tool running nightly benchmarks across hundreds of models for latency, throughput and memory footprint. The stack is built on open-source MLIR and IREE with proprietary hardware-specific optimization on top, and targets NPUs, MCUs and heterogeneous SoCs with quantization (INT8, blocked, symmetric, asymmetric, dynamic), dynamic shapes for on-device LLMs and mixture-of-experts support. Published work includes NXP eIQ Neutron NPU LLM enablement, Vulkan 1.3 and Arm SVE support in IREE, and day-0 support for Liquid AI LFM2. Roofline is a strategic partner of the Edge AI Foundation and raised a seed round from Serena and First Momentum Ventures. It sells compiler licenses to hardware vendors and embedded software teams: there is no developer program, no public API, no documentation host and no registry-published package. Every product page ends at a Contact Sales form, and the only machine-readable document Roofline publishes anywhere is an llms.txt on its marketing site.

providers.name: Selective Insurance Group
providers.description: Selective Insurance Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: SIGI) is a Branchville, New Jersey holding company whose insurance subsidiaries underwrite standard commercial lines, standard personal lines, and excess and surplus lines property and casualty insurance, plus flood insurance written through the National Flood Insurance Program's Write Your Own program. Coverage is distributed exclusively through independent insurance agents and brokers across the Eastern and Midwestern United States. Selective operates customer and agent self-service portals (MySelective, and the agent portal at customer1.selectiveinsurance.com) and supports policy, billing and claims download into agency management systems, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract as of this profile.

providers.name: SequoiaDB
providers.description: SequoiaDB (巨杉数据库) is a distributed, document-oriented NoSQL database built for financial-grade workloads and widely deployed across banking, insurance, securities, and government systems in China — running in production at more than 100 banks. A single cluster scales to 500 physical servers, 3.0 PB of storage, and 1.4 trillion rows, with remote disaster recovery targeting RPO=0 and RTO under 15 seconds. The platform is multi-model: a native distributed storage engine with full ACID transactions, a MongoDB-protocol-compatible document store (dds) with built-in vector indexing for AI workloads, a MySQL-compatible SQL engine (SequoiaSQL-MySQL), and an S3-compatible object interface (SequoiaCM). The core engine is open source under Apache-2.0, and access is provided through native client drivers for Java, Python, C, C++, PHP, and C#/.NET rather than a public HTTP REST API. SequoiaDB is backed by DCM Ventures and Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Slalom
providers.description: Slalom is a global business and technology consulting firm headquartered in Seattle, Washington, founded in 2001 and privately held, with roughly 12,000 employees across dozens of markets in North America, Europe, Asia and Australia. The firm delivers strategy, artificial intelligence, data, cloud and engineering, customer experience, legacy modernization, digital product building, and privacy and security consulting, and operates the Slalom Build brand for custom software, data platform and product engineering work. Slalom is a delivery partner for Microsoft, AWS, Salesforce, Google Cloud, Adobe and NVIDIA. It sells consulting engagements rather than software, and publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; the machine-readable surface it does publish is an llms.txt at its marketing root and a security.txt on the Slalom Build site.

providers.name: Stacks
providers.description: Stacks is an AI-native financial close and accounting platform for controllers, CFOs, and accounting teams. It automates the monthly close across existing ERPs with agentic tooling for account reconciliations and transaction matching, journal-entry posting and review, close-management checklists and approvals, and AI-powered analysis, variance explanation, and reporting. Stacks connects directly to ERP systems (Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite, SAP S/4HANA, Workday), data warehouses (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift), file storage, and spreadsheets, and offers an Excel add-in for manual journals. A developer API for custom reconciliation logic is announced as "coming soon." Stacks is a fintech company backed by EQT Ventures, General Catalyst, Lux Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Version One Ventures. Profile enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public web surfaces (no public API specification is yet available).

providers.name: Standout
providers.description: Standout (standout.work) is an AI talent agent for tech professionals in the United States. Candidates run a CLI (`npx standout`) that assesses how they think, build, and debug to create a living, verified profile of capability rather than a resume. Standout matches candidates to hiring companies and brokers a direct introduction to the founder when a match looks right — no applications and no recruiter middle layer. It is free for candidates; companies pay only on a successful hire. Backed by Y Combinator.

providers.name: Udacity
providers.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

providers.name: Valmont Industries
providers.description: Valmont Industries is a global leader in producing fabricated metal products, designing and manufacturing engineered support structures for infrastructure (utility poles, lighting, traffic), mechanized irrigation equipment (Valley center pivot systems), and industrial coatings services. Valmont's Valley brand is the world's leading manufacturer of center pivot and linear irrigation systems, with digital platforms including AgSense 365 and BaseStation3 providing remote monitoring and control of irrigation pivots.

providers.name: Valspar
providers.description: The Valspar Corporation was a global manufacturer of paints and coatings founded in 1806 before being acquired by Sherwin-Williams in 2017 for approximately $11.3 billion. Valspar continues to operate as a brand within Sherwin-Williams, offering consumer paints, industrial coatings, and protective coatings. Digital tools include color visualizers, virtual painters, and color consultation services. No public developer API is available; color and product integrations are available through Sherwin-Williams' partner programs including BIMsmith and Autodesk Revit.

providers.name: Vastrm
providers.description: Vastrm is a custom-tailored menswear e-commerce company selling made-to-fit polo shirts with 24 different fits and sizes plus additional free adjustments, an online design-your-own configurator, corporate solutions for businesses, and a retail partners program. Vastrm is a Y Combinator and a16z-backed company tracked in the API Evangelist network; it operates a consumer storefront at vastrm.com and publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Virgin Pulse
providers.description: Virgin Pulse is a corporate health and employee wellbeing platform that in 2024 merged with HealthComp and rebranded as Personify Health, operating today at personifyhealth.com. The company delivers a personalized health platform that unites wellbeing, healthcare navigation and advocacy, benefits administration, third-party administration (TPA), and rewards into a single employee experience for enterprises, health plans, and health systems. Integration with Personify Health is handled through an authentication-gated developer portal (developer.personifyhealth.com) and a partner marketplace (marketplace.personifyhealth.com); there is no publicly documented, open API specification. This profile was seeded as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and enriched from the company's live public surface (llms.txt, status page, developer portal, and DNS/TLS probes).

providers.name: Weee
providers.description: Weee! is America's largest online Asian grocery store and delivery platform, operating as a direct-to-consumer online supermarket serving major metropolitan areas across the United States. It curates and fulfills inventory through regional distribution centers and cold-chain logistics, bringing together products and ingredients commonly found in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai, Filipino, and Indian supermarkets. The storefront spans fresh produce, frozen meats, seafood, pantry staples, snacks, sauces, hot pot ingredients, beverages, and household essentials, accepts EBT/SNAP in eligible cities, and runs a multilingual experience (English, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese, Thai). Weee is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and the SoftBank Vision Fund. As of this profile Weee publishes no public developer API; this record captures its public web identity and AI-indexing (llms.txt) surface.

providers.name: Zipcar
providers.description: Zipcar is a Boston, Massachusetts-based car sharing service operating in more than 500 cities across North America and Europe, including major US metros (Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York, Philadelphia, Portland, San Francisco, Seattle, Washington DC) and Canadian cities (Toronto, Hamilton, the Golden Horseshoe). Members reserve vehicles by the hour or day through the Zipcar mobile app, unlock cars with their phone, and pay per usage with gas, EV charging, standard damage protection insurance, and professional maintenance included. Zipcar serves consumer members, universities (Zipcar for Universities), and businesses (Zipcar for Business) with weekday fleet programs. Zipcar is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Avis Budget Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: CAR), which acquired the company in March 2013 for approximately $500 million. Zipcar exposes a REST-based Partner API at api.zipcar.com/partner-api, documented at owa.zipcar.com/documentation, that returns JSON for Location List and Location Detail resources (vehicles available at a lat/long); access is gated and granted on request via developerportal@zipcar.com — there is no public OpenAPI spec, SDK, or self-service developer signup. Zipcar also operates a public GitHub organization (github.com/Zipcar) hosting internal DevOps tooling (Concourse resources, Ansible helpers, BOSH helpers, monitoring agents) rather than client-facing API artifacts.

providers.name: Actifio
providers.description: Actifio is an enterprise data management company that pioneered "copy data management" (CDM) built on its Virtual Data Pipeline (VDP) technology, letting organizations capture a single physical copy of production data and instantly provision virtual copies for backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, test/dev, and analytics. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, Actifio was acquired by Google Cloud in December 2020. Its technology now underpins the Google Cloud Backup and Disaster Recovery (Backup and DR) service and Actifio GO, delivering SaaS backup and DR for Google Cloud and hybrid workloads. Actifio VDP exposes automation via a RESTful API and CLI on the appliance, but there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, or published client SDK.

providers.name: Agreena
providers.description: Agreena is a Copenhagen-based agtech and climate finance company, founded in 2021, that helps farmers transition to regenerative agriculture and monetize the resulting soil-carbon outcomes. Its AgreenaCarbon platform combines farmer enrollment, a satellite-, AI-, and soil-sampling-based digital measurement, reporting and verification (dMRV) engine, and Verra-certified carbon credit issuance. Agreena also offers standalone remote-sensing products such as a field-boundary-detection API for agrifood supply-chain monitoring. The platform spans roughly 5 million hectares and 2,500+ farmers across ~20 European countries. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and HV Capital and is being enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Agreena publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI surface at this time.

providers.name: Allswell
providers.description: Allswell is an online mental health platform providing virtual, trauma-informed therapy for the LGBTQ+ community. Licensed therapists with master's degrees in social work, counseling, or marriage and family therapy deliver individual telehealth sessions alongside peer support groups and skills-building resources, covering trauma, anxiety, depression, identity exploration, and relationship dynamics. Allswell serves clients in Maryland, DC, and Virginia, accepting Medicaid and major insurance plans as well as cash-pay. Backed by Techstars, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: American Axle and Manufacturing
providers.description: American Axle & Manufacturing (AAM), now operating as Dauch Corporation following the February 2026 acquisition of Dowlais Group (GKN Automotive and GKN Powder Metallurgy), is a global Tier 1 automotive supplier designing, engineering, and manufacturing driveline and metal forming technologies for electric, hybrid, and internal combustion vehicles. AAM operates an iSupplier Portal for supplier communication, EDI integration for forecasts and releases, and the Demand AAM aftermarket parts portal.

providers.name: Amperos
providers.description: Amperos provides AI-powered insurance claims management and revenue recovery for healthcare providers, using agentic AI to recover insurance revenue end-to-end and drive more collections, faster. The platform automates denial management, claims processing, and collections workflows while keeping human experts in the loop for complex cases, and integrates with major EHR / practice-management systems including eClinicalWorks, Athenahealth, NextGen, Epic, ModMed, and Dentrix. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Amperos exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface at this time; the product is delivered as a managed service and web application.

providers.name: AnswersNow
providers.description: AnswersNow is a virtual Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapy provider for individuals with autism, delivering personalized, evidence-based care from board-certified behavior analysts (BCBAs) through its proprietary telehealth platform. Families access one-on-one therapy sessions, caregiver and parent training, and individualized treatment plans remotely, expanding access to ABA care in areas with limited in-person availability. AnswersNow accepts major insurance carriers including Medicaid, is BHCOE accredited and a CASP member organization, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. This profile has been enriched with company identity and domain-security posture; AnswersNow publishes a consumer web application (web.getanswersnow.com) but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Apis Partners
providers.description: Apis Partners is a London-headquartered private equity asset manager investing in tech-enabled financial infrastructure and financial services businesses across Europe and Growth Markets. With additional offices in Dubai and Singapore, the firm backs companies in payments, digital banking, insurance technology and lending, taking minority positions with governance rights. Apis manages approximately $2.3 billion in assets under management and reports over $1 billion in portfolio realizations, with portfolio companies reaching more than 244 million people. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the firm is an investor rather than an API producer, so it exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: August AI
providers.description: August AI is a consumer health-AI companion that helps people understand their symptoms, lab reports, prescriptions, and medications, and connects them to licensed physicians through asynchronous, chat-based telehealth visits. Founded in 2022 by Anuruddh Mishra after a four-month misdiagnosis, August operates as a 24/7 health assistant available on iOS, Android, and WhatsApp, storing lab reports and conversation history in long-term memory to deliver personalized guidance. The service pairs a free AI symptom-assessment experience with paid online doctor consultations from board-certified MDs licensed across all 50 US states. August reports serving millions of users across 160+ countries in 30+ languages, and publishes medical benchmarks including 100% accuracy on the USMLE, 97.4% on MedQA, 99.4% on lab-report document processing, and 100% precision/recall on emergency escalation. It is backed by Accel and Claypond Capital. August is a consumer application and does not currently publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Baselane
providers.description: Baselane is an all-in-one financial platform (financial operating system) for independent landlords and real estate investors, combining FDIC-insured landlord banking, automated rent collection, bookkeeping and expense tracking, analytics and reporting, and cash-flow tools in a single product. Banking services are provided through partner Thread Bank, and account connectivity to external banks is powered by Plaid. Baselane is a consumer/SMB fintech application (web and mobile apps) rather than an API platform: it publishes no first-party public developer API, developer portal, or API reference. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Sector: fintech / proptech.

providers.name: Bibit
providers.description: Bibit is an Indonesian retail investment application that lets everyday users invest in mutual funds (reksa dana), government bonds (SBN/SBR/ORI), fixed-rate bonds, and stocks. Built for beginner investors, it uses robo-advisor technology to recommend diversified portfolios and is licensed by Indonesia's financial regulator OJK. Bibit operates within the Stockbit group and is a portfolio company of Prosus Ventures. As of this profile no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published; this repo tracks the company's public surface (security.txt, legal, help, blog) for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Candid Co.
providers.description: Candid Co. (candidco.com), operating today as CandidPro, is a New York-based dental-technology company that delivers custom clear aligners for teeth straightening. Founded in 2017 as a direct-to-consumer brand backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Greycroft, and e.ventures, Candid pioneered at-home impression kits and remote monitoring, and has since pivoted to a dentist-directed model: aligners are prescribed and overseen by a licensed dentist with orthodontist support and convenient virtual visits (CandidMonitoring). Candid handles the clinical treatment plan, 3D-printed aligner manufacturing, and patient communication for crowding and common bite misalignments. This is a consumer/health brand with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, domain security posture, and commercial link properties.

providers.name: Carbon
providers.description: Carbon is a digital manufacturing company that builds an integrated 3D printing platform combining Digital Light Synthesis (DLS) printing hardware, advanced photopolymer resins, and cloud-connected computational design software. Its technology enables production-scale additive manufacturing of end-use polymer parts across automotive, medical, dental, consumer goods, and industrial applications, with the Design Engine tool for lattice and part design and the Carbon Academy knowledge base for operational guidance. Carbon is a frontier-tech portfolio company backed by GV. As of this profile Carbon exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or event surface; enrichment is limited to verified company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Charter Space
providers.description: Charter Space is a London-based space technology company, founded in 2021, building software and financial infrastructure for the New Space economy. Its flagship product, Ubik, is a browser-native, model-based systems engineering and program management platform that unifies requirements management, project management, block diagrams, test procedures, and scheduling in a single collaborative environment, cutting manual systems-engineering admin for spacecraft programs. Ubik is in beta with organizations including teams at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and exposes native integrations (OneDrive, Google Drive, Jira, GitHub) plus an API for connecting specialized tooling. Charter has also expanded into space insurance, capturing manufacturing and test data at the source to feed an underwriting interface tied to the largest space-insurance carriers, and operates an insurance brokerage for New Space companies insuring satellites and spacecraft. Backed by Techstars and Capital Factory.

providers.name: Coin98
providers.description: Coin98 is a crypto super-app built around a non-custodial, multi-chain wallet spanning 80+ blockchains across iOS, Android, a Chrome browser extension, Telegram, and web. Its product surface includes the Coin98 Super Wallet, an AI wallet with autonomous agents (Cypheus), the SwapX DEX aggregator routing across 50+ DEXs, on-chain perpetual futures (Coin98 Perps), the Fusion Visa debit card, PowerPool C98 staking, the Zen hardware card, Coin98 Markets data, and a token distribution Vault. For developers, Coin98 publishes a Developer Guide and the Coin98 Adapter — a React/Next.js wallet-connection SDK with useWallet and useWalletModal hooks and prebuilt connect UI — plus a Connect SDK and Telegram Mini App SDK, integrating dApps with the wallet across 40+ chains. Surfaced originally as a multicoin-capital portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cyberpsyc
providers.description: CyberPsyc Software Solutions, operating as WellTrack Boost (now part of ProtoCall Services), builds self-guided, clinically-supported digital cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) tools for behavioral health and wellness. The platform lets users assess and understand their mental health on their own devices and schedule through MoodCheck mood tracking, the Zen Room, a Thought Diary, an Activity Scheduler, Fun and Achievement planning, and guided modules for stress, anxiety, and depression. WellTrack Boost is deployed by college counseling centers and certified community behavioral health clinics, offering institutional single sign-on through a SAML integration surface. No public developer REST API or OpenAPI is currently published.

providers.name: Delve Bio
providers.description: Delve Bio is a genomic diagnostics company commercializing clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for infectious disease diagnosis. Its flagship test, Delve Detect, analyzes all nucleic acids in a single cerebrospinal fluid sample to simultaneously detect bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites, screening against a curated database of more than 68,000 pathogen species to diagnose meningitis and encephalitis with results in roughly 48 hours. The company is the exclusive licensee of the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) mNGS technology developed at the Center for Next-Gen Precision Diagnostics, founded by Charles Chiu, Joe DeRisi, Michael Wilson, Pardis Sabeti, and Matthew Meyerson, and backed by investors including GV. Delve Bio operates as a CAP/CLIA-certified clinical laboratory serving labs and clinicians; it exposes no public developer API surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a gv portfolio lead.

providers.name: Deposco
providers.description: Deposco is a cloud supply chain execution platform combining order management (OMS) and warehouse management (WMS) for retailers, brands, 3PLs, and DTC ecommerce sellers. Its Bright Suite gives real-time visibility into inventory, orders, and shipments across the fulfillment lifecycle - receiving, putaway, picking, packing, and shipping. Deposco integrates through a REST API exposed on its Developer Portal (developer.deposco.com) using resource paths under /integration/{code}/, secured with OAuth 2.0 / per-merchant API credentials and scoped by tenant code and business unit. API access is provisioned per customer through a Deposco account manager rather than through open self-service signup, and Deposco also ships 150+ pre-built connectors and EDI integrations.

providers.name: Dianxiaomi
providers.description: Dianxiaomi (店小秘) is a free cross-border e-commerce ERP platform operated by Shenzhen Meiyunji Network Technology Co., Ltd., serving more than 1.8 million cross-border sellers worldwide. It unifies product listing and data collection, multi-platform order processing, warehouse and inventory management, procurement, financial and profit analytics, and customer service across 70+ marketplaces including AliExpress, Amazon, Shopee, Lazada, and TikTok Shop, with integrations to 1,700+ logistics providers and 130+ overseas warehouses. The platform is user-facing SaaS; no public developer/API open platform is currently published.

providers.name: Dorsata
providers.description: Dorsata is a women's health technology company based in Arlington, Virginia that reimagines the electronic health record (EHR) experience for obstetrics and gynecology providers, life sciences, and health plans. Its flagship Dorsata Prenatal platform overlays a practice's existing EHR with an ACOG-aligned prenatal flowsheet and a clinical rules engine that surfaces the right guidance at the right point of care, improving diagnosis, treatment, and documentation while reducing physician burnout. Additional products include Dorsata Insights, which gathers standardized real-world clinical data from women's health providers (including populations historically underrepresented in clinical studies), Dorsata Pathways, and an Adnexal Mass solution. The platform serves 300+ practice sites and thousands of clinical users across roughly 20 states, documenting hundreds of thousands of pregnancies. Dorsata raised a $5.2M Series A with participation from QED Investors, Women's Health USA, LabCorp, Fool Ventures, and Gore Range Capital. This API Evangelist profile tracks Dorsata as a healthtech company; the company exposes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: DZone
providers.description: DZone is one of the world's largest online communities and a leading publisher of knowledge resources for software engineering professionals. Founded in 1997 with roots in Javalobby, DZone reaches millions of developers each month with articles, tutorials, research guides, and Refcards covering topics including cloud architecture, Java, JavaScript, microservices, containers, data, DevOps, AI, and more.

providers.name: Electric Car Scheme
providers.description: The Electric Car Scheme is a UK B Corp providing electric vehicle salary sacrifice as an employee benefit. Employees lease any electric car of their choice with the monthly cost deducted from gross salary before Income Tax and National Insurance, saving 20-50% versus a personal lease, while employers save on Class 1A National Insurance. Packages are all-inclusive (lease, insurance, maintenance, servicing and breakdown) with Complete Protection covering employees who leave partway through a lease term. The company integrates with employer payroll systems via API or SFTP and offers Single Sign-On for employees, plus an included Charge Scheme for charging access.

providers.name: Erebor
providers.description: Erebor is a digital-first, FDIC-insured national bank built for the innovation economy — technology startups, cryptocurrency and stablecoin businesses, and AI and defense companies that traditional banks have historically underserved. Co-founded by Palmer Luckey (Anduril) and Joe Lonsdale (8VC) and backed by Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Haun Ventures, and 8VC, Erebor received OCC preliminary conditional approval in October 2025, FDIC deposit-insurance approval in December 2025, and launched in February 2026. It offers deposit accounts, wires and money movement, and stablecoin operations. Erebor exposes a developer API at api.erebor.bank secured with API keys, an Auth0-authenticated developer dashboard at developer.erebor.bank, and Fern-based developer documentation at docs.erebor.bank. The public developer docs are login-gated, so the machine-readable surface captured here is limited to what is observable without credentials.

providers.name: Finkargo
providers.description: Finkargo is a Latin American foreign-trade commerce platform that helps importers overcome the operational and financial barriers to growing their import businesses. Its product suite spans Paga (alternative supplier financing with revolving USD credit lines and 30-150 day terms), Analiza (market-intelligence dashboards that turn trade data into strategic decisions), Verifica (global supplier verification for product quality and legitimacy), and Protege (warehouse-to-warehouse cargo insurance). Operating across Colombia and Mexico and backed by QED Investors, Finkargo digitizes the full import-operations lifecycle from evaluating suppliers and planning imports to financing, transport, and arrival. Finkargo does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; this profile captures the company's public product, legal, and security surfaces.

providers.name: Forterro
providers.description: Forterro is a pan-European industrial software company, founded in 2012 and headquartered in London, that provides enterprise resource planning (ERP) and specialised business software to the industrial mid-market. Built through a series of acquisitions, Forterro operates a portfolio of regional and vertical ERP brands - including Abas, Jeeves, Garp, Proconcept, Sylob, Silog, Myfactory, Orderwise, Clipper, 123Insight, BPSC, Helios, Proffix, Prodaso and its cloud-native Fortee product - alongside best-in-class point solutions such as warehouse management (WMS), point of sale (POS), material requirements planning (MRP) and business intelligence. The company serves more than 13,000 industrial businesses across manufacturing, warehousing, wholesale and retail from 40+ offices worldwide.

providers.name: GoodShip
providers.description: GoodShip is a freight orchestration and procurement platform for shippers, brokers, and asset-based carriers. It unifies TMS tender, contract-award, and location data, enriches it with real-time market rates, and layers AI-assisted bid analysis (via its Laney AI transportation analyst), lane- and carrier-level performance analytics, carrier scorecards, and in-app collaboration on top. Teams run mini-bids and full-network RFPs, benchmark spend against the market, and take corrective action without dedicated developer resources. Plug-and-play with major transportation management systems; backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and serving US and Canadian operations.

providers.name: GovGuard
providers.description: GovGuard is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) GovTech company building AI infrastructure for government agencies, starting with Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request automation. Its AI agents route incoming public-records requests, search across municipal archives (emails, meeting minutes, PDFs, and shared drives), flag personally identifiable information and other exempt material for redaction against the relevant state exemption codes, and draft response letters for clerk review while maintaining a complete audit trail. Agencies retain full ownership and control of all records and metadata, and GovGuard states that it does not train models on client data. The company was founded by Aditya Sabharwal and Gleb Hulting and is based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Graylark
providers.description: Graylark is an AI-powered geolocation intelligence company serving law enforcement, government, and enterprise customers. Its technology extracts location data from ordinary images at varying levels of precision, marketed under the GeoSpy brand (geospy.ai). The platform offers Global Search (1-50 km accuracy with worldwide coverage), Street Search (meter-level precision across 1,000+ cities), and Property Search (100+ million records for matching a scene to a specific structure). Graylark positions these capabilities for investigations, fraud detection, insurance validation, and journalistic verification of visual content. Access is gated to qualified government and enterprise organizations via a contact-sales/licensing model; the company publishes no public self-service API, developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time. Backed by General Catalyst.

providers.name: Halter
providers.description: Halter is a New Zealand-founded agri-technology company that builds GPS-enabled, solar-powered smart collars for cattle paired with a mobile and web app, letting farmers set and move virtual fences, remotely shift and hold herds, and monitor animal location, behavior, heat and health without physical fencing or manual labor. The platform combines wearable IoT devices (including direct-to-satellite connectivity) with pasture-management and grazing-allocation tools for dairy and beef operations. Halter operates across New Zealand, Australia and the United States and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Bond Capital and DCVC. No public developer API surface has been identified; this profile captures the company identity, web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Homebound
providers.description: Homebound is a tech-enabled, personalized homebuilder that pairs a proprietary software platform with a managed network of trade partners to build homes on a customer's lot, sell finished and in-progress inventory homes, and run disaster rebuild programs — most notably wildfire recovery in California. Homeowners track budget, schedule, documents, and construction progress through a Homeowner Portal. Backed by Fifth Wall, Forerunner Ventures, and GV, Homebound operates in the construction-tech sector. Homebound does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its public engineering footprint is the homebound-team GitHub organization and the first-party open-source packages it publishes to the @homebound npm scope (the Beam design system, form-state, and truss). This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched from public company surfaces.

providers.name: Housable
providers.description: Housable is a California-focused proptech company that helps rental-property owners and operators develop Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) as a portfolio value-add strategy. Its platform manages ADU projects end to end — from concept and financial feasibility analysis through design, permitting, bidding, construction, and lease-up — and lets operators run many parallel developments across their properties at once, converting underused spaces such as leasing offices, garages, and parking areas into new rental units alongside ground-up ADU construction. Housable is an early-stage startup backed by Kindred Ventures and other seed investors. It is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Hykso
providers.description: Hykso, Inc. is the company behind FightCamp, an at-home boxing and kickboxing training system that pairs a free-standing bag, quick-wrap gloves, and wireless motion-tracking punch trackers with an on-demand library of trainer-led workouts. The Hykso punch trackers began as standalone wearable sensors that measure punch count, speed, and output for boxers and gyms, and now power FightCamp's real-time performance stats and workout scoring. This profile is a company stub in the API Evangelist network; Hykso/FightCamp is a direct-to-consumer connected-fitness brand and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: HZO
providers.description: HZO is a protective coating company specializing in Parylene and thin-film conformal coatings that safeguard electronics from moisture, humidity, salt fog, corrosion, and harsh chemicals. Founded in Salt Lake City and now headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, HZO delivers turnkey coating services and manufacturing solutions across consumer electronics, automotive and mobility, industrial, medical device, IoT, and battery markets, with coating facilities and centers of excellence in the United States, Hungary, China, and Vietnam. HZO is a physical-materials and contract-manufacturing business ("Protection from the Inside Out") rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract. This profile records the public web hygiene surface it does serve — an llms.txt discovery file, an RFC 9116 security.txt, and domain security posture.

providers.name: International Trade Commission
providers.description: The United States International Trade Commission (USITC) is an independent, nonpartisan, quasi-judicial federal agency that fulfills a range of trade-related mandates. The USITC provides high-quality analysis of international trade issues to the President and the Congress, and serves as the primary forum for the adjudication of intellectual property and trade disputes. The agency exposes U.S. trade and tariff statistics through the USITC DataWeb interactive data service.

providers.name: Lockton
providers.description: Lockton Companies is the world's largest privately held, independent insurance brokerage, founded by Jack Lockton in 1966 and headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri, United States. Lockton is a broker and intermediary rather than a risk carrier: it places commercial property and casualty, specialty and financial lines, employee benefits and people solutions, private client coverage, and — through Lockton Re — treaty and facultative reinsurance, for tens of thousands of clients across a global network of associates and offices reaching more than 140 locations. Its API posture is honestly characterized as partner-gated with no public API surface. As of July 2026 Lockton publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or Swagger definition, no GraphQL endpoint, no Postman workspace, and no webhook or event catalog. The hostnames developer.lockton.com, developers.lockton.com, docs.lockton.com and api.lockton.com do not resolve in DNS, and a crawl of the 6,953 URLs in global.lockton.com/sitemap.xml surfaces no developer, API, ACORD, IVANS, OpenAPI or Swagger path. Client-facing technology is delivered through authenticated regional Lockton Client Portals and the proprietary Lockton SAGE intelligence and analytics ecosystem, which is presented on the website behind a contact form with no self-serve access, no documented data feed and no published integration surface. This is the expected posture for a US broker-intermediary: the United States has no federal insurance regulator and no open-insurance mandate, so data exchange between carriers, brokers and agency management systems runs on ACORD standards in an EDI and forms idiom rather than a public API idiom. Lockton's most substantive standards signal is governance rather than implementation — in July 2026 Nidhi Howell, Chief Business Technology Officer of Lockton Re, was appointed to the ACORD Solutions Group Board of Directors representing the reinsurance broking channel — but no ACORD AL3, ACORD XML, NGDS or IVANS agency-download implementation is documented on any public Lockton property.

providers.name: Memorick
providers.description: Memorick is a 500 Global-backed company operating a live web application at memorick.com. Based on its observable application surface, it is a destination photography booking platform connecting customers with photographers across destinations, handling packages, orders, reviews, coupons, and messaging. The product is built on Laravel (Inertia.js single-page front end) and exposes an OAuth2 authorization server via Laravel Passport (authorize/token/clients/scopes plus personal access tokens), Sanctum first-party session auth, and optional two-factor authentication. It publishes no public API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; the /api/* routes back the first-party application and are authentication-gated. This profile was enriched from live probing of the public surface.

providers.name: Multiply
providers.description: Multiply is an AI-native media agency built specifically for B2B companies, pairing human paid-media strategists with a fleet of 25+ specialized AI agents to run and continuously optimize LinkedIn and Google Search advertising. Its "Self-Learning Advertising" platform plugs into a company's own data — sales call recordings (e.g. Gong), CRM closed-won outcomes, case studies, website content, competitive kill sheets and product documentation — and runs hundreds of structured ad experiments that refine audiences, copy and creative from real revenue signals. Multiply is a managed service (not a self-serve API product), founded by Matt Jayson (ex-Google, ex-Brex) and Ashish Warty (ex-HackerOne SVP Engineering, ex-Dropbox), and raised $9.5M led by Mayfield in March 2026. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Mayfield portfolio company; two enrichment passes confirmed it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. It does publish an llms.txt and three named service tiers — Growth (from $6K/mo), Scale (from $12K/mo) and Enterprise — priced against monthly ad spend rather than API usage.

providers.name: Murphy
providers.description: Murphy is a Barcelona-based fintech building AI voice and omnichannel agents that automate debt collection and servicing for banks, fintechs, utilities, telecoms and debt collection agencies. Founded in 2024 by Borja Sole and Marc Sanchez, the platform runs 24/7 AI agents across voice, SMS and email in 15+ languages, handling inbound and outbound recovery with human escalation, behavioural personalisation and fully audited, compliance-bounded interactions (ISO 27001, GDPR and EU AI Act aligned). Murphy claims materially higher recovery rates and 50-70% lower operational cost. It raised roughly $15M (seed + pre-seed) led by Northzone with ElevenLabs, Lakestar, Seedcamp and Enzo Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, SDK or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Myclubs
providers.description: Myclubs is a Vienna- and Zurich-based digital sports membership company, founded in 2014 by Tobias Homberger, that gives members flexible access to a network of more than 1,200 sports and fitness providers across Austria and Switzerland through a single subscription. One membership covers over 35 sport and activity types and more than 10,000 bookable workouts per week, from gyms and yoga studios to tennis, boxing and cross training. Myclubs also runs a corporate fitness program used by over 300 employers as an employee benefit. The company was acquired by Urban Sports Club in August 2024 and is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. Myclubs is a consumer-facing membership brand and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Myndlift
providers.description: Myndlift is a digital neurofeedback and mental-health company that pairs a consumer/clinical mobile app with a wearable EEG brain-sensing headband (Muse) to deliver therapist-guided, personalized brain-training programs. The platform provides brain mapping and assessments, gamified real-time neurofeedback sessions, progress tracking, and remote-monitoring dashboards used by both individuals and mental-health practitioners for attention, anxiety, stress, sleep, and peak-performance goals. Backed by 500 Global, the company reports 26,000+ members and more than one million neurofeedback sessions delivered. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record with verified identity links.

providers.name: NOCD
providers.description: NOCD is a virtual mental-health provider specializing in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder. Through its web and mobile applications the company matches members with licensed therapists trained in Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) therapy, delivers live video sessions, and provides between-session messaging, a peer community, and in-app therapeutic tools. NOCD is in-network with a large number of US health plans and serves children, adolescents, and adults. The product is delivered as an end-user clinical service — the company operates a private mobile/web application backend at api.treatmyocd.com but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Numero
providers.description: Numero is an all-in-one donor database and call-time platform built for political campaigns at the federal, state, and local levels. It combines a fast, filterable donor CRM with auto-deduplication and pledge tracking, a mobile call-time dialer with one-click SMS, email, and voicemail follow-up plus virtual local numbers, prefilled one-click contribution forms with access to a large 1-click donor network, event and RSVP fundraising tools, and a deliverability-focused email platform. Campaigns use Numero to identify prospect donors, run efficient candidate call time, and raise money faster. Numero is backed by Initialized Capital. It currently exposes no public developer API surface; api.numero.ai serves the web application backend only.

providers.name: One Month
providers.description: One Month is an online coding education platform that teaches beginners practical software and web development skills through short, project-based video courses designed to be completed in about a month. Its catalog spans programming languages and frameworks such as Ruby, Ruby on Rails, Python, JavaScript, HTML & CSS, SQL, and WordPress, alongside professional skills like project management, using a "watch, do, repeat" methodology of hands-on lessons and follow-along projects. One Month markets itself to career changers and non-programmers looking to accelerate into technical roles, and publishes a supporting blog of programming tutorials and career guidance. It is a consumer-facing learning product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Optivolt Labs
providers.description: Optivolt Labs (operating as Optivolt) is a Burlingame, California solar technology company building intelligent home solar systems with power electronics embedded directly inside each panel. Its patented Balancer device shuffles power from stronger to weaker zones within a panel to keep energy flowing in shaded and non-ideal conditions, delivering up to 50% more annual energy and improved shaded performance versus conventional panels. The product line includes 450W N-type mono half-cut panels, universal battery and inverter compatibility, and a real-time monitoring app for tracking energy and savings. Optivolt is a Techstars-backed hardware company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Pandai
providers.description: Pandai is a Malaysian education technology company founded in 2020 that operates a digital learning platform for primary and secondary school students. The app aligns to Malaysia's national curriculum (DSKP) across KSSR Years 1-6 and KSSM Forms 1-5, including SPM exam preparation, and helps learners improve their grades through interactive quizzes, tests, exams, topical practice, notes, flashcards, videos, and live tutoring. Features include personalized assessments, an AI-powered revision assistant (Ask Pbot), gamified learning with battles, leaderboards and rewards, and performance tracking via scorecards and report cards. Pandai is a consumer-facing learning app and does not publish a public developer API surface; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Papernest
providers.description: Papernest is a French technology company, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Paris, that provides a digital platform for managing, switching, and cancelling household subscriptions — energy, telecom and internet, mobile plans, and home insurance — through a single interface. Built around the moment people move home, the service is free to end users and monetized through commissions from supplier partners across France, Spain, Italy, and the UK, having helped more than 3 million customers. Papernest does not publish a public developer API; it runs a private B2B partner integration program and maintains an official GitHub organization of archived open-source utilities.

providers.name: Photomath
providers.description: Photomath is a mobile math-learning application that lets students scan a printed or handwritten math problem with their phone camera and returns step-by-step explanations, custom visual aids, and animated solving methods across topics from elementary arithmetic through calculus. Originally built by Croatian computer-vision company Microblink and later spun out as an independent education company backed by Menlo Ventures and Goldman Sachs, Photomath was acquired by Google in 2023 and now operates within Google (support is handled through Google's Help Center). It is a consumer subscription product distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish an official public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. The company previously stated it would not release a public Photomath SDK. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio company and enriched to capture the company's public web and domain-security surface; no first-party API surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: Plenful
providers.description: Plenful is an AI-powered workflow automation platform for pharmacy and healthcare operations, founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco with an office in New York City. The platform automates complex, high-ROI administrative pharmacy workflows — 340B audit and optimization, 340B referral capture, rebate and Maximum Fair Price (MFP) reconciliation, benefits verification and prior authorization, and infusion order intake — using large language models and machine learning tuned to each organization's data. It ingests PDFs, flat files, APIs, HL7 feeds, and databases, supports unlimited organizational logic rules, and serves 100+ healthcare organizations including Prisma Health, Renown Health, Temple Health, Cencora, and Samaritan Health Services. Plenful is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Notable Capital (formerly GGV Capital), SUSA Ventures, TQ Ventures, and Waterline Ventures. Plenful ships an enterprise SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Plobal Apps
providers.description: Plobal Apps is a no-code mobile app builder for Shopify merchants that turns online stores into native iOS and Android shopping apps without engineering. The platform offers drag-and-drop app design with HTML/CSS/JavaScript code blocks, push-notification marketing campaigns, live selling, AI-powered product recommendations, advanced search and smart filtering, and real-time analytics tracking 60+ in-app actions, plus omnichannel flows such as in-app ordering with in-store pickup. It installs through the Shopify App Store and is used by direct-to-consumer brands to grow mobile commerce revenue and customer retention.

providers.name: Prosper Health
providers.description: Prosper Health is a telehealth provider focused exclusively on autistic and neurodivergent adults, offering virtual autism diagnostic assessments and ongoing affirming, strength-based therapy delivered by licensed psychologists and therapists who specialize in adult autism. Its adult-validated, telehealth-native assessment (an alternative to the child-oriented ADOS) runs entirely online across two psychologist sessions plus a feedback session, with results reported within roughly two weeks. Prosper Health accepts major insurers (Aetna, BCBS, Cigna, Oscar, Oxford, United) across 20-plus US states. It is a direct-to-consumer clinical care company with no public developer API surface; this profile tracks its web, security, and identity properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rula
providers.description: Rula is a telehealth mental health platform that connects patients with licensed therapists and psychiatric providers who accept their insurance. Operating as an in-network behavioral health marketplace across all 50 states, Rula matches individuals with more than 23,000 licensed clinicians for individual, couples, family, child, and teen therapy as well as psychiatric medication management, covering 90+ conditions including anxiety, depression, ADHD, PTSD, OCD, and addiction. Rula is in-network with 120+ insurance plans nationwide (Aetna, Cigna, Optum, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross, Kaiser), with patients paying an average of about $15 per session with insurance. Rula publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or partner API surface as of this profile; care is delivered through its patient and provider web applications.

providers.name: Sankun
providers.description: Sankun (산군) is a South Korean construction-industry big data platform based in Seoul that aggregates and sells access to eight integrated construction databases covering roughly 280,000 construction companies, some 820,000 project sites, government e-procurement bids, contract awards, professional reputation reviews, and construction news. Alongside its web application and a construction sales CRM (Sankun Sales), the company markets a Sankun API (data.sankun.com) for programmatic access to its construction data, though public developer documentation is gated behind sales and login. Sankun is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: SIEMonster
providers.description: SIEMonster is a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) vendor whose flagship SIEMonster V5 platform ingests, correlates, and alerts on 2M+ security events per second for threat detection and response, deployed via AWS Marketplace or as a managed SaaS. Its EDG3 product is an autonomous AI SOC built on an edge-resident security lakehouse. Documentation covers platform deployment and agent installation, a knowledgebase, and FAQs; SIEMonster does not publish a public developer REST API, SDKs, or API reference at this time.

providers.name: Skool
providers.description: Skool is an all-in-one community platform that combines discussion communities, online courses, live calls, and gamification in a single product, founded by Sam Ovens and popularized in partnership with Alex Hormozi. As of this review, Skool does NOT publish an official public or partner developer REST API. The only official programmatic surface is a Zapier integration, gated to the paid Pro plan, that exposes a small set of triggers and actions via a per-group API key used solely to link a Skool group to Zapier - it is not a general-purpose developer API. All broader "Skool API" offerings found in the wild (Apify actors, docs.skoolapi.com, reverse-engineered clients, Chrome extensions) are unofficial third-party tools built on Skool's undocumented internal endpoints and are not endorsed or supported by Skool. This catalog entry is an honest gated stub: no public API surface is modeled because none is documented.

providers.name: SM Energy
providers.description: SM Energy Company (NYSE: SM) is an independent oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado. Founded in 1908 (originally as St. Mary Land & Exploration Company), SM Energy focuses on acquiring, exploring, developing, and producing crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids (NGLs) from top-tier assets across the Permian Basin in West Texas and New Mexico, the Maverick Basin in South Texas, the DJ Basin in Colorado, and the Uinta Basin in northeast Utah. The company is a Fortune 1000 member with approximately 1,241 employees and average daily net production of 206.8 MBoe/d. SM Energy completed a merger with Civitas Resources in early 2026. The company does not offer a public developer API; investor data is accessible through financial data APIs and SEC EDGAR.

providers.name: TourHero
providers.description: TourHero is a social travel platform and end-to-end group trip operations partner that lets creators, coaches, and community leaders host fully customized group trips in 50+ countries, with itinerary design, vetted local operators, payments, and on-the-ground logistics handled by TourHero. Travelers can browse and book public trips on its Explore page, and hosts plan for free while TourHero earns commission from local suppliers. Backed by 500 Global and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it is a consumer platform with no publicly documented developer API surface at this time, though it publishes an llms.txt profile for AI agents.

providers.name: VidCruiter
providers.description: VidCruiter is a Moncton, Canada based recruitment technology company that provides a modular hiring platform - pre-recorded and live video interviewing, automated interview scheduling, skills and pre-employment testing, automated reference checking, audio interviews, and video proctoring. VidCruiter does not publish a public, self-service developer API. Its programmatic surface is a partner and enterprise integration capability: pre-built connectors to major ATS/HCM, background-check, calendar, job-board, SSO, and video-conferencing providers, plus a bidirectional web-services integration in which an institution's unique, account-provisioned API endpoint is exchanged with a system of record (for example Slate) to push application records into VidCruiter and pull completed interview results back out. API access is gated behind a VidCruiter account representative; there is no public API reference, OpenAPI document, base URL, or self-serve key issuance.

providers.name: Vocca Ai
providers.description: Vocca is a healthcare voice-AI company (backed by Speedinvest) that builds AI voice and text agents acting as a 24/7 receptionist for medical groups and practices. Vocca handles inbound and outbound patient calls, appointment bookings, reminders, and follow-ups across specialties including imaging, dental, cardiology, gynecology, ophthalmology, anesthesiology, general medicine, hospitals, and multi-practice clinics, so clinical teams spend less time on admin and more time on care. The company operates a customer-facing product with French and English coverage; it does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification, so this profile carries company identity and website link-properties only.

providers.name: Wallet Studio
providers.description: Wallet Studio, built by Miss Moneypenny Technologies GmbH, is a no-code SaaS platform for creating, deploying, and managing Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes. Aimed primarily at insurance carriers, it turns policy administration, claims, and CRM systems into wallet-based customer engagement channels reaching the four billion people who already carry a digital wallet, without replacing existing backend infrastructure. The platform offers visual pass editors with one-click publishing, prebuilt insurance templates, integrated automation, a REST API and webhooks for connecting to third-party systems, and authenticated links to portals and value-added services. Hosting is GDPR-compliant and the company describes the platform as certified for enterprise security standards. Backed by Earlybird, the company raised roughly EUR 7 million in 2025. There is no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification; the REST API is provisioned per customer.

providers.name: Worktrace AI
providers.description: Worktrace AI is an enterprise workflow-automation platform that helps organizations discover, reimagine, and automate repetitive work. A desktop application observes work across existing tools to identify high-ROI AI automation opportunities, surfaces process-optimization recommendations aligned with company KPIs, and generates blueprints for building automations on third-party platforms such as n8n, Crew AI, and Asteroid. The 8VC-backed company targets financial services, healthcare, high tech, insurance, logistics, and telecom, and publishes a Vanta trust center covering SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR. No public API or developer documentation is published as of July 2026.

providers.name: Zoomin
providers.description: Zoomin is a content and knowledge orchestration platform that unifies unstructured product content — documentation, in-product help, knowledge base and community answers — into personalized self-service and in-app experiences across customer support, success and experience teams. Founded in Tel Aviv, Zoomin was acquired by Salesforce on November 1, 2024 and now powers the Unified Knowledge and Agentforce/Data Cloud offerings. Its products include the Content Delivery Platform, Documentation Portal, In-Product Help, Zoomin for ServiceNow, Unified Knowledge and Zoomin Analytics. Zoomin does not publish a public, self-serve developer API surface; its integrations are delivered through customer implementations and the Salesforce platform. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio company.

providers.name: Zzish
providers.description: Zzish is an EdTech company (a Techstars-backed startup) building a K-12 learning product suite used by teachers and students across 180 countries. Its flagship product, Quizalize, is a classroom quiz and formative-assessment platform; the portfolio also includes Blockerzz (a 3D game engine with quiz games and coding tutorials), Marvely.ai (AI-powered, exam-aligned language tutoring), Quizalize Insights (leadership dashboards for tracking academic progress), and QUAT (a customer-analytics platform for schools and EdTech partners). Zzish reports 250k+ teachers onboarded in the last two years and 250m+ questions answered since launch. As of this enrichment pass, Zzish publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer-documentation surface.

providers.name: Acre Open Data
providers.description: Acre Open Data is a state government open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 20 datasets.

providers.name: Aitomatic
providers.description: Aitomatic, Inc. (Palo Alto, CA) builds DanaOS, an operating system for industrial AI. DanaOS is a governed, neurosymbolic, self-improving platform that runs autonomous AI agents inside a customer's own boundary — for semiconductor fabs, building and process operations, energy grids, and heavy industry. It combines neural flexibility with symbolic precision: a Sector Ontology encodes domain expertise as executable knowledge, Small Specialist Agents (SSAs) reason over it in a See-Think-Act-Reflect loop, and a governance substrate (the Dana Ontologist) verifies every action against ontology and policy before it commits — all deployable on-prem and air-gapped. Aitomatic is a founding member of the AI Alliance and publishes the open-source Dana agent-native language, the OpenSSA framework, and SemiKong, the first open-source semiconductor-industry LLM. Founded by Christopher Nguyen (CEO).

providers.name: AO Smith
providers.description: A. O. Smith Corporation is a global manufacturer of residential and commercial water heaters, boilers, and water treatment products. AO Smith offers connected water heater products with IoT capabilities through its iCOMM connected technology platform, enabling remote monitoring and control of water heating systems via mobile app and third-party integrations.

providers.name: APA Corporation
providers.description: APA Corporation is an independent energy company that explores for, develops, and produces natural gas, crude oil, and natural gas liquids, with operations in the United States, Egypt, the United Kingdom, and Suriname. Organized in Delaware and headquartered in Houston, Texas, APA is listed on Nasdaq (APA) and listed on Nasdaq Texas since March 2026.

providers.name: Astro Sea
providers.description: Astro (PT Astro Technologies Indonesia), operating at astronauts.id, is an Indonesian quick-commerce platform that delivers groceries and everyday essentials in as little as 15 minutes. Its consumer mobile apps (iOS and Android) offer more than 3,000 curated products spanning fresh produce, frozen goods, groceries, beauty, household items, and electronics, with 24/7 service across the Greater Jakarta (JADETABEK) region. Astro is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was surfaced through that portfolio into the API Evangelist network. Astro is a business-to-consumer application company; it publishes a consumer app, a corporate site, and an RFC 9116 security contact, but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal.
