providers.description: Bahia Open Data is a state government open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 21 datasets.

providers.name: Besoundbreast
providers.description: BeSound (Besoundbreast) is a women's-health technology platform offering modern, radiation-free breast imaging using ABUS ultrasound to help find cancers that mammograms can miss, particularly in women with dense breast tissue. BeSound connects patients with independent partner medical groups who deliver the imaging; results reach a secure patient portal within 24-48 weekday hours. Screening breast ultrasound is $349, with locations in Los Angeles (Melrose Ave) and Beverly Hills. BeSound is a consumer healthcare service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and the machine-readable llms.txt it publishes for AI agents.

providers.name: Biostate AI
providers.description: Biostate AI is a Houston-based precision-health biotechnology company combining proprietary wet-lab chemistry with generative AI to make RNA and DNA sequencing dramatically cheaper and more accessible. Its BIRT (Barcode-Integrated Reverse Transcription) plus PERD (Probes for Excess RNA Depletion) platform delivers Total RNA sequencing from around $60 per sample, and its N-Act and RNAstate AI models turn omics data into clinical insights for autoimmune, cardiovascular, and cancer diagnostics. The company operates a cloud data lake for AI-ready omics data and runs research partnerships across the U.S., India, and China. As of this profile Biostate publishes a marketing and publications site plus open research model repositories on GitHub, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK client library, or developer portal.

providers.name: Blink Charging
providers.description: Blink Charging Co. (Nasdaq BLNK) operates the Blink Network of Level 2 and DC Fast electric vehicle chargers across North America and Europe, alongside brands acquired via SemaConnect, Blue Corner, BlueLA, and Envoy. Blink's charger hardware (Series 7/8/9) is OCPP 2.0.1 certified for CSMS interoperability, and in 2025 Blink joined Hubject's Intercharge eRoaming platform as a charge point operator using the OCPI protocol so third-party e-mobility service providers can route drivers and billing to Blink stations. Blink also runs a gated BlinkMap API developer program (station locations, hours, and live network status) and a Blink Fleet platform that partners such as Presto and BetterFleet integrate with via API for fleet charging, sessions, and billing. None of these programs currently publish a full public self-serve API reference; access requires signing up directly with Blink.

providers.name: Bloomy
providers.description: Bloomy (bloomylearning.com) is an AI-powered adaptive learning platform for K-12 students, founded by Alex Southmayd and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch). The product diagnoses each student's knowledge gaps, builds a personalized standards-aligned learning path across English Language Arts, Math, and Writing, and delivers Socratic AI tutoring plus mastery-based practice, requiring 90%+ mastery before a student advances. It integrates third-party diagnostic/assessment data (i-Ready, NWEA MAP) and provides a real-time teacher dashboard. Bloomy serves traditional districts, charter schools, homeschools, and microschools, and sells to families via monthly or annual subscriptions (with ESA/EFA fund eligibility in some states). As of this profile Bloomy publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; this record captures its verified public identity and legal/account surface only.

providers.name: Bodyport
providers.description: Bodyport is a San Francisco healthcare technology company delivering remote heart-failure monitoring. Its FDA-cleared Cardiac Scale captures hemodynamic biomarkers through a patient's feet in under 30 seconds and transmits the readings over cellular to care teams within minutes. The company's Congestion Index algorithm combines multiple hemodynamic biomarkers to detect worsening heart failure earlier than standard weight-based rules, and its connected Care Platform surfaces monitoring, alerts, and care coordination through a clinical dashboard and a patient portal. Bodyport works with health systems and pharma partners including Geisinger, Boehringer Ingelheim, Stanford, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Duke, and Yale. The company publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its product, portal, and compliance surfaces.

providers.name: BridgeCare Finance
providers.description: BridgeCare (getbridgecare.com) is an integrated, modular software platform for the early care and education (ECE) system. It gives state agencies, cities and counties, child care resource and referral organizations (CCR&Rs), nonprofits, and school districts one system to run Pre-K program administration, family navigation, coordinated eligibility and enrollment, centralized eligibility screening, licensing, workforce development, quality management (QRIS), grants management, subsidy administration, tri-share administration, and program assurance. The platform is used by 500,000+ families, 50,000+ providers, and 500+ counties. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, BridgeCare is backed by Techstars and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. BridgeCare operates an API host but publishes no public OpenAPI or developer documentation, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Brumbrum
providers.description: Brumbrum is an Italian online used-car marketplace, part of the pan-European Aramis Group, that sells certified pre-owned vehicles fully online with home delivery, financing, trade-in (permuta), warranty coverage, a 14-day return trial and a best-price guarantee. Vehicles are inspected and reconditioned at its Reggio Emilia facility (300+ quality checks) with retail presence near Milan. Brumbrum is a consumer e-commerce brand rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification. This profile in the API Evangelist network captures the company's public web identity and the security/discovery signals probed from its domain.

providers.name: Candy Fanatics (fka Candy Digital)
providers.description: Candy Digital (branded simply as "Candy") is a digital collectibles platform operating at candy.io under the tagline "Crave. Collect. Connect." It is best known for officially licensed Major League Baseball (MLB) digital trading cards and NFT drops, sold through a consumer-facing, wallet-native web application for buying, collecting, and trading licensed digital collectibles. Founded in 2021 and backed by investors including Insight Partners, the company runs an active consumer product (e.g. the 2026 MLB Base Series drops). The former candy.com domain has since been divested and is now listed for acquisition via Hilco Digital Assets; the live brand and product run at candy.io. Candy Digital is a consumer-facing product and does not currently publish a public API program, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI — this profile captures its real public web surface.

providers.name: Defense Technical Information Center
providers.description: The Defense Technical Information Center (DTIC) is the U.S. Department of Defense field activity that acquires, manages, and disseminates scientific and technical information from DoD-funded research, development, test, and evaluation. DTIC operates a public Research and Engineering (R&E) Gateway, the Discover service for searching technical reports, the DoDTechSpace and Minsky natural-language platforms for defense researchers, and Dimensions for collaborative discovery. Most DTIC services require authentication tied to DoD or registered-user roles. DTIC does not publicly publish a developer API, though tools such as Dimensions and Minsky offer programmatic capabilities to authorized users.

providers.name: Drag Bot
providers.description: drag&bot is a web-based industrial robotics software platform for the intuitive setup, programming, and operation of industrial robots without prior robotics or coding skills. Founded in Stuttgart in 2016 and acquired by KEBA in 2021, it lets production workers assemble robot programs by dragging and dropping reusable Function Blocks. The platform is built on ROS (Robot Operating System), making it vendor-neutral across robot brands such as KUKA, ABB, Universal Robots, FANUC, Denso, Kinova, and Aubo, as well as a wide range of grippers and peripheral tools. Developers extend the platform with Python/JSON Function Blocks and ROS-based Components (hardware drivers), and integrate with factory equipment over Modbus TCP/IP and MQTT. drag&bot has been integrated into KEBA's Kemro X automation platform. Its programmatic surface is exposed as ROS services, topics, and messages rather than a public REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Education Holdings 1 (The Princeton Review)
providers.description: Education Holdings 1 operates The Princeton Review, an educational services company offering standardized test preparation, one-on-one and on-demand tutoring, and college, graduate, medical, and law school admissions counseling. The Princeton Review prepares students for the SAT, ACT, PSAT, AP, MCAT, DAT, OAT, LSAT, GRE, GMAT, SSAT, ISEE, and SHSAT through live, self-paced, and honors courses, publishes college and graduate school rankings and guidebooks, and provides free practice tests, events, and study resources. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. The Princeton Review operates a consumer web presence rather than a public developer program; it publishes an llms.txt AI-discovery file but does not expose a documented public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Finn
providers.description: FINN (finn.com) is a Munich-based consumer car-subscription service that lets individuals and businesses lease a car on a flexible monthly subscription, with insurance, maintenance, registration, taxes, and roadside assistance bundled into one all-inclusive price. Subscribers pick from more than twenty vehicle brands on terms from six to twenty-four months, and the company also runs a fleet/business offering. Backed by HV Capital, FINN operates in Germany, the United States, and other European markets. FINN is a consumer, direct-to-customer business with no public developer API or partner API program surfaced at this time; this profile captures its public web, security, and legal surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: grasp
providers.description: Grasp is a members-based, AI-powered learning platform based in London, England that builds personalized, AI-curated short courses. Learners discuss a goal with an AI mentor, which co-creates a syllabus and assembles a structured "learning path" from the clearest, most credible resources on the web - organized into focused, roughly hour-long lessons with clear outcomes and practice exercises. Grasp is delivered as a client-rendered React single-page app with a 14-day free trial and a single monthly membership; a selection of public courses and lessons is browsable without an account, and a sister product, Grasp Concepts, lives at concepts.grasp.study. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and point-nine.

providers.name: Gyant
providers.description: Gyant was a San Francisco-based digital health company that built an AI-powered conversational virtual assistant for health systems, guiding patients through symptom checking, care navigation, and triage across web and messaging channels. In 2022 Gyant was acquired by Fabric (fabrichealth.com), and gyant.com now redirects to Fabric's healthcare care-access platform, which combines conversational AI with physician-built clinical protocols for virtual care, patient engagement, and clinical automation. Gyant does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's identity, published legal/compliance surface, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Heven AeroTech
providers.description: Heven AeroTech (formerly Heven Drones) is a Dulles, Virginia headquartered manufacturer of hydrogen fuel-cell powered, runway-independent unmanned aircraft systems built for defense, national security and public safety missions. Founded in 2019, the company designs its own hydrogen propulsion stack and ships six named airframes — Raider, Z1, H2D55, Refueler, Atlas and Urban X — marketed on multi-hour endurance, low thermal and acoustic signature, and rapid payload and hydrogen-tank swaps. The Z1 is listed as a Blue UAS Select platform and the H2D55, Raider and Z1 are advertised as NDAA compliant. Heven operates sites in Dulles VA, Bingen WA, Mevo Carmel Israel and Mumbai India, and raised a $100M Series B led by IonQ. Heven AeroTech is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Highbeam
providers.description: Highbeam is a business banking and finance platform built for modern consumer brands (direct-to-consumer and e-commerce). It brings together operating and high-yield accounts, a charge card that pays cashback on advertising spend, working capital and credit lines, automated bill pay, and spend intelligence, alongside Luma, an applied-AI finance assistant. Banking services are delivered through partner banks (Thread Bank, member FDIC) and Airwallex. Highbeam is based in New York City. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification; this entry captures the company identity, its public web properties, and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Hitachi Construction Machinery
providers.description: Hitachi Construction Machinery provides operational data about machines and equipment on construction sites through the Telematics API, which complies with the ISO 15143-3 (AEMP 2.0) standard. The API enables higher efficiency, productivity, and safety while reducing life cycle costs.

providers.name: instabridge
providers.description: Instabridge is a global internet connectivity company operated by Degoo Backup AB in Stockholm, Sweden, and backed by Balderton Capital and Creandum. Its mobile apps give users access to a crowdsourced map of roughly 20 million free WiFi hotspots and to prepaid eSIM mobile-data plans covering 190+ countries with no roaming fees. With more than 200 million app downloads, Instabridge combines community-shared WiFi, pay-as-you-go global data, a data-saving browser, VPN, and cloud storage, and runs a distribution-partner program for prepaid top-up resellers. It is a consumer app company with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Instride Health
providers.description: InStride Health is a virtual mental health provider delivering specialized, insurance-based treatment for children, teens, and young adults ages 7 to 24 who struggle with anxiety, OCD, panic, phobias, school avoidance, and related disorders. Its structured four-to-eight month program pairs each patient with a coordinated care team of a therapist, a psychiatric prescriber, and an exposure coach, combining evidence-based cognitive behavioral therapy and exposure-and-response prevention delivered over telehealth. The company is backed by General Catalyst and tracked in the API Evangelist network; it operates as a clinical care provider and publishes no public API, developer program, or SDK.

providers.name: Intact Financial
providers.description: Intact Financial Corporation is the largest provider of property and casualty insurance in Canada, headquartered in Toronto and trading on the TSX as IFC. It underwrites personal auto, personal property, and commercial P&C lines through the Intact Insurance, belairdirect, BrokerLink, Intact Prestige, Intact Public Entities, and On Side Restoration brands in Canada, through Intact Insurance Specialty Solutions in the United States, and through Intact Insurance UK, EU, IE and 123.ie internationally following the 2021 acquisition of RSA. Distribution runs through a network of more than 6,000 independent broker offices plus direct-to-consumer channels. Its API posture is partner-gated and closed. There is no public, self-serve developer portal, no published API reference, and no downloadable OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI artifact on any Intact domain probed. developer/developers/docs/api subdomains on intactfc.com and intact.ca do not resolve; /developers, /api, /developer and /partners return 404. The only integration surfaces are login walls — the Intact Portal for brokers at portal.intactinsurance.com (brokers.intact.ca redirects there) and the customer Client Centre behind IBM Security WebSEAL at apps.intactinsurance.com. Broker connectivity in Canada is mediated by CSIO, the industry standards body whose EDI, XML, eDocs and JSON API standards are the Canadian analogue of ACORD. Intact Insurance is listed in the CSIO member directory but appears on none of CSIO's certified-member lists (eDocs, CL Data, Compliance/Z-code, API Security Standards, JSON API Standards) and is recorded as "Not Yet Rated" on both the personal and commercial tracks of CSIO's 2026 Standards Certification Ratings. No ACORD reference was found anywhere on the company's public web properties.

providers.name: Juniper Behavioral Health
providers.description: Juniper Behavioral Health (now operating as Camber, camber.health) is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) software company for specialty and behavioral health providers. Founded in 2021 and backed by a16z, Y Combinator, and Craft Ventures, the company automates medical billing, claims processing, denial management, and payment analytics so behavioral and specialty clinicians (ABA, PT, ENT, allergy) can collect more from insurance and spend less time on administrative overhead. Their platform is built on AI systems trained on more than $2.5B in claims data. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from the public Camber website; the company exposes a customer web application (app.camber.health) and a published responsible-disclosure policy but no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Kickstarter
providers.description: Kickstarter is a public-benefit crowdfunding platform where creators launch funding campaigns for creative projects — film, music, art, design, games, technology, publishing, and more — and backers pledge money to help bring them to life on an all-or-nothing funding model. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Brooklyn, New York, it has channeled billions of dollars in pledges to hundreds of thousands of successfully funded projects. Kickstarter does not currently operate a public developer API program or developer portal; its GraphQL and REST endpoints power its own web and mobile clients and are not documented for third-party integration. The company does maintain an active open-source GitHub organization (including its iOS and Android app source), a help center, and a company blog. This API Evangelist profile tracks Kickstarter's public developer, security, and platform surface for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Komodor
providers.description: Komodor is an autonomous AI SRE platform for Kubernetes observability, troubleshooting, and operations across multiple clusters. The platform surfaces cluster events, deployment timelines, dependency maps, and remediation runbooks to help platform and SRE teams diagnose incidents faster. Komodor exposes a REST API plus a Terraform provider for managing clusters, services, monitors, and policies, authenticated with API keys generated from the User Settings page.

providers.name: Life is Tech
providers.description: Life is Tech, Inc. (ライフイズテック株式会社) is a Tokyo-based education technology company founded on 6 July 2010 by Yusuke Mizuno, delivering digital, programming and AI education to Japanese teenagers, schools, municipalities and employers. Its products are "Life is Tech !" IT camps and year-round schools for junior and senior high school students, "Life is Tech ! Lesson" — a cloud-based information and programming curriculum used by roughly 4,000 public and private schools across some 600 municipalities — "Life is Tech ! Leaders" for university students, "Life is Tech ! Career" digital job-hunting support, and DX Readiness corporate digital-skills training. The company is a certified B Corporation (October 2022, the first Japanese EdTech to certify) and holds the PrivacyMark. Life is Tech sells finished learning products to schools and consumers; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Loft Orbital
providers.description: Loft Orbital is a space infrastructure company operating under the banner "Space Made Simple" that integrates, launches, and operates low-Earth-orbit satellites so customers can fly physical payloads or deploy software "virtual missions" without building or operating their own spacecraft. Its Cockpit mission-control platform lets operators task payloads, monitor telemetry, and downlink data in real time through a secure web UI or an authenticated API, and a customer SDK provides frameworks, documentation, and satellite APIs (including Azure Orbital space-edge deploys) for onboard sensors and compute. The Cockpit API and developer docs are gated behind login at api.cockpit.loftorbital.com, so no public specification is available. Backed by Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Mobilize
providers.description: Mobilize (mobilize.io) is a community and learning software platform purpose-built for associations and professional networks, now operating under the Forj brand (forj.ai). The platform unifies member community and continuing education in one place through its products Forj Connect (peer-to-peer and group member communication), Forj Learn (a learning management system for continuing education, certification, and social learning), and Journey by Forj (a combined community-and-learning experience). Mobilize was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a member/admin web application (app.mobilize.io) and a Zendesk help center but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so this profile carries verified company identity and link properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.description: Modena Open Data is a municipal government open-data portal for Italy running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 111 datasets.

providers.name: Nabu
providers.description: Nabu is an AI-powered customs clearance platform that automates international trade compliance end to end. It collects shipment data from emails, PDFs, Excel files, databases, and TMS records via API, EDI, SFTP, or email, prepares complete compliant customs files, and generates pre-filled import/export declarations ready for submission in standard customs software. Nabu targets customs brokers and declaration teams, offering autonomous processing, workload flexibility to absorb staffing gaps, and full auditability across multiple regions and local regulatory regimes. Backed by Techstars. No public developer API, documentation, or SDKs are published at this time.

providers.name: Nextdata
providers.description: Nextdata OS is a unified, automated data management platform for unstructured and structured data, designed for AI and analytics workloads. Founded by Zhamak Dehghani (creator of the data mesh paradigm), Nextdata enables organizations to build autonomous data products with embedded governance and discovery.

providers.name: NGINX Service Mesh
providers.description: NGINX Service Mesh (NSM) is a service mesh from F5 NGINX powered by NGINX Plus, designed to manage container-to-container traffic in Kubernetes environments. It provides mTLS, traffic policies via the Service Mesh Interface (SMI), traffic splitting, rate limiting, observability (Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger), and integration with NGINX Plus Ingress Controller. NGINX Service Mesh exposes a control-plane REST API and a `nginx-meshctl` CLI for installation, sidecar injection, certificate management, and policy configuration. The upstream GitHub repository is archived; F5 announced End of Sale (EoS) for the NGINX Microservices Bundle as of July 1, 2023, and the project's successor for ingress and L7 routing is NGINX Gateway Fabric.

providers.name: Omni Network
providers.description: Omni Network is a crypto interoperability protocol that makes the entire multi-chain ecosystem feel like a single chain for users and developers. Its core product, SolverNet, is a network of solvers that fulfill cross-chain intents on a user's behalf, letting a dApp deployed on one chain be used by people whose funds live on another. Developers integrate SolverNet through the Omni SDK (the @omni-network/core and @omni-network/react TypeScript packages) to bridge, swap, deposit, and bundle arbitrary contract calls across any supported chain from a single frontend. The project is built on a Go/Cosmos-SDK monorepo with Solidity contracts and ships the OMNI ERC-20 token on Ethereum L1. In 2026 the company rebranded from Omni to Nomina, consolidated on Ethereum, and now also operates Nomina, a unified trading terminal for power users trading perpetual futures across decentralized exchanges. It is backed by Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, Two Sigma, Spartan Group, and Vessel.

providers.name: Petsapp
providers.description: PetsApp is a veterinary client engagement and practice communication platform used by more than 1,000 veterinary practices worldwide, with millions of pets registered and millions of dollars in payments processed. It gives clinics two-way SMS and in-app messaging, appointment booking, video consultations, digital payments, wellness and health-care plan management, automated reminders, and a lightweight CRM for building client relationships. PetsApp does not publish a public developer portal or open API; API access and documentation are offered privately to technology and PIMS integration partners through its partner program, and its public docs subdomain is a Jira Service Management customer help center rather than API reference documentation.

providers.name: Pipelinedb
providers.description: PipelineDB was a high-performance PostgreSQL extension for continuous, incremental aggregation of time-series data using continuous SQL views, avoiding the need to store raw event data. It also offered Stride, a hosted streaming-analytics API with first-party Python, JavaScript, and Go client SDKs, plus extensions for Apache Kafka and Amazon Kinesis ingestion. The company joined Confluent in 2019; the open-source extension reached a final 1.0.0 release (Apache-2.0) and is now archived, while the pipelinedb.com website and the hosted Stride service have been retired. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of DCVC.

providers.name: Play Versus
providers.description: Play Versus (PlayVS) is North America's leading scholastic and collegiate esports platform, operating competitive gaming leagues for middle schools, high schools, and colleges alongside an esports curriculum and college recruitment services. The platform partners with major publishers including Riot Games, EA, Blizzard, and Psyonix, and runs its competitions and rosters through the app.playvs.com web application. PlayVS is a consumer/education product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface; this profile captures its published identity, support, and policy properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Podchaser
providers.description: Podchaser provides one of the most comprehensive podcast databases, exposed through a GraphQL API designed to drive podcast discovery for listeners, podcasters, brands, and platform partners. The API surface is GraphQL-only and is therefore not represented as an OpenAPI specification in this index.

providers.name: Prepared
providers.description: Prepared is an AI-powered emergency response platform for 911 communications, now operating as the intelligence layer of Axon 911. Its assistive AI helps call-takers, dispatchers, and supervisors across the emergency response lifecycle with non-emergency call triage and deflection, real-time transcription and automated detail capture, live translation (40+ spoken languages and 200+ for text), multi-channel dispatch monitoring, and real-time quality assurance and training. The company reports supporting 1,000+ PSAPs (public safety answering points) and protecting 90M+ people, with claims of up to 50% faster call processing. Prepared is backed by a16z and General Catalyst and was surfaced through the API Evangelist venture-portfolio pipeline. The company runs a hosted dispatch console at preparedapp.com but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: PuTTY
providers.description: PuTTY is a free and open-source terminal emulator, serial console and network file transfer application. It supports several network protocols, including SCP, SSH, Telnet, rlogin, and raw socket connection.

providers.name: Rondonia Open Data
providers.description: Rondonia Open Data is a state government open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 14 datasets.

providers.name: Santa Catarina Open Data
providers.description: Santa Catarina Open Data is a state government open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 112 datasets.

providers.name: Sarwa
providers.description: Sarwa is a UAE-based fintech platform and mobile app that lets everyday investors trade U.S. stocks and ETFs, invest passively through managed portfolios, and save in high-yield accounts, all in one place. The company is regulated by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) of the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) and operates as Sarwa Digital Wealth (Capital) Limited. Sarwa is a portfolio company of 500 Global and offers consumer products (Sarwa Trade, Sarwa Invest, Sarwa Save) through its web and mobile apps; it does not currently publish a public developer API. This profile captures the company's public identity, security posture, and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Seaboard
providers.description: Seaboard Corporation is a diverse global agribusiness and transportation company involved in pork, commodity merchandising, grain processing, sugar production, electric power generation, and ocean transportation.

providers.name: Serve First
providers.description: Serve First is a UK-based AI-driven customer experience (CX) platform that unifies reviews, surveys, receipts, in-location feedback terminals, operational audits, and mystery shopping into a single dashboard. It turns real-time customer feedback into role-based, actionable insight, with sentiment analysis and unified reporting across retail, hospitality, facilities management, health & wellness, and franchise businesses. Serve First also provides Client Connect journey/workflow automation and Martyn's Law public-protection compliance management. Serve First does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; this profile captures company identity plus verified security and compliance posture (SOC 2 and ISO 27001 via a Sprinto-hosted trust center).

providers.name: Somethings
providers.description: Somethings is a teen mental health support platform that connects adolescents with Certified Peer Specialist Mentors through a mobile app for iOS and Android. Rather than traditional therapy or AI chatbots, teens can call or chat anytime with trained mentors who have personal lived experience overcoming challenges like anxiety, depression, self-harm, eating disorders, and ADHD, backed by clinical supervision. The service is HIPAA-compliant and sold to health plans, insurers, employers, and directly to parents. Somethings is a venture-backed company in the API Evangelist network; it operates a consumer/clinical mobile product and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Sonder
providers.description: Sonder is a hospitality company that designs, leases, and operates a global portfolio of boutique, design-forward apartment-style accommodations and hotels for short- and extended-stay travelers. Guests book directly through Sonder's website and mobile app, where a tech-enabled experience spans contactless check-in, in-app service requests, and 24/7 local support across cities in North America, Europe, and the Middle East. In 2024 Sonder entered a long-term licensing agreement with Marriott that lists its properties in the Marriott Bonvoy program. The company is publicly traded and was backed by venture investors including Greylock. Sonder publishes no public developer API; the only machine-facing surface documented here is its responsible security-disclosure program and the site's domain-security posture.

providers.name: Squire
providers.description: Squire is a barbershop management software platform that gives barbers and shop owners the tools to run their business: online booking and scheduling, client management and loyalty, integrated payment processing with same-day deposits, a custom-branded client mobile app, point-of-sale, inventory and business analytics. Booking is surfaced through Google, Instagram and Squire's own consumer channels. Squire operates as a closed SaaS product with login-gated web and mobile applications; no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or partner/integration program is published as of this profile. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of CRV, ICONIQ Capital and Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: StepStone Group
providers.description: StepStone Group is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The StepStone Group API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Take-Two Interactive Software API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: TCP/IP
providers.description: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the foundational communication protocol suite that powers the internet and most computer networks. It provides reliable, ordered delivery of data between applications across diverse network hardware through a layered architecture of protocols. The suite encompasses protocols at multiple layers including TCP, IP, UDP, HTTP, and many others, defined through IETF RFCs maintained at the RFC Editor.

providers.name: Tenstorrent
providers.description: Tenstorrent is an AI hardware company designing Tensix and Tensix++ based AI accelerators on the open RISC-V architecture, including the Wormhole and Blackhole generations of cards, the TT-QuietBox workstation, and the Galaxy Blackhole 6U server housing 32 Blackhole chips. The company is unusual in the AI silicon space for shipping a fully open-source software stack including TT-Metal (the low-level kernel and operator library), TT-Forge (an MLIR-based compiler for PyTorch, JAX, and ONNX), TT-MLIR, TT-XLA, the TT-Inference-Server, and RISC-V cores and toolchains. Pricing is published from 999 dollars for an entry card up to 440,000 dollars for a base Galaxy supercluster. Tenstorrent does not currently offer a public hosted-inference API, so this profile catalogs hardware, SDKs, compilers, and open-source repositories rather than an HTTP API surface.

providers.name: Terminal
providers.description: Terminal (terminal.io) is a talent platform for hiring vetted remote and nearshore software engineers for full-time, contract, and contract-to-hire roles. It combines AI-fluency assessment and technical vetting (accepting roughly the top 7% of applicants) with Employer of Record (EOR) services that handle HR, payroll, and benefits across 180+ countries, sourcing engineers from Latin America, Canada, and Europe. Terminal is a B2B staffing and hiring platform rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by 8VC and Lightspeed Venture Partners; added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: The Coca-Cola Company
providers.description: The Coca-Cola Company is the world's largest non-alcoholic beverage company, owning and marketing more than 200 brands across sparkling soft drinks, water, hydration, sports, coffee, tea, juice, dairy, and plant-based drinks. The company sells its products in more than 200 countries through a bottling and distribution partner network. While Coca-Cola does not currently publish a broadly available public REST API, it is a heavy enterprise API consumer running an internal API program on MuleSoft that connects ERP, manufacturing, distribution, retail, marketing, and consumer engagement systems through a Center for Enablement (C4E) model. Historical Coca-Cola Enterprises (CCE) Product and Location APIs at developer.cokecce.com are no longer maintained as a public-facing developer program.

providers.name: TrueCare24
providers.description: TrueCare24 is a nationwide care platform providing care professionals and services for home and business. Its offerings span in-home care, on-demand healthcare staffing, visiting nurses, behavioral health and counseling, and workplace health programs including flu vaccination, diabetes screening, and COVID-19 testing and vaccination services. A 500 Global portfolio company, TrueCare24 operates customer dashboards and a provider portal but publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: Vedanta Biosciences
providers.description: Vedanta Biosciences is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 19 Blackstone Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded by PureTech Health together with a group of scientific co-founders who pioneered the modern understanding of cross-talk between the human microbiome and the immune system. The company develops a potential new category of oral Live Biotherapeutic Products built from rationally defined consortia of human commensal bacteria grown from pure clonal cell banks rather than donor-derived stool, and it maintains technical expertise in the manufacture of live organisms. Its lead program, VE303, is an eight-strain defined bacterial consortium in the global Phase 3 RESTORATiVE303 registrational study for the prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, following Phase 2 results showing a greater than 80% reduction in the odds of CDI recurrence versus placebo; VE202 is in development for inflammatory bowel disease and VE707 for prevention of multidrug-resistant organism infections. Vedanta has raised a $68 million Series D and a $106.5 million financing, and its programs are supported by non-dilutive awards from BARDA and CARB-X. Vedanta is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it runs a WordPress marketing and corporate site, publishes no developer portal, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract, and an August 2026 probe of vedantabio.com found no OpenAPI, no /llms.txt, no MCP endpoint, no A2A agent card and an empty /.well-known/ discovery surface.

providers.name: Verint Systems
providers.description: Verint Systems is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Verint Systems API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Wikifolio
providers.description: wikifolio (wikifolio Financial Technologies AG) is a European social- and copy-trading platform that lets everyday investors follow, compare, and invest in the strategies of experienced traders. Traders build virtual portfolios ("wikifolios") that are published transparently; in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland the best-performing wikifolios can be securitized as exchange-listed wikifolio certificates that investors buy through their bank or broker. The platform surfaces thousands of trading ideas with published rules, fees, and live performance tracking. wikifolio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and is profiled in the API Evangelist network; it does not appear to publish a public developer API at this time.

providers.name: AMP Robotics
providers.description: AMP Robotics (operating as AMP Sortation) is an artificial-intelligence company for the waste and recycling industry that designs, builds, and operates advanced, cost-competitive facilities to process single-stream recycling and municipal solid waste. Its Smart Sortation technology suite combines computer vision (real-time material characterization), high-speed air-jet sortation (Jet and MicroJet), and robotic-arm sortation (Delta) to raise material-recovery rates, cut contamination, and extend landfill life. The flagship AMP ONE platform delivers fully automated, facility-scale sortation processing from 10K to 1M+ tons annually for waste haulers, material-recovery facilities, and municipalities. AMP Robotics is a Google Ventures (GV) portfolio company. No public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; this profile is maintained for network discovery and identity.

providers.name: AvantStay
providers.description: AvantStay is a technology-enabled luxury vacation rental management and hospitality company operating professionally designed short-term rental homes built for group travel across premium destinations throughout the United States. Beyond curated beachfront villas, desert estates, and mountain cabins, AvantStay runs a full-service homeowner property-management program through its Lighthouse owner portal, a 24-hour guest concierge, and a real-estate brokerage for buyers acquiring investment vacation homes. It is a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital tracked in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass AvantStay publishes a consumer booking website and homeowner portal but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Bayer
providers.description: Bayer is a German multinational pharmaceutical and life sciences company operating across pharmaceuticals, consumer health, and crop science. Bayer does not publish a single corporate-level public developer portal; integration is delivered through enterprise partner programs, the Bayer Crop Science Climate FieldView ecosystem (partner-gated APIs and certified-partner integrations), pharmacovigilance and clinical-trial data exchange, and EDI / x12 channels with distributors and pharmacy benefit managers.

providers.name: Bellhops
providers.description: Bellhops (branded as Bellhop) is a US technology-enabled moving-services company that operates an online booking platform for residential and commercial relocations. Customers get a free estimate and reserve local moves, long-distance relocations, hourly moving labor, packing help, and last-minute moves with no money down, then manage their reservation through an online dashboard staffed by background-checked movers. The company reports more than 300,000 completed moves and a 4.8/5 average rating across 20,000+ reviews. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and Initialized Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Bellhops is a consumer-facing service with no publicly documented API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface as of this profile.

providers.name: Biobeat
providers.description: Biobeat Technologies is an Israeli med-tech company whose remote patient monitoring (RPM) health-AI platform pairs a disposable short-term chest-monitor and a reusable long-term wrist-monitor - both using a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor - to continuously track up to 13 vital signs, including FDA-cleared cuffless blood pressure, pulse rate, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation, temperature, stroke volume, cardiac output, and one-lead ECG (chest-monitor). Readings stream to Biobeat's HIPAA- and GDPR-compliant, cloud-based patient management platform, where clinicians view real-time data, trends, and configurable alerts. Biobeat offers programmatic data access and EMR/EHR integration as a paid add-on for hospitals, health systems, and research partners; there is no publicly documented self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Bizible Marketing Analytics
providers.description: Bizible was a B2B marketing attribution and revenue analytics platform that connected marketing activity to pipeline and revenue across advertising, web, CRM, and marketing-automation channels. Acquired by Marketo in 2018 and subsequently by Adobe, the product now ships as Adobe Marketo Measure (formerly Bizible); the bizible.com domain 301-redirects to Adobe and its product documentation has moved to the Adobe Experience League. It has no standalone public developer portal, OpenAPI, or API reference of its own — integration is handled through Adobe/Marketo Measure and CRM connectors.

providers.name: Blidz
providers.description: Blidz is a membership-based social and gamified e-commerce platform ("Make Money, Save Money, Have Fun") offering deeply discounted deals across grocery, electronics, home goods, and other consumer categories through its iOS and Android shopping apps. Backed by General Catalyst, Blidz operates a consumer mobile marketplace rather than a public developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or public API surface. This APIs.json profile captures the company identity and the security posture of its public web domain.

providers.name: Booqed
providers.description: BOOQED is a Hong Kong-based proptech company building flexible workplace technology that turns underutilized real estate into bookable, on-demand workspace. Its flagship product QUBIC is a line of sound-isolating, modular smart booths and work pods (for one to six people) with soundproofing, ventilation, power, and a proprietary access-control system managed through a mobile web app. Alongside the hardware, BOOQED offers space-management SaaS that makes existing meeting rooms and desks bookable and trackable with utilization analytics, plus the BOOQED app for individuals to book hot desks and meeting rooms on demand across Hong Kong, Singapore, and Shenzhen. Founded by David Wong, Charles Oh, and Ken Huang, BOOQED went through the Colliers and Techstars proptech accelerator and raised seed funding in 2019. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; BOOQED does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Brelyon
providers.description: Brelyon is an MIT Media Lab spin-off building headset-free virtual displays — desktop monitors that use electro-optics and computational rendering to produce monocular image depth rather than autostereoscopic 3D. Its Ultra Reality line delivers a 122-inch virtual screen filling roughly 110 degrees of field of view, alongside Ultra Reality Extend (a multi-focal monitor that renders AI-generated overlays at different depths), Ultra Reality Mini, and experimental Hyper Displays. The company is headquartered in San Mateo, California with an international office in Taichung, Taiwan, and sells into enterprise simulation, training, teleoperation and medical visualization; prosumer flight simulation, gaming, trading and content production; and automotive in-vehicle HMI integration. Brelyon ships desktop software (Brelyon Suite, Focal Studio, Visual Engine, Stream Weaver) for distortion correction, monitor merging and multi-focal content creation, but publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK.

providers.name: Carbon Robotics
providers.description: Carbon Robotics is a Seattle-based physical-AI and agricultural robotics company building autonomous systems that help farmers cut costs and reduce chemical use. Its flagship LaserWeeder G2 uses computer vision and high-power lasers to eliminate weeds without herbicides, and its Carbon Autonomy product adds remote-supervised autonomy to compatible John Deere tractors. The underlying Carbon AI Large Plant Model is trained on 150 million labeled plants across 15 countries and 100+ crops. Carbon Robotics operates a customer grower cloud portal and Starlink-connected fleet control, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal as of this profiling.

providers.name: Character.AI
providers.description: Character.AI is a consumer conversational-AI platform that lets users create and chat with AI personas (Characters) via web and mobile apps. Character.AI does not publish a public developer API; product surfaces are accessed through the consumer apps. Community-maintained reverse-engineered clients exist but are unofficial and unsupported.

providers.name: Chi Longevity
providers.description: Chi Longevity is a Singapore-based longevity medicine and healthy-aging clinic that focuses on biological-age optimization rather than reactive medicine, built on The Maier Method developed by co-founder Professor Andrea Maier. The practice combines precision health mapping (blood panels, genetic and cognitive testing, cardiovascular and metabolic analysis), flagship and specialised longevity programmes, cognitive and physical training, a branded NMN supplement, and ongoing support through health coaching, physician and dietitian consultations, and a client portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is currently published, so this profile carries the company identity, domain-security posture, and published web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Choice Hotels
providers.description: Choice Hotels International (NYSE: CHH) is a United States hotel franchisor headquartered in North Bethesda, Maryland, operating 7,575 hotels with 656,825 rooms open across 49 states, the District of Columbia and 50 countries and territories as of December 31, 2025. Its brands include Comfort, Quality, Clarion, Sleep Inn, Econo Lodge, Rodeway Inn, MainStay Suites, Suburban Studios, WoodSpring Suites, Everhome Suites, Cambria Hotels, Ascend Hotel Collection and the Radisson Americas brands. Choice sits on the supply side of the travel distribution chain as a franchisor rather than an owner: its proprietary choiceEDGE central reservation system pushes rate, inventory and availability to ChoiceHotels.com, the Choice Privileges mobile apps, the global distribution systems (Sabre, Amadeus), the OTAs (Expedia, Booking.com) and metasearch (Kayak, Tripadvisor), while its proprietary choiceADVANTAGE property management system runs the majority of its franchised properties. API posture is honestly none-published — no public developer portal, no published API reference, no machine-readable contract, and no exit path. A TIBCO Mashery API gateway answers at api.choicehotels.com but every probed path returns ERR_596_SERVICE_NOT_FOUND, and developer.choicehotels.com is an unprovisioned Mashery CNAME returning 404 under a mashery.com certificate. All real integration is reached through gated franchisee and vendor channels (connect.choicehotels.com, choicecentral.com, the SkyTouch /CONNECT interface program) that require a commercial agreement.

providers.name: Club Feast
providers.description: Club Feast is a technology-enabled restaurant delivery and corporate catering company founded in 2020 by Atallah Atallah, Ghazi Atallah, and Chris Miao. It began as a subscription-based consumer meal service delivering signature dishes from neighborhood restaurants at deep discounts through a pre-order, scheduled batch-delivery model, and has since focused on corporate catering, group meal ordering with individual customization, event catering, and managed office pantry services for teams. Club Feast handles restaurant partnerships, menu curation, driver logistics, and delivery while employees select meals through its web app. The company raised seed funding led by General Catalyst and operates primarily in the San Francisco Bay Area. Club Feast does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or specification; this profile tracks its company identity and public web surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Clubessential
providers.description: Clubessential is a Cincinnati-based provider of club management software for private country, golf, city, athletic, and yacht clubs. Its cloud suite unifies club websites and mobile apps, tee-time and dining reservations, membership CRM, point-of-sale, accounting, business intelligence, and integrated payments so club staff can manage operations and member experiences from a single platform. Part of Clubessential Holdings (unified under Xplor Technologies alongside ClubReady, foreUP, Vermont Systems, PrestoSports, and Exerp), the company serves more than 1,300 private clubs and, with its sister brands, thousands of courses and clubs worldwide. Backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: CNC24
providers.description: CNC24 is a German online manufacturing platform for ordering custom CNC parts and precision components. Customers upload CAD files (STEP, STP, DWG, DXF, PDF and 3D data) and receive a binding quote within 48 hours, with production routed through a vetted network of 500+ manufacturers across 21 countries and roughly 5,500 machines. An AI-powered matching algorithm assigns each request to partners with the right expertise and production environment. Supported processes include CNC milling, turning, laser and waterjet cutting, sheet metal bending, punching, EDM, 3D printing, injection molding and die casting, serving aerospace, automotive, medical, robotics, construction and energy customers. The platform runs a fully digital workflow from quoting to delivery with order tracking, ISO 9001:2015 quality assurance, AES-256 encryption and anonymized drawings shared with partners. CNC24 is a Seedcamp portfolio company. No public developer API, SDKs or API documentation are published.

providers.name: Con.doit
providers.description: Con.doit (condoit.io) is a digital platform for electrical contractors that turns field-captured electrical infrastructure data into recurring service revenue. Its mobile capture app collects on-site photos, thermal scans, and system data, then generates same-day infrared thermography reports, auto-updating single-line diagrams, asset tags, arc flash studies, and NFPA 70B preventive-maintenance programs. Con.doit is a FLIR Global Approved App and reports over 4.5 million electrical assets under management across 2,000+ critical facilities nationwide. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification is currently published; this profile is enriched from the public marketing surface only.

providers.name: Cubic Corporation
providers.description: Cubic Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cubic Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Daupler
providers.description: Daupler provides a cloud-based Response Management System (RMS) for utilities, public works, and service organizations that automates and coordinates emergency and service-request response. Its product suite spans Daupler Answering (after-hours call center), Dispatch Assist and AI-driven call management, Callout crew notification, Notify mass notification via SMS/email/phone, Engage customer portal, Event Detection for multi-incident coordination, and Analytics for incident and team-performance insight. Daupler serves water, sewer, electric, multi-utility, trash-collection, and public-works operators. The RMS is built on RESTful services and integrates with CMMS, work-order, AMI, IoT sensor, billing, CIS, CRM, OMS, GIS, and citizen-request systems, though Daupler exposes no public self-serve developer API or documentation. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Defense Contract Audit Agency
providers.description: The Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA), under the authority, direction, and control of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller), provides audit and financial advisory services to Department of Defense and other federal entities responsible for acquisition and contract administration. DCAA publishes guidance, audit programs, and reports through its website but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Defense Contract Management Agency
providers.description: The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) is the Department of Defense component that works directly with defense suppliers to help ensure that DoD, federal, and allied government supplies and services are delivered on time, at projected cost, and meet performance requirements. DCMA performs contract administration, quality assurance, and earned value management oversight, but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Defense Finance and Accounting Service
providers.description: The Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) is the agency within the Department of Defense responsible for paying members of the U.S. military, DoD civilian employees, contractors, and annuitants, as well as providing finance and accounting services to DoD components and other federal agencies. DFAS exposes member-facing self-service portals such as myPay but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: defi SOLUTIONS
providers.description: defi SOLUTIONS is an auto and consumer lending technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Westlake, Texas. It provides cloud-native, API-enabled loan origination software (defi ORIGINATIONS), a servicing platform for account, collateral, and default management, digital borrower acquisition and self-service portals, and outsourced (BPO) managed servicing. The platform serves captive auto finance companies, banks, credit unions, and consumer finance companies, and ships 135+ pre-built partner integrations (Dealertrack, RouteOne, TransUnion, Equifax, LexisNexis, Experian, Black Book, J.D. Power, Zest AI, and more). APIs move borrower and loan data between origination and servicing but are exposed to enterprise customers and integration partners rather than through a public developer portal.

providers.name: Desjardins Group
providers.description: Desjardins Group (Mouvement Desjardins) is the largest cooperative financial group in North America, founded in 1900 in Lévis, Quebec by Alphonse Desjardins. It is a federation of caisses populaires (member-owned credit unions) rather than a share-capital chartered bank, comprising the Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec and its subsidiaries, the caisses in Quebec and the Caisse Desjardins Ontario Credit Union, regulated in Quebec by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). It holds roughly CAD $470 billion in assets and serves more than 7.8 million members and clients with personal, business, wealth-management and insurance products. On open finance, Desjardins publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification; developer.desjardins.com and other API-portal subdomains do not resolve, and consumer financial-data access is delivered today through third-party aggregators (Flinks, Plaid, Finicity, Tink) via screen-scraping/aggregator connectivity rather than a documented Desjardins API. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated (Budget 2024/2025, overseen by the FCAC) but not yet operational; as a cooperative outside the Big Six, Desjardins may opt in to Phase 1 rather than being mandated.

providers.name: Diagonal Therapeutics
providers.description: Diagonal Therapeutics is a Watertown, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2022 by CEO Alex Lugovskoy in partnership with Atlas Venture, developing "clustering" agonist antibodies that switch broken signaling pathways back on rather than inhibiting them. Its DIAGONAL product engine pairs computational epitope filtering with experimental screening — generating roughly 200,000 candidate antibody sequences per target, clustering them by predicted shape, binning by receptor complementarity and assembling multispecific antibodies from those bins — to make agonist antibody discovery tractable. The lead program, DIAG723, is a first-in-class ALK1:BMPRII clustering agonist antibody that restores ALK1 signaling; it holds US FDA and EMA orphan drug designation for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) and entered the Phase 1/2 DIAMOND trial (NCT07623525), with a first patient dosed in July 2026, alongside preclinical work in pulmonary arterial hypertension. The pipeline extends into hematology, hepatology, nephrology and cardiovascular disease. The company has raised roughly USD 255 million across a USD 128 million Series A (April 2024, co-led by BVF Partners and Atlas Venture) and an oversubscribed USD 125 million Series B (January 2026, co-led by Sanofi Ventures and Janus Henderson Investors). Diagonal is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it operates a Next.js marketing site backed by a Sanity CMS, and publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: DiversyFund
providers.description: DiversyFund is a San Diego based private-markets investment platform that packages institutional-style fixed income and multifamily real estate offerings for individual accredited investors. Formed in 2016 and qualified under SEC Regulation A+, the firm acts as sponsor, developer and manager of its own funds rather than as a broker, and reports having acquired more than $300 million across 20+ multifamily properties for a base of 28,000+ investors. Its current offering, the Distressed Income Fund, is a Reg D 506(c) preferred-equity vehicle sold to accredited investors with a target allocation of $100K to $1M. Investing is transacted through a private, authenticated investor portal at portal.diversyfund.com (WorkOS AuthKit); DiversyFund publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Divi Official
providers.description: Divi Official Inc. (Divi Growth Care) is a direct-to-consumer haircare and scalp-care brand formulated "for women by women," selling vegan, science-backed serums, shampoos, conditioners and supplements aimed at the hair-growth journey. The company operates an e-commerce storefront hosted on Shopify at diviofficial.com, with a subscription "Club Divi" program, a content blog, and a customer-account experience. Divi is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. It is a consumer packaged goods / beauty commerce business and does not publish a first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal; the only machine-readable surfaces on its domain are the Shopify Customer Accounts OAuth/OIDC discovery documents that the storefront platform exposes. This profile captures the company's public identity, web properties, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dollar Shave
providers.description: Dollar Shave Club is a direct-to-consumer men's grooming and personal-care brand founded in 2011 and acquired by Unilever in 2016, best known for pioneering the subscription razor model that ships blades, shave butter, skincare and body-care products to members on a recurring schedule. The company sells through its own e-commerce storefront (dollarshaveclub.com, built on Shopify) as well as retail channels, offering razor handles and cartridges, grooming kits and gift sets. It surfaces in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. Dollar Shave Club does not operate a public developer program or documented API; its digital surface is a consumer Shopify storefront whose only machine-discoverable interface is Shopify's customer-account OAuth/OIDC (including a customer-account MCP API scope) exposed at the store's /.well-known/ discovery endpoints.

providers.name: Easop
providers.description: Easop is a global equity compensation platform that helps startups and growing companies award and manage employee stock options and equity incentives across 70+ countries. It automates the legal workflows, board consents, country-specific tax and regulatory compliance, and employee education required to grant equity to international teams, and offers equity projection and compensation-grid planning plus integrations with cap-table tools such as Carta and Pulley. Easop was acquired by Remote in 2024. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Partech portfolio company; Easop is a business SaaS application and publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or well-known discovery surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Enurgen
providers.description: Enurgen is a solar energy software company whose DUET platform uses 3D physics-based modeling to optimize photovoltaic assets across their entire lifecycle. The platform spans three products - Design, Construction, and Operations - helping large-scale solar developers, independent power producers, EPC engineers, and asset managers improve energy yield estimates, validate construction against expected performance, and monitor plants in production to close the gap between forecasted (P50) and actual field output. Enurgen is a Techstars-backed company; customers include Scatec, Potentia, Lightsource, Eni, and Kiewit. The company operates a customer web application at app.enurgen.com but does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass that captures the company's public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: EquityBee
providers.description: EquityBee is a fintech marketplace that helps startup employees fund the exercise of their stock options before those options expire, giving them the cash needed to purchase their equity while the company is still private. On the other side of the marketplace, EquityBee connects accredited investors with the opportunity to invest in pre-IPO companies by funding those employee option exercises in exchange for a share of the future proceeds. Founded in 2018, the company operates a two-sided platform spanning startup employees, accredited investors, and the private companies whose equity underlies each funded position. EquityBee publishes a public marketing and account website but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: Fenergo
providers.description: Fenergo is a financial services SaaS platform for Client Lifecycle Management (CLM), Know Your Customer (KYC), client onboarding, transaction monitoring, and regulatory compliance. The Fenergo SaaS Platform exposes API specifications across Entity Data, Journey, ETL, Data Migration, External Data, Policy, Legal Entity Screening, Risk, Event Notification & Ingress, Portal, Review Journey Scheduling, and Transaction Monitoring domains.

providers.name: flatfair
providers.description: flatfair is a UK-based tenancy deposit platform for letting agents, landlords, and Build-to-Rent operators, offering deposit alternatives and deposit administration products. Its products include No Deposit (tenants pay 28% of one month's rent plus VAT instead of a five-week cash deposit), Deposits, Unlock Deposits, Deposit Boost, tenant Referencing, and Tenant Guarantor. flatfair is used by more than 850 agents and Build-to-Rent operators to reduce move-in friction and cut deposit administration time by around 60 minutes per tenancy. The company operates a web application for agents and tenants but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Flease
providers.description: Flease is a French vehicle-leasing marketplace offering flexible long-term (LLD, 24-50 month) and medium-term (LMD, 1-12 month) car and utility-vehicle rental to SMEs and small businesses. It sources quasi-new vehicles (under two years old, fewer than 30,000 km), delivers within a week for LMD and a month for LLD, and bundles a fleet-management web application (webapp.flease.fr) for tracking mileage, drivers, maintenance, contracts, and invoices. Flease positions on transparent pricing and a roughly 20% lower total cost of ownership versus traditional leasing, with a circular-economy angle of redeploying used vehicles. Backed by Partech. No public developer API or documentation is published; the customer-facing webapp is a Vue single-page app authenticated with AWS Cognito.

providers.name: Foresight
providers.description: Foresight is a predictive project-delivery platform for complex construction and infrastructure megaprojects, with a particular focus on data centers, government, and critical infrastructure. Founded by Dr. Atif Ansar and Igor Shifrin (Oxford) and headquartered in London, it layers on top of existing scheduling tools such as Microsoft Project and Excel to turn raw schedule data into forecasts, risk assessment, delay prediction, and portfolio-wide project assurance. The company reports managing $100B+ in mission-critical projects and is backed by Creandum and Macquarie Capital. Foresight is delivered as a SaaS web application and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Glass Health
providers.description: Glass Health is a San Francisco-based clinical AI company founded in 2021 by Dereck Paul (CEO) and Graham Ramsey (Head of Product) that builds an AI clinical decision support (CDS) and ambient scribing co-pilot for physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, residents, and medical students. The Glass platform combines large language model reasoning with curated, physician-reviewed clinical guidelines to generate ranked differential diagnoses, evidence-based assessment and plans, chart summaries, and direct answers to clinical questions ("Consult"), all delivered with inline citations. Glass also provides ambient scribing that listens during patient encounters and generates History and Physical notes, progress notes, discharge summaries, and patient-facing instructions, plus EHR integration via SMART on FHIR to pull demographics, problem lists, medications, laboratory values, vital signs, imaging, and encounter data into the workflow. Glass offers a tiered SaaS plan (Lite free tier, Starter at $20/month, Pro at $90/month, Max at $200/month) along with iOS and Android apps, and a public Glass Developer API ($250/month minimum, token-metered beyond the floor) that exposes the same clinical AI agent — Consult, Differential Diagnosis, Assessment and Plan, and Scribing endpoints — for third-party healthcare products. Glass is backed by Breyer Capital and graduated from Y Combinator's W23 batch, with roughly $6.5M in total disclosed funding. The provider does not publish an open OpenAPI specification or open-source SDKs; integration details are gated behind the developer portal and an enterprise contact at enterprise@glass.health.

providers.name: Grove Collaborative
providers.description: Grove Collaborative is a digital-first consumer products company and online marketplace for sustainable everyday household essentials — eco-friendly cleaning supplies, bamboo and recycled paper products, personal care, beauty, pet, and vitamins & supplements from hundreds of vetted brands. Orders meet strict ingredient standards and are carbon neutral, and the company operates as a plastic-neutral, sustainability-focused retailer sold through grove.co (a Shopify-hosted storefront) and retail partners. Grove is a public benefit company (NYSE: GROV) that was an early portfolio company of 500 Global and Bullpen Capital. It publishes no first-party developer API or public developer program; this profile captures its public web, security, and Shopify-platform discovery surface.

providers.name: H.B. Fuller Company
providers.description: H.B. Fuller Company is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The H.B. Fuller Company API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Hallow
providers.description: Hallow is the #1 Catholic and Christian prayer, meditation, and Bible app, offering guided daily prayer, the Rosary, Lectio Divina, the Examen, Christian meditation, faith-based sleep stories, Scripture readings, and audio-guided sessions led by well-known voices. Founded in 2018 and based in Chicago, Hallow is a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) with a subscription tier (Hallow Plus), and it runs programs for parishes, families, and gifting. Hallow does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile captures its public web and product surface. Backed by General Catalyst, Homebrew, and Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Halogen Capital
providers.description: Halogen Capital is Malaysia's first and only licensed digital asset fund manager, regulated by the Securities Commission Malaysia (License eCMSL/A0388/2023) and headquartered in Kuala Lumpur. The firm gives high-net-worth individuals, family offices, corporates, and institutional investors regulated access to cryptocurrency and traditional assets through unit trust structures, offering Shariah-compliant Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Crypto Titans basket funds alongside a MYR liquid fund, a ringgit income fund, and an enhanced income fund, all secured with multi-signature custody. Backed by Kenanga Investment Bank and 500 Global, Halogen manages roughly RM400 million in assets under management and is expanding into real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web presence and domain-security posture; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Happy5
providers.description: Happy5 is a Jakarta-based employee performance management platform, operated by Happy5 For The World Pte. Ltd. and founded in 2013, that unifies goal and OKR management, project tracking, and 360-degree performance reviews in one tool for HR teams. It automatically surfaces the goals hit, projects delivered, and milestones completed inside every performance review, and integrates with tools teams already use such as Jira, Asana, Slack, and Google Sheets. Its customers span major Indonesian banks, startups, and SMEs. Happy5 is a closed SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; this profile captures its verified public identity and web properties as a lead.

providers.name: Harbor Lab
providers.description: Harbor Lab is an AI-powered port cost and disbursement account (DA) management platform for the maritime industry, headquartered in Athens, Greece. Its cloud software helps shipowners, ship managers, charterers, and port agents manage port calls, validate and approve disbursement accounts, benchmark and negotiate port service pricing across a marketplace of thousands of port service providers, and automate payment and settlement — improving operational efficiency, digitizing the process, and delivering cost transparency across port cost management. The company is backed by Speedinvest, VentureFriends, Atomico, and others. As of this profile Harbor Lab exposes a web dashboard product only; no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Helloworld Travel
providers.description: Helloworld Travel Limited (ASX: HLO) is an Australian travel distribution group headquartered in Sydney, operating retail agency networks, corporate travel, wholesale packaging, air ticket consolidation and inbound tour operations across Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and Europe with more than 700 staff and over 2,700 retail members. It sits on the demand side of the travel distribution chain — an aggregator and reseller of third-party air, hotel and land content rather than an inventory owner — reaching travellers through its member agencies and reaching air supply through GDS-based consolidation and ticketing (Air Tickets, Express Tickets, SmartTickets). Its API posture is closed. There is no public developer portal, no OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI or Postman artifact, and no machine-readable contract of any kind. Every trade system is behind an agent login — ReadyRooms (B2B hotel and activity booking), AOTonline.net (inbound trade booking engine), Air Tickets and Express Tickets. A developer host is provisioned at developer.readyrooms.com.au but returns HTTP 401 with a Basic auth challenge on every path probed, so access is partner-only. There is no published exit path — the only documented way to get data back is a Privacy Act access request to the Helloworld Privacy Officer.

providers.name: Hidrate
providers.description: HidrateSpark is the world's smartest water bottle brand, tracking daily water intake with a Bluetooth-connected sensor puck that glows to remind you to drink and syncs to the HidrateSpark hydration app, Fitbit, and Apple Watch. The company (originally Hidrate, Inc., a Techstars-backed startup) sells its smart bottles and accessories through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at hidratespark.com. It does not publish a first-party developer or product API; the only machine-facing surface is the Shopify platform layer — OIDC/OAuth customer accounts and the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) agent-commerce endpoints that let buyer-approved AI shopping agents browse and check out.

providers.name: Hornet
providers.description: Hornet is a queer social networking platform operated by Queer Networks, Inc., serving the global LGBTQ+ community with more than 100 million users worldwide. The Hornet app combines profiles, feeds, live video, one-on-one video chat, messaging, and location-based discovery into a privacy-first digital home for gay men and the broader queer community. Backed by 500 Global (and previously part of BlueCity Holdings), Hornet operates as a consumer social/media company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs — so this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public identity, policy surface, and domain-security posture rather than developer artifacts. Hornet is number one in several key markets including France, Brazil, Turkey, and Taiwan, and monetizes through premium subscriptions and queer-audience advertising.

providers.name: Houst
providers.description: Houst is a global short-term rental and Airbnb management company founded in 2015, operating in 17 cities across 8 countries and managing over 11,650 properties. Houst handles the full hosting lifecycle for homeowners and landlords - multi-platform listing creation and optimization, dynamic pricing, professional photography, 24/7 guest communication and vetting, check-in coordination, cleaning, linen and maintenance - powered by a proprietary host dashboard that tracks earnings, occupancy, bookings and performance. The company operates on a commission model and also runs an operating-partner and affiliate programme.
