Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Hum Capital
providers.description: Hum Capital operates an AI-powered funding marketplace that connects growth companies with the right institutional capital. Through its Intelligent Capital Market platform, companies share their financial and operating data once and are matched to a network of 900+ lenders and investors for non-dilutive and structured financing (typically $1M-$50M), while investors receive curated, data-driven deal flow. Hum reports more than $700M in capital deployed across 6,000+ companies. Headquartered in New York, the company operates in the financial services, capital markets, and alternative-financing sector. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and enriched from the company's public web surface; Hum publishes no public developer API, so this entry is identity- and security-focused.

providers.name: Improbable
providers.description: Improbable (Improbable Worlds Ltd) is a London-based technology company and venture builder. Founded in 2012, it originally built SpatialOS, a distributed simulation and networking platform for large-scale real-time multiplayer games, and later Morpheus / M² (MSquared), a network of interoperable metaverse worlds. Today Improbable operates primarily as a venture builder and capital allocator, partnering with founders to launch and scale companies across AI, Web3 and the metaverse. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and the SoftBank Vision Fund. Its historical developer surface centered on the SpatialOS Platform SDK, Worker SDK and the `spatial` CLI (distributed via NuGet), plus the improbable-eng and spatialos GitHub organizations; the standalone documentation, status and IMS subdomains have since been retired as the company pivoted away from a standalone developer platform.

providers.name: INBOTIQA
providers.description: INBOTIQA is a UK-based fintech whose flagship product, YUDOmail, is an Intelligent Business Email and shared-mailbox management platform for high-volume group inboxes at banks, BPOs and financial-services operations teams. YUDOmail layers over Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace to turn incoming emails into assigned, trackable tasks with ownership, due dates, SLA tracking, machine-learning triage and sentiment analysis, audit trails and analytics, without replacing the underlying email platform. It deploys in the cloud or on-premises, integrates with Symphony chat and Microsoft Teams, and is used across KYC, FX, collateral, settlements and trade-support functions. INBOTIQA was a 2019 Barclays Accelerator (powered by Techstars) company.

providers.name: Industrious
providers.description: Industrious is a global flexible workspace provider operating private offices, dedicated and open coworking memberships, and on-demand meeting rooms across hundreds of locations worldwide. Members manage access, bookings, and workspace services through the Industrious member portal and iOS/Android mobile apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Fifth Wall and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Industrious publishes a consumer/member web and mobile experience but no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile therefore captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Instrumental
providers.description: Instrumental is a platform for manufacturing intelligence that helps companies detect and prevent product failures during the manufacturing process. The Instrumental API enables programmatic access to retrieve unit and inspection test data and metadata from Instrumental projects.

providers.name: InventoryQuant
providers.description: InventoryQuant automates inventory and contents documentation for the insurance claims industry. Public adjusters, restoration firms, and insurance claim handlers record video or audio walkthroughs of a loss, and the platform transcribes each spoken line item, detects and describes the contents, matches replacement pricing from major retailers, and generates a submission-ready report in XactContents or PDF format. It supports smart glasses, photos, multiple speakers, self-corrections, background noise, and 100+ languages, turning days of manual contents-claim work into minutes. Founded in the Y Combinator Winter 2026 batch by Sander Schulhoff.

providers.name: Jiraaf
providers.description: Jiraaf (Jiraaf Platform Private Limited, Bangalore, India) is an online fixed-income investment platform that lets retail investors discover, analyze, and invest in listed and secured bonds. Its curated product shelf spans listed corporate bonds, sovereign gold bonds, treasury bills, G-Secs and State Development Loans (SDLs), securitized debt instruments (SDIs), and fixed deposits, each surfaced with transparent yields, credit ratings, and a documented credit-evaluation process. Alongside the investing surface it publishes research reports, a bond analyser, a bond directory, a glossary, calculators, and educational content (Bond Gurukul webinars, blogs, and newsletters). Backed by Accel. Jiraaf is a consumer-facing web and mobile investing product and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kpt
providers.description: kpt is a package-centric toolchain that enables a configuration authoring, automation, and delivery experience, which simplifies managing Kubernetes platforms and KRM-driven infrastructure at scale by utilizing resource configuration as the artifact of record.

providers.name: Lagou
providers.description: Lagou (拉勾招聘) is a Chinese online recruitment platform operated by Beijing Lagou Network Technology Co., Ltd., focused on hiring for the internet and technology sector. It matches software engineers, product managers, designers and other digital-economy professionals with employers across major Chinese cities, publishing verified job listings alongside a browseable directory of hiring companies. Around the core job board it runs Lagou Enterprise (easy.lagou.com) for employer-side recruiting, Lagou Campus (xiaoyuan.lagou.com) for graduate hiring, and Lagou Education (kaiwu.lagou.com) for professional-skills courses. Lagou was surfaced through the Qiming Venture Partners portfolio. It publishes no public API, developer portal or API documentation — open.lagou.com carries a "Lagou Open Platform" title but serves only a stub page — so this profile captures the company's public web and security surface rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Lilium
providers.description: Lilium was a German eVTOL aircraft developer building the Lilium Jet, a seven-seat (including pilot) ducted-fan electric jet designed for regional air mobility with target cruise speeds around 175 mph and ranges in excess of 100 nautical miles. Lilium pursued concurrent EASA and FAA Type Certification and signed pre-orders with operators across Europe, the Middle East, the United States, Brazil, and Saudi Arabia. In October 2024 Lilium's board approved self-administration for its German subsidiaries after failing to secure a guarantee for a EUR 50 million Bavarian government loan, and in December 2024 the company ceased operations and laid off approximately 1,000 employees. A consortium called Mobile Uplift Corporation GmbH announced a partial asset acquisition in late December 2024, but in February 2025 Lilium's German entities filed a second insolvency after the promised takeover financing failed to materialize. As of this profile (May 2026) Lilium remains non-operational and the website and social channels may be intermittently available; this profile is preserved for historical and archival reference.

providers.name: Loft Dynamics
providers.description: Loft Dynamics is a Swiss aviation technology company (founded 2016, headquartered in Dübendorf, Switzerland with a North American office in Santa Monica) that builds virtual reality flight simulation training devices (FSTDs) for helicopters, fixed-wing aircraft, and eVTOLs. Its simulators combine full-scale replica cockpits, dynamic motion platforms, 360-degree VR visuals, and advanced pose tracking, and were the first VR aircraft simulators to earn EASA and FAA qualification. Products include VR simulators for the Airbus H145, Airbus H125, and Robinson R22 helicopters, with Boeing 737 and eVTOL platforms in development. Customers include Alaska Airlines, the FAA, Airbus Helicopters, the LAPD, and Marshall University. The company operates the LoftHUB customer platform but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: London House Exchange (Property Partner)
providers.description: London House Exchange, formerly Property Partner, is an FCA-regulated online platform that operates the world's only regulated exchange for individual residential, student and commercial properties. Founded in 2014 and now owned by US digital homeownership company Better, the platform lets retail investors buy fractional shares in professionally managed UK properties, earn monthly dividends from rental income, and trade those shares with other investors on a secondary market. It also offers property-backed mortgage bonds, an ISA, and bridging finance, with over £100m of fractionalised property assets under management and thousands of investors across more than 80 countries. It was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Lower
providers.description: Lower is a U.S. direct-to-consumer mortgage lender and servicer (Lower, LLC, NMLS #1124061) offering home purchase loans, refinancing, and home equity products including conventional, FHA, VA, jumbo, and adjustable-rate mortgages, HELOCs, and cash-out options. Lower operates a mobile-first application experience with dedicated loan officers and conducts business in 47 states plus the District of Columbia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. Lower publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface at this time; this profile captures its public web, legal, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Magic
providers.description: Magic, Inc. is a Y Combinator-backed virtual assistant company that matches busy professionals, executives, and entrepreneurs with dedicated, vetted human assistants rather than AI bots. Through its Magic Match screening (assistants drawn from the top 0.5% of applicants), Magic 24/7 backup coverage, and ongoing training, the service handles email and inbox management, calendar and scheduling, travel planning, customer support, research, data entry, and other recurring business and personal tasks. Magic is a consumer- and business-facing staffing/concierge service delivered through a web workspace; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Makani *
providers.description: Makani was an Alphabet (Google X) moonshot developing airborne wind energy — "energy kites" that flew in crosswind loops to generate electricity and sent power to the grid down a tether. Backed within Alphabet and partnered with Shell, Makani wound down in 2020 after roughly 13 years of development. On closure the team open-sourced its full flight-simulation, autopilot controller, visualization, and avionics software stack under Apache-2.0 and published the Energy Kite Collection of technical reports, designs, and flight logs. Makani has no commercial or developer API surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company for network completeness.

providers.name: Mayvenn
providers.description: Mayvenn is an Oakland, California beauty-commerce company that sells quality virgin human hair extensions, sew-in weave bundles, closures, frontals, and human hair wigs directly to consumers and through a network of more than 100,000 hair stylists. Founded by Diishan Imira and backed by a16z and 500 Global, Mayvenn pairs its hair products with a stylist-driven distribution model and a 30-day return policy, running its storefront on Shopify at shop.mayvenn.com. The company does not currently publish a public first-party developer API; this profile captures its web identity, security posture, and commercial link surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Medzoomer
providers.description: Medzoomer is an on-demand prescription delivery platform that connects pharmacies, healthcare providers, and patients through a secure, HIPAA-compliant network of verified couriers. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Tampa, Florida, the company handles last-mile medication logistics, including controlled substances (Schedule II-V), with tamper-evident packaging, FDA/TSA-approved envelopes, and real-time order tracking. Pharmacies and couriers operate through dedicated web and mobile applications, and the platform is backed by Techstars, UnitedHealthcare Accelerator, and other investors. Medzoomer operates a private pharmacy integration API but publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Mend
providers.description: Mend is a HIPAA-compliant telehealth and patient engagement platform for mental and behavioral healthcare organizations, powering appointment scheduling, automated reminders, secure video visits, digital intake forms and consents, patient messaging, payments, and AI no-show prediction. Mend integrates with EHR and practice-management systems through a combination of HL7, SFTP, and an API served from api.mendfamily.com. That API exists and is used by Mend's own portal for session initialization and signaling, but its reference documentation is delivered through a login-gated customer knowledge base rather than a public developer portal, so Mend's programmatic surface is best characterized as partner- and customer-gated rather than openly self-serve.

providers.name: Min Doktor
providers.description: Min Doktor is a Swedish digital healthcare provider (operated by MD International AB) offering online primary care through its mobile app and web service. Founded in 2013 as one of Sweden's first digital-first care providers, it connects patients with doctors, psychologists and nurses for consultations, prescriptions, referrals and vaccinations, and also runs white-label care services for partners such as Skandia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of EQT Ventures. Min Doktor operates as a consumer/patient-facing service and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its verifiable public security, identity and compliance footprint.

providers.name: Mision Admision
providers.description: Misión Admisión is a Mexican education-technology company based in Mérida that prepares high school and university applicants for standardized admission exams such as EXANI I, EXANI II, PAA, and the UNAM, IPN, and UAM entrance tests. Its consumer web platform (misionadmision.com) delivers self-paced online courses, video lessons, interactive study capsules, thousands of practice questions, full-length exam simulators, live virtual and in-person classes, and the physical Sputnik smartbook guides. Founded in 2001 and online since 2015, the company is a seed-stage portfolio company of 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing EdTech platform and publishes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for tracking and enrichment.

providers.name: MorphCast
providers.description: We expertly craft safe browser-processing, energy-efficient, accurate Emotion AI solutions to analyze facial emotions, empowering AI Agents and delivering empathetic, data-driven, and dynamic digital experiences.

providers.name: N-Drip
providers.description: N-Drip is an Israeli agritech manufacturer of gravity-powered micro-irrigation systems, led by Prof. Uri Shani, Israel's former Water Commissioner. Its patented drip system operates on gravity alone at under 0.87 PSI / 0.06 BAR, requiring no pumping station and no pressure-based filtration, and is positioned as a direct replacement for flood irrigation — which still accounts for roughly 85 percent of the world's irrigated agriculture and wastes an estimated 70 percent of the water it uses. Alongside the hardware the company ships N-Drip Connect, a sensor-and-app decision-support platform that measures root-zone water potential and available nitrogen, layers NDVI satellite imagery over the field, and issues irrigation and fertilization recommendations to growers. N-Drip technology is deployed in ten countries and five US states across 25 crop types including rice, corn, soybeans, potatoes, sugar cane, alfalfa and cotton, with a US production hub in Yuma, Arizona. N-Drip publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API contract: N-Drip Connect is delivered strictly as a closed web and mobile application.

providers.name: NACCO Industries
providers.description: NACCO Industries is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The NACCO Industries API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Nexthop Systems
providers.description: Nexthop AI (Nexthop Systems) builds power-efficient AI networking infrastructure for hyperscalers and NeoClouds — scale-out and scale-across Ethernet switches, a networking software portfolio, and optics and cables engineered to lower the cost per token of training and serving large AI models. Founded and led by CEO Anshul Sadana, the company is backed by Battery Ventures and raised an oversubscribed $500M Series B in 2025 at a $4.2 billion valuation. Nexthop runs a public marketing, blog and news site plus a login-gated customer Support Hub and Learning Hub; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface.

providers.name: omniX labs
providers.description: omniX labs is a New York-based AI machine-vision analytics company (owned by EverWash) serving car wash, oil-change/lube, and related quick-service automotive businesses. Its platform ingests real-time video of the physical business, applies computer vision and AI to synthesize customer interactions, and returns operational insights that help operators boost throughput, optimize staffing, prevent loss, predict demand, and grow revenue. omniX labs was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. It operates a customer web portal but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Operon
providers.description: Operon is an AI-powered manufacturing intelligence platform (Y Combinator S2026) that turns P&IDs (Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams), schematics, datasheets, and scanned engineering documents into one structured, queryable model of a plant. Its P&ID Recognition detects equipment, instruments, valves, and piping symbols across ISA, ISO, and proprietary symbology; its P&ID Agent generates standards-compliant diagrams from text, simulation data, or sketches; and Knowledge Chat lets engineers query plant documentation in natural language and build agentic workflows for safety, compliance, HAZOP/PHA, EHS, material take-offs, brownfield digitization, and management-of-change. Operon exports structured DEXPI data and offers cloud and on-premise deployment with encryption, role-based access control, and audit trails. As of July 2026 the product is in private beta (pid.operonsolutions.com) and publishes no public API.

providers.name: OrderCircle
providers.description: OrderCircle is a B2B wholesale order management software platform, founded in 2015 in San Francisco, that gives fast-growing brands one system to automate wholesale orders, track inventory in real time, generate invoices, and run a self-service B2B eCommerce portal for their buyers. It targets wholesale operations in apparel, coffee, jewelry, food and beverage, hemp, vape, and CBD, and connects to existing tools through pre-built integrations with Shopify, WooCommerce, QuickBooks, Xero, ShipStation, Stripe, Square, PayPal PayFlow, and Authorize.Net. OrderCircle does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; its programmatic surface is limited to its packaged third-party integrations. This profile was seeded as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Packhelp
providers.description: Packhelp is a European custom and wholesale packaging platform that lets businesses design, order, and warehouse branded packaging — boxes, mailers, bags, tubes, and accessories — through online design tools and a curated catalog of EU-based producers. Packhelp also markets "the first-ever API for packaging," a sales-gated set of web services that let 3PL, fulfillment, marketplace, logistics, and food-delivery platforms embed packaging quoting, ordering, and a drag-and-drop packaging editor directly into their own applications and whitelabel storefronts.

providers.name: PadSplit
providers.description: PadSplit is an Atlanta-based co-living marketplace that makes affordable housing accessible by connecting members seeking private rooms in shared homes with property owners who host them. The platform offers flexible weekly payments, fast move-ins, all-inclusive rent (utilities, wifi, and furnishings), member background screening, and a rewards program that helps residents build credit. PadSplit operates across multiple U.S. metros as a two-sided marketplace serving both members (renters) and hosts (property owners), and was backed by Techstars. The company has no public developer program, API, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: ParkPow
providers.description: ParkPow is software to manage and enforce parking lots. It lets you track vehicles, get custom alerts, and enforce your parking rules. The ParkPow API documentation requires application access and is not publicly available.

providers.name: Possible Finance
providers.description: Possible Finance is a consumer fintech company offering small-dollar installment loans and credit-building products through a mobile app. Its core products are the Possible Loan (up to $500 with flexible repayment schedules), the Possible Advance (up to $300 drawn against a future paycheck), and Bill & Rent Reporting that builds credit history by reporting on-time payments to the credit bureaus. The company charges no late fees or penalty charges and uses AI-driven underwriting based on real banking activity rather than FICO scores, serving borrowers who are underserved by traditional credit. Possible Finance operates as a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation and is backed by Union Square Ventures. It is a mobile-app, consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PROOF
providers.description: PROOF is a digital art and NFT platform built on the belief that "art is proof of our collective humanity." It is the company behind Moonbirds (its flagship profile-picture collection), the 1,000-member PROOF Collective, and collections including Oddities, Mythics, and the Grails art-collector experience, alongside the Lunar Society community-governance program, a research arm, live events, and a podcast. PROOF is backed by a16z and Kindred Ventures. Its public surface is a consumer/collector documentation site (docs.proof.xyz) and marketing site; PROOF does not currently publish a programmatic developer API, OpenAPI spec, SDKs, or webhooks.

providers.name: Provenmetal
providers.description: ProvenMetal is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building fast-turn, American-made printed circuit board (PCB) assembly. The company lets customers upload a Gerber file, automatically infers the board specification, and returns instant quoting for a 7-day standard turnaround with no expedite fees. ProvenMetal automates the traditional manufacturing bottlenecks — part procurement, design for manufacturability (DFM) review, and assembly — and performs 100% X-ray inspection of every board (AI-assisted, cited at 99.8% confidence) before shipment, including the inspection data with each order. It is a domestic B2B PCB manufacturing service aimed at reshoring electronics production, operated out of San Francisco. As of this profile ProvenMetal exposes a customer ordering portal at order.provenmetal.com but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Python Standard Library and Popular
providers.description: A collection of commonly used Python APIs and libraries including the standard library and popular frameworks like Flask, Django, FastAPI, Pandas, and NumPy.

providers.name: Qbiq
providers.description: Qbiq is an AI-powered space planning and architectural visualization platform for real estate. It lets brokers, architects, developers, and space planners generate optimized 2D floor plans, photorealistic 3D renderings, virtual tours, Revit/CAD models, and quantity takeoffs from an uploaded space plan (CAD, PDF, or JPEG) in minutes. Qbiq automates test-fits and layout optimization for offices and commercial real estate, comparing multiple design options against program requirements. The company is backed by Insight Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Qbiq operates a hosted web application (plan.qbiq.ai) and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Quinto Andar
providers.description: QuintoAndar is a Brazilian proptech real-estate marketplace that lets people rent and buy homes online without a guarantor, with digital visit scheduling, digital contract signing, rent and sale pricing intelligence (QPreço), owner financial management, and a real-estate consortium financing program. It operates a two-sided marketplace across major Brazilian cities including São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Belo Horizonte, Porto Alegre, Campinas, and Curitiba, earning revenue on rental and sales commissions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of ribbit-capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found; the company does publish a security.txt with a Bugcrowd bug bounty program.

providers.name: Regular Finance
providers.description: Regular Finance (Regular) is a French fintech offering a consumer digital-asset yield account. Customers deposit euros by bank transfer and earn roughly 5.50% annual interest paid daily, backed by regulated stablecoins such as EURC and USDC placed into on-chain liquidity pools and yield protocols. Withdrawals are free at any time and no crypto knowledge is required. Regular is a Techstars-backed company headquartered in France; the product is entirely consumer-facing (web and mobile app at app.regular.eu) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: REST API
providers.description: Representational State Transfer (REST) is an architectural style for designing networked applications using standard HTTP methods and stateless communication between client and server. REST APIs define how client and server applications communicate over the web using GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and PATCH methods against resource-oriented URLs. REST is the dominant API paradigm, used by 89% of organisations as their primary API format. This index covers the REST API landscape including specifications, tools, frameworks, best practices, and educational resources.

providers.name: REST Services
providers.description: Representational State Transfer (REST) is an architectural style for designing networked applications using stateless communication and standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) to interact with resources identified by URLs. REST services underpin modern web APIs and support the full software development lifecycle from design through deployment and maintenance. This index covers REST service implementations, frameworks, best practices, patterns, tooling, and educational resources that guide how REST services are built, managed, and consumed.

providers.name: Robocurve
providers.description: Robocurve is a San Francisco Public Benefit Corporation (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building open-source tools and independent benchmarks to help society understand what AI and robots can actually do in the physical world. Its flagship framework, Inspect Robots ("the Inspect AI for robotics"), runs any vision-language-action policy on any embodiment against any benchmark with full trace logs and live Rerun visualization, and integrates with ROS, Isaac Lab, and LeRobot. World Evals is its curated catalog of physical-world benchmarks (KitchenBench, DataCenterBench). Everything ships MIT-licensed as Python packages with a command-line interface rather than a hosted REST API.

providers.name: Safari Ai
providers.description: Safari AI is a vision-AI company for physical operations, turning an organization's existing camera networks into an automated operational system. Its Action Center platform measures on-site activity (people counts and footfall, occupancy, heatmapping, throughput, queue wait time, dwell time, vehicle counts, and license-plate recognition), raises alerts, recommends and dispatches actions, and attributes outcomes — measurement to action in under 60 seconds. Safari AI serves theme parks and cultural attractions, stadiums and arenas, QSR and drive-thrus, retail and shopping malls, parking, and logistics. Backed by General Catalyst, it exposes no public developer API; customers consume results through a hosted real-time dashboard (Grafana) rather than a self-serve API surface. This profile was surfaced from the VC portfolio graph and enriched from the company's public site.

providers.name: Saysh
providers.description: Saysh is a direct-to-consumer athletic footwear and apparel brand founded by Olympic champion sprinter Allyson Felix, designing sneakers engineered specifically for women's biomechanics under the banner "Women Deserve Better." Its lineup spans performance running shoes (the Felix Runner and Evelyn Runner) and the everyday Saysh One, plus apparel, accessories, and the Saysh+ Run Club membership. The saysh.com storefront runs on Shopify, so customer-facing commerce is served through the Shopify platform rather than a first-party Saysh developer API; no public Saysh API program, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal were found. Backed by Redpoint Ventures.

providers.name: Seso
providers.description: Seso is an all-in-one employee management platform built for U.S. agricultural operations, serving customers across all 50 states including 35 of the top 100 agricultural employers. Its software combines a modern farm HR system, compliant digital onboarding (I-9/W-4 with direct E-Verify integration), H-2A visa filing and compliance backed by legal resources, self-serve and managed payroll, and digital paycards for paycheck delivery. Seso also provides H-2A worker services such as consulate scheduling, recruiting, and logistics coordinated from its Monterrey, Mexico office. Backed by Bond Capital and Index Ventures. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Shuttle Central
providers.description: Shuttle Central (shuttlecentral.com) is a ground transportation booking platform for airport and point-to-point shuttle transfers across Mexico, the Caribbean, the United States, and Latin America, covering 100+ destinations including Cancun, Punta Cana, Nassau, Los Cabos, Mexico City, Puerto Vallarta, Montego Bay, and Miami. Travelers book confirmed transfers online with secure payment, instant confirmation, and 24/7 support, and a separate transportation-provider program (shuttlecentralinc.com) lets ground operators sell transfers through the platform. The company is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Smartex
providers.description: Smartex is an AI and computer-vision company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Porto, Portugal that builds hardware-enabled software for the textile manufacturing industry. Its systems inspect fabric in real time on the knitting machine to detect defects at the source, cutting textile waste, CO2 emissions, water, energy and rework. The product suite spans CORE (a machine-vision inspection add-on for circular knitting machines), FACT (an all-in-one digital factory-management platform for production visibility and quality control) and LOOP (supply-chain communication and traceability). Smartex is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, DCVC, Tony Fadell's Build Collective, H&M Group, SOSV/HAX, Spider Capital, Momenta Ventures and Fashion for Good. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; customer access is through the FACT platform login. This profile was surfaced from the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from Smartex's public web surface.

providers.name: Solovis
providers.description: Solovis is a multi-asset investment analytics and portfolio management software platform for institutional investors, including endowments, foundations, pension plans, outsourced CIOs (OCIOs), and family offices. It aggregates data across public and private asset classes into a single dashboard for portfolio modeling, performance analysis, risk analytics, and reporting. Core products include Portfolio Analytics, Risk Analytics, Predict (performance and risk prediction for asset allocation), Risk Pro (factor-based risk analytics, formerly Venn Pro), and Analyst Services for outsourced data capture and portfolio data aggregation. Solovis became part of Nasdaq's investment intelligence business following its 2020 acquisition. The platform is delivered as a private, authenticated SaaS accessed through a client login; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, OpenAPI specification, or `/.well-known/` discovery surface. The host api.solovis.com exists but is fully authentication-gated (HTTP 401) with no public specification.

providers.name: Standard Operating Procedures
providers.description: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are documented step-by-step instructions for routine operations and processes to ensure consistency, quality, and compliance across an organization. They are essential for regulated industries such as healthcare, pharmaceuticals, finance, food service, aviation, and manufacturing. SOPs establish clear responsibilities, document institutional knowledge, support regulatory compliance, enable process auditing, and facilitate employee onboarding. Software platforms for SOP management include SweetProcess, Trainual, Guru, Document360, and Notion; many offer developer APIs for embedding SOP workflows into other business systems.

providers.name: Stere
providers.description: Stere is a New York-based insurance infrastructure company (founded 2021) that lets insurers, MGAs, and distribution partners build and launch digital insurance products - rating, quoting, binding, policy issuance, claims, and premium payments - in weeks rather than years. Its core offering is a "Stere API-as-a-Service" underwriting API (insurers can bring their own API or have Stere build one) plus a separate Stere Unified API and Stere Distribution layer that let brokers, wholesalers, fintechs, and embedded partners reach multiple carriers/products through a single connection (API, SDK, and webhooks). Stere Claims handles FNOL and claims workflow (portions of claims assessment and resolution are marketed as in-development/coming soon), and Stere Pay / Stere Pay Later provides a buy-now-pay-later gateway for insurance premiums. There is no self-serve public developer portal, published API reference, OpenAPI/Swagger document, or sandbox signup on stere.io; the marketing site references a "Stere Docs," "API Changelog," and "API Status" area under /developer/, but those paths return 404 publicly and integration is provisioned per customer after a sales-led partner/insurer onboarding engagement. The APIs below are honestly modeled from Stere's own product marketing pages, not from a published API reference.

providers.name: SyncOnSet Technologies
providers.description: SyncOnSet Technologies is an Emmy Award-winning digital continuity, inventory, and money-tracking platform for film and television production, now part of Entertainment Partners. It replaces paper continuity binders with a collaborative online/offline web and mobile app that manages automatic script breakdowns and revisions, continuity photos, costume and wardrobe pieces, hair and makeup looks, props, set decoration, and locations, alongside per-character and per-scene budgeting and asset reports from prep through wrap. SyncOnSet is a login-gated SaaS application (production teams access it by account) and exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or self-serve developer program, so this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Tiff's Treats
providers.description: Tiff's Treats is an Austin, Texas cookie company founded in 1999 by University of Texas students Tiffany Taylor and Leon Chen, built around warm, baked-to-order cookies delivered same-day. The company operates roughly 90 bakery-storefronts across Texas and the southern and western United States, combining walk-in retail with an owned delivery fleet, an online ordering platform at cookiedelivery.com, and iOS and Android ordering apps. Alongside consumer delivery it runs a substantial corporate gifting, catering, e-gift-card and special-events business, plus an "Elites" subscription membership and a rewards program. Tiff's Treats has raised more than $50 million in outside investment, including a $25 million round led by Morgan Stanley Expansion Capital, and counts Andy Roddick, Brooklyn Decker, Kendra Scott and Dirk Nowitzki among its investors. It is a direct-to-consumer food and delivery operator, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: TrackMan
providers.description: TrackMan A/S is a Danish sports-technology company (headquartered in Vedbaek, Denmark) that builds Doppler radar and optically tracked launch monitors, simulator software, and data platforms for golf, baseball, football, and US football. Its hardware lineage includes the TrackMan 4 outdoor/indoor launch monitor, TrackMan iO indoor launch monitor, the V3 stadium ball-tracking system used by every Major League Baseball club, and the portable B1 baseball launch monitor. On the software side TrackMan operates TrackMan Range (a connected driving-range platform), Virtual Golf 3 (the simulator rendering and gameplay engine), the TrackMan Golf App for performance and social play, TrackMan 360 for golf-club business operations, and a cloud data platform that aggregates measurements across products. TrackMan exposes several developer-facing surfaces — a TrackMan Cloud GraphQL API at api.golf.trackman.com/graphql for tournaments and facility data, the TrackMan Range REST API at docs.trackmanrange.com for range/bay/session integration, a device-local TM4 WebSocket protocol for receiving live shot measurements over LAN/UPnP from a TrackMan 4 unit, and the TrackMan Baseball Data API (Swagger-documented, OAuth-client + username/password) for ingesting V3 stadium and B1 portable measurements and media. The TrackMan public GitHub organization hosts internal Unity tooling rather than client SDKs, and most developer access is partner-gated through TrackMan Sports Solutions or the Golf B2B program. The commercial model is hardware sales plus tiered software subscriptions (TrackMan Range, TrackMan 360, V3 Cloud) sold direct to teams, leagues, ranges, and consumers.

providers.name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Vertex Pharmaceuticals is a global biotechnology company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, focused on scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases. The company specializes in cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, beta thalassemia, APOL1-mediated kidney disease, pain, and other serious conditions. Vertex is committed to responsible sharing of clinical trial data with qualified researchers through formal data request processes.

providers.name: Waffle Labs
providers.description: Waffle Labs, Inc. (Waffle Insurance) is a consumer InsurTech company and licensed digital insurance agency, founded at MIT and accelerated through Barclays Techstars and MIT Delta V. Waffle offers an all-in-one, mobile-first platform that lets consumers get quotes and bind coverage in under 90 seconds across renters, pet, home & auto, term life, personal cyber, and travel insurance in all 50 US states, partnering with vetted carriers rather than underwriting risk itself. The company also runs an embedded-insurance program that lets partners offer Waffle products through a no-code embed. Waffle is a consumer/partner product with no public developer program or API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Watsi
providers.description: Watsi is a San Francisco-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit crowdfunding platform that lets donors directly fund surgeries and medical care for patients in low-income countries, working through vetted medical partners across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Founded in 2011 and the first nonprofit funded by Y Combinator, Watsi has directed more than $20 million to patient healthcare. Watsi previously published a read-only JSON API at developers.watsi.org, but that developer portal and api.watsi.org no longer resolve, so no public API surface is currently available.

providers.name: WeiMai
providers.description: WeiMai (微脉) is a Chinese healthcare technology company operated by Choice Technology Inc. and headquartered in Hangzhou. It runs an internet-based medical services marketplace and licensed internet hospitals (including Hainan WeiMai Internet Hospital) that connect patients with doctors for online consultation, pharmaceutical products, medical devices, and health-management service packages, delivered primarily through the WeiMai consumer mobile app. WeiMai also operates a partner-facing Open Platform (微脉开发平台) at openapi.myweimai.com that exposes a Swagger 2.0 API surface for approved integrators; the public specification is a minimal stub with no operations exposed without partner credentials. The company is backed by IDG Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio company.

providers.name: Wonderskin
providers.description: Wonderskin is a direct-to-consumer beauty and cosmetics brand best known for its WONDER BLADING all-day peel-off lip stain, along with longwear eyeliners, serum foundations, blush, brow products, skincare, and beauty tools sold through its Shopify-powered online store. The company runs a SKINSIDER loyalty membership, publishes THE SKINSIDER beauty and lifestyle blog, and partners with athletes and celebrities on product marketing. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. As a consumer e-commerce retailer, Wonderskin publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures the brand identity, customer-facing web properties, and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: WOO Sports
providers.description: WOO Sports makes a sensor-based performance-tracking system for kitesurfing, wingfoiling, and windsurfing. The WOO 4.0 device mounts to a board and measures jump height, airtime, G-force, and landing impact, syncing sessions through the WOO Sports mobile apps (iOS, Android, Apple Watch, Wear OS, and Garmin) to a global community platform with leaderboards, spots, activity feeds, and events. More than 100,000 riders use WOO to track sessions and compete, including on the GKA Kite World Tour. WOO Sports is a Techstars-backed brand operated under Boards & More. This profile was enriched from the provider's public web surface; no public developer API was found (docs.woosports.com is a consumer user guide, not an API reference).

providers.name: Xpeng
providers.description: XPENG (Xiaopeng Motors) is a Chinese smart electric-vehicle company headquartered in Guangzhou that designs and manufactures smart EVs (G6, G7, G9, P7/P7+, X9, MONA M03) with in-house advanced driver-assistance and in-car software, listed on the NYSE (XPEV) and HKEX (9868). Surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and idg-capital. XPENG publishes no public developer API: its open platform (open.xiaopeng.com) is geo-restricted and account-gated, and no public API docs, specs, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: xTool
providers.description: xTool is a Shenzhen-based digital-fabrication brand, spun out of Makeblock and backed by HongShan, making CO2, fiber, and diode laser cutters and engravers, laser welders, and DTF printers for makers and small businesses, driven by its xTool Creative Space (XCS) desktop software. xTool sells through a Shopify storefront and runs a support and academy portal, a user community, and the Atomm maker-project platform, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Zyla
providers.description: Zyla API Hub is an API marketplace that provides unified access to over 10,000 APIs through a single account, API key, and SDK, simplifying API discovery, integration, and management for developers.

providers.name: Aaptiv
providers.description: Aaptiv is a digital fitness and wellness platform offering 10,000+ on-demand audio and video workout classes, AI-powered coaching, access to a network of gyms and studios, and wellness resources such as meditation and mindfulness. It is sold to employers as an employee benefit, to health plans, and to individuals seeking personalized fitness. Backed by Insight Partners. Aaptiv publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, support, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Aboon
providers.description: Aboon is a digital 401(k) retirement-plan platform and third-party administrator (TPA) that helps financial advisors and employers design, launch, and manage workplace retirement plans. It pairs AI-powered workflows with dedicated human plan consultants to generate customized 401(k) proposals in minutes, streamline recordkeeper onboarding, handle digital plan contracting and census intake, and run ongoing compliance testing and Form 3(16) administration. Aboon markets partnerships with major recordkeepers (American Funds, Empower, John Hancock, and others) and serves a network of advisors nationwide. It is a fintech company backed by Bain Capital Ventures. No public developer/API surface has been identified.

providers.name: Aletiq
providers.description: Aletiq is a French software company building a next-generation, AI-powered Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Product Data Management (PDM) platform for regulated manufacturers. The platform centralizes technical data (CAD files, drawings, bills of materials, configurations, and work instructions), enforces traceability and regulatory compliance, and automates business processes such as approvals, engineering change management, and project milestones. Aletiq emphasizes rapid deployment and high adoption across operational teams, and integrates with major CAD tools (SolidWorks, CATIA, Autodesk Inventor, Siemens NX, Creo) and ERP systems (SAP, Sage, Cegid, Infor, Odoo) via connectors and a custom-integration API. It serves aerospace and defense, medical devices, energy, electronics, automotive, and luxury-goods industries. Aletiq is backed by Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead profile.

providers.name: AmplifyMD
providers.description: AmplifyMD is a virtual care platform for hospitals and health systems, providing a nationwide network of remote specialists across more than 15 essential fields. It powers telemedicine across emergent, inpatient, asynchronous, SNF/LTAC, virtual clinic, and direct-to-patient care models, and integrates with major EHR systems including Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth, Allscripts, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, TruBridge, and MedHost to help organizations build sustainable clinical staffing models. Backed by Forerunner Ventures.

providers.name: Analytics
providers.description: A curated index of analytics platforms, SDKs, and open source solutions spanning the full analytics spectrum — from web and product analytics (Google Analytics, Mixpanel, Amplitude, PostHog, Plausible, Matomo, Heap) to customer data platforms (Segment, mParticle, RudderStack), mobile analytics (Firebase Analytics, Adjust, AppsFlyer, Braze), business intelligence (Looker, Tableau, Metabase, Redash), event streaming (Kafka, Kinesis), and real-time analytics infrastructure (ClickHouse, Druid, Pinot). Covers both SaaS and self-hosted, open source and commercial offerings.

providers.name: Augmedix
providers.description: Augmedix is a San Francisco-based health technology company providing ambient AI medical documentation (AI scribe) services that capture patient-clinician conversations and generate clinical notes so that physicians can focus on patient care instead of EHR data entry. Founded in 2012, the company went public on Nasdaq in 2021 (AUGX) and was acquired by Commure in October 2024, becoming part of Commure's clinician-workflow platform alongside HCA Healthcare-aligned tooling. Augmedix's product line spans three service tiers — Augmedix Go (self-service AI scribe), Augmedix Assist (AI drafting with human editing, coding, and referral-letter support, notes ready within an hour), and Augmedix Live (full-service dedicated medical documentation specialist before, during, and after the visit) — plus specialty variants for Emergency Medicine, oncology, and other specialties. The platform integrates with major EHRs including Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth, Meditech, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, and iKnowMed, and is HIPAA-compliant and HITRUST-certified. Augmedix's GitHub presence consists of internal QA, scribe-app base, and ambient API automation repositories; there is no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification — integration with Augmedix is handled through enterprise EHR partnerships and the Commure clinician platform rather than a self-service developer surface.

providers.name: Aura Finance
providers.description: Aura Finance is an employer-sponsored financial wellness platform that blends behavioral psychology with money management to help employees reach financial stability and peace of mind. The San Francisco fintech — a Techstars Economic Mobility 2023 company and an SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD 318940) — delivers goal-based automated investing, one-on-one financial coaching over chat, budgeting and saving tools, financial-literacy workshops, mindfulness exercises to reduce money stress, and a money-personality quiz, offered through a B2B2C model to organizations and their workforces. The company publishes no public developer program, API, or SDKs; its member application lives at web.aurafi.io.

providers.name: Aurora Networks
providers.description: Aurora Networks is the broadband and access networks brand of Vistance Networks, Inc. (Nasdaq: VISN), the company CommScope renamed itself to in January 2026 after divesting its Connectivity and Cable Solutions segment to Amphenol. Aurora Networks builds end-to-end access network infrastructure for global cable and broadband service providers: HFC and PON access systems, cable headend optics platforms, CMTS and CCAP gear, Distributed Access Architecture (DAA) devices, optical hubs, nodes and passives, RF and RFoG equipment, and video processing, security and delivery systems. Its ServAssure NXT family adds network performance management, alarm handling and service assurance software on top of that hardware estate. The brand originates with Aurora Networks, Inc., founded in Santa Clara, California in 1999 as a pure-play optical transport supplier to cable operators, backed by Battery Ventures among ten investors across roughly $60M raised, and acquired by Pace plc for $323M in 2013 before passing through ARRIS and CommScope. Aurora Networks is a network equipment vendor rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer portal, no public API reference, and no machine-readable API specification. Product and integration documentation, including the ServAssure NXT web service and message-bus integration surfaces, sits behind authenticated customer support portals.

providers.name: Auto Finance
providers.description: Auto Finance is a decentralized finance (DeFi) liquidity-management protocol built by Tokemak. Its core product, Autopools, are automated onchain vaults that autonomously optimize, rebalance, and auto-compound liquidity-provider yield across major DeFi venues (Curve, Fluid, Inverse, Morpho, AAVE) and networks (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base), abstracting away the complexity of manual LP management. The protocol is governed and secured through AUTO token staking, and its onchain surface is a public set of audited Solidity smart contracts rather than a REST API. Documentation is published via GitBook with an agent-readable llms.txt index.

providers.name: Baby2Body
providers.description: Baby2Body is the flagship consumer wellness app from Body Collective, a female-focused health and wellness company founded by sports psychologist Melinda Nicci. The app delivers personalized fitness, nutrition, and mental-health support across the fertility, pregnancy, postpartum, parenting, and broader women's-health stages, paired with an AI health coach named Bella, on-demand programs (prenatal fitness, meal plans, labor prep), expert-backed articles, and a stage-specific newsletter. Baby2Body reports over two million users and is backed by 500 Global. This profile has been enriched from the company's public consumer surfaces; no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable specification was found.

providers.name: Bank of Hawaii
providers.description: Bank of Hawaii is a state-chartered commercial bank organized under the laws of the State of Hawaii in 1897, a member of the Federal Reserve System and FDIC-insured. It is the principal banking subsidiary of Bank of Hawaii Corporation (NYSE: BOH), a Honolulu-headquartered regional financial services company serving Hawaii, Guam, and other Pacific islands with consumer, commercial, and wealth-management banking. As a regional US institution, Bank of Hawaii publishes no first-party public developer portal and exposes no documented public API surface; probes of developer.boh.com and developers.boh.com do not resolve. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and consumer-permissioned data access to Bank of Hawaii accounts is available in practice only through third-party aggregators (for example Plaid), not through a direct bank-operated API. No Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership and no published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture were found at the time of this record.

providers.name: Basebuild
providers.description: Basebuild Labs, Inc. builds Beams, an AI project manager for construction and real estate teams. The product automatically transcribes project meetings, tracks decisions and action items, and assembles a searchable knowledge base from those discussions, capturing information without requiring a bot to join the call. It is aimed at giving construction and real estate project teams real-time visibility and control over teams, projects, budgets, and finances. Basebuild is an early-stage Canaan Partners portfolio company based in Santa Monica, California, and this API Evangelist profile tracks its public-facing surface. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site and a product login only, with no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or documentation surface to catalog.

providers.name: Belvedir
providers.description: Belvedir is an autonomous private AI platform built by Fractal Machine Research, Inc. (a Y Combinator Summer 2026 company). It lets individuals and teams train custom AI models and memory systems, host them privately on single-tenant infrastructure, and continually improve them through use: it collects agent calls and production traces, converts those traces into training data, and fine-tunes models with reinforcement learning in a continuous loop before redeploying on private infrastructure. The stated aim is to let everyday individuals own their own artificial intelligence rather than rent it from a shared provider. The product is in closed alpha and access is currently granted by request; there is no public API or developer documentation yet, so this profile captures the company's public identity and will be enriched as a developer surface appears.

providers.name: BlackSwan Technologies
providers.description: BlackSwan Technologies is an enterprise AI software company founded in 2014 by Michael and Elinoar Ouliel, headquartered in London with engineering across Israel, Poland and India. Its flagship product, ELEMENT, is marketed as an Enterprise AI Operating System: a low/no-code platform-as-a-service combining a data fabric, knowledge graphs, machine learning and composite AI so banks and other regulated enterprises can assemble applications for KYC on demand, enhanced due diligence, financial crime, transaction intelligence, market intelligence and underwriting without first consolidating their data. Its software engineering unit, BST LABS, built and open-sourced CAIOS (Cloud AI Operating System) and a family of Python developer tools (DynaCLI, CLVM, PyJdict, PyComposite, AuthK). BlackSwan Technologies was acquired by HUB Cyber Security Ltd. (NASDAQ: HUBC) in a stock-for-stock transaction that closed on 27 January 2025, and its corporate domain blackswantechnologies.ai no longer resolves in DNS; the secured data fabric technology is now marketed under HUB Technologies. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract (OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, MCP, A2A) was found for BlackSwan Technologies during enrichment.

providers.name: Boldr
providers.description: Boldr is a Techstars-backed consumer hardware company building energy-saving smart home climate control devices. Its two products are Kelvin, a smart infrared heater, and Klima, a smart thermostat controller for mini-split air conditioners that also monitors appliance health so units last longer with fewer issues. Both devices are managed through the Boldr mobile app, which lets homeowners control climate settings remotely and track energy usage to lower utility bills. Boldr also runs Boldr Pro, a program for HVAC contractors. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted online store at shopboldr.com and does not currently publish a first-party developer API; its only public machine-readable surface is the Shopify Customer Account OIDC discovery served at the storefront host.

providers.name: Boston Heart Diagnostics (Eurofins Scientific)
providers.description: Boston Heart Diagnostics is a specialty cardiovascular diagnostics laboratory, part of Eurofins Scientific, that has been improving patient outcomes since 2007 through a combination of integrated diagnostics, advanced lipid and metabolic testing, genetic risk evaluation, personalized reporting, and a scientifically designed nutrition and lifestyle program. It serves clinicians and patients through a provider portal and a patient portal (mybostonheart.com) rather than a public developer API; there is no published developer portal, OpenAPI, or programmatic surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the identity and security-posture fields below are captured from the provider's public web presence.

providers.name: BuzzFeed
providers.description: BuzzFeed Inc. is a digital media company founded in 2006 and headquartered in New York City, best known for its viral entertainment, quizzes, pop-culture coverage, and commerce content. The company operates a portfolio of brands including the flagship BuzzFeed site, the news operation HuffPost, and the food brand Tasty, and produces video, podcasts, and shoppable content across web and social platforms. BuzzFeed is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: BZFD) and monetizes through advertising, brand partnerships, and commerce. It does not publish a general-purpose public developer API program; its public machine-readable surface consists of content syndication (RSS feeds), an advertising/partnerships business, and a security.txt vulnerability-disclosure program via HackerOne. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from an a16z portfolio lead and enriched with the provider's real public surface.

providers.name: C the Signs
providers.description: C the Signs is a London-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2016 by Dr Bea Bakshi and Dr Miles Payling, that uses artificial intelligence to help clinicians detect and refer patients at risk of cancer at the earliest, most treatable stage. Registered as an MHRA Class I medical device, its clinical decision support platform analyzes more than 1,000 validated, evidence-based data points across signs, symptoms and risk factors to recommend the right investigations or urgent referrals in under 60 seconds. The platform is used widely across the UK's NHS and health systems, has helped identify over 70,000 patients with cancer across 100+ cancer types at reported 99% sensitivity, and is backed by an $8M Series A investment from Khosla Ventures. It has no public developer API; this profile tracks the company as an API Evangelist network lead.

providers.name: Cantaloupe Seed API
providers.description: The Cantaloupe Seed API connects point-of-sale and self-service retail equipment to Cantaloupe's cloud-based vending management platform, enabling cashless payment processing, real-time sales tracking, and consolidated reporting across vending, micro markets, office coffee, and unattended retail channels. Seed APIs compile transactions, fees, and payments into a single bill and expose sales analytics so operators can monitor performance, payment types, and profitability across their fleet.

providers.name: Casa
providers.description: Casa is a home management membership service that helps homeowners handle maintenance and everyday household tasks through a mix of digital home documentation and professional services. A $199/month membership bundles a concierge for project research, vendor negotiation and scheduling, monthly handyman hours, an Autopilot maintenance care plan, a 3D home inventory (appliances, paint colors, safety systems), utility and property-tax tracking, package handling, and recurring-vendor management. Casa is available in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, and Austin, and is backed by Forerunner Ventures and True Ventures. No public developer/API surface has been identified.

providers.name: Chief
providers.description: Chief is a private membership network built to connect and support senior women leaders, serving executives across more than 10,000 companies with roughly 44% of members in C-suite roles. Membership combines vetted peer Core Groups, one-on-one and group executive coaching, business training (including programming with partners such as The Wharton School), member Clubhouses, and ChiefX events, plus an enterprise offering for companies sponsoring their women leaders. Chief is a membership-and-community company rather than an API provider, so this profile is an identity record in the API Evangelist network with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cleverdeck
providers.description: CleverDeck is a spaced-repetition flashcard application for iOS, built by an independent developer to help people learn and retain vocabulary and other material more efficiently. It ships hand-made premium decks covering roughly the 3,000 most common words in major foreign languages — Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Italian, Portuguese, Turkish, Persian, Russian and advanced English — with translations, transliterations, images, native-speaker audio, and example sentences in both English and the target language. The app uses the SM-2 spaced-repetition algorithm (as popularized by SuperMemo and Anki) with a customizable learning schedule, cross-device sync, and full offline support. It is free to create and study your own content, with unlimited access to the premium decks for $3 per month. CleverDeck is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or agent-facing surface.

providers.name: Comprehensive Pharmacy Services
providers.description: Comprehensive Pharmacy Services, now operating as CPS Solutions, LLC, is a healthcare company with more than 50 years of experience providing pharmacy and hospital solutions across the care continuum. It serves independent hospitals, health systems, integrated delivery networks (IDNs), and specialized health facilities with specialty pharmacy, pharmacy management, telepharmacy (24/7/365 support), 340B program compliance, supply chain management, rehabilitation services, and consulting. The company operates two proprietary SaaS platforms — CPS Optimizer for pharmacy management and TherigySTM for specialty pharmacy management — supported by 2,500+ healthcare professionals serving 800+ customers across the United States and Puerto Rico. No public API or developer program is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Crossoverhealth
providers.description: Crossover Health is an advanced primary care provider that delivers integrated, team-based healthcare for employers and their members through its proprietary Care Platform. Its services span primary care, physical medicine, mental health, health coaching, care navigation, and occupational medicine, delivered through on-site and near-site health centers and a 50-state virtual provider network. Crossover Health is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification has been found on its web properties.

providers.name: Earn.com
providers.description: Earn.com was a cryptocurrency startup founded in 2013 as 21e6 and later known as 21 Inc and 21.co, backed by a16z and others, which raised over $116 million. It began as a Bitcoin mining venture selling the 21 Bitcoin Computer, then pivoted to a paid-messaging marketplace where senders paid recipients in cryptocurrency to read and reply to email. Coinbase acquired Earn.com in April 2018 for a reported $120 million, and co-founder Balaji Srinivasan became Coinbase's first Chief Technology Officer. The standalone Earn.com product was retired and the brand was folded into Coinbase Earn, the learn-and-earn program. As of July 2026 the earn.com domain issues a blanket HTTP 301 redirect for every path to https://www.coinbase.com/earn, and no developer, documentation, or API subdomain resolves. Earn.com therefore has no independent API surface; any remaining API capability lives under Coinbase.

providers.name: EarnBetter
providers.description: EarnBetter is a consumer job-search platform that gives workers free AI-powered tools to land better work, including an AI resume builder, cover letter generator, personalized job matching across more than five million listings, and a job-search tracker. The service is positioned as 100% free to job seekers and was acquired by EarnIn, the earned-wage / payroll-access company. EarnBetter surfaces as a portfolio company of a16z and was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this pass EarnBetter publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; this profile therefore captures company identity and public link properties only, with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: EAT Club
providers.description: EAT Club is a corporate meal-delivery platform founded in 2010 in Redwood City, California by Kevin Yang and Rodrigo Santibanez, built around the idea of a "virtual cafeteria" for offices with no on-site dining. Instead of tray-style catering, each employee picks an individually packaged meal from a rotating daily menu produced by EAT Club's own kitchens and restaurant partners, and every order for a building arrives in one synchronized delivery. The company markets the program as an employee lunch benefit and reports 21 million meals delivered to roughly 1,145 companies across nine cities. Compass Group USA acquired EAT Club in October 2020 and folded its ordering, production and delivery technology into Compass Digital Labs, where it now underpins workplace, education and healthcare dining accounts across the US and Canada. The consumer-facing product is a React ordering app served from www.eatclub.com; EAT Club publishes no developer program, no API reference, no SDK and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: EcomExperts
providers.description: EcomExperts is a Latin American ecommerce ERP and technology platform that helps online sellers manage, synchronize, and automate their stores from a single screen. It centralizes omnichannel operations across marketplaces and sales channels (including multi-account Mercado Libre management), synchronizes prices and stock in real time, and issues electronic invoices automatically in bulk. Delivered as a SaaS application with a hosted dashboard and a 7-day free trial, EcomExperts operates across Argentina, Chile, Mexico, Uruguay, Colombia, and Peru. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. EcomExperts does not currently publish a public developer platform, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this profile captures company identity and public-surface signals only.

providers.name: Eloquii
providers.description: ELOQUII is a plus-size women's fashion retailer offering trend-driven, fashion-forward apparel and accessories in sizes 14 through 32, including dresses, workwear, outerwear, denim, and occasion wear with frequent seasonal collection refreshes. Known for its fit-obsessed design and inclusive sizing, the brand operates a direct-to-consumer ecommerce storefront at eloquii.com alongside select retail locations. ELOQUII was founded as a plus-size line, acquired by Walmart in 2018, and is now part of FullBeauty Brands. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a consumer ecommerce experience but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Enable
providers.description: Enable Medicine is a healthcare and life-sciences data company that licenses an integrated, AI-ready index of clinical, spatial, cellular, and molecular data. Its research platform helps biopharma companies, academic institutions, and healthcare providers run spatial-biology analysis — spatial proteomics, cell phenotyping, tumor-microenvironment characterization, immune profiling, and biomarker identification — across 20+ disease areas over harmonized datasets spanning 10M+ patients and 125M+ cells. The platform is delivered through a login-gated web application at app.enablemedicine.com; no public developer API is currently documented. Backed by initialized-capital, insight-partners, lightspeed-venture-partners, menlo-ventures, norwest-venture-partners, and sierra-ventures.

providers.name: enrich
providers.description: Enrich is a private, invite-only membership network for senior technology leaders — VPs, Directors, and CXOs from companies including Google, Slack, Anthropic, and OpenAI. It runs peer-led conversations with executive coaching, curated small-group and monthly in-person dinners, expert-led operator discussions, topic-based peer groups (organizational design, career transitions), and a private Slack community for real-time peer advice. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Cowboy Ventures, and added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead. Enrich publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface — it is a community/membership product, not an API provider.

providers.name: Eton Solutions
providers.description: Eton Solutions, L.P. is a Morrisville, North Carolina wealth-technology company that builds AtlasFive, a purpose-built ERP platform for single-family offices, multi-family offices, private funds and the ultra-high-net-worth families they serve. AtlasFive consolidates general ledger and partnership/fund/trust accounting, investment management and performance, bill pay and transaction processing, tax workflow, CRM and document management onto one data core, and aggregates positions and transactions from more than 1,500 banks and custodians via direct electronic feeds, portal scrapes, PDF statement extraction and partner aggregators. The EtonAI product line layers a knowledge graph and generative-AI assistants over that core. Integration is delivered through customer-scoped Reporting APIs and a Power BI connector rather than a public developer program: Eton Solutions publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK or sandbox as of August 2026. The company does publish a substantial compliance posture — ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management), ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II, with GDPR and CCPA alignment — and the platform is hosted on Microsoft Azure. Founded out of the multi-family office Eton Advisors and led by CEO Robert Mallernee with Executive Chairman Satyen Patel, with additional offices in Dubai and Bengaluru.

providers.name: Federal Trade Commission
providers.description: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is a U.S. federal agency that enforces antitrust and consumer protection laws affecting virtually every area of commerce. The FTC publishes developer-facing data products and APIs through ftc.gov/developer and partner platforms, including the National Do Not Call Registry telemarketer access program and the Consumer Sentinel Network of consumer complaint data shared with law enforcement.

providers.name: Ferrum Health
providers.description: Ferrum Health is a healthcare AI governance company whose AI Governance Suite lets health systems deploy, validate, orchestrate, and monitor clinical AI models securely behind their own firewall, without protected health information leaving the health system. The vendor-neutral, privately deployed platform integrates once with existing EMR, PACS, and worklist infrastructure, then routes every clinical AI model — FDA-cleared, CE-marked, open-source, or homegrown — through a single secure path via its Deployment Fabric, curates 60+ applications in its Model Hub across radiology, cardiology, oncology, neurology, and musculoskeletal specialties, and continuously links predictions, ground truth, and outcomes for bias and drift detection through its Observability Lens. It is SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR aligned, and is used by Sutter Health, Carle Health, and 250+ sites.

providers.name: Fig 1
providers.description: Fig.1 (Figure 1 Beauty) is a direct-to-consumer skincare brand created through 8VC's Build program, co-founded with Harvard-trained dermatologist Dr. Courtney Rubin, focused on demystifying and democratizing skincare through transparent, efficacy-driven, in-house formulations sold across a small launch line of cleansers, treatments, and moisturizers. Its public surface is a Shopify-hosted ecommerce storefront at fig-1.co; Fig.1 publishes no first-party developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation. This API Evangelist profile records the brand's identity, storefront policy pages, and domain-security posture. The /.well-known/openid-configuration served on the host is Shopify's shared Customer-Account platform OIDC, not a Fig.1 API.

providers.name: Flock Homes
providers.description: Flock Homes is a real estate investment platform, founded in 2020 and backed by a16z, that lets individual rental-property owners retire from active landlording by contributing their single-family and multifamily homes into a professionally managed, diversified residential real estate fund. Flock uses a 721 Exchange (an UPREIT contribution) so owners can trade appreciated rental property for fund shares on a tax-deferred basis, deferring capital gains and depreciation-recapture taxes while eliminating repair, vacancy, and eviction responsibilities. Fund investors receive quarterly cash-flow distributions and long-term appreciation across a nationwide portfolio, with Flock handling all property management, maintenance, and tenant operations. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface has been found; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Flossy
providers.description: Flossy is a Santa Monica, California healthcare technology company that builds AI agents ("AI coworkers") for dental practices, veterinary clinics and med spas. Its named agents cover front-office and revenue-cycle work: Fiona handles inbound and outbound patient communication and scheduling across phone, SMS and web chat; Betsy scores call-center quality and marketing performance; Michael captures insurance, verifies benefits and surfaces billing insights; and Reid forecasts revenue and optimizes schedule capacity and staffing. FlossyHQ is the operator console the practice works in, and Agent Builder lets practices assemble custom agents. Founded in 2020 by Miles Beckett and Steve Seigel, Flossy began as a pay-as-you-go dental care marketplace and has since repositioned around agentic automation for practice operations. Flossy publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the one publicly reachable first-party integration surface is the embeddable Fiona web-chat widget.

providers.name: Foodsmart
providers.description: Foodsmart is a telenutrition company that pairs the nation's largest network of registered dietitians with a digital food-benefits platform, delivering personalized nutrition care via telehealth to more than three million members. The company partners with health plans and employers to reach Medicaid, Medicare, and commercial members, combining one-on-one dietitian counseling with meal planning, grocery ordering, and SNAP benefits enrollment. Foodsmart's "Foodscription" model connects clinical nutrition guidance to affordable, healthy food access to improve outcomes and lower the cost of diet-related chronic disease. This profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Foodsmart exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Genome Medical
