Its current products include Dala Studio and Jitume, applying LLMs and proprietary data to build AI agents and workforce-intelligence tools for the African digital economy. Gebeya is backed by Partech. As of this profiling it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK.

providers.name: General Services Administration
providers.description: The General Services Administration (GSA) provides workplaces by constructing, managing, and preserving government buildings and by leasing and managing commercial real estate. GSA acquisition solutions offer private sector professional services, equipment, supplies, and IT to government organizations and the military. GSA also promotes management best practices and efficient government operations through the development of governmentwide policies, including a broad portfolio of public APIs.

providers.name: Get
providers.description: Get (useget.com) is a Singapore-based fintech company offering a mobile banking and financial-literacy platform for children, teens, and their families. The Get app pairs separate kid and parent accounts with prepaid Visa cards, parental spending controls, automated weekly allowances, a chore-based reward system, real-time spending analytics, and savings-goal folders, so young people can practice using real money tools in a safe, supervised environment. Get sells consumer subscription tiers (Get Core and Get Plus) plus a family account, and operates under a Payment Services exemption in Singapore. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification is published at this time; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Giftly
providers.description: Giftly is a digital gifting platform that lets anyone send a flexible monetary gift redeemable at a specific local or national business, or as cash. Senders pick a place or category, customize the card design and tagline, choose a gift amount up to $1,000, and deliver it by email, text, print, or mail. Recipients redeem a Giftly gift as a Visa or Mastercard gift card by mail, as a credit to their bank account, or as a credit to their PayPal account; gifts never expire and carry no inactivity fees. Giftly also runs a corporate and business program for companies sending gifts at scale. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital; Giftly publishes a consumer web product and a business portal, but no public developer API, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Greenboard
providers.description: Greenboard is an AI-native compliance software platform for SEC- and FINRA-regulated financial institutions, consolidating communications archiving, employee compliance monitoring, marketing/advertising review, firm-wide compliance management, and third-party (vendor) compliance into a single system of action. It serves independent advisors, RIAs, hedge funds, private funds, and broker-dealers, automating regulatory workflows and reducing review times. Greenboard is a General Catalyst portfolio company. Its product is delivered as a hosted SaaS application; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published at this time, so this profile captures corporate identity, trust/compliance posture (SOC 2 Type II), and domain security rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Hidden Level
providers.description: Hidden Level is a U.S.-based defense and aerospace technology company that turns radio-frequency (RF) activity into trusted airspace intelligence. Its passive RF sensing platform detects and tracks unmanned aerial systems (drones) and other activity across air, ground, sea, and space domains without requiring emitters or heavy on-site infrastructure. Hidden Level packages this as hardware sensor platforms, software platforms, and data platforms serving defense and military, critical infrastructure protection, homeland security, and public safety customers. The company hosts its platform on AWS with least-privilege access, MFA, and TLS 1.3 API communications, aligns corporate controls to NIST SP 800-171, and emphasizes U.S. design and manufacturing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks Hidden Level's public web and security surface; the company does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs.

providers.name: iCapital Network
providers.description: iCapital (Institutional Capital Network, Inc.) is a New York-headquartered financial technology company, founded in 2013, that operates the alternative investments marketplace and the operating infrastructure behind it. Its platform lets wealth managers, RIAs, family offices and institutional investors research, subscribe to, service and report on private markets funds, hedge funds, structured investments, annuities, model portfolios and separately managed accounts, while asset managers use it to distribute those products into the wealth channel. iCapital Marketplace advertises access to funds from 700+ asset managers and reports $945B+ in global platform assets. Around the marketplace sit Architect (portfolio construction and analytics), Data Solutions (alternative data management and consolidated reporting), Identity Solutions (KYC/AML), and iCapital DLT, an API-first distributed ledger platform built on the Canton Network. Integration with custodians, fund administrators, transfer agents and advisor platforms (BNY, Fidelity, Envestnet, Orion, Morningstar, Vestmark, TradePMR, GeoWealth, Ultimus, UMB) happens through SSO, embedded workflows and partner data integrations. As of the 2026-08-01 enrichment pass iCapital publishes no public developer portal, API reference, machine-readable API contract or client SDKs; API documentation is described as available to integration partners only, through the sales and technical-support organization.

providers.name: Internal Revenue Service
providers.description: The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is the United States federal tax collection agency and a bureau of the Department of the Treasury. The IRS publishes developer resources for tax software providers and transmitters including the Modernized e-File (MeF) system for electronic tax return submission, the e-Services suite for authorized e-file providers, and Publication 4164 (the MeF Guide for Software Developers and Transmitters) which documents the XML schemas and transmission protocols required for integration.

providers.name: iovation
providers.description: iovation is a device-intelligence and online fraud-prevention service acquired by TransUnion in 2018 and now delivered as TransUnion TruValidate Device Risk (the SDK was formerly branded "FraudForce"). It fingerprints web and mobile devices into an encrypted "blackbox," evaluates it against a shared reputation database of billions of devices plus configurable rulesets, and returns a transaction risk assessment. Device data is collected client-side with first-party JavaScript and native iOS/Android SDKs; server-side integration is a SOAP CheckTransactionDetails call over HTTPS. iovation is used for account takeover, new-account fraud, payment fraud, and bot detection.

providers.name: Jaspersoft
providers.description: Jaspersoft is a business intelligence and embedded analytics platform, now part of Cloud Software Group (formerly TIBCO). Its flagship products are the open-source JasperReports Library — a Java reporting engine (net.sf.jasperreports) — and JasperReports Server, a reporting and analytics server that exposes a REST API (rest_v2) for managing the repository, running and scheduling reports, executing queries, and administering users, roles, and organizations. Developers embed Jaspersoft content into their own applications with Visualize.js and the js-visualize component library, and interact with the server programmatically through official Java and PHP REST clients. Sector: data analytics / business intelligence. Backed by Sapphire Ventures; surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: Kodiak AI
providers.description: Kodiak AI, Inc. (formerly Kodiak Robotics) is a Mountain View, California company building the Kodiak Driver, an AI-powered ground autonomy system for driverless trucking and defense vehicles. Founded in April 2018 by Don Burnette, Kodiak develops a purpose-built autonomous driving stack — sensor pods, 4D radar, sparse maps, and fallback systems — that integrates into third-party driving platforms rather than shipping a vehicle of its own. The company runs commercial driverless freight lanes in Texas, Oklahoma, Ohio and Indiana with partners including Atlas Energy Solutions, Maersk, Martin Brower, Roehl Transport, JB Hunt and Werner, and it adapts the same driver to defense and industrial missions with General Dynamics Land Systems, Textron Systems and the US Army. Kodiak raised a $125M Series B in 2021 with Lightspeed Venture Partners, Battery Ventures, CRV, SIP Global Partners and others participating, and became a public company through a business combination with Ares Acquisition Corporation II. Kodiak publishes a corporate web presence, a news/RSS feed and an llms.txt for agents, but does not currently operate a public developer program, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Kraka
providers.description: Kraka Technologies GmbH is a Berlin-based industrial AI company whose platform turns plain video recordings of shop-floor tasks into standardized, multilingual, step-by-step work instructions. Kraka Studio is the core product, extended by Training, Maintenance and Quality modules covering workforce qualification, AI-assisted fault diagnosis and checklist-driven quality control. Kraka positions itself as closing the execution gap between ERP systems that manage data and the work actually performed on the factory floor. Backed by Seedcamp. No public API, developer portal or SDK is published as of July 2026.

providers.name: L'Oréal
providers.description: L'Oréal is the world's largest cosmetics and beauty company, producing skincare, makeup, haircare, and fragrance products. The group operates a portfolio of over 35 brands, including Lancôme, Maybelline, Garnier, NYX Professional Makeup, Kérastase, La Roche-Posay, and Kiehl's, sold in over 150 countries. L'Oréal's primary developer surface is the ModiFace platform (a wholly owned subsidiary), which exposes an AR virtual try-on SDK and API for partner brands and retailers. L'Oréal Group itself does not operate a general-purpose corporate developer portal.

providers.name: LaborUp
providers.description: LaborUp is an AI-powered recruiting platform for American manufacturing, connecting skilled industrial workers — machinists, CNC programmers, welders, and maintenance technicians — with manufacturing employers. The platform combines voice-first AI screening, skills verification, and constraint-aware matching with dedicated recruiter support, and claims 5-10x faster hiring, more than 50% lower cost than traditional staffing agencies, 3x better post-hire retention, and a proprietary network of 25,000+ vetted workers. Founded by Simba Jonga, LaborUp raised $7.74M ($1.935M pre-seed plus a $5.8M seed announced in August 2025) led by NVP with Torch Capital, Threshold, Heartland VC, Daybreak, Westbound, Marketplace Capital, and Market Square Ventures. Early traction is concentrated in the Knoxville, Tennessee manufacturing corridor and in aerospace, shipbuilding, and critical infrastructure. As of July 2026 LaborUp publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification; the product is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application.

providers.name: Lightelligence
providers.description: Lightelligence (legal entity Shanghai Xizhi Technology Co., Ltd. / 曦智科技, founded 2017 as an MIT spin-out) builds optoelectronic hybrid computing hardware — photonic accelerators and optical interconnect fabric for AI and high-performance computing. Its product line is physical: the PACE 2 optoelectronic accelerated computing card (a PCIe Gen4 x16 accelerator built around a 128x128 optical matrix multiplier), the Gazelle optical computing evaluation board, the Photowave CXL optical interconnect, and the Lightsphere X distributed optical circuit switch, supported by the company's oMAC, oNOC and oNET optical core, network-on-chip and inter-chip network technologies. The software surface is a device-side stack — ONNX, OpenCL, PyTorch and TVM support plus a Python SDK (lt_sdk) that compiled and ran models on the optical processing unit — not a web API. As of this profile the company publishes no public web API, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, and no developer portal; the lightelligence-sdk package and its Read the Docs reference have both been withdrawn. Its remaining public developer-facing surface is a GitHub organization of chip design and verification tooling (Bazel Verilog build rules, RTL/UVM linters, the yis interface-spec generator) and an Optical Computing Developer Community of research cases and papers.

providers.name: Limepay
providers.description: Limepay was a Melbourne-based Australian embedded-payments and white-label buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) company that let merchants and platforms accept card payments and offer pay-in-instalments through a single drop-in checkout and a REST API. Its developer surface covered an embeddable Checkout, a Payments API (orders, order-pay, transaction capture/void, refunds, 3-D Secure and wallet payments such as Apple Pay and Google Pay), and a Platform API for marketplaces to onboard and manage sub-merchants, run KYC/identification, and pull settlement reports. Authentication used a Publishable API key for frontend/checkout calls, a Secret API key for server-to-server calls, and a platform API key for administrative onboarding, all passed as Bearer tokens. After a failed 2021 IPO, Limepay was acquired by ASX-listed Spenda in 2024 and its product line was continued under the April Solutions brand; the primary domain limepay.com.au now redirects to meetapril.com and the docs.limepay.com.au developer portal is gated behind a Redocly login. This profile documents Limepay's real, historically public API family honestly; no machine-readable OpenAPI is currently downloadable.

providers.name: Medix Infusion
providers.description: Medix Infusion, Inc. is a technology-enabled infusion care provider headquartered in Addison, Texas, that administers infusion and injectable therapies — anti-infectives, biologics, IVIG and other specialty medications — to chronically and acutely ill patients through a network of ambulatory infusion suites and in the home. The company concentrates on rural, suburban and other under-served markets, coordinating benefits investigation, prior authorization, scheduling, pharmacy and nursing around each referral, and is accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Health Care (ACHC). It raised a $35M Series B led by Echo Health Ventures in January 2023 alongside existing investor Noro-Moseley Partners. Medix Infusion operates as a care-delivery organization: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract on any public host as of this profile.

providers.name: Merlin Labs
providers.description: Merlin (Merlin Labs, Inc., NASDAQ: MRLN) is a Boston-headquartered aerospace and defense company founded in 2018 that builds takeoff-to-touchdown flight autonomy for legacy and next-generation aircraft. Its product is the Merlin Pilot, an aircraft-agnostic, AI-powered autonomy stack that pairs machine-learning mission planning with deterministic, hardcoded fallback flight systems, and that has flown hundreds of autonomous flights from test facilities in Kerikeri (New Zealand), Quonset Point (Rhode Island) and Bedford/Hanscom (Massachusetts). Merlin is a prime contractor to USSOCOM for C-130J autonomy, works with the U.S. Air Force on KC-135 tanker autonomy, and collaborates with Northrop Grumman, Honeywell, GE Aerospace and Israel Aerospace Industries. The company holds a New Zealand Part 146 aircraft design organization designation and reached Stage of Involvement 3 (SOI 3) with the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand in August 2026. Merlin became publicly traded in March 2026 through a business combination with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp IV. Merlin sells embedded flight-autonomy software to aircraft OEMs, primes and government programs; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Mind Candy, Moshi
providers.description: Mind Candy Ltd is a London-based children's media and technology company, originally known for the Moshi Monsters online game and now operating Moshi, an award-winning children's app for sleep, relaxation and learning. Moshi offers hundreds of hours of bedtime stories, sleep sounds, music, white noise and educational activities delivered through iOS and Android consumer apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. Moshi is a direct-to-consumer subscription product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Miso Robotics
providers.description: Miso Robotics is a Pasadena, California kitchen-automation company that builds AI-powered robotics and restaurant operations software for commercial food service. Its flagship product, Flippy, is an autonomous fry station that uses computer vision and NVIDIA-accelerated motion planning to identify food items, detect doneness and run up to 100 baskets per hour on existing commercial fryers from Frymaster, Henny Penny and Pitco. Miso also ships Zippy (built on the acquired Zignyl platform), a real-time digital shift manager for forecasting, scheduling, task management, incentives and payroll that connects to restaurant point-of-sale systems. Customers include White Castle, Jack in the Box, CaliBurger and Auntie Anne's. Miso publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contract and no SDKs; its integrations are delivered as private partner connections (Toast, PAR and other POS vendors) arranged through sales, and its public GitHub organization carries ROS/robotics and cloud-infrastructure forks used internally rather than a client-facing API surface.

providers.name: OJO Labs
providers.description: OJO Labs is an Austin, Texas real estate technology company founded in 2015 that operates Movoto, one of the largest consumer real estate search portals in the United States, alongside OJO's homeownership platform for buyers, sellers and existing homeowners. The company pairs AI-driven property search and home-value tracking with human real estate advisors, and monetizes primarily through an agent referral network that routes qualified consumers to licensed brokerages. OJO acquired Movoto in 2020 and The LEAD Syndicate in 2024, launching Lever by Movoto as its industry-facing agent platform, and was itself acquired by Columbus, Ohio mortgage lender Lower in May 2025. OJO Labs is an end-user product company: it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and its lead delivery to agent CRMs is handled through email parsing and third-party middleware rather than a documented partner API.

providers.name: Onlia
providers.description: Onlia is a Canadian digital insurance brokerage, operating as the registered business name of Onlia Agency Inc. and backed by Southampton Financial Inc. (the Southampton group of companies). It sells personal lines direct to consumers online and by phone — auto (car, motorcycle, ATV, snowmobile, trailer, motorhome), property (home, condo, tenant, landlord, second home, mobile home) and lifestyle lines (boat, pet, life, travel, seasonal) — plus group and bundle programs. Onlia does not underwrite; it places business with a panel of Canadian carriers disclosed publicly on its broker-disclosure page, including Aviva, Gore Mutual, Economical/Definity, Pembridge, Pafco, Echelon, Wawanesa, Unica, Forward, Premier, Facility Association (Intact) and APOLLO. Its home market is Canada, concentrated in Ontario, where market conduct sits with FSRA while OSFI supervises the federally-regulated carriers behind the policies. API posture, recorded honestly: Onlia publishes NO public developer portal and NO self-serve API. developer., developers., docs. and api. under onlia.ca do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer and /integrations on the marketing site all return 404. The only quote/bind/issue/FNOL surface is app.onlia.ca, a consumer-facing Angular single-page app running on a white-labelled Ignite Insurance policy administration platform whose backend is private to the app. The one "partner" page is a B2B marketing page inviting affinity discount partnerships by email, with no technical onboarding. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference appears anywhere on the public site. The app's own bundle shows the private backend runs on MuleSoft Anypoint CloudHub ESB services (auto and home policy, authentication, documents, VIN/MVR, claims) plus an Ignite Insurance authentication service — real REST plumbing behind the SPA, but undocumented, uncredentialed and not offered to third parties, so no API entry is claimed here.

providers.name: OpenFX
providers.description: OpenFX is a cross-border payment infrastructure provider delivering real-time foreign exchange liquidity and settlement for institutional clients across emerging markets. Backed by Accel and Northzone, it pairs traditional-finance reliability with blockchain-rail speed to settle fiat and stablecoin payments in minutes across 40+ currency pairs and 25+ local payment rails, and exposes a programmatic Trading API (REST, FIX and Streaming) to automate quotes, trades, deposits and withdrawals. Serves remittance companies, FX on/off ramps, payment service providers and stablecoin infrastructure providers.

providers.name: Outschool
providers.description: Outschool is an education-technology marketplace for live, small-group online classes for learners ages 3-18. It connects families and independent teachers across 140,000+ subjects — from math and coding to art, music, and hobbies — offered as one-time sessions, ongoing courses, camps, and social clubs delivered over live video. Outschool also serves schools and districts through its for-organizations program. Backed by Bond Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Union Square Ventures, and Y Combinator, the platform is a consumer web application; it exposes no publicly documented developer API. The site is powered by an internal, undocumented GraphQL endpoint (outschool.com/graphql) used only by its own front end and largely blocked to crawlers. This profile is an API Evangelist network company record enriched from the provider's public web surface.

providers.name: OwnBackup
providers.description: OwnBackup (Own Company) is a SaaS data protection platform providing backup, recovery, and sandbox seeding for Salesforce and other cloud applications.

providers.name: Parallel Learning
providers.description: Parallel Learning is a special education services and staffing platform that connects K-12 schools and districts with a nationwide network of licensed clinicians for the remote delivery of specialized student support. Through its proprietary, HIPAA/FERPA-compliant Pathway platform it delivers virtual psychoeducational and neurodevelopmental assessments, speech-language therapy, behavioral and mental-health counseling, specialized instruction in reading, writing, and math, and executive-function coaching, pairing secure teletherapy with progress tracking and clinical oversight so districts can meet compliance requirements and improve student outcomes. The company serves thousands of students across dozens of states and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Passes
providers.description: Passes is a creator monetization and accelerator platform founded in 2022 by Lucy Guo and headquartered in Los Angeles. Creators use Passes to build direct, paid relationships with their audiences through subscriptions, paid DMs, livestreams, one-on-one video calls, merchandise, automated message sequences, and instant payouts, while keeping 90% of what they earn. Backed by Bond Capital and Multicoin Capital, the company rebranded in 2026 as a creator accelerator. Passes does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its real public web surface — llms.txt, security.txt, mobile deep-link association files, and domain-security posture — harvested by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: PawnHero
providers.description: PawnHero is the Philippines' first online pawnshop, offering instant collateral-based cash loans against jewelry, gold, luxury designer bags, watches, gadgets, and Apple devices. Customers create a pawn ticket online, an in-house courier ("Pawntrooper") collects the item for appraisal, and approved funds are disbursed within minutes via bank transfer or e-wallet, with loan terms up to 180 days and renewal options. The business is supervised by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). PawnHero operates as a consumer-facing web and mobile service and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Pivotal Health
providers.description: Pivotal Health (formerly Radix Health) is a healthcare technology company and self-described "IDR Authority" that helps medical providers secure fair out-of-network reimbursement through the federal Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process created by the No Surprises Act. Its platform combines automated eligibility screening, dispute submission software integrated with major revenue cycle management (RCM) systems, payer data, and white-glove managed services across emergency medicine, anesthesiology, radiology, surgery, pathology, air ambulance, and hospitals and health systems. Pivotal Health is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: PlanetiQ
providers.description: PlanetiQ is a commercial space-weather and atmospheric data company headquartered in Golden, Colorado, operating the GNOMES constellation of small satellites carrying its Pyxis GNSS radio occultation (GNSS-RO) sensor. Pyxis receives signals from all four global navigation constellations (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou) and turns the refracted signal into vertical atmospheric profiles of temperature, pressure, density, refractivity and humidity at 100 m vertical resolution, plus ionospheric total electron content, scintillation phase and polarimetric precipitation observations. The data is sold as Level 1B calibrated phase/SNR and Level 2 bending angle/refractivity products, primarily under U.S. government contracts (NOAA Commercial Data Program radio occultation data buys, NASA Commercial Satellite Data Acquisition, U.S. Air Force STRATFI) and redistributed to authorized users in netCDF via NASA's Satellite Data Explorer. PlanetiQ publishes no public developer program, no API, and no machine-readable API contract; commercial and defense access runs through a sales conversation rather than self-service onboarding.

providers.name: Polsia
providers.description: Polsia is an autonomous AI business-management platform marketed as "AI that runs your company while you sleep." It deploys a set of specialized AI agents — business planning, competitor research, social media, ads, email outreach, customer support, code generation, finance, and deployment — coordinated by an orchestrator to run a company's daily operations on recurring schedules for a monthly subscription plus a share of revenue generated on the platform. Founded by Ben Sera and backed by True Ventures and Sound Ventures (raised $30M at a $250M valuation in 2026), Polsia is a hosted consumer/SMB SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server.

providers.name: proteanTecs
providers.description: proteanTecs is an Israeli deep data analytics company for advanced electronics. It embeds on-chip monitoring Agents (UCT, margin, path margin, I/O and power monitors) into semiconductor designs and pairs them with cloud and edge machine-learning applications that report health, performance, reliability and quality of chips and systems from design through production test into field operation. Solutions cover power and performance optimization, RAS, functional safety and diagnostics, chip production, system production and advanced packaging, and are consumed by semiconductor, data center, AI/HPC, automotive, telecom and mobile customers. The company markets APIs and data connectors for integrating its analytics with ATE testers and third-party analytics tools, but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Qualifi
providers.description: Qualifi is a recruiting and hiring platform that streamlines candidate screening through asynchronous, voice-based phone interviews, automated scheduling, and live video interviews. Recruiters send candidates a pre-recorded phone screen, review responses on their own schedule, and move qualified applicants forward faster, reducing time-to-hire while keeping the candidate experience high. Qualifi offers 50+ applicant tracking system (ATS) integrations, a "Qualifi Copilot" that surfaces the tool directly inside your ATS, and Google/Microsoft calendar sync. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and is SOC 2 Type II certified.

providers.name: Raenest
providers.description: Raenest (formerly Geegpay) is a global money platform for freelancers, creators, remote workers, students, and businesses in Africa and beyond. It provides multi-currency accounts in USD, GBP, EUR, USDT, and USDC, virtual and physical Visa cards, international payment collection from 190+ countries, smart invoicing tools, US stock investing, stablecoin support, and a rewards program. Raenest is delivered through its mobile and web apps (app.raenest.com); as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. Backed by QED Investors and Techstars.

providers.name: RankScience
providers.description: RankScience is a San Francisco based SEO and AI-visibility agency (RankScience LLC) that helps startups, SaaS companies, and enterprises grow search traffic through foundational and technical SEO, strategic content, and link building, alongside next-generation AI-search optimization services (Generative Engine Optimization, Large Language Model Optimization, and Answer Engine Optimization) for platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity. It began as a YC-backed SEO A/B testing platform and now operates as a services agency. RankScience does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public web and AI-discovery surface (a published /llms.txt and domain security posture).

providers.name: Ray White
providers.description: Ray White is Australasia's largest real estate group, a family-owned brokerage network founded in 1902 and headquartered in Brisbane, Australia, running 550+ Australian offices and roughly a thousand offices in total across Australia, New Zealand, Indonesia, Hong Kong, China, Papua New Guinea, the Middle East and Atlanta USA, spanning residential sales, auctions, commercial (Ray White Commercial / rwc.com.au), rural and livestock, property management, projects, marine, hotels, valuations, business sales, insurance and mortgage broking through sister brand Loan Market. In the Australian property value chain Ray White sits on the AGENCY side of a portal duopoly — it lists into REA Group's realestate.com.au and Domain rather than operating a portal or a registry of its own — and it is an API CONSUMER, not an API producer. In December 2025 Ray White named realestate.com.au and PropTrack its data partners explicitly for their "industry leading API architecture", piping that licensed market data into its proprietary OneSystem, NurtureCloud and Pulse platforms. Its API posture is therefore honestly stated as none-published — as of 2026-07-26 no developer portal, no public API documentation, no OpenAPI or OData $metadata contract, and no published partner-API application path could be found on raywhite.com or any developer/api/docs subdomain (all of which fail DNS resolution). RESO is absent — Ray White does not appear in the RESO certification directory, which is unsurprising because RESO is a North American, NAR-driven mandate with no Australian counterpart; Australia's closest thing to a required machine-readable property rail is PEXA electronic conveyancing, which Ray White transacts through as a participant rather than exposes.

providers.name: RCS Capital
providers.description: RCS Capital Corporation (RCAP) was a publicly traded holding company focused on the financial services industry, founded by Nicholas Schorsch and taken public in June 2013. The firm owned a diversified group of businesses including independent broker-dealers, investment banking, capital markets, and transaction management services. It assembled Cetera Financial Group to become the second largest network of independent broker-dealers in the United States, with approximately 9,100 financial advisors managing $220 billion in assets under administration for 2.5 million clients. RCS Capital filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in January 2016, citing $1.39 billion in debts, and emerged in May 2016 as Aretec Group, Inc., the holding company of Cetera Financial Group. No public developer APIs were offered under the RCS Capital brand.

providers.name: Reindeer AI
providers.description: Reindeer AI is an enterprise agentic AI platform that automates back-office business operations across finance, banking, insurance, supply chain, procurement, legal compliance, and global business services. Founded in 2024 with offices in New York and Tel Aviv, Reindeer deploys custom AI agents that learn from operational workflows using its Fast Track Training approach (functional models in roughly two weeks from a small number of samples), with human-in-the-loop escalation, continuous learning, and Model Reality Grounding safeguards against hallucination. It ships 200+ pre-trained skills and 200+ out-of-the-box integrations into systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Workday, ServiceNow, and Salesforce, is model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Bedrock, DeepSeek, GLM), and emphasizes customer data ownership and enterprise security (ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type 2, GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA). Reindeer is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, TEAM8, and Vesey Ventures. Reindeer does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or a developer portal; the product is delivered as an enterprise engagement, so this profile captures company identity and security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Rescripted
providers.description: Rescripted is a digital women's health platform dedicated to empowering women across the entire lifecycle, from first period to last. It combines an editorial content hub of expert-reviewed articles, videos, and clinical research with Clara, an AI-powered health companion built on thousands of real questions and reviewed by medical experts. The platform spans menstrual health, fertility, pregnancy, sexual health, general wellness, and condition management for PCOS, endometriosis, and related concerns, and works with 200+ health and wellness partners. Founded by Kristyn Hodgdon and Abby Mercado and backed by Techstars, Rescripted is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: River Health
providers.description: River Health is an employer-sponsored virtual-first health plan operated by Mountain (joinmountain.com) that gives employees comprehensive primary and behavioral care at no cost to them. Members get unlimited virtual primary care and in-person doctor visits, behavioral health and therapy, thousands of free medications with home delivery or pharmacy pickup, free preventive care and screenings, after-hours urgent care, no-cost specialty and chronic- condition care, and free lab testing through Quest Diagnostics. Employers from small businesses to the Fortune 500 sponsor the plan; members enroll and manage care through the River Health member app at app.helloriver.com. River Health is a portfolio company of Techstars. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal has been published.

providers.name: Ruma Care
providers.description: Ruma Care is a healthcare software company that streamlines the prior authorization process for biologic and infusion medications in infusion clinics. Its AI-powered platform pulls patient and insurance data from electronic health records (EHRs) to identify payer requirements, auto-populates payer-specific prior authorization forms with clinical data, flags missing documentation, and then manages insurer communication and follow-up until an authorization is approved. Built by former infusion clinic staff, Ruma Care consolidates the manual portal, fax, and paper workflows behind buy-and-bill and infusion services into a single platform to reduce denials and accelerate patient access to biologics. Ruma Care is a Y Combinator-backed company. As of this profile the company exposes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Signal Sciences
providers.description: Signal Sciences is a web application and API protection (WAAP) company whose Next-Gen Web Application Firewall (WAF) and Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP) defend web apps, APIs, and microservices against the OWASP Top 10, account takeover, and malicious bots without the tuning burden of legacy WAFs. Founded in 2014 by Andrew Peterson, Nick Galbreath, and Zane Lackey and backed by CRV, Index Ventures, and others, Signal Sciences was acquired by Fastly in October 2020 for approximately $775M and is now sold as the Fastly Next-Gen WAF. The product retains its own control plane and REST API at dashboard.signalsciences.net/api/v0, which remains live for existing customers and lets developers programmatically manage corps, sites, requests, events, custom signals, rules, redactions, lists, rate-limited sources, thresholds, virtual patches, and workspace alerts. Product documentation now lives on the Fastly developer documentation site.

providers.name: Simplifeye
providers.description: Simplifeye is a dental practice management platform that helps practices grow and streamline front-office operations through integrated payments, online scheduling, live webchat, and patient-engagement campaigns. Its HIPAA-compliant payments product supports in-office transactions, invoicing, and customizable payment plans; its 24/7 real-time online scheduler lets patients self-book appointments; and its live webchat is staffed by real people who answer patient questions and qualify leads outside business hours. Simplifeye was acquired by Vyne Dental and integrates with the Vyne Trellis billing platform for claims, eligibility, and revenue acceleration. Simplifeye operates a private, authenticated backend (api.simplifeye.co) that powers its dashboard and patient-facing widgets, but publishes no public developer program, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Skyryse
providers.description: Skyryse is an El Segundo, California aviation technology company founded in 2016 by Mark Groden and Mitch Adler that builds SkyOS, a universal operating system for flight. SkyOS is a retrofittable hardware and software stack that replaces complex mechanical flight controls with a triply redundant, software-driven system, letting a pilot fly an airplane or helicopter with a single control stick and touchscreens. The platform delivers simplified flight controls, inherent stability, automated maneuvers, emergency autorotation, automated zero-visibility landing, envelope protection, and optionally piloted capability. Skyryse also produces Skyryse One, a SkyOS-powered production helicopter, and Skylar, a universal AI flight assistant. Customers and partners span the U.S. military, law enforcement, Cal Fire, emergency medical services, disaster response, and private operators. In February 2026 the company raised over $300 million in Series C funding at a $1.15 billion post-money valuation, co-led by Autopilot and Fidelity Investments. Skyryse operates as a certified-avionics and aircraft manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: SpartanNash
providers.description: SpartanNash is a Byron Center, Michigan food solutions company that operates as both a wholesale grocery distributor and a retail grocer. Its wholesale segment supplies roughly 2,100 independent retail locations, national accounts and e-commerce partners from a network of distribution centers, and through its MDV business it is the leading distributor of grocery products to United States military commissaries and exchanges worldwide. Its retail segment operates roughly 200 corporate-owned supermarkets under banners including Family Fare, Martin's Super Markets, D&W Fresh Market, VG's Grocery, Dan's Supermarket, Family Fresh Market, Needler's Fresh Market, Fresh City Market, Forest Hills Foods and Supermercado Nuestra Familia, alongside pharmacy and fuel centers. Formed by the 2013 merger of Spartan Stores and Nash Finch, the company traded on Nasdaq as SPTN until C&S Wholesale Grocers completed its acquisition of SpartanNash on September 22, 2025; SpartanNash now operates as part of C&S and its corporate web properties are progressively being folded into cswg.com. SpartanNash publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; supplier and customer system integration is transacted over EDI through trading-partner onboarding rather than a public API.

providers.name: Stockly
providers.description: Stockly (Stockly SAS, headquartered in Vitry-sur-Seine, France) operates a global inventory network for e-commerce, positioning itself as "the first global inventory for Retail." It connects online retailers that are missing stock (Demanders) with brands and official retailers that hold surplus inventory (Suppliers), detecting out-of-stock variants and filling the gaps in real time so that e-shops never run out of stock. Stockly integrates directly with a retailer's e-commerce infrastructure via API, a CMS, or a marketplace, and is building toward a stock exchange for e-commerce inventory in compliance with brands' distribution policies. The company reports 300+ partnered retailers across Europe and 100M+ available items, and is backed by Techstars. Stockly is primarily a partner-onboarded platform rather than a broad self-serve public developer API.

providers.name: Straiker
providers.description: Straiker is an AI-native security company for agentic AI, founded by security veterans from Palo Alto Networks. It protects every layer of AI agent deployments from prompts to infrastructure with a closed-loop system that pairs autonomous adversarial testing with sub-second runtime defense. Its products are Ascend AI (autonomous AI threat detection that integrates into CI/CD to test agents for prompt injection, tool manipulation, goal hijacking and data leakage), Defend AI (agentic runtime security that blocks identity abuse, memory poisoning, data exfiltration and malicious MCP connections in real time using proprietary LLM judges), and Discover AI (agent/MCP discovery and posture management). Straiker is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its developer documentation and API/SDK integration surface are gated behind an enterprise access code; there is no public API reference.

providers.name: Stuf Storage
providers.description: Stuf is a next-generation, tech-enabled self-storage operator that partners with commercial real estate owners to convert underutilized space — basements, garages and retail vacancies — into modern neighborhood storage facilities. Stuf runs 36 facilities across seven US metros (New York City, Los Angeles, the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, Atlanta, Boston and Washington, DC). Members search and book units online, pay month-to-month with all-inclusive pricing and no hidden fees, and open facility doors with a digital key issued through the Stuf Member Dashboard. Stuf publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract; the one machine-readable surface it does serve is a substantial, actively maintained llms.txt at https://www.stufstorage.com/llms.txt, alongside an AI-crawler-permissive robots.txt.

providers.name: SunPower
providers.description: SunPower is a residential solar energy company (Nasdaq: SPWR) that designs, installs, and finances solar systems and battery storage for homeowners. The original SunPower Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in August 2024; its assets were acquired by Complete Solaria in September 2024, which rebranded as SunPower Inc. in April 2025. SunPower maintains the GitHub org github.com/SunPower, hosting open-source solar modeling tools including pvfactors (view-factor model for bifacial PV modeling), PVMismatch (mismatch loss calculations), and SolarUtils. These Python libraries are used by solar energy professionals and researchers for photovoltaic system modeling and simulation.

providers.name: The Naked Market
providers.description: The Naked Market is a San Francisco-based consumer packaged goods (CPG) company and brand incubator founded in 2019 by Harrison Fugman, Alex Kost, and Tim Marbach. It uses a "fast fail" end-to-end infrastructure to take a food or beverage product from idea to market in roughly three months, launching and acquiring socially conscious direct-to-consumer brands across snacks, drinks, and better-for-you categories. Its portfolio has included Project Breakfast, Flock crispy chicken chips, Avocrazy avocado puffs, Beach House Bowls, Rob's Backstage Popcorn, and the low-alcohol aperitif brand Haus. The company raised $27.5 million in Series A funding in 2021 and is backed by HV Capital. It operates as a consumer brand holding company and does not publish a traditional developer API program, but its Shopify-hosted storefront exposes an agent-commerce surface: llms.txt agent instructions, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, OpenID Connect discovery, and a live MCP endpoint for catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout.

providers.name: Think Parametric
providers.description: Think Parametric is an online learning platform for architecture, engineering, and design professionals, offering expert-led courses and professional certifications in computational and parametric design tools including Rhino, Grasshopper, Revit, Dynamo, SketchUp, and V-Ray. Membership plans give individuals and organizations access to a library of 60+ courses taught by practitioners from leading firms such as SOM, BIG, Gensler, AECOM, and Arup, alongside community forums, downloadable assets, and progress tracking. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: ThinkUp
providers.description: ThinkUp was a social media analytics application, co-founded by Gina Trapani and Anil Dash, that gave individuals insights into their own activity across Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, and other social networks. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, it ran as both a hosted subscription service and an open-source project (ThinkUpLLC/ThinkUp on GitHub, 3.2k+ stars) before its hosted service was shut down in 2016. The thinkup.com domain is no longer operated by the company (it now resolves to an unrelated coupon-code site), and no public developer API surface is available for enrichment.

providers.name: ThredUp
providers.description: ThredUp (NASDAQ: TDUP) is one of the world's largest online resale and consignment platforms for secondhand women's and kids' clothing, shoes, and accessories. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Oakland, CA, it lets consumers buy and sell pre-owned fashion via mailed Clean Out Kits, and powers branded recommerce for 60+ retailers through its Resale-as-a-Service (RaaS) platform. ThredUp does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI; RaaS integrations are arranged through its partner sales team, so this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web, engineering, and policy surface rather than a documented API program.

providers.name: VCNC
providers.description: VCNC is a South Korean mobile technology company behind Between, a private messaging and photo-sharing app for couples, and TADA, a ride-hailing and mobility service operating in Korea. A 500 Global portfolio company, VCNC maintains an open source presence on GitHub, including Haeinsa, a multi-row transaction library for HBase published on Maven Central. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API client SDKs.

providers.name: Verve Motion
providers.description: Verve Motion is a wearable robotics company spun out of the Harvard Biodesign Lab that builds SafeLift, a soft powered exosuit for industrial workers who lift repetitively. Inertial sensors woven into the suit detect lifting motion and trigger assistive force that the company says takes up to 40% of the strain off a worker's back, while Verve Logic — its cloud platform — collects the resulting movement data and reports ergonomic risk, unsafe-posture trends and exosuit utilization to safety managers. SafeLift is sold as a subscription bundling the exosuit, the Verve Logic data portal and Verve Care support, and is distributed in part through partners such as HexArmor. Verve Motion publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the Verve Logic portal at logic.vervemotion.com is a customer-only single-page application that disallows crawling in robots.txt.

providers.name: Virgin Australia
providers.description: Virgin Australia (IATA code VA, ASX:VGN) is Australia's second-largest airline group, founded in 2000 and headquartered in Brisbane, operating a domestic and short-haul international network alongside charter and cargo services with more than 8,000 team members and the 13-million-member Velocity Frequent Flyer loyalty program. It sits on the airline side of a concentrated Australian duopoly with Qantas, and reaches travel agents and travel management companies almost entirely through GDS intermediation — Amadeus, Sabre and Travelport/Galileo — rather than through any direct machine interface of its own. Virgin Australia selected Sabre as its preferred NDC IT technology provider in October 2023 and renewed a multi-year Amadeus distribution agreement covering EDIFACT today and NDC in future, but as of July 2026 no Virgin Australia NDC endpoint, developer portal or API documentation is published anywhere on virginaustralia.com. Its API posture is honestly stated as none-published: developer.virginaustralia.com, developers., api., apis. and docs. subdomains do not resolve; /developers, /api, /api-docs, /openapi.json and /swagger.json all return 404; and the only partner surface is the Agency Hub, whose Travel Agent Main Agreement requires current IATA or ATIS accreditation, GDS access for BSP sales, and Virgin Australia's absolute discretion to approve an account. The one genuinely public programmatic-adjacent surface is the Virgin Australia app in ChatGPT, launched 10 June 2026 for flight and Velocity Reward Seat search only — it cannot book, amend, cancel or take payment, and its underlying interface is not documented.

providers.name: Viva Translate
providers.description: Viva Translate is an AI-powered real-time translation platform that acts as a personal meeting analyst, delivering live translation, transcription, automatic summaries, and action items across Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Zoom. Reported usage spans 1M+ minutes translated, 20+ countries, and 1.8k+ companies. The company ships a consumer/B2B product (no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time) and has open-sourced its browser-based translation tooling as a Chrome extension that consumes third-party DeepL, Gladia, and OpenAI APIs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of general-catalyst and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Viz.ai
providers.description: Viz.ai is a healthcare AI company that builds an intelligent care coordination platform. Its FDA-cleared, AI-powered software analyzes medical imaging (CT, CTA, MRI, echocardiography) to detect suspected disease — stroke (large vessel occlusion, ICH), aneurysm, pulmonary embolism, and cardiovascular conditions — and automatically alerts and connects the multidisciplinary care team in real time to accelerate diagnosis and treatment. Backed by CRV, GV, Insight Partners, Scale Venture Partners, Seedcamp, Susa Ventures, and Threshold Ventures. Viz.ai exposes no public developer API; integration is delivered through clinical/enterprise deployment, and its governance-relevant public surface is a Drata-hosted Trust Center documenting a broad security and compliance program (SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and an extensive ISO family including ISO 42001 for AI management).

providers.name: VoidZero
providers.description: VoidZero is the JavaScript tooling company building a unified, high-performance open-source toolchain for web development: the build tool Vite, the test runner Vitest, the Rust-based bundler Rolldown, and the Oxc language toolchain (including the oxlint linter and oxc-parser), all brought together under the commercial unified entry point Vite+. Founded by Evan You, creator of Vite and Vue.js, and backed by Accel and Peak XV, VoidZero joined Cloudflare in 2026. The company ships its capabilities as open-source npm packages and command-line tools rather than as a hosted REST API.

providers.name: Vouch
providers.description: Vouch is a San Francisco, California business insurance broker and risk advisor purpose-built for high-growth startups and the venture ecosystem. Founded in 2018 by Sam Hodges and Travis Hedge and backed by investors including Ribbit Capital, SVB Capital, Redpoint Ventures, Y Combinator, and MS&AD Ventures, Vouch offers a tailored portfolio of commercial coverages — Directors & Officers (D&O), Errors & Omissions (E&O / Tech E&O / Professional Services E&O), Cyber, Employment Practices Liability (EPL), General Liability, Business Property, Fiduciary, Crime, and contract-required coverages — sold to technology, healthcare and life sciences, financial services, and professional services companies. The business model is broker-of-record commissions and, since 2021, a Vouch-owned insurance carrier underwriting select lines. Vouch is best known in the developer community for its embedded insurance program, which lets ecosystem partners (Carta, StartupOS, and similar founder platforms) pre-fill applications, surface quotes, and bind coverage inline via Vouch's partner API. Public developer documentation, an OpenAPI specification, and a self-serve sandbox are not exposed; the partner API and Vouch Corporate documentation (hosted on GitBook) are gated to onboarded venture, technology, and service-provider partners contracted through hello@vouch.us.

providers.name: Wander
providers.description: Wander is a vertically integrated luxury hospitality company offering smart vacation homes with hotel-grade amenities, dedicated remote-work spaces, and 24/7 concierge service across North America. Founded by John Andrew Entwistle and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Wander powers owners and operators through WanderOS, its proprietary agentic AI operating system that automates dynamic pricing, operations, and guest support. The company raised a $50M Series B in 2025 co-led by QED Investors and Fifth Wall, with Redpoint Ventures, Uncork Capital, Starwood, and Breyer Capital participating, bringing total funding past $100M. Wander ships no public developer API, but publishes a deliberately agent-ready web surface: an llms.txt, an AI sitemap of 8,500+ markdown property pages with live 90-day pricing and availability refreshed daily, and Content-Signal AI-use permissions in robots.txt.

providers.name: Wenspiredata
providers.description: Wenspiredata is an enterprise cybersecurity vendor delivering all-in-one, zero-trust Privileged Remote Access Management (RPAM) for high-risk access. Its platform secures and governs remote privileged access for IT, OT, and third-party vendors, including air-gapped and industrial (OT) environments, and pairs with OsecT for OT-native intrusion detection and continuous visibility. Wenspiredata also offers security assessment services (external attack surface and internal vulnerability assessments) and helps organizations across manufacturing, telecom, finance, and healthcare meet regulatory compliance requirements. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment; the company markets a demo-led enterprise product and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Whirl
providers.description: Whirl AI is an enterprise IT platform that uses AI agents to help IT teams understand, enhance, and transform business processes and core systems. It automates research and impact analysis, generates business requirements, epics and user stories, and accelerates configuration and code changes across applications and integrations, compressing enterprise system changes from weeks and months into days and hours. Whirl runs on dedicated single-tenant AWS infrastructure per customer with immutable, versioned, auditable pipelines (no SSH access), FIDO2 device-based access, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. Founded by former Snowflake CIO Sunny Bedi and backed by ICONIQ, with advisors from Okta, Splunk, and VMware.

providers.name: Xpertsea
providers.description: Xpertsea is an aquaculture technology company (backed by QED Investors) that has rebranded its product as Kampi (bekampi.com) — an AI-powered shrimp-farming management app used by producers in Ecuador to monitor ponds, track growth and feed, and make production decisions in real time from mobile and web apps. xpertsea.com now 301-redirects to bekampi.com. The company publishes no public developer program or API surface: no docs/api/developer subdomains, no OpenAPI, and no API client SDKs (its @xpertsea npm scope holds two 2022-era UI-component forks). bekampi.com does publish an llms.txt, captured in this repository.

providers.name: Youtrip
providers.description: YouTrip (You Technologies Group, you.co) is a Singapore-based fintech that operates a multi-currency mobile travel wallet paired with a prepaid Mastercard, letting consumers hold and spend in over 150 currencies with no foreign-exchange fees and competitive in-app exchange rates. Launched in 2018, the company also runs YouBiz, a business account and corporate card product for SMEs, and offers international transfers to more than 40 countries. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, YouTrip processes billions of dollars in transactions annually across Singapore, Thailand, and Australia. As of this enrichment pass YouTrip exposes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or GitHub organization; consumer-facing account access is available only indirectly through open-banking aggregators.

providers.name: Alvee Health
providers.description: Alvee Health is an AI-powered care navigation platform for social determinants of health (SDOH) and whole-person care coordination. It surfaces unmet social and clinical needs from documentation, auto-codes Z-codes, automates patient outreach and benefits enrollment through an autonomous care navigator, generates compliant billing documentation, and tracks outcomes so providers can capture reimbursement for CHI, PIN, CCM, PCM, and G0136 care-coordination codes. The platform is HIPAA compliant and SMART on FHIR certified, integrating with EHRs to embed social drivers of health into clinical workflows. Alvee is a Techstars Iowa (2022) portfolio company.

providers.name: Botrista
providers.description: Botrista, Inc. is a San Francisco based beverage-automation company founded in 2017 that builds the DrinkBot robotic beverage dispenser and the CloudBar cloud platform behind it. The DrinkBot automates craft beverages — infused teas, flavored lemonades, iced coffees and mocktails — dispensing a drink in roughly twenty seconds from a touchscreen order, and every unit is internet connected so it pulls recipes, reports consumption, tracks ingredient levels and pushes maintenance alerts back to Botrista. CloudBar is the operator-facing web application used by restaurant, campus dining, convenience and theme-park operators to manage recipes, inventory replenishment and sales/menu performance analytics across a fleet of machines, alongside a separate Botrista Data Portal. Botrista sells beverage automation as a service rather than as a developer platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract, and POS integrations are handled case-by-case through its commercial team.

providers.name: Cargolux
providers.description: Cargolux Airlines International S.A. is Europe's largest all-cargo airline, headquartered at Luxembourg Findel Airport in Luxembourg and operating a global Boeing 747 freighter network under IATA designator CV and air waybill prefix 172 (with Cargolux Italia on prefix 356). In the logistics chain Cargolux is the main-leg air carrier: it sells capacity to freight forwarders and general sales agents rather than to shippers, hands cargo to terminal and ground handling operators such as its Luxcargo Handling subsidiary, and files customs and security data on behalf of the contracted forwarder. Its API posture is honestly a customer-contract one. Cargolux publishes no developer portal and no machine-readable contract of any kind — developer.cargolux.com, developers.cargolux.com and docs.cargolux.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/ all return 404 on www.cargolux.com. The only public self-service surfaces are HTML: a track-and-trace widget and a flight scheduler on the marketing site, plus a login-walled Customer Portal at my.cargolux.com. A real quote-and- booking API exists, but it is a bilateral, commercially negotiated forwarder interface — piloted with Kuehne+Nagel in 2021 and extended to DB Schenker — with no published reference, and it is complemented by indirect distribution through the cargo.one, CargoAi and WebCargo by Freightos marketplaces. Underneath, Cargolux runs IBS Software's iCargo SaaS cargo management system and holds a large minority stake in Luxembourg's CHAMP Cargosystems, whose developer.champ.aero portal is the developer surface Cargolux's ecosystem actually reads — CHAMP's, not Cargolux's. IATA e-AWB "Single Process" is documented; no IATA ONE Record or Cargo-XML publication was found.

providers.name: Ecovadis
providers.description: Ecovadis is a global leader in providing sustainability ratings and performance improvement tools for companies looking to assess and improve their environmental and social practices. Their platform helps organizations evaluate the sustainability performance of their suppliers, partners, and vendors, enabling them to make more informed decisions when it comes to selecting business partners.

providers.name: Enjamb Labs
providers.description: Enjamb Labs builds an AI-agent platform for pharmaceutical drug development. Its browser-based "integrated research environment" runs specialized agents across the full R&D lifecycle -- clinical evidence synthesis, trial design and statistical programming, and regulatory submission preparation -- while connecting to the systems pharma teams already use (Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, SAS) so no data migration is required. The workspace bundles Word/Excel/PowerPoint editors, Python and R compute environments, and 100+ scientific integrations, and emphasizes auditability, traceability, and human review, keeping each output attached to its sources, files, code, and decisions. Backed by Y Combinator and Founders, Inc., Enjamb reports early usage across major pharmaceutical companies including Johnson & Johnson, Merck, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, and Sanofi.

providers.name: Ferro Corporation
providers.description: Ferro Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Ferro Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Fetch Robotics
providers.description: Fetch Robotics is a provider of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for the manufacturing, distribution, and fulfillment industries, enabling customers to optimize warehouse and material-handling workflows through robotic automation. Its Fetch and Freight robots are programmed through a ROS (Robot Operating System) interface — standard ROS topics, services, and actions conforming to ROS Enhancement Proposals (REPs) — rather than an HTTP/REST API, and the first-party client, driver, and simulation libraries are published as open source in the fetchrobotics GitHub organization. Fetch Robotics was acquired by Zebra Technologies in August 2021 for approximately $290M; fetchrobotics.com now redirects to Zebra and the autonomous-mobile-robot product line is being wound down (2025-2026), though the open-source ROS packages remain available.

providers.name: Fibraweb, S.p.a.
providers.description: Fibraweb S.p.A. is an Italian telecommunications infrastructure operator, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Perugia (Umbria), that designs, builds and operates its own fiber-optic access network for businesses, wholesale operators and public administrations. The company delivers FTTH/FTTB ultra-broadband internet access, dedicated internet access circuits, and local and long-distance voice/telephony services across the Umbria, Marche, Toscana and Lazio regions, with a proprietary network of roughly 1,500 km of fiber reaching 150 industrial zones and the ability to connect over 30,000 companies. Fibraweb is a Battery Ventures portfolio company (investors also include Equiter and GTD Grupo Teleductos) and holds ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27017 certifications. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Foundation Building Materials
providers.description: Foundation Building Materials (FBM) is a leading North American distributor of interior building products — drywall, steel framing, acoustic ceilings, insulation, and complementary construction supplies — serving commercial and residential contractors across the United States and Canada. Headquartered in Santa Ana, California, FBM operates a national branch network and a unified customer ordering platform at myfbm.com (consolidating the legacy fbmsales.com, MyRIS, and MyFBM portals) along with iOS/Android mobile apps for contractors. In April 2025, FBM acquired KCG/Rew Materials, adding 800 employees and 45 distribution branches across 23 states. In August 2025, Lowe's announced an agreement to acquire FBM. Brand families operating under FBM include FBM, RIS, Pacific Source, and Unified Door. FBM does not currently expose any public developer APIs, OpenAPI documentation, partner integration program, SDK, or GitHub organization — its digital surface is limited to buyer-facing e-commerce (search, ordering, order tracking, quick-order PDF/photo ingestion via "Quick Order Entry") rather than a developer/integration product.

providers.name: FTI Consulting
providers.description: FTI Consulting is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The FTI Consulting API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: G2 Track
providers.description: G2 Track (formerly Cleanshelf) was a SaaS management platform providing SaaS spend monitoring, contract tracking, and usage insights. The product has since been acquired and is now offered as BetterCloud Spend Optimization.

providers.name: Gammastack
providers.description: GammaStack is a sports betting and iGaming software provider that integrates third-party APIs (betting odds, fixtures, payments, KYC) into customer-facing sportsbook platforms. GammaStack does not publish its own public API; this repository tracks the company and the categories of APIs it integrates.

providers.name: Gen.G
providers.description: Gen.G is a global esports organization founded in 2017 (originally KSV eSports) that connects the United States and Asia, operating from Los Angeles, Seoul, and Shanghai. It fields professional teams across League of Legends, Valorant, PUBG, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, Fortnite, Brawl Stars, Honor of Kings, Mobile Legends, NBA 2K, Overwatch, Rainbow Six Siege, and EA FC, and runs a youth esports academy program alongside merchandise and fan-engagement businesses. Backed by Canaan Partners among other investors, Gen.G was valued at roughly $250 million as of 2022. It is a consumer esports brand and merchandise operator with a Shopify-based storefront; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: General Fusion
providers.description: General Fusion is a Canadian fusion energy company founded in 2002 by physicist Dr. Michel Laberge and headquartered in Richmond, British Columbia, in the Vancouver area. It is developing Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF), an approach that combines plasma formation, mechanical compression by a liquid metal liner, and practical heat capture for electricity generation. The company operates LM26, which it describes as the world's largest and most powerful operational fusion plasma injector, and reports 24 plasma prototypes, more than 200,000 plasma experiments, 35+ peer-reviewed papers, and roughly 210 issued and pending patents. In July 2026 General Fusion completed a business combination with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III and became the first publicly listed fusion energy company, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker GFUZ. It is an energy hardware and research company rather than a software or API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts. Its only machine-readable public surfaces are a Yoast-generated llms.txt and the WordPress REST discovery index behind its marketing site.

providers.name: Gridwiz
providers.description: Gridwiz Inc. is a South Korean clean-energy software and hardware company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Seoul. It operates one of Korea's largest demand response (DR) aggregation portfolios, gathering electricity that industrial and commercial customers curtail and selling it into the national power market, and it pairs that with energy storage (ESS), renewable energy / RE100 and PPA advisory, and an e-mobility line covering EV charging controllers, CCS communication modems (EVCC/SECC), bidirectional V2G chargers and the Skyblue consumer charging service. Its e-mobility products are built to the international EV charging standards DIN SPEC 70121, ISO 15118 (including 15118-20 AC/DC) and OCPP, and its demand response management system is described as OpenADR-based. Gridwiz sells energy services and certified hardware to utilities, EVSE suppliers and enterprises; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Health Scholars
providers.description: Health Scholars — which rebranded to UpSkillAI in 2025 and now trades at upskillai.com — builds AI-powered extended reality (XR/VR) simulation training for mission-critical, hands-on work in healthcare, emergency medical services, stroke assessment and defense. The platform pairs voice-driven VR simulations with simulation management and readiness reporting, letting hospital systems, first responders and government programs run standardized protocol training on headsets without instructors or extra equipment. Customers reach it through a hosted web console at app.upskillai.com. The company publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, webhook catalog or public pricing. The production backend behind its own application (api.upskillai.com, with the legacy AWS API Gateway host api.healthscholars.com) is private and rejects unauthenticated requests.

providers.name: Hiphen Plant
providers.description: Hiphen Plant provides advanced image analytics solutions for agricultural research. As plant scientists, they build tools that revolutionize how plants can be assessed, bringing the power of image analytics to agricultural research programs for decision-making on genetics, chemistry, and practices.

providers.name: Husk Power Systems
providers.description: Husk Power Systems is an energy technology company, founded in 2008 and headquartered in Fort Collins, Colorado with operating hubs in Patna, Mumbai and Pune (India) and Abuja (Nigeria), that builds, owns and operates AI-enabled distributed renewable energy systems — community solar minigrids, commercial and industrial solar, and residential rooftop — for unserved and underserved communities, businesses and households across Africa and Asia. Husk operates one of the largest minigrid fleets in the world and pairs it with pay-as-you-go smart metering, a customer mobile app (HUSKify) and an internal operations platform (Husk Neuron). Its software is delivered as end-user and operator products; Husk publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Ionis Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Ionis Pharmaceuticals is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Ionis Pharmaceuticals API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Juxta
providers.description: Juxta is a San Francisco positioning-technology company building a hardware-free Universal Positioning System (UPS) that delivers real-time indoor and outdoor tracking for people, assets, and robots with sub-meter accuracy indoors and roughly 3-meter accuracy outdoors. Rather than relying on satellites, beacons, or cameras, Juxta uses the inertial (IMU) sensors already present in mobile devices, robots, and machinery combined with machine-learning "synthetic fingerprinting" to map and track subjects in GPS-denied environments such as warehouses, hospitals, underground facilities, and battlefields. Its drag-and-drop deployment ingests a floorplan, satellite image, or CAD file and goes live in hours, priced by mapped area and assets tracked. Juxta serves defense, logistics and robotics, and healthcare, and is backed by Y Combinator and other early-stage investors. Access today is through a partner portal and booked demo; no public developer API is documented.

providers.name: Kaavio
providers.description: Kaavio is an AI-powered product content platform for B2B distributors and manufacturers. It sources product data from supplier submissions, PDFs, spec sheets, internal systems (PIM, DAM, ERP) and the web, validates it with conflict detection and confidence scoring, generates market-ready content (structured attributes, SEO descriptions, FAQs, comparisons, substitutes), and deploys it to destination systems such as PIMs, e-commerce platforms, and channels. The platform handles catalogs ranging from 20,000 to more than a million SKUs and claims a 90% reduction in the time and effort to get market-ready SKU content online. Founded by Derek Gregg and Sam Bobb, based in San Francisco, and backed by Baukunst, Techstars, and Looking Glass Capital ($2.9M pre-seed).

providers.name: Kaman Corporation
providers.description: Kaman Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Kaman Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: KCL
providers.description: KCL (Kusion Configuration Language) is a constraint-based record and functional programming language designed for configuration and policy scenarios. It provides features like type safety, automation, and validation for cloud-native configurations.

providers.name: Mechanical Orchard
providers.description: Mechanical Orchard is an enterprise software company, founded by Pivotal veterans, that modernizes mission-critical legacy and mainframe systems. Its flagship platform, Imogen, uses AI to observe how legacy applications actually behave, then incrementally rewrites them into modern, cloud-ready code while continuously verifying that behavior is preserved so nothing breaks during migration. The company pairs the Imogen platform with professional services and a free proof of concept, integrates with AWS Transform and Google Cloud, and serves both commercial enterprises and government agencies looking to retire risky COBOL and mainframe estates. It is backed by Bloomberg Beta, Emergence Capital, and GV.

providers.name: Meela
providers.description: Meela is an AI voice companion and voice-based ride service built for older adults, backed by Bain Capital Ventures. Members connect through scheduled phone calls with no app, device, or subscription required — Meela calls on a chosen schedule, remembers names, preferences, and past conversations, and shares select privacy-conscious insights with caregivers. A "Meela for Business" offering brings the same companionship to senior living facilities with care-team dashboards, mood/engagement alerts, and EHR documentation, and the company advertises HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance. Meela publishes only a consumer marketing site and a member sign-in portal; it exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Modern Animal
providers.description: Modern Animal is a membership-based veterinary healthcare company operating physical primary and urgent care clinics across major U.S. metropolitan regions, combining in-clinic visits with 24/7 virtual veterinary consultations, pharmacy and prescription management, dental care, surgery, and preventive care. It runs a subscription membership model (All Access, Essential, and Pay As You Go tiers) with transparent, upfront pricing and a companion mobile app for booking and virtual care. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and susa-ventures. Modern Animal is a consumer veterinary brand and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: MODIFI
providers.description: Welcome to the MODIFI partnership API developer hub. You'll find comprehensive guides and documentation to help you start working with the partnership API as quickly as possible, as well as support if you get stuck.

providers.name: Modular Robotics
providers.description: Modular Robotics is a Boulder, Colorado hardware and educational-robotics company best known for Cubelets, magnetic modular robot construction blocks organized into SENSE, THINK, and ACT categories, and the MOSS building system. It also produces the Dexter Industries STEM product line, including the GoPiGo Raspberry Pi robot, BrickPi (LEGO Mindstorms plus Raspberry Pi), GrovePi, and the micro:bit GiggleBot.
