Started at Harvard Innovation Labs in 2021, Stellar Sleep also offers clinician and employer programs, with clinical-system integrations arranged by its team. It is a consumer digital-health product with no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface.

providers.name: Storyboard
providers.description: Storyboard is a fleet-operations AI platform that gives trucking and logistics companies voice-first, hands-free AI workers for their drivers. The system automates dispatch updates, driver coaching, safety alerts, and compliance monitoring (including hours-of-service and idling) so back-office teams field fewer phone calls and drivers stay hands-free on the road. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Santa Monica, California, Storyboard began as an enterprise podcast and internal-audio communication platform (a $4.5M seed round led by CRV in 2020) before pivoting to AI-powered fleet operations. It is distributed through in-cab telematics marketplaces such as Platform Science and ISAAC Instruments. Storyboard exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; access is via its web and mobile apps at app.storyboard.com. This profile was surfaced as a CRV portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Synyi
providers.description: Synyi (森亿智能 / Shanghai Synyi Medical Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Shanghai-based medical artificial-intelligence company founded in April 2016 that builds AI and big-data systems for hospitals. Its platform uses medical natural-language processing, large-scale medical knowledge graphs and multi-agent LLM applications to normalize and mine the unstructured clinical records held in Chinese hospital information systems, and sells that capability as deployed hospital software spanning clinical decision support, medical-record quality control, hospital operations management, an AI-driven clinic model and clinical research tooling. IDC's "China Healthcare Big Data Solution Market Share, 2023" ranked Synyi first in its market. Synyi publishes no public API, no developer portal and no machine-readable contract; its products are enterprise systems deployed inside customer hospitals and reached through a direct sales motion.

providers.name: Tagged
providers.description: Tagged is a social discovery and dating platform founded in 2004 and based in San Francisco, where members browse profiles of people nearby or worldwide, chat, play social games, exchange tags and virtual gifts, and make new connections. Originally a standalone social network backed by early investors including Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC), Tagged was acquired by MeetMe in 2017 for roughly 60 million dollars and today operates as a consumer brand within The Meet Group (part of the ParshipMeet Group) alongside apps such as MeetMe, Skout, and LOVOO. The current tagged.com is a consumer-facing web and mobile social-dating experience with no public developer program or API; a legacy REST-style API (tagged.com/api.php) that once powered third-party integrations has been retired. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Targetspot
providers.description: Targetspot is a global digital-audio advertising (AdTech) company founded in 2007 and headquartered in New York, connecting brands with audiences across podcasts, online radio, streaming, in-video audio, mobile gaming, and in-home/out-of-home audio. Its Passport product is a self-serve ad-serving platform for publishers and advertisers, with granular reporting data made available via a partner API, and Targetplay extends audio advertising into gaming and in-app inventory. Targetspot is now part of the Azerion platform. This profile originated as a Union Square Ventures portfolio lead and has been enriched from public web probes.

providers.name: Tellus
providers.description: Tellus is a consumer fintech company whose mobile app pairs high-yield savings tools with real-estate-backed lending and property management. Members earn competitive rates on cash held in Tellus accounts, funded by the company's portfolio of residential real-estate loans, with deposits held at FDIC-insured partner banks. The app also offers a mobile wallet, a business wallet, and property-management tooling for landlords and property owners. Tellus is a private, venture-backed startup (an a16z portfolio company); it operates as a direct-to-consumer mobile product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: The Campbell's Company
providers.description: The Campbell's Company (formerly Campbell Soup Company) is an American manufacturer and marketer of branded convenience food products including soups, simple meals, beverages, and snacks. Major brands include Campbell's, Rao's, V8, Pace, Pepperidge Farm, Snyder's of Hanover, Lance, Cape Cod, Kettle Brand, Goldfish, and Prego. The company operates consumer-facing digital properties, an investor relations portal, a careers platform, and supplier resources, but does not publish general-purpose public APIs.

providers.name: Transfercar
providers.description: Transfercar is a free vehicle relocation marketplace that connects rental car and motorhome companies who need vehicles moved between their depots with travelers willing to drive those vehicles one-way. Rental operators list relocation deals for cars and campervans that need to be repositioned, and drivers book them to travel between cities at little or no rental cost, often with extras such as free days, fuel allowances, or ferry contributions. The service operates across New Zealand, Australia, and the United States as a consumer-facing web booking platform rather than a developer API provider. Transfercar was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; this profile has been enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: TREBEL Music
providers.description: TREBEL Music (operated by M&M Media, Inc.) is an advertising-sponsored, legally licensed music download and streaming service that lets people download and listen to music offline at no cost. Founded in 2014 by Gary Mekikian, Corey Jones and Luis Soto Durazo and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut with offices in Mexico City, Jakarta, Bogota, Los Angeles and Miami, TREBEL licenses catalog from Universal Music Group, Sony Music Entertainment, Warner Music Group and independent labels, and monetizes through digital advertising, branded experiences, virtual goods and a TREBEL Max tier rather than a conventional paid subscription. TREBEL is a consumer mobile product distributed through the Apple App Store, Google Play and Huawei AppGallery; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: TT Labs
providers.description: TT Labs is the company behind VideoPixie, a freelance marketplace that connects clients with professional video creators — videographers, video editors, directors, animators, and motion designers — available for hire. Clients post a project brief in about five minutes and receive competitive bids from vetted creators, then choose a creator based on portfolio and price. VideoPixie serves crowdfunding and Kickstarter videos, product and explainer videos, game trailers, wedding videography, screencasts, and full production campaigns, with example budgets ranging from a few hundred to tens of thousands of dollars. Backed by 500 Global, VideoPixie is a customer-facing marketplace web application (AngularJS) and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Turing Labs
providers.description: Turing Labs (turingsaas.com) is a product-led growth platform for consumer packaged goods companies. Its "Growth OS" helps CPG and consumer-product teams pressure-test which product bets will win before spending, perfect formulations, and fund launches from recovered margin, consolidating product development, formulation R&D, and go-to-market decisioning into a single engine rather than a stack of disconnected tools. The company is backed by Insight Partners and Menlo Ventures. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface was found during enrichment; the product is delivered through a login-gated web application at app.turingsaas.com.

providers.name: Unlearn
providers.description: Unlearn is a San Francisco AI company that builds digital twin generators for clinical trials — machine learning models trained on patient-level historical data that forecast an individual participant's clinical outcomes under control or standard of care. Sponsors use these AI-generated digital twins to plan trials, monitor clinical data, and run smaller, more powerful studies; the approach is qualified by the EMA and aligned with current FDA guidance. Unlearn is backed by 8VC and DCVC and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Wintrust Financial
providers.description: Wintrust Financial Corporation is a Rosemont, Illinois-based financial holding company operating a network of chartered community banks (Wintrust Bank, N.A. and its affiliates) primarily across Illinois, Wisconsin, Indiana and Florida, plus specialty lending, wealth management and mortgage businesses. Wintrust does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; its programmatic surface is delivered through commercial treasury management. Wintrust describes "API banking" that connects businesses directly to its secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) for account balance and activity reporting, payment files (Positive Pay, ACH, wires, EDI, lockbox) and data-format translation (NACHA, EDI 820, BAI2). Consumer and small-business account data is reachable to third parties through open-banking aggregators — Plaid is the confirmed aggregator supporting Wintrust / iBusinessBanking access.

providers.name: Zorus
providers.description: Zorus is a cybersecurity company that provides DNS web protection and filtering built for managed service providers (MSPs), managed security service providers (MSSPs), and IT teams. Its Archon agent delivers DNS filtering without requiring per-router DNS changes, layered with CyberSight behavioral user analytics, geo-IP and network filtering, zero-trust device isolation, and SaaS inventory and usage visibility. Zorus is delivered as a multi-tenant SaaS platform administered through a partner portal (portal.zorustech.com), positioned as an alternative to Cisco Umbrella, WebRoot DNS, and WebTitan. Zorus does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation; its API surface (api.zorustech.com) sits behind the authenticated product portal. This profile captures the company's public web properties and probed security posture.

providers.name: 3T Biosciences
providers.description: 3T Biosciences is a clinical-stage immunotherapy company based in South San Francisco, developing next-generation T-cell receptor (TCR) therapeutics for solid tumors and other immune-mediated diseases. Founded in 2017 on research from K. Christopher Garcia's lab at Stanford University, the company operates its proprietary 3T-TRACE (T-Cell Receptor Antigen and Cross-reactivity Evaluation) platform, which combines high-diversity yeast-display target libraries with active machine-learning to screen billions of protein fragments and identify novel shared TCR targets and specificities. 3T has raised a $40M Series A from Westlake Village BioPartners and Lightspeed Venture Partners and has struck cancer-immunotherapy collaborations with Boehringer Ingelheim worth up to $268M in milestones. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and enriched into the API Evangelist network; 3T publishes no public developer API, SDK, or specification surface.

providers.name: 8th Wall
providers.description: 8th Wall is a web-based augmented reality (WebAR) platform originally founded in 2016 and acquired by Niantic in March 2022. Following Niantic's 2025 sale of its gaming division to Scopely and the spin-off of Niantic Spatial, Inc. as an independent geospatial AI and XR company, 8th Wall's hosted cloud editor, login, and Niantic Studio services were retired on February 28, 2026 and the platform transitioned to a free, open-source distribution model. Existing published 8th Wall experiences continue to run through February 28, 2027. The 8th Wall stack centers on the XR Engine — a SLAM-based WebAR runtime providing World Tracking, Image Targets, Face Effects, Sky Segmentation, and World Effects — exposed to developers as a TypeScript/JavaScript SDK that integrates with A-Frame, three.js, PlayCanvas, and Babylon.js. The Distributed Engine Binary (released January 2026) ships SLAM under a binary-only license for commercial and noncommercial use, while the surrounding framework, utilities, and example projects are MIT-licensed on the 8thwall GitHub organization. 8th Wall Studio (formerly Niantic Studio) is a real-time visual editor and game engine for authoring 3D and XR experiences that can be deployed to any web host. 8th Wall does not publish a public REST or HTTP API; the developer surface is a client-side JavaScript SDK plus command-line and utility tooling distributed through GitHub.

providers.name: Ai Fabrik
providers.description: AI Fabrik is an infrastructure company building an edge inference delivery network for high-performance AI tokens. Incubated within Gruve and led by founder Tarun Raisoni alongside Swati Deshpande and Tanuj Mohan, the company has deconstructed the traditional data center model and rebuilt every layer for real-time AI, delivering distributed inference close to users and cloud providers with sub-20ms latency, cost efficiency, and built-in compliance. AI Fabrik is deploying five initial production sites with 6,000+ B300 GPUs launching in 2026, backed by Mayfield, Xora (Temasek), Acclimate Ventures, and Cisco Investments.

providers.name: AiSensum
providers.description: AiSensum (AISensum) builds agentic AI "teammates" that work alongside front-line staff to drive revenue, improve quality, and reduce labour while keeping the human in the lead. Operating since 2017 with a presence across Southeast Asia, it deploys purpose-built AI teammates for enterprise front-line operations in retail, F&B, hospitality and entertainment, each specialising in one measurable outcome: Daniel (revenue teammate, personalised counter offers/upsell), Sasha (time and cost teammate, bulk product-photo editing and approval), and Nicole (progress teammate, conversation scoring and cashier coaching against brand SOPs). Deployments are scoped through a half-day IFA (Intelligent Front-line Automation) Workshop. AiSensum publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal; it is a portfolio company of 500 Global tracked in the API Evangelist network. This profile was enriched from the company's public web presence and an on-site llms.txt.

providers.name: Aramya
providers.description: Aramya is a direct-to-consumer (D2C) women's ethnic wear brand from India, operated by DSLR Technologies Pvt. Ltd. and based in Jaipur, Rajasthan. Founded by Ankush Goyal, Aramya sells premium cotton kurtas, kurta sets, bottoms, dresses, co-ord sets, and dupattas with a strong focus on inclusive sizing (XS to 10XL) and affordable, comfortable everyday, office, and occasion wear. The brand runs on a Shopify-based storefront at aramya.in with weekly launches, cash on delivery, and free returns, and has raised multiple rounds (seed, pre-Series A, and an ~INR 80 Cr Series A) co-led by Accel India and Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India). Aramya is a consumer retail brand and does not publish a public developer API; it does publish an llms.txt describing its shopping surface for AI assistants.

providers.name: Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company
providers.description: Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company (AIUC) is a San Francisco-based AI agent standards and insurance company that builds confidence infrastructure for enterprises adopting AI agents. It pairs AIUC-1 — described as the world's first AI agent standard, spanning data & privacy, security, safety, reliability, accountability, and societal risk — with insurance products that protect organizations against AI agent failures. Developed with input from over 100 Fortune 500 CISOs and mapped to frameworks including ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, and MITRE ATLAS, AIUC certifies AI agents against defined controls through accredited auditors. The company is backed by Emergence Capital and does not currently publish a public API or developer surface.

providers.name: ARX Robotics
providers.description: ARX Robotics is a European defense technology company building autonomous unmanned ground systems and the software that runs them. Its flagship Mithra OS is an AI-driven autonomy platform that turns legacy and modern military vehicles into software-defined, autonomous units, while its Gereon RCS line delivers scalable robotic ground vehicles for reconnaissance, firepower, clearance, surveillance, cargo, and casualty evacuation across defense and commercial missions. Headquartered in Munich with offices in Berlin, the UK, and Ukraine, ARX operates one of Europe's largest autonomous defense systems production facilities and has delivered unmanned ground systems to Ukraine. The company is venture-backed (a €31M Series A extended by €11M, with HV Capital among its investors) and partners with RENK, DEUTZ, Helsing, and Quantum Systems to strengthen Europe's technological resilience and defense sovereignty. ARX publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web presence and an llms.txt it publishes for AI agents.

providers.name: Asaak
providers.description: Asaak is an East African fintech company, headquartered in Kampala, Uganda, that provides asset financing and working capital to small businesses and individual entrepreneurs who are underserved by traditional banks. Its core products are loans for boda boda motorcycles, fuel, and smartphones, delivered through a mobile-first application with a simple four-step flow of apply, qualify, receive financing, and repay to build credit. Asaak operates branches across Uganda (Kampala, Jinja, Mukono, Matugga, Nabbingo, Fort Portal, Gulu, and Soroti) and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It runs a backend admin platform at api.asaak.net and a Wix-hosted marketing site that exposes a live Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint for agentic access to public site content. Asaak does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Associated Bank
providers.description: Associated Bank, N.A. is the primary banking subsidiary of Associated Banc-Corp (NYSE ASB), a nationally chartered commercial bank and the largest bank holding company headquartered in Wisconsin, based in Green Bay. With roughly $50 billion in total assets following the April 2026 acquisition of American National Corporation, Associated operates a full-service Midwest banking franchise of more than 200 locations across Wisconsin, Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri and Nebraska, offering consumer, business, commercial and wealth-management services. Associated does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. Its digital banking runs on a core-provider stack (Jack Henry), and consumer-permissioned data access is delivered through third-party aggregators (Plaid, Tink/TrueLayer) rather than a direct first-party API. Its commercial treasury customers use the login-gated Associated Connect platform. No FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented as of this review.

providers.name: Atalanta
providers.description: Atalanta is a mathematical AI company building provably correct decision-making for the world's most important missions. Its flagship platform, Argo, is described as the first software understanding platform - it uses mathematical proof and formal verification to establish safety, security, and performance guarantees for software-defined and autonomous systems at operational speed, moving beyond the limits of traditional testing. Argo identifies failure modes before deployment and verifies compliance with critical constraints across energy (nuclear and grid control systems), space (satellite and communications networks), and defense (complex military systems and data isolation). Atalanta was founded by Anjana Rajan and Jonathan Ring, is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and is backed by Felicis and In-Q-Tel.

providers.name: Athos
providers.description: Athos is a sports performance technology company founded in 2012 and based in Redwood City, California, that builds athletic apparel with embedded surface electromyography (EMG) sensors. Its garments and snap-on Athos Core module capture muscle activity, effort, and motion data, streaming it over Bluetooth to a mobile app and coaching dashboard so athletes, trainers, and sports scientists can measure muscular exertion, fatigue, and return-to-play readiness in real time. Athos is a consumer and team hardware brand with no publicly documented developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Avenews
providers.description: Avenews (Avenews-GT) is a Nairobi-based agri-fintech and Digital Credit Provider licensed by the Central Bank of Kenya that delivers transaction-backed, recurring working-capital financing to agricultural SMEs across Kenya. Rather than requiring traditional collateral, Avenews underwrites using digital trade data, M-Pesa and bank statements, and supply-chain history. Its products include the Agri Credit Line (recurring capital to restock inputs), Agri Supplier Financing (invoice financing), Agri Buyer Financing (deferred-payment terms), and Stockist Financing (direct distributor payments). The public site is built on Wix and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint plus an llms.txt file for agentic AI access, though Avenews does not publish a bespoke developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars-connected portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Axiom Space
providers.description: Axiom Space, Inc. is a privately funded American space infrastructure developer headquartered in Houston, Texas, founded in 2016 by Kam Ghaffarian and former NASA International Space Station Program Manager Michael Suffredini. The company is building Axiom Station, the world's first commercial space station and planned successor to the ISS, and has flown private astronaut missions to the ISS (Ax-1 through Ax-4). Axiom Space also develops the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) spacesuit for NASA's return to the lunar surface, and sells human spaceflight, microgravity research, in-space manufacturing, and Orbital Data Center services (in-orbit cloud compute, with the ODC T1 node built alongside Kepler Communications and Skyloom Global). As of this enrichment pass Axiom Space publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract — every offering is transacted through direct enterprise, agency, and government engagement, and its only public code presence is a two-repository GitHub organization holding forks of NASA simulation software (Trick and GUNNS).

providers.name: Banyansoftware
providers.description: Banyan Software is a global acquirer and permanent operator of vertical market software (VMS) businesses, headquartered in Toronto, Canada. Built as an "evergreen" alternative to private equity, Banyan buys profitable, growing enterprise software companies that hold dominant positions in niche markets (typically $2M-$30M in annual revenue) and holds them for the long term rather than reselling. It has acquired 100+ companies across sectors including healthcare IT, education, manufacturing, broadcast, public sector, and fintech, and supports them through a Growth Ops team spanning AI, talent, sales and marketing, payments, product, finance, cybersecurity, and legal. Banyan Software is a holding/operating company and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Bench IQ
providers.description: Bench IQ is a legal technology company building an AI-powered judicial intelligence platform that analyzes how individual judges reason and rule. Rather than limiting analysis to the roughly 3% of matters that produce written opinions, Bench IQ studies the reasoning behind all of a judge's rulings so litigators can anticipate decisions, craft stronger arguments, and shape case strategy. Founded by the team behind ROSS Intelligence — CEO Jimoh Ovbiagele and CTO Maxim Isakov — together with former Kirkland & Ellis restructuring partner Jeffrey Gettleman, the company says four of the top five AmLaw 100 firms rely on its analysis. It is backed by Battery Ventures, Inovia Capital, and Haystack, along with leading law firms including Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati, Fenwick & West, and Cooley.

providers.name: Berkshire Grey
providers.description: Berkshire Grey is a Bedford, Massachusetts-based AI and robotics company that builds integrated pick-and-place, parcel sortation, trailer-unloading, and shuttle-sortation systems for eCommerce fulfillment, retail replenishment, and parcel logistics operations. Its product portfolio is organized around four flagship robotic systems — Core robotic picking system, Dispatch parcel sorter, Scoop trailer unloader, and Stride shuttle sorter — supported by the BG Flex mobile robotic platform and a centralized operating environment that orchestrates fleets of industrial-grade mobile robots for induct, transport, sort, sequence, and fulfill workflows including buy-online-pickup-in-store, curbside, and store replenishment. The company holds 700+ awarded patents (300+ pending) and has deployed solutions with Global-100 retailers and logistics service providers including Walmart, Target, and FedEx, with FedEx expanding from small-parcel sortation into broader AI robotic package-handling capabilities. Berkshire Grey originally went public via SPAC merger with Revolution Acceleration Acquisition Corp in 2021, then entered into a definitive merger agreement with SoftBank Group in 2023 (approximately $375M / $1.40 per share) and is now operated as a private SoftBank portfolio company. Integration with warehouse-management systems is delivered through a proprietary RESTful API surfaced via professional services and a 24/7 remote monitoring and predictive-maintenance support model; the API, BG-OS platform, and any associated SDKs are not publicly documented, and Berkshire Grey does not operate a public developer portal, downloadable SDK, or open-source release for its robotic operating environment.

providers.name: Bounce
providers.description: Bounce operates the world's largest luggage storage network, connecting travelers with more than 32,000 vetted partner locations across 4,000+ cities worldwide where they can securely drop off bags, luggage, and packages by the hour or day and explore hands-free. Founded by Cody Candee in 2018, the company runs a two-sided marketplace: travelers book storage in advance or on the spot through the Bounce web and mobile apps, while local shops, hotels, and businesses earn revenue as storage partners. Bounce also offers luggage-delivery between hotels, airports, and city locations, a hotel solutions program, and an affiliate program. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, and Sapphire. This profile currently tracks the company's public web surface; Bounce publishes an llms.txt but no public developer API.

providers.name: Branch8
providers.description: Branch8 is a digital solutions and managed contracting company headquartered in Hong Kong with operations across Asia (Singapore, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines). Founded in 2015, it provides managed technical squads and blended onshore/offshore teams that deliver e-commerce implementation (Adobe Commerce, Shopify Plus, and marketplace operations on Shopee, Lazada, and Amazon), CRM and CDP strategy (Salesforce, HubSpot, Segment, mParticle, Braze, Dynamics 365), digital product and mobile engineering, AI and workflow automation (n8n, Make, Windmill), and data engineering (Snowflake, BigQuery, dbt, Fivetran). Branch8 serves mid-market to enterprise clients including Chow Tai Fook, Chow Sang Sang, Lacoste, Hong Kong International Airport, Hotai/Toyota, and HKBN. It is a services firm rather than an API producer and publishes no public developer API, but it does expose an agent-native llms.txt describing its services.

providers.name: Calastone
providers.description: Calastone operates the world's largest global funds network, connecting asset managers, distributors, custodians and platforms to automate and digitalize the investment funds marketplace. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in London, it provides order routing, settlements, share-class conversions, dividends, transfers, reporting, money market services and tokenized fund distribution. More than 4,500 clients across 58 countries and territories use the network, processing over £300 billion of investment value each month. API and messaging connectivity is delivered through client onboarding rather than a public self-service developer portal. Calastone is a wholly owned subsidiary of SS&C Technologies Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: SSNC).

providers.name: Calysta
providers.description: Calysta, Inc. is a cellular agriculture company founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, with operations in Memphis, Tennessee (NouriTech), Wilton/Teesside in the United Kingdom (Calysta UK Ltd.) and Singapore (Calysta Asia Pte Ltd.). It produces protein ingredients through a patented gas-fermentation platform in which a naturally-occurring microorganism converts carbon and energy into a non-GMO single-cell protein, using no arable land and no plant or animal inputs. Its product family includes FeedKind for aquaculture and livestock, FeedKind Pet, FeedKind Net Zero and Positive Protein for human food ingredients; FeedKind Aqua is sold globally through Calysseo, a 50/50 joint venture with Adisseo whose first production plant in China manufactures thousands of tonnes per year. Calysta sells physical protein ingredients to feed and food manufacturers — its fermentation platform is industrial process technology, not commercial software — and it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: CelLink
providers.description: CelLink (CelLink Technologies / CelLink Corporation) manufactures large-format, high-conductance flexible circuits that consolidate power, data, and sensing into thin, lightweight layers, replacing traditional wire harnesses and busbars. Its product lines are Battery Pack Interconnect, Flex Harness, and Data Center power delivery, serving automotive, aerospace, industrial, data center, and grid-storage electrification markets. Founded by CEO Kevin Coakley and VP Engineering Malcolm Brown, the company is headquartered in San Carlos, California, with sites in Georgetown, Texas; Wixom, Michigan; Hamburg, Germany; and Shanghai, China. CelLink circuits have been in electric-vehicle production since 2020. CelLink is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Certivity
providers.description: Certivity is a Munich-based RegTech company, founded in 2021, that operates an AI-native regulatory intelligence platform for regulated industries such as automotive, aerospace, and connected vehicles. Its product, Certivity Core, turns complex regulations, standards, and internal documents into structured, machine-readable, engineering-ready requirements with full traceability and real-time monitoring of legal changes across 50+ jurisdictions. The platform digitizes and structures regulatory content from publishers such as ISO, IEC, CEN, CENELEC, ASTM, UL, and SAE using a proprietary ingestion pipeline and a regulatory knowledge graph, and integrates directly into engineering workflows (including Jama Connect) via an official API. Backed by Earlybird, High-Tech Gruenderfonds, UVC Partners, and Almaz Capital, Certivity added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and enrichment lead.

providers.name: Checkerspot
providers.description: Checkerspot is an Alameda, California biotechnology company, founded in 2016 and incorporated as a Public Benefit Corporation, that designs and produces functional fats and oils through precision fermentation of microalgae. Its biology-driven molecule licensing platform pairs algal strain development, an advanced analytical platform, bioinformatics, high-throughput screening, fermentation scale-up and downstream oil refining, built around the proprietary microbe Prototheca moriformis, which the company reports reaches over 80% oil content by dry cell weight. The commercial molecule portfolio includes a high sn-2 palmitate algal oil that mimics the triglyceride structure of human milk fat for infant nutrition, an Omega-7 (palmitoleic acid) algal oil, a designer high-oleic tropical-fat alternative to palm oil, and Algolein tG C18/80 for cosmetic formulation; earlier work commercialized algae-derived urethane composites through the WNDR Alpine outdoor brand. Checkerspot works through ingredient and manufacturing partners including AAK, Huvepharma and La Fabrique Vegetale, and closed a USD 55 million Series C led by ArrowMark Partners with participation from Cox Enterprises. It is a business-to-business ingredient and molecule licensing company rather than a software vendor: it operates a WordPress marketing site, publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and has no GitHub organization.

providers.name: Context.ai *
providers.description: Context (context.ai) is a unified enterprise AI platform for building, deploying, and improving AI agents at scale. The product is organized into modular components: a Workspace for authoring agent workflows in plain English, an Engine with 800+ connectors and IdP-brokered identity, Unify as a knowledge/institutional-context repository, and Evals for rubric-based quality scoring. It is model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, or open weights) and offers hosted, VPC, on-prem, or air-gapped deployment. The company originated as a GV (Google Ventures) and Theory Ventures backed product-analytics-for-LLMs startup and now operates as an enterprise agent platform used by teams including Qualcomm, Stripe, and Palantir. This repo carries no public developer/API surface: the provider publishes no OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or developer documentation, so most machine-readable artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: Cosm
providers.description: Cosm is a Los Angeles-based immersive technology, media and entertainment company formed in 2020 from the merger of LiveLike VR (now Cosm Immersive) and C360, followed by the acquisition of planetarium pioneers Evans & Sutherland and Spitz. It operates three lines: Cosm Tech (the CX System LED dome, Digistar planetarium software, and end-to-end immersive display systems sold to planetariums, museums and attractions), Cosm Media (immersive content production and licensing through Cosm Studios) and Cosm Venues (the "Shared Reality" experiential venues in Los Angeles and Dallas, with Atlanta, Detroit and Cleveland following). Cosm sells and operates systems and venues rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification. The one API it markets — the Digistar scripting/automation interface, advertised as "the most fully featured API across the planetarium industry" — is documented only inside the customer support portal at partners.cosm.com, which requires a login.

providers.name: Curative
providers.description: Curative is a health insurance and healthcare services company founded in 2020 that reengineered the employer-based health plan around simplicity, engagement, and cost transparency. Its fully insured and level-funded plans give members a competitive monthly premium with zero copays, deductibles, or out-of-pocket costs, starting each member with a baseline visit that tailors a preventative care plan. Curative serves more than 1,200 employer clients and over 165,000 members, reached profitability, and achieved unicorn status ($1.275B valuation) following a $150M Series B round backed by DCVC. Curative operates as a HIPAA-regulated health plan; it has no public developer/API program, so this API Evangelist profile captures company identity, its member/provider web surface, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Dagangan
providers.description: Dagangan is an Indonesian tech-enabled wholesale e-commerce platform serving small and medium retailers (SMEs) in tier 3-4 cities and rural areas. Through a hub-and-spoke network of 50+ micro-warehouses across remote regions, it connects large suppliers to traditional local retailers, giving them affordable mobile access to daily necessities and groceries while reducing delivery costs and supply-chain friction. The company operates a consumer/retailer Android shopping application (Dagangan Mall), is backed by 500 Global, and is recognized as a Rural Digitalization Partner of Indonesia's Ministry of Villages, Disadvantaged Regions, and Transmigration. As of this profile, Dagangan publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Defer
providers.description: Defer was a TypeScript-first background job and workflow automation platform for Node.js applications that let developers schedule, queue, and orchestrate serverless functions with built-in retries, throttling, concurrency controls, and scheduled (CRON) execution. Defer integrated with frameworks such as Next.js, Remix, and SvelteKit through an SDK and a managed control plane. The defer.run service has since transitioned and the defer.run domain currently redirects to digger.tools; this entry preserves the historical profile and links to the surviving documentation, GitHub organization, and references.

providers.name: Deppon Express
providers.description: Deppon Express (德邦快递), operated by Deppon Logistics Co., Ltd., is a major Chinese express delivery and logistics provider specializing in large-parcel (heavy/bulky) express, less-than-truckload freight, full-truckload, air freight, warehousing, supply chain, and cross-border services. Founded from Cui's Freight Company (1996) and incorporated in 2009, it became part of the JD Logistics group in 2022 and ranks among China's largest express carriers by market share. For developers and enterprise partners, Deppon runs the Deppon Open Platform (德邦开放平台, established 2015) at dpopen.deppon.com, offering system-integration APIs for order creation, standard track/tracking queries, and electronic waybill (面单) printing, with access granted to contracted monthly-settlement customers.

providers.name: Dil Mil
providers.description: Dil Mil is a South Asian dating and matchmaking platform built to help singles find meaningful, culturally-grounded connections. Its mobile app offers matching algorithms, interest-based community chat rooms, global matching that reaches beyond geography, and a VIP Elite membership tier with premium features such as unlimited likes, rewind, and advanced filtering. The company markets itself under the tagline "Find Something Real" and highlights thousands of documented success stories among South Asian singles worldwide. Dil Mil is a consumer mobile application with no public developer or API surface; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking.

providers.name: Diraq
providers.description: Diraq is a quantum computing company headquartered in Sydney, Australia, with offices in Palo Alto, California and Boston, Massachusetts. Spun out of UNSW Sydney in 2022 by Professor Andrew Dzurak, Diraq builds quantum processors from silicon spin qubits — quantum information encoded in the spin of single electrons held in quantum dots formed inside structures derived from conventional CMOS transistors, so the qubits can be fabricated on standard semiconductor foundry lines. The company works with imec, NVIDIA and Quantum Machines, has advanced through DARPA's utility-scale quantum computing initiative, and targets a first commercial processor toward the end of the decade. Diraq is a pre-commercial hardware and research organization: as of this profile it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and its stated commercial pathway — cloud access to its processors — is still on the roadmap rather than in market.

providers.name: DXY
providers.description: DXY (丁香园) is China's leading digital healthcare technology company, founded in 2000 in Harbin and headquartered in Hangzhou. It operates a "D+C" dual strategy: a professional physician community and clinical toolset (drug reference "用药助手", clinical case database, medical education, and the "Insight" pharmaceutical data analytics platform) alongside consumer health services under the "丁香医生" (Dingxiang Doctor) brand. DXY also runs the Biomart / 丁香通 life-sciences supplies marketplace. Its Medical Data Open Platform (open.dxy.cn) exposes standardized healthcare data services — newly-approved drugs, drug SKU and drug search, disease search, and hospital/institution search — as REST/JSON APIs under api.dxy.cn for pharmaceutical, medical, and health-tech partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Eclipse Foods
providers.description: Eclipse Foods is a Berkeley, California plant-based food company making non-dairy ice cream and soft-serve engineered from cassava, corn, rapeseed, and potato to replicate the taste and texture of traditional dairy. Marketed as chef-crafted (co-founder brings 16-Michelin-Star kitchen experience) and sold in gallon tubs and soft-serve mixes to consumers and foodservice operators. Backed by Initialized Capital. This is a consumer/CPG brand with a WordPress marketing storefront and no public developer API; the profile captures its web identity, published llms.txt, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Eclypsium
providers.description: Eclypsium is a supply-chain and infrastructure security company that delivers firmware, hardware, and low-level software assurance for enterprise and national infrastructure. Its cloud-based platform continuously scans laptops, servers, network gear, and other devices for firmware implants, rootkits, backdoors, vulnerable components, and integrity drift below the operating system, giving security teams device-level visibility, threat detection, and supply-chain risk management across the hardware and firmware lifecycle. Eclypsium integrates with SIEM, SOAR, and IT workflows and is used to defend against firmware-level attacks, enforce device integrity, and meet supply-chain security and compliance requirements. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and is profiled here in the API Evangelist network. No public self-service developer API is currently published; enrichment captured the company's security, trust, and disclosure posture.

providers.name: Edge Case Research
providers.description: Edge Case Research (operating as "Edge Case", ecr.ai) is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania company founded in 2013 that provides functional safety engineering, risk management and safety-assurance software for autonomous and other "frontier technology" systems. Its DevSafeOps methodology carries safety through the whole product lifecycle — hazard identification in design, verified safety evidence in build, and continuous safety monitoring in operations — and its nLoop live-safety-case platform assembles evidence from design, simulation, test and field operations into an auditable, continuously updated safety case. The company works across aerospace and defense, automotive and autonomous trucking, space, oil and gas, and supply chain and logistics, and publishes the Open Autonomy Safety Case framework as SACM XML on GitHub. Edge Case publishes no public product API or OpenAPI; the only machine-readable surface reachable on its own host is the Wix-provided site MCP endpoint advertised in its llms.txt.

providers.name: Embark
providers.description: Embark Veterinary is a dog genetics company that sells at-home canine DNA testing kits for breed identification, health condition and genetic-risk screening, trait analysis, and relative matching, alongside supplements and breeder/veterinary testing programs. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, the company operates a direct-to-consumer storefront, a help center, and a resources/blog library, but does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile was surfaced from VC-portfolio data; no machine-readable API surface (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP) was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Ennis Inc
providers.description: Ennis Inc is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Ennis Inc API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Euler Motors
providers.description: Euler Motors is an Indian electric commercial vehicle manufacturer headquartered in New Delhi, building battery-electric cargo and light commercial vehicles for last-mile logistics — the HiLoad and Turbo electric three-wheelers and the Storm EV four-wheeler light commercial vehicle range. Alongside the vehicles the company operates Euler Shepherd, a connected-vehicle telematics platform delivered as two end-user products: Shepherd Lite (a mobile app for real-time vehicle location, battery state of charge, range, charging status and alerts) and Shepherd Enterprise (a browser-based fleet console with trip, utilization and operations reporting). Euler Motors publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog or partner integration documentation on any host it controls. The Shepherd web console is a single-page application whose backend answers anonymous requests with 403, so the telematics data surface is reachable only to vehicle owners inside the product. The company does publish an llms.txt at its web root, directing AI crawlers to its product, service-network and blog pages.

providers.name: Exactera
providers.description: Exactera is a corporate tax technology and advisory company that pairs AI-powered software with expert tax professionals to help multinational corporations manage the full corporate tax lifecycle. Its SaaS platform and services span transfer pricing compliance and benchmarking, R&D tax credits, fixed-asset depreciation, indirect (sales and use) tax advisory, tax provision, and the RoyaltyStat royalty-rate and transfer-pricing data platform. Exactera automates documentation, benchmarking studies, and regulatory reporting so tax and finance teams can reduce audit exposure and meet global compliance requirements. Backed by Insight Partners, the company serves enterprise tax departments and advisory firms worldwide.

providers.name: ezCater
providers.description: ezCater is a corporate and workplace catering marketplace that connects businesses with a nationwide network of local restaurants and caterers. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Boston, the platform lets organizations order food online for meetings, events, and recurring team meals, and layers workplace-food management on top: meal programs, per-team and per-location spend controls, group ordering, delivery coordination, and centralized invoicing and reporting. ezCater serves companies of every size across the United States and is backed by ICONIQ Capital, Insight Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and the SoftBank Vision Fund. The company does not publish a public developer API; integrations are arranged through its enterprise and partner sales channels. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer, security, and trust surface.

providers.name: Fiber
providers.description: Fiber is an Express-inspired web framework for Go built on Fasthttp for building fast and scalable microservices and APIs.

providers.name: Field AI
providers.description: FieldAI builds general-purpose robot intelligence through its Field Foundation Models (FFMs) and EDGE brain — a new class of physics-first, risk-aware foundation models for embodied AI. FieldAI's embodiment-agnostic autonomy lets robots navigate dynamic, unstructured environments without maps, GPS, or predefined trajectories, and has been proven across quadrupeds, humanoids, wheeled robots, and passenger-scale vehicles. Founded in 2023 (formerly AI for Humanity) and based in Mission Viejo, California, the company is led by veterans from DeepMind, Google Brain, Tesla Autopilot, NASA JPL, and SpaceX, and serves construction, energy, mining, logistics, manufacturing, power and utility, agriculture, and federal applications. FieldAI has raised over $405M from investors including Bezos Expeditions, Canaan Partners, Khosla Ventures, Temasek, Intel Capital, Hyundai Motor Company, and Prysm Capital.

providers.name: FlyHomes
providers.description: Flyhomes is a Bellevue, Washington-based real estate and mortgage financial technology company whose Buy Before You Sell platform lets homebuyers purchase a new home before selling their existing one. Its products—Flyhomes Cash Offer, Instant Equity, and Guaranteed Backup Contract—turn financing into competitive cash-like offers, unlock home equity without requiring a prior sale, and reduce a buyer's debt-to-income ratio so they can qualify for larger loans and move only once. Flyhomes reaches homebuyers through a network of in-network loan officers and real estate agents and also operates an AI-powered home search portal. Flyhomes does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, discovery surface (llms.txt), and domain-security posture.

providers.name: FreightRoll
providers.description: FreightRoll is a logistics technology company whose flagship product, YardOS, is a customizable Yard Operating / Management System (YMS) that turns shipping and receiving yards into driver-friendly, self-service hubs. YardOS reduces truck-driver wait times, improves yard throughput, and streamlines gate and dock operations, with the company citing up to a 50% reduction in truck turnaround time, 95%+ fewer human-to-driver interactions, and $100K+ annual savings per facility across a network of 150,000+ registered drivers. FreightRoll integrates with existing systems across API, EDI, and SFTP mechanisms and deploys remotely in under an hour. The company is backed by 500 Global. FreightRoll does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition; its public website is Wix-hosted and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic AI access to public site content.

providers.name: FreshToHome
providers.description: FreshToHome (Freshtohome Foods Private Limited) is a Bangalore-headquartered direct-to-consumer e-commerce company selling fresh, antibiotic-residue-free fish, seafood, poultry, mutton, ready-to-cook and heat-and-eat food. Founded in 2015 by Shan Kadavil, Mathew Joseph and Jayesh Jose, it runs its own farm-and-boat-to-doorstep cold chain, sourcing from thousands of fishermen and farmers and delivering across cities in India and the United Arab Emirates. The company sells through its website and its consumer iOS and Android apps. It publishes an llms.txt at its web root but operates no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Fundamental Technologies
providers.description: Fundamental Technologies Inc. (Fundamental) is an AI company building foundation models for predictive decision-making across enterprises and governments. Its flagship product, NEXUS, is a large tabular model pre-trained on billions of real-world enterprise tables and designed to capture the complex, non-linear feature interactions in structured data that large language models handle poorly. NEXUS is positioned to be deployed "with just one line of code" with a deep AWS integration and confidential-computing privacy controls. Founded by DeepMind alumni and led by serial entrepreneurs, the company raised a $255M Series A in February 2026 and is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes a marketing and research presence at fundamental.tech but no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Gerson Lehrman Group (GLG)
providers.description: Gerson Lehrman Group (GLG) is the world's leading platform for trusted human expertise, connecting organizations with a network of senior-level subject-matter experts to inform strategic decision-making. For more than 25 years GLG has facilitated expert calls and meetings, on-demand expert content and transcripts, quantitative and qualitative research and surveys, in-person and virtual events, and advisory and placement engagements. Its myGLG platform layers AI-powered and agentic research tools over that expert network. GLG was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. GLG operates no public developer API or documented developer program; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and security surface.

providers.name: Glow
providers.description: Glow (glowing.com) is a women's health and reproductive-health technology company whose consumer mobile apps track periods, ovulation, fertility, pregnancy, and early baby development for a community of more than 25 million members. Its app suite spans Glow (ovulation and fertility), Eve by Glow (period tracking), Glow Nurture (pregnancy), and Glow Baby (infant development), and it layers AI-powered health insights through GlowGPT along with a Glow Premium subscription and a companion Glow Shop for hardware such as basal thermometers, test strips, and a smart breast pump. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network, Glow is a consumer app business with no public developer program: no API portal, developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface could be located during enrichment.

providers.name: Good Driver
providers.description: Good Driver Club (formerly Good Driver Mutuality) is an insurtech company backed by Ribbit Capital and Hedosophia. It runs a membership-based, cost-sharing alternative to traditional collision and comprehensive auto coverage: members pay weekly pledges into a shared community pool that covers vehicle damage from accidents, weather, theft, and other qualifying events across 5,000+ partner repair shops nationwide, and accident-free members keep their unused pledge balances as savings. It is explicitly not insurance. The product is delivered through a consumer mobile app (Good Driver Club on Google Play); the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Gradiant
providers.description: Gradiant is a global water and wastewater infrastructure company founded in 2013 out of MIT and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, that designs, builds and operates end-to-end industrial water systems from intake to discharge. It positions itself as "the Water Layer of the AI Economy", supplying ultrapure water, process water, wastewater recycling, minimal- and zero-liquid-discharge and resource-recovery systems to semiconductor fabs, AI data centers, energy producers and applied industries including pharmaceuticals, mining, food and beverage, refining and chemicals, textiles and renewables. Its proprietary technology portfolio includes Counterflow Reverse Osmosis (CFRO), Semi-Batch Reverse Osmosis (SBRO), Carrier Gas Extraction (CGE), Selective Contaminant Extraction (SCE), Free Radical Oxidation (FRO), Bio Infinity, the ForeverGone PFAS destruction process, the HyperSolved data-center cooling-water platform, the CURE Chemicals specialty-chemicals line and SmartOps AI, a machine-learning platform for optimizing and predicting plant operations. Gradiant raised a Series E at a $2 billion valuation in May 2026. It is an industrial equipment, chemicals and build-own-operate services company: it publishes no public developer portal, no developer API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and SmartOps AI is delivered as a customer-facing operations platform rather than as a public API.

providers.name: Gridwise
providers.description: Gridwise is an earnings-tracking and optimization platform for rideshare and delivery gig workers, aggregating mileage, trip, and income data across gig platforms such as Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Grubhub, Instacart, and Amazon Flex so drivers can see where they earn most and drive more strategically. Alongside the consumer app, Gridwise operates Gridwise Analytics, a B2B mobility-data business that turns millions of anonymized driver location, trip, and earnings records into industry benchmarking, KPI, and market-intelligence products for gig mobility platforms, financial services, retailers/merchants, and autonomous vehicle fleets. Data is delivered as aggregated weekly reports, record-level trip datasets, and consumer/driver surveys through commercial engagement. Gridwise does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its consumer, data-product, support, and policy surfaces.

providers.name: HireRight
providers.description: HireRight is a leading global provider of employment background screening, drug and health screening, and workforce verification services, helping more than 28,000 organizations across 200+ countries and territories run and manage their screening programs. Founded in 1990 and headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, HireRight offers 250+ products and services spanning criminal, financial, identity, education and employment verification, compliance, driving records, and Form I-9 checks, and screened roughly 85 million people in 2025. HireRight does not publish a public developer REST API or developer portal; its integration surface is partner- and contract-based, delivered through 70+ prebuilt connectors with 45+ HCM and ATS partners (including Workday, ADP, Oracle, and UKG) and the Applicant Center candidate experience. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's public, machine-readable, and security/compliance surface (llms.txt, trust center, disclosure, domain security) rather than an open API.

providers.name: HomeLane
providers.description: HomeLane is an Indian end-to-end interior design company that delivers customized home interiors — modular kitchens, wardrobes, storage, bedroom, living room, bathroom, and home-office designs — pairing in-house digital design and 3D visualization tools with material selection and professional installation, backed by a 45-day delivery guarantee on end-to-end modular interiors. Founded in Bangalore and backed by Accel, HomeLane operates across major Indian cities through design studios, a franchise/partner network, and a customer mobile app. HomeLane currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks its digital, security, and identity surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hungryroot
providers.description: Hungryroot is a personalized grocery and meal-planning service that blends meal-kit convenience with grocery-store variety. Its AI-driven personalization engine builds each customer's cart from dietary preferences, health goals, and budget, drawing on a catalog of 50,000+ recipes and curated grocery products that support high-protein, gluten-free, vegan, and other dietary needs. Hungryroot is a direct-to-consumer company backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners; it operates a consumer web and mobile app experience rather than a public developer platform. This profile was surfaced through the venture portfolio graph and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which probed the provider's domain and public discovery surfaces (no public API, OpenAPI, SDKs, well-known catalog, security.txt, or llms.txt were found as of this pass).

providers.name: Intus Care
providers.description: IntusCare (Intus Care, Inc.) is a Providence, Rhode Island health technology company building an end-to-end software and services ecosystem for PACE — Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly. Founded in 2019 by Brown University students Robbie Felton, Evan Jackson and Alex Rothberg, it launched population health analytics at PACE of Rhode Island in 2020 and now serves 70+ PACE organizations. Its products are CareHub, a PACE-native ONC-certified EMR and care-management platform; IRIS, a risk-adjustment and coding system for PACE and value-based care organizations; and a Population Health & Utilization Management suite delivered with fractionally-staffed Integrated Care Services clinicians. IntusCare markets interoperability and out-of-the-box third-party administrator (TPA) integrations, but as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract — customer-facing surfaces are the authenticated CareHub and analytics applications.

providers.name: Jays
providers.description: JAYS is a Swedish consumer audio brand founded in 2006 by Jens and Johan, headquartered in Sweden and owned by the Northbaze Group AB. It designs and sells wireless and wired headphones, true-wireless earbuds, Bluetooth and multiroom speakers, and audio accessories, sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at jaysheadphones.com. JAYS publishes no first-party developer API; its only machine-accessible surface is the Shopify-provided agent-commerce layer: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted MCP shopping endpoint, Customer Account OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, and an llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio/commitment lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Julienne Bruno
providers.description: JULIENNE BRUNO is a London-based food company that creates, develops and produces naturally plant-based fresh cheeses. Its Collection 01 comprises Burrella, Superstraccia and Crematta - dairy-free, fermented products positioned as original foods in their own category rather than vegan imitations. Products are sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront and stocked at Ocado, Whole Foods, Planet Organic, Harrods and Selfridges, and featured on the menus of 800+ restaurants, pubs and cafes. Founded in 2020 and backed by Seedcamp, the brand and assets were later acquired by Harvey & Brockless (The Compleat Food Group). This is a consumer packaged goods company; it publishes no developer API - the profile is enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Kampi
providers.description: Kampi is an aquaculture technology company headquartered in Samborondón, Ecuador, building an AI-powered mobile app and platform for real-time shrimp farm management. Created by the team behind XpertSea (KAMPI AQUA SOLUTIONS S.A. / XpertSea Solution Inc.), Kampi converts daily farm records into personalized guidance using machine learning, an approach it calls dynamic precision farming. The platform combines three integrated tools — Pond Vision (intelligent pond monitoring), FarmAI (predictive biomass analytics) and Farmbook (digital team integration) — to deliver biomass monitoring, biological parameter tracking, real-time alerts, harvest planning and FCR optimization from a smartphone, online or offline. Kampi is a marketing-and-mobile-app company with no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its published web presence and a verbatim llms.txt it serves.

providers.name: Kasa Living
providers.description: Kasa Living, Inc. (operating as Kasa) is a San Francisco-founded, tech-enabled hospitality company that partners with institutional real-estate owners to convert multifamily, single-family and hotel inventory into professionally managed, apartment-style flexible accommodations across 90+ U.S. cities. Founded in 2016 by Roman Pedan, Kasa runs a proprietary hospitality operating system covering dynamic pricing, automated operations, keyless self check-in and a 24/7 remote "Virtual Front Desk" instead of an on-site front desk, and distributes inventory direct at kasa.com plus through OTAs and GDS via the NextPax supply API. Kasa publishes no public developer API, developer portal or machine-readable API specification; its one machine-readable, agent-facing artifact is a hand-authored llms.txt served at kasa.com/llms.txt.

providers.name: Keploy
providers.description: Open-source, AI-native testing platform that captures real production API traffic with eBPF and replays it in CI as deterministic tests, auto-generated mocks, and production-like sandboxes with zero code changes. Offers a Cloud REST API, a hosted MCP server, llms.txt, and generated agent skills.

providers.name: Kerys
providers.description: Kerys Software is a European (Palaiseau, France) cybersecurity company behind YS::Desktop, a Type 1 hypervisor that runs multiple fully isolated environments on a single workstation. By preallocating dedicated CPU cores to the hypervisor versus VM workloads and adding hypervisor-level encryption, YS::Desktop closes VM escape and cross-VM attack vectors while sustaining roughly 92% native performance. It replaces dedicated admin machines, air-gapped OT laptops, and traditional VDI for regulated organizations in aerospace and defense, energy, finance, construction, and the public sector, with a mandatory Security Domain model (no unmanaged VMs) administered through the YAC console. The company positions around NIS2, IEC 62443, and ANSSI multi-environment workstation guidance and sells 100% through resellers. Kerys does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or pricing; it was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and enriched here from its public site.

providers.name: Kodiak Robotics
providers.description: Kodiak Robotics, which now operates publicly as Kodiak AI, is an autonomous vehicle company founded in April 2018 by CEO Don Burnette and headquartered in California with a Texas operations center. Its flagship product is the Kodiak Driver, an AI-driven autonomy system that pairs onboard artificial intelligence with modular, swappable sensor hardware and offboard services so that a single driverless stack can be carried across different vehicle platforms. The company sells into three markets — long-haul trucking, defense, and industrial ground transportation — and positions driverless operation as a safety improvement, citing that more than 85% of U.S. truck crashes are caused by human error. Kodiak reports more than 2.6 million autonomous miles driven and over 7,000 loads delivered. Kodiak publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs; enrichment probes of kodiak.ai found no /.well-known/ discovery documents and no api/docs/developer subdomains. It does publish an llms.txt, an RSS news feed, and a corporate safety report, so this profile is maintained as a company record rather than an API producer profile.

providers.name: KokkanLogis Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: KokkanLogis Co.,Ltd. (주식회사 곳간, branded KOKKAN / 도심창고 곳간) is a South Korean urban self-storage and logistics operator headquartered in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. It rents managed storage units in five sizes (S, M, L, XL, XXL, from 1.0m cubes up to 2.0 x 2.0 x 2.0m) across 22 branches in Seoul, Busan, Incheon, Gyeonggi and Chungbuk, serving households storing seasonal appliances, clothing, bedding and baby goods as well as businesses storing samples, inventory, documents and office equipment. Customers select a branch, choose a unit size, pay and manage their contract through the KOKKAN mobile apps for iOS and Android, with recurring monthly card billing through a Korean payment gateway, long-term and promotional discounting, an address-rental (주소지 임대) product, and an optional pickup service for moving stored goods. The company also runs a franchise and partnership program for operators who want to open a KOKKAN branch. It was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio. As of this profile KokkanLogis publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or technical documentation — the product surface is a consumer website plus native mobile apps.

providers.name: Kuli
providers.description: Kuli is an AI agent for influencer marketing, built for consumer brands. It runs the full creator marketing lifecycle end to end — discovery, vetting, outreach, and reporting — so a small marketing team ships like a much larger one. Unlike platforms that filter creators on metadata such as follower counts and engagement rates, Kuli's agent watches actual creator videos frame by frame across TikTok and Instagram, assessing brand safety, content style, audience signals, and brand fit, then drafts personalized outreach in the brand's own voice and reports campaign ROI on a schedule. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Levallois-Perret, Paris, Kuli is a Y Combinator company. As of this profile Kuli publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs — its only machine-readable surface is an llms.txt.

providers.name: Lapse
providers.description: Lapse is a London-founded consumer photo company (Lapse Ltd) whose iOS app turns an iPhone into a disposable camera - a one-tap Lock Screen shutter, a film "developing" delay, and a friends-only photo journal built on a "Friends not followers" thesis of no ads, no data sales, and no public follower counts. The app is invite and friends-gated Early Access, free to use, iOS only, and screens uploads with AI moderation; contacts are hashed and encrypted on device. Lapse is backed by Greylock, GV and Speedinvest. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or documentation as of the July 2026 enrichment pass, so this profile captures company identity, the published policy and support surface, and probed security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: LARQ
providers.description: LARQ is a direct-to-consumer water technology company that designs self-cleaning and filtering drinkware and home water products. Its flagship Bottle PureVis uses UV-C light to neutralize up to 99.9999% of harmful, odor-causing bacteria in the bottle and on the water surface, and the range extends to filtered bottles, filtered pitchers, an under-sink water filter, and the cuva beverage flavor line. The company positions itself around sustainable hydration — reducing single-use plastic bottle consumption — and funds environmental nonprofits from a portion of each purchase. LARQ is a consumer hardware and e-commerce business: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Lean
providers.description: Lean is an open-source theorem prover and programming language based on dependent type theory, designed for formal verification of mathematics and software. It supports interactive proof development and is used by mathematicians and computer scientists.

providers.name: Lil Snack
providers.description: Lil Snack is a Manhattan Beach, California games company, founded in 2024, that builds "snackable" daily games and party games — short pop-culture puzzle, word, and trivia titles that refresh every day. It runs its own consumer destination at lilsnack.com (Clue Daily, Scattergories Daily, Swap, DownWords, Pickle, Lite Brite Daily, Wheel of Fortune TODAY, Quiz Climb, Venn, Chain, and more) and also powers games embedded inside partner consumer platforms, citing BuzzFeed, FOX, Hasbro, the Los Angeles Times, Netflix, Peacock, Prime Gaming, Reddit, and Sony. The company reports 40M+ games played and 10M+ players all-time, and monetizes through platform partnerships, sponsorships, and brand licensing. As of this profile Lil Snack publishes NO public developer surface — no API, no documentation portal, no SDKs, no public GitHub organization, and no /.well-known documents; its partner game integrations are arranged through business development rather than self-serve APIs. This API Evangelist profile therefore captures verified company identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: LVX (formerly LetsVenture)
providers.description: LVX — formerly LetsVenture — is an India-based private market investing platform founded in 2013 by Shanti Mohan and headquartered in Bengaluru, with teams in Delhi and Mumbai. The platform connects startup founders raising capital with angel investors, family offices and VCs, and has been a SEBI-regulated entity since its Angel AIF was approved in 2018. Its product surface spans LVX start (early-stage angel investing), LVX grow (growth-stage and co-investment deals), LVXschool (private market investor education), LVX Debt (non-dilutive debt financing for startups) and LVX Track (portfolio dashboards), alongside the sister platform trica. The company publicly reports 35K+ startups, 14K+ investors and over Rs 1500 Cr of AIF assets under management. LVX rebranded from LetsVenture in July 2025 and letsventure.com now redirects to lvxventures.com. LVX operates no public developer API program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition or SDKs were found, and the platform-backing API at api.lvxventures.com is a private token-authenticated service.

providers.name: Mask API
providers.description: Mask API is a powerful and flexible tool designed to help programmers and companies customize the response format of endpoint APIs, enabling selective field filtering and data transformation in API responses.

providers.name: Mint State Labs
providers.description: Mint State Labs (mintstatelabs.com, operating as Wildnet Edge) is an AI-first custom software development and IT outsourcing company delivering custom AI, machine learning, mobile, web, and cloud engineering services to enterprises and Fortune 500 clients. Its offerings span custom AI model and agent development, generative AI, ChatGPT app development, mobile and web app development, DevOps, data engineering, business intelligence, and staff augmentation ("build a team" / white-label) across a broad set of frameworks and platforms. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; the public presence is a marketing and services site with no first-party API product, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Modern Meadow
providers.description: Modern Meadow is a bio-design and materials-science company founded in 2011 in Brooklyn by Andras Forgacs, Francoise Marga, Gabor Forgacs and Karoly Jakab, now headquartered in Nutley / Pine Brook, New Jersey, where it operates an innovation lab opened in 2017. The company applies synthetic biology and protein engineering to build animal-free, bio-fabricated alternatives to leather and other petrochemical-derived materials, through the Bio-Alloy technology platform (an alloy of engineered proteins and bio-based polymers), the BIO-VERA material launched in 2023, and its current flagship INNOVERA, a next-generation leather alternative made from plant proteins, biopolymers and recycled rubber with more than 80% renewable carbon content. It sells into interiors, fashion and accessories, footwear, and automotive, and has partnered with BASF, tannery HELLER-LEDER (a 2026 European joint venture) and Allbirds (the Terralux footwear line). Modern Meadow has raised roughly $236M. It is a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: profiling on 2026-08-01 found no public API, no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI/GraphQL/MCP surface, no /.well-known/ documents, and no GitHub organization. Its corporate site (modernmeadow.com, Craft CMS) largely redirects to the product site innovera-world.com.

providers.name: MyWear
providers.description: MyWear (operating as vPersonalize Inc.) is a Houston, Texas based, Accel-backed software company founded in 2014 that provides a cloud platform for on-demand apparel manufacturing and mass customization. Its integrated toolset spans the full production lifecycle: a 3D product customizer and 3D uniform builder for real-time design, an online pattern-making CAD with automated size grading, web-to-print and print-layout automation with color management (PANTONE, CMYK, custom SPOT), an automated catalog builder, e-commerce storefront integration, and order and factory management across multiple suppliers. The company holds six US patents covering its automation and pattern-generation technology and targets apparel brands, sportswear makers, and print-on-demand operators. The public surface is a marketing and product site (vpersonalize.com); no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: NanoLumens
providers.description: NanoLumens is an American designer and manufacturer of direct-view LED (dvLED) displays and video walls, headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia and founded in 2006 by Rick Cope. It builds fixed and flexible indoor and outdoor displays in custom sizes, shapes and curvatures across the Engage Pro, Engage, NXT, Nixel, NanoPanel 55, Captivate, Performance, CLRVision, CLRVU and NanoBanner product lines, together with Aurora video processing and the NanoSuite display-management software. Its displays are deployed in retail, casinos, higher education, sports and arenas, control rooms, hospitality, themed entertainment, government, corporate and transportation environments. The software side of the business — the AWARE platform and NanoSuite, powered by the ISAAC ecosystem — markets a JSON REST API and webhook-based alerting for remote diagnostics, content scheduling and display-fleet monitoring, but that API is delivered to display owners through an authenticated tenant and has no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: National Labor Relations Board
providers.description: The National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) is an independent federal agency responsible for protecting the rights of employees and employers in the United States. The NLRB administers the National Labor Relations Act, which guarantees the rights of employees to form unions and engage in collective bargaining with their employers.

providers.name: National Technical Information Service
providers.description: The National Technical Information Service (NTIS) is a government agency that serves as the largest central resource for government-funded scientific, technical, engineering, and business-related information, collecting, archiving, and disseminating data and reports on energy, aerospace, health, and environmental topics.

providers.name: Nix
providers.description: Nix (Nix Biosensors) develops wearable biosensor technology that analyzes sweat to deliver real-time hydration and electrolyte data.
