providers.description: Efficient Capital Labs (ECL) is a fintech providing fast, flexible non-dilutive, revenue-based capital to global B2B SaaS and AI companies. Founded in 2022 and backed by QED Investors, ECL turns predictable recurring revenue (ARR) into upfront growth capital without dilution, using its AURA AI underwriting engine for cross-border funding decisions in days rather than months. Its product suite spans Non-Dilutive Capital, ECL Flex (capital, payments, and financial insights), ECL Flow (cross-border payments with up to $1M/month free transfers), and Embedded Finance that lets platforms embed ECL financing into their own experience. ECL reports $200M+ deployed across 250+ founders globally with an 80%+ return-customer rate.

providers.name: Elephant Healthcare
providers.description: Elephant Healthcare is a global health-technology company, headquartered in the UK, that partners with governments to digitise and strengthen public health systems across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Its flagship product, ElephantOS, is a mobile- and offline-first electronic health record (EHR) that streamlines clinical workflows for primary and secondary care facilities, serving over 19 million contracted patients across Nigeria, Kenya and Pakistan. The company also builds Elephant Nudge, a clinical co-pilot that guides and rewards quality of care, and Elephant Platform, an emerging AI-driven marketplace that connects clinicians to third-party healthcare software, medical devices and supply-chain partners. Elephant is backed by General Catalyst and Seedcamp. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Encurate
providers.description: Encurate provides a Keto Diet API offering over 450 keto recipes across 11 categories (drinks, smoothies, staples, dips, desserts, soups, fish, beef, appetizers, snacks, and breakfast) with structured nutritional values including calories, fats, carbohydrates, and proteins. The REST API returns JSON and is distributed via RapidAPI with a free testing tier and a paid unlimited production tier for integration into health, fitness, and nutrition applications.

providers.name: First Horizon
providers.description: First Horizon Corporation is a Fortune 500 financial services holding company headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee. Through First Horizon Bank it provides commercial, private, consumer, and mortgage banking, wealth management, and capital markets services across the southern United States. First Horizon operates a real API Banking developer portal for Treasury Management clients, exposing RESTful products for money movement, ACH origination, real-time account information, and routing-number lookups, secured with OAuth 2.0 and a sandbox for build-and-test integration. Onboarding is partner/relationship gated and no OpenAPI/Swagger specifications are publicly downloadable — this repository captures the documented API surface honestly, humanURL-only.

providers.name: Herb
providers.description: Herb (herb.co) is a leading digital media and e-commerce platform dedicated to cannabis culture, education, and lifestyle. It publishes cannabis news, strain databases, product reviews, dispensary and brand guides, deals, recipes, and city-level legalization guides, and operates the "Herb Agency" offering branding and marketing services to cannabis companies. The consumer site is built on Gatsby (React) with a GraphQL data layer, Algolia search, and a Firebase/serverless backend hosted on Netlify. Herb is backed by Bullpen Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network from that portfolio; the company exposes no public developer API program at this time, so this profile captures its published web, content, and discovery surface (llms.txt, domain security posture, and identity/link properties) rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Hobart
providers.description: Hobart is a leading commercial food service equipment manufacturer that offers an API integration to automate work order workflow and streamline the exchange of data between partner systems and Hobart service operations.

providers.name: Immunitas Therapeutics
providers.description: Immunitas Therapeutics is a Boston, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company that discovers and develops novel antibody therapeutics for patients with cancer and autoimmune disease. It was founded by cancer-research and therapeutic-antibody scientists from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Mass General Cancer Center, the Broad Institute and MIT, whose single-cell analysis drug-discovery platform identified CD161 as a T-cell target. The lead program, IMT-009, is an anti-CD161 antibody in a Phase 1/2a study in solid tumors and hematological malignancies; a second, preclinical anti-CD161 program (IMT-380) for chronic inflammatory disease was licensed to Boehringer Ingelheim in May 2026. Immunitas publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable API contract. Its only public software is open source research tooling from the immunitastx GitHub organization, notably the MIT-licensed Python package monkeybread for analyzing cellular niches in single-cell spatial transcriptomics data.

providers.name: Jitjatjo
providers.description: Jitjatjo is a New York City based on-demand staffing and workforce management platform operated by JJJ International, matching hospitality, healthcare, education, facilities, retail and logistics businesses with W2 temporary talent in real time. The company runs two consumer-facing products — "Ondemand by Jitjatjo" for businesses booking shifts and "Flex by Jitjatjo" for talent picking up gigs — alongside "Network", a frontline vendor management system (VMS) for contingent labor that is integrated with SAP Fieldglass. JJJ International was acquired by Dayforce in September 2025 and the platform is being rebranded as Dayforce Flex Work; the Jitjatjo web apps now call API hosts on dayforceflexwork.com. Jitjatjo publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK or webhook catalog was found on any host the company controls.

providers.name: Kiavi
providers.description: Kiavi (formerly LendingHome) is a technology-driven private lender for residential real estate investors, providing fix-and-flip bridge loans, new-construction financing, and DSCR rental loans across 49 states plus Washington, D.C. The company has originated more than $30 billion in loans and funded over 100,000 investment properties, pairing a digital application and portfolio-management experience with institutional capital. Kiavi is backed by Cowboy Ventures and Ribbit Capital. As of this enrichment pass Kiavi publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site, a real-estate-investing blog, legal/policy pages, and a HackerOne-based security vulnerability disclosure program.

providers.name: Kymera Therapeutics
providers.description: Kymera Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 500 North Beacon Street in Watertown, Massachusetts, pioneering targeted protein degradation as a way to build oral small-molecule medicines against targets that conventional inhibitors cannot reach. Rather than blocking a protein's activity, Kymera's degraders recruit the body's own protein-disposal machinery so that a binding event alone is sufficient to eliminate the disease-driving protein, an approach the company describes as a disease-agnostic modality. Its wholly-owned pipeline is led by KT-621, a once-daily oral STAT6 degrader in Phase 2 for Type 2 inflammatory diseases including atopic dermatitis, asthma, COPD and chronic spontaneous urticaria, and KT-579, a first-in-class oral IRF5 degrader in Phase 1 for lupus, Sjogren's syndrome and rheumatoid arthritis. Partnered programs include the oral IRAK4 degrader KT-485/SAR447971 with Sanofi and the CDK2 molecular glue degrader KT-200 with Gilead Sciences. Kymera publishes no public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web, investor, patient and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: La Solive
providers.description: La Solive is a French vocational training organization (organisme de formation) preparing career-changers and apprentices for the trades behind building energy renovation and the climate transition. It runs state-recognized, practice-based programs — chef de projet en rénovation énergétique, conducteur de travaux, plombier chauffagiste pompe à chaleur et gaz, technicien de maintenance CVC, installateur de panneaux photovoltaïques, QualiPAC and agent de maintenance du bâtiment — delivered across campuses in Paris, Lyon, Nantes, Marseille, Toulouse and Lille plus a distance-learning track, with Qualiopi certification and France Travail / Mon Compte Formation / Transitions Pro financing. La Solive reports 1,500+ students trained and 500+ recruiting partner companies. It is a Partech portfolio company in the Climate sector. As of this enrichment pass La Solive publishes no public API, developer portal, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; it does publish an /llms.txt agent-readable site index, captured in this repo.

providers.name: MediaBeacon
providers.description: MediaBeacon is a Digital Asset Management (DAM) platform from Esko with a highly flexible architecture and open APIs that enable integration into many products. Its APIs support hands-off data transfer between services, reducing human intervention and enabling workflow automation.

providers.name: Medley
providers.description: Medley is a leadership development company that delivers group-based executive coaching at enterprise scale, pairing professional coaches with AI-enabled tooling to bring quality and a human touch to Fortune 500 organizations. Founded in 2020 by Edith Cooper and Jordan Taylor, the platform runs curated small-group coaching cohorts focused on trust, empathy, communication, and collaboration to drive organizational transformation. Medley raised a $3.7M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It operates as a B2B services and coaching platform and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: MidFirst Bank
providers.description: MidFirst Bank is a federally chartered savings association (thrift) headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, and owned by Midland Financial Co. Founded in 1982 with roots in Midland Mortgage from the early 1950s, it is the largest privately owned bank in the United States, with roughly $42 billion in assets and retail banking, private banking, commercial real estate lending, and nationwide mortgage servicing operations across Oklahoma, Arizona, California, Colorado, Nevada, Texas, and Utah. MidFirst does not operate a first-party public developer portal or publish downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. Its open-finance posture is aggregator-mediated: through its "Open Access" program, MidFirst adds direct API connections between its Business Online Banking platforms and consumer-permissioned data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Stripe, Intuit, Mastercard/Finicity, Envestnet Yodlee, and Morningstar), replacing screen scraping. There is no publicly documented first-party API surface, and no FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is published on its site as of this review.

providers.name: Nike
providers.description: Nike is the world's largest supplier of athletic shoes and apparel and a major manufacturer of sports equipment, designing, developing, and marketing products under the Nike, Jordan, and Converse brands.

providers.name: OakNorth
providers.description: OakNorth is a UK-based commercial bank and business-lending institution founded in 2015, providing debt financing to mid-market and lower-mid-market businesses in the UK and, through its New York team, the United States. Its products span business loans (from roughly GBP 1m to tens of millions), commercial real estate lending, commercial & industrial cash-flow financing, fund finance, and business and personal savings accounts. OakNorth is backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. It publicly exposes no developer API, open-banking API, or developer portal; its public technical surface is limited to a HackerOne responsible-disclosure program and standard web/legal properties. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Oboe
providers.description: Oboe is an AI-powered learning platform whose mission is to teach one billion people one trillion things. Positioned as "AI that won't make you stupid," it lets anyone learn virtually any subject through a conversational interface that generates personalized, on-demand courses and lessons ("magical courses made just for you"). Founded in New York and backed by Homebrew, Oboe is building what it calls the world's first completely generalized AI-powered learning platform, focused on making humans smarter rather than only making machines smarter. As a consumer web application, Oboe does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; api.oboe.com serves only an XML sitemap index for public course pages.

providers.name: ObserveIT (Proofpoint)
providers.description: ObserveIT was an insider threat management (ITM) vendor acquired by Proofpoint in 2019 and folded into the Proofpoint Insider Threat Management product line within Proofpoint's Information Protection portfolio. The platform provides endpoint visibility, user activity monitoring, session timelines, and data-loss detection across careless, malicious, and compromised users, correlating activity across endpoints, email, and cloud. Integration is delivered through webhooks that let SIEM and SOAR tools ingest alerts and automated exports to customer-owned AWS S3 storage; ObserveIT no longer operates as a standalone brand and publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-service API documentation.

providers.name: OnlineNIC
providers.description: OnlineNIC offers a RESTful API with JSON format response for our partners to directly manage their products and orders. We intends to help our partners automate the purchase process and enpower them to provide enduser a better user experience.

regulatory.note: provider carries no tags; regime could not be determined

providers.name: Operation Support Equipment
providers.description: API for managing and accessing operation support equipment data, inventory, maintenance records, and deployment information for operational logistics and equipment lifecycle management.

providers.name: Poker Skill
providers.description: Poker Skill is a mobile-first poker-training app for iOS and Android that turns learning poker into a daily habit. It teaches through interactive puzzles, bite-sized guided lessons, and daily practice reps that adapt to the player's skill level, from complete beginner to serious improver. At its core is "Showdown AI", a versioned game-theory engine that deals practice hands, plays the opponents, and grades every decision by its expected value — an approach the company says replicates the methods behind Pluribus, the first AI to beat top professionals at six-max no-limit hold'em. The product is subscription-funded with a free-to-start funnel, and is backed by Initialized Capital. Poker Skill is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: Pratilipi
providers.description: Pratilipi is India's largest digital storytelling platform, democratizing story creation and consumption across languages, formats, and boundaries. Built by Nasadiya Technologies Private Limited and headquartered in Bangalore, it lets more than 300,000 self-published writers reach roughly 25 million monthly readers across twelve Indian languages (Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, Bengali, English, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Urdu, and Odia). The ecosystem spans Pratilipi Literature, Pratilipi FM (audio books, podcasts, and folk songs), Pratilipi Comics (the largest Hindi online comic platform), Westland Publications, and IVM Podcasts, carrying a story "from someone's draft to someone's screen." Pratilipi does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's identity, web properties, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: R1 RCM
providers.description: R1 RCM is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The R1 RCM API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Racing Data
providers.description: Racing Data is a developer-focused API providing real-time updates and historical statistics across racing series, including Formula One, IndyCar, and others. It is intended for building custom data sets and analytics experiences on top of motorsports data.

providers.name: RightHand Robotics
providers.description: RightHand Robotics builds autonomous piece-picking robotic systems for order fulfillment. Its RightPick platform combines computer vision, machine learning, and adaptive grasping hardware to pick and place millions of SKUs at cycle times as fast as three seconds across e-commerce, pharmaceutical, apparel, health & beauty, and grocery operations. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and SoftBank Vision Fund. RightHand Robotics does not publish a public web API; integration, deployment, and operator documentation is provided to authorized customers and partners through a login-gated partner portal (rhrdocs.com). The public GitHub organization hosts open-source ROS packages and C control libraries for the earlier ReFlex robotic hand hardware rather than web-API client SDKs.

providers.name: Saffron Finance
providers.description: Saffron Finance is a decentralized peer-to-peer interest-rate risk adjustment protocol built on Ethereum. Underlying DeFi yield is transformed by a smart-contract vault system according to each user's indicated risk preference, splitting deposits into senior (fixed-income, risk-averse) and junior (variable, risk-seeking) tranches across Uniswap V3 fixed-income vaults. The protocol is governed by the Saffron DAO and its SFI token, and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital in the crypto-web3 sector. Saffron is an on-chain protocol rather than a hosted web-API provider: its developer surface is Solidity smart contracts, published documentation, audits, and whitepapers rather than a REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Second Spectrum (Genius Sports)
providers.description: Second Spectrum is a Los Angeles–based computer vision and AI sports tracking company, acquired by Genius Sports in 2021 for roughly $200M. It supplies skeletal and optical tracking, machine-learning analytics, and augmented broadcast products to major leagues, clubs, and broadcasters — most notably the NBA (official tracking partner from 2017 to 2023), the Premier League (official tracking partner via Football DataCo), and MLS. The customer-facing offering is the Performance Studio platform, used by club analysts and coaching staff to access tracking data, visualizations, and tagged clips. There is no public developer portal, no published OpenAPI, and no self-serve API keys; data and integration access are delivered exclusively under enterprise agreement with Genius Sports. The product surface is effectively a sales-led, league/club-tier offering rather than a developer API.

providers.name: tab32
providers.description: tab32 is a cloud-based dental practice management, imaging, and analytics platform for dental practices and dental service organizations (DSOs). tab32 offers a real, commercial API - powered by Google Apigee and HIPAA / SOC 2 Type II compliant - that exposes tab32's patient, provider, schedule, charts, notes, ledger, and payments data objects to DSOs and third-party developers. Access is partner-gated, not open self-service - developers reach the API through tab32's developer API portal after establishing a partnership or enterprise relationship, and full endpoint reference, authentication, and base URL details live behind that portal rather than on the public website. The API entries below are modeled from tab32's publicly documented data objects and API messaging; their endpoint paths are not published publicly and are therefore illustrative, not confirmed.

providers.name: Teesnap
providers.description: Teesnap is an all-in-one golf course management platform and point-of-sale system for golf operators, founded in 2013 and based in Las Vegas, Nevada. Its cloud software suite covers a tee sheet and tee-time booking engine, golf and food-and-beverage point of sale, customer and membership management, an online store, websites, payments, and a marketing and reporting system. Teesnap connects to the wider golf ecosystem through partner integrations - GolfNow (its official online tee-time distribution partner via NBC Sports Next), Priswing dynamic pricing, Golf Genius tournament management, QuickBooks Online accounting, Gallus mobile apps, Heartland payment processing, and range hardware from eRange and Select Pi. As of this catalog's review date Teesnap does not publish a public, self-service developer API or developer portal; integrations are delivered through partner-gated, business-development relationships. The APIs listed here are honestly modeled from Teesnap's public product surface and are not sourced from published API documentation.

providers.name: The Meta
providers.description: The Meta is the gaming-performance company behind KovaaK's Aim Trainer (formerly "Kovaak 2.0: The Meta"), a PC esports training platform distributed on Steam that pairs guided, skill-specific training modules with Kovaak's Sandbox aim trainer and its library of 2,600+ user-generated scenarios. The platform lets FPS players measure, diagnose, and improve their mechanical aim and in-game habits, feeding back insights on weaknesses so players can target their practice. Founded by Duncan Haberly, Jay Brown, and Chris Olson and backed by Canaan (Beta Fund), Village Global, Courtside VC, betaworks, GFR, and Akatsuki Entertainment Technology (AET Fund). The Meta operates a consumer game product, a community wiki, and a Discord community; it does not currently publish a public first-party developer API.

providers.name: Tooth Fairy
providers.description: Toothfairy is a UK dental telehealth platform billing itself as the world's first dentist on-demand, pairing registered dentists with a consumer mobile app to deliver teeth straightening with clear aligners, prescription teeth whitening, and same-day emergency video dental consultations 24/7, plus employer dental plans for businesses. The company is health-regulated in the UK, backed by Seedcamp, and ships its product as iOS and Android apps with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Tripledot
providers.description: Tripledot Studios (Tripledot Group) is a London-headquartered mobile games developer and publisher focused on data-driven casual games, with chart-topping titles including Woodoku, Solitaire, Duplica, Wordhop, Solitaire Scapes, Sudoku, Spider Solitaire and Blackjack played by more than 25 million daily active users. Founded as an independent studio and named Best Developer at the Pocket Gamer Mobile Games Awards 2023, Tripledot closed an $800 million acquisition of AppLovin's mobile games studio portfolio (ten studios) on July 1, 2025, and is backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners. Tripledot publishes no first-party developer API, portal or SDKs, but its website ships a real llms.txt and a live, publicly connectable MCP endpoint (the Wix Site Visitor Assistant) for agentic access to site content.

providers.name: truBrain
providers.description: truBrain is a Santa Monica, California nootropics and functional-beverage brand that makes "natural superfuels for performance" — drinkable nootropic shots (2,000mg of natural nootropics per 1oz bottle for focus and motivation), drinkable ketones (Ketone XL, 11g of pure ketones per shot for athletic energy and recovery), plus gummies, functional-mushroom blends, capsules, NAD+, hydration, and sleep supplements, packaged in recycled paper bottles. Founded by a team of neuroscientists and backed by 500 Global, the company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront and has run a Regulation A+ public equity offering. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. truBrain is a consumer packaged-goods company: it publishes no first-party developer API, documentation, or SDKs. The only machine-readable surface at its domain is Shopify's Customer Accounts OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 discovery metadata.

providers.name: Unspun
providers.description: Unspun is a fashion-technology company building Vega, the world's first 3D weaving machines, which transform yarn directly into finished woven garments in about twenty minutes for automated, localized, on-demand apparel manufacturing. Founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin and operating from Oakland, California and Hong Kong, the company pairs its weaving hardware with software for custom-fit patternmaking and design automation, working with manufacturers and brands to eliminate overproduction, with a mission of reducing global human carbon emissions by one percent. Unspun is backed by DCVC and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: YRC Worldwide
providers.description: YRC Worldwide (rebranded as Yellow Corporation in 2021) was a holding company whose subsidiaries — YRC Freight, Holland, Reddaway, New Penn, and HNRY Logistics — provided less-than-truckload (LTL) freight transportation, brokerage, and logistics services across North America. The company ceased operations on July 30, 2023 and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on August 6, 2023, ending nearly 100 years of operation. Bankruptcy asset sales redistributed terminals and equipment to Saia, XPO, Estes, and other carriers; no public developer APIs were ever published.

providers.name: Zum
providers.description: Zum is a student transportation technology company that runs school bus operations for K-12 school districts through its Connected Mobility Experience (CMX) platform. Founded by Ritu Narayan and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Zum unifies parents, students, drivers, and district administrators with real-time ride tracking, route optimization, parent notification apps, driver tooling, fleet management dashboards, and an electrified bus program. The company serves roughly 6,500 schools and districts, has completed more than 159 million rides, and is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. Zum operates consumer-facing parent and driver mobile apps and district dashboards, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface at this time.

providers.name: AbbVie
providers.description: AbbVie is a research-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, manufactures, and markets advanced therapies in immunology, oncology, neuroscience, and other specialty areas. AbbVie's portfolio includes treatments for autoimmune diseases, various cancers, neurological disorders, and aesthetics through the Allergan Aesthetics portfolio.

providers.name: Agentero
providers.description: Agentero is a digital insurance network and insurtech platform, founded in 2017 and based in Oakland, California, that gives independent property & casualty insurance agents market access to 100+ national and regional carriers alongside modern agency technology. Its unified command center lets agents get appointed, quote and bind policies, manage carrier appointments, and reconcile commissions from a single portal, with no startup fees or minimum-volume requirements. Agentero also offers an AI Appetite Checker that matches risks to the right carriers and Producerflow, a compliance and producer-management solution for carriers, MGAs, and agencies. Agentero is a portfolio company backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Agile Robots
providers.description: Agile Robots SE is a Munich-based robotics and artificial intelligence company founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics. The company develops force-sensitive industrial and service robots, robotic arms (Diana series), grippers and hands (Agile Hand), mobile robotics, and the AgileCore / AgileAI software platform that lets system integrators and operators build and deploy AI-driven automation for the automotive, consumer electronics, healthcare, and service industries. Headquartered in Munich's Sendling district with manufacturing across Europe, China, and India, Agile Robots reached unicorn valuation in a 2021 Series C and is backed by investors including Hongshan (Sequoia Capital China). This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Agile Robots does not currently publish a public developer portal, REST API, or first-party SDKs.

providers.name: Albo
providers.description: Albo (albo.com, formerly albo.mx) is a Mexican digital financial services company founded in 2016 and operating since 2022 as an Institución de Fondos de Pago Electrónico (IFPE) authorized by the Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores (CNBV) and regulated by Banco de México. Albo ships a mobile-first personal account with a Mastercard debit card — SPEI transfers, bill payments, cash deposit and withdrawal at partner locations, and real-time notifications — alongside "albo empresa", a business account for payroll, employee cards, and bulk dispersion of up to 3,000 transactions at a time. Adjacent credit (abea, by Aureo Lab) and crypto (albit, by Indigo DeFi) products are offered by independent partners. Albo publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog, or sandbox was found on any albo.com, albo.mx or albo.live host.

providers.name: Alta
providers.description: Alta (Alta Daily) is a New York City-based consumer AI styling and agentic-shopping app built by Flagship AI, Inc. It digitizes a user's wardrobe into a searchable digital closet, generates daily outfit recommendations from natural-language prompts, weather, and occasion, lets users virtually try outfits on a personalized avatar, and surfaces shoppable recommendations across 4,000+ partner brands. Powered by more than a dozen proprietary in-house multimodal generative AI models, Alta was named a TIME Best Invention of 2025 and raised an $11M seed round led by Menlo Ventures. It is offered as a free iOS and Android mobile app; as of this profile there is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Alta VR
providers.description: Alta VR (legally Another Axiom LLC) is a virtual reality game studio behind Gorilla Tag, one of the most-played VR titles ever, and the newer social VR world Orion Drift. The studio builds imaginative, physics-driven multiplayer experiences centered on hand-based locomotion and social play across Meta Quest, Steam, and other VR platforms. It runs an Another Axiom Creator Program for community map-building and content creation, and publishes game code and Unity map-export tooling through its public GitHub organization. Alta VR is a portfolio company of a16z. As a VR consumer game studio it does not currently operate a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program; its developer-facing surface is limited to open-source game code, custom map tooling, and creator resources.

providers.name: Andela
providers.description: Andela is a global talent platform and AI services provider founded in 2014 by Jeremy Johnson, connecting enterprises with vetted, remote technologists and AI engineers across 135+ countries. It grew into a unicorn (valued at $1.5B in 2021) serving 650+ clients, with a network of 200,000+ trained technologists. Its services span hiring AI engineers for application building, systems integration, and platform engineering; building enterprise AI solutions from data readiness to production deployment; and upskilling teams through AI curricula developed with partners such as NVIDIA and Google. Andela operates a fully remote model and is backed by GV, SoftBank Vision Fund, and Susa Ventures. It publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Apeel
providers.description: Apeel (Apeel Sciences) is a food technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Goleta, California. It produces a plant-derived, edible coating, made from lipids and glycerolipids found in the peels, seeds and pulp of produce, that is applied to fresh fruit and vegetables at packing houses to slow water loss and oxidation, extending shelf life and reducing food waste across the supply chain. Apeel-treated produce is sold through grocery retailers in multiple countries. In 2021 Apeel acquired ImpactVision and added hyperspectral imaging to its supplier installations to grade interior quality, ripeness and freshness. Apeel is a materials-science and supply-chain operator: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, or self-serve developer sign-up.

providers.name: AstraZeneca
providers.description: AstraZeneca is a British-Swedish multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology company focused on oncology, cardiovascular, renal, metabolism, and respiratory therapies. AstraZeneca does not publish a general developer portal or commercial public APIs; technology integration is delivered through enterprise partner programs, clinical trial data portals such as clinicaltrials.gov and the Vivli platform, and EDI/x12 channels used by distributors and pharmacy benefit managers.

providers.name: Authy
providers.description: Authy is a two-factor authentication (2FA) product originally built by Authy Inc. and acquired by Twilio in 2015. It provided a consumer authenticator app (TOTP soft tokens, encrypted cloud backup, and multi-device sync) alongside a developer-facing Authy API for one-time passwords over SMS and voice, soft tokens, and push authentication. Twilio has since folded the Authy developer API into the Twilio Verify API, deprecated and archived the first-party Authy client SDKs, and discontinued the Authy desktop applications in 2024. The consumer Authy mobile app remains available. New integrations are directed to Twilio Verify. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and is enriched here from Authy's remaining public surface (marketing site, archived GitHub organization, and deprecated SDK registries).

providers.name: BARK (BarkBox)
providers.description: BARK, Inc. (operating as BarkBox) is a New York-based dog-focused consumer company founded in 2011 by Henrik Werdelin and Matt Meeker, serving over two million dogs monthly through its BarkBox and Super Chewer subscription boxes, the BARK Bright dental line, the BARK Air pet travel experience, and retail distribution. The company went public via a SPAC merger in 2021 (NYSE: BARK). BarkBox does not operate a public developer program or externally documented API portal; its engineering surface is a set of mostly-internal Ruby services and open-source libraries published under the github.com/barkbox organization (including the barkbox_client Ruby API client and cursor-pagination gems). This profile was surfaced as a Slow Ventures portfolio company and enriched with verified public identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Beyond Math
providers.description: BeyondMath is an AI company that has built what it calls the world's first foundational AI model of physics. Its Generative Physics Engine runs full-fidelity, engineering-grade simulations covering fluid, thermal, and structural analysis directly from uploaded geometry, without pre-meshing or preprocessing, and returns results up to 1000x faster than traditional CFD/FEA solvers while generalizing across unseen geometries without retraining. The platform lets engineering teams explore thousands of design variations in minutes rather than months across automotive, aerospace, energy, defense, semiconductor, construction, telecommunications, and electronics. Founded by Alan Patterson (CEO) and Darren Garvey (CTO), the company raised an $18.5M seed round and partners with NVIDIA and AWS. Access is gated behind a waitlist for the Generative Physics Studio; on-premise and private-cloud enterprise deployment is offered. No public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI is published at this time.

providers.name: BoaConsulta
providers.description: BoaConsulta is a Brazilian digital-health platform, founded in 2012 and part of the Pixeon healthtech group, that connects patients, health professionals, and institutions. It pairs a free B2C marketplace for booking in-person consultations, teleconsultations, exams, and vaccinations with a full B2B/SaaS practice-management system (150+ integrated modules covering smart scheduling, electronic health records, telemedicine, financial management, TISS insurance billing, inventory, and automated reminders). The platform reports more than 58,000 health professionals, 1.7 million registered patients, and over 2 million appointments, with LGPD-compliant end-to-end encryption and daily automated backups. It has no public developer API; this profile is enriched from BoaConsulta's own public surfaces (llms.txt, status page, help center, blog, and legal pages).

providers.name: Booko
providers.description: Booko is an Australian book, eBook, audiobook, DVD, music and collectibles price-comparison service operating since 2007. It aggregates new and used prices across many online retailers and regions, calculates shipping, and converts international prices to the shopper's local currency to surface the cheapest place to buy a title. Booko also offers shopping lists with bundled shipping calculations, barcode scanning, reading lists, price alerts and notifications. It is a consumer-facing comparison site rather than a retailer or a public API provider, earning referral fees from partner shops (including Amazon Associates) when shoppers buy through its links. Booko is a solo developer-run product surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio company.

providers.name: Brite
providers.description: Brite is a white-label learning management system (LMS) platform for STEM education, giving educators, academies, and learning centers a single operational tool to run computer-science programs in game and web development. It bundles a ready-made curriculum, classroom and roster management, student progress reporting, and teacher accounts, replacing spreadsheets and disparate software with one branded platform. Brite is offered on free, per-student Professional, and custom school/district tiers. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Brown & Brown
providers.description: Brown & Brown, Inc. (NYSE: BRO) is a Daytona Beach, Florida headquartered insurance brokerage and risk-management intermediary founded in 1939, and one of the largest independent brokers in the United States. Following the 2025 acquisition of Accession Risk Management Group (Risk Strategies and One80 Intermediaries), it reports through two segments: Retail — property and casualty insurance, employee benefits, private client, captive solutions and financial/wealth services — and Specialty Distribution — programs, wholesale brokerage and MGA/binding-authority businesses including Arrowhead. As a distributor rather than a carrier, Brown & Brown places risk with insurers instead of underwriting it, and its US home market has no federal insurance regulator and no open-insurance mandate. Its API posture reflects that honestly: Brown & Brown publishes no public developer portal and no self-serve API. developer.bbrown.com, developers.bbrown.com, docs.bbrown.com and api.bbrown.com do not resolve, and every /developers, /api, /partners and /integrations path returns 404. Every discoverable application subdomain is a login wall — agent, client and vendor portals behind Microsoft Entra ID SSO or third-party sign-in. The only real programmatic surface is partner-gated: the Arrowhead Programs "Enterprise API" (EAPI), a quoting integration distributed through comparative raters and aggregators such as CoverHound, Tarmika, Semsee and DAIS, with no public documentation, base URL or specification. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference is published on any Brown & Brown first-party property; carrier data exchange runs, as it does across US retail brokerage, through the agency management system layer — Brown & Brown is a publicly referenced Vertafore AMS360 agency — and IVANS agency download rather than through any API Brown & Brown itself exposes. In July 2026 the company announced an AI-first transformation with Anthropic, McKinsey and Accenture, deploying Claude across 23,000 teammates and Claude Code across its software engineering organization; that is internal adoption and has so far produced no external API, developer portal or agent-facing surface. The only machine-readable documents Brown & Brown publishes are two RSS feeds — the blog and investor news releases.

providers.name: Cado Gifts, Inc.
providers.description: Cado Gifts, Inc. (CADO Gifting) is a luxury and corporate gifting company operating a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at cadogifting.com, serving the UAE and international markets with curated executive, host, and occasion gift collections plus a corporate/bulk gifting program. The business runs on Shopify (customer accounts, checkout, and blog/journal content) rather than a first-party public API; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No developer program, OpenAPI, or public API documentation is published; the only machine surface discovered is Shopify's Customer Account OIDC/OAuth well-known documents served under the store's own host.

providers.name: Carwow
providers.description: Carwow is a UK-based online automotive marketplace that helps consumers buy, sell, lease, and finance cars without haggling or hidden fees. Buyers browse new and used car deals, compare dealer quotes, arrange leasing (including salary sacrifice and fleet through Carwow Leasey), find electric-vehicle deals, and access vehicle financing and credit brokering. Sellers get free car valuations, part-exchange, and van sales. Carwow also publishes professional car reviews and ratings, runs a large YouTube channel, and offers comparison tools, EV charging maps, a car history checker, and insurance services. Founded in London and backed by Accel, Balderton Capital, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Carwow operates across the UK and Europe. It maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source engineering tooling but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Catalent
providers.description: Catalent is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Catalent API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: CBS (Paramount Global)
providers.description: CBS is the flagship broadcast television network of Paramount Global (NASDAQ: PARA, PARAA). It encompasses CBS Entertainment, CBS News, CBS Sports, CBS Stations (owned and operated), and feeds Paramount+ streaming service. CBS does not publish a consumer developer portal. Partner, syndication, advertising, and distribution APIs are operated privately through Paramount Global's business development, ad sales, and affiliate operations teams.

providers.name: Centivo
providers.description: Centivo is a primary-care-centered health plan administrator for self-funded employers, founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York City. Sold through benefits brokers and consultants, it serves mid-market employers (roughly 50 or more employees) and covers about 77,000 members across 160 businesses. Members get $0 primary care to encourage early intervention, and employers typically save 15-30% versus traditional fully-insured plans through a primary-care-first model, the cost advantages of self-funding, and directly negotiated health-system partnerships. Centivo operates member, employer, provider, and referral portals plus iOS/Android member apps; it does not publish a public developer API. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and JPMorgan Chase's Morgan Health.

providers.name: CesiumAstro
providers.description: CesiumAstro designs, manufactures, and tests full-stack communication systems and satellites for space, air, and ground missions. The Austin, Texas company, founded in 2017, builds active phased array payloads (Vireo), software-defined radios (SDR-1001/2051/2104/3104), reconfigurable processing units, SATCOM terminals (Skylark), tactical ISR/PNT payloads (Nightingale), and the integrated Element LEO satellite platform. Its hardware enables inter-satellite links, high-speed downlinks, lunar communications, and 5G non-terrestrial networks. CesiumAstro publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; this profile tracks the company as an aerospace hardware provider in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ClassAction
providers.description: ClassAction operates enjin (集団訴訟プラットフォーム enjin), a Japanese class-action / group-litigation platform that connects consumers who have suffered damages from the same party with registered attorneys to pursue collective lawsuits. Victims report their damages, registered lawyers volunteer to take on cases, and participants share legal costs and evidence so that even small-value claimants can afford to litigate. The service launched in May 2018 and is free for users. This is a consumer-facing legal-tech website with no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Commons
providers.description: Commons is an Oakland, California consumer climate-fintech company founded in 2018 by Sanchali Seth Pal and operated under the name Joro until its March 2023 rebrand. Its free iOS and Android app connects a user's bank accounts and credit cards through Plaid and runs every transaction through a proprietary carbon-estimation engine, the Carbonizer, which translates dollars spent into an estimate of kilograms of CO2e, alongside budgeting, savings goals, expert-reviewed sustainable brand ratings, a rewards program, monthly community challenges and an optional paid offset membership. The company has raised roughly USD 13.9 million across three rounds from investors including Sequoia Capital and Amasia. Commons is a direct-to-consumer mobile product rather than an API vendor: thecommons.earth is a Webflow marketing site with no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract, its brand directory and member exchange run on Next.js and Softr respectively, and its only public GitHub organization, CommonsTech, holds a single 2023 repository publishing carbon-offset provider evaluations rather than code.

providers.name: Conduent
providers.description: Conduent is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Conduent API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Confluence Unity
providers.description: Confluence Unity is the unified fund administration and reporting platform from Confluence Technologies, a software provider focused on the global investment management industry. The Unity suite (including Unity Financial Reporting, Unity Performance, and Unity Rex for AI-driven reconciliation) consolidates data, regulatory and shareholder reporting, and performance analytics for asset managers, fund administrators, and asset servicers. Confluence operates Unity as a hosted SaaS platform with integrations into client data warehouses; the public site does not publish open developer API documentation, so developer access is typically arranged through Confluence account teams.

providers.name: Crabi
providers.description: Crabi is a Mexican digital auto-insurance company (insurtech) offering fully online vehicle policies purchasable in about fifteen minutes from a mobile device. Coverage spans material damage, theft, third-party civil liability, medical expenses, and roadside and legal assistance across 27 Mexican states, sold and serviced through its mobile apps, online quoter (cotizador), and customer login portal. The company is regulated in Mexico by the CNSF and CONDUSEF and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Crabi publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Dalma
providers.description: Dalma is a French insurtech offering pet health insurance for dogs and cats, reimbursing veterinary bills (up to 100%, no deductible, EUR 2,500 annual ceiling) with fast payouts (50% within 30 seconds) and unlimited teleconsultations with veterinarians via its mobile app. Founded in Paris and backed by Northzone, Dalma insures 60,000+ pets across France and has expanded to Germany. It is a direct-to-consumer insurance brand with a member app (app.dalma.co) and a quote/subscription funnel; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Draftea
providers.description: Draftea is a Mexico-based daily fantasy sports and real-money sports gaming platform, billed as the first daily fantasy sports (DFS) product for the Spanish-speaking world. Fans draft lineups of real athletes across soccer, American football (via an NFL partnership), basketball, baseball, and Formula 1, enter paid contests, and compete against other users for cash prizes rather than against a bookmaker. The company operates in Mexico under regulatory approval (DGAJS/SCEVF/P-06/2005-TER), distributes through native iOS and Android apps, and is backed by Sequoia, Kaszek, Bullpen Capital, Stepstone Group, and Courtside Ventures, along with athlete investors. Draftea is a consumer product company and does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public web, support, legal, and open-source engineering surface.

providers.name: Dyndrite
providers.description: Dyndrite develops GPU-accelerated software for digital and additive manufacturing, focused on laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and other metal 3D-printing processes. Its platform streamlines build preparation, materials development, process qualification, and production automation for industrial manufacturers, machine builders (OEMs), and software vendors. Products include Dyndrite LPBF Pro for end users and the Application Development Kit (ADK) for machine makers, exposing low-level toolpathing control (Vector and Raster Toolpathing APIs) plus a scriptable Python geometry engine. Dyndrite is backed by Amplify Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an AI/ML and manufacturing automation company. It does not currently publish a public web/REST API, OpenAPI definition, or self-service developer portal; its APIs are embedded scripting and integration interfaces delivered inside its desktop software and ADK.

providers.name: Earnix
providers.description: Earnix provides an AI orchestration system (Earnix AIOS) purpose-built for insurance and banking decisioning. The platform unifies pricing, an enterprise rating engine, automated underwriting, and real-time customer engagement so insurers and financial institutions can price smarter, underwrite faster, and engage customers better. Earnix serves 100+ leading insurers worldwide, processing billions of transactions annually and compressing rate creation from months to days. Earnix is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Earnix is an enterprise B2B vendor with no public self-serve developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Eat Just
providers.description: Eat Just, Inc. is a food technology company founded in 2011 by Josh Tetrick and Josh Balk, headquartered in Alameda, California, that makes plant-based alternatives to animal products. Its flagship product is JUST Egg, a liquid and folded plant-based egg made from mung bean protein, alongside JUST Meat, JUST Protein and JUST condiments. Its GOOD Meat subsidiary produces cultivated chicken and in December 2020 became the first company in the world to receive regulatory approval to sell cultivated meat, in Singapore, followed by US FDA and USDA approval in June 2023. The company sells through retail, foodservice, restaurant and industrial channels in North America and Europe. Eat Just publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; this profile records its public web and corporate surface only.

providers.name: Elroy Air
providers.description: Elroy Air develops autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo aircraft for defense, commercial, and rapid-response logistics. Its flagship Chaparral is a hybrid-electric aircraft designed to carry up to 300 pounds of cargo across roughly 300 miles with no crew onboard, taking off and landing vertically and cruising autonomously between points. Founded in 2016 and based in San Francisco, the company works with partners including FedEx, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, and Lockheed Martin, and was selected for the U.S. Department of Transportation eVTOL Integration Pilot Program. Elroy Air is a hardware and autonomy company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security data.

providers.name: EnduroSat
providers.description: EnduroSat is a Sofia, Bulgaria-based satellite manufacturer and space service provider working to make space universally accessible by lowering the cost and complexity of accessing space data. The company builds CubeSat and SmallSat platforms (FRAME Max, FRAME L, FRAME S buses and 8U/12U/16U CubeSats), avionics and communication modules (X-Band SDR, S-Band and UHF transceivers, EPS power modules, solar panels, and antennas), and delivers end-to-end Space Service, SpaceOps, and SpaceDev offerings that take customers from idea to orbit in roughly six months. EnduroSat has deployed 100+ satellites with 3,500+ modules in operation, downlinked 500+ TB of data, and serves ~450 customers including NASA, ESA, and IBM Space. It maintains an open-source GitHub organization publishing Cubesat Space Protocol (CSP) implementations and NextGen ground-station and onboard API frameworks. Backed by Founders Fund and GV.

providers.name: Fabric Technologies
providers.description: Fabric Technologies operates Fabric by Gerber Life, a direct-to-consumer financial services platform built for parents and families. The company offers term life insurance with an instant online quote and application flow, UGMA custodial investment accounts and 529 college-savings plans for children, and digital estate-planning tools including free wills. Fabric is backed by Gerber Life, part of Western & Southern Financial Group, and was originally venture-funded by Bessemer Venture Partners. The platform emphasizes fast, accessible, mobile-first family financial planning spanning protection, wealth-building, and legacy planning. Fabric is a consumer-facing service and does not currently publish a public developer API or portal.

providers.name: Fabrix
providers.description: Fabrix (Fabrix Security) is an AI-native identity and access management company building AI agents for identity security. Its platform centers on the Identity Knowledge Graph, which unifies fragmented human, machine, and AI-agent identities across providers, and a set of AI agents that automate identity visibility and intelligence, user access reviews, just-in-time privileged access, identity lifecycle management, identity security posture management (ISPM), and non-human / AI-agent governance. Deployed as an agentless solution, Fabrix uses cross-provider identity resolution (deterministic matching, heuristics, and AI) plus natural-language analysis to speed access reviews, risk scoring, and compliance. Founded as a venture-backed startup (Norwest Venture Partners, Merlin, Jibe) and ISO 27001 aligned, Fabrix announced it is joining Silverfort in 2026 to build a runtime identity security platform. This profile currently tracks the company and its public web surface; Fabrix does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or API reference.

providers.name: FITCO
providers.description: Fitco is the leading management software for boutique fitness studios and gyms in Latin America. It lets centers administer reservations, memberships, payments, online classes and check-in, and provides a custom website and mobile app for each studio's members. It specializes in pilates, barre, indoor cycling, yoga, functional training, strength, sports academies and wellness centers. Fitco operates in Mexico, Peru, Colombia, Chile, Argentina and the United States; as of May 2026 more than 1,400 fitness centers use it. It integrates online payments via Stripe and Mercado Pago and customer acquisition via Wellhub and TotalPass.

providers.name: Focal Systems
providers.description: Focal Systems is a San Francisco-based deep-learning company building the operating system for brick-and-mortar retail. Its platform combines proprietary shelf-mounted computer-vision cameras, real-time AI, and streaming data to digitize physical stores hourly — tracking on-shelf availability, out-of-stocks, planogram and price-tag compliance, shrink, and inventory. Products include Computer Vision cameras, Shelf AI, the Action Tool associate mobile app, and the Impact analytics dashboard, used by leading grocery and retail chains such as Walmart Canada to reduce waste, redeploy labor, and recover lost sales. Focal Systems is a Y Combinator and Uncork Capital-backed company and operates as an enterprise SaaS vendor; it does not publish a public self-serve developer API or SDK.

providers.name: Frec
providers.description: Frec is a San Francisco fintech offering tax-aware, automated direct indexing for retail investors. Its products — Classic Direct Indexing, Long Short Direct Indexing, Diversify, Trade, Treasury cash management, and a Portfolio Line of Credit — replicate market indices with individual stocks while running automated tax-loss harvesting to minimize capital gains taxes at fees starting around 0.09%. Frec is an SEC-registered investment adviser and SIPC member managing over $1.25B in assets, founded by Mo Al Adham and backed by Greylock. The company ships a consumer investing app and website but does not currently expose a public developer API, so this profile is identity- and security-posture-only.

providers.name: FundersClub
providers.description: FundersClub is an online venture capital firm and investment platform based in San Francisco that lets accredited investors browse, evaluate, and invest in curated early-stage technology startups through professionally managed, single-purpose venture funds. Founders apply for funding and, once selected, gain access to capital, a partner network, and post-investment support. Backed by a16z, Felicis, and Y Combinator, FundersClub pioneered the online VC model. The company publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks its web, identity, and domain-security surface for the network.

providers.name: Gankster
providers.description: Gankster is a consumer competitive-gaming social platform — a web and mobile "looking for group" (LFG) network that helps players team up, practice, and compete across titles including Valorant, League of Legends, Dota 2, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, Fortnite, and World of Warcraft. It matches players by rank, playstyle, and reputation to find duos, five-stacks, and fill players, and lets teams organize scrims, tournaments, and recruitment. Gankster operates entirely outside the game client (no overlays or client modifications) and ships the Gankster Duos mobile app on iOS and Android. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and raised $4.25M for its all-in-one competitive gaming platform. Gankster does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Helio AI LLC
providers.description: Helio AI LLC operates Helio.AI, an AI-powered recruiting and applicant tracking (ATS) platform for HR and talent-acquisition teams. It automates the end-to-end hiring workflow — job posting and distribution, resume screening, candidate tracking, real-time analytics, and team collaboration — and pairs the ATS with a gamified personality test to evaluate candidates. The product is offered in multiple languages (English, Russian, Georgian, Armenian, Azerbaijani, and Uzbek) and targets markets across Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Uzbekistan. Helio AI is backed by 500 Global. The company runs its customer application at app.helio-ai.com and does not currently publish a public developer API program or documentation.

providers.name: Hula Earth
providers.description: Hula Earth is a Munich-based environmental technology company providing real-time biodiversity monitoring. It combines solar-powered, maintenance-free Hula BioT IoT sensors with AI-powered species detection, satellite-based Earth Observation, and the Hula Platform dashboard so organizations can monitor, manage, and report on biodiversity at landscape scale. Hula Earth serves renewables (solar and wind), agriculture, nature conservation, and urban development, turning environmental uncertainty into operational confidence and compliance-ready reporting.

providers.name: Ike Robotics (Nuro)
providers.description: Nuro is an autonomous-vehicle technology company that builds the Nuro Driver, an AI-first self-driving system it now licenses to automakers and mobility providers rather than operating its own delivery fleet. Nuro acquired the assets and team of Ike Robotics, an autonomous-trucking startup, folding that self-driving expertise into its Level 4 autonomy platform. The company partners with firms such as Uber and Lucid to deploy robotaxis and other autonomous applications, and pairs the Nuro Driver with the Nuro Toolkit for validation and deployment. Nuro operates a B2B licensing model and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Indrive
providers.description: inDrive is a global ride-hailing, delivery, and urban-services platform built around a peer-to-peer, name-your-price model in which passengers propose a fare and nearby drivers accept, counter, or decline it directly. Founded in 2012 by Arsen Tomsky in Yakutsk, Russia and now headquartered in Mountain View, California, the company operates across roughly 48 countries and more than 1,000 cities, with over 400 million app downloads. Beyond city rides it offers intercity transport, courier and freight delivery, on-demand task services, and driver lending. inDrive was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bond Capital and General Catalyst. inDrive does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; its GitHub organization hosts internal engineering frameworks and an engineering handbook rather than external API definitions.

providers.name: InfiniGods
providers.description: InfiniGods is a gaming studio building fun, free-to-play, Web3-powered mobile games centered around ancient mythologies. Its titles — Immortal Siege, King of Destiny, and InfiniMerge — share interoperable gaming assets, items, power-ups, and currencies that span the InfiniGods Universe (IGU). Players collect blockchain assets such as the Elder Gods (a 4,488-piece Gen 0 NFT collection that unlocks abilities and boosts scoring across all titles) and the InfiniPass VIP membership (early access, bonus play, exclusive NFT drops, and in-game boosts). The company is backed by Pantera Capital. InfiniGods is a consumer game studio with no public developer/API program; this profile captures its public web, legal, community, and code-org surface.

providers.name: Insify
providers.description: Insify is a Dutch insurtech offering fully digital business insurance for freelancers, self-employed professionals (ZZP'ers) and small-to-medium enterprises in the Netherlands. Its online-first product line covers disability/income protection (arbeidsongeschiktheid, AOV), professional liability (beroepsaansprakelijkheid, BAV), business liability (bedrijfsaansprakelijkheid, AVB), business inventory and goods, electronics, in-vehicle equipment and auto cover, sold and managed entirely online with no setup, advisory or cancellation fees and daily cancellation. Serving more than 40,000 entrepreneurs across professions from IT and photography to care and construction, Insify pairs instant quoting and fast claims with AI-assisted guidance (SmartGuide). Backed by Accel, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an insurance-tech provider profile; it is a consumer-facing insurer and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Instruct
providers.description: Instruct ("AI that works for you") is an AI automation platform that lets non-technical users delegate repetitive work across their connected applications. Users describe a task in natural language and Instruct's AI pulls context from one integrated app, acts on it in another, and can turn any successful one-off task into a recurring scheduled workflow, spanning use cases across education, recruiting, sales, and operations. It is a hosted end-user application with a free plan and Google/email sign-up. As of this profile Instruct does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. Instruct is backed by Creandum.

providers.name: Isar Aerospace
providers.description: Isar Aerospace is a European space launch service provider founded in 2018 and headquartered in Ottobrunn near Munich, Germany. The company designs and manufactures Spectrum, a two-stage orbital small-lift launch vehicle capable of carrying up to 1,000 kg to low Earth orbit or up to 700 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit, using liquid oxygen and propane propulsion. Spectrum is fully developed and produced in-house with automated, scalable manufacturing including additive manufacturing and carbon-composite structures. Isar Aerospace offers dedicated, lead, and rideshare launch services for small and medium satellites and constellations. Backed by more than EUR 500 million in private capital from investors including Earlybird and HV Capital, the company employs over 400 people from nearly 50 nations and conducted the inaugural Spectrum test flight from Andoya Spaceport, Norway, on 30 March 2025.

providers.name: Kidas
providers.description: Kidas is a Techstars-backed trust-and-safety company that builds white-label scam detection and online-protection solutions for enterprises and consumers. Its ProtectMe platform monitors PC gaming and Discord voice and text channels for cyberbullying, predators, phishing, and scams, and its broader suite adds SMS scam detection, email protection, a scam-screening chatbot, and deepfake/impersonation defense that integrate into existing customer channels. Kidas markets custom builds and lists Aura, Comcast, Overwolf, Razer, Walmart, Intel, and Best Buy among its customers. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Kindred
providers.description: Kindred is a members-only home exchange platform where verified members swap their real homes with one another instead of paying for traditional accommodation. The service runs on a credit economy — members earn one night of travel credit for every night they host, and new members start with five nights of credit. Kindred verifies every member and home, provides professional cleaning before and after each stay, and includes up to $100K in damage protection. There are no membership fees; travelers pay only a cleaning and service fee per trip. The platform operates across 190+ cities in North America and Europe and is backed by a16z, Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, Index Ventures, and NEA. Kindred is a consumer travel product and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Lightberry
providers.description: Lightberry is a San Francisco robotics software company (Y Combinator Fall 2025) that builds conversational AI "personality" software for humanoid and quadruped robots. Its platform lets a robot listen, speak, see its surroundings, and act on natural-language instruction without the owner writing any code, emphasizing emotional intelligence, contextual awareness, and autonomy rather than a simple speech-to-text voice pipeline. Lightberry ships pre-installed on robots sold through its partnership with Unitree, and the company runs a manufacturer-compatibility program with robot makers including Fourier, Booster Robotics, and High Torque. Its published documentation today covers device setup (power-on, WiFi provisioning, starting a conversation) plus an MCP architecture note describing a Model Context Protocol server that routes tool calls to individual Lightberry devices, which each expose a REST endpoint. There is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI definition at this time.

providers.name: Linearity
providers.description: Linearity GmbH is a Berlin-based design-technology company building AI-assisted design and animation software for individuals, marketing teams, and enterprises. Its two flagship products are Linearity Curve, a professional vector design and graphic art tool formerly released as Vectornator, and Linearity Move, an animation tool that turns static designs into motion graphics with Auto-Animate and keyframe control. The platform adds an AI Design Generator that produces entire marketing campaigns, social posts, ads, and templates from a text prompt as fully editable vector files rather than flat images, along with an AI Vector Generator, Auto-Resize for adapting assets across channels, brand-kit management, and collaborative team workspaces with role-based permissions. Products ship on macOS and iOS with a web workspace. Linearity publishes no public HTTP API, developer portal, or SDKs as of July 2026; it does publish an llms.txt, dated release notes, a help center, and a public status page.

providers.name: Lolli
providers.description: Lolli is a bitcoin and cash-back rewards company founded in 2018 by CEO Alex Adelman, on a mission to make bitcoin accessible to everyone. Through a browser extension, website, and mobile app, Lolli gives shoppers a percentage of their purchase back in bitcoin or cash when they shop online and in-store at 25,000+ merchants including Adidas, Microsoft, Ulta, and Kroger. Merchants pay Lolli for driving sales, and Lolli shares that commission with users as rewards paid into their Lolli wallet. The company reports having distributed over $10 million in bitcoin rewards and onboarded thousands of people into bitcoin for the first time. Lolli is a consumer product; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Marcus by Goldman Sachs
providers.description: Marcus by Goldman Sachs is the U.S. consumer banking brand of The Goldman Sachs Group, launched in 2016 to offer no-fee high-yield Online Savings Accounts and Certificates of Deposit (CDs) directly to retail customers online. Deposits are held at Goldman Sachs Bank USA, a New York State-chartered bank and member of the Federal Reserve System, insured by the FDIC. After Goldman's broad retreat from consumer lending, Marcus no longer originates personal loans and now centers on digital deposit products. Marcus operates NO public first-party consumer developer API and runs no self-serve developer portal for its retail banking products; the Goldman Sachs Developer platform (developer.gs.com) serves institutional Transaction Banking and Marquee offerings, not Marcus consumer banking. Consumer-permissioned account data (balances, transactions, account/holder info) is reachable only through third-party open-finance aggregators such as Plaid, Flinks, and MX, not a documented Marcus API. As a bank chartered in the U.S., Goldman Sachs Bank USA is subject to the emerging CFPB Section 1033 personal financial data rights framework, but no first-party FDX-conformant Marcus developer interface is publicly documented as of this record.

providers.name: Markt Pilot (aka MP)
providers.description: MARKT-PILOT GmbH is a German software company (registered in Beilstein, business address Stuttgart, with a US office in Chicago) that provides a unified pricing performance platform for industrial manufacturers. Its flagship product, MP ONE, combines an Intelligence Engine (real-time competitor and market data with AI-powered cross-reference part matching), a Decision Engine (cost-plus, market-based, and attribute-based pricing workflows), and a Performance Engine (portfolio, revenue, and margin analysis with executive dashboards). MARKT-PILOT serves 200+ manufacturers across agriculture, construction and mining, machine tooling, packaging, and industrial equipment, helping them move from static annual spare-parts pricing to dynamic, data-driven pricing. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. The company operates a marketing site, blog, and a hosted (Better Stack) status page, but publishes no public developer/API surface: no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, well-known discovery endpoints, or client SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Matera
providers.description: Matera is a French proptech company providing a digital platform for condominium management (syndic de copropriété), rental property management (gestion locative), and real estate transactions. Founded in Paris, Matera lets co-owners self-manage their buildings with software backed by 200+ in-house accountants, lawyers, and works experts, plus embedded services such as building insurance, legal protection, and a Treezor-powered payment account. It serves 150,000+ co-owners across France and is a certified B Corporation.

providers.name: Medeloop
providers.description: Medeloop is an AI platform for the clinical research lifecycle, describing itself as an operating system for clinical research that spans grant discovery and funding, real-world evidence generation from patient data, and delivering actionable intelligence at the point of care. Its products include Medeloop Analytics (AI agents that analyze EHR, claims, and registry data without requiring users to code), EvidenceKit (analytics paired with all-payer claims data), Medeloop Grants (AI-assisted grant discovery and proposal writing), and Medeloop Care (population health and care management). The platform is federated (compute moves to the data, which stays in the customer's infrastructure), CDM-agnostic (Epic, Cerner, Meditech, OMOP, i2b2, or custom schemas), and model-agnostic (routing tasks across OpenAI, Anthropic, or DeepSeek), with multi-cloud deployment across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-premise. It serves pharmaceutical and life-sciences companies, health systems, and clinical researchers. As of this enrichment pass Medeloop publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; its documentation host (docs.medeloop.ai) is gated behind Okta authentication and its analytics application is a private client login.

providers.name: Mindful Health Solutions
providers.description: Mindful Health Solutions is a behavioral-health-care provider specializing in innovative, evidence-based psychiatric treatments for depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, and other treatment-resistant conditions. Founded in 2007 (originally as TMS Health Solutions) by Dr. Richard Bermudes, the company pioneered TMS-focused clinics in the United States and offers Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS), SPRAVATO (esketamine) nasal spray, IV Ketamine infusion therapy, medication management, and psychiatric care across roughly 20 clinics in California, Texas, and Washington. Mindful Health Solutions maintains one of the world's largest TMS and esketamine patient-outcome repositories. It is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. As a clinical healthcare provider it publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, an AI-crawler llms.txt it publishes, and its domain-security posture.

providers.name: MOD Pizza
providers.description: MOD Pizza is a Seattle-based fast-casual restaurant chain built around individually sized, made-to-order artisan-style pizzas and salads sold at one fixed price regardless of how many of its 40-plus toppings, finishing sauces and dressings a guest chooses. The company operates and franchises hundreds of locations across the United States and runs a digital guest surface consisting of a WordPress marketing site, a Yext-powered store locator, a Koala-powered online ordering storefront at orders.modpizza.com, and a Punchh-powered MOD Rewards loyalty app on iOS and Android. MOD Pizza is a consumer of restaurant-technology APIs rather than a publisher of them: as of this profiling pass it operates no developer program, publishes no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or MCP contract, and exposes no partner or franchisee API documentation on any host it controls. Delivery is fulfilled through third-party marketplaces such as DoorDash rather than a first-party delivery API.

providers.name: Moleaer
providers.description: Moleaer Inc. is a Hawthorne, California nanobubble technology company that designs and manufactures nanobubble generators — Clear, Bloom, Lotus, Neo, Nexus, Trinity, Freya, Indalo, Titan and XTB, plus the NanoShield service — used to raise dissolved oxygen, act as a chemical-free oxidant, and control algae and biofilm in aquaculture, horticulture and irrigation water, lakes and ponds, wastewater treatment, food and beverage, car washes, mining, and oil and gas. Its only digital surface is a customer-only remote monitoring service, launched in 2020 with industrial IoT provider AMI Global, that reports equipment status and water-quality readings (DO, pH, ORP, temperature, conductivity) into a login-gated portal at www.monitoring-moleaer.com. Moleaer publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification; equipment-level integration is offered through industrial control protocols (SCADA/Modbus/EtherNet-IP) on the generators themselves, not through a web API.

providers.name: Monitaur
providers.description: Monitaur is an enterprise AI governance platform that helps regulated organizations manage machine learning and AI responsibly across the full model lifecycle. Its software lets teams define enterprise-wide AI governance policies, manage and monitor model performance for drift and bias, and automate model validation, risk assessment, stress testing, and vendor governance at scale. Monitaur is built for regulated industries such as insurance and financial services, delivering audit-ready documentation and compliance reporting.
